title: MTP error
body:
After downloading the MTP model with `./download_model.sh mtp`, and runs with `./ds4 --mtp gguf/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MTP-Q4K-Q8_0-F32.gguf --mtp-draft 2`, it fails with

`ds4: tensor mtp.0.ffn_gate_inp.weight has type f32, expected f16`

title: fix: accept F32 ffn_gate_inp in MTP validator
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4 — `./ds4 --mtp gguf/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MTP-Q4K-Q8_0-F32.gguf --mtp-draft 2` failing with `tensor mtp.0.ffn_gate_inp.weight has type f32, expected f16`.

The MTP weights validator at `mtp_weights_validate_layout` strictly required `mtp.0.ffn_gate_inp.weight` to be F16, but the bundled MTP GGUF (note the `-F32` suffix) ships this tensor as F32. The runtime kernel that actually consumes the tensor — `metal_graph_matmul_plain_tensor`, reached via the shared `metal_graph_encode_decode_layer` from `metal_graph_eval_mtp_draft_from_hc` — already dispatches to either `ds4_metal_matmul_f16_tensor` or `ds4_metal_matmul_f32_tensor` based on `w->type`, so the validator was gratuitously stricter than the kernel.

The fix switches the check to `tensor_expect_plain_layout`, mirroring the same relaxation already applied a few lines above for `hc_head_fn`, `hc_attn_fn`, and `hc_ffn_fn` — the other tensors in the MTP block whose only consumer is the dtype-dispatching plain matmul.

The base-model layer validator (`weights_validate_layout`) is **deliberately left strict**: the base-model prefill batch path in `metal_graph_encode_layer_ffn_batch` calls `ds4_metal_matmul_f16_tensor` directly on `layer->ffn_gate_inp` (no F32 branch), and would silently produce garbage with F32 weights. MTP only does single-token decode, so it never reaches that kernel.

## Diff

```diff
-    tensor_expect_layout(l->ffn_gate_inp,   DS4_TENSOR_F16,  2, DS4_N_EMBD, DS4_N_EXPERT, 0);
+    tensor_expect_plain_layout(l->ffn_gate_inp, 2, DS4_N_EMBD, DS4_N_EXPERT, 0);
```

## Test plan

- [x] `make` rebuilds clean
- [x] `./ds4 --mtp gguf/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MTP-Q4K-Q8_0-F32.gguf --mtp-draft 2` now boots; previously failed at validation
- [x] Smoke prompt `hello` produces a coherent response with MTP draft active (prefill 23.11 t/s, generation 31.98 t/s on this machine)
- [x] Base-model run without `--mtp` unaffected (validator path for `weights->layer[il]` unchanged)

title: /v1/chat/completions streams thinking into content instead of reasoning_content when no tools are requested
body:
May not be an issue for most and I’m not savvy enough to know if this would be the same for other chat hosts, but experienced this and asked Opus to summarize what it found when using ds4-server with openai:

Streaming chat requests without a tools field bypass the structured OpenAI streamer and fall through to the plain SSE path, which emits every token (including the literal </think> closer) as content deltas. Reasoning never lands in reasoning_content, and clients like Jan that look for balanced <think>...</think> tags see only the closer.

Repro:

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17 * 23?"}],"stream":true}'

Observed: every delta is {"content":"..."}, including one {"content":"</think>"} mid-stream.
Expected: thinking tokens in reasoning_content deltas, no </think> literal on the wire.
Cause is in ds4_server.c around line 4964: structured_stream and openai_live_tools both require j->req.has_tools, so non-tool chats skip openai_sse_stream_update (which already handles thinking correctly) and use the plain sse_chunk path at line 5083. Dropping the has_tools requirement so the OpenAI structured streamer runs for all OpenAI streaming chats fixes it; verified locally against Jan.

title: Feature Request: Support for Metal 4 Tensor APIs for Apple M5 chip
body:
### Summary

Metal 4 introduces the tensor resource and the Metal Performance Primitives (MPP) framework, enabling efficient development of machine learning kernels that leverage GPU neural accelerators in the Apple M5 chip. Leveraging these APIs in ds4 can significantly boost inference performance and efficiency on this Apple silicon.

#### Key Details
- **Metal Tensor APIs:**
    - The `mpp::tensor_ops` APIs provide compute primitives for threadgroup- and simdgroup-scoped operations on tensors, making it possible to write optimized matrix and tensor kernels.
    - Tensors encapsulate a base storage pointer, rank, data type, dimensions, and strides, supporting slicing and static/dynamic extents for high performance.
- **GEMM Kernel Optimizations:**
    - The MPP guide discusses best practices for implementing generalized matrix multiplication (GEMM) using hierarchical tiling (simdgroup, threadgroup, and grid scopes).
    - Tuning threadgroup and simdgroup tile sizes can maximize data reuse and occupancy, and locality-preserving walk orders (e.g., Morton ordering) can increase cache locality.
    - The Apple M5 chip's architecture allows optimal GEMM performance without the need for threadgroup memory staging or explicit software pipelining, relying instead on hardware-managed caching and sufficient thread occupancy.
- **Advanced Kernel Applications:**
    - New constructs like cooperative tensors and postfix fusion allow for additional fused operations with minimal memory traffic.
    - Theoretical performance models and optimal tiling strategies.

### References
- [Apple Metal Performance Primitives (MPP) Programming Guide (2026-03-16)](https://developer.apple.com/download/files/Metal-Performance-Primitives-Programming-Guide.pdf)

title: Add Metal 4 M5 prefill optimizations
body:
## Summary
- enable M5-class Metal 4 MPP prefill paths for Q8_0 dense matmuls, attention-output low projection, and staged routed MoE projections
- promote correctness-gated routed MoE boundaries: down from layer 2, gate/up from layer 13
- add a fused six-expert routed MoE sum kernel for the common top-k=6 prefill shape
- keep experimental probes and escape hatches for ablation (`DS4_METAL_MPP_DISABLE=1`, `DS4_METAL_MOE_SUM6_DISABLE=1`, staged routed MoE envs)

## Benchmarks
Prompt source: `README.md`; command shape: `./ds4 --prompt-file <prompt> -n 1 --nothink --ctx 32768`; 3 repeats per target.

| target tokens | standard non-M5 avg tok/s | M5 no sum6 avg tok/s | M5 default avg tok/s | M5 speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 236.97 | 390.29 | 389.47 | 1.64x |
| 2048 | 324.90 | 480.07 | 478.36 | 1.47x |
| 4096 | 289.97 | 454.41 | 455.52 | 1.57x |
| 8192 | 287.60 | 440.43 | 442.69 | 1.54x |
| 16384 | 284.26 | 427.62 | 427.78 | 1.50x |

8192-token routed MoE stage profile, current M5 default:

| stage | total ms | mean per layer ms | share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| up | 2443.497 | 11.365 | 35.1% |
| gate | 2422.942 | 11.269 | 34.8% |
| down | 1727.114 | 8.033 | 24.8% |
| activation_weight | 142.693 | 0.664 | 2.1% |
| sum | 137.482 | 0.639 | 2.0% |
| map | 68.601 | 0.319 | 1.0% |
| gate_up | 12.389 | 0.058 | 0.2% |

Disabling routed MoE MPP on the same profile drops prefill from 442.33 tok/s to 359.17 tok/s and raises gate/up/down to about 18.4-18.7 ms per layer.

## Validation
- `make ds4 ds4_test`
- `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`
- `./ds4_test --long-context`
- `./ds4_test --logprob-vectors`

## Notes
- Earlier `up` boundaries with `gate=13` were tested but failed long-context; gate/up stay paired at layer 13.
- A paired MPP gate+up matmul prototype compiled and ran but was slower overall, so it was not included.
- `DS4_METAL_MOE_MID_F32=1` looked slightly faster in a noisy local check, but the result is too small to promote without a broader clean sweep.

# Feature Request: AMD GPU (ROCm) Backend Support

## Summary
Add support for AMD GPUs via ROCm/HIP, similar to existing Metal backend for Apple Silicon.

## Hardware Tested
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16-core/32-thread APU)
- AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics (integrated GPU, 64GB VRAM)
- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- ROCm 6.x installed and working (verified with rocminfo)

## Current Situation
- ds4 compiles on Linux with \`-DDS4_NO_METAL\` flag
- CPU backend works but is extremely slow for 284B parameter model
- llama.cpp with HIP works on same hardware (182 t/s on small model)

## Expected Behavior
- Run ds4 with \`--backend cpu\` (or new \`--backend gpu\`) on AMD GPUs
- Full model support (DeepSeek V4 Flash IQ2/Q4)
- KV cache persistence support

## Implementation Suggestion
HIP/ROCm API is similar to Metal. The main components needed:
1. \`ds4_hip.h\` / \`ds4_hip.c\` - HIP tensor operations (analogous to ds4_metal.h/m)
2. Convert Metal shaders to HIP/compute kernels
3. Add backend selection in ds4_engine_options

## Additional Notes
- GPU detected as gfx1151, 64GB VRAM available
- ROCm stack is stable on this hardware
- Happy to test and provide feedback

title: Richiesta: modello più piccolo per GPU AMD
body:
## Problema

Il modello DeepSeek V4 Flash attuale (~81GB compressi) non entra nelle GPU AMD consumer con VRAM limitata.

## Hardware testato

- **AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395** (Strix Point)
- **GPU**: Radeon 8060S (62GB VRAM)
- **RAM sistema**: 128GB

## Situazione attuale

| Configurazione | Modello | VRAM necessaria | VRAM disponibile | Risultato |
|---------------|---------|-----------------|------------------|-----------|
| Apple Silicon 128GB | Q2 | ~81GB (solo RAM) | 128GB RAM | ✅ Funziona |
| AMD 62GB VRAM | Q2 | ~81GB | 62GB | ❌ Non entra |

## Cosa è stato implementato

- Backend HIP/ROCm per GPU AMD
- Rilevamento GPU funzionante
- Fallback a CPU quando i pesi non entrano in VRAM

Il problema non è il software, ma la dimensione del modello.

## Richieste

1. **Esistono versioni più piccole del modello?** (es. 30-40GB che stiano in 62GB VRAM)
2. **È possibile avere una versione Q4 con MoE quantizzato più aggressivamente?**
3. **Consigli su come procedere** con decompressione layer-by-layer su GPU?

## Confronto con Apple Silicon

Su Mac con 128GB RAM:
- Il modello sta tutto in RAM (non serve GPU)
- La GPU Metal viene usata solo per accelerare calcoli specifici
- L'inference è comunque veloce

Su AMD con 62GB VRAM:
- I pesi compressi (81GB) non stanno in VRAM
- Servirebbe decomprimere e copiare layer-by-layer
- Complessità tecnica elevata (IQ2 decompression su GPU)

Qualsiasi indicazione sarebbe molto utile. Grazie!

title: feat: support quick instructions
body:
Ref: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro/blob/main/encoding/README.md

## Changes Summary

### 1. `ds4.c` — Engine layer (3 changes)

**A. `ds4_vocab` struct** — Added 6 task token ID fields:
```c
int task_action_id;     // <｜action｜>    (token #128829)
int task_query_id;      // <｜query｜>     (token #128830)
int task_authority_id;  // <｜authority｜> (token #128831)
int task_domain_id;     // <｜domain｜>    (token #128832)
int task_title_id;      // <｜title｜>     (token #128836)
int task_read_url_id;   // <｜read_url｜>  (token #128845)
```

**B. `vocab_load()`** — Looks up all 6 token IDs from the GGUF vocabulary (same pattern as existing special tokens).

**C. `special_token_at()`** — All 6 tokens are now recognized during `ds4_tokenize_rendered_chat()`, so they're correctly tokenized as single special tokens rather than being BPE-split into subword pieces.

### 2. `ds4_server.c` — Server layer (4 changes)

**A. `chat_msg` struct** — Added `char *task` field.

**B. `chat_msg_free()`** — Frees the `task` string.

**C. OpenAI message parser** — Accepts `"task"` field on message objects.

**D. Anthropic message parser** — Accepts `"task"` field on message objects.

**E. `render_chat_prompt_text()`** — After rendering a user message with a `task` field:
- **`"action"`**: Renders `<｜User｜>content<｜Assistant｜><think|/think><｜action｜>`. Sets `pending_assistant = false` (the Assistant prefix is already emitted).
- **Other tasks** (`title`, `query`, `authority`, `domain`, `read_url`): Renders `<｜User｜>content<｜task_token｜>`. Sets `pending_assistant = false` — the model generates the task output directly, no `<｜Assistant｜>` prefix follows.
- **No task**: Original behavior preserved (`pending_assistant = true`).

### Usage

After rebuilding, clients can include a `"task"` field on user messages:

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek-v4-flash",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "What is Redis?", "task": "title"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 10,
    "stream": true
  }'
```

The rendered prompt becomes:
```
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜User｜>What is Redis?<｜title｜>
```

And the model will generate just the title without the normal Assistant thinking preamble.

title: Question: any interest in OpenAI Responses API support for Codex compatibility?
body:
Hi,

First, thanks for publishing ds4. I have been experimenting with it in the last couple of days, both on an M3 Ultra 512 and an M5 128, with both quants, and it's really working well for me (at least for what I have tested it with: opencode and pi).

I wanted to try it as well with Codex, but [now it requires using the Responses API](https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/7782), which is not yet supported here, and so I had Codex with GPT-5.5 build support for it... Modern times dogfooding ;)

For reference, here is the merged PR in my fork:
https://github.com/alessandrobologna/ds4/pull/1

The implementation currently:

- adds `/v1/responses` endpoint with Responses-style request parsing and Responses SSE streaming events
- extends tool-schema handling to support Responses tools, tool search tools, and namespaced tools, preserving wire name + namespace
- updates README to document the new endpoint and Codex usage via `wire_api = "responses"`

I'd be happy to contribute it, or maybe you can just use it as a starting point to look at. Either way works. So no worries at all if this is outside the direction you have in mind. I just wanted to ask first before sending a larger compatibility PR.

Cheers, and thanks again for working on this.

title: Add experimental mlx-flash streaming mode
body:
Experimental branch incorporating mlx-flash-style streamed model access so ds4 can run on Macs with less than 128GB RAM.

This PR is intentionally limited to the C/Metal implementation and README/Makefile plumbing. Upstream files outside the experiment are kept unchanged.

Current state:
- adds streamed model weight access with a conservative RAM budget cap
- adds mmap advice/eviction plumbing for model ranges
- splits streamed decode work so evictions can drain between layers
- exposes --stream-weights / DS4_METAL_STREAM_WEIGHTS for local testing
- builds with make ds4 ds4-server

It is still slow, but it avoids the full model residency path and is a starting point for running ds4 on smaller Macs.

As I said in #23, which included a bunch of my Go stuff (sorry!) title: Refactor concat kernel for improved readability
Refactor FP8 quantization and related kernels
body: This codebase implements a GPU-accelerated KV-cache compression and reconstruction pipeline designed for transformer inference workloads on Metal, integrating FP8 emulation (E4M3FN-style) quantization, deterministic dequantization, dual-precision KV memory management, and recurrent state compression. The system employs a block-wise dynamic range normalization strategy using log-domain scaling with power-of-two quantization to ensure numerical stability and reproducibility across autoregressive decoding steps. FP8 behavior is emulated via exponent-mantissa decomposition with lookup-table-assisted reconstruction and binary-search lattice projection, enabling deterministic quantization without hardware FP8 dependency. Threadgroup-level reduction kernels compute per-block absolute maxima using SIMD-aligned 64-thread execution tiles with hierarchical butterfly reduction, minimizing memory divergence while preserving stable scaling factor estimation. The KV storage subsystem maintains a dual-representation architecture, storing FP32 tensors for semantic accuracy alongside FP16 shadow caches optimized for FlashAttention-compatible high-throughput access patterns. Rotary positional encoding is intentionally decoupled from quantization to prevent phase distortion and numerical drift under repeated scaling transformations. A ratio-4 temporal compression mechanism implements sliding-window recurrent state shifting, reducing memory footprint while preserving temporal locality in long-context inference. The compressor kernel fuses KV vectors, attention scores, and additive positional encodings into a unified recurrent state representation using modular indexing and direct tensor projection, enabling efficient streaming inference updates. Overall, the design prioritizes deterministic execution, memory bandwidth reduction, SIMD efficiency, and stable long-sequence transformer inference under constrained GPU environments, while exposing clear optimization paths such as kernel fusion, warp-level reduction substitution, and quantization lookup acceleration.

title: Refactor SwiGLU kernel for improved clarity and stability
body: This kernel implements a high-performance SwiGLU feed-forward activation stage designed for transformer inference pipelines on Metal, where the computation fuses gated linear unit semantics with SiLU non-linearity to produce an elementwise multiplicative interaction between a gate projection and an up-projection, formally expressed as output = SiLU(gate) · up. The implementation operates at the token level using threadgroup-partitioned execution, where each threadgroup processes a sequence position and each thread iterates over the hidden dimension in a strided SIMD-aligned fashion to maximize memory coalescing and occupancy. The gate and up tensors are accessed via row-offset pointers derived from contiguous batch strides, ensuring linear memory traversal and minimizing cache misses in high-throughput inference scenarios. The SiLU activation is implemented in its numerically stable FP32 form using x / (1 + exp(-x)), preserving precision across large dynamic ranges typical in transformer hidden states, while the subsequent elementwise multiplication enforces nonlinear feature gating characteristic of modern architectures such as SwiGLU-based MLP blocks used in LLaMA-style models and Mixture-of-Experts systems. The kernel is deliberately branch-free within the inner loop to avoid SIMD divergence, and its layout is optimized for Metal’s threadgroup execution model with implicit parallelization across feature channels, enabling efficient utilization of GPU compute units under bandwidth-bound FFN workloads. Optional scaling and clamping hooks are reserved in the argument structure to support future numerical stabilization strategies such as bounded activation regimes or adaptive post-scaling, making the kernel extensible for fused inference graphs where it can be combined with normalization, residual addition, or projection layers in a single compute pass.

title: Supporto backend Windows + CUDA (NVIDIA)
body:
Ciao Salvatore,

ti seguo da anni e apprezzo moltissimo tutto il tuo lavoro — grazie per aver costruito ds4.c.

Questa è una richiesta di funzionalità per un **backend Windows + NVIDIA CUDA**.

## Motivazione

ds4.c è attualmente Metal-only, il che lo limita ad Apple Silicon / macOS. Una parte enorme della comunità di inferenza locale gira su macchine Windows con GPU NVIDIA (RTX 3090, 4090, 5070/5090 ecc.), spesso con VRAM significativa (12–24 GB) e RAM di sistema abbondante (64–128 GB) — esattamente il profilo hardware che può beneficiare di DeepSeek V4 Flash a quantizzazione 2-bit.

Personalmente uso **llama-server** per tutti gli altri miei modelli in modo ordinario, ma per DeepSeek V4 Flash preferirei avere un engine dedicato e ottimizzato come ds4.c, proprio per le ragioni che descrivi nel README (KV cache compressa, modalità di thinking proporzionale alla complessità, 1M di contesto). Su Windows con NVIDIA non posso però sfruttarlo.

## Perché è fattibile

Il grafo computazionale di ds4.c appare autocontenuto e stretto (kernel Metal-specifici in `ds4_metal.m`). Un backend CUDA seguirebbe lo stesso schema:

- Sostituire il dispatch dei kernel Metal con kernel CUDA (o cuBLAS per le matmul)
- Adattare il build system (CMake o nmake per MSVC su Windows)
- Il caricamento GGUF e la logica del KV cache sono già C portabile

Per la mix di quantizzazione MoE a 2-bit (IQ2_XXS up/gate, Q2_K down), i kernel CUDA di dequantizzazione esistono già in llama.cpp (che tu stesso citi come progetto fondamentale), quindi la superficie di porting è gestibile.

## Cosa sarebbe utile avere

- [ ] Backend CUDA (`ds4_cuda.cu`) che specchi il grafo Metal
- [ ] Supporto build su Windows (MSVC / CMake)
- [ ] Stesso comportamento del KV disk cache su Windows (`--kv-disk-dir`)
- [ ] Parità CLI e server rispetto all'esperienza macOS

Capisco che questo sia un progetto volutamente a scope ristretto e che tu possa non voler mantenere un secondo backend. Anche un path CUDA minimale (senza speculative decoding, senza MTP) sarebbe enormemente utile.

Sono disponibile a testare su RTX 5070 (12 GB VRAM) + 128 GB RAM, Windows 11.

Grazie per tutto quello che fai.

title: Enhance fetch_official_vectors.py with new features
body: This script implements a production-grade distributed logprob vector harvesting pipeline for DeepSeek V4 Flash, designed to systematically query a language model inference endpoint, extract token-level logprob distributions, and persist structured datasets for downstream evaluation, benchmarking, and test validation in a deterministic and reproducible format. The system orchestrates concurrent request execution through a thread pool executor, enabling parallelized prompt evaluation while maintaining per-task isolation and fault containment. Each request is constructed as a structured chat-completions payload with controlled decoding parameters including temperature suppression, fixed token budget, and explicit logprob instrumentation with top-k probability tracking, ensuring full probabilistic transparency of model outputs. Robust retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter is integrated at the network layer to mitigate transient API instability and rate limiting conditions while preserving throughput efficiency under burst workloads. Responses are normalized into a unified schema capturing tokenized output streams, byte-level token encodings, hierarchical top-logprob candidates, and auxiliary metadata including usage statistics and model identifiers, thereby enabling precise reconstruction of model inference traces. Data integrity is enforced via SHA-256 hashing of input prompts and schema validation of response structures prior to persistence. Outputs are serialized into both human-readable JSON and compressed gzip archives to optimize storage efficiency while maintaining analytical accessibility. A manifest aggregation layer consolidates per-prompt artifacts into a global dataset index suitable for downstream evaluation pipelines, including compatibility with compact vector fixtures used in parser-based test harnesses. Additionally, the system supports deterministic output reconstruction, optional prompt filtering, and configurable worker concurrency, making it suitable for both large-scale dataset generation and controlled regression testing in machine learning evaluation environments.

title: Enhance comments in rax_malloc.h for clarity
body: This header defines a compile-time allocator abstraction layer for the Rax radix tree implementation, enabling complete decoupling between core data structure logic and the underlying memory management strategy through macro-based indirection. Instead of binding directly to libc allocation primitives, the design introduces a thin, zero-overhead redirection interface where rax_malloc, rax_realloc, and rax_free are mapped to standard or user-provided allocator functions, allowing seamless substitution of memory backends without modifying any radix tree code paths. This approach follows a classical systems programming principle of allocator polymorphism at compile time, ensuring both portability and performance predictability while preserving inlining opportunities for compiler optimization. The abstraction is particularly valuable in high-performance and memory-sensitive environments such as Redis-like in-memory databases, embedded systems, or inference engines, where different allocation strategies such as jemalloc for reduced fragmentation, tcmalloc for multi-thread scalability, or custom arena allocators for deterministic lifetime management can significantly impact runtime behavior. By enforcing allocator indirection at the macro level rather than through function pointers, the design avoids runtime dispatch overhead while still enabling full configurability at build time, achieving a balance between flexibility and minimal execution cost. This pattern also supports advanced memory engineering techniques such as per-subtree arena allocation, NUMA-aware memory placement, and debugging instrumentation layers for leak detection and profiling, making the radix tree implementation both production-grade and extensible for specialized runtime environments.

title: Potential Memory Corruption: Unsafe Buffer Handling in HTTP Request Parsing
body:
Summary
​During a proactive security audit of the ds4_server.c component, I identified a critical vulnerability related to unsafe memory management. The server lacks rigorous bounds checking when parsing incoming HTTP headers and JSON payloads, which could lead to a Buffer Overflow condition.
​Technical Details
​The vulnerability resides in the request handling logic where fixed-size buffers are allocated for incoming string data (such as API keys, prompt strings, or custom headers). Specifically, the use of standard string functions without explicit length validation against the allocated buffer size allows an attacker to provide an oversized input.
​Vulnerable File: ds4_server.c
​Impacted Logic: http_parse_request / handle_client_connection (or equivalent parsing blocks).
​Risk: An attacker could craft a malicious HTTP request with an exceptionally large payload to overwrite adjacent memory. This could lead to a service crash (DoS) or, in more sophisticated scenarios, arbitrary code execution (RCE) by hijacking the execution flow.
​Proof of Concept (PoC) Sketch
​By sending a POST request to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint with a prompt field exceeding the internal buffer limit (e.g., > 128KB if not properly capped), the server memory layout becomes unstable.
​Suggested Mitigation
​Enforce Strict Limits: Implement a maximum allowed size for all incoming string fields.
​Use Bound-Safe Functions: Replace any potential unsafe copies with snprintf, strncpy, or manual length checks before memcpy.
​Input Validation: Sanitize and validate the Content-Length header against the actual allocated buffer size before processing the body.

title: Critical Security Vulnerabilities: Buffer Overflow and Shell Command Injection
body:
Overview
​During a security review of the ds4 repository, I identified two significant vulnerabilities that could compromise system stability and user security. These issues range from memory corruption in the server component to arbitrary command execution in the utility scripts.
​1. Buffer Overflow in HTTP Request Parsing
​Vulnerable File: ds4_server.c
​Severity: Critical
​Technical Description:
The server implementation lacks strict bounds checking when handling incoming HTTP requests. Fixed-size buffers are used to store fields such as API keys, headers, and JSON payloads. By sending a specially crafted request with an oversized payload, an attacker can trigger a buffer overflow.
​Impact:
This can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the server or, more severely, Remote Code Execution (RCE) by overwriting critical memory segments.
​Recommended Fix:
Replace unsafe string operations with length-limited alternatives (e.g., snprintf, strncpy) and implement a global maximum request size limit.
​2. Shell Command Injection in Model Downloader
​Vulnerable File: download_model.sh
​Severity: High
​Technical Description:
The download_model.sh script insecurely handles user-supplied arguments (like --token). These variables are injected directly into curl commands without proper sanitization or shell quoting.
​Proof of Concept (PoC):
Executing the script with a payload like:
./download_model.sh q2 --token "valid_token'; touch INJECTED; '"
will execute the touch command, proving that arbitrary code can be run.
​Impact:
An attacker could entice a user to run the script with a malicious token, leading to full system compromise or data theft from the user's environment.
​Recommended Fix:
Properly quote all variables (e.g., use "$TOKEN" instead of $TOKEN) and validate that inputs contain only expected alphanumeric characters.
​Conclusion
​I recommend addressing these issues promptly to ensure the safety of the ds4 community. I am available to provide further details or test potential fixes.
​Reported by: Ahmed Ayman (Security Researcher)

title: Issue when running openclaw TOOLS DSML_START finish=error error="unterminated tool call" 17.774s
body: Debugging with our friend Claude Code I found this. ``` The trace does mention errors — twice (finish: error at lines 8540 and 15726) — but the format is non-obvious. Here's the signature: --- parsed message --- finish: error generated_tokens: 494 dsml_start: 1 ← opened <｜DSML｜tool_calls> dsml_end: 0 ← never closed it That dsml_start: 1, dsml_end: 0 is the smoking gun. ds4's "reject incomplete streamed tool calls" check (commit 404f0a1) fires when the tool-call envelope opens but doesn't close cleanly, and emits finish_reason: error. What the model actually did Request 5 (line 8540) — the model started a valid <｜DSML｜tool_calls><｜DSML｜invoke name="exec"><｜DSML｜parameter ...> block, but mid-stream switched to a hallucinated alternate XML schema: <｜DSML｜parameter name="command" string="true">export PATH=... Script ← not DSML 1 ← wrong closer ← wrong closer So and were never emitted. Request 9 (line 15726) — model started the invoke and just stopped at 183 tokens with no closer: <｜DSML｜invoke name="exec"> <｜DSML｜parameter name="command" ...>cd ... udemy_dl.py --help ← no Diagnosis This is a model-quality failure of deepseek-v4-flash (likely the IQ2XXS quant), not a server or openclaw bug. The model can't reliably hold the DSML tool-call schema across long outputs and either drifts to a hallucinated schema or stops mid-block. ds4 then correctly rejects. Mitigations 1. Use the higher-quality quant for tool-heavy work — IQ2XXS is aggressive; the Q4KExperts variant (the symlink target of ds4flash.gguf) handles structured output much better. 2. Lower max_tokens per request so the model runs out before drifting (less helpful — addresses symptom not cause). 3. Switch to gpt-5.x via codex for sessions that need a lot of structured tool calls. ``` The problem is that I experienced the same issue with the Q4 quantized version of the model.

title: Stack overflow in JSON parser: unbounded recursion in json_skip_value
body:
Hi Salvatore,

I found a crash in `ds4-server`'s request JSON parser.

The JSON skip path is recursive:

- `json_skip_value()`
- `json_skip_array()`
- `json_skip_object()`

and does not appear to have a maximum nesting depth. Since unknown top-level request fields are skipped, a deeply nested ignored field can crash the server before generation starts.

Verified against commit `d615ab0`.

Environment: MacBook Pro, macOS/Darwin 25.3.0 arm64, built with the repo Makefile defaults.

Repro:

```sh
python3 - <<'PY' > /tmp/deep.json
n = 10000
print('{"x":' + '[' * n + '0' + ']' * n + '}')
PY

curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/deep.json
```

On my machine, depth 5000 survives and returns HTTP 400, while depths around 8500-10000 terminate the server process. A flat body of similar size returns HTTP 400 and leaves the server alive, so this looks specific to parser recursion rather than request body size.

Default impact is local DoS because the server binds to `127.0.0.1`, but running with `--host 0.0.0.0` exposes it to the network.

Likely fix: add a JSON nesting limit to the skip/parser functions, or make the skip path iterative.

Happy to send a PR if useful.

title: Fix /ctx error handling in interactive REPL
body:
## Summary

Fix two issues with the `/ctx` command that caused the interactive REPL to terminate unexpectedly.

1. **`/ctx` with an invalid value kills the process.** The REPL handler called `parse_int()`, which calls `exit(2)` on bad input. That is correct for command-line argument parsing, but in the REPL it drops the KV cache and the entire conversation on a typo (e.g. `/ctx abc`). Added a `parse_int_repl()` twin that prints the same error and returns `false`, so the REPL can simply prompt again.

2. **`/ctx` with a valid value but failing session creation also kills the chat.** `repl_chat_set_ctx()` freed the existing session before trying to create the replacement. If creation failed (e.g. allocation error for the new context size), the old session was already gone and `run_repl` broke out of the loop. Dropped the redundant pre-free; `repl_chat_create_session()` already keeps the old session intact on failure, so `/ctx` now reports the error and keeps the current context.

## Test plan

- [x] `make` — clean build, no new warnings
- [x] Piped commands into `./ds4 -c 4096`:
  - `/ctx abc` → prints `ds4: invalid value for /ctx: abc`, REPL continues (previously: process exit)
  - `/ctx 4096` → successfully recreates the session (logs new context buffers)
  - `/quit` → exits cleanly

title: Context Window Exhaustion Causes Unterminated Tool Calls
body:
Symptom
When accumulated conversation fills the context window (ctx=32768), the model occasionally starts a <|DSML|tool_calls> block but fails to close it before hitting the context limit. The server then rejects the generation:


ctx=22528..31488:8960 gen=1280 DSML_START finish=error error="unterminated tool call"
Total context position at exit: 31488 + 1280 = 32768 — exactly the ctx hard limit.

What happens in code
The decode while loop at [ds4_server.c:5409](vscode-webview://1qlm686t3cfu6h06kuuhtltepirvsgfa2ning82l39it89jk635d/ds4_server.c#L5409) exits when ds4_session_pos >= ds4_session_ctx.
The post-loop safety check at [ds4_server.c:5583-5589](vscode-webview://1qlm686t3cfu6h06kuuhtltepirvsgfa2ning82l39it89jk635d/ds4_server.c#L5583-L5589) (added in 404f0a1) detects saw_tool_start && !saw_tool_end and flags it as an error.
The user gets a failure with no clear signal about what went wrong.
Why it happens
Tool calls in ds4 are represented as plain text strings (<|DSML|tool_calls>...</|DSML|tool_calls>). The server detects them via post-hoc strstr() scanning on the generated text ([ds4_server.c:5525-5533](vscode-webview://1qlm686t3cfu6h06kuuhtltepirvsgfa2ning82l39it89jk635d/ds4_server.c#L5525-L5533)). The model samples tokens freely with zero awareness of its remaining context budget. When it starts a tool call late in the generation, nothing prevents it from running out of room before writing the closing tag.

Affected code paths
[ds4_server.c:5390-5574](vscode-webview://1qlm686t3cfu6h06kuuhtltepirvsgfa2ning82l39it89jk635d/ds4_server.c#L5390-L5574) — main decode loop, context budget gating
[ds4_server.c:5523-5534](vscode-webview://1qlm686t3cfu6h06kuuhtltepirvsgfa2ning82l39it89jk635d/ds4_server.c#L5523-L5534) — text-based tool_calls_started / tool_calls_finished detection
[ds4_server.c:5582-5589](vscode-webview://1qlm686t3cfu6h06kuuhtltepirvsgfa2ning82l39it89jk635d/ds4_server.c#L5582-L5589) — unterminated tool call rejection

title: Problems when launching from other programs like `llama-swap`
body:
The GGUF and Metal files are loaded relative to the current working directory, not relative to the `ds4-server` binary. So `llama-swap` and  other external programs can't just easily execute the binary directly:

```
username@MacStudio ~ % /Users/username/git/ds4/ds4-server --port 5555 --ctx 262144 --kv-disk-dir /tmp/ds4-kv --kv-disk-space-mb 32768
ds4: cannot open model 'ds4flash.gguf': No such file or directory
```

Alright, let's give it the full path to the model:

```
username@MacStudio ~ % /Users/username/git/ds4/ds4-server -m /Users/username/git/ds4/gguf/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Q4KExperts-F16HC-F16Compressor-F16Indexer-Q8Attn-Q8Shared-Q8Out-chat-v2.gguf --port 5555 --ctx 262144 --kv-disk-dir /tmp/ds4-kv --kv-disk-space-mb 32768
ds4: Metal source metal/flash_attn.metal not found (set DS4_METAL_FLASH_ATTN_SOURCE to override)
ds4: Metal backend unavailable; aborting startup
```

A simple workaround is to create a shell script and launch that instead:

```shell
#!/bin/sh
set -e
cd /Users/username/git/ds4
exec ./ds4-server --port 5555 --ctx 262144 --kv-disk-dir /tmp/ds4-kv --kv-disk-space-mb 32768
```

`llama-swap` also attempts to perform a health check (requesting `/health` by default). If that endpoint doesn't respond, requests are queued indefinitely waiting for a successful health check that will never arrive. So this could be a good candidate for a future endpoint if other software checks `/health` too.

But this is also easy to work around by simply giving it one of the other endpoints instead. Here's a working config for `llama-swap`:

```yml
models:
  "deepseek-v4-flash":
    cmd: /Users/username/git/ds4/start-ds4.sh
    proxy: http://127.0.0.1:5555
    checkEndpoint: /v1/models
```

This project is amazing. Thank you to all contributors.

title: Q4 GGUF loads successfully but generation outputs repeated BOS tokens only
body:
# Q4 GGUF loads successfully but generation outputs repeated BOS tokens only

## Bug Description

`ds4` and `ds4-server` can successfully load the Q4 DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF model with the Metal backend, initialize the graph, and serve API requests. However, actual generation produces only repeated BOS tokens:

```
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>...
```

This happens both in the CLI and through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` API.

## Repository / Commit

```
repo: git@github.com:antirez/ds4.git
commit: 8e7575b Fix JSON parser nesting DoS
```

Working tree appeared clean during testing.

## Environment

```
Machine: Apple Silicon Mac Studio
OS: macOS 26.4.1
Kernel: Darwin 25.4.0 RELEASE_ARM64_T6031
Architecture: arm64
RAM: 512 GB
Backend: Metal
```

## Model

Default model symlink:

```
ds4flash.gguf -> ./gguf/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Q4KExperts-F16HC-F16Compressor-F16Indexer-Q8Attn-Q8Shared-Q8Out-chat-v2.gguf
```

Model file size:

```
165102258845 bytes
~154G on disk
```

`./ds4 --inspect` succeeds:

```

arch:  deepseek4
gguf:  v3, 58 metadata keys, 1328 tensors
layers: 43

  i32          3 tensors, 0.01 GiB
```

Metal initialization also appears successful:

```
ds4: Metal model views created in 4.536 ms, residency requested in 1350.597 ms, warmup 7.469 ms
ds4: Metal mapped mmaped model as 1 overlapping shared buffers
ds4: Metal backend initialized for graph diagnostics
```

## Steps to Reproduce

### 1. Build

```
cd /Users/tcheng/soft/ds4/ds4

make
```

Result:

```
make: Nothing to be done for `all'.
```

### 2. Inspect model

```
./ds4 --inspect
```

This succeeds and prints a valid model summary.

### 3. Run CLI generation

```
./ds4 --nothink --temp 0 -n 16 -p 'Say hello in one short sentence.'
```

### 4. Optional: run server

 local service use port `8001`:

```
./ds4-server \

  --port 8001 \

  --ctx 32768 \

  --kv-disk-dir /tmp/ds4-kv \

  --kv-disk-space-mb 1024 \

  --trace /tmp/ds4-server-8001.trace
```

Verify models endpoint:

```
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
```

This succeeds and returns `deepseek-v4-flash`.

### 5. Run API generation

```
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/chat/completions \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -d '{

    "model":"deepseek-chat",

    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one short sentence."}],

    "max_tokens":8,

    "temperature":0

  }'
```

## Expected Behavior

The model should generate a normal short assistant response, for example:

```
Hello, nice to meet you!
```

or any semantically valid natural-language completion.

## Actual Behavior

CLI output:

```
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>
```

CLI performance line:

```
ds4: prefill: 65.80 t/s, generation: 37.51 t/s
```

API response:

```
{

  "id": "chatcmpl-1",

  "object": "chat.completion",

  "model": "deepseek-chat",

  "choices": [

    {

      "index": 0,

      "message": {

        "role": "assistant",

        "content": "<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>"

      },

      "finish_reason": "length"

    }

  ],

  "usage": {

    "prompt_tokens": 11,

    "completion_tokens": 8,

    "total_tokens": 19

  }

}
```

## Notes

-   The model loads successfully.
-   Metal backend initialization succeeds.
-   Prefill runs through all 43 layers.
-   Server API works structurally.
-   The failure appears to be in inference correctness, logits, sampling, tokenizer mapping, or Q4 GGUF compatibility.
-   The symptom is deterministic with `--temp 0`: every generated token is BOS.

## Additional Context

The server process used for this test has been stopped after reproduction. Port `8001` is no longer listening.

Potential areas to inspect:

-   logits after first decode step
-   whether logits are all `-inf` except token `0`
-   sampler behavior under greedy decode
-   BOS / special-token handling

title: Don't kill the REPL on /ctx with invalid input
body:
## Summary

The `/ctx` command in the interactive REPL called `parse_int()`, which exits the process via `exit(2)` on bad input. That is correct for command-line argument parsing at startup, but in the REPL it kills the entire `ds4` process — dropping the KV cache and the conversation — on a typo like `/ctx abc`.

All other failure paths in the REPL already print and continue: `/ctx` with no argument, `/read` on a missing file, an unknown command. Only invalid `/ctx` numeric values exited.

This PR adds a `parse_int_repl()` twin of `parse_int()` that prints the same error and returns `false` instead, and switches the `/ctx` handler to use it. Behavior on every other path — including a valid `/ctx N` that fails inside `repl_chat_set_ctx()` — is unchanged from `main`.

## Test plan

- [x] `make` — clean build, no new warnings
- [x] Piped commands into `./ds4 -c 4096`:
  - `/ctx abc` → prints `ds4: invalid value for /ctx: abc`, REPL continues (previously: process exit)
  - `/ctx 4096` → still works, recreates the session
  - `/quit` → exits cleanly

## Note

There is a sibling PR — focused on a separate, independent failure mode (the chat losing its session when `repl_chat_set_ctx()` itself fails) — that I will open right after this one. It is intentionally split because it includes a behavioral change worth its own review.

title: Keep the chat session when /ctx fails to recreate it
body:
## Summary

`repl_chat_set_ctx()` freed the existing session before trying to create the replacement:

```c
static int repl_chat_set_ctx(ds4_engine *engine, repl_chat *chat, int ctx_size) {
    ds4_session_free(chat->session);
    chat->session = NULL;
    chat->ctx_size = 0;
    return repl_chat_create_session(engine, chat, ctx_size);
}
```

If the new session failed to allocate (e.g. asking for a context size the backend can't satisfy), the old session was already gone and `run_repl` had no choice but to break out of the loop, ending the chat.

This PR drops the redundant pre-free. `repl_chat_create_session()` already has the safe ordering — it tries to create first and only frees the old session on success — so removing the pre-free restores that protection. The `/ctx` handler is updated to print a warning and keep the current context on failure rather than exiting the REPL.

## Heads up: behavioral change

This is not pure cleanup — it changes user-visible behavior:

- **Before**: `/ctx N` with a valid number that fails to allocate terminates the REPL.
- **After**: prints `ds4: /ctx N failed; keeping current ctx M` and stays at the prompt.

I think keeping the session is the friendlier default (matches every other REPL failure path), but this is a design call and I'm happy to drop the `run_repl` change if you'd rather keep the terminate-on-failure semantics. The `repl_chat_set_ctx()` cleanup still stands on its own — it's a real bug regardless of how the caller responds.

## Relation to #54

Independent of #54. Both touch the `/ctx` handler so they will textually conflict on whichever lands second; happy to rebase. The two PRs address different failure modes:

- #54 — `/ctx abc` (parse error)
- this PR — `/ctx N` where N is valid but creation fails (resource error)

## Test plan

- [x] `make` — clean build, no new warnings
- [x] Piped `/ctx 4096` then `/quit` into `./ds4 -c 4096`: session recreated successfully, exits cleanly. The failure path is hard to exercise reliably without injecting an allocation failure into `ds4_session_create()`; relying on inspection for that branch.

title: Fix session cache misses for thinking mode (no tools)
body:
Problem
-------
With `think=true` and `tool_context=false`, multi-turn conversations never get
KV cache hits. Every request re-prefills the entire context from scratch.

Root cause
----------
After generation, the checkpoint contains the full thinking output:

    <think>reasoning...</think>Answer

On the next turn, the template re-renders the conversation with reasoning
stripped (think_start → think_end with no content between them). The checkpoint
diverges at the think_start/think_end boundary, so `common_prefix()` returns a
position before all prior turns.

Note: with tools enabled this doesn't happen — BPE round-trip through
tool_context is lossless because reasoning is preserved in the template.

Fix
---
Add `canonicalize_thinking_checkpoint()`, called after generation when thinking
is active and tools are not. Mirrors the existing `canonicalize_tool_checkpoint()`
pattern: re-tokenize the expected next-turn representation and overwrite the
checkpoint suffix.

Before: ctx=0..407:407 (full re-prefill)
After:  ctx=397..407:10 (cache hit)

Includes unit tests (5 cases) and an integration test that verifies cache hits
via prefill span logging.

The original implementation used a fixed 672 MiB model-view overlap. The q4 GGUF has 1152 MiB expert tensors, so on this machine one tensor can straddle two mapped Metal views and fail startup with:

title: feat(loader): support stock-recipe (Q8_0/F32) abliterated GGUFs end-to-end on Metal
body:
## What this changes

DeepSeek-V4-Flash GGUFs produced by the upstream llama.cpp converter without
per-tensor type overrides ship most of the small projections at Q8_0 (and the
routed-expert router at F32) where the antirez recipe keeps them at F16.

Examples: the [cyberneurova/CyberNeurova-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-abliterated-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/cyberneurova/CyberNeurova-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-abliterated-GGUF)
models. On stock `ds4` main these load fails at the first F16-strict
validator (`token_embd`, then `output_hc_fn`, then `hc_attn_fn`, …), and even
after the validators are relaxed, several Metal kernel paths read weight bytes
directly via offset arithmetic that hard-codes F16/F32 strides and produce
silently wrong output for Q8_0.

This PR makes the embed / HC / compressor / indexer / router validators **and**
the corresponding Metal kernel paths polymorphic, so the same GGUF loads and
runs on Metal end-to-end on [audreyt/pi-ds4](https://github.com/audreyt/pi-ds4).

## Validators (`ds4.c`)

* New `tensor_expect_dispatch_layout` helper accepts F16, F32, or Q8_0 and is
  applied to every projection that flows through a type-dispatching
  matvec/matmul: `output_hc_fn`, `hc_attn_fn`, `hc_ffn_fn`,
  `attn_compressor_{ape,gate,kv}`, `indexer.{attn_q_b,proj}`,
  `indexer_compressor_{ape,gate,kv}`, `ffn_gate_inp`.
* `token_embd` keeps its own inline F16/Q8_0 check because its CPU embed
  kernel doesn't go through `matvec_any`.
* The two compressor decode-time guards (`attn_compressor` and
  `indexer_compressor` pair-projection paths) relaxed from "F16 only" to
  "F16 or Q8_0, paired type must match".

## CPU paths (`ds4.c`)

* Refactor `embed_token_f16` into an `embed_token` dispatcher; add
  `embed_token_q8_0` (block-wise dequant of `block_q8_0`).
* Replace the remaining direct `matvec_f16` / `matvec_f16_serial` callers
  (HC fn, `output_hc_fn`, `ffn_gate_inp`) with the existing `matvec_any`
  dispatcher; add `matvec_any_serial` for the HC pre/post path.
* Polymorphic Metal-side dispatch helpers `metal_graph_matmul_plain_tensor`
  and `metal_graph_matmul_pair_plain_tensor` (extended for Q8_0; the pair
  fuses with the existing F16-pair kernel when both tensors are F16,
  otherwise dispatches to two single matmuls). All 22 hardcoded
  `ds4_metal_matmul_f16{,_pair}_tensor` call sites in `ds4.c` (HC mix,
  attn/indexer compressors, indexer projections, output head, router)
  converted to use these wrappers.

## Metal kernels

* `metal/get_rows.metal`: `kernel_get_rows_q8_0` (one float per thread,
  dequantizes its source block on the fly).
* `metal/dense.metal`: `kernel_mul_mm_f32_f32` template instantiation for the
  multi-token F32 weight matmul that the F32 router path needs in prefill
  (mirrors the existing F16/Q8_0 `mul_mm_t` instantiations).
* `metal/dsv4_kv.metal`: a Q8_0 branch added to
  `kernel_dsv4_compressor_store_one`. Without this, the decode-time
  single-row compressor store treats Q8_0 ape as F32 and reads garbage.

## Metal wiring (`ds4_metal.m`)

* Register `g_get_rows_q8_0_pipeline` at init; clear at cleanup.
* Both `ds4_metal_embed_{token,tokens}_hc_tensor` and the shared
  `ds4_metal_encode_get_rows` helper take a new `weight_type` parameter
  (GGUF type code: 1=F16, 8=Q8_0). 8 callers in `ds4.c` forward
  `weights->token_embd->type` unchanged. `ds4_metal_embed_row_layout` picks
  the right per-row stride and pipeline.
* `ds4_metal_matmul_f32_tensor` extended with a multi-token branch that
  dispatches to `kernel_mul_mm_f32_f32` (`n_tok > 1`); existing `n_tok = 1`
  path unchanged.
* `ds4_metal_encode_compressor_score_with_ape` and the equivalent loop in
  `ds4_metal_compressor_store_batch_tensor`: for Q8_0 ape, dequantize on the
  CPU into a *per-call* private `MTLBuffer` and feed that into the existing
  `add_f32_1d`. Two new helpers (`ds4_metal_half_bits_to_float`,
  `ds4_metal_cpu_dequant_q8_0_rows`) implement the conversion; the CPU
  dequant matches `gguf-py`'s `dequantize` reference byte-for-byte (verified
  in a standalone numeric check). A per-call buffer is required because
  multiple CPU writes to the previously-shared
  `g_compressor_store_ape_buffer` within one command buffer collapse to the
  last write at execute time (Metal kernels run in encode order, but CPU
  writes don't participate in that ordering when the same scratch is
  reused). The per-call buffer is retained until cb completion via
  `addCompletedHandler` because Metal does not strongly retain buffers
  bound to encoders.
* Six `ape_type` validators relaxed to also accept `8` (Q8_0).
* Six `ape_bytes` calculations centralized through a new
  `ds4_metal_ape_bytes(ape_type, n_elems)` helper that returns the correct
  stride for F16 / F32 / Q8_0.
* `metal_graph_matmul_plain_tensor` extended with a Q8_0 branch.

## Why CPU dequant for Q8_0 ape (and not a Metal kernel)

I first wrote a `kernel_cpy_q8_0_f32` Metal kernel using the same
`block_q8_0` indexing pattern that the working dense Q8_0 matvec/matmul
kernels in `metal/dense.metal` use. It compiled cleanly but produced
silently wrong values for the actual compressor APE shapes (4 rows × 1024
cols of `block_q8_0`). I confirmed this by a side-by-side numeric check
against `gguf-py`'s `dequantize` reference: my CPU dequant matches
byte-for-byte; the Metal kernel does not. I left `kernel_cpy_q8_0_f32` in
`metal/cpy.metal` (its registration in `ds4_metal.m` is harmless) so that a
future debug session can pick it up; the compressor paths use the CPU
dequant as the active route.

## What this PR does not cover

* The CPU MoE path (`ds4.c:5198, 5291`) still hardcodes
  `if (gate_w->type != IQ2_XXS) ds4_die(...)`. That path is reference/debug
  per `AGENT.md` and the production Metal flow doesn't touch it. If
  something forces CPU fallback (Metal disabled, MTP without Metal, certain
  trace modes) on a stock-recipe Q8_0 GGUF you'll see "expected IQ2_XXS
  expert tensors" and need a Q8_0 dispatch added there too. Out of scope
  for this PR; the production Metal flow is fine.
* No quantization changes, no recipe changes, no new GGUF formats. This is
  a loader/dispatcher change so existing GGUFs that happen to use the
  stock recipe become loadable.

## Test matrix (macOS / M5/ Metal)

* `make ds4-server` clean (one pre-existing `-Wpointer-sign` warning from
  the unrelated MoE path, not introduced by this PR).
* Cyberneurova Q2_K GGUF entirely unmodified, default flags:
  21-token prompt → coherent generation
  ("An LLM, or Large Language Model, is a type of artificial intelligence").
  Without the compressor APE fix, this prompt generated a few coherent
  tokens then `<BOS>` token spam.
* Pre-harmonized variant (`token_embd` / HC / compressor / indexer all
  F16): still works byte-for-byte the same as before, no F16/F32 path
  regressions.
* `make ds4-server` build clean across both branches.

title: feat(server): support llama.cpp-style raw completions
body:
## Summary

This adds an opt-in `--raw-completions` mode for `ds4-server`.

When enabled, `POST /v1/completions` treats the request `prompt` as an already-rendered model prompt and continues it directly, instead of wrapping it in the built-in DS4 chat template. The default behavior is unchanged.

## Why

This aligns ds4 with llama.cpp-style raw completions for clients that own prompt rendering and expect the server to perform only continuation.

That unlocks prompt-template-owning clients, text-completion/instruct frontends, and raw prompt experiments that send model-specific templates directly.

## Notes

- `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/messages` are unchanged.
- Default `/v1/completions` behavior is unchanged unless `--raw-completions` is passed.
- In raw mode, thinking markers and other model control tokens should be included by the client as part of the rendered prompt.
- This branch was freshly ported onto current `origin/main` after the Responses API changes.

## Testing

- `make ds4-server ds4_test`
- `./ds4_test --server`
- `./ds4-server --help | rg -n "raw-completions|/v1/completions|responses"`

title: KV prefix cache may miss final response prefix in pi tool sessions
body:
### Summary

In a long tool-enabled `ds4-server` session driven by pi coding agent, KV reuse is high across consecutive tool-call turns. However, after the model eventually produces a normal assistant text response with `finish=stop`, the next short user message can fail to reuse the long conversation prefix and fall back to a much shorter disk KV entry, such as `4096` tokens.

This causes the next request to re-prefill tens of thousands of tokens even though the client only appended a short follow-up user message.

The affected transition appears to be:

```text
many tool-use turns -> final assistant text response (`finish=stop`) -> next short user message
```

Tool-call continuations themselves generally reuse the live checkpoint correctly.

### Environment

```text
Repository: antirez/ds4
Commit: 8e7575be0ef44bd97c5ebaccf49ef85e05048b7b

Machine: Mac Studio
Model Identifier: Mac15,14
Chip: Apple M3 Ultra
CPU cores: 32 total, 24 performance + 8 efficiency
Memory: 512 GB
macOS: 15.7.5
Kernel: Darwin 24.6.0 arm64

Model:
  ds4flash.gguf ->
  gguf/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Q4KExperts-F16HC-F16Compressor-F16Indexer-Q8Attn-Q8Shared-Q8Out-chat-v2.gguf

Model file size:
  164633502304 bytes

MTP:
  Not used in the server command below.

Client:
  pi coding agent
  @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.74.0
  pi --version: 0.74.0
  npm dist-tag latest: 0.74.0

API:
  OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with tools
```

### Server Command

```sh
./ds4-server \
  --ctx 100000 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --kv-disk-dir ./kv-cache \
  --kv-disk-space-mb 8192
```

Note: `./kv-cache` was not empty at server startup. However, the key observation below does not depend on old cache contents: immediately before the bad fallback, `ds4-server` stores a fresh long `reason=evict` checkpoint with `56639` tokens, then still only matches the older `4096`-token checkpoint for the incoming prompt.

### Expected Behavior

After a long tool-enabled session ends with a final assistant text response, the next short user message should reuse the long live prefix or a long disk KV prefix.

Expected log shape:

```text
chat ctx=<large_previous_prefix>..<large_previous_prefix + small_delta>:<small_delta> TOOLS prompt start
```

For example:

```text
chat ctx=56639..56678:39 TOOLS prompt start
```

or similar.

### Actual Behavior

After a final normal assistant text response, the next short user message falls back to a short disk KV prefix:

```text
kv cache hit tokens=4096 ...
chat ctx=4096..56678:52582 TOOLS prompt start
```

This results in a large unexpected prefill:

```text
chat ctx=4096..56678:52582 prompt done 131.349s
```

### Reproduction Shape

The original prompts contain private/local project details, so I am describing the reproduction shape rather than exact prompt text.

1. Start `ds4-server` with disk KV enabled using the command above.
2. Connect pi coding agent to `ds4-server` through the OpenAI-compatible chat completions API.
3. Send an initial broad project-analysis prompt that causes many tool-use turns.
4. Let the model perform multiple tool calls.
5. Let the model eventually produce a long normal assistant text response with `finish=stop`.
6. Send a short follow-up user message.
7. Observe that the next request may start from a short disk KV prefix such as `4096`, instead of the previous long conversation prefix.

### Relevant Logs

During the tool-use loop, live checkpoint reuse works well and tool checkpoints are canonicalized:

```text
0510 20:42:21 ds4-server: tool calls ctx=4096..4524:428 n=2 names=[bash,bash]
0510 20:42:22 ds4-server: tool checkpoint canonicalized ctx=4096..4524:428 common=4678 live=4678 canonical=4679
0510 20:42:22 ds4-server: chat ctx=4679..5798:1119 TOOLS prompt start

0510 20:42:33 ds4-server: tool calls ctx=4679..5798:1119 n=4 names=[read,read,read,read]
0510 20:42:33 ds4-server: tool checkpoint canonicalized ctx=4679..5798:1119 common=6003 live=6003 canonical=6004
0510 20:42:33 ds4-server: chat ctx=6004..13672:7668 TOOLS prompt start

0510 20:45:58 ds4-server: tool calls ctx=50121..53172:3051 n=2 names=[bash,bash]
0510 20:45:58 ds4-server: tool checkpoint canonicalized ctx=50121..53172:3051 common=53322 live=53322 canonical=53323
0510 20:45:58 ds4-server: chat ctx=53323..54437:1114 TOOLS prompt start
```

The final assistant response is a normal text response, not a tool call:

```text
0510 20:46:30 ds4-server: kv cache stored tokens=55087 trimmed=0 reason=continued size=746.13 MiB save=147.2 ms
...
0510 20:47:35 ds4-server: chat ctx=53323..54437:1114 gen=2202 TOOLS finish=stop 96.940s
```

After the next short user message, `ds4-server` first stores the previous live checkpoint as an evict checkpoint:

```text
0510 20:47:52 ds4-server: kv cache stored tokens=56639 trimmed=0 reason=evict size=766.51 MiB save=127.0 ms
```

But that freshly stored long checkpoint is still not usable for the incoming prompt. The next request falls back to the short 4096-token disk KV entry:

```text
0510 20:47:52 ds4-server: kv cache hit tokens=4096 quant=4 load=9.2 ms file=./kv-cache/9028727382e663d593b638a027ec1be847beb51b.kv
0510 20:47:52 ds4-server: chat ctx=4096..56678:52582 TOOLS prompt start
```

This causes a long prefill:

```text
0510 20:47:52 ds4-server: chat ctx=4096..56678:52582 TOOLS prefill chunk 4096/56678 (7.2%) chunk=0.00 t/s avg=0.00 t/s 0.000s
...
0510 20:50:04 ds4-server: chat ctx=4096..56678:52582 TOOLS prefill chunk 56678/56678 (100.0%) chunk=271.32 t/s avg=400.33 t/s 131.347s
0510 20:50:04 ds4-server: chat ctx=4096..56678:52582 TOOLS prompt done 131.349s
```

The important observation is that the server did save a fresh long `reason=evict` KV checkpoint immediately before the fallback, but the incoming prompt still only matched the 4096-token checkpoint.

Full raw `ds4-server` logs with user prompt text redacted can be provided if useful.

### Hypothesis

The tool-call path canonicalizes the checkpoint after `finish=tool_calls`, so tool-result continuations usually match the live token prefix.

After a normal assistant text response (`finish=stop`) in a tool-enabled chat, the live checkpoint may contain the exact sampled token sequence produced by the model. On the next request, pi coding agent sends the assistant text back as message history, and `ds4-server` re-renders and re-tokenizes the conversation.

The rendered text may be semantically identical, but its token IDs may not be identical to the sampled live token sequence.

Since both live checkpoint matching and disk KV lookup are based on exact token IDs, not text equivalence, the next request can fail to match the long prior prefix and fall back to an older short disk KV entry.

In short:

```text
sampled assistant output token IDs
!=
tokenize(render(history containing that assistant output))
```

This would explain why consecutive tool-call turns reuse the cache well, while the next user turn after a final long text response can miss badly.

### Notes

This issue is not proposing a specific fix yet. The design space likely has tradeoffs:

- canonicalizing final assistant text checkpoints after `finish=stop`
- saving safer disk KV frontiers around stable prompt/tool boundaries
- improving trace diagnostics for token-prefix divergence after final assistant messages
- adding a lower-cost way to preserve graph frontiers for canonical rewrites

A naive synchronous fix could move the cost from the next request to the end of the current response, so the right solution likely needs careful design.

title: Speculative Decoding via "Draft KV Stitching"
body:
## Description
The current MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) path is experimental and provides "at most a slight speedup." We can improve this by implementing Draft KV Stitching.

## Proposed Changes
* **Small Draft Model Integration:** Allow the engine to load a tiny (e.g., DeepSeek 1.3B) model purely for drafting.

* **KV Alignment:** Ensure that when a draft is accepted, the "compressed KV" of the main model is updated without a full re-prefill.

title: Q4KExperts GGUF produces NaNs from layer 0 on Metal; Q2 works
body:
### Summary

I am testing `ds4` with the DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF files from:

- Repo: `antirez/deepseek-v4-gguf`
- Q2 file: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2.gguf`
- Q4 file: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Q4KExperts-F16HC-F16Compressor-F16Indexer-Q8Attn-Q8Shared-Q8Out-chat-v2.gguf`

The Q2 model works correctly, but the Q4 model loads and runs while producing invalid activations/logits. Generation degenerates to repeated BOS tokens:

```text
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>...
```

With `--dump-logprobs`, Q4 has no finite top logprobs, while Q2 has normal finite logits.

### Important note: downloaded file size appears correct

I initially suspected a corrupted or incomplete Q4 download, but the file size looks correct when accounting for GB vs GiB units.

I added temporary diagnostics guarded by an env var:

```

DS4_METAL_GRAPH_FINITE_LAYER=0
```

Then ran Q4:
