title: add Specprefill support for DS4F
server: fix prompt-cache miss on whitespace-only thinking channels
body:
## Summary

Fixes a prompt-cache miss that hit **every turn** of a DeepSeek thinking-mode conversation when the assistant produced an empty reasoning channel.

## Root cause

Thinking-mode clients pad an empty reasoning channel with a single space so the echoed `reasoning_content` isn't rejected as an empty string. On the next request the conversation is re-rendered as:

```
 thinking<space> response
```

but the model actually samples the opening tag immediately followed by the closing tag, with **no space** between them. That extra space token desyncs the byte-prefix match, so the live KV prefix is invalidated and the server falls back to a full re-prefill on every turn.

## Fix

Render a whitespace-only thinking channel back as empty, so the reconstituted prompt matches the clean `thinking response` boundary the live KV was sampled from. Added a regression test (`test_thinking_whitespace_renders_empty`).

Also dropped the verbose `--trace` cache-miss diagnostics block: the trace files it produced weren't enough to diagnose these misses, and the live server warning already reports the relevant numbers.

## Testing

- `make ds4-server` builds clean.
- Server unit-test suite passes (incl. the new regression test): `ds4-server tests: ok`.

title: server: native Prometheus GET /metrics endpoint
body:
## Summary

`ds4-server` now answers HTTP `GET /metrics` with Prometheus text exposition format, so a Prometheus server (or any compatible scraper) can collect request, token, and key-value cache statistics directly from the process. Until now the only way to get these series out was to parse the server's log output with a sidecar exporter; a native endpoint removes that moving part and works identically on every platform the server builds on.

The endpoint is read-only, needs no new dependencies, and is entirely opt-in: unless something requests `/metrics`, the only cost is the counter updates on the server's existing accounting paths.

## Exported series

Requests and latency:

- `ds4_requests_total` — completed requests, by endpoint and status.
- `ds4_active_requests` — requests currently being served.
- `ds4_request_duration_seconds` — end-to-end request latency histogram.
- `ds4_prompt_duration_seconds` — prompt-evaluation (prefill) latency histogram.

Tokens and throughput:

- `ds4_prompt_tokens_total` — prompt tokens evaluated, counted per prefill chunk rather than per prompt, so scrape intervals shorter than a long prefill still see accurate rates.
- `ds4_generated_tokens_total` — generated tokens, by phase.
- `ds4_prefill_tps` / `ds4_decode_tps` — instantaneous prefill and decode rates, tokens per second.
- `ds4_context_tokens` / `ds4_context_limit_tokens` — context occupancy and configured limit per session.

Key-value cache (disk store and reuse):

- `ds4_kv_cache_hit_total` / `ds4_kv_cache_miss_total` — cache hits by source (live key-value reuse or the on-disk store) versus misses.
- `ds4_kv_cache_stored_total` / `ds4_kv_cache_stored_bytes_total` — entries and bytes written to the store.
- `ds4_kv_cache_trimmed_tokens_total` — tokens evicted by trimming.
- `ds4_reused_tokens_total` — prompt tokens served from reuse instead of re-evaluation.

Example exposition (truncated):

```
# HELP ds4_prompt_tokens_total Prompt tokens evaluated by prefill
# TYPE ds4_prompt_tokens_total counter
ds4_prompt_tokens_total 86
# HELP ds4_generated_tokens_total Tokens generated, by phase
# TYPE ds4_generated_tokens_total counter
ds4_generated_tokens_total{phase="decode"} 200
```

## Implementation

Three commits:

1. The endpoint itself: text format rendering and routing in `ds4_server.c`.
2. Additional accounting: cache hits split by source, a reused-token counter, and the latency histograms; the key-value store reports hit sources through a small callback (`ds4_kvstore_set_metrics_fn`) so the store code stays free of server types.
3. Prompt-token counting moved from per-prompt to per-chunk accounting, which keeps rate queries correct while a long prefill is still in flight.

No new build flags, no new command-line options, and no changes to any existing behavior when the endpoint is not requested.

## Verification

- Warning-free builds on macOS (Darwin, default `make ds4-server`) and on ROCm (gfx1151, `make strix-halo`).
- The same three commits have been running on our production branch (two-machine ROCm pair, DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP4) with Prometheus scraping the endpoint; series names above are copied from live output.

title: ROCm backend on discrete gfx1100 (RX 7900 XTX) — has anyone tried it?
body:
Hi, first off — great project, the asymmetric quantization approach for V4 Flash is really clever.

I'm looking into running the ROCm backend on a discrete AMD GPU (Radeon RX 7900 XTX, gfx1100 / RDNA3) instead of a Strix Halo APU (gfx1151 / RDNA3.5). Before spending time on it I wanted to check whether anyone has already tried this, since all the ROCm documentation and code I could find (STRIXHALO.md, the `rocm_tier_valid` single-GPU check, `ds4_gpu_args_probe_auto_cuda`) seems to target Strix Halo specifically.

**Full disclosure up front: I'm an engineer with a strong background in math and a real passion for programming, but not a professional software developer. I've been using AI assistance (Claude) to help me read through the codebase and put this analysis together, and I'll be using AI assistance for the implementation work too if this turns out to be feasible. I'm saying this openly because I want any feedback to account for that — I'm approaching this as a serious, hands-on hobbyist project, not pretending to have more systems/GPU programming experience than I do.**

A few things I've dug into on my own, posting in case they're useful context:

1. **Compute kernels**: `ds4_rocm.cu` uses `__dp4a` via the `amd_mixed_dot` builtin, which maps to `v_dot4_i32_i8` on "gfx11-class" AMD GPUs generally, not something gfx1151-specific as far as I can tell. From what I could find on RDNA3 vs RDNA3.5 ISA differences, the two share the same core dot-product/matrix instruction set the notable differences (scalar FP ops, VGPR file size, texture/interpolation rates) don't seem to touch the kernels this project uses. gfx1100 actually has the same large 192KB VGPR file as gfx1151, unlike the smaller gfx1150.

2. **Memory model**: this looks like the real difference. Strix Halo is unified memory (GPUVM/GTT mapping system RAM as GPU-visible), which is why STRIXHALO.md needs the `amdgpu.gttsize` kernel param trick. A discrete GPU has real dedicated VRAM instead. Looking at `ds4_rocm_compat.cu`, `ds4_gpu_tensor_alloc_on` for ROCm is a direct `hipMalloc` with no offload/spill path  which would be fine for whatever fits in 24GB, but there's no RAM/SSD spillover mechanism for ROCm the way Strix Halo has via GTT, or CUDA has via managed memory. Is that assessment right, or is there something I'm missing?

3. **Single GPU limitation**: `rocm_tier_valid()` and the `ds4_gpu_args_probe_auto_cuda` error message ("ROCm supports one GPU per process") both hardcode single-GPU. That's fine for my use case (I'd run two separate `ds4` processes  (one CUDA, one ROCm) using `--role coordinator`/`--role worker` and `ds4_distributed.c` over localhost TCP to combine VRAM across an NVIDIA card and the XTX). Just flagging in case that's a relevant detail for anyone else with mixed-vendor setups.

**Questions:**
- Has anyone actually run `make strix-halo` with `ROCM_ARCH=gfx1100` (or similar) on a discrete RDNA3 card? Any reports, even partial/broken ones, would save me some time.
- Is the memory-model gap (no offload path for ROCm on cards where the full model doesn't fit in VRAM) accurate, or is there something in the pipeline I haven't found?
- Any known gfx1100-specific issues with rocWMMA or the attention/MoE kernels that wouldn't show up on gfx1151?

Happy to test on my end (RX 7900 XTX 24GB + RTX 4080 Super 16GB, Ubuntu) and report back either way — I can test the ROCm backend standalone on the XTX, the CUDA backend standalone on the 4080S, and eventually the two-process distributed setup across both.

title: ROCm/gfx1151: `--metal-kernels` fails 6 assertions in the paired Q8_0 decode case
body:
## Summary

On a Strix Halo (gfx1151) ROCm-only host, `make test-rocm` at `c1d4597` reports
`ds4 tests: 6 failure(s)`. All six are inside `--metal-kernels`, in
`test_metal_q8_0_decode_pair_exact_case`. They are **two independent problems**:

1. **`-ffast-math` breaks the bit-exactness assertion.** The project's default
   `CFLAGS` include `-ffast-math`, and `test-rocm` inherits them. Rebuilding the
   same test without `-ffast-math` makes the paired kernel bit-identical to the
   two standalone dispatches, exactly as the test intends.
2. **`hipMemcpy` H2D fails with `invalid argument`** for the second weight
   range, which makes `ds4_gpu_matmul_q8_0_tensor()` return 0 and leaves the
   comparison running on uninitialised output. This one is *not* explained by
   fast-math and I could not reproduce it standalone.

This is **not a regression from the recent ROCm MXFP4 work** — control below.

## Environment

```
GPU     AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 128 GB unified
OS      Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-30-generic
HIP     7.14.60850-0000000
cc      gcc 15.2.0
ds4     c1d4597, built with `make strix-halo` (--offload-arch=gfx1151)
model   DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731
```

## Reproduce

```sh
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm/core-7.14/lib
make strix-halo
make test-rocm            # or, much cheaper, just the failing case:
./ds4_test --metal-kernels
```

## Output

```
metal-kernels:
ds4-test: paired Q8_0 exactness mismatches=57/77 max_abs=1.90735e-06, 14/19 max_abs=9.53674e-07
tests/ds4_test.c:807: assertion failed: mismatch0 == 0
tests/ds4_test.c:808: assertion failed: mismatch1 == 0
ds4: ROCm model range copy failed for q8_0 at 0.00/0.32 MiB: invalid argument
tests/ds4_test.c:774: assertion failed: ds4_gpu_matmul_q8_0_tensor(ref1, weights_raw, weight_alloc, weight1_offset, in_dim, out1_dim, x, 1) != 0
ds4: ROCm model range copy failed for q8_0_pair1 at 0.00/0.32 MiB: invalid argument
tests/ds4_test.c:777: assertion failed: ds4_gpu_matmul_q8_0_pair_tensor(pair0, pair1, weights_raw, weight_alloc, 0, weight1_offset, in_dim, out0_dim, out1_dim, x, 1) != 0
ds4-test: paired Q8_0 exactness mismatches=19/19 max_abs=20.6578, 71/77 max_abs=3203.74
tests/ds4_test.c:807: assertion failed: mismatch0 == 0
tests/ds4_test.c:808: assertion failed: mismatch1 == 0
metal-kernels: ERR
```

The `max_abs=20.6578 / 3203.74` line is downstream of the two failed copies —
`ref1` and `pair1` were never written — so it is one bug, not two.

---

## Part 1 — `-ffast-math` vs the bit-exactness assertion

The assertion is a `memcmp` on floats, i.e. strictly bitwise:

```c
if (memcmp(&ref0_host[i], &pair0_host[i], sizeof(float)) != 0) mismatch0++;
```

Rebuilding **the same test at the same commit** with `-ffast-math` removed from
both `CFLAGS` and `ROCM_CFLAGS`:

| build | case `out0=77,out1=19` |
|---|---|
| default flags (`-ffast-math`) | `mismatches=57/77 max_abs=1.90735e-06, 14/19 max_abs=9.53674e-07` |
| same tree, no `-ffast-math` | **no mismatch line — assertion passes** |

So the paired kernel *is* bit-identical to two standalone dispatches; the
divergence is reassociation in the fast-math build.

`test-rocm` passes the project default `CFLAGS` straight through:

```make
test-rocm:
	$(MAKE) -B ds4_test ... CFLAGS="$(CFLAGS) $(ROCM_HOST_CFLAGS) -DDS4_ROCM_BUILD" ...
```

and `CFLAGS` contains `-ffast-math`. The Makefile already does
`$(filter-out -ffast-math,$(QUALITY_CFLAGS))` for `q4k-dot-test` /
`mxfp4-dot-test`, so the pattern exists — it just does not reach `ds4_test.o`
or the ROCm device objects.

I did not isolate host vs device: I removed `-ffast-math` from both at once.

## Part 2 — `hipMemcpy` H2D returns `invalid argument`

Call site, `cuda_model_range_acquire()` in `ds4_cuda.cu`:

```c
err = cudaMalloc(&dev, (size_t)bytes);                       /* succeeds */
const char *src = (const char *)model_map + offset;
err = cudaMemcpy((char *)dev + done, src + done, (size_t)n,
                 cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);                    /* invalid argument */
```

Parameters, derived from the failing case
(`test_metal_q8_0_decode_pair_exact_case(out0_dim=19, out1_dim=77)`):

```
in_dim       = 4096
row_bytes    = (4096/32)*34            = 4352
weight1_off  = round_up(19*4352, 4096) = 86016
weight1_len  = 77*4352                 = 335104   (= 0.32 MiB, matches the message)
weight_alloc = round_up(86016+335104, 4096)       (so the range is in bounds)
```

Note it is the **second** range that fails; the range at offset 0 is fine, and
the mirrored case (`out0=77, out1=19`, a 0.08 MiB second range) does not fail.

### What I ruled out

- **Offset / size / alignment.** A standalone HIP program doing exactly
  `hipMalloc(335104)` + `hipMemcpy(dev, base+86016, 335104, H2D)` from a
  page-aligned `posix_memalign` buffer succeeds. Reproducer attached below.
- **Memory pressure.** Same program with 40, 80 and **95 GiB** of `hipMalloc`
  ballast resident: still `no error` in every case. The real failure happens
  with ~80 GiB of model resident, so this was the obvious suspect and it is out.
- **Stale range cache.** `ds4_gpu_set_model_map()` calls
  `cuda_model_range_release_all()` when the base pointer changes, which clears
  `g_model_range_by_offset`, so a stale entry from a previous case is not it.
- **`hipHostRegister` capability.** `DS4_CUDA_WEIGHT_CACHE_VERBOSE=1` prints no
  `mapped ... MiB` line, so the mapped path is never taken and every range goes
  through `hipMalloc` + `hipMemcpy`. But standalone,
  `hipHostRegister(Mapped|ReadOnly)` and `hipHostGetDevicePointer` both succeed
  on this GPU — so the capability is there and something sets
  `g_model_range_mapping_supported = 0` earlier (that branch swallows the
  error, which is also why there is nothing in the log to point at).

I could not get past this without knowing the intended lifetime of the model
map here, so I have stopped and am reporting what is pinned down.

## Control — this is not from the MXFP4 series

`make test-rocm` is new (#526 / `7891f27`), so this is the first time these
assertions could run on a ROCm-only host at all. To check whether the ROCm
MXFP4 kernels caused it:

- `tests/ds4_test.c` is **byte-identical** between `84cc882` and `c1d4597`
  (`git diff --quiet` confirms).
- The only `ds4_rocm.cu` change in that range is +14 lines from `39a8f18`: a
  `cuda_block_mxfp4` struct, a `static_assert`, and a `__constant__` lookup
  table. Nothing on the Q8_0 path.
- Decisive: I built the **current** test harness and linked the **old**
  `ds4_rocm.o` from `84cc882`. Byte-identical failures — same counts
  (`57/77`, `14/19`, `19/19`, `71/77`) and same `max_abs`
  (`1.90735e-06`, `9.53674e-07`, `20.6578`, `3203.74`).

Also worth noting for anyone comparing: #526 reports
`./ds4_test --metal-kernels` → `metal-kernels: OK` on the same GPU on
2026-07-09, but `427e281` (2026-07-18) added this case afterwards. So there is
no contradiction — the case has simply never passed here.

## Attached reproducer

```cpp
// hipcc -O2 --offload-arch=gfx1151 -o repro repro.hip.cpp
// ./repro        -> both cases "no error"
// ./repro 95     -> 95 GiB ballast first, still "no error"
#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <vector>

static int try_copy(const char *tag, const void *host_base,
                    unsigned long long off, unsigned long long len) {
    void *dev = nullptr;
    hipError_t e = hipMalloc(&dev, (size_t)len);
    if (e != hipSuccess) { printf("  %-18s hipMalloc -> %s\n", tag, hipGetErrorString(e)); return 1; }
    e = hipMemcpy(dev, (const char *)host_base + off, (size_t)len, hipMemcpyHostToDevice);
    printf("  %-18s off=%-8llu len=%-8llu -> %s\n", tag, off, len, hipGetErrorString(e));
    hipFree(dev);
    return e != hipSuccess;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    const unsigned long long page = 4096, row_bytes = (4096ull / 32ull) * 34ull;
    std::vector<void *> ballast;
    if (argc > 1) {
        const size_t chunk = 1ull << 30;
        for (int i = 0, n = atoi(argv[1]); i < n; i++) {
            void *p = nullptr;
            if (hipMalloc(&p, chunk) != hipSuccess) break;
            hipMemset(p, 0, chunk);
            ballast.push_back(p);
        }
        printf("  ballast: %zu GiB\n", ballast.size());
    }
    int fails = 0;
    const unsigned int dims[2][2] = {{77, 19}, {19, 77}};
    const char *tags[2] = {"case A (out1=19)", "case B (out1=77)"};
    for (int c = 0; c < 2; c++) {
        unsigned long long w0 = dims[c][0] * row_bytes;
        unsigned long long off = ((w0 + page - 1) / page) * page;
        unsigned long long len = dims[c][1] * row_bytes;
        unsigned long long alloc = ((off + len + page - 1) / page) * page;
        void *base = nullptr;
        if (posix_memalign(&base, (size_t)page, (size_t)alloc)) return 2;
        memset(base, 0x5a, (size_t)alloc);
        fails += try_copy(tags[c], base, off, len);
        free(base);
    }
    for (void *p : ballast) hipFree(p);
    printf("  failures: %d\n", fails);
    return fails != 0;
}
```

Output on this machine:

```
  case A (out1=19)   off=335872   len=82688    -> no error
  case B (out1=77)   off=86016    len=335104   -> no error
  ballast: 95 GiB
  case A (out1=19)   off=335872   len=82688    -> no error
  case B (out1=77)   off=86016    len=335104   -> no error
  failures: 0
```

## Suggested next steps

- For Part 1: filter `-ffast-math` out of the objects that back exactness
  assertions, the way `q4k-dot-test` / `mxfp4-dot-test` already do — or relax
  the assertion to a tolerance and say so.
- For Part 2: the `else` branch in `cuda_model_range_acquire()` that sets
  `g_model_range_mapping_supported = 0` swallows the `hipHostRegister` error.
  Printing it under `DS4_CUDA_WEIGHT_CACHE_VERBOSE` would probably show why the
  mapped path is abandoned on this host, which is likely upstream of the copy
  failure. Happy to run any instrumented build on this hardware.

Related: #526 (rocm-test target), #525 (GPU kernel tests on ROCm), #16 (Strix
Halo discussion).

title: Consolidate ROCm exactness, distributed v3, DSpark speculation, and NHI tensor parallelism for Strix Halo
body:
## What this does

This is the **single consolidated PR** for the Strix Halo ROCm/distributed work: the exact-kernel and protocol-v3 groundwork, distributed DSpark speculation, the complete **two-node tensor parallelism over Thunderbolt/USB4 NHI** implementation, and the start of **multi-session batched serving** for the layer-split pipeline deployment.

**Rebased onto** antirez/ds4 `main` @ `9139e2a` (Qwen3.8 Flash Next, CUDA SSD, n-gram packaging). Branch head **`5d3801b`** = the 18-commit rebase + one new commit `server: allow configuring exclusive prefill quantum`. Conflicts resolved as unions in `.gitignore`, `Makefile`, `ds4.c`, `ds4.h`, `ds4_kvstore.h`; range-diff 18=18, no extra commits. Validation: Mac Metal clean build 0 warnings + full model-free `make test` set green; gfx1151 Strix Halo pair `make strix-halo -j8` 0 warnings, both nodes byte-identical; `test-mxfp4-rocm`, `test-rocm-qkv-fusion`, `test-q8-krow-rocm`, `test-tp-combine-rocm`, `test-graph-deferred-dump-rocm` pass. ROCm/CUDA/NHI/perf changes since the last banner: new `--prefill-quantum N` flag (exclusive-prefill slice, default 2048) — production now runs `--prefill-quantum 8192` so the `--dist-prefill-window 3` pipeline stays full; measured single-client cold ~16k prefill 188.7 → 238.3 tok/s (+26%) on the pair. Decode unchanged (~15 tok/s; speculative-decode A/B showed MTP/DSpark provide no gain as shipped). Production redeployed (MXFP4, `--batched-session 2`, kv-disk) with the flag. `make test-rocm` still exits nonzero solely on the Linux-generic upstream `tests/test_tp_tcp` failure (abort/hang, not ROCm-specific; reported upstream).

Extra Metal validation also found a pre-existing header issue: this branch's inline non-ROCm helpers use `NULL`, but `ds4_gpu.h` did not include `<stddef.h>`. The one-line include fix is folded into the introducing commit (3), and standalone header compilation passes at every commit. Previous rebase decisions remain: `DS4_SPEC_PREFIX_SLOTS=5` on all backends, upstream's `block_start` alongside `can_mtp_spec`, and the reset-site guard variant for the CPU test-hook ROCm build. For reviewability the branch retains **8 thematic commits** plus the follow-ups listed after them:

1. `server: Prometheus metrics endpoint and prefill-rate accounting`
2. `rocm: exact-rows decode tiers, QKV norm+RoPE fusion, MXFP4 span exactness`
3. `distributed: descriptor-framed protocol-v3 transport with TCP and NHI backends`
4. `rocm: NHI tensor-parallel gates — combine kernels, transport core, engine wiring`
5. `dist: DSpark pipeline speculative decoding with exact-span verification`
6. `rocm + server: tensor-parallel lifecycle, batched TP prefill, NHI pipelining`
7. `dist server: multi-session batched decode spans (L0+L1)`
8. `rocm: add decode-kernel bandwidth POC bench (verdict: at the DRAM wall)`
9. `docs: persistent TP gate kernel POC — negative result, code kept as a patch` (docs + harness only, see below)
10. `build/test: rebase onto f4d03f6 — ROCm build vs upstream Metal TP, CPU test-hook stubs, ROCm test links`
11. `tp: accept GLM MTP and multimodal sync frames in the command size allow-list` (fix found by upstream's new `tests/test_tp_commands.c`, see the rebase note below)
12. `server: ds4_active_requests counts inference jobs, not open connections` (the gauge counted every open socket, including the Prometheus scrape itself)
13. `server: batched dispatch prefers an empty slot over evicting a conversation`
14. `deepseek: live-prefix rewind — restore the KV frontier instead of rebuilding` (new; see "Live-prefix rewind" below)
15. `server: hold a resend for its draining home slot instead of rebuilding elsewhere`
16. `server: metrics for rewind refusals, capture skips, dispatch holds, reuse by source` (`ds4_rewind_refused_total{reason}`, `ds4_rewind_capture_skipped_total{reason}`, `ds4_dispatch_held_total`, `ds4_reused_tokens_by_source_total{source}` — the first two stay at zero on a healthy pipeline). Its unit test also caught a GCC 15.2 `-O2/-O3` IPA-CP miscompile on the ROCm build (a `uint64_t` parameter fed by `(uint64_t)int` at one call site and constant `0` at the others had its low 32 bits folded to zero; `-fno-ipa-cp` made it pass) — the helper now returns the table entry instead of taking the value as a parameter, with a comment so it is not reintroduced.
17. `server: score a continuation of the slot's own conversation as full reuse` (with thinking on, the raw common prefix stops at the previous prompt boundary and the hidden reasoning looked like loss, so a reasoning-heavy turn could migrate its conversation to the other slot and back; found by the Terminal-Bench run below)

Commit 10 carries the build/test glue: `DS4_NO_GPU` fallbacks so the CPU test-hooks build links, a `ROCM_TEST_LINK_OBJS` list for the standalone ROCm tests (complementing upstream's `ade4d62`, which fixed its own standalone tests and the Metal-only TP hook calls this commit used to guard), the new upstream CPU tests linked with the ROCm objects they now need, the reset-site guard variant for the CPU test-hook ROCm build (upstream's `49ec955` already carries the original `g_glm_rocm_guard_available_baseline` fix that was needed on `f4d03f6`), two stale test anchors, and a repaired `clean` target (its main `rm -f` line had absorbed neighbouring rule text during the previous rebase and deleted sources — fixed at the commits that introduced it, so no commit on the branch has the bad recipe). NHI handshake frames are 22/23 (upstream took 19/20 for `RDMA_WARM/POSTED` and 21 for `GLM_MTP`).

The main pieces are:

- **ROCm exactness/performance groundwork:** fused QKV normalization + RoPE, exact Q8 k-row kernels, MXFP4 small-batch dispatch, the guarded Q8→F16 expanded-weight cache path, and a tiny-batch direct Q8 verify kernel.
- **Versioned distributed transport:** negotiated protocol v3 with descriptor-framed TCP and opt-in NHI backends, bounded payloads/generations/sequences, lifecycle hardening, and legacy-v2 compatibility.
- **Tensor parallelism over NHI:** ROCm TP gate engine (in-band stamp spin-detect combine kernels, strict in-order NHI slot acquire/submit/consume, signal-aware shutdown); **pipelined big-gate exchange** (TX/RX phase split with ring-capacity windowing; the previously serialized ~34 ms/layer FFN all-reduce at 256-token chunks now costs ~2 ms/layer); TP attention row-split kernels for all three prefill attention shapes; MXFP4 expert-ownership kernels; `ds4-server` owns the same TP parser and lifecycle as the CLI.
- **Measured defaults so users do not guess:** ROCm TP defaults to a 512-row prefill chunk (ladder below). The server warns at startup when the thunderbolt_stream module cannot prove zerocopy series ≥ 18.
- **Multi-session batched serving (L0+L1, new):** `--batched-session N` coordinator slots share one worker registry; **L1 row-batched decode spans** carry one token per session in a single WORK over the shared link (batched embed + QKV + shared gate/up, per-row session planes), negotiated via a new protocol-v3 capability (`MULTI_SESSION_V1`) that fails closed. The single-session path is unchanged and remains the production default.
- **Server/build/test support:** native Prometheus `/metrics`, protocol/static suites, ROCm test/benchmark targets, and a bench-only decode-kernel bandwidth POC harness.
- **Live-prefix rewind for DeepSeek (new, commit 14):** an identical resend, a cancel-then-resend, or a regenerate no longer re-prefills the whole prompt. Details below.
- **Batched-serving dispatch fixes (commits 13, 15):** a new conversation prefers an empty slot over evicting one that shares only the chat-template preamble (score = reuse − loss instead of longest common prefix), and a resend that arrives while its own slot is still finishing a cancelled request waits for that slot instead of rebuilding on — and evicting — another.

No model files, kernel module, or machine-specific validation artifacts are part of the PR. The companion kernel-module work lives in the strix-rdma repo.

## Live-prefix rewind (DeepSeek, commit 14)

`ds4_session_rewind` was GLM-only: DeepSeek's ratio-4 pooled compressors cannot be rolled back by truncating their row counts, so a prompt that is a strict prefix of the live checkpoint (client retry, cancel-then-resend, regenerate) logged `token-mismatch` and rebuilt the prefix — 52 s for a 10k-token prompt on the pair, with the slot already holding exactly those positions.

The fix builds on the DSpark frontier primitive that already existed on both the coordinator and the worker. After a request's prefill, the slot is synced to `prompt_len-1` and a **rewind frontier** is captured there: copies of the compressor carry rings (attention + indexer), the 128-row raw SWA ring, and the per-layer row counters (≈24 MB per slot). A later strict-prefix request restores it, truncates the timeline to `prompt_len-1`, re-evaluates the final prompt token and decodes — the same branch GLM already used (`cached = prompt_len-1`, `cache_source = "memory-rewind"`). Frontiers are bound to the token prefix they were captured for (hash verified on restore) and dropped on session invalidation or a disk-snapshot load, so a rebuilt or restored conversation can never inherit a stale one. GLM/CPU paths are untouched (the new code is dead for them).

Over the distributed route the worker's slice has to rewind too. Two WORK flags ride the ordinary single-session span, the way `F_SPEC_ROLLBACK` rides a re-eval span: `F_REWIND_CAPTURE` (snapshot at `pos0` before evaluating) and `F_REWIND` (restore the frontier captured at `pos0`, truncate, recompute the prefix hash, evaluate). They are gated by a new capability, `DS4_DIST_V3_CAP_REWIND_V1` (0x20): advertised by new peers, selected only when both offer it, refused by the caps validator otherwise, never combined with speculative/multi-session/reset spans, single-worker routes only. A worker that cannot honor `F_REWIND` returns a work error and the coordinator's existing transcript replay rebuilds — refusal degrades to today's behavior, never to a client-visible error. `ds4_session_rewind_reason()` surfaces refusals in the server log.

Measured on the pipeline pair (temperature 0, think off; fresh vs resend vs second resend **token-identical** in every case):

| prompt | fresh | identical resend | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1.2k–1.6k tokens, all four `len%4` residues, 200-token decode | 22–24 s | 13.6–14.1 s | `cached = prompt-1`; decode crosses the 128-row raw window |
| 8.5k tokens, all four residues | 59–60 s | 14.6–15.5 s | |
| 3.3k tokens, **cancel mid-decode** (socket closed after 82 tokens) → resend | 27.6 s | 8.9 s | rewinds from the cancelled position |
| regenerate the last turn of a multi-turn conversation | — | 2.9 s | `cached = prompt-1` |

Multi-session: each `--batched-session` slot rewinds its own conversation. Fresh requests also got faster on the pair (30.8 → 22.3 s for 1.3k tokens) because two silent fallbacks found during validation are fixed in the same commit: the v3 negotiation allow-list dropped the new capability bit, and the worker's frame-mask check rejected the flags (both made the coordinator quietly replay the transcript). `tests/test_dist_v3` gains caps-gate and negotiation cases (148 → 169 checks). The model-backed exactness test is registered as `ds4_test --frontier-rewind-exactness`; the API-level exactness above is what was run on the pair (the pair's model does not fit one node, so the single-node test cannot run there).

## Compatibility and release posture

- Legacy-v2 framing remains available; v3 capability negotiation fails closed (including the new multi-session capability).
- NHI remains opt-in and inert without the out-of-tree tbstream module/device.
- Speculative decode remains **default-off**; this PR makes no end-to-end speculation speedup claim.
- Batched sessions are opt-in (`--batched-session N`); single-token spans are byte-identical to the serial path.
- Rewind is automatic for DeepSeek GPU sessions and needs no flag; across a distributed link it is negotiated (`CAP_REWIND_V1`) and fails closed with older peers. Dashboards: `ds4_active_requests` now counts inference requests only (queued or generating) instead of open connections, and `ds4_kv_cache_hit_total` gains `source="memory-rewind"`; commit 16 adds the four counters above so a refused rewind (which otherwise falls back silently to the disk cache or a rebuild) is visible on a dashboard.
- TP protocol frames renumbered above upstream's `SYNC_MULTIMODAL` (`NHI_READY=22`, `NHI_CLOSED=23`); protocol version tracks upstream (9).

## Validation — September 11 rebase (`0bafad0` on `6289c51`)

- Clean macOS/Metal build of all five executables: 0 warnings. Server and agent unit tests, session-state/vision-prefix and TP-command tests, rewind API guards, all remaining model-free `make test` steps, and the three static suites pass. Transport: 126/126; dist-v3: 169/169; CLI GPU arguments: 96/96.
- Isolated Metal `test-mxfp4-metal` and `test-metal-ssd-experts`: PASS, including exact SSD batch-cache outputs, eight-expert eviction, and bounded mapping lifetime. SSD-cache sizing, quality-API parser, and model-free terminal PTY/hints regressions also pass.
- `make clean` leaves the working tree clean; audited clean recipes and compiled `ds4_gpu.h` standalone across all 17 commits. Focused independent rebase review found no blockers.
- **Not rerun on this head:** ROCm/CUDA builds, model-loaded inference/vision, two-node live tests, and performance/benchmark suites. Production was not restarted or redeployed. The earlier hardware/benchmark results below are historical, not validation of `0bafad0`.

### Prior validation (`5c90fe2` / `16409d6` on `c0a6119`; older items at `fe77cd7` unless noted)

- **Terminal-Bench-Local Core-19 (kyuz0/terminal-bench-mini, Terminus-2, pass@2) on `16409d6`: 18/19 (94.7 %)**, identity matching the published dual-strix-halo MXFP4 run (19/19): pass@1 16/19 vs 15/19, wall 14.4 h vs 20.1 h, 96 % of prompt tokens from the resident KV cache, 0 infrastructure errors in 22 trials; the one miss (`extract-elf`) also failed attempt 1 in the published run. Results gist: https://gist.github.com/jyatesdotdev/ae1f90d86e0c58e773f5f79b62d788bd
- **Rebased head `16409d6`:** Mac/Metal build 0 warnings; all model-free `make test` steps (`ds4-eval` validate/extractors, `ds4_agent_test`, `ds4_test --server`, `test_layer_pack` 97/97, `test_engine_mgpu_placement` 109/109, `test_gpu_args` + CLI 96/96, `test_prompt_prefix`, `test_sampling`, `test_deepseek4_vision_image`, `test_session_state`, `test_tp_commands`), `test_transport` 126/126, `test_dist_v3` 169/169; `make clean` leaves `git status` clean. Both gfx1151 nodes: `make strix-halo` 0 warnings, byte-identical binaries; full `make test-rocm` green with 0 warnings (incl. `test_tp_combine_rocm` 9/9 + 1/1, `test_graph_deferred_dump_rocm`, `test_gpu_args_cli` 96/96); `test-mxfp4-rocm`, `test-rocm-qkv-fusion`, `test-q8-krow-rocm`: PASS. Deployed to the production two-node pipeline: decode 14.3 tok/s (flat), rewind resend `cached = prompt-1`, output identical to the fresh generation.

- Commits 12–16: Mac/Metal build 0 warnings; `ds4_test --server` (model-free unit tests for the metrics gauge, the dispatch scores, the draining-slot hold, the rewind API guards), `test_dist_v3` 169/169, `test_transport` 126/126. `make strix-halo` 0 warnings, byte-identical binaries on both nodes. Deployed to the production two-node pipeline and exercised end-to-end (rewind table above; dispatch: cancel a 3.3k-token request during prefill, resend within 0.5 s → continues on its own slot from the last quantum, the other slot's conversation untouched).

- Mac/Metal build clean (0 warnings); `make test` steps: `ds4_agent_test`, `ds4-eval` extractors + 92 core / 50 hard cases, `test_layer_pack`, `test_engine_mgpu_placement` 109/109, `test_gpu_args` + CLI, `test_prompt_prefix`, `test_sampling`, `test_deepseek4_vision_image`, upstream's new `test_session_state` and `test_tp_commands`, `test_transport` 126/126, `test_dist_v3` 148/148, the three static suites: PASS (`ds4_test` needs a full model, which the Mac used here does not have).
- `make strix-halo` builds clean (0 warnings, byte-identical binaries) on **both** Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) nodes; full `make test-rocm` passes (incl. `test_gpu_args_cli` 96/96); `test-mxfp4-rocm`, `test-tp-combine-rocm` 9/9 and 1/1 (`DS4_TEST_TP_PREQUANT=1`), `test-graph-deferred-dump-rocm`, `test-q8-krow-rocm`, `test-rocm-qkv-fusion`: PASS.

- Two-node NHI TP on the `ac03bca` binaries: 197-token prefill + 128-token decode, **14.01 tok/s**, completion byte-identical to every earlier run of the same prompt, NHI stats `failures=0 event_drops=0 crc=0 overrun=0`. (Not re-run on `47917e9`; the TP changes since are the frame renumbering and the allow-list fix, both unit-tested.)
- Earlier (pre-rebase) validation still stands: 3373-token prefill + decode across the chunk ladder, batched sessions token-exact vs serial, old-worker/new-leader negotiation fails closed.

## Performance (two Radeon 8060S nodes, TB5 link, MXFP4 model, layer-split pipeline 0:21/22:output)

Earlier branch measurements (not rerun after the September 11 rebase), with the iGPU performance level pinned `high` on both nodes (see "Clock management" below):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Prefill, 6k-token prompt | 250 tok/s |
| Prefill, 23k-token prompt | 274 tok/s |
| Decode, short runs | 15.5 tok/s |
| Decode, 6,144-token thinking run | 14.3–14.4 tok/s |
| Decode vs context (0.8k/3k/6k) | flat (≈14 tok/s) |
| 2-client `--batched-session 2` aggregate | +3% (short prompts) to +14% (long prompts) vs serial |

TP-over-NHI chunk ladder (unchanged, this is why 512 is the TP default): 256 → 126.1 tok/s, **512 → 137.5 tok/s**, 1024 → 122.9 tok/s. On a 2-node Thunderbolt link, pipeline mode remains the faster deployment; the TP path is the correctness-proven transport foundation and the candidate for topologies where pipeline depth runs out. TP decode is gate-bound, and a per-gate trace now says exactly how (next section).

**Decode kernels are at the DRAM wall.** The new POC bench (`tests/bench_matvec_poc_rocm`, 24-copy weight cycling to force DRAM misses) measures the dense Q8 decode matvec at 202 GB/s vs a 208 GB/s pure-stream upper bound, and the MXFP4 MoE gate/up decode kernel at 222 GB/s at the real production shape. Split-K, LDS-staging, ILP, and aligned-load variants are all null; a cross-stream shared/MoE overlap prototype measured net negative. There is no kernel-level decode headroom left on this part; the remaining single-session costs are the pipeline bubble (each node idles while the other computes) and clock management. At the wall, **weight-stream amortization via session batching is the only aggregate-throughput multiplier**, which is the direction L0/L1 starts.


### Persistent TP gate kernel POC — negative result (docs only, `docs/tp_persist_gate/`)

To test whether TP decode was paying for per-gate kernel launches and event waits, I built a resident gate kernel (host-written command ring, TX/RX worker waves, mapped flags, guarded device-wide runtime calls) behind `DS4_TP_PERSIST_GATE=1`. It was bit-exact and its single-node loopback floor reached 11.5 µs/gate — and the two-node A/B was **slower**: 13.99 → 11.92 tok/s. The code is not in this PR; it is preserved as `docs/tp_persist_gate/persist-gate.patch` with the requirements/design/plan and a full write-up in `BASELINE.md`. What is worth keeping is the per-gate trace it produced (both ranks stamp `wall_clock64` at TX release / peer stamp seen / RX done; joining on the gate sequence gives one-way latency `L=(X0+X1)/2` and rank skew `(X0−X1)/2` with no cross-node clock sync):

| per decode gate (86/token) | legacy path | persistent path |
|---|---:|---:|
| gate window mean / p50 | 244 / 209 µs | 221 / 210 µs |
| NHI one-way latency L (p50 / p99) | — | **215 / 240 µs** |
| rank skew \|s\| mean (signed mean ≈ 0) | — | **191 µs** |
| host detect + submit ioctl | ~15 µs | ~15 µs |
| compute segments per token | ~50 ms | ~65 ms |

So the decode gate window is ~245 µs on both paths and is made of transport latency plus MoE routing skew between the ranks (symmetric — the routed expert count per rank varies per layer per token, so no static rebalancing helps); launch overhead was ~20 µs of it, and the resident kernel cost ~15 ms/token in the compute segments between gates. The earlier "~0.44 ms/gate of choreography" figure came from a biased `DS4_TP_GATE_STATS` mean (prefill big gates included, gates where the peer was already waiting dropped). Remaining TP decode levers, for the record: cut L (transport), cut skew (routing-aware placement or coarser exchange granularity), or overlap the gate with independent compute.

### Pipeline vs tensor parallelism, same pair (post-rebase, 2026-09-04)

Same nodes, same MXFP4 model, same prompt text. Pipeline through the deployed `ds4-server` units (`--layers 0:21`/`22:output`, `--dist-transport auto` → TCP over the Thunderbolt IP link since no NHI device is passed), driven via `/v1/completions` at temp 0 and read from `/metrics`; TP via `ds4-bench --tensor-parallel --transport nhi`.

| workload | pipeline (TCP) | TP (NHI) |
|---|---:|---:|
| prefill, ~4–5k-token prompt | **242 tok/s** | 166 tok/s |
| decode, 1024 tokens, small context | **15.08 tok/s** | 13.86 tok/s |
| decode, 128 tokens at ~4–5k context | 14.01 tok/s | 12.93 tok/s |

Pipeline is ~1.45× faster on long prefill and ~8–9% faster on decode, consistent with the gate decomposition above (86 gate hops per token vs one activation hop). Guidance unchanged: on a two-node Thunderbolt link, pipeline is the deployment; TP is the correctness-proven transport foundation for topologies where pipeline depth runs out.

**Clock management matters on this APU.** Under default PMFW management the GPU decodes at ~1.75 GHz (max 2.9) at ~50% duty. Pinning `power_dpm_force_performance_level=high` on the host takes server decode from 14.65 → 15.5 tok/s and prefill from ~210 → 250–274 tok/s. Host-level setting, no code change; recommended for deployments.

**Next up:** routed-MoE row batching inside the multi-session span (the MoE is ~62% of per-token DRAM traffic and still runs per-session; the MXFP4 direct launcher already guarantees bit-exact rows for n≤8, so this is span plumbing on the L1 pattern), then batched attention decode and shared-down/HC batching. Projected ~1.5–1.8× aggregate decode at 2–4 clients.

## For testers on this thread

Pull the rebased branch (history rewritten again for the `6289c51` rebase; the 17-commit structure is unchanged), rebuild the strix-rdma module from its main (series 18 prints at load and via `zc_series`), let the new 512-row TP default apply — do not pass `--prefill-chunk 4096` — and consider pinning the iGPU performance level `high` for serving.

title: metal: speed up IQ2_XXS MoE prefill with half LUT and split MPP

title: cuda: fix Ampere token-tile ldmatrix IMA
body:
## Summary

The CUDA token-tile HMMA attention path IMA's on Ampere (`sm_80`) as soon as prefill hits `n_tokens >= 128`. Hopper / GB10 already ran this kernel; Ampere did not.

Root cause is the `ldmatrix` PTX, not the architecture gate. The three `ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n8.{x4,x2,x2.trans}.b16` helpers omitted `.shared`. On Ampere that makes `[addr]` a generic address, so a shared-memory pointer is decoded as global and the load IMA's. Adding `.shared` is the actual fix; `ds4_cuda_attn_tokentile_arch_ok()` stays `major >= 8`.

## What changed

- Add `.shared` to the three token-tile `ldmatrix` PTX strings.
- Predicate raw/comp/record `cp.async` against the live mirror size so a padded stage cannot issue an unconstrained global load.
- Cover the dense HMMA geometry (128 tokens, 64 heads, dk=512, SWA 128, ratio 4) in `tests/cuda_long_context_smoke.c`.

Metal, ROCm, CPU, and the heads8/cuBLAS fallbacks are untouched.

## Testing

On a CMP 170HX (`sm_80`, 64 GB):

- Isolation (compute-sanitizer cannot attach; GPU debugging is disabled on this card): skip-Q / skip-KV / skip-MMA were clean; IMA was inside `tt_hmma_score_stage` `ldmatrix` even with identity swizzle and without `cp.async`. Adding `.shared` made one-block and full-grid launches pass.
- `make cuda-regression CUDA_ARCH=sm_80` → `cuda long-context regression: OK`
- Hetero ROCm coordinator `0:26` + CUDA worker `27:output`, Q2 GGUF, `--dist-prefill-chunk 4096`:
  - 128-token prefill: 46.60 t/s prefill, 19.05 t/s decode
  - 4096-token prefill: **248.44 t/s** prefill, 16.49 t/s decode (previously IMA; chunk 64 was ~87 t/s)

Not re-run here: GB10 / `sm_121` (the kernel already shipped there), Metal, SSD streaming.

## Notes

Gating Ampere off and keeping HMMA on `sm_90+` / `sm_121` only would also avoid the crash, but that leaves Ampere on the slow heads8 path. The PTX space qualifier is the smaller correct fix.
