title: STRIXHALO.md: amd_iommu=off and amdgpu.gttsize are not required (and amd_iommu=off disables the NPU)
body:
I ran DS4 on a Strix Halo host without two of the four kernel parameters in §3, and it worked. Since one of those two silently disables the machine's NPU, I think the document is worth softening.

**Host:** ASUS ROG Flow Z13 (GZ302EA), Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 128 GB, NixOS 26.11, kernel 7.1.0 (mainline).
**Model:** a community `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-…-Q2` GGUF, 80.76 GiB — same size class as the one §5 recommends, same `iq2_xxs` / `q2_k` / `q8_0` quant family.

Kernel command line, in full — note what's *absent*:

```
… iommu.passthrough=0 amd_pstate=active amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x600 ttm.pages_limit=25165824 ttm.page_pool_size=25165824
```

No `amd_iommu=off`. No `amdgpu.gttsize`. `iommu.passthrough=0` means IOMMU translation is *active*, which is the demanding case rather than a soft-disable. Result:

```
ds4: ROCm backend initialized on AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics (sm_115)
ds4: ROCm startup model preparation covered 80.76 GiB of tensor spans in 57.063s
ds4: prefill: 21.99 t/s, generation: 13.70 t/s
```

Coherent output, no errors.

**On `amdgpu.gttsize`:** `ttm.pages_limit` alone sets the ceiling, exactly. `ttm.pages_limit=25165824` × 4096 = 103079215104 bytes, and `mem_info_gtt_total` reads 103079215104 — a 1:1 map with `gttsize` never set. Separately, ROCm issue #5595 advises against setting `amdgpu.gttsize` and `ttm.pages_limit` together, so recommending both invites the conflict it warns about.

**On `amd_iommu=off`:** the same package that has the iGPU also has an **XDNA2 NPU**, and its `amdxdna` driver requires an IOMMU to be present for PASID. With `amd_iommu=off` there is no IOMMU at all and the NPU stops working — so following §3 as written costs Halo users their NPU. This isn't my finding; it's documented by the NixOS [`nix-amd-ai`](https://github.com/noamsto/nix-amd-ai) flake, which has a section titled "`amd_iommu=off` would kill the NPU". On this host the NPU (FastFlowLM, `flm validate` → 8 columns, firmware 1.1.2.65) and DS4 coexist fine, because the IOMMU is left on.

I haven't measured whether `amd_iommu=off` buys anything — the Strix Halo wiki claims a small memory-read speedup. My claim is narrower: it isn't a prerequisite for running DS4, and it has a cost the document doesn't mention. If you'd rather keep it as an optional performance note with an NPU warning attached, that works too and I'll rework the diff.

One knock-on the diff also fixes: the "verify" block a few lines down greps for `gttsize` and expects `amdgpu: 126976M of GTT memory ready`, which only appears when `gttsize` is set — so following the new parameter list would have made the documented expected signs fail. It now checks `mem_info_gtt_total` against `pages_limit * 4096` instead.

Caveat for the record: one host, one model, one configuration. I'm claiming "not required here", not "wrong".

title: CUDA: reject prefill mixed shapes wider than the shared scores window (#803)
body:
Fixes #803.

## What

`attention_prefill_mixed_kernel` (the scalar prefill fallback) stores every attention score in a fixed `__shared__ float scores[512]`, and neither the kernel nor the last hop of `attention_prefill_mixed_launch` caps `n_score = raw_count + visible_comp`. Shapes wider than 512 write past the array — silently while the overflow lands in the adjacent `partial[256]`, and as an invalid shared write beyond that (see the analysis in #803).

Following the fix suggested in the issue, and mirroring what the ROCm side already does (`rocm/ds4_rocm_attention_launch.cuh`, `DS4_ROCM_ATTENTION_PREFILL_MIXED_SCORE_CAP`):

- **Host**: `attention_prefill_mixed_launch` computes the worst-case score count (`max_raw = min(window, n_tokens)` or `n_tokens` when `window == 0`, plus `n_comp`) and refuses the launch with the same log line as ROCm when it exceeds 512. Both `ds4_gpu_attention_prefill_static_mixed_heads_tensor` and `ds4_gpu_attention_prefill_masked_mixed_heads_tensor` go through this launch, so both are covered.
- **Kernel**: `if (raw_count + visible_comp > 512u) return;` before any shared write, as defense in depth, matching the ROCm kernel.

## Regression test

New case in `tests/cuda_long_context_smoke.c` (runs under `make cuda-regression`):

- an overflow shape (`n_tokens=1024, window=0, ratio=4` → 1280 scores) must be refused by the launcher;
- a windowed shape that fits (128 raw + 256 comp = 384) must keep working.

`head_dim != 512` keeps the launcher off the token-tile / window / cublas paths so the test deterministically exercises the scalar fallback, without env vars.

## Validation

Environment: RunPod community pods, RTX 3080 and RTX 3090 (sm_86), driver 580.x, CUDA 12.4 toolkit, `make cuda CUDA_ARCH=sm_86`, upstream `c1d4597`. compute-sanitizer from CUDA 13.0 (`cuda-sanitizer-13-0`) — note for other reproducers: the 12.4 sanitizer fails to start at all on 580+ drivers (`Target application terminated before first instrumented API call`).

| | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` on the new test | 40 × `Invalid __shared__ write` at `ds4_cuda.cu:7149` in `attention_prefill_mixed_kernel` (RTX 3090; 100+ on RTX 3080 with a wider run) | 0 invalid writes |
| new regression case | overflow shape accepted | overflow shape refused with the log line, fitting shape passes, `cuda long-context regression: OK` |
| `make test` | — | passes up to the suites that need the real GGUF (not run: no model weights on the pod) |

Two unrelated sanitizer reports remain before and after the patch: `cudaErrorNotSupported` from `cudaHostRegister` in `cuda_model_range_ptr` (`ds4_cuda.cu:747`), reached from the pre-existing decode test. That is the discrete-GPU host-register behavior discussed in #791, not introduced here.

Not done: a before/after `ds4-bench` run, since the pod had no model weights. The guard adds one comparison per launch on the host path only; the kernel guard is two integer adds and a compare per block before any shared traffic.

## Transparency

A commit referencing this issue (`2a2a887f`, by @marcodelpin) appears in #803's timeline, but the fork it lived in is no longer reachable and no PR ever landed. This implementation was done independently against current main.

title: tokenizer: fix bpe_emit_piece's O(n^2) merge loop (#853)
body:
Fixes #853.

## Root cause

`bpe_emit_piece`'s merge loop rescanned every adjacent symbol pair on every
merge iteration (`ds4.c`, previously around line 37174). Real CJK/no-space
prompts pre-tokenize into a single very long piece, so `n` stays large across
the whole merge process and the rescan-per-merge makes it O(n²).

## Fix

Replaces the flat-array rescan with a min-heap of candidate adjacent merges
over a doubly-linked symbol list (same shape as llama.cpp's own BPE tokenizer
and the classic HF-tokenizers approach): each merge only pushes the (at most
two) newly-adjacent pairs it created, instead of rescanning everything.
O(n log n) instead of O(n²).

- Tie-breaking is unchanged: the heap orders by `(rank asc, left-position
  asc)`, which reproduces the original scan's "leftmost pair wins on equal
  rank" behavior exactly.
- Staleness of a popped heap entry is detected by snapshotting both symbols'
  lengths at push time and comparing against their current length at pop
  time — cheap and sufficient, since a symbol's length only ever grows (by
  absorbing its right neighbor), so any change since the candidate was queued
  shows up as a length mismatch.

## Verification

Built both the pre-fix and post-fix binary and diffed `--dump-tokens` output
(byte-for-byte identical token id sequences in all cases):

- Small ASCII with punctuation/whitespace/newlines
- A tie-break-heavy repeated-bigram case (`"ab"` × 800)
- Empty prompt, single character
- Large English prose (~46 KB)
- A large CJK repetition stress case (~72 KB, no whitespace boundaries —
  reproduces the reported worst case): **18.03s → 0.23s (~79x)**, output
  identical
- Both of the repo's own long-context fixtures,
  `tests/long_context_story_prompt.txt` (~140 KB, 30475 tokens) and
  `tests/long_context_security_prompt.txt` (~149 KB, 36667 tokens) — already
  fast pre-fix (normal English word-boundaries keep pieces small), confirming
  no regression on the common case, byte-identical output

Also checked for leaks with `leaks --atExit` on the large-prose case: 0
leaks. Builds clean with `-Wall -Wextra -std=c99`, no new warnings.

Model used for all of the above: the repo owner's own deployed
DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0731 quant (Q4K/IQ2XXS mixed), via
`ds4 --dump-tokens --prompt-file` — this path only loads tokenizer vocab/
merge-rank metadata, not model weights, so none of this required loading the
full model.

title: Tune the Metal backend for M3 Ultra
body:
# Tune the Metal backend for M3 Ultra

Eleven commits. **+2.38% decode, prefill flat** on an M3 Ultra, measured with
interleaved A/B sweeps across 32 context lengths. Every change is
bit-exactness-verified against the shader it replaces.

**Roughly half of this PR's value is negative results.** Three changes were
implemented, measured, and reverted. A fourth -- raising the prefill chunk --
was implemented, measured as a *regression* in the standard benchmark
workload, and replaced by a fix for the crash it exposed. A systematic retune
found nothing to retune. Metal 4 turned out to work here and be slower. All of
it is written up under *What did not work*, so nobody re-derives it.

There is also a methodology finding worth more than the speedup: on this
machine a single unalternated benchmark sweep per arm produces errors of
5-6%, larger than everything being measured. See *How these numbers were
measured*.

> **Rebased onto current `main` (110afdd) and re-measured from scratch.**
> The headline number above is from the rebased branch against the current
> `main`, not carried over from the original campaign. What was and was not
> re-verified on this base is listed under *What was re-checked after the
> rebase*.

## Machine and model

| | |
|---|---|
| Device | Apple M3 Ultra, 80 GPU cores, 512 GB, macOS 26.5.2 |
| `MTLDevice.architecture.name` | `applegpu_g15d` (generation 15, tier d) |
| Backend | Metal |
| Model | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, **MXFP4** experts / F16 HC+compressor+indexer / Q8 attn+shared+out |
| Residency | 145.26 GiB resident, no SSD streaming |

## End-to-end result

Two blocks of four interleaved sweeps, arms in **M-B-B-M** and then **B-M-M-B**
order with a rebuild between each. Pooling the two blocks is what makes this
trustworthy: each arm occupies run positions {1,4} in one block and {2,3} in
the other, so any position-dependent effect -- including a non-linear one that
a single ABBA block cannot cancel -- drops out.

```sh
./ds4-bench -m ds4flash.gguf \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt \
  --ctx-start 2048 --ctx-max 65536 --step-incr 2048 --gen-tokens 128
```

| ctx | main prefill | branch prefill | Δ | main decode | branch decode | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 639.28 | 639.57 | +0.04% | 42.80 | 43.88 | +2.54% |
| 8,192 | 567.65 | 568.04 | +0.07% | 38.35 | 39.27 | +2.39% |
| 16,384 | 539.11 | 539.21 | +0.02% | 37.52 | 38.39 | +2.31% |
| 32,768 | 487.97 | 487.57 | -0.08% | 36.01 | 36.86 | +2.35% |
| 65,536 | 411.13 | 410.61 | -0.13% | 33.49 | 34.17 | +2.02% |
| **mean (32 ctx)** | | | **-0.04%** | | | **+2.38%** |

Decode range across the 32 contexts: +2.02% to +2.65%, positive at every one.
Prefill is flat by design -- every win here is in the FP8 KV path, which is
decode-side work.

Per-block agreement, as a check that the pooling is not hiding a split:

| block | order | prefill | decode |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `dsA` | M-B-B-M | -0.04% | +2.32% |
| `dsB` | B-M-M-B | -0.04% | +2.43% |
| **pooled** | position-balanced | **-0.04%** | **+2.38%** |

## GLM 5.3 Flash: a control, and it behaves like one

GLM 5.3 Flash Q4_K (177.8 GiB, also fully resident) was measured the same way,
one M-B-B-M block.

| ctx | main prefill | branch prefill | main decode | branch decode |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 429.77 | 429.53 | 21.06 | 21.04 |
| 8,192 | 391.63 | 391.90 | 20.64 | 20.66 |
| 16,384 | 388.09 | 388.25 | 20.56 | 20.54 |
| 32,768 | 380.06 | 380.66 | 20.43 | 20.41 |
| 65,536 | 362.99 | 366.68 | 20.18 | 20.21 |
| **mean (32 ctx)** | | **+0.58%** | | **+0.02%** |

**Decode: +0.02%** -- a null. The per-context deltas run -0.17% to +0.29% and only 16 of 32 are positive, which is a coin flip.

**Prefill: +0.58% as pooled, but that number is an artefact and should be read as a null too.** The whole difference comes from one sweep: the first main sweep runs ~0% off the second across the early frontiers and about +3.8% slow across the last six. That is a transient in the tail of one sweep, not a cold cache -- a cold cache would show up at the *start*. Excluding that sweep gives prefill +0.12% and decode -0.02%. Post-hoc exclusion is not evidence, so the honest statement is that this single block does not resolve GLM prefill; it is consistent with null, and there is no mechanism in this branch that could move GLM prefill in the first place.

This is the expected result and it is worth having on the record: every speed
change in this PR is in an FP8 KV / MXFP4 / E4M3 path that GLM 5.3 does not
use. Its `rope_dimension_count` is 0, so it takes a different KV path
entirely. The point of running it is to show the branch does not *regress* a
model it was never aimed at.

Two caveats on this block specifically. It is a single M-B-B-M block, so it is
position-balanced only to first order, unlike the DeepSeek result. And
`ds4-bench` defaults `--ctx-alloc` to `ctx-max + gen-tokens + 1` = 65665, which
is above the `DS4_GLM_METAL_LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` of 65536, so the whole
sweep runs with the full-attention cap clamped to 4096.

## What worked

### Speed

| commit | effect |
|---|---|
| replace the E4M3FN binary search with branch-free rounding | **+1.37% decode** |
| reduce the FP8 KV amax with `simd_max` | **+1.27% decode** |
| restrict the matvec reduction tree to simdgroup 0 | **+0.47% decode** |

Combined, measured together against `main`: **+2.38% decode**, prefill flat.

The per-commit attributions above are from the original campaign against the
pre-rebase `main`; only the combined figure has been re-measured on this base.

### Correctness (no speed effect)

- **zero the FP8 amax scratch on partial KV blocks.** The fused
  norm+RoPE+FP8-store kernel dropped the `else` that seeds the reduction
  buffer, so a partial final block folded uninitialised threadgroup memory
  into the amax -- wrong *and* irreproducible between runs. Later subsumed by
  the `simd_max` rewrite; see *Notes on two commits*.
- **bound the IQ2_XXS grid staging to 64 threads.** Five kernels derived a
  staging position from `32*sgitg + tiisg` with no upper bound, correct only
  at `nsg == 2`. Safe today only because the host pins these pipelines to 2.
  Collapsed onto one shared helper so no open-coded copy is left -- that
  duplication is what produced the bug above.
- **assert the FP8 KV prefix is 64-aligned.** Six call sites across three
  backends assume `key_length - rope.dimension_count` is a multiple of 64;
  nothing said so.
- **clamp an out-of-range prefill chunk.** `--prefill-chunk 9216` is a
  documented flag that aborted with `gpu layer 2 attention batch encode
  failed` and no hint at the cause. The raw KV cache is sized
  `align_up(raw_window + prefill_cap, 256)` clamped to 8192 rows, so a larger
  chunk cannot be staged. Now clamps and warns. Inert for both defaults.

### Infrastructure

- **an E4M3FN conversion equivalence oracle.** 65536 inputs covering every
  representable magnitude, every midpoint and one ULP either side, the
  subnormal range, the saturation boundary and a full-range sweep. Confirmed
  to have teeth by mutation: breaking only the ties-to-even rule produces 130
  mismatches.
- **report GPU architecture, generation and core count.** Reporting only.
- **add `DS4_METAL_FORCE_METAL4`.** Off by default; makes the pre-M5 default a
  measured decision rather than an untested one.
- **a `speed-bench` CSV and plot for this hardware.**

# What did not work

Everything in this section was measured against the pre-rebase `main`. None of
it changes any code that ships in this PR, so the rebase does not affect the
conclusions, but the numbers have not been re-taken.

## 1. Raising the prefill chunk looked like a win and was not

This branch originally raised the Flash prefill chunk from 4096 to 8192 on M3
Ultra, behind a device gate, and claimed +1.95% prefill on the strength of a
single-frontier measurement at ctx 8192.

That claim was wrong, and the way it was wrong is the most useful thing in
this PR.

Measured properly -- the same branch against itself, gate on vs gate off, four
interleaved sweeps -- the chunk change **costs** prefill in the standard
benchmark workload:

| ctx | prefill Δ (gate on vs off) |
|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | **-2.11%** |
| 8,192 | -0.62% |
| 16,384 | -0.53% |
| 65,536 | -0.50% |
| **mean (32 ctx)** | **-0.62%** |

The reason is that the benchmark prefills in 2048-token increments, which is
below both the 4096 and the 8192 cap, so the larger chunk is never used --
but it still raises `raw_kv_rows` from 4352 to 8192, allocating roughly double
the raw KV staging workspace that this workload never touches. The cost is
largest at short context where that overhead dominates.

It does help when the cap actually binds, i.e. one large prompt prefilled in a
single call -- but the gain decays as the prompt outgrows the cap:

| single-frontier prefill | cap 4096 | cap 8192 | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ctx 8,192 | 612.79 | 624.07 | +1.84% |
| ctx 16,384 | 588.84 | 596.08 | +1.23% |
| ctx 32,768 | 553.12 | 556.38 | +0.59% |

So it is workload-dependent: better for one-shot prefill, worse for
incremental prefill, which is also the chat/continuation pattern. It cannot be
made conditional cleanly, because `prefill_cap` is fixed at session creation
from `ctx_size`, before anything knows how the caller will prefill. And it adds
little that is not already reachable: `DS4_METAL_PREFILL_CHUNK=8192` already
exists, so the commit only changed the default.

**Dropped.** What survives is the useful part: the 8192 ceiling is now
documented in the source, and the crash it exposed is fixed (see *What
worked*).

## 2. Three changes were implemented, measured, and reverted

Each was verified bit-identical and benchmarked before being removed. None
regressed anything -- they simply were not improvements, and a tuning PR
should not carry changes that cannot be justified on measurement.

| change | measured | why reverted |
|---|---|---|
| Q8_0 decode weights as 16-bit pairs (7 sites) | +0.19% decode, n=12/arm, ranges overlap | at the noise floor |
| bitonic sort barriers narrowed to simdgroup scope | +0.08% decode, n=6/arm, ranges overlap | top-k is not a meaningful share of decode |
| IQ2_XXS SwiGLU epilogue kept in registers | +0.11% decode on the IQ2XXS model, n=4/arm, ranges overlap | IQ2-only, and noise there too |

Two are worth a specific note against the review that suggested them:

- The Q8_0 load widening was billed as *"the biggest single win"* available.
  It is not; on this hardware it is indistinguishable from noise.
- The IQ2_XXS epilogue fix cannot affect an MXFP4 or Q4_K deployment at all.
  Both dynamic-`float4` sites are in IQ2_XXS kernels; the MXFP4 kernels
  already use a scalar `simd_sum(sumf[row])` per row.

The bitonic change did at least surface a real bug in the advice: guarding on
`j < 32` alone is wrong, because `j == 1` is the last step of each `k` and the
next `k` opens with a cross-simdgroup step. The correct condition is
`j >= 32 || j == 1`.

## 3. There was nothing to retune

The premise going in was that thresholds tuned on a narrower M3 would be badly
wrong on an 80-core part. Tested directly: every one of the 24 `PRE_M5`
features is default-ON here, so each was disabled in turn, interleaved with
baseline so drift cancels.

| disabled | Δ decode |
|---|---|
| `DECODE_PORTS` | **-6.27%** |
| `MXFP4_MOE_DECODE_NSG1` | -2.28% |
| `MXFP4_MOE_DECODE_FIXED_ROUTE_PAIR` | -2.14% |
| `ROUTER_SIMD_FINALIZE` | -2.02% |
| `MXFP4_MOE_DECODE_TG_MULTIPLE` | -1.91% |
| `COMPRESSOR_RATIO4_DECODE_PACK_FUSION` | -1.70% |
| 17 more | -1.2% to -0.2% |
| `COMPRESSOR_EXACT_REDUCTION_FUSION` | +0.05% (noise) |

All 24 earn their keep. Four prefill features additionally cost 1.6-2.9%
prefill when disabled. `DS4_METAL_Q8_MV_NSG` is likewise already optimal at
its default of 4 -- raising it to 8 gains nothing, lowering it to 1 costs
1.18%.

The best MoE decode configuration is **`NSG1`**: *one* simdgroup, worth 2.28%
over the alternative. More GPU width did not want more parallelism per output
row; the winning shape is fewer simdgroups with more rows in flight. That
inverts the intuition the retune was based on.

**No threshold changes are included in this PR, because none were justified.**

Still 24 features on current `main` -- upstream added none in the 97 commits
this branch was rebased over.

**Scope note:** all 24 of those flags are on DeepSeek paths. `ds4_metal.m` has
939 GLM references and *zero* `PRE_M5` gates among them, so "there was nothing
to retune" is a statement about the DeepSeek path only. The GLM path has never
been through this exercise. See *Adjacent work this does not do*.

## 4. Metal 4 works on M3 Ultra and is slower

`supportsFamily:MTLGPUFamilyMetal4` is true here, the compile probe passes,
the pipelines build and run, and output is byte-identical to the default path.
It is simply not faster:

| | prefill | decode |
|---|---|---|
| default (off) | 622.94 | 39.512 |
| `DS4_METAL_FORCE_METAL4=1` | 620.8 | 39.530 |

-0.34% prefill, with the wider spread of the two arms. This matches MLX, which
gates its Neural Accelerator path at `gen >= 17` and would decline this
generation-15 device too.

It also settles a larger question without opening it: porting flash-attention
prefill onto the same MPP path is not worth attempting, because the MPP shape
does not win where it is already implemented.

The flag ships off by default. Its value is that the pre-M5 default is now a
measured decision rather than an untested one, and it can be re-measured on
future hardware.

## 5. Two directions ruled out before implementing

- **Dispatch overhead** (`NSString` per pipeline lookup, linear model-view
  scan, command-buffer stalls). Decode measures at **~98% GPU utilisation**
  (`DS4_METAL_GPU_BUSY_PROFILE`: 12468 ms busy over 12.71 s wall on a
  512-token decode run), so there is no CPU stall to reclaim. Hot pipeline
  lookups are also already cached at 93 call sites on current `main` (91 when
  this was first written; upstream added two). I had assumed the opposite
  before measuring and was wrong.
- **The barrier-free matvec shape selected by `out_dim`, and the `yl[32]` MoE
  staging rewrite.** The NSG results above show the current shape is already
  the better one for the Q8 path, and the `yl[32]` staging is IQ2_XXS-only.

## 6. Why the wins were where they were

Every measurable improvement came from removing a **barrier or a serial
dependency**. Every attempt to save arithmetic or narrow load-issue slots
measured as noise:

| change | Δ decode | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| E4M3 binary search -> branch-free | +1.37% | serial dependency chain removed |
| FP8 amax tree -> `simd_max` | +1.27% | 8 barriers per block -> 2 |
| matvec reduction -> simdgroup 0 | +0.47% | redundant reductions removed |
| Q8_0 byte loads -> 16-bit pairs | +0.19% | noise -- reverted |
| bitonic barriers narrowed | +0.08% | noise -- reverted |
| IQ2 epilogue spill removed | +0.11% | noise -- reverted |

That is consistent with the utilisation number: at 98% GPU-busy while moving
roughly a fifth of peak memory bandwidth on a bandwidth-bound operation, the
machine is busy waiting, not busy computing.

---

## How these numbers were measured

Worth stating separately, because it invalidated an earlier version of this
PR's headline claim and would invalidate anyone else's.

**A single unalternated sweep per arm is not reliable on this machine.** A full
sweep takes several minutes, so running `main` then the branch back to back
gives the two arms different page-cache warmth on a 145 GiB model, different
thermal state, and any background load in between. Measured that way, this
branch appeared to gain **+5-6% prefill and +6-7% decode** -- a flat offset
across all 32 contexts, which looks exactly like a real systematic improvement.

None of the prefill gain survived alternation, and the decode gain was roughly
halved.

Every number in this PR therefore comes from **interleaved** runs, and the
post-rebase measurement goes further: two blocks, **M-B-B-M** and **B-M-M-B**,
with a rebuild between every sweep and an untimed warmup sweep whenever the
model changes. Pooled across the two blocks each arm occupies run positions
{1,4} once and {2,3} once, which cancels position effects that a single ABBA
block cannot -- a drift curve that rises and then falls would otherwise flatter
whichever arm sits in the middle.

Within-arm run-to-run drift under that scheme was 0.32% on average (1.47% worst case), small enough to
resolve the ~2% effect here.

**Concurrent disk I/O invalidates a run completely.** One measurement round was
thrown away entirely because a large file copy was running against the same
disk. It produced a ~2% *uniform level shift* per sweep -- per-context shape
reproduced tightly (sd 0.26-0.30%) while the whole sweep moved -- which is
indistinguishable from a real effect if you only look at one block, and which
happened to inflate whichever arm ran in the middle. If you re-measure this PR,
check the machine is otherwise idle, and treat a per-sweep level shift larger
than a few tenths of a percent as a sign that it was not.

If you re-measure this PR, please alternate. A single before/after pair will
give you a number several times larger than the real one, in either direction.

## What was re-checked after the rebase

Re-verified on current `main`:

| | |
|---|---|
| End-to-end speed | re-measured, two position-balanced blocks |
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q4_K | newly measured as a control |
| Full test suite | 21 suites green (was 13 before upstream added GLM 5.3 and vision suites) |
| 24 `PRE_M5` features | still exactly 24; upstream added none |
| 64-alignment assert | safe for upstream's new `glm5-next` shape |
| Prefill-chunk clamp | inert for all five shipped defaults |
| Conflicts with #621 | re-measured against its current head |
| Cached pipeline call sites | 91 -> 93 |

Carried over from the original campaign and **not** re-measured: the
per-commit speed attributions, everything under *What did not work*, and the
98% GPU-utilisation figure. None of them gate any code in this PR.

## No new device gate

An earlier version of this branch added `ds4_gpu_device_is_m3_ultra()` to gate
the prefill-chunk change, which would have introduced a third
device-identification style to a file that already has two. That commit is
gone, and so is the helper.

What remains is reporting-only: `ds4_gpu_device_architecture()`,
`ds4_gpu_device_generation()` and `ds4_gpu_device_core_count()`. Nothing
dispatches on them. They exist because no existing gate can distinguish an
80-core M3 Ultra from a 10-core M3 -- `ds4_gpu_device_name_contains("M3")` is
equally true of both -- so any future width-dependent tuning has an input to
work from. `DS4_METAL_GPU_ARCH` and `DS4_METAL_GPU_CORES` override them so such
paths can be exercised on other hardware.

Given the retune found nothing to change (see above), landing them as
measurement rather than as a gate is the honest scope.

## Compatibility with #621

Re-verified against #621 at `75503b9`, its current head.

Note that #621 is **not** rebased onto current `main` -- it branches from
`3da2da9` -- so the two branches no longer share a merge base, which
they did when this section was first written.

**Three conflicts, all mechanical**, unchanged in shape from the original
analysis: two in `metal/moe.metal`, one in `ds4_metal.m`. `Makefile`, `ds4.c`
and `tests/ds4_test.c` merge clean.

**`metal/moe.metal`, conflict 1** -- #621 appends a 259-line
`ds4_metal_iq2xxs_half_values` table immediately after `#define iq2xxs_grid`;
this branch appends the staging helper at the same anchor. Both self-contained.
Keep both.

**`metal/moe.metal`, conflict 2** -- #621's `c230e3f` and this branch's IQ2
staging commit **fix the same bug the same way**, arrived at independently.
Their inline grid-stride block and this branch's helper call collide at one
kernel. Take the helper call: identical semantics, and it removes the
duplication rather than leaving two forms of the same fix in one file.

**`ds4_metal.m`** -- #621 adds `ds4_gpu_test_iq2_addr_mid_only_oracle` and this
branch adds `ds4_gpu_test_e4m3fn_dequant` at the same anchor. This one looks
like adjacency but is not: both functions end with the identical
`}` / `return 1;` / `}` tail, so git treats that tail as shared context and the
conflict cuts mid-function. Concatenating both sides nests one function inside
the other. #621's function needs its closing brace, `return 1;` and brace added
explicitly before the second begins.

### On the overlapping fix

#621 got to the IQ2 staging bug independently and their grid-stride form is
better than what this branch originally had, which bounded staging to a fixed
64 threads. That is correct for nsg >= 2 but under-stages at nsg == 1, leaving
the upper half of both tables unwritten. This branch now uses their shape,
credited in the commit message, applied through the shared helper so it covers
all sites rather than two.

### A note on the failure mode this class of merge has

`metal/*.metal` are concatenated and compiled **at runtime**, not at build
time. A shader signature mismatch introduced by a merge therefore passes
`make` cleanly and fails only when the Metal library loads -- CI that builds
but does not run the binary would go green on a broken tree. An earlier version
of this branch changed `helper_mv_reduce_and_write`'s signature and #621 adds a
call site to it, which produced exactly that. That signature change has since
been dropped (it bought nothing measurable), so the helper now matches `main`
and no call site is touched.

### One pre-existing failure in #621, unrelated to this branch

On a clean checkout of #621 at `bfd3554` with no merge involved,
`./ds4_test --metal-kernels` was red:

    ds4-test: output HC weights4 total mismatch=1/16 max_ulp=2
    tests/ds4_test.c:6658: assertion failed: stats.mismatch_count == 0

Identical signature before and after merging this branch, so it was theirs, not
merge damage. Flagging it so it is not mistaken for one later. This has **not**
been re-checked against #621's current head.

## Backend impact

`CONTRIBUTING.md` asks that PRs touching more than one backend be checked on
each. Nine of the eleven commits are Metal shaders, `ds4_metal.m`, tests or
benchmark data, and cannot affect another backend. Two touch shared code in
`ds4.c`, and both are no-ops on current behaviour:

- **64-alignment assert.** Runs on every backend. A no-op on all five shipped
  variants -- their non-RoPE prefix is 448 or 512 -- and only fires if a future
  variant breaks an invariant that six call sites across Metal, CUDA and ROCm
  already depend on silently. Upstream's new `glm5-next` shape is the case this
  was written for: it has `rope_dimension_count = 0`, giving a 512 prefix, so
  it passes. Confirmed against the shipped GLM-5.3-Flash GGUF metadata as well
  as the shape table.
- **prefill chunk clamp.** Only reachable when a caller requests a chunk above
  8192, which currently aborts the run. All shipped defaults are at or below
  the limit -- 4096, PRO's 8192, CUDA tensor-parallel's 2048, and upstream's
  new `DS4_GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK_TOKENS` of 2048 -- so no configuration changes
  value.

No default prefill chunk is changed by this PR.

**I could not test CUDA or ROCm: I have no such hardware.** The reasoning above
is from reading the gates, not from running them. `make cpu` builds clean. A
maintainer with a CUDA machine should confirm `make cuda-regression` before
merging, though neither commit changes any value on that path.

## Adjacent work this does not do

Reading the GLM paths while re-validating this rebase turned up several
constants that take no input from how much memory the machine has. Recording
them here because they are the same shape as the prefill-chunk finding above,
and because the next person to look should not have to re-derive them. **None
of this is measured, and none of it is changed by this PR.**

- `glm_graph_full_attention_cap` gives the **SSD-streaming** path a full
  attention cap of 8192 and the **fully-resident** path 4096. The
  memory-constrained machine gets the larger window; the resident branch is
  the unexamined one. Above a 65536 context both clamp to 4096, so the
  asymmetry is only reachable below that.
- `DS4_GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK_TOKENS` is a flat 2048 with no device, memory or
  residency input -- half what the GLM 5.2 path uses and a quarter of the 8192
  structural ceiling documented above.
- `DS4_GLM_METAL_INDEXED_PREFILL_SCORE_SCRATCH_MB` is a fixed 256 MB that
  directly clamps how many rows can be scored per dispatch.
- A trap for anyone testing the first two: `DS4_GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK_TOKENS`
  (2048) and `DS4_GLM_METAL_FULL_ATTN_LAYER_FLUSH_CONTEXT` (2048) are the same
  number and the comparison is a strict `>`, so the default chunk sits exactly
  on the boundary where per-layer command-buffer flushing switches **off**.
  Raising the chunk to 4096 also switches flushing on across 46 layers. Those
  are two changes, not one, and measuring them together would likely produce
  the same false negative the DeepSeek prefill chunk did.

## Other corrections to the review that prompted this work

Beyond the ones above:

- **"Pre-scale the activation, don't unpack the weight ... the most valuable
  idea in the repo."** Already implemented: `kernel_mul_mv_q4_K_f32_impl`
  masks without shifting and folds the zero point into a `sumy` accumulator
  outside the inner loop.
- **Site counts.** The IQ2_XXS staging is 5 sites, not 6, and one already had
  the guard. The FP8 amax loop is 5 sites, not 3 (`dsv4_rope.metal` has two
  more). The Q8_0 scalar loop is 7 sites, not 5.
- **The 64-alignment assert cannot live in `config_validate_fixed_shape`.**
  `config_validate_model` returns early for `glm-dsa` and never reaches it, so
  the check sits at the shared entry point instead. Still true after upstream's
  restructuring of that function.

## Notes on two commits

**The E4M3 rewrite is simpler than the MLX port that was suggested.** E4M3FN
magnitudes are exactly `(8 + mant) * 2^(e-10)`, and the subnormal binade
continues the same `2^-9` spacing. So the rounded integer `q` is `8 + mant` and
`q * scale` is already the answer -- no code index, no encode step, no table
lookup. Since `code = (e-1)*8 + q`, code and `q` always share parity, so
`rint()` reproduces the ties-to-even-code rule exactly.

It was checked against the previous implementation over **every finite float32
bit pattern -- 4,278,190,080 values, 0 mismatches** -- before the shader was
touched, then confirmed on GPU by the new oracle.

**The `simd_max` rewrite subsumes the partial-block fix.** That bug existed
because a shared staging array's tail lanes went uninitialised on the final
block. Reducing the amax from a register removes the staging array altogether,
so the hazard is structurally impossible rather than guarded against. Both
commits are kept: the first is the minimal fix and explains the defect, the
second is the one that makes it unreachable.

## Verification

Per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, run at every commit:

```sh
make clean && make
make test
./ds4_test --all
./ds4_test --metal-kernels
make cpu        # then: rm -f ds4 ds4-server ds4-bench ds4-eval ds4-agent && make
```

All green on the rebased branch, zero warnings. `./ds4_test --all` is now **21
suites** (it was 13 before upstream added the GLM 5.3 and vision suites); three
skip for optional models this machine does not have
(`dspark-verify-depth`, `mtp-verify-depth`, `glm53-continued-prefill`).

Bit-exactness for each shader change was verified by running one
binary against the previous shader through the `DS4_METAL_*_SOURCE` overrides
(shaders are concatenated from `metal/*.metal` at runtime) and comparing greedy
output byte for byte. The override mechanism itself was confirmed by pointing
it at a deliberately broken file and observing the shader compile fail --
otherwise an A/B could silently compare a shader against itself.

## One thing a reviewer should know

`DS4_PREFILL_MAX_CHUNK` records a structural limit, not a tuned value: 8192 is
the largest chunk the graph can stage, because the raw KV cache is sized
`align_up(raw_window + prefill_cap, 256)` and clamped to 8192 rows. Verified
empirically -- 8192 runs, 8448 does not. Requests above it are now clamped with
a warning rather than aborting mid-encode.

## The remaining headroom is in neither review document

Decode is GPU-saturated (~98% busy) while moving roughly a quarter of the
achievable memory bandwidth on what is fundamentally a bandwidth operation.
That gap is the largest thing left on this hardware, and neither review
document covers it.

What it is *not*, as far as I can tell: a layout problem. Expert weights are
one tensor per layer -- `blk.N.ffn_gate_exps.weight` is `[4096, 2048, 256]` --
so each expert is a contiguous 4.46 MB slab. A token reads 18 such slabs per
layer (6 experts x gate/up/down), each a sequential multi-megabyte stream.
774 sequential reads per token is a well-behaved access pattern, so DRAM page
locality and TLB pressure are unlikely explanations, and dynamic gathering
into a contiguous staging buffer cannot help batch-1 decode at all: it would
read the same bytes, write them, then read them again.

The volume checks out -- 6 x 3 x 4.46 MB x 43 layers = 3.45 GB/token, about
150 GB/s at the measured decode rate -- but I have not measured what this
machine actually achieves for a sequential read, so "a quarter of achievable"
is inferred from spec rather than observed.

Three explanations remain and my data cannot separate them: the bandwidth
ceiling is lower than assumed, the expert access pattern costs more than its
shape suggests, or the MoE decode kernel is not bandwidth-saturating in the
first place. I would lean toward the third -- the winning decode configuration
is `NSG1`, which is a latency-oriented shape -- but that is a hypothesis, not
a finding.

The cheap way to settle it, before anyone builds anything: a microbenchmark
reading the same byte volume three ways -- purely sequential, in the expert
access pattern, and through the real kernel -- which separates ceiling from
pattern from kernel efficiency. If it turns out to be genuinely
bandwidth-bound, no kernel change helps and the lever is amortising the read
across more tokens, which this tree already has in MTP/speculative decode.

title: agent: accept --rocm in ROCm builds
body:
On a ROCm build `ds4-agent` disagrees with itself. The help, which it shares with the other tools, offers `--metal | --rocm | --cpu` and `Backend name: metal, rocm, or cpu`. The parser then refuses both:

```
$ ./ds4-agent --rocm --help
ds4-agent: unknown option: --rocm
$ ./ds4-agent --backend rocm --help
ds4-agent: invalid backend: rocm
```

`ds4_agent.c` has no `DS4_ROCM_BUILD` handling at all, while `ds4_cli.c:217` and `ds4_cli.c:1941` have carried it since the ROCm target landed. I copied that idiom instead of inventing a second one.

**This changes behaviour: a ROCm build now rejects `--cuda`.** ds4, ds4-server, ds4-bench and ds4-eval have always rejected it, so this makes ds4-agent consistent, but it breaks anyone who scripted `ds4-agent --cuda` on a ROCm box. If you would rather not break that, I can keep `--cuda` working as an undocumented alias instead.

```
GPU     AMD Radeon 780M (gfx1103), Ryzen 7 8845HS, 58 GiB usable RAM
OS      CachyOS, kernel 7.2.0-1-cachyos
ROCm    7.2.4
ds4     c1d4597 plus this commit
build   make rocm ROCM_ARCH=gfx1103 HIPCC="hipcc --rocm-path=/opt/rocm"
```

Both flags are accepted after the change, `--cuda` is rejected. I also built the default Metal target on an M4 Pro, 0 errors and 0 warnings, to check the non-ROCm side is untouched. No CUDA host here, so that path is compile-checked only.

title: cli: name only the backends the build actually has
body:
The message names three flags, but no build accepts all three.

`ds4_backend_supports_ssd_streaming` at `ds4.c:399` has four outcomes rather than two: ROCm, Linux CUDA, Apple, and `DS4_NO_GPU`. One message could not match all four, so it always named at least one flag the running binary rejects.

The clearest case is the default macOS build, where the predicate excludes CUDA through its `__APPLE__` arm. `ds4 --cuda --ssd-streaming` gets refused by a message that then suggests `--cuda`. On Linux the same line suggests `--metal`, which passes this check and dies 360 lines later at `ds4.c:57893` with "Metal backend requested but this build is linked with CUDA".

I should say I found this by reading the code, not by hitting it in a run. What I did check is what each build actually prints, by reading the strings back out of the binaries:

```
make       (M4 Pro, macOS)             ... only with --metal
make rocm  (Radeon 780M, ROCm 7.2.4)   ... only with --rocm
make cpu   (same Linux host)           requires a GPU build; this binary is CPU-only
```

Each arm now names one flag that works in that build, keyed off the same macros as the predicate. The `--ssd-streaming` help line had the same problem, listing Metal/CUDA/ROCm unconditionally three lines below an `#ifdef` that gets it right.

0 errors on all three builds. The ROCm one has a warning at `ds4_server.c:11329` that is there without my change. No CUDA host here, so that arm is compile-checked only.

title: readme: --ssd-streaming and --mtp cannot be combined
body:
The DSpark section says the main model may be resident or use `--ssd-streaming` on Metal. The code refuses that combination everywhere:

```
ds4.c:57822   --ssd-streaming is not compatible with --mtp yet
ds4.c:57454   --dspark requires --mtp FILE
```

Since `--dspark` needs `--mtp`, and `--mtp` is refused alongside streaming, DSpark never runs with a streamed main model on any backend.

There is a second case the old wording missed. The guard sits inside a `distributed.role == DS4_DISTRIBUTED_NONE` branch, and so does the `model_open` for the support model, so a distributed run takes neither path and drops `--mtp` without saying anything. The new text covers both.

Docs only, no code touched.

title: docs: bring-up notes for AMD parts outside the Strix Halo matrix
body:
This one is separate from #875, #876 and #877, and safe to close on its own: it adds a file and changes no code.

STRIXHALO.md covers Ubuntu, GRUB and gfx1151. Bringing the ROCm backend up on a Radeon 780M under CachyOS needed three things that are not in it, and none of the three failures points at its own cause:

1. `hipcc` calls `clang++` without the ROCm include directory, so every HIP source dies on `hip/hip_runtime.h` even though the header is sitting in `/opt/rocm/include`. `--rocm-path=/opt/rocm` fixes it.
2. rocWMMA 2.2.0 enumerates eleven architectures and gfx1103 is not one of them, although it has the same RDNA3 WMMA instructions as gfx1102. Aliasing the two is enough, and the AUR already carries a `rocwmma-gfx1103` package for this.
3. The GTT aperture comes from `LINUX_OPTIONS` in `sdboot-manage.conf` rather than grub, and `amdgpu.gttsize` is in MiB while `ttm.pages_limit` is in 4 KiB pages, so the two have to be worked out separately for the same size.

One thing in there is worth knowing even on a Strix Halo: override `HIPCC`, not `ROCM_CFLAGS`. `ROCM_CFLAGS` carries `--offload-arch=$(ROCM_ARCH)`, so replacing it wholesale makes `ROCM_ARCH` inert and pins the architecture to whatever string you copied. I did exactly that for an evening before noticing.

What I verified on this machine: `make rocm` builds, `make test-mxfp4-rocm` passes, `make cpu` still builds. What I did not: `make test`, which wants a model file. No published GGUF fits 58 GiB resident, so nothing has run end to end here, and the file says so in its first paragraph rather than reading like a support claim.

On provenance: the machine, the failures and the measurements are mine, and I used a coding agent to read the tree and cross-check what the file claims.

If you would rather not carry a file for a part outside your QA matrix, I understand. In that case tell me and I will move it to the ROCm discussion issue instead.

title: [Feature Request] ds4-server: support --nothink flag and generic model aliases for GLM 5.2
body:
Currently, ds4-server rejects the --nothink CLI flag and defaults to high-effort thinking for all unrecognized model names (such as glm-5.2). To disable thinking in GUI clients like Cherry Studio, one has to alias the model ID to deepseek-chat or pass custom JSON parameters (think=false).
Suggested improvements:
Allow passing --nothink or --default-thinking none/high/max directly to ds4-server at launch.
Support standard OpenAI/client flags like enable_thinking: false or reasoning_effort: "none" in /v1/chat/completions.

title: CUDA single GPU: --gpu-vram + --ssd-streaming refused as "multi-GPU placement" (misleading message)
body:
## Summary

On a **single** CUDA GPU, passing an explicit `--gpu-vram N` together with `--ssd-streaming` refuses to start with:

```
ds4: --ssd-streaming is not compatible with multi-GPU placement
```

There is no multi-GPU placement — one device, one budget. The message sent us down the wrong path twice before we found the working invocation (drop `--gpu-vram`, streaming manages VRAM itself).

## Environment

- RunPod pod, 1× RTX 3090 24 GB (sm_86), driver 580.65.06, 251 GB RAM
- `make cuda CUDA_ARCH=sm_86`, commit `c1d4597`
- Model: `ds4f-q2` (81 GB)

## Repro

```sh
./ds4-server -m ./ds4flash.gguf --cuda --ssd-streaming --gpu-vram 21 --ctx 8192   # refused
./ds4-server -m ./ds4flash.gguf --cuda --ssd-streaming --ctx 8192                 # works
```

## Where it comes from (reading the source)

With an explicit budget, `engine_classify_multi_tier()` runs the placement: an 81 GB model against a 21 GB budget classifies most layers as CPU-spill entries, the placement becomes tiered, and `e->multi_tier` turns on with a single GPU. The guard at `ds4.c:57748` then fires, but its message names multi-GPU rather than the real condition (explicit budget produced a tiered placement that streaming does not support).

## Suggested fix (either is fine)

- Message: say what happened — e.g. `--ssd-streaming does not support tiered placement; with an explicit --gpu-vram budget smaller than the model, layers spill to CPU. Drop --gpu-vram to let streaming manage VRAM.`
- Or behavior: with `n_gpus == 1` and streaming requested, ignore the explicit budget (with a log line) instead of refusing.

Happy to send a small PR for the message variant if useful.

title: CUDA --ssd-streaming: illegal memory access at first 2048-token prefill in ds4-bench (RTX 3090, layer-major FFN encode)
body:
## Summary

`ds4-bench` with CUDA `--ssd-streaming` crashes with an **illegal memory access at the very first prefill** (2048 tokens), on a plain RTX 3090. The failing stage is the layer-major streaming prefill, FFN encode of layer 2. Reproduced 3/3 runs; while a `ds4-server` on the same build, same box, same model serves short-prompt chat completions for hours without issue (we ran one idle for 4 h during the #836 measurement).

Likely the same family as the mid-prefill poisoning on GB10 (#759 / #847), but this signature is different: consumer sm_86, first prefill of a fresh process, deterministic, and reachable with the project's own bench tool — so it may be the easiest handle on this class of bug so far.

## Environment (per CONTRIBUTING.md)

- RunPod pod, 1× RTX 3090 24 GB (sm_86), driver 580.65.06, 251 GB RAM
- `make cuda CUDA_ARCH=sm_86`, CUDA 12.4 toolkit, commit `c1d4597`
- Model quant: `ds4f-q2` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-...-0731, 81 GB)

## Repro (deterministic, 3/3)

```sh
./ds4-bench -m ./ds4flash.gguf --cuda --ssd-streaming \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt \
  --ctx-start 2048 --ctx-max 8192 --step-incr 2048 \
  --gen-tokens 64 --csv /tmp/speed.csv
```

Output:

```
ds4: CUDA model range alloc failed for hc_scale (0.00 MiB): an illegal memory access was encountered
ds4: CUDA model range copy failed for hc_base at 0.00 MiB: an illegal memory access was encountered
ds4: CUDA model range alloc failed for hc_base (0.00 MiB): an illegal memory access was encountered
ds4: gpu layer 2 ffn batch encode failed
ds4: gpu layer-major prefill layer 2 encode failed
ds4: CUDA synchronize failed: an illegal memory access was encountered
ds4-bench: prefill to 2048 failed: cuda prefill failed
```

(The `model range alloc failed` lines are the poisoned-context cascade; the first IMA happens earlier in the layer-major prefill.)

## Notes

- Identical behavior on unpatched `c1d4597` and with PR #872 applied — that patch is host-side shape validation in the attention prefill fallback and is unrelated; mentioning it only because we found this crash while trying to run the before/after bench for that PR.
- Without `--ssd-streaming` the model cannot fit a 24 GB card (arena alloc OOM), so on this class of hardware the bench currently has no working path.
- Happy to run diagnostics on a rented pod if a compute-sanitizer trace or an env-var A/B (`DS4_CUDA_NO_TOPK_STREAM`, etc.) would help — CUDA 13.0 compute-sanitizer works on these drivers, the 12.4 one does not start.

title: kvstore: reject disk KV checkpoints written under different model weights (#805)
body:
Fixes #805.

## What

`ds4_engine_model_id()` returns the compile-time model variant, so the 1-byte `model_id` in the disk KV cache header identifies the model *shape*, not the weights: two GGUFs with the same structure — the issue's official-vs-Huihui case, or any requant — share it, and a checkpoint written under one set of weights is silently restored under another.

Following the header's own compatibility pattern:

- **`ds4_engine_weights_fp24()`** — a 24-bit FNV-1a fingerprint of the loaded weights: file size, tensor count, and the head of *every* tensor (so no single-tensor edit slips between samples). A few hundred 64-byte `pread`s, once per engine, off the hot path; reads via the descriptor so it also works under SSD streaming where the mapping is partial on purpose.
- Stored in the **free header bytes 21..23** (no version bump, no layout change).
- Every restore path rejects on mismatch with a clear reason (`cached checkpoint was written for different model weights`): `ds4_kvstore_try_load_text`, the agent checkpoint restore, the server tool-map scan, prefix lookup, and the continued-supersede check.
- **Headers written before the fingerprint carry 0 there and stay accepted**, mirroring the `model_id` 0 rule documented in `ds4_kvstore.h` — existing caches keep working, protection applies to checkpoints written from now on.

## Limits (stated, not hidden)

- 24 bits: a 1-in-16M chance that two different weight sets collide, versus the current 100%. If a full-width fingerprint is preferred, it needs a `KV_CACHE_VERSION` bump and a wider field — happy to do that variant instead if you'd rather.
- Legacy (fingerprint-0) checkpoints remain loadable by design; a stricter mode could refuse them, but that would invalidate every existing cache on upgrade.

## Validation (per CONTRIBUTING.md)

- Machine: Linux x86_64, CPU build (`make cpu`, `-DDS4_NO_GPU`), commit `c1d4597`. This change touches no inference path — header bytes, lookup filters and one sampling pass at engine init — so no backend regression surface; `make cpu` builds warning-free.
- New regression tests in the server unit group (`./ds4_test --server`, all green):
  - `test_weights_fp24_of_fd_tells_weights_apart`: two files identical except one tensor byte → different fingerprints; same bytes → same fingerprint (the issue's scenario in miniature);
  - `test_kv_cache_lookup_rejects_wrong_weights`: lookup skips a checkpoint fingerprinted under other weights, still returns its own, still accepts a legacy 0-fingerprint entry.
- Mutation check: breaking the header parse on purpose turns the new test red.
- Not run here: `--logprob-vectors` / `--long-context` (need the model GGUF; no weights on this machine). The change does not touch tokenization, attention or logits.

title: engine: clearer refusal when --ssd-streaming meets a single-GPU --gpu-vram budget (#880)
body:
Fixes #880.

With one CUDA device, an explicit `--gpu-vram` budget smaller than the model classifies the remaining layers as CPU spill, the placement becomes multi-tier, and the streaming guard refuses with *"not compatible with multi-GPU placement"* — on a machine with a single GPU. That message sent us hunting for a phantom second device (repro in #880: two commands, one flag apart).

Message-only change, per the issue's first suggested fix: when `gpu_cfg->n_gpus == 1` the refusal now names the real condition and the way out (drop `--gpu-vram\`, streaming manages VRAM itself). Actual multi-GPU placements keep the existing wording. No behavior change — the guard still refuses exactly the same configurations.

Validation: `make cpu` builds warning-free on commit `c1d4597`; the touched code is a refusal path with no inference surface. Verified the exact refusal text on an RTX 3090 pod while working #836 (that is how the issue was found).

title: cuda: fix illegal memory access on long sessions with indexed attention and support models
body:
### Summary

Fixes an `illegal memory access` crash encountered on CUDA backends (specifically reproducible on NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10 `sm_121` during long context generation sessions with speculative decoding).

### Root Causes & Fixes

1. **Scratch Buffer Collision in Multi-Token Indexed Attention**:
   - `ds4_gpu_attention_indexed_mixed_batch_heads_tensor` previously allocated the sorted top-k array using `cuda_tmp_alloc_on` (`g_cuda_tmp`).
   - Immediately following attention, output projection kernels (`ds4_gpu_attention_output_low_dense_quant_tensor`) reused `g_cuda_tmp`, overwriting sorted indices with quantized activations while the asynchronous attention kernel was actively reading them.
   - **Fix**: Added a dedicated, dynamically resized scratch buffer (`indexed_topk_sort_scratch_ensure`) for top-k sort that does not alias `g_cuda_tmp`.

2. **`UINT32_MAX` Sentinel Handling in Online Attention**:
   - On long contexts (>32k tokens, $n_{\text{comp}} > 8192$), `ds4_gpu_indexer_topk_tensor` uses chunked tree-merge reductions which use `UINT32_MAX` as padding sentinels.
   - Unlike the offline indexed attention kernel, `attention_indexed_mixed_heads8_online_kernel` directly dereferenced `topk[...]` without clamping.
   - **Fix**: Clamped `comp_idx` to `[0, visible_comp)` before indexing `comp_kv`.

3. **Support Model Device Pointer Resolution**:
   - In `cuda_model_range_ptr`, when `g_model_device_owned == 1`, pointer lookup unconditionally bypassed range tables even for secondary support models (`dspark_model`), returning host mmap pointers.
   - **Fix**: Restricted device-owned bypass to `model_map == g_model_host_base`.

### Validation
- Validated against DGX Spark / GB10 hardware for long session generations past 32k tokens.

title: server: reject NaN float arguments
body:
`parse_float_arg()` validates with a range comparison:

```c
if (!s[0] || *end || v < minv || v > maxv) {
```

Every comparison against NaN is false, so `nan` passes **both** bounds checks and is accepted. `inf` and `-inf` are already rejected, since `inf > maxv` and `-inf < minv` hold — NaN is the only value that slips through.

Reproduced against current `main`:

| argument | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `--mtp-margin nan` | **accepted**, `engine.mtp_margin = NaN` | rejected |
| `--mtp-margin inf` | rejected | rejected |
| `--mtp-margin -inf` | rejected | rejected |
| `--mtp-margin 0.5` | accepted | accepted |
| `--mtp-margin 2000` | rejected | rejected |

The NaN reaches the engine rather than failing at the boundary, where it propagates silently through whatever arithmetic consumes it.

Affected flags: `--mtp-margin`, `--glm-mtp`, `--directional-steering-ffn`, `--directional-steering-attn`.

The fix adds `!isfinite(v)`, which rejects NaN at parse time and leaves every other case unchanged. `math.h` is already included, so there is no new dependency.

Builds clean with no new warnings on macOS/Metal (`make ds4-server`).

title: cli: add --version to every binary
body:
There is currently no way to ask a built binary what it is. The five tools report nothing identifying, so a binary that has outlived its checkout — or was copied to another machine — cannot be matched back to a commit.

This matters for anyone keeping benchmark results: a number is only interpretable if the build that produced it can be identified later, and `ds4-server`'s mtime is a poor substitute.

Adds `--version` to `ds4`, `ds4-server`, `ds4-bench`, `ds4-eval` and `ds4-agent`. The string is computed **once** in the Makefile:

```make
DS4_VERSION ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
```

and passed to each translation unit that needs it, so every tool from a single build reports the same value:

```
$ ./ds4-server --version
ds4-server c1d4597-dirty
$ ./ds4-agent --version
ds4-agent c1d4597-dirty
```

An `#ifndef DS4_VERSION` fallback keeps the files compiling standalone if the define is absent, and `?=` means a packager can override it (`make DS4_VERSION=1.2.3`).

The flag is handled next to `--help`, before any other parsing, so it works without a model or a valid configuration.

All five binaries build clean with no new warnings on macOS/Metal.

Independent of #885, which touches the same file but a different function.

title: ROCm: optimize DeepSeek V4 Flash prefill and DSpark on gfx1151
body:
This PR adds gfx1151 performance optimizations for DeepSeek V4 Flash IQ2 inference and DSpark, primarily targeting prefill and speculative decoding. The optimized paths are selected automatically; no performance environment variables are required.

## Performance

Measured with ROCm 10.0 and rocBLAS `5.6.0.8d1ae90e` on a Framework Desktop with Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128 GB unified memory, up to 124 GB iGPU GTT, and `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731.gguf`.

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| 4,096-token prefill | 187.26 tok/s | 292.86 tok/s |
| ROCm 10.0 DSpark 4,096-token prefill | 153.52 tok/s | 293.09 tok/s |
| DSpark, 50 generated tokens on a short C coding prompt with high proposal acceptance | 15.23-15.24 tok/s | 24.83-24.86 tok/s |
| DSpark default scheduler, 2,048-token source-code prompt, 128 generated tokens | 15.57 tok/s | 20.58 tok/s |
| Ordinary decode | 16.87 tok/s | 16.87 tok/s |

The source-code workload is a plain-text prompt containing an excerpt of LLVM 22.1.6 source files. LLVM is not built or executed; its source is used only as representative coding context for speculative decoding.

## Main changes

- Routed-MoE prefill uses the four-wave wave32 `x64/y64` IQ2 MMQ tile selected by the production-shape sweep. In the isolated 2,048-token gate/up test it takes 34.435 ms versus 51.586 ms for the `x128/y128` reference, a 33.2% reduction. The launch bounds each expert by `n_tokens` instead of `n_tokens * top_k`, and larger IQ2 batches are processed in bounded 2,048-row tiles.
- Prefill attention uses 32-head wave32 rocWMMA kernels and an 80-key online-attention tile; the indexed path also vectorizes F32-to-F16 KV staging. A separate `4096 x 2048 x 8192` F16 rocWMMA kernel handles the large attention-output-B projection, reducing that live call from 25.89 to 11.88 ms and producing an 8.9% end-to-end gain at warm 4,096-token prefill within the tuning stack.
- Other retained prefill paths use output-shape-specific Q8 row tiles, vectorized Q8 activation staging, native-F16 rocWMMA kernels for the measured M=24, M=64/256/512/1024 and M=8192 projections, and cooperative Q2_K weight staging once per 256-value K slab. These are exact production-shape dispatches; unmatched shapes keep their existing paths.
- Greedy DSpark drafts five tokens from the previous target hidden state, prepends the current target token and verifies all six rows in one target batch. Full and partial accepts commit the captured verifier prefix directly. When five rows are accepted before the sixth rejects, DS4 restores the four-row prefix and evaluates only the fifth accepted row instead of replaying all five.
- The gfx1151 target verifier uses the native tile-4 IQ2 gate/up kernel, one-wave Q8_1 MMVQ for dense projections, eight independent Q8_1 MMVQs for grouped attention-output A, and a fused 128-thread Q2_K down-plus-sum kernel. The dense-Q8, grouped-attention and fused-down specializations are gated to target verification because extending them to the five-row support-model stages was slower. The proposal stage separately moves confidence-zero greedy Markov-plus-argmax to the GPU and skips confidence scoring when the configured threshold is zero.
- rocBLAS solution indices are selected only for known library builds and exact shapes. rocBLAS `5.5.0.cd957402` in ROCm 7.14 uses `-217/-216`; `5.6.0.8d1ae90e` in ROCm 10.0 uses `-50/-49`, plus `-401` for the N=5/N=6 `4096 x N x 8192` attention-B projection. `-401` is 1.30x faster in isolation and cuts verifier time per cycle by about 14%. Unknown builds, unsupported shapes and rejected solutions fall back silently to the default rocBLAS path. Matching performance on another rocBLAS build may require retuning these solution choices.
- The gfx1151 scheduler observes 16 speculative cycles because the measured workload begins with a low-acceptance phase before reaching repeated full accepts. It then bypasses DSpark for the remainder of a low-acceptance request, while profitable requests remain speculative. This policy is automatic and independent of the optional rocBLAS solution override; other backends retain their existing four-cycle behavior.
- Loading the DSpark support model no longer evicts the resident target weight cache, removing the roughly 2x DSpark prefill regression. `ds4-bench` now accepts the DSpark support model and restores local sweep frontiers from session snapshots so prefill intervals are measured without untimed prefix replay.

## Validation

The final ROCm 10.0 build reaches 20.58 tok/s aggregate and 21.53 tok/s steady while generating 128 tokens from that fixed 2,048-token source-code prompt, with 270.98 tok/s prefill in the same process. The verifier-depth test commits 128 speculative tokens at draft depth five with zero argmax gap. Deterministic C, mathematics, Python and prose prompts exercise full, partial and one-row prefix-extension commits with zero verifier errors. All five binaries build and pass smoke tests.

Correctness was checked with `score_official` built from each exact DS4 revision, using the official 100-case Flash manifest at context 4096. Every run completed all 100 cases and 2,313 target tokens with no incomplete or non-finite result.

| Platform and revision | Average NLL | First-token matches | Average greedy prefix |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ROCm 10.0, pre-optimization baseline | 0.402107528 | 55/100 | 4.650 |
| ROCm 10.0, this PR | 0.403662338 | 55/100 | 4.690 |
| CUDA 13.0 on NVIDIA DGX Spark, pre-optimization baseline | 0.404811251 | 55/100 | 5.150 |
| CUDA 13.0 on NVIDIA DGX Spark, this PR | 0.404811251 | 55/100 | 5.150 |

The pre-optimization baseline is commit `c1d4597a80e300b803dc642519718f2c999589da`, the exact parent of the first performance commit. On ROCm, average NLL changes by +0.387%, API top-1 agreement changes from 85.863% to 85.949%, and pair-order agreement changes from 98.665% to 98.686%. On CUDA 13.0, the baseline and this PR produce byte-identical scorer TSVs, confirming that the changes do not alter the CUDA arithmetic path.

Terminal Bench Mini is currently running against this PR. Its results will be added when complete; this is the long-horizon check for whether the small ROCm scorer divergence still preserves quality on coding and agentic tasks.

Ordinary SSD streaming remains supported and passes a 512-token tuned-IQ2 prefill run. DSpark cannot currently be combined with SSD streaming.

title: GLM-5.3-Flash Metal: prefill fails for prompts > 4096 tokens (compact indexed path) — HTTP 500 'metal GLM-5.3 prefill failed at token 0'
body:
## Summary

On the `glm-5.3-flash` branch (a60a2a0), GLM 5.3 Flash on **Metal** fails to prefill any prompt longer than **4096 tokens**. Short prompts work fine. This breaks any long-context use (e.g. 50K-token prompts) on the very hardware the branch advertises (128GB M-series).

## Environment

- Machine: MacBook Pro M5 Max, 128 GB unified memory, macOS 27
- Backend: Metal
- Branch: `glm-5.3-flash` @ `a60a2a0` ("Add GLM 5.3 Flash inference")
- Model: `antirez/glm-5.3-flash-gguf` → `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf` (~90 GiB, resident)

## Repro

```sh
./ds4-server -m gguf/GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf --metal --ctx 1000000 --port 4005
```

Then POST a chat completion with a prompt of N tokens (N varied below):

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4005/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say OK. <N tokens>"}],"max_tokens":5}'
```

## Results

| Prompt tokens | HTTP | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 3000 | 200 | ok |
| 4096 | 200 | ok |
| **5000** | **500** | `{"error":{"message":"metal GLM-5.3 prefill failed at token 0","type":"invalid_request_error"}}` |
| 8000+ | 500 | same |

Fails in ~2s regardless of size — it's an immediate path failure, not an OOM/timeout.

## Server log (successful boot)

```
ds4: GLM session ctx=1000000 (model max=1048576); full-attention prefill/work cap=4096; compact indexed decode is used beyond the cap
ds4: GLM graph allocating full-attention KV cache: work_ctx=4096 layers=0:44 (45) f16 2.75 GiB
ds4: GLM graph allocating compact DSA cache: rows=1000000 logical_ctx=1000000 kv_layers=45 indexer_layers=11 f16 11.15 GiB
```

The 4096 boundary matches `full-attention prefill/work cap=4096`; the **compact indexed prefill path** (used beyond the cap) is what fails on Metal.

## Expected

Prompts up to `--ctx` (here 1M) should prefill. A 50K-token prompt is the advertised use case on 128GB machines.

## Notes

- Also observed: at `--ctx 1000000 --mtp` the server OOMs Metal during decode (`kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory` at layer 44 'FFN mHC expand'); at `--ctx 512000 --mtp` it works. MTP is not the primary issue here — the >4096 prefill failure happens with MTP off.
- Related: #595/#608 are the same compact-indexed prefill signature on CUDA/ROCm for GLM-5.2.

title: GLM-5.2 Metal + --ssd-streaming: compact indexer warmup fails for prompts > 8192 tokens ("model range not covered by mapped model views")
body:
## Summary

On Metal with `--ssd-streaming`, GLM-5.2 (`GLM-5.2-UD-Q2_K_RoutedQ2K.gguf`) fails at prompt-processing time whenever the prompt exceeds the full-attention prefill/work cap (8192 tokens). Prefill reaches 100%, then the compact indexed path fails its warmup:

```
ds4: Metal model range 2.29..2.29 GiB is not covered by mapped model views
ds4: Metal model range 2.29..2.29 GiB is not covered by mapped model views
ds4: prompt processing failed: metal GLM compact indexer warmup failed
```

Prompts under the cap work fine on the same setup (generation happily runs past position 8192, so compact indexed *decode* seems fine — only the compact indexed *prefill* warmup fails).

## Environment

- MacBook Pro M5 Max, 128 GB unified memory, internal SSD
- macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), binaries built arm64 native (`arch -arm64 make`)
- ds4 @ c1d4597a80e300b803dc642519718f2c999589da (latest main as of filing)
- Model: `GLM-5.2-UD-Q2_K_RoutedQ2K.gguf` (244 GB, from `./download_model.sh glm-antirez-q2`)

## Repro

```
./ds4 -m gguf/GLM-5.2-UD-Q2_K_RoutedQ2K.gguf --metal --ssd-streaming \
  --prompt-file prompt.txt -n 9000 --temp 0.7 -c 32000
```

Results by prompt size (same flags otherwise, only `-c` varied to fit):

| prompt tokens | ctx (`-c`) | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 827 | 16 000 | ✅ works — 47.5 t/s prefill, 3.1 t/s gen, ran well past position 8192 |
| 5 137 | 18 000 | ✅ works |
| 8 777 | 20 000 | ❌ `metal GLM compact indexer warmup failed` |
| 18 509 | 32 000 | ❌ same |
| 84 449 | 115 000 | ❌ same (prefill reports 100% first) |

The startup log on the working runs shows the boundary explicitly:

```
ds4: GLM session ctx=16000 (model max=1048576); full-attention prefill/work cap=8192; compact indexed decode is used beyond the cap
ds4: GLM compact indexed prefill chunk=4096 score_rows=4096 score_scratch=250.00 MiB
```

## Notes

- DeepSeek V4 Flash on the same machine/build is unaffected: an 84 449-token prompt prefills and generates fine (both the q2 and q2-q4 GGUFs, fully resident in RAM).
- Possibly related: #890 (GLM-5.3-Flash Metal, prompts > 4096, compact indexed path), #595 (CUDA) and #608 (ROCm) GLM prefill failures with `--ssd-streaming`. The "model range X..X GiB is not covered by mapped model views" message (zero-length range) suggests the compact indexer requests a mapping the streaming views never cover.

Happy to run patched builds or add instrumentation if useful — the machine and model stay available.

title: GLM-5.3 Flash on M5 Max: bring-up measurements + K-width speculative MTP (DS4_GLM_MTP_WIDTH)
body:
# GLM-5.3 Flash on M5 Max: bring-up measurements + K-width speculative MTP (DS4_GLM_MTP_WIDTH)

Brings upstream `glm-5.3-flash` up on an M5 Max 128 GB and adds a working K-width speculative decode cycle for GLM-5.3's nextn MTP block, measured honestly against the upstream width-2 path.

## Measured baseline (M5 Max, Q2 GGUF, ctx 8192, greedy `--temp 0`)

| mode | prefill | decode |
|---|---|---|
| serial | 76–80 t/s (474 t/s @ 4500-tok prompt) | 33.0 t/s |
| `--mtp` (width 2, upstream) | same | **40.5 t/s** |

MTP acceptance 89.6% over 135 cycles, verify2 median 37.4 ms, head+draft ~6 ms. `make test-glm53-kda` PASS. Greedy goldens byte-identical across serial / `--mtp` / wide-MTP at widths 3, 4, 6.

## What's in the box

**`glm_graph_mtp_step` gains a `raw_hidden` mode.** Chained drafts consume the previous nextn step's own output hidden instead of the target's hc state. Two non-obvious correctness constraints, both load-bearing:

1. The snapshot of `g->next` must be taken *before* the embed stage overwrites it with the next-token embedding — a snapshot in the hnorm stage silently feeds the draft model its own token embedding as "hidden" and produces garbage drafts (symptom: `!defdef`-style doubled tokens).
2. The nextn KV slots at `pos..pos+rows-1` must be populated by the previous cycle's chain steps. Fresh seeding steps are skipped by default (`DS4_GLM_MTP_SEED_STEPS=1` restores) because accepted slots already hold the correct entries, and stale slots after a reject only degrade draft quality — every draft is re-verified, so output correctness never depends on them.

**`ds4_session_glm_spec_cycle_wide`**: verifies `first_token` + K−1 drafts in one layer-major forward (`glm_graph_forward_tokens` / indexed variant), scores every row through the shared head, commits the matching prefix, and on reject restores the KDA snapshot and replays the accepted prefix as a batch. Dispatched only when `DS4_GLM_MTP_WIDTH > 2`; the default path is bit-identical to upstream.

**`DS4_GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK`** env override for prefill chunk diagnostics (1024/2048/4096 ABBA: 451/437/449 t/s median — noise-level; default unchanged).

## Findings (why the default stays width 2)

- **Decode is dispatch/latency-bound on this model**: a 2-token forward costs 1.23× a one-token forward (37.4 ms vs 30.3 ms). Speculative *width*, not kernel speed, is the lever — consistent with the Qwen3.8 finding that n_tok=2 is near-flat.
- Depth-2 draft acceptance is only ~45% (vs 89.6% at depth 1) even with correct raw chaining, and every reject costs a KDA restore + prefix replay (a second full forward). Per-token cost: W=3 → 30.6 t/s, W=4 → 20.8, W=6 → 16 — all worse than width 2.
- The wide machinery is kept because it flips profitable the moment KDA state supports per-row checkpointing (the reject tax disappears).
- Rejected with evidence: relaxing the `n_expert == 6` gate on `kernel_mul_mm_id_iq2_xxs_pair_swiglu_f16` to GLM's 8/288 fanout (bit-identical output, prefill ABBA median 296 vs 304 t/s — the fused epilogue only pays off at DSV4's 6-of-256).

`next-step.md` has the full measurement log: per-stage decode/prefill profiles, the flush-interval and indexed-decode null results, and MTP cycle math.

## Verification

- `make test-glm53-kda` PASS (GPU unit test for the KDA kernels).
- Greedy goldens: serial == `--mtp` == widths 3/4/6, byte-identical (`cmp`).
- Default width-2 path exercised end-to-end on the 90 GiB Q2 GGUF at ctx 8192 and on a 4500-token prompt.

## Not included

DFlash2 draft support for GLM-5.3: the draft GGUFs exist (qwen3-arch, same tokenizer) but this branch has no dflash2 machinery — it lives in `origin/ornith15`, bound to the Qwen graph. A port is scoped in `next-step.md` as a separate feature branch; the in-GGUF nextn MTP remains the draft mechanism here.
