title: ROCm build fails: host-side `rsqrtf()` in `rocm/ds4_rocm_deepseek4_vision.cuh`
body:
I've been rebasing a shared-library `ds4`  fork which includes CI/CD and test Docker images.  My latest rebase picked up this `rocm` build issue that creeped up in recent work.

Posting the LLM summary, but in the end it is a one-line code change for `rsqrtf`.

----

## Summary

`make rocm` (and `make strix-halo`) no longer compiles on ROCm 7.2.4. The
DeepSeek Vision-Exp ROCm path added in e976a54 calls `rsqrtf()` from host code,
but under HIP `rsqrtf` is only declared as a `__device__` function, so hipcc
rejects the call.

## Environment

- Upstream `main` at 6289c51 (pristine checkout, no local changes)
- Ubuntu 24.04, ROCm 7.2.4 (`/opt/rocm-7.2.4`, clang 22), `--offload-arch=gfx1151`
- `make rocm ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151`

## Error

```
/opt/rocm/bin/hipcc -O3 -ffast-math -g -fno-finite-math-only -pthread -D__HIP_PLATFORM_AMD__ -Wno-unused-command-line-argument --offload-arch=gfx1151 -c -o ds4_rocm.o ds4_rocm.cu
In file included from ds4_rocm.cu:181:
./rocm/ds4_rocm_deepseek4_vision.cuh:239:25: error: no matching function for call to 'rsqrtf'
  239 |     const float alpha = rsqrtf((float)head_dim);
      |                         ^~~~~~
/opt/rocm-7.2.4/lib/llvm/lib/clang/22/include/__clang_hip_math.h:671:7: note: candidate function not viable: call to __device__ function from __host__ function
  671 | float rsqrtf(float __x) { return __ocml_rsqrt_f32(__x); }
      |       ^
1 error generated when compiling for gfx1151.
make[1]: *** [Makefile:521: ds4_rocm.o] Error 1
make: *** [Makefile:223: strix-halo] Error 2
```

## Cause

The call is in `ds4_gpu_attention_visual_mixed_batch_heads_tensor()`, computing
the cuBLAS/hipBLAS `alpha` scale on the host before
`cublasSgemmStridedBatched`. CUDA's host math headers provide a host `rsqrtf`,
so this compiles with nvcc, but glibc has no `rsqrtf` and HIP only supplies the
device overload. The other `rsqrtf` uses in `rocm/ds4_rocm_attention.cuh` are
inside kernels and are fine.

## Fix

Use a plain reciprocal square root for the host-side scale:

```diff
--- a/rocm/ds4_rocm_deepseek4_vision.cuh
+++ b/rocm/ds4_rocm_deepseek4_vision.cuh
@@ -236,7 +236,7 @@
     if (!cuda_ok(cudaGetLastError(), "visual attention KV pack launch"))
         return 0;
 
-    const float alpha = rsqrtf((float)head_dim);
+    const float alpha = 1.0f / sqrtf((float)head_dim);
     const float beta = 0.0f;
     cublasStatus_t status = cublasSgemmStridedBatched(
```

With this change `make rocm ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151` builds cleanly in the same
container. Happy to send it as a PR if you prefer.

title: kvstore: stamp checkpoints with a behavioral tokenizer fingerprint
body:
Supersedes #983 (GitHub refuses reopen after the rebase force-push; same branch, rebased onto current main - merge cost was one trivial hunk).

**Problem.** A checkpoint saved by a different tokenizer build (or a different gguf vocab - both happened to me in production: a model-file migration produced four foreign-vocab restores that the text-keyed tiers trusted, each one a multi-thousand-token silent corruption or a pinned re-prefill loop) restores without complaint and then poisons every following turn.

**Fix.** The engine computes `ds4_engine_tokenizer_fingerprint()` once: a hash over n_vocab, every token's length+bytes in id order, the merge-rank table contents, and a small **append-only behavioral probe set** run through the real tokenizer - covering data *and* pre-tokenizer code change with no human-maintained version constant. Every save writes it as the first trailer section (TOKFP, auxiliary ext bit 1<<5, so key_kind and existing consumers are untouched); the loader pre-checks it with a 16-byte seek **before** touching the payload and rejects mismatched files, leaving the session untouched so the ordinary fallback chain walks to the next candidate or a cold rebuild, which rewrites fresh under the key. Unstamped legacy files remain trusted (status quo ante).

Design note carried from #983's review: @JordiPosthumus caught that the first version hashed the raw `ds4_str` array (pointers) - restart-stable on my machine by luck, wrong on any other allocator layout. The shipped version hashes content only; regressions: two fresh processes print identical fp (`e467e62ceeadf47e`), a single-byte flip in a clone of the model file changes it (`5f83c7a25a3b184e`).

**Validation:** production soak since #983: the stamp paid for itself during a model-file migration - one bounded cold rebuild, zero silent corruption after. Cross-restart restore of a 32768-token grid: 69 ms, zero mismatches.

## CONTRIBUTING.md compliance

- Machine / backend / model: Apple M5 Max, 128 GB, Metal, Qwen3.8 Flash Next Q4_K (production config), default `make` build.
- Commands run on the current head (`5915b7b`, merged with latest main): `make clean && make` (clean build, no warnings), `./ds4_test --server` -> `server: OK`, `./ds4_test --metal-kernels` -> ok. (`make test` additionally needs `ds4flash.gguf` for the logprob-vector track; the model-backed groups were not re-run for this change, which touches the disk-cache trailer/key path, not inference or tokenization.)
- Notable failures: none.
- Response to @emilianbold's review (what needs fingerprinting): see the comment thread — the probe set is append-only and covers vocab data *and* pre-tokenizer code paths via the real tokenizer; happy to add specific probes if you have a drift case in mind.

title: server: auto-discard reload-loop checkpoints (frontier-contradicted)
body:
**Problem.** The text-keyed disk tier validates text, not tokens. When a checkpoint's stored tail diverges from how future prompts re-tokenize the same bytes (BPE boundary variants across sampled thinking/DSML regions - the familiar two-variant equilibrium), the file restores fine, misses again next turn, and re-restores forever: pinned `reason=token-mismatch` at the same `common=` on every following turn, growing re-prefill each time. Production evidence from my fork running this same tier: clusters at common=118557 (43 turns), 273833 (18), 451784, 325177 - the only cure observed was a manual turn-abort, which routes through the existing prefill-failed discard and lets the fallback chain land on a lower valid file.

**Fix.** Same recovery, automated and provable: each slot remembers its last disk-restored (file, frontier). A second consecutive restore of the **same file at the same depth** means the session cannot have advanced between restores - the tail is dead weight by construction. Unlink it under `kv_mu` (exactly the prefill-failed discard semantics already in this file), log `reason=frontier-contradicted`, and retry the load once: the refresh pass walks to the next candidate or a cold rebuild, which rewrites fresh under the key. Any successful memory-tier continuation clears the tracker, so legitimate re-restores of the same correct file after real progress are never punished; disagreement falls back to today's behavior verbatim.

**Blast radius:** ~40 lines, one helper beside `kv_cache_discard_failed_disk_entry`, one two-attempt loop at the existing call site, one clear on memory-tier success. No format, no key, no session-state changes; worst case is one wasted reload per poisoned file instead of an unbounded loop.

**Validation:** optimized build clean (0 errors/0 warnings, M5 Max); ds4-server unit suite green on this head; the mechanism it automates (unlink + invalidate + fallback walk + fresh re-store) is the same one two production manual-abort recoveries exercised end-to-end, and the fork build with the automated detection self-healed two live loops on its first day (discarded at frontier 322155 -> adopted 321371 same second; 338690 -> 331026 same second).

title: server: opt-in auto-reduction of over-budget image histories (DS4_VISION_KEEP_IMAGES)
body:
Supersedes #971 (rebased onto current main as `fa0af86`; the encode-loop hunk auto-merged with 81a7658, only the doc moved from README to docs/SERVER.md).

**Why.** Coding agents that screenshot per tool round accumulate image histories past the 16-image default and get hard 400s at exactly the moments the context matters most. Dropping the oldest images is what the model's own context window would do anyway - but that's a lossy policy change, so it stays strictly opt-in: unset env = today's reject-400 behavior verbatim (with an error message that now hints at the knob).

**What.** `DS4_VISION_KEEP_IMAGES=N` (1..1024, validated once; invalid values log a warning and fall back to reject): keep the last N images, splice a fixed visible note over each dropped sentinel in the prompt text so the transcript stays coherent (`[oldest image omitted to fit the vision budget]`), and serve. Cache identity is unaffected (markers are canonicalized, and the reduction is deterministic for a given history length, so disk tiers key consistently).

**Validation (this head):** clean optimized build, ds4-server unit suite green; live on M5 Max: keep=16 with a 20-image request served with kept 16 / omitted 4, invalid env value warned and rejected, 17 rejected by default with the hint, keep=2 worked, and the production session ran 128-image-budget turns for a week (130 -> kept 128 / omitted 2 on the largest replay).


## CONTRIBUTING.md compliance

- Machine / backend / model: Apple M5 Max, 128 GB, Metal, Qwen3.8 Flash Next Q4_K + vision encoder (mmproj Q8_0).
- Commands run on the head (`fa0af86`): `make clean && make` (clean build), `./ds4_test --server` -> ok. Production: the flag is in daily use on a screenshot-per-round agent loop; it turned the former hard 400 into a lossy-but-working reduction, and @Flor1an-B independently reproduced the before/after behaviour (table in the comment thread).
- No inference backend is touched (server-side request-text reduction only), so no ds4-bench delta is attached; prefill/decode paths are unmodified.
- Notable failures: none on this revision.

title: Enable GLM 5.3 tensor parallelism on the ROCm backend
body:
Enables GLM 5.3 (GLM_DSA family) on the two-node ROCm tensor-parallel backend from #813, then makes it fast enough to use. Before this, GLM TP never armed on ROCm: the GLM graph's TP initialization was guarded `#if defined(__APPLE__)`, so `tp_world` stayed 0 and every rank silently computed the full expert set against its half-resident weights (word salad, no error). With this PR, GLM-5.3-Flash Q4_K (177.76 GiB, unrunnable on one box) runs across two 128 GB Strix Halo boxes, including 47k-token contexts and ds4-server tool-call conversations.

Opt-in, like the backend itself: `DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1` on both ranks.

## Branch layout (stacked)

Integration lineage of `rocm-tensor-parallel` (#813) with upstream main merged in (`bd177c9`/`da15223`, `8025b22`, `0fff703`, `5dc45b7`). #813 stays at its original trunk point as the historical base (it shows conflicts with `main` and is not being rebased), so its ROCm TP transport is reviewable here; #835 and #1018 are kept mergeable on their own. Stack order: #813 → #835 → #1018 → this PR. Commits new here:

- Enablement: `ea7057d` merge fixups, `4dd3f4d` GLM TP on ROCm (the core change), `848fb67` lock static weight spans under streaming, `1a646f6` avoid the faulting Q4_K sorted down kernels, `682cdb4` restore the CPU build.
- Transport: `0e02528`, `4402b61`, `cb7cb70` verbs fixes (RDMA bulk-window reset, `DS4_TP_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS`, RC queue pairs, real `ibv_post_*` codes); `7598395` OdinLink loss recovery (same as #1018); `2a0977d` odl batch/big gates without the TCP header rendezvous (same as `15b6d6b` in #1018).
- Decode performance: `5272bda` pre-quantized k-slice Q8_0 matvec, `5b31f6d` gate arrive/wait split with the shared expert overlapping the FFN exchange, `b6f965b` vectorized small-output BF16 row matvec, `ebfe289` no periodic decode-stream flush on ROCm, `9b708e9` vocab-split output head, `50a3f9f` fewer and wider small launches, `5da2545` tiled long-context DSA kernels, `8f3505c` KDA attention split by heads, `4dac2b5` one-wave-per-row Q4_K expert gate/up kernel.
- Prefill performance: `10f5531` Q4_K routed experts through the vendored MMQ tensor-core GEMMs, `e9cfbde` indexer scores as batched f32 GEMMs, `e39e8dd` batch FFN big gate overlapped with the shared expert.
- Portability: `91ae988` guards the ROCm-only split gate wait (Metal and CUDA keep the single-call gate); the CPU build stub for the KDA state sync came in with `0fff703`.
- Disk KV cache under TP: `70b16d9` restores snapshots on both ranks (the leader restores, then streams the same payload to the worker over the control socket; before this a TP disk hit rebuilt both ranks with a full prefill, so a fresh 15k-token session took 123 s and now takes 4.3 s with a byte-identical answer); `5801a05` stages snapshots in the cache directory instead of /tmp (RAM-backed tmpfs, which OOM-killed the server once with a 6 GiB snapshot).

## Changes

- GLM graph TP init guard extended to `DS4_ROCM_BUILD`; the refusal gated behind `DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1`; GLM exempted from the Q8_0 output-head requirement (its head is replicated under TP).
- Streaming: operator-precedence fix in the ROCm GLM streaming gate; `mlock` of SSD static spans on ROCm and post-upload discards that skip locked spans (the GPU cannot fault file-backed pages back in).
- Q4_K sorted-pairs down GEMM routed through the proven per-pair kernel, `moe_sum` epilogue kept (see failures below).
- Decode path on ROCm TP: Q8 k-slice on prequantized activations; gate arrive/wait split; each rank projects half of the 154880-row head during single-token decode and the session merges the halves (off with `--mtp`); one launch for the KDA q/k/v projections and one for f_a/g_a/beta; 1024-lane float4 RMS norms; float4 router matvec.
- Long-context DSA layers: the indexed decode attention is now three kernels (a 16-key LDS tile scored against every head with RoPE applied once per key, a pv kernel handling all of the rank's heads per 128-key chunk, a chunk-order reduce), the indexer scorer runs one wave per key row. Old kernels stay as fallback (`DS4_ROCM_GLM_LEGACY_INDEXED_ATTN=1`). Kernel time per DSA layer 1000 + 776 us → 98 + 66 us.
- KDA head split (single-token decode only): each rank runs 32 of the 64 KDA heads (half-row projections, the conv + delta-rule recurrence on its half of the layer state, output projection K-sliced into the layer's ATTN gate, now in the gate schedule: 87 gates per token). Replicated KDA paths (prefill/verify rows, batched-session decode, session save via the new `DS4_TP_FRAME_GLM_KDA_SYNC` frame) re-gather the state halves first with one big-gate swap per layer. Off with `--mtp`, SSD streaming, an unsupported `kda_output` type, or `DS4_GLM_TP_KDA_HEAD_SPLIT_DISABLE=1` on both ranks. BF16 gets `ds4_gpu_glm53_matmul_bf16_kslice`.
- Prefill experts: Q4_K batches of 16+ tokens compact the rank's owned (token, slot) pairs and run gate/up and down as `ds4_mmq_q4_K_moe_pair` / `ds4_mmq_q4_K_moe` calls with one expert per row, then the existing scatter + `moe_sum` epilogue (gfx1151 default, `DS4_ROCM_MMQ_Q4K=0` keeps the tile kernels). The tile kernels ran at a few percent of both roofs.
- Prefill indexer: the GLM-5.3 indexer scores (every query against every pooled key, 34% of a 24.7k-token prefill in a one-block-per-pair kernel) run as strided-batched f32 hipBLAS GEMMs over the heads plus a reduce kernel for relu, per-head weights and the causal pooled mask; same f32 products, `DS4_ROCM_GLM_INDEXER_GEMM_CHECK=1` reports a relative deviation of ~3e-7 against the block kernel. `DS4_ROCM_GLM_INDEXER_GEMM=0` restores it.
- Batch FFN under TP: the routed-partial swap is kicked before the shared expert is encoded and waited on after it (`ds4_gpu_tp_big_gate_kick_nowait` / `ds4_gpu_tp_big_gate_wait_encode`); payload and add unchanged.

## Test evidence (per CONTRIBUTING.md)

Machine: 2x AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 128 GB unified), Fedora 44, ROCm, Thunderbolt 5 direct link (odl transport from #1018; rdma/tcp also work). Model: GLM-5.3-Flash Q4_K (`glm53-q4` GGUF, sha256 c7a0d950...). Build on both boxes:

```sh
make strix-halo -j32 CFLAGS="-O3 -ffast-math -g -march=native -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -fPIC -D_GNU_SOURCE -fno-finite-math-only" \
  ROCM_LDLIBS="-lm -pthread -lamdhip64 -lhipblas -lhipblaslt -lrocblas"
make cpu   # also verified clean
```

```sh
# box2                                                  # box1
env DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1 ~/ds4/ds4 -m GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf --tensor-parallel --role worker \
  --coordinator 10.0.2.1 7300 --transport odl --ctx 8192
env DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1 ~/ds4/ds4 -m GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf --tensor-parallel --role coordinator \
  --listen 10.0.2.1 7300 --transport odl --ctx 8192 -p "<prompt>"     # or --prompt-file
```

Correctness runs, all clean (no faults, desyncs or timeouts on either rank): short exact-prefill prompts ("two plus two" → "Four"); 227- and 323-token prompts with accurate summaries; a 47,288-token prompt at ctx 49152 with an accurate summary of the fed source file; ds4-server with `--batched-session 4` (two-turn weather-tool conversation with KV reuse, the same under a concurrent generation, a 6,181-token multi-chunk tool prompt reusing 6,192 cached tokens); after the head split, a server session with three turns, two concurrent requests, a follow-up, and an 810-token conversation saved to the KV disk cache.

Numerical checks: `DS4_ROCM_GLM_DSA_CHECK=1` and `DS4_GLM_TP_KDA_CHECK=1` run the previous or replicated kernels next to the new ones on the same inputs; over ~1000 (DSA) and 2800 (KDA) layer calls per rank the relative L2 deviations stay at 1e-7 to 1e-6, no non-finite values. Greedy texts flip at near-tie tokens against earlier builds (changed accumulation order; int8 activations in the k-slice path), with both continuations correct; the 45-token test prompt reproduces earlier outputs byte for byte across several builds. The MMQ prefill path was checked by running the same prompts with the path on and off.

## Performance

2x gfx1151 over odl, greedy. "Q8-attention GGUF" is a data-only requant of the official file (KDA projections + head to Q8_0) used to measure the code with the BF16 tensors out of the way; it is not part of the PR.

| Test | first submission | now |
|---|---|---|
| official Q4_K GGUF, 45-token prompt decode | 8.9 t/s | 13.1 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, 45-token prompt decode | 15.4 t/s | 19.4 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, decode after 24,764 tokens | 11.8 t/s | 19.0 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, decode after 44,267 tokens | 11.1 t/s | 15.4 t/s (at `5da2545`, not re-measured since) |
| Q8-attention GGUF, prefill 323 / 2,500 / 24,764 tokens | 69 / 72 / 52 t/s | 146 / 140 / 122 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, MTP 1 draft | 10.4 t/s | 11.6 t/s (plain decode remains faster) |
| row-gate exchange (odl), average | 172 us | 86-106 us |

Where the time went, from roctracer timelines on both ranks: the first decode step (114 ms on the official GGUF) was 57 ms of BF16 KDA projections streamed at 160 GB/s, 13 ms of experts, 8.7 ms of gate spin, 5 ms of an 80 GB/s k-slice kernel, ~17 ms of ~1,500 small launches. After the rounds above a Q8-model step is ~52 ms: ~35 ms of memory-bound kernels near the 227 GB/s roof, ~6 ms of gates (84 exchanges of ~90 us, the odl round trip plus rank skew), ~4 ms of launch gaps, ~6 ms of small kernels. Prefill on a 2,500-token prompt spent 59% of its time in the Q4_K expert tile kernels before `10f5531`; at 24.7k the indexer scoring kernel was another 34% before `e9cfbde`. What remains of a 24.7k prefill (~200 s): MMQ expert GEMMs ~47 s, the exposed part of the big-gate exchanges ~20 s, the sequential KDA prefill recurrence 23 s, hipBLAS attention and dense GEMMs ~70 s.

Two intermediate pv-kernel designs for the long-context attention both sat at 200-240 us per layer: the scattered KV rows come from DRAM every token and both designs kept the same number of loads in flight per CU; reading each row once for all heads over 16 blocks brought it to 68 us.

## Transport reliability (`7598395`)

The OdinLink transport lost whole 1 MiB gate messages whenever a Thunderbolt frame failed CRC (`odl_tb5: RX CRC error ... dropping message`), which parked both ranks on their spin kernels until the 300 s bulk timeout and killed the session (seen 4096 tokens into an 11k-token ds4-server prefill). The loss-recovery commit reviewed in #1018 (per-message headers, receiver-driven retransmission from retained frames, idle ranks serving requests from their control-channel waits) is cherry-picked here. Validated with `DS4_TP_ODL_DROP_TEST`: 15.35 vs 15.23 t/s decode with every 400th gate message dropped (output byte-identical), 69.1 vs 67.5 t/s prefill with every 50th dropped (output identical).

## Speculative decoding (MTP)

Works with two-rank TP (CLI and ds4-server, 226 tokens to 47k, tool-call conversations) with no code beyond this PR; runtime settings: `--mtp` on both ranks, `DS4_GLM_MTP_DRAFTS=1`, `--batched-session 1` on ds4-server. It remains a net slowdown here: the 2-row verify span costs about twice a plain decode step and draft agreement stays below break-even. Default-off is right for this hardware. The KDA head split and the vocab-split head turn themselves off with `--mtp`.

## Notable failures root-caused on the way

1. **Q4_K sorted-pairs down-projection fault.** Batch prefills of 32+ tokens aborted both ranks with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION` (surfacing as "GLM TP batch gate failed" in ds4-server). Stage-skipping isolated it to the sorted/tile down kernels (`moe_down_q4K_expert_tile{4,8}_row32`, `moe_down_q4K_sorted_qwarp32`); every input validates clean and the per-pair kernel reads the same weights without faulting. `1a646f6` routes the sorted-path down GEMM through the per-pair kernel and keeps the `moe_sum` epilogue for q4k (without it, batches of 128+ tokens silently dropped the MoE output). Why the tile down kernels fault is still open (possibly related to #890 / #998 / #608 / #595); with `10f5531` the prefill down projection runs through MMQ anyway.
2. **Static-weight pageout under streaming**, fixed by the mlock extension and discard guards in `848fb67`.

## Not done / caveats

- Balancing the routed experts by splitting each expert's FFN dimension across ranks: the Q4_K `down` matrices' K-halves are strided per row, so it needs whole `down` matrices per rank or a ~27 GB repack at load.
- Prefill stays replicated for the KDA layers (a split would need a Q8 K-slice GEMM on ROCm and 34 more big gates per chunk).
- The KV disk-cache restore of a session under TP was not exercised after the KDA head split (saves were; the restore path clears the split flag).
- Not run: the full `make test` suite (needs the CPU test fixtures); everything above was validated end-to-end on real hardware on both ranks.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: MoE Q4 sorted-pairs path sums non-finite expert outputs: intermittent all-NaN logits on GB10 (sm_121)
body:
Summary

On a DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121`), DeepSeek V4 Flash with mixed q2-q4 quantization
degenerates intermittently: after the first token, **every** decode step produces
an all-NaN logit vector, `sample_argmax_unrolled8` never finds a maximum and
stays on index 0, which is `<|begin_of_sentence|>`. The visible result is a
stream of special tokens.

Measured over 45 independent restarts, **19 (42%) produced at least one ruined
generation**.

The proximate cause is that the **Q4 sorted-pairs MoE path is the only MoE path
in the engine that sums expert contributions without an `isfinite` check**. The
Q4 expert computation does produce canonical NaNs (`0x7fffffff`) during prefill;
`moe_mmq_sum_kernel`, `moe_mmq_swiglu_weighted_clamp_kernel` and the attention
softmax all discard non-finite values, this path propagates them into the
residual stream, then into the KV cache, and decode reads them back.

Environment

- **Dell Pro Max with GB10** (the Dell edition of the NVIDIA DGX Spark),
  `aarch64`, DGX OS 7.5.0 on Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.17.0-1031-nvidia.
- GPU **NVIDIA GB10 Blackwell**, compute capability **12.1 (`sm_121`)**, driver
  **580.173.02**, **CUDA 13.0** (V13.0.88). 128 GB unified LPDDR5X, no dedicated
  VRAM.
- ds4 at commit `b6af0adf8ca97c89145c9f9c15be70c9fd6c4507`, built with
  `make cuda-spark CUDA_ARCH=sm_121` (i.e. `-O3 --use_fast_math -gencode
  arch=compute_121a,code=sm_121a`).
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Layers37-42Q4KExperts-OtherExpertLayersIQ2XXSGateUp-Q2KDown-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-fixed-0731.gguf`
  (90.89 GiB). Only layers 37-42 take `q4k_path`; the other expert layers are
  IQ2_XXS and go through the aligned artifacts path.
- Reproduced with `ds4-server` on `127.0.0.1`, `--ctx 8192`, no DSpark/MTP,
  temperature 0. Reproduced both with and without
  `--disable-exact-dsml-tool-replay` at the same rate (see below); that flag is
  unrelated.

How it shows up

Only the **first request after a restart** is likely to be hit, and at most one
request per process: over 20 restarts with two requests each, 9 restarts had the
first request ruined, 2 had the second one ruined, and **none had both**.

Adding a probe that counts non-finite terms right before the sum:

| restarts | non-finite terms in `down` | NaN decode steps | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 of 8 | 0 | 0 | clean |
| 4 of 8 | 5 to 20+ | 79 of 80 | **ruined** |
| 1 of 8 | 3 | 0 | clean (see below) |

Every ruined run has non-finite values in the per-expert `down` buffer; no run
without them was ever ruined. 50 of 61 observed values were exactly
`0x7fffffff`, i.e. a **computed** NaN (`inf-inf` or `0*inf`), not garbage memory.
`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --kernel-name 'regex=moe'` went through model
load and the whole prefill with **zero** out-of-bounds accesses.

The one clean run that still produced NaNs is explained by the attention
softmax guard (`float p = isfinite(row[k]) ? expf(row[k] - max_s) : 0.0f;`): the
NaN landed on a key that then got silently ignored. So the 42% figure is a
**lower bound** on how often the model is affected.

It also corrupts tool calls, sometimes silently

Re-running the same probe with a tool-calling conversation instead of plain
prompts (2026-09-10, same unguarded build, 20 restarts) shows two distinct
shapes, both starting on the **first request after the restart**:

Visible — the DSML block collapses mid-emission:

```
<｜DSML｜tool_calls>
<｜DSML｜invoke name="leggi_misura">
<｜DSML｜parameter name="nome"<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜><｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>…
```

logged by the server as
`TOOLS invalid tool call returned as assistant text finish=length [saw_start=1 saw_end=0]`.

**Silent, and worse** — a structurally valid tool call with a corrupted function
name. This one returned `tool_calls=1`, `finish_reason=tool_calls`, no special
tokens and no repetition, i.e. it passes every marker-based or
repetition-based check, but the function name was `leggi_m FOX` instead of
`leggi_misura`. An agent harness would dispatch a call to a tool that does not
exist and surface an unrelated error downstream.

This matters for anyone using the engine agentically: **a marker-only degeneracy
check under-reports the defect**, and the corruption can reach the tool
dispatcher rather than the user's screen.

Not the DSML tool replay map

Worth stating because the symptom looks like it. `--disable-exact-dsml-tool-replay`
makes **no difference** to the failure rate: 1/10 restarts ruined with the flag,
1/10 without it, on the same unguarded build (Fisher exact p = 1.0). In both
ruined runs the failure is on **turn 0**, where the trace shows

```
tool_replay: mem=0 disk=0 canonical=0 missing_ids=0
```

i.e. no tool history exists yet and `tool_memory_*` returns immediately, so the
replay map is not in play at all when the corruption appears.

## Where the guard is missing

`moe_sum_kernel` (`ds4_cuda.cu:23896` at this commit) sums unconditionally:

```c
for (uint32_t e = 0; e < n_expert; e++) acc += down[((uint64_t)tok * n_expert + e) * out_dim + row];
```

while `moe_mmq_sum_kernel` (`ds4_cuda.cu:1183`), used by the MXFP4, MMQ and
aligned IQ2 paths, has had the guard all along:

```c
if (!guard_nonfinite || isfinite(v)) acc += v;
```

The decode-side direct-sum kernels have the same gap, and this one bites *during*
generation rather than at the first token:

- `moe_down_sum6_qwarp32_kernel` (`:22018`)
- `moe_down_sum3_qwarp32_kernel` (`:22216`)
- `moe_down_q4K_sum6_qwarp32_kernel` (`:22248`)
- `moe_down_q4K_sum3_qwarp32_kernel` (`:22490`)

all doing `if (lane == 0) total += acc;`.

Note that the clamp in the tile kernels does not help: a NaN fails every
comparison, so `if (gate[p] > clamp) gate[p] = clamp;` leaves it untouched.

Fix that works here

Five one-line changes, applying the convention the engine already uses
elsewhere — treat an expert whose contribution is not finite as contributing
zero:

```c
/* moe_sum_kernel */
const float v = down[((uint64_t)tok * n_expert + e) * out_dim + row];
if (isfinite(v)) acc += v;

/* the four direct-sum kernels */
if (lane == 0 && isfinite(acc)) total += acc;
```

Measured on the machine above, 20 independent restarts per arm, ctx 8192:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| restarts with a ruined generation | 11 / 20 | **0 / 20** |
| `7 * 8` answered exactly `56` | 18 / 20 | **20 / 20** |
| prefill (mean from ctx 8192 up) | 800.1 t/s | 816.8 t/s |
| decode (first chunk, clean requests) | 13.08 t/s | 12.96 t/s |

Both throughput figures are within run-to-run noise: the guard is free. The
probe still fires in **12 of 20 restarts** afterwards, so the NaNs keep being
produced at the same rate, they just no longer reach the output.

Guarding only `moe_sum_kernel` was not enough: it left 2 ruined runs out of 20,
with the avalanche starting mid-sentence instead of at the first token, which is
what pointed at the decode-side sums.

Held up under wider conditions afterwards (2026-09-10): **44 further restarts,
492 tool-calling turns, 0 ruined**, spanning ctx 8k / 100k / 1M, with and
without DSpark (`--dspark --mtp-exact-sampling`), and tool results from 20 bytes
to 9 KB. Every tool call had the correct function name and argument. 95%
confidence bound on the per-restart failure rate afterwards: **0 - 8%** (0 -
0.77% per request).

Workaround without patching

`DS4_CUDA_MOE_NO_Q4_SORTED=1` also gives 0/20, because it makes layers 37-42
fall back to a guarded path — but it costs **3.11x on prefill** (688 -> 221 t/s
in our measurement), so it is not a good trade.

What I could not determine

Which operation actually creates the NaN.** It is born in the Q4 expert
product during prefill and it is a canonical NaN, so something upstream
overflows to infinity first. Candidates I did not manage to separate: the
`dev_dot_q4_K_q8_K_block*` accumulation, the q8_K quantization of `mid`, or an
overflow made more likely by `--use_fast_math` (`-ftz`, approximate intrinsics)
which is in the project's build flags. A guard is a mitigation; the arithmetic
question is the real bug and I am happy to run further experiments on this
hardware if that helps.

Two hypotheses I did test and **ruled out**, in case they save someone time:
uninitialized reads of the sorted-pairs scratch (zeroing the entire scratch
leaves the failure rate unchanged at 40%), and out-of-bounds writes (memcheck
clean across prefill).

title: Make BPE merging O(n log n) for large CJK pieces
body:
## Problem

The merge loop in `bpe_emit_piece` rescans every adjacent pair and shifts the symbol array on every merge, so it is quadratic in the number of symbols per piece. Punctuation-free CJK text forms letter-run pieces of hundreds of thousands of symbols under both pre-tokenizers, and tokenizing a ~1M-token Chinese prompt stalled for 34+ minutes (single thread, still running) — while the same scale in Italian tokenizes in about two minutes because whitespace keeps pieces tiny.

Sampled the stuck server with `sample`: nearly 100% in `bpe_tokenize_text -> bpe_emit_piece`, with the memmove-heavy array shifts dominating.

## Change

Fast path with identical merge semantics (always merge the leftmost pair with the minimal rank):

- symbols are `(start,end)` ranges into the encoded buffer — no per-symbol allocations, no concatenation copies
- doubly linked list instead of array shifts
- pair ranks cached and recomputed only for the two pairs touching each merge point
- min-heap ordered by `(rank, original symbol index)` with lazy invalidation, which reproduces the leftmost tie-break exactly

`DS4_BPE_SLOW=1` selects the original path, kept as reference and rollback.

## Verification

- Identical token counts vs the original path on seven text categories: punctuation-free Chinese, punctuated Chinese, English, Python, mixed zh/en, needle-marker lines, JSON blobs.
- Byte-identical greedy generation for the same prompt under both paths.
- The original failure case now completes: a 1,028,610-token Chinese context prefills normally with 5/5 needle retrieval (before the fix, tokenization alone never finished).
- A 12K-symbol single piece drops from 24.7s to 5.1s end to end; the gap widens quadratically beyond that.

Tested on M3 Ultra 512GB (Metal), GLM 5.3 Flash Q4_K and DeepSeek V4 Flash MXFP4.

title: rocm: model weights in host RAM on integrated APUs (Strix Halo)
body:
Fixes OOM loading resident DeepSeek V4 Flash Q2 (80.76 GiB) on Strix Halo systems, and unlocks the other 128 GB UMA resident models on ROCm.

## Problem
The ROCm model arena allocates weights with `hipMalloc`, which on integrated APUs is bound by the small device memory pool exposed to the GPU (~62 GiB, set by the BIOS UMA frame buffer). A resident Flash Q2 (80.76 GiB) therefore failed during tensor-span preparation:

```
ds4: model arena alloc failed for tensor-span:108 (528.00 MiB request): out of memory
```

## Fix
On integrated APUs, allocate model arena chunks via `hipHostMalloc` (falling back to `hipMallocManaged`), mirroring how llama.cpp's `GGML_HIP_UMA` keeps weights in host RAM while they stay GPU-visible over the UMA fabric. Discrete GPUs keep the existing `hipMalloc` path untouched; `DS4_ROCM_FORCE_DEVICE_MEM=1` restores the previous behavior.

## Scope
The documented alternative for the small-pool problem is raising the GPU-visible pool via kernel boot parameters (`amdgpu.gttsize=126976 ttm.pages_limit=32505856 ttm.page_pool_size=32505856`, see docs/STRIX_HALO.md), which gives ~124 GiB GTT. Hosts that already apply those parameters do not need this change.

This patch is for the stock case: some integrated systems expose only ~62 GiB to the GPU with default firmware/kernel settings and cannot (or do not want to) change boot parameters or reboot. There, routing the resident weight arena to host memory makes 80-91 GiB resident models load without any host configuration change. Verified on a Bosgame M5 (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S, 128 GB) running stock boot parameters.

## Verified
Bosgame M5 (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S, 128 GB, ROCm 10.0, this branch).

DeepSeek V4 Flash models, resident:

| model | prefill (new interval) | steady gen | peak resident |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flash Q2 | 273-284 tok/s (ctx 4-8k) | 13.0-13.7 tok/s | 80.76 GiB |
| Flash Q2 + DSpark drafter | 206-286 tok/s | 22.8-24.3 tok/s | 80.76 GiB + 5.6 GiB |
| Flash Q2-Q4 (L37-42 Q4K) | 103-151 tok/s | 13.1-13.6 tok/s | 90.88 GiB |

All load in ~30 s; KV is 0.41-0.46 GiB. GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 also runs resident (90 GiB) with `DS4_GLM_MEMORY_GUARD=0` (the guard budgets from the ~61 GiB device pool); vision mode (V4 Flash Vision-Exp + encoder) works on ROCm.

Note: this approach is complementary to #361 (opt-in `DS4_CUDA_MANAGED` for high-context OOM on large-carveout UMA APUs): #361 addresses long-context scratch by defaulting weight/scratch placement policy on demand, while the change here makes resident weights work on integrated APUs out of the box by routing the weight arena to host memory.

title: CUDA: use selected expert cache for IQ2 SSD prefill
body:
Fixes CUDA SSD streaming for routed MoE models.

1. IQ2/Q2 batch prefill now uses the compact selected-expert table rather than resolving full expert tables.
2. `--ssd-streaming-cache-experts` is a bounded CUDA LRU, released on model/lifecycle changes.
3. Resident experts are stored in contiguous gate/up/down slabs. When the selected set is resident, kernels receive the slab bases plus remapped stable slot IDs, avoiding per-layer GPU-to-GPU copies into compact staging.
4. CUDA now supports `--expert-profile` / `DS4_EXPERT_HOTLIST` to collect routed-expert locality data.

AProjQ4 matched prefill (GB10, e9528de, ctx 1024, forced batch prefill):
- Before: 1.09 t/s; CUDA file cache 78.62 GiB.
- Selected-expert path: 2.59 t/s; CUDA file cache 6.06 GiB.
- Result: 2.38x prefill (+138%) and 92.3% less file cache.

AProjQ8 cache-size tuning smoke (GB10, ctx 1024, deterministic prompt):

| Expert slots | Expert cache | Flash generation | Vision generation |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256 | 1.69 GiB | 1.62 t/s | 1.61 t/s |
| 512 | 3.38 GiB | 2.05 t/s | 3.04 t/s |
| 1024 | 6.76 GiB | 4.02 t/s | 4.17 t/s |
| 2048 | 13.52 GiB | 6.24 t/s | 6.00 t/s |

The two locally available Flash variants show the same capacity curve: 256 is below the routed working set, 1024 is the measured throughput/memory compromise, and 2048 favors generation throughput where the extra memory is available. Flash hit/miss at 256/512/1024/2048: 755/18,056; 5,027/13,784; 11,066/7,745; 13,809/5,002. Vision: 721/18,048; 8,707/10,062; 11,546/7,223; 13,922/4,847. These are single-run GB10/model-specific tuning observations, not a general performance claim.

A follow-up can expose a non-binding runtime hint based on `4 × (local routed layers × top-k)` when the memory planner permits it; this PR intentionally does not alter the user-selected cache budget.

Validation:
- `make -j4 cuda-spark`: PASS
- `make test-cuda-q8-scratch`: PASS
- Deterministic SSD-streaming smoke: PASS, identical output.

title: CUDA TP with exactly two GPUs is classified single-tier and OOMs on GPU 0
body:
**Environment:**
2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB, sm_120), driver 595.91.07 (open kernel module), CUDA 13.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash MXFP4 GGUF (145.26 GiB).

**Command:**
./ds4 --cuda --cuda-tensor-parallel --gpu-devices 0,1 --ctx 10000

**Symptom:**
only `dev=0` initializes; startup copies the whole model into GPU 0 and dies with `CUDA model arena alloc failed ... out of memory` at ~56 GiB, then `cuda failed to prepare optional model cache`.

**Root cause:**
`engine_classify_multi_tier` derives `multi_tier` from layer spread across placement entries. CUDA TP places partner tiers by half index, never in `placement[]`. With two GPUs there is one stage, every entry is tier 0, and the engine takes the single-tier path: one device, no per-device caches, no partner. The single-tier startup walk then needs the whole mmap host-registered (`cudaHostRegisterReadOnly`), which the open kernel module reports unsupported (`HostRegisterReadOnlySupported=0`), so it falls into the device arena and fills GPU 0 until OOM. Four- and eight-GPU layouts never hit this because multiple stages already spread the layers.

**Fix:**
treat a requested CUDA decode TP layout as multi-tier.

    --- a/ds4.c
    +++ b/ds4.c
    @@ -62278,6 +62278,12 @@ static int engine_classify_multi_tier(...)
    +    /* CUDA decode TP pairs every layer-home tier with a partner tier that
    +     * never appears in placement[] (partners are derived from the half
    +     * index). A single-stage pair therefore looks single-tier above, yet
    +     * its partner is always a second device that must take the multi-tier
    +     * path (per-device caches, partner scratch). */
    +    if (!multi_tier && engine_cuda_tp_decode_requested(e)) multi_tier = 1;
         e->multi_tier = multi_tier;

**Verified:**
same command now initializes both devices, validates peer access (DIRECT), installs 76.47 GiB on tier 0 and 75.48 GiB on tier 1 (half-resident experts, replicated dense, 2-way output shard), and answers a prompt at 69 tok/s generation. Built with `make cuda CUDA_ARCH=sm_120`.

title: metal: add opt-in slab residency for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash （M2 192GB 0.25tk/s -> 13tk/s)
body:
Attach owned SSD expert-cache slabs to a queue residency set on macOS 15+, opt-in with `DS4_METAL_STREAMING_SLAB_RESIDENCY=1`. This fixes the multi-second command submission delay reproduced with large slabs on M2 Ultra. Pressure relief detaches the set until cache rebuild. The reviewer-requested simplification and explicit allocation fallback warning are included, with an injected-failure test.

### Current revalidation: 2026-10-30

Merged upstream `ee7e840`. M2 Ultra 192 GiB, macOS 15.7.4, unchanged `iogpu.wired_limit_mb=0`, AtomicChat DwarfStar Flash-1017 IQ2_XXS/Q2_K (366 GB, full SHA256 verified). Same-binary ABBA, fresh process per run, automatic cache, 2K prompt; OS/file cache not flushed.

8-token decode: off **0.29 / 0.26**, on **10.66 / 10.67 t/s**. All four outputs byte-identical. Short-run residency-cliff evidence, not sustained throughput; on-arm steady decode **13.96 / 13.95 t/s**. System swap stayed zero. Slab lifecycle, pressure relief, rebuild and usable-buffer fallback under injected residency-creation failure pass with Metal API validation.

Separate integration tree (#1033 + #1034 + #1234 FP4 fix, native upstream Engram) passes exact forced-eviction logits/history/cache-span parity and public session/snapshot/prefix-reuse/cancellation/bounds checks with Metal API validation. Combined decode: **16.26 / 16.14 / 14.66 t/s at 2K / 8K / 32K**, with 512 / 128 / 128 generated tokens. These combined numbers are not isolated gains from this PR.

### Limits

Pristine upstream still fails the FP4 E4M3 kernel parity test (mode 3, index 5428). The full kernel suite passes with #1234; that independent fix is not included in this focused PR. No new CUDA/ROCm hardware, 64K/128K, timed idle/resume, physical SSD-byte accounting or production-soak result is claimed.

[Full protocol, hashes, dated CSVs and earlier measurements](https://github.com/Dango233/ds4/blob/perf/metal-streaming-slab-residency/speed-bench/v41_slab_residency_m2_ultra.md#flash-1017-revalidation-2026-10-30).

title: metal: reduce decode synchronization for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash SSD streaming
body:

Combined decode: **16.26 / 16.14 / 14.66 t/s at 2K / 8K / 32K**, with 512 / 128 / 128 generated tokens. These combined numbers are not isolated gains from this PR.

No new CUDA/ROCm hardware, 64K/128K, timed idle/resume, physical SSD-byte accounting or production-soak result is claimed.

title: engram: parallelize DeepSeek V4.1 Flash decode reads on macOS
body:
This partitions macOS single-token Engram reads into four joined readers, preserving input order and disjoint output ranges. The switch is off by default. Inputs are validated before dispatch and worker errors propagate after joining. Upstream now parallelizes large batches on non-macOS platforms; this PR still covers the separate macOS 24-row decode path and preserves the new upstream path.

Enable with `DS4_ENGRAM_PARALLEL_DECODE=1`.

### Revalidation against current upstream

Measured on 2026-09-14 after merging `a04f46fa423e45712c8c7e430eff422479f314a3` (DeepSeek V4.1 CUDA support). M2 Ultra, 192 GiB, macOS 15.7.4, Metal; calibrated V4.1 Flash IQ2_XXS/Q2_K. Same binary per comparison, 2,048-token prompt, 8,257 allocated context, automatic expert cache, fresh engine per run; OS/file cache was not flushed.

Both arms use `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_STREAMING_EXPERT_SLABS=1` to isolate this change. No companion optimization is enabled.

Mean 512-token decode: **10.205 → 10.740 tokens/s** (+5.2%).

| Run | Switch | Prefill t/s | Decode t/s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | off | 68.43 | 10.20 |
| 2 | on | 68.65 | 10.72 |
| 3 | on | 68.63 | 10.76 |
| 4 | off | 68.66 | 10.21 |

All four decoded outputs match. These are two observations per variant on one host. Original 2026-09-13 measurements remain in the report.

### Validation and limits

Serial/parallel row equality, duplicate IDs, output guards, invalid inputs, EDOM in each worker, EIO, and upstream batch error checks pass. The real-model session fixture passes under Metal API validation with parallel reads enabled.

Clean Metal build, CPU compilation, frontend/Engram/GGUF/quality-tool unit tests and seven targeted Metal kernel subtests pass. **The full Metal kernel suite is not green**: the new router check fails at `tests/test_deepseek41_metal.c:105`; pristine upstream reproduces the exact same actual/reference values. No kernel or tolerance was changed to bypass it.

The two existing SDK 15 unused Metal 4 symbol warnings remain. Full legacy `make test` and CUDA/ROCm hardware validation were not run.

[Commands, model hash, raw CSVs and full results](https://github.com/Dango233/ds4/blob/perf/v41-parallel-engram-read/speed-bench/v41_engram_m2_ultra.md#upstream-revalidation-2026-09-14).

title: ROCm: add DeepSeek V4.1 Flash support for Strix Halo (gfx1151)
body:
Adds **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Q2 text and vision on ROCm 10.0 / Strix Halo `gfx1151`**: resident experts, single-machine SSD streaming, and two-machine inference over TCP or RoCE.

- V4.1 operators, CED prefill, disk-backed Engram and session state.
- FP32 split-key decode attention, optimized quantized projections, matrix-based prefill and exact batched top-512 selection.
- Two-machine inference splits the experts and vocabulary projection; shared-expert prefill overlaps peer transfers, and scalar gate waiting/reduction is fused.
- V4.1 ROCm optimizations use guarded dispatch with no required tuning environment overrides. Ordinary TCP over USB4 Ethernet uses the same TCP commands.

### Performance

Native `ds4-bench`, published Q2, 34,816 allocated context, 128 greedy output tokens per frontier, no DSpark or images. First row of each table is fresh prefill; subsequent rows append to restored prefixes. Startup excluded; one final sample per cell, not cold-cache measurements. Values are **prefill / decode tokens/s**.

| Context tokens | Appended tokens | TCP, 100 GbE | RoCE, 100 GbE |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | 8,192 | 395.61 / 16.59 | 391.56 / 17.33 |
| 16,384 | 8,192 | 382.74 / 16.32 | 380.32 / 17.13 |

| Context tokens | Appended tokens | SSD streaming, 76 GiB cache request |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 2,048 | 47.32 / 10.18 |
| 4,096 | 2,048 | 86.48 / 10.27 |
| 8,192 | 4,096 | 154.58 / 10.46 |
| 16,384 | 8,192 | 271.06 / 10.34 |
| 32,768 | 16,384 | 333.84 / 10.34 |

- Two 128 GB Framework Desktops, 16-core Strix Halo. Coordinator/SSD node: Ryzen AI Max+ 395, SK hynix PC711 1 TB (PCIe 3.0 ×4, ext4). Worker: engineering sample `100-000001243-50_Y`, Kingston FURY Renegade 2 TB (`SFYRD2000G`, PCIe 4.0 ×4, btrfs).
- Intel E810-C QSFP, 100 Gb/s, MTU 9000; NIC attachment PCIe 3.0 ×4 on coordinator and 4.0 ×4 on worker. Hardware counters verify actual RoCE payload traffic.
- Linux 7.2.5, ROCm SDK `10.0.0-4` / HIP `7.15.26333`, TuneD **`accelerator-performance`**. Scalar transport polling uses about half an additional CPU core per host during decode.

### Quality and validation

Official scoring: **227 cases per mode** (new 112-case continuation suite plus previous 115). New suite: 6,923 targets; API comparisons use 6,858 aligned positions, excluding case 047's reference alignment mismatch. Lower NLL/MAE is better.

| Mode | New 112 NLL | Long 12 NLL | API logprob MAE | API top1 agreement | Previous 115 NLL |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ROCm resident | 0.39578030 | 0.19736021 | 0.21899533 | 90.449% | 0.39737428 |
| ROCm SSD | 0.39618195 | 0.19406948 | 0.21957840 | 90.478% | 0.39357626 |
| ROCm RoCE | 0.39619718 | 0.20031244 | 0.21992302 | 90.522% | 0.39393896 |
| CUDA SSD, NVIDIA GB10 | 0.39251799 | 0.20265270 | 0.21669296 | 90.580% | 0.39295501 |

- CUDA has lower aggregate NLL; ROCm has lower NLL on the 12 long cases. Full panels precede the final optimizations; follow-up official checks preserve scores exactly, including all 112 resident cases for the query-layout change and focused final resident/TCP/RoCE cases.
- Matrix-path checks preserve full kernel outputs, 129,280-logit vectors and 128-token continuations. Vision attention preserves 63 full encoder captures across seven images; 390 independent kernel checks pass.
- Resident, SSD, TCP and RoCE pass practical coding/tool-use, state recovery and all 23 vision/cache cases. Final TCP/RoCE serving checks each complete 16 JSON replies, 16 SSE replies and four cancellations; protocol/state checks pass.
- Shared units, Linux TCP stress tests, ROCm transport/gate failure checks and five frontend build/link/help checks pass. No fresh physical Metal or GLM regression run is claimed.

### Limits and setup

- Exactly two machines, each fitting its assigned experts in RAM. Cluster SSD streaming is unsupported. DSpark is supported with resident experts over TCP or RoCE; its speed depends on the workload.
- RoCE requires compatible adapters/providers and stages transfers through system RAM. Ordinary TCP over USB4 Ethernet uses the same TCP commands.
- Populated 256K quality and long-running production endurance are unqualified. Images may need a smaller SSD cache.

Exact commands and results: [single-node setup](https://github.com/kyuz0/ds4/blob/cab73696812bc07548407deae551bd08786ea226/docs/STRIX_HALO.md#deepseek-v41-flash), [TCP/RoCE cluster](https://github.com/kyuz0/ds4/blob/cab73696812bc07548407deae551bd08786ea226/docs/CLUSTERING_ROCM.md), [QA](https://github.com/kyuz0/ds4/blob/cab73696812bc07548407deae551bd08786ea226/QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md#deepseek-v41-flash-rocmgfx1151).

### Update — 16 September 2026

Removed Linux USB4STREAM support and its setup/kernel-patch documentation. On the tested AMD systems it required a custom kernel patch and offered no meaningful performance benefit over the retained TCP/RoCE options. A shared tiny-buffer TCP stress failure was reproduced on unchanged main; its resolution is recorded below.

### Update — 17 September 2026

Integrated upstream changes and completed resident/SSD/concurrent serving, TCP/RoCE and 23 vision/cache cases in all four modes. The earlier description called differing concurrent replies an unresolved issue; that characterization was incorrect. Different batching schedules can change floating-point results and token choices, which upstream accepts; reply equality across schedules is not a promised contract.

### Update — 21 September 2026

Rebased on current main and added optimized vision attention, query-tile layout and scalar transport waiting. Tables above report current measurements and the expanded official references. The upstream tiny-buffer TCP test fix is included and that test now passes.

### Update — 28 September 2026

I added DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark speculative decoding on ROCm/gfx1151 for resident and two-rank inference. The implementation loads a separate support GGUF, captures the three target feature layers, runs the three-stage draft model, verifies up to five drafts in one target pass, and commits or rolls back target, Engram and draft state together. Adaptive scheduling bypasses speculation when recent verifier cost and acceptance make it unprofitable.

The qualified support file is [`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-DSpark-MXFP4.gguf`](https://huggingface.co/kernelpool/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4-GGUF/resolve/22a073e51781f43e6814885bb4b3cbe540f175ef/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-DSpark-MXFP4.gguf) at immutable repository revision `22a073e51781f43e6814885bb4b3cbe540f175ef`: 7,966,294,016 bytes, SHA256 `7a2217ca6ef27cbce4ac934d8b6f59f2f6158ec288527bbe72b86dcbed95d4b5`. It retains the released native-MXFP4 draft experts. Use it with `--mtp-model FILE --dspark`; ordinary positive-temperature sampling does not require `--mtp-exact-sampling`.

Resident Q2, 7,599 prompt tokens plus exactly 256 generated tokens, temperature 1.0, top-k 0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0.05 and seed 424242. These are absolute rates from two 192 GB Strix Halo systems:

| System | Target-only decode | DSpark decode | Accepted drafts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 14.67 tok/s | 18.57 tok/s | 121/200 (60.50%) |
| B | 14.59 tok/s | 15.93 tok/s | 121/200 (60.50%) |

The same production sampling settings on two 128 GB systems over RoCE, with 7,642 prompt tokens plus 256 generated tokens, measured 16.25 tok/s target-only and 15.76 tok/s with DSpark. DSpark accepted 52/79 drafts with zero errors. This qualifies distributed execution but is not a distributed speed recommendation.

`make test-rocm`, all 130 isolated V4.1 ROCm shapes, RDMA completion accounting, full-model depth-five verification, sampling/admission/reset contracts, complete coding/tool/structured-output requests, cancellation and session reuse passed. A shared-path DeepSeek V4 DSpark regression also completed 256 generated tokens with 38/52 drafts accepted and zero errors. Official target scoring is unchanged because DSpark does not alter the target weights; changed-path tests separately verified active proposal, verification, acceptance and rollback. DSpark requires resident target experts: the Q2 target contributes about 151.76 GiB of resident tensor spans and the support model about 7.42 GiB before context and runtime buffers. SSD expert streaming remains unsupported for DSpark.


### Update — 29 September 2026

I optimized DeepSeek V4.1 prefill on ROCm/gfx1151. Partial-row Q8 projections now use guarded WMMA dispatch, routed IQ2 experts fuse SwiGLU write-back, large prefill attention uses a tiled D512 kernel derived from Gufo, and the two F16 control projections share one batched launch. Decode arithmetic and the DSpark target/draft state contract are unchanged.

Resident Q2 on one 192 GB Strix Halo system with ROCm 10, fixed 8,192-token coding input and fresh context:

| Workload | Measured result |
|---|---:|
| Exact prefill, repeat 1 | 382.23 tok/s |
| Exact prefill, repeat 2 | 382.20 tok/s |
| Sampled target-only decode | 13.86 tok/s |
| Sampled DSpark decode | 18.34 tok/s |

The sampled request used 7,642 prompt tokens plus exactly 256 generated tokens, temperature 1.0, top-k 0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0.05 and seed 424242. DSpark accepted 162/225 drafts (72.00%) with zero errors and zero replay fallbacks.

Two-rank Q2 prefill with the same final source:

| Transport | Fresh 8K | 8K append at 16K |
|---|---:|---:|
| TCP | 437.84 tok/s | 430.07 tok/s |
| RoCE | 441.24 tok/s | 428.28 tok/s |

General100 passes 100/100 cases and 2,994/2,994 targets with weighted NLL 0.3682673852; its score and first-logit files match the preceding published stack byte for byte. The final integrated source passes complete make test-rocm runs on three Strix Halo systems, including RDMA completion accounting. Resident and SSD real-image agent tests, exact and bounded API/vision panels, TCP/RoCE target and DSpark requests, cancellation, cache reuse, tool calls and four overlapping sessions pass. SSD streaming remains target-only because the engine explicitly rejects SSD+DSpark.

### Update — 30 September 2026

I optimized small V4.1 HC and F32 router projections on gfx1151. HC batches token launches and prefetches aligned operands; the router reuses weights across verification rows. Both preserve the scalar accumulation/reduction order. Quantization and DSpark sampling policy are unchanged.

Resident Q2 with the native-MXFP4 DSpark file linked above, ROCm 10, one 192 GB gfx1151 system. Each coding request generates exactly 256 tokens with temperature 1.0, top-k 0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0.05 and seed 424242. Rates exclude model loading and prefill; decoder SWA bounded replay is disabled.

| Coding request | Prompt tokens | Target decode | DSpark decode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JSON Patch task | 7,642 | 15.14 tok/s | 23.32 tok/s |
| Second JSON Patch task | 7,826 | 15.13 tok/s | 17.25 tok/s |

The 7,642-token request on two 128 GB systems measured 16.22/17.74 tok/s target/DSpark over TCP and 16.88/18.14 over RoCE on the 100 GbE link described above. DSpark throughput depends on the generated content and acceptance.

| Validation | Result |
|---|---|
| General100 | 100 cases, 2,994 targets; weighted NLL 0.3682673852; scores and captured logits unchanged |
| V4.1 ROCm operators | 188 isolated shapes passed |
| `make test-rocm` | Passed on three systems |
| API and vision | API 16/16; vision thinking, append and full-image checks passed |
| Coding and state | Executable code, JSON, tools, cache reuse, cancellation and 1,024-token continuation passed |
| SSD and two-rank inference | Target-only SSD and target/DSpark TCP/RoCE checks passed |

The dependent bounded-replay PR has separate measurements and passes the same affected quality checks.

### Update — 9 October 2026: DeepSeek V4 Flash prefill

I added the V4 Flash Halo prefill kernels from [MadRocK-AI/ds4](https://github.com/MadRocK-AI/ds4/tree/551219f499dcdeb6a3793f739b124b6ba7830862), adapted to preserve the current ROCm attention path and arithmetic. The optimization targets DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 IQ2_XXS/Q2_K with selected Q8 tensors on gfx1151; it does not change V4.1 dispatch, weights or quantization. Supported 2K/4K shapes select it automatically, with layout and execution-mode guards.

On one 128 GB Strix Halo system with ROCm 10, warm prefill of a complete 4,096-token prompt measured **466.15 tokens/s**, the mean of two independent timed runs. Model loading and a separate warmup are excluded. This is full-prompt throughput, not a 2K-to-4K interval.

| V4 validation | Result |
|---|---|
| Flash100 | 100 cases, 2,313 targets; weighted NLL 0.401858465476; scores and captured logits unchanged |
| Long-code, 4K chunks | 4 cases, 523 targets; NLL 0.477362220138; scores and captured logits unchanged |
| Long-code, 2K chunks | 4 cases, 523 targets; NLL 0.473459099562; scores and captured logits unchanged |
| Coding | All 24 answers unchanged; both builds pass 21/24 tasks and 130/138 checks |
| State and continuation | Complete state/logits through 32K, tails, checkpoint restores, SSD and production sampled DSpark checks passed |
| Vision subset | All five captured answers unchanged; the four-case scored subset remains 3/4 on both builds |
| Serving | Resident and SSD overlap, adaptive scheduling, cancellation, cache reuse, slot reuse and tool checks passed |
| Kernel and integration suites | Full FP32/F16 expert outputs and canaries pass all six routing cases; complete ROCm and affected DeepSeek/Qwen/GLM suites pass |

The current complete toolbox overlay also passes raw-completions tests, replay/draft-reset checks and all five frontend build/help checks. The coding and vision scores above retain the same failures in both builds; this change does not fix those cases. No new V4.1 performance result is claimed for this V4-specific addition.

### Update — 10 October 2026: DeepSeek V4.1 resident prefill

I added co-computed IQ2 expert gate/up and Q2 input/weight reuse for resident DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Q2 on gfx1151. The kernels select automatically for the 2,048-row workspace, preserve native quantization and multiplication order, and use about 12 MB of scratch memory. Other shapes, quality mode, SSD experts and tensor-parallel execution retain their existing paths. Weights and quantization are unchanged.

On one 192 GB Strix Halo system with ROCm 10, resident experts and disk-backed Engram, two warmed runs per cell measured these complete-prompt prefill rates in tokens/s. Model loading and separate warmups are excluded; these are whole-prompt rates with no generated tokens, not append intervals. Bounded replay uses the existing opt-in [bounded-replay PR](https://github.com/kyuz0/ds4/pull/2).

| 8,192 | 429.98–438.72 | 517.72–518.56 |

The default path enables its existing exact decoder-suffix optimization at 8K, so throughput need not decrease monotonically with prompt length.

The kernel changes preserve arithmetic within each replay mode. Bounded replay remains a separate approximation and stays disabled by default.

All 240 paired resident state, token and logit payloads also match through 32K, including continuation, restoration, tail chunks and forced replay. Another 30 SSD state/logit/token payloads match with a 32 GB expert cache; SSD retains its existing execution path.

title: test_deepseek41_metal: new router check fails on M1 Ultra (pre-M5); sqrt(softplus) compared at 3e-6 but 1.0f+exp is ~0.7% imprecise
body:
**Clarification:** this report is about a failure in the model-free `tests/test_deepseek41_metal` router numerical check on our M1 Ultra. V4.1 inference works on this machine: we have successfully run server requests and inference benchmarks. We are not reporting an inference crash or inability to generate. The test failure also reproduces on pristine upstream `a04f46f`, without our KV compression PR (#186); see the fresh reproduction below in the comments.

---

`tests/test_deepseek41_metal` fails the new router check on M1 Ultra:

```
router n=256 mode=0 rows=1 row=0 expert=4 logit=-11.8886719 actual=0.00263455603 ref=0.00262947031
tests/test_deepseek41_metal.c:105: fabs(probs[t * n + e] - ref[e]) <= 3e-6 * (1 + ref[e])
ds4: Metal cleanup discarded 5 live tensor handles
make: *** [test-deepseek41-metal] Error 1
```

## Repro

```sh
make tests/test_deepseek41_metal && ./tests/test_deepseek41_metal
```

No model or GGUF needed. Fails every run, identical values.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| ds4 commit | `a04f46f` (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash support for CUDA) |
| Hardware | Mac Studio, Apple M1 Ultra, 128 GB |
| OS | macOS 26.6.2 (Darwin 25.6.0) |
| Backend | Metal, `make` default target |
| Metal 4 | unavailable, engine logs `Metal 4 tensor API disabled for pre-M5/pre-A19 devices` |

## Not a regression: the check is new

`check_router` is added wholesale by `a04f46f`; every line of it is new in that commit's diff of `tests/test_deepseek41_metal.c`. Confirmed by bisect on this machine:

| commit | result |
|---|---|
| `bd66c40` DeepSeek v4.1 Flash support for Metal | PASS |
| `a04f46f` DeepSeek v4.1 Flash support for CUDA | FAIL |

So the kernel behaviour is presumably unchanged; the new check is simply tighter than pre-M5 Apple GPUs can satisfy.

## Root cause

The check compares two independent FP32 evaluations of `sqrt(softplus(x))` for a logit of about -11.9, where that expression is ill-conditioned.

Kernel, `metal/dsv4_misc.metal:5188` (and the same form at `:5349`):

```metal
const float4 sp = select(log(1.0f + exp(x)), x, x > 20.0f);
```

Host reference, `tests/test_deepseek41_metal.c:98`:

```c
ref[e] = sqrtf(v > 20 ? (float)v : logf(1.0f + expf((float)v)));
```

For `x = -11.8886719`, `exp(x)` is about 6.87e-6. Adding that to `1.0f` discards most of it: float resolution near 1.0 is 1.19e-7, so the addend carries roughly **0.68% relative error** before the log. Against the true value:

| | value | error vs exact |
|---|---|---|
| exact, `sqrt(log1p(exp(x)))` in double | 0.00262063751 | — |
| host reference, `1.0f + expf` | 0.00262947031 | +8.83e-6 |
| Metal kernel | 0.00263455603 | +1.39e-5 |
| FP32 using `log1pf(expf(x))` | 0.00262063742 | -9.17e-11 |

Both sides are wrong by several times the tolerance, in the same direction, by different amounts. Their gap is 5.09e-6 against a bound of 3.01e-6. The check therefore only passes where the GPU happens to round this expression the same way the host does, which is presumably true on M5 Max and M3 Ultra and is not true here.

Note the second row of that table independently: the router probability the kernel produces is about **0.53% high** for logits near -12. Switching the kernel to `log1p(exp(x))` would remove essentially all of it.

## Suggested fix

Two options, and the choice is yours since they differ in intent:

1. **Fix the reference only.** Use `log1pf(expf(v))` in the test and widen the tolerance enough to cover the kernel's genuine FP32 error at small logits. Keeps kernel behaviour, makes the check portable. The comment at `tests/test_deepseek41_metal.c:96` says the `1.0f +` form was chosen deliberately to match Metal, so this is the smaller change.
2. **Fix the kernel too.** Use `log1p(exp(x))` in `metal/dsv4_misc.metal:5188` and `:5349`, then keep a tight tolerance against an accurate reference. This also removes the 0.53% routing-probability error above.

## Scope of verification

Verified on Metal, M1 Ultra only. CUDA and ROCm untested. I do not have an M5 or M3 to confirm the check passes there.

title: v41: queue single-box decode layers and commit each without waiting (+37% decode on M3 Ultra, bit-exact)
body:
On a single Mac, `ds41_graph_step` commits **and waits** for the GPU after every one of the 40 layers; only the two-Mac TP path keeps the token's command buffers queued. This PR queues them on one box too (draining at layer 13, before the shared Engram input is reused, and at the last layer — exactly where the TP path drains) and additionally commits each queued layer without waiting, so the GPU starts a layer while the CPU encodes the next.

Related: #1034 (Dango233) opens the same queue as an opt-in restricted to SSD streaming, measured +11 % on an M2 Ultra Q2. The resident path gains more and nothing in the mechanism is streaming-specific, hence default-on here with rollback envs, mirroring the TP path's `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_TP_DECODE_QUEUE`.

### Measurements

Mac Studio M3 Ultra 512 GB, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Q4.gguf` fully resident, `./ds4 -p … -n N --temp 0`, ABBA on the same binary (A = per-layer drain via the rollback env, B = this PR), **generated text byte-identical in every pair** (md5 of the output equal across all runs).

| prompt / tokens | per-layer drain | queued | queued + commit per layer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2k / 128 | 17.08 / 16.78 t/s | 21.73 / 21.72 | — |
| 16k / 128 | 16.67 / 16.68 | 21.47 / 21.42 | — |
| 2k / 512 | 16.68 | 21.60 | — |
| 2k / 256 | — | 21.63 / 21.63 | **23.08 / 23.09** |

Per-token GPU stage timestamps (non-blocking, from #828, extended to the V4.1 graph on that branch) explain the size of the gain: with the drains, 37.3 ms of GPU busy inside a 46.9 ms span per token — 9.6 ms of scheduling gap from the 40 waits; queued, 36.9 ms busy in a 37.7 ms span (0.75 ms gap). The remaining per-token cost is the kernels themselves (routed experts 8.6 ms, attention output 4.8, attention projections 4.3, shared expert 3.1, router 2.7 …), which this PR does not touch.

Composes with #1035 (parallel Engram decode reads): both together 24.86 / 24.85 t/s on this box, i.e. +48 % over the current default.

### Rollbacks

- `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_DECODE_QUEUE=1`: per-layer drain on a single box (previous behaviour).
- `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_DECODE_FLUSH=1`: keep the token in one command buffer between drains (queue only).

Not changed: the batched-session path (`ds41_graph_step_batch` has its own layer-13 drain), TP, quality/imatrix modes (`layer_resident` still drains per layer).

title: v41: fuse the single-box decode glue (HC, MoE, attention): +20% on M3 Ultra on top of #1041, bit-exact
body:
## What

The V4.1 single-token decode graph mirrors the reference `model.py` op by op: per layer, 19 dispatches of hyper-connection glue (norm, mix matvec, split/sinkhorn, collapse, BF16 rounding, weighted norm, BF16, expand, BF16, …), 22 of MoE glue (router matvec + ten generic select dispatches; shared expert gate/up/down with three BF16 passes, SwiGLU and its rounding; the routed + shared sum and its rounding) and ~14 of attention glue (projections each followed by a BF16 rounding dispatch, two norms, RoPE, FP8 quantization, window copy, the heads' rounding + inverse RoPE). DeepSeek's production decode runs these as a handful of fused kernels per layer (tech report §3.2: Mega-mHC, Mega-Gate, fused RoPE-attention-cast).

This PR fuses ds4's sequences while keeping every reduction tree and every rounding point of the standalone kernels, so the output is byte-identical. Six commits, each its own step:

1. **HC glue (19 → 6)**: `kernel_dsv41_hc_collapse_norm4` (split/sinkhorn + collapse with the previous sublayer's `pre` + BF16 + weighted RMSNorm + BF16), `kernel_dsv41_hc_expand4_bf16` (post/comb expand + BF16, optional `pre` carry, optional folded routed + shared sum), and the existing exact norm+mix fusion `kernel_dsv4_hc_rms_norm_mix_f16` accepting V4.1's 4×5120 row (1024 norm threads and an empty matvec tail there too).
2. **Router (11 → 2; → 1 on M5)**: `kernel_dsv41_router_select` reproduces sqrt(softplus), the bias, the canonical (score desc, idx asc) top-6 and the normalized weights with the six-lane `sum_rows` reduction, the clamp, the row division and the scale as separately rounded ops. The single-dispatch form (last-arriving threadgroup selects, DeepSeek's Mega-Gate shape) is enabled on M5 only, like V4's `kernel_dsv4_router_project_select_fused`: on the M3 Ultra the other groups' logits were not reliably visible to the last one (nondeterministic output, caught by the on-box kernel test). Elsewhere the standalone F32 matvec runs first and one threadgroup selects.
3. **Shared expert (12 → 3)**: `kernel_dsv41_shared_gate_up_swiglu_q8_0` (both Q8_0 matvecs at the dispatch's nsg, gate/up rounded before SwiGLU, the product after), the down projection rounded on its store, and the routed + shared sum with its rounding folded into the FFN tail's expand. The down projection deliberately runs **before** the routed experts: a fused tail that read `shared_mid` after the routed kernel saw clobbered values on the M3 Ultra (greedy output differed) while the same kernel was byte-exact in isolation.
4. **Attention glue**: `kernel_dsv41_mul_mv_q8_0_f32_bf16` / `kernel_dsv41_mul_mv_f16_f32_4_bf16` (the standalone walks and reduction trees, nsg from the dispatch, the nr0=4 F16 shape included) round on the store, removing the rounding dispatch after q_a, q_b, kv, output_b, the shared down, the compressor and indexer projections; `kernel_dsv41_qkv_norm_kv_tail` does the q LoRA and KV weighted norms with their roundings, then the KV RoPE, FP8 (E8M0) block quantization and the raw-window store (6 → 1); `kernel_dsv41_bf16_rope` is the rounding pass over all heads plus the inverse RoPE (2 → 1); the logits' collapse + output norm reuse the collapse kernel without a split (4 → 1).

Single box only; the TP graph keeps the unfused sequences. Rollbacks: `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_HC_FUSE` (everything), `_MOE_FUSE`, `_ROUTER_FUSE`, `_SHARED_FUSE`, `_ATTN_FUSE`, `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_MATVEC_BF16`, `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_ROUTER_SINGLE_DISPATCH`.

## Tests

`tests/test_deepseek41_metal --hc-fuse`, `--moe-fuse`, `--attn-fuse` (also in the default suite on Apple): random data at V4.1's shapes, the standalone dispatch sequences through the public `ds4_gpu_*` entry points vs the fused kernels, `memcmp` on every output (mix, split, x, norm, expanded rows, carried `pre`; logits, probs, selected, weights, mid, shared, block; six matvec shapes, q/kv rows, window row, heads, the logits' x/norm). Pass on M4 Pro and M3 Ultra. Ties in the router (a zero-input round) are checked against the canonical order the fused select defines.

## Numbers

Mac Studio M3 Ultra 512 GB, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Q4.gguf` (resident), `./ds4 -m … -p <2k of promessi_sposi> -n 256 --temp 0`, on top of #1041 + #1035 (`DS4_ENGRAM_PARALLEL_DECODE=1`):

| | generation t/s | md5 of the 256 greedy tokens |
|---|---|---|
| all fusions | 29.80 / 29.88 | 40e4c6fa… |
| attention fusions + matvec bf16 off | 28.70 / 28.66 | 40e4c6fa… |
| everything off | 25.34 | 40e4c6fa… |

**+18-20 %**, output byte-identical. GPU busy per token (stage timestamps, #828) 36.9 → 31.2 ms; pre_attn 2.81 → 2.13, post_attn 2.16 → 1.16, after_moe 0.65 → 0.24, moe_route 2.70 → 1.15, moe_shared + FFN tail 3.07 + 0.65 → 2.50 + 0.24, attn_kv 0.69 → 0.27, attn_project 4.31 → 3.77. Prefill unchanged (the batched path is untouched).

Independent of #1041; measured on top of it because that is what the box runs.

title: metal: Q4_K group-6 expert table by default for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (+2.3% decode on M3 Ultra, greedy-identical)
body:
## What

The Q4_K routed experts of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (6 of 384, 5120 × 2304) run the generic `pair_swiglu` path. ds4 already ships opt-in expert-table kernels sized for 384-expert models (`DS4_METAL_ENABLE_Q4_GROUP6_EXPERT_TABLE` = 64 × 6, `..._GROUP8_...` = 48 × 8, `..._GROUP24_...` = 16 × 24). On V4.1 they are all faster than the default and the greedy output is identical; group-6 is the best. This makes group-6 the default for V4.1's routed shape only (`expert_in_dim == 5120 && expert_mid_dim == 2304`); other 384-expert models keep the opt-in, `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_Q4_GROUP6_EXPERT_TABLE` still turns it off.

## Numbers

Mac Studio M3 Ultra 512 GB, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Q4.gguf` (resident), `./ds4 -m … -p <2k of promessi_sposi> -n 256 --temp 0`, on top of #1041 + #1035 + #1042:

| routed path | generation t/s | md5 of 256 greedy tokens |
|---|---|---|
| group-6 expert table (this PR's default) | 30.57 / 30.56 | 40e4c6fa… |
| `pair_swiglu` (`DS4_METAL_DISABLE_Q4_GROUP6_EXPERT_TABLE=1`) | 29.89 / 29.85 | 40e4c6fa… |

64-token sweep of the opt-ins from the same prompt: pair_swiglu 30.25 / 30.20, group-6 31.00, group-8 30.82, group-24 30.50 (all md5-identical); `DS4_METAL_ENABLE_Q4_GROUPED_EXPERTS` runs at 0.38 t/s with a different output on this box and is not touched here. GPU stage timestamps (#828): moe_routed 8.68 → 8.07 ms per token.

One line, no kernel change.

title: Improve Metal router softplus accuracy for small logits
body:
Use a four-term log1p series for exp(x) below 1/32 in all four DeepSeek router transform sites. Clamp the polynomial input so its unselected branch stays finite, and compare Metal probabilities against the shared accurate reference without widening the tolerance.

Refs antirez/ds4#1039. Validated on M5 Max with a fresh default build, test_deepseek41_metal, test_deepseek41_graph --vision-routing, and full Metal test runs with DS4_METAL_DISABLE_PRE_M5_ROUTER_TRANSFORM_FINALIZE_FUSION=1 and DS4_METAL_MATH_SAFE=1. No model required. Pre-M5 validation and model-level speed/SSD checks remain outstanding.

title: V4 Flash 0731 (Q4K chat-v2 imatrix): greedy / low-temp decoding enters a verbatim repetition loop on long analytical answers
body:
## Summary
On M3 Ultra 256G, macOS, ds4 at bd66c40, the V4 Flash 0731 chat-v2 Q4 checkpoint falls into a
verbatim paragraph-level repetition loop when answering a long analytical prompt in Chinese
(find-the-bug task, ~4 KB script + symptom description). The loop persists regardless of
thinking mode or DSpark, and disappears at higher temperature.

## Reproduction matrix (same prompt, same model, `ds4 -p` one-shot, ctx 32768)
| Run | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | DSpark + `--temp 0` | loops after stating the correct root cause; repeats the same paragraph dozens of times (113 KB output) |
| 2 | no DSpark + `--temp 0.2 --top-p 0.9 --min-p 0.01` | loops (numbered analysis points cycle 18→19→20→…) |
| 3 | no DSpark + `--temp 0.2` + `--think` | loops (reaches item 55 and keeps cycling) |
| 4 | no DSpark + `--temp 0.8 --top-p 0.95` | clean completion, 4.5 KB, zero repetition |

## Notes
- Run 1 shows the model actually derives the correct root cause before degenerating, so this is
  a decode-sampling pathology, not a capability limit.
- DSpark is not the trigger (runs 2-3 loop without it), but since DSpark requires greedy
  sampling, the combination is effectively unusable for analytical prompts on this checkpoint.
- No repetition of this kind was observed on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Q2 resident / Q4 SSD
  streaming) or GLM 5.3 Flash Q4 with temp 0.2 on the identical prompt.

Happy to provide the raw outputs if useful.

title: ds4-agent: `-p` one-shot mode fails with "failed to start line editor"
