title: Metal: resolve keep-alive pipeline before starting keep-alive threads
body:
The queue keep-alive thread and the TP keep-alive thread each looked up `kernel_dsv4_tp_keepalive` themselves, via `ds4_gpu_get_pipeline(...)`. That lookup reads `g_pipeline_cache` and, on a miss, inserts into it. `g_pipeline_cache` is a plain `NSMutableDictionary`. The queue keep-alive thread is on by default and starts right after model view warm-up, which is exactly when the main thread is lazily compiling and inserting pipelines for the first prefill. Concurrent mutation of an `NSMutableDictionary` is undefined behaviour and can crash or corrupt the cache.

The fix:
- Resolve the pipeline once, on the thread that starts the keep-alive, into `g_keepalive_pipeline` before `pthread_create`. Both keep-alive threads use that copy.
- If it can't be resolved, don't start the thread. The TP path already prints "continuing without".
- `ds4_gpu_cleanup` drops the copy along with the cache, unless the TP keep-alive thread is still running.

## Testing

Tested on an M4 Max with 128 GB, macOS 27.0, Metal backend, with DeepSeek V4 Flash (`IQ2XXS-w2Q2K` Q2).

- `make ds4 ds4_test ds4-bench` and `make cpu` both build without warnings.
- `make test`: everything passes except `metal-kernels`. That one fails on exactly the same assertions on unmodified `origin/main` (ds4_test.c:1675, 1751–1755, 3312, 3362–3363), so it isn't caused by this PR.
- **The keep-alive thread still runs.** `sample` on a live `ds4 -p ... -n 3000` run shows `ds4_gpu_queue_keepalive_thread` in its dispatch loop (encoding at `ds4_metal.m:11353`, sleeping at 11363).
- **Speed.** I compared this branch with `origin/main` using `ds4-bench --prompt-file promessi_sposi.txt --ctx-start 2048 --ctx-max 8192 --step-incr 4096 --gen-tokens 64`, 3 reps in alternating order. The spread is within noise:

  | ctx | prefill t/s (main / PR) | gen t/s (main / PR) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 2048 | 307.6–314.5 / 308.1–318.5 | 31.09–31.26 / 30.94–31.56 |
  | 6144 | 261.6–275.3 / 263.5–273.0 | 29.45–29.94 / 29.58–30.45 |
  | 8192 | 259.5–267.0 / 255.4–266.5 | 29.32–29.76 / 29.41–29.96 |

- **Not shown:** I didn't reproduce the race itself, because the window is small and only happens at startup. The case for the fix rests on the code. I also couldn't test the TP keep-alive path, which needs a multi-Mac tensor-parallel setup.

title: Speed up callback-driven Metal prefill with layer overlap
body:
- Overlap CPU encoding of the next DeepSeek prefill layer with GPU execution of the previous layer, with at most two layers in flight. After the second layer, drain both command buffers before reporting completed progress. The final layer is always drained, including when the layer count is odd or logits are not requested.
- Avoid CPU/GPU races on cached attention-output group IDs: use a retained transient ID buffer when a pending command buffer could still read the cached one.
- Apply this only to resident, single-device, single-tier Metal prefill chunks of 32-512 tokens with a display-progress callback. Streaming, TP, nonresident placement, visual input, imatrix, profiling, power throttling, larger chunks, and the already-batched nonsplit path retain their existing scheduling. Set `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_PREFILL_LAYER_OVERLAP=1` to restore per-layer synchronization (`=0` enables overlap for same-process A/B tests).
- Add `--display-progress` to the Metal prefill variant benchmark so both variants exercise the server-style callback path.

## Why

Callback-driven split prefill previously waited for each layer to complete before encoding the next. A plain replacement of that wait with `ds4_gpu_flush_commands()` is unsafe: flush commits the current buffer, opens the next, and does not wait for completion. This change bounds retained work, uses the batch opened by flush, leaves CPU-written inputs immutable while GPU reads are pending, and emits progress only after completion.

## Performance

Measured on an M5 Max with 128 GiB RAM and the 81 GiB DeepSeek V4 Flash IQ2XXS model. Control and candidate were interleaved in ABBA/BAAB order (four runs each); the control set `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_PREFILL_LAYER_OVERLAP=1`. Timings cover `ds4_session_sync` through final logits, including output-head work and readback. All compared full-vocabulary logits were bit-exact.

| Callback prefill | Synchronized | Overlapped | Throughput change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 tokens, one chunk | 268.83 tok/s | 276.51 tok/s | +2.86% |
| 256 tokens, two 128-token chunks (first without logits) | 266.94 tok/s | 281.24 tok/s | +5.36% |
| 512 tokens, one chunk | 570.84 tok/s | 582.07 tok/s | +1.97% |

A separate 128-token Metal command-buffer trace showed about 18 ms of summed inter-buffer GPU gaps for the overlapped runs versus 29 ms for a later synchronized control, with roughly 411-412 ms of reported GPU busy time in both. Trace logging adds overhead, so this is diagnostic rather than a separate throughput estimate. Trials at 1024 and 2048 tokens did not show reliable gains (-0.85% with substantial drift and -0.59%, respectively); these sizes remain synchronized.

## Validation

- `make test-metal-command-memory`: all five modes passed under Metal API validation.
- Model-backed `tests/test_metal_session_batch`: passed with exact logits (`max_abs=0`).
- Callback-path ABBA/BAAB comparisons: bit-exact full-vocabulary logits, including an intermediate no-logits chunk. A 128-token run under `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1` was also bit-exact.
- No-callback benchmark mode: bit-exact; it takes the unchanged nonsplit path, so its noisy timing is not used as evidence of a speedup.

Injected GPU failures, actual server/TTY cancellation flows, and hardware other than this M5 Max were not tested. These should be validated before broadening the eligible paths.

title: Metal: reject unsupported shapes in five kernels (BF16 partial blocks, head groups, visual mask, Qwen4 n_rot, tile maxima)
body:
This PR adds five shape and argument guards, one commit each. One fixes a real bug, in GLM-5.3 vision. The other four are latent: no shipping model reaches them, but each covers undefined behaviour or silently wrong output if a future shape ever does.

1. **BF16 matmul uses the mat-vec kernel when `in_dim % 16 != 0`** (real, GLM-5.3 vision only). `kernel_mul_mm` dequantizes whole 16-value BF16 weight blocks, and `bc_inp` only zeroes the tail of the activation. With a partial last block, each row reads the start of the next row, and the last row reads past the end of the tensor. The activation zeros don't make that safe, because `NaN * 0` is still NaN. The only such shapes are the vision patch embeddings:
   - GLM-5.3 (`in_dim` 1176): the overread lands in the neighbouring weight row, so the output is slightly wrong.
   - DeepSeek V4 (`in_dim` 588): the weight is the last tensor in the GGUF, so the overread lands in the zero-filled page tail.
2. **Reject `n_head % 8 != 0` in `ds4_gpu_attention_indexed_mixed_batch_heads_tensor`** (latent). These kernels run 8 heads per threadgroup. Simdgroups past `n_head` return early and never reach the threadgroup barriers the rest of the group waits on, which is undefined behaviour. The DeepSeek V4 and GLM shapes use 64 or 128 heads, and TP splits them to 32.
3. **`ds4_gpu_fill_visual_mixed_batch_mask` rejects `n_raw > pos0 + n_tokens`** (latent). `first_raw_pos = pos0 + n_tokens - n_raw` would wrap in `uint32_t`, and the mask would hide the wrong keys. Callers pass the live raw ring row count, which is never that large.
4. **The Qwen4 indexer block-key kernels require `n_rot <= 64` and even** (latent). The kernels rope into `float tmp[64]` with `rope_freq[32]`. An odd `n_rot` would silently leave one dimension unrotated. `n_rot` comes from the model shape (64, or 8 for mini), which is checked against the GGUF at load.
5. **Pass tile maxima to the Qwen4 selector only when the scorer wrote them** (latent). Only the vectorized Metal scorer writes tile maxima. The prefiltered selector re-checked the device/env gate but not the scorer's shape limits (`n_idx_head * idx_dim <= 512`, `idx_dim % 4 == 0`), so a shape outside those limits would have selected top-k from stale maxima. The PR factors that decision into `ds4_gpu_qwen4_idx_score_emits_tile_max()`. The CUDA scorer always fills tile maxima when given a buffer, so its version returns 1. The shipping 4×128 indexer shape is inside the limits.

## Testing

Tested on an M4 Max with 128 GB, macOS 27.0, Metal backend.

- `make ds4 ds4_test ds4-bench` and `make cpu` both build without warnings.
- `make test`: everything passes except `metal-kernels`. That one fails on exactly the same assertions on unmodified `origin/main` (ds4_test.c:1675, 1751–1755, 3312, 3362–3363), so it isn't caused by this PR.
- `make test-qwen4-kernels`: all pass, including idx score (MM) and idx select.
- **GLM-5.3 vision (commit 1).** GLM-5.3 Flash Q2 with `GLM-5.3-Flash-Vision-Encoder.gguf`, `--temp 0 --nothink`, on an 896x504 image (576 image tokens):
  - Output is deterministic both before and after.
  - With the fix, the wording changes from the first token. Both descriptions are accurate.
  - Speed is unchanged. Prefill: 194.05 t/s before, 198.55 after. Generation: 27.03 before, 27.00 after.
- **Speed.** DeepSeek V4 Flash (`IQ2XXS-w2Q2K` Q2), `ds4-bench --prompt-file promessi_sposi.txt --ctx-start 2048 --ctx-max 8192 --step-incr 4096 --gen-tokens 64`, 3 reps in alternating order against `origin/main`:

  | ctx | prefill t/s (main / PR) | gen t/s (main / PR) |
  |---|---|---|
  | 2048 | 335.3–345.7 / 319.8–348.0 | 32.76–33.30 / 32.38–32.98 |
  | 6144 | 299.9–315.1 / 278.3–309.0 | 31.36–31.79 / 31.12–31.71 |
  | 8192 | 277.1–303.9 / 266.1–296.8 | 31.04–31.43 / 30.76–31.72 |

  The PR's low numbers all come from rep 3. The PR ran last in that rep, and both builds were already slowing down. Reps 1 and 2 match.
- **Not tested:**
  - The CUDA stub has not been compiled (no NVIDIA machine).
  - I didn't run Qwen3.8 end to end. On an M4 Max the vectorized scorer and the prefiltered selector are both off, so commit 5 doesn't change anything here.
  - No shipping model reaches the latent guards (2–5), so none of them has been triggered.

title: Metal MiMo V2.6 Flash text inference (resident Q2 experimental)
body:
## Scope

Add MiMo V2.6 Flash text inference on Metal: native 48-layer graph (9 global and 39 sliding-window layers, top-8 of 256 experts), ChatML turns, thinking and tool calls, server and agent integration, SSD expert streaming, and directional steering. Include native MTP and optional DFlash drafting, GGUF conversion/validation for Q2 and MXFP4, kernel checks, and conversion instructions. Source weights are pinned to XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL revision `5711b268169967567844e1e560e8a3966da959b1`. No model weights are in this PR.

## Quality status

This PR is a draft. The resident Q2 tiers are experimental and fail the planned quality gate. Against 100 temperature-zero, no-thinking Xiaomi FP8 continuations routed through OpenRouter (`xiaomi/fp8`), clean-imatrix Q2/Q8-attention matched the first token 65/100 (local mean NLL 0.339311); Q2/Q4-attention matched 62/100 (0.356618). MXFP4 with SSD streaming matched 92/100 (0.262704). MXFP4 and clean Q2 differ in hosted-match status on 29 cases, so their direct first-token agreement is at most 71/100, below the 89/100 resident-pair gate. Prefer MXFP4 SSD on a 128 GB Mac when quality matters. The earlier calibration corpus included all 100 fixture prompts; these Q2 scores use a new 200-prompt zero-overlap corpus, covering 12,020/12,032 expert slots.

Both hosted endpoints omit token logprobs. The fixture supports text continuation comparison and local teacher-forced NLL; no hosted probability-parity claim is made. API and local prompt-token counts matched 100/100. Full request settings, raw responses, case-level scores, and bounds are in `gguf-tools/quality-testing/mimo-v2.6-flash-20260924-openrouter/`; release criteria are in `QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md` section 20.

On a 128 GB M5 Max, recorded 4K-context/128-token rates were 669.60 prefill and 38.06 decode t/s for the initial resident Q2 artifact, versus 452.20 and 26.46 for GLM 5.3 Flash Q2. MXFP4 SSD recorded 38.74 prefill and 13.31 decode t/s. Clean Q2 passed 8/12 bounded hard-smoke and 53/92 mixed-budget core cases; MXFP4 passed 8/12 and 58/92. These are descriptive mixed-budget scores. Native MTP slowed one Q2 hard prompt (27.68 versus 39.63 t/s plain); DFlash draft width 3 reached 41.69 t/s in one run. Do not infer a general drafting speedup.

## Verification and limits

Built on Apple M5 Max, macOS Metal, 128 GB. Passed `make -j8`, `make -j8 test-mimo2-kernels test-dflash-kernels test-quality-api`, and `./ds4_test --server`. Real Q2 checks passed `--mimo2-mtp-verify` (three matching greedy streams), `--mimo2-dflash-verify` (three matching streams, up to eight committed tokens), one-pair direction capture (48 x 4096), and local server chat and structured tool calls. Source-backed Q2/MXFP4 GGUF validation is recorded in section 20.
The MXFP4 SSD CLI completed a cold 30-token prompt and eight-token continuation. The continuation stopped before an arithmetic answer; this run checks the streaming path only.

The full `make test` with this workstation's default GLM 5.3 GGUF failed 13 assertions in Flash-vector, SSD pressure, local-golden, and warm-state server groups. The same four groups and 13 assertions reproduced on untouched upstream main (`0aaea5a`) with the same GGUF. Isolated `./ds4_test --server` passes on both. An absent model stops the suite at its first model-required test; the matching Flash fixture model is unavailable locally. Metal text inference only; no CUDA, ROCm, vision, audio, or published download artifact is claimed. Resident Q2 remains unqualified pending a clean 89/100 pair gate.
The hosted `continuations/case_004.txt` ends with a literal space. It is retained verbatim; default `git diff --check` flags that raw-data line.

title: CUDA: give the ldmatrix helpers the .shared state space
body:
The three CUDA `ldmatrix` helpers (`tt_ldmatrix_x4_addr`, `tt_ldmatrix_x2_addr`, `tt_ldmatrix_x2_trans_addr`) take a 32-bit shared-memory offset from `__cvta_generic_to_shared`. The `ldmatrix` they emit has no state space, so PTX treats the operand as a generic address. ptxas then subtracts the shared window base from it a second time (visible in the SASS as `IADD3 Rn, Rm, -c[0x0][0x18]` just before `LDSM`), so the load reads outside the block's shared memory. The fix adds `.shared` to the three asm strings.

The vendored ggml `ldmatrix` in `cuda/mmq/mma.cuh` passes a 64-bit generic pointer (`"l"`) and is correct as is.

## Symptom

On an NVIDIA A10 (`sm_86`), `make test-qwen4-cuda` fails with `CUDA tensor read failed: an illegal memory access was encountered` in `test_attn_mm`, and none of the tests after it run. This is the same on unmodified `main` (0aaea5a) with nvcc 12.8 and nvcc 13.0. `compute-sanitizer` reports:

```
Invalid __shared__ read of size 16 bytes
  at tt_ldmatrix_x2_addr ... ds4_cuda.cu:10639
  Device Frame: qwen4_cuda::attention_group(...) ds4_qwen4_cuda.cuh:276
```

A standalone kernel that fills a `__shared__ __half[16][264]` and does one `ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n8.x4.b16` at offset 0 faults the same way on this A10. The same kernel with `.x4.shared.b16` runs with 0 sanitizer errors. A control kernel without `ldmatrix` runs fine, and the GPU is in pass-through mode (not vGPU).

## Testing

NVIDIA A10 24 GB (Lambda, Ubuntu 24.04, driver 580.105.08), CUDA backend, kernel tests only (no model weights).

| build | `test_qwen4_cuda` before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, nvcc 12.8, `CUDA_ARCH=sm_86` | illegal memory access in `test_attn_mm` | all 288 checks pass, "all qwen4 kernel tests passed" |
| `main`, nvcc 13.0 (container), `sm_86` | same crash | not rerun |

- `make cuda CUDA_ARCH=sm_86` builds without warnings, before and after.
- The fix also compiles without warnings for `sm_89`, `sm_120` and `cuda-spark` (`sm_121`), with nvcc 13.4 in a container (no GPU).
- `make test`, `make cpu` and `ds4-bench` on macOS: not applicable. `ds4_cuda.cu` isn't part of the Metal or CPU builds.

**Please check on Ada / Blackwell / Spark.** I haven't run the fix on those, only compiled it. My guess is that it works there today because those GPUs' shared window base has zero low 32 bits, so the extra subtraction does nothing, but I haven't verified that. The DeepSeek V4 Flash token-tile attention kernels use the same helpers with `tt_smem_addr()` offsets (ds4_cuda.cu:11137, 11282, 11287), so Flash's CUDA attention was probably affected on Ampere too. I haven't run it end to end.

title: Read integer request seeds without rounding them through a double
body:
`/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` read `seed` as a double and then cast it to `uint64_t`:

```c
r->seed = v > 0.0 ? (uint64_t)v : 0;
```

Two things go wrong for valid JSON integers:

- At or past 2^64 the cast is undefined. On x86-64 it yields 0, and a zero seed means "no seed" (`uint64_t rng = j->req.seed; if (!rng && !random_bytes(...))`), so `"seed": 18446744073709551615` or `"seed": 1e20` silently becomes a random seed. On arm64 the same cast saturates, so the result depends on the platform.
- Above 2^53 the double rounds, so different seeds collapse onto the same sampling stream (`9007199254740993` → `9007199254740992`).

This is the same kind of problem that 8340f35 fixed for `json_int()`; the seed path was left out.

The fix adds `json_seed()`. A plain integer is read from its digits with `strtoull()`, which saturates at `UINT64_MAX`. Any other number keeps the previous reading through a double, now clamped at 2^64 before the cast, so zero, negatives and NaN still mean "no seed" and requests that worked before parse the same way. Both parsers call the new helper.

Tested:
- `test_api_seed_parse` in the `DS4_SERVER_TEST` block (run by `ds4_test --server`): exact integers above 2^53, `UINT64_MAX`, one past it, `1e20`, `42.0`, `4.2e1`, `0`, `0.5`, `-1`, and non-numbers (`"42"`, `true`, empty input).
- Against the old conversion, the same cases fail 4 of 11 on x86-64 (2^53+1, `UINT64_MAX`, 2^64, `1e20`).
- On Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu 24.04, container): `make cpu` with gcc and clang without warnings, `ds4_test --server` (built with `-DDS4_NO_GPU`) and the other model-free steps of `make test`.

Not tested: macOS/Metal, CUDA or ROCm builds and anything that needs a model. The change is plain C in the request parser and does not touch sampling itself.

title: Vision: valid interlaced, 16-bit and low-bit grayscale PNGs are rejected
body:
`ds4_image_decode_memory()` returns "invalid or unsupported PNG image" for several kinds of valid PNG, because `third_party/iris/png.h` accepts only non-interlaced 8-bit images (plus palette images at 1/2/4/8 bits):

- interlaced (Adam7) images: `png_load_mem()` fails when the IHDR interlace byte is not 0
- 16-bit images of any color type (gray, gray+alpha, RGB, RGBA): `bit_depth != 8` fails
- grayscale at 1, 2 or 4 bits, which is common for scanned documents: the same check

The HF preprocessing these models are compared against loads images with PIL, which decodes all of these. Interlaced PNGs still show up on the web, and 16-bit PNGs come out of some screenshot and scientific tools. Today a client sending one gets an error, not a description of the image.

Repro, with no model: generate the images with Python's `zlib` and decode them with `png_load()` (the generator is 30 lines, happy to attach it):

```
rgb8.png         decoded
rgb8_adam7.png   REJECTED
rgb16.png        REJECTED
gray1.png        REJECTED
gray16.png       REJECTED
rgba16.png       REJECTED
```

The decoder fails closed, so this is not a safety problem. It is missing support, and the "unsupported" wording suggests the limit may be deliberate. Before writing anything: would you take a PR that adds Adam7 deinterlacing, 16-to-8-bit reduction and 1/2/4-bit grayscale expansion to `png.h`, with generated fixtures and checks in `tests/test_image_decode.c` like the JPEG ones? If you'd rather keep the decoder small, a clearer error ("interlaced PNG is not supported") would also help clients.

title: Anthropic API + Qwen: system message sent with a tool_result is dropped by live continuation, then forces a full re-prefill
body:
## Summary

With the Anthropic `/v1/messages` API and a Qwen3.8 model, a `role: "system"` message that the client adds in the **same request as a `tool_result`** is dropped by the live-continuation fast path. The model never sees it in that turn. On the next request the full render places that system message elsewhere in the prompt, so the live KV no longer matches and the whole prompt is prefilled again.

Claude Code triggers this every time a user sends a message while a tool is running. It delivers that message as a mid-conversation system note ("The user sent a new message while you were working: …") right after the tool result.

## Environment

- ds4 `0aaea5a` (main as of 2026-09-20), Metal, M1 Ultra 128 GB
- Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf`, `--ctx 65536 --batched-session 6`
- Client: Claude Code 2.1.280, persistent `--input-format stream-json` session, Anthropic API

## Reproduction

1. Send: ``Run `sleep 15; date -u` in bash and tell me the output.``
2. About 6 s later, while the tool is running, send: `Also: include the word PINEAPPLE in your answer.`
3. After the answer, send: `What exact word did I ask you to include earlier? Answer with the word only, or NONE.`

Request after the tool result (message tail, captured at the client):
```
3 user      tool_result: "Sat Sep 26 18:59:18 UTC 2026"
4 system    text: "The user sent a new message while you were working:\nAlso: include the word PINEAPPLE..."
```

Server log:
```
anthropic live continuation match=tool-output-ids ids=1 cached=14588 prompt=14624
chat ctx=14588..14624:36 TOOLS prompt start
chat ctx=14588..14624:36 gen=54 TOOLS finish=stop
live kv cache miss live=14678 prompt=14779 common=13041 vision=match reason=token-mismatch
chat ctx=0..14779:14779 TOOLS prompt start      <- full re-prefill, ~30 s
```

- Turn 1's answer only reports the date. `PINEAPPLE` is absent: the continuation added only the 36-token tool output.
- Turn 2's answer is `PINEAPPLE`: the full render includes the note.

## Expected

- The continuation path either appends every new message in the request, including a `system` message after the `tool_result`, or falls back to a full render when the request contains more than tool outputs.
- Mid-conversation system messages are rendered where they occur, so the next request still extends the live KV.

## Notes

`render_qwen_chat_prompt_text` collects all system-role messages into the top system block. That is also why per-turn client system notes invalidate the cache even without tools (related: #364). In our setup, rendering mid-list system messages in place, for example as a user-side note, would fix both symptoms.

title: Keep mid-conversation system messages in place (#1133)
body:
Fixes #1133. Related: #364.

**Problem.** Claude Code sends `role: system` notes inside `messages[]`. One example is a user message that arrives while a tool runs. ds4 dropped the note on the live tool-result path. It also moved every system message to the top of the prompt, so the next request missed the KV cache and prefilled the whole prompt again.

**Fix.** Only leading system messages go at the top. Later ones stay where they are (Qwen, GLM) and are kept in the live tail. DeepSeek V4 keeps its template and falls back to a full render. Prompts with no mid-list system messages are unchanged.

**Tested.** New server unit tests pass. On an M1 Ultra with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Claude Code: the note now reaches the model in the same turn, and the next turn prefills 17 tokens instead of the whole ~14.8k prompt.

title: Fix future-token leakage in Metal batched compressed attention
body:
# Fix future-token leakage in Metal batched compressed attention

This fixes future-token leakage in Metal's batched attention when using top-k
compressed keys.

Previously, the code built a correct causal mask, then overwrote its
compressed-key portion with the top-k selection mask. When fewer than `top_k`
causal keys existed, top-k could also select future keys scored at `-∞`. The
selection mask marked those entries as allowed (`0`), accidentally making
them visible to attention.

The fix replaces the plain mask copy in `ds4_metal.m` with
`kernel_dsv4_causal_comp_mask` in `metal/dsv4_misc.metal`. A compressed key
is visible only when both conditions hold:

- The compressed key is selected.
- Its index is below `(token_position + 1) / compression_ratio` (integer division).

Future compressed keys remain masked with `-∞`, regardless of selection.
Raw-key attention remains unchanged, including intentional bidirectional
attention within images.

The correction applies to both text and visual callers that use a compressed
selection mask through the shared batched-attention function. The normal
text top-k path uses a separate indexed-attention implementation; this PR
does not claim that all text inference was affected. The end-to-end reproducer
exercises visual prefill, and the analytic regression covers both wrappers.

The regression is included in `--metal-kernels`, with FP32/FP16 cached K/V,
selection patterns, compression boundaries, image/text queries, and a tensor
view with a nonzero offset.

## Related work

Closed PR #149 addressed a related first-prefill correctness issue by splitting
the initial chunk at 2048 tokens. This change instead enforces causality when
copying compressed-key selection into the visual attention mask, while keeping
raw image bidirectionality. A 2026-09-27 check found no equivalent fix in the
reviewed upstream PRs; upstream main was still `0aaea5a`.

## Correctness

Tested against baseline `0aaea5a238fb41a35106a551e73c8409dfb751ac` on an Apple
M5 Max with 128 GiB RAM, macOS 27.0 (26A428), Metal, and
`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8.gguf` with its
`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Encoder.gguf`.

- New analytic regression: original code fails with 110,592 mismatched values
  and maximum error 0.078125; fixed code has zero mismatches, maximum error
  5.96046e-8. All 64 test combinations pass after the fix.
- Real image suite: six fixture questions, short and ~3.1K-token prompts,
  before/after in resident and 16 GiB-cache SSD modes, plus a 2048-token-chunk
  causal control. All 60 generations finish and all fresh replays reproduce
  the complete next-token logit vector exactly.
- Short-prompt logits are bit-identical before/after in both resident and SSD
  modes. Fixed long-prompt logits are closer to the smaller-chunk control in
  all six cases, and match resident/SSD execution exactly.
- Strict fixture grading is 10/12 for every arm: both screenshot cases emit
  `exit status is **2**` instead of the literal substring `status 2`. Review
  confirms the required facts, including exit status 2. SSD's short-photo
  answer also contains an unsupported South America detail, identically in
  baseline and fixed output. These checks establish no observed regression;
  the small suite does not demonstrate general answer-quality improvement.
- `make -j8 cpu`, `make -B -j8 all`, `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`, image
  preprocessing/decoding tests, and `make -j8 test-frontends` pass.
- With `DS4_TEST_MODEL` set to the supplied file,
  `./ds4_test --long-context --tool-call-quality` passes: 30,474-token recall
  and tool-call handling in fast/exact modes.
- Existing `test_glm53_vision_prompt` passes image identity/reuse, invalidation,
  embedding sensitivity, and exact restoration in resident and SSD modes.

The checkpoint-matched follow-up on 2026-09-27 uses the publisher's
`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731.gguf`,
with its published SHA-256 verified:

- Baseline and patched builds pass all five official continuation cases
  (14 steps), the local golden fixture, and the 16 GiB SSD cache-pressure test.
- Full `make -j8 test DS4_TEST_MODEL=<Flash-0731 path>` passes, exit 0.
  The new causal-mask regression again has zero mismatches.
- The separately enabled SSD streaming decode-prefill test passes all five
  cases with a 16 GiB cache: cold/warm and repeated logits are exactly equal.
  Canonical versus optimized prefill passes existing numerical tolerances.
- Metal 4 automatic-route comparison passes all five cases on both builds,
  with identical printed metrics. The short cases have zero logit difference;
  long cases retain baseline numerical differences (worst RMS 0.910255,
  maximum absolute difference 4.34817), with no top-1 or greedy failures.
- The local golden fixture passes existing tolerances on both builds with
  identical reported results: top-20 overlap 20/20, top-64 overlap 58/64,
  top-20 maximum absolute difference 2.0019. This is not a bit-identity claim.

## Speed

Same hardware and the Vision-Exp model, AC power, power 100, one GPU workload at a time. Four
processes in before/fixed/fixed/before order. Each text sweep uses:

```sh
./ds4-bench --metal -m MODEL.gguf \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt --prefill-chunk 4096 \
  --ctx-start 2048 --ctx-max 32768 --step-incr 2048 --gen-tokens 128 \
  --csv RESULT.csv
```

| Aggregate rate | Before | Fixed | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill tokens/s | 661.1523 | 661.1742 | +0.0033% |
| Generation tokens/s | 39.2524 | 39.1504 | -0.2598% |

The measured text workload uses the separate indexed-attention path, so the
affected visual wrapper was measured separately. Median component latency: initial 2052-token batch
22.2360 to 17.4245 ms; late 2048-token batch at 32K, 25.6995 to 25.1845 ms.
The initial case removes invalid attention work and is not an equal-work
speedup claim. An initial 32-token-batch anomaly (0.5635 to 1.1610 ms) did not
persist in a longer-warmup ABBA run: 0.5640 to 0.5630 ms, with overlapping
interquartile ranges and 1000 measured samples per arm. The cause of the
transient was not established; both datasets are retained.

No sustained performance regression was demonstrated by these runs. The image
quality suite's incidental timings are not used for throughput claims.

## Coverage limits

Official continuation vectors were run against Flash-0731, separately from
the Vision-Exp image and performance runs. The full test command skips
Qwen3.8/GLM-specific cases and MTP/DSpark verification requiring other model
files; those paths are not claimed as validated. CUDA runtime and physical
distributed execution were not tested. No CUDA code, shared engine API, or
distributed protocol changes are included. Cross-batch-size logits are not
exactly equal, and this patch does not claim to resolve those existing
numerical differences.

Local evidence and reproduction details: `README.md` in this directory and
`../causal-mask-bench-20260926/README.md`, and
`../causal-mask-flash0731-20260927/README.md`, with raw CSVs, full logits,
answers, the comparison harness, and before/after regression logs. These ignored local
artifacts are not automatically included in a GitHub PR.

title: Anthropic: preserve visible output when thinking consumes a tiny remaining budget
body:
## Problem

For Anthropic `/v1/messages` requests on reasoning models, ds4 clamps `max_tokens` to the remaining context room. When only a small budget remains (for example 180 tokens), the model can spend the whole budget inside `<think>` and return no visible text. Claude CLI automatic compaction then reports an empty summary instead of recovering.

The current Anthropic overflow error also does not use the wording Anthropic clients recognise for a truncated-history retry.

## Proposed behavior

Add `--anthropic-thinking-min-budget N` with default `1024`; `0` disables it.

On the first decode pass only, when all of these hold:

- endpoint is Anthropic
- reasoning mode is active
- real decode budget is `<= N`
- no recovery completion or DSML recovery is active
- the stream is untouched

append the model syntax's think-close suffix tokens to the live KV state, update thinking and Anthropic stream state, then decode visible text. Derive the suffix from the model syntax's thinking and non-thinking generation prompts; do not hand-write model-specific token ids.

Also return Anthropic overflow text exactly as:

`prompt is too long: N tokens > M maximum`

OpenAI-compatible endpoints must remain byte-identical.

## Safety constraints

- Do not re-render, re-tokenise, re-parse, or cold-prefill the prompt.
- Use the decoder's real position, not rendered prompt length.
- Append pre-resolved suffix ids through the existing batched decode path under the model lock; do not call the session evaluator directly.
- Run only once and never after tool/recovery re-entry or after any stream output.
- Re-derive thinking and stream state after the suffix.
- If suffix evaluation fails partway, invalidate the session and clear live slot state before returning the existing error.
- A syntax without a pure close suffix is a no-op.
- Do not expose hidden reasoning as visible text.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover threshold values `180`, `1024`, `1025`, disabled `0`, reasoning off, recovery paths, already-streamed output, partial suffix failure, and unchanged OpenAI output.
- Qwen's derived suffix detokenises to exactly `\n</think>\n\n`.
- A near-limit Anthropic request with `max_tokens=180` returns a non-empty text block and no thinking block.
- Repeating a long prompt preserves KV reuse; continuation after a tail-closed answer does not cold-prefill.
- A normal high-budget reasoning request still emits thinking normally.
- `./ds4_test --server` passes.

This change is intentionally limited to the server.

title: Close reasoning at the tail when an Anthropic budget is tiny (#1136)
body:
A /v1/messages request whose prompt nearly fills --ctx is clamped to the room left (e.g. 180 tokens). A reasoning model spends all of it inside <think> and the client gets an empty answer.

When the real decode budget is <= --anthropic-thinking-min-budget (default 1024, Anthropic's minimum thinking budget; 0 disables), the first decode pass appends the model's think-close suffix ids to the live KV through the decode path, switches thinking and stream state to non-thinking, and decodes visible text. The suffix is the difference between the syntax's thinking and non-thinking generation prompts (Qwen: "\n</think>\n\n"; GLM: "</think>"; DeepSeek has none, so it is a no-op there). It is tokenized once at startup and checked to render back exactly with a single </think> token. The prompt is never re-rendered, so the prefilled KV is kept. The rule never runs after a recovery re-entry or once anything but message_start was streamed. If an id fails, the session checkpoint is invalidated and the slot's live state cleared before the existing error response.

The Anthropic overflow error now reads "prompt is too long: N tokens
> M maximum", which Anthropic clients retry with truncated history.
OpenAI-compatible bodies are unchanged.

title: cuda: make stream top-512 compaction decision uniform across warps
body:
Fixes #847.

## Problem

Long prompts on CUDA die with `an illegal memory access` shortly after the 32768-token mark, and the error poisons the CUDA context, so every following request fails until restart.

`indexer_topk_stream512_kernel` (picked for `top_k == 512`, `n_comp > 8192`, `n_tokens >= 32`, i.e. every prefill chunk past ~32k tokens on ratio-4 layers) tests `s_cnt` for compaction with no barrier before the next tile's `atomicAdd`. A warp that skips compaction can advance and bump `s_cnt` while a slower warp is still evaluating the test. The warps then disagree: one enters compaction alone (divergent `__syncthreads`), or all skip it while the 2048-entry shared buffer overflows.

## Fix

Read `s_cnt` once into a register, then `__syncthreads()` before acting on it, so every thread makes the same decision and no warp starts the next tile early.

## Test

New `cuda-regression` check `check_stream_topk_uniform_compaction`: 1024-token rows at `n_comp` 8193, 9728, 10240, 16421 and 32768. Even rows rise along the kernel's scan order, so every tile passes the threshold and the buffer hits its compaction boundary every fourth tile. Odd rows are random. All rows are checked rank by rank against a CPU top-k (value descending, index ascending).

Results on an NVIDIA A100-SXM-64GB (sm_80), CUDA 12.2:

| | Result |
|---|---|
| unfixed kernel, new check | `illegal memory access` at `n_comp=16421` iter 2 |
| `make cuda-regression` with the fix | OK, all sizes |
| `./ds4_test --server` | OK |

End to end on 4×A100-64GB with `--cuda --cuda-tensor-parallel --gpu-devices 0,1,2,3`, `--ctx 131072`, model `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731`, 66,564-token `--prompt-file`:

| | Result |
|---|---|
| unfixed, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | `CUDA indexer topk stream launch failed: an illegal memory access`, layer 2, right after the 32768-token chunk |
| unfixed + `DS4_CUDA_NO_TOPK_STREAM=1` | OK, prefill 618 t/s |
| fixed | OK, prefill 624 t/s |

The fix adds one barrier per 512-candidate tile; I measured no prefill slowdown.

## Relation to #975

#975 targets the same crash by switching the kernel to 256 threads × 8 items. That keeps the unsynchronized `s_cnt` test, so the race remains; the CUB `BlockExchange` fault in the #847 coredump is where warps that disagree about compaction end up, not a separate CUB problem. With the #975 kernel patched into the same tree, the new check fails in 3 of 3 runs on A100 (`illegal memory access` at `n_comp=8193`, `8193` and `9728`). The fixed kernel passes 3 of 3. #975's own check uses 32 tokens of hashed data, which rarely drives the buffer to the compaction boundary while warps are out of step.

title: Reject malformed chunked HTTP request framing
body:
## Summary

Adds bounded, strict HTTP chunked-transfer request decoding. Rejects ambiguous
Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding framing, repeated or unsupported transfer
encodings, invalid header names and controls, malformed chunk sizes/extensions,
and non-CRLF chunk/trailer boundaries. Chunk-extension whitespace is accepted
only when attached to a following semicolon or equals sign.

The encoded request body remains bounded at 64 MiB. Socket regressions exercise
valid fragmented requests and malformed requests through the production client
path, asserting HTTP 400, connection close, and client-count discharge.

## Verification

- Apple clang 21.0.0, arm64 macOS: `make -j2 ds4_test ds4-server`
- `./ds4_test --server`: `server: OK`, `ds4 tests: ok`
- The new whitespace regression failed with 24 assertions before the fix and
  passed after it.
- `git diff --check 0aaea5a238fb41a35106a551e73c8409dfb751ac..3373b75aae45a562bbcdc7ca503c99aca1639c80`
- Independent source review found no blockers in the cumulative patch.

These are model-free parser/socket tests and source review, not deployed-server
or inference qualification. No inference backend, model, or GPU operation changed;
backend throughput/model regression runs do not apply.

title: Let Qwen and GLM make several tool calls per turn
body: This PR adds support for parallel tool calls for Qwen and GLM models. Previously, DS4 stopped decoding after the first tool call, so these models could only make one call per turn. I've tested this against Qwen3.8 Flash Next, GLM-5.3 Flash, and GLM-5.3.

title: [ROCm 10.0 / gfx1151] Pipeline-parallel coordinator segfaults in libhsa-runtime64 on a large D2H hipMemcpy (bare-HIP control is fine)
body:
## Summary

Pipeline parallelism (2 ranks, 2× Strix Halo / `gfx1151`, ROCm 10.0) **segfaults in ROCm's
`libhsa-runtime64`** as soon as the coordinator prefills the prompt. The route is established
correctly; the crash happens inside a device→host `hipMemcpy`.

Localized with gdb to a crash that, **within the ds4 coordinator process**, follows a size boundary:

> **In the ds4 PP coordinator process**, a single D2H `hipMemcpy` of more than 1 MiB (2^20 bytes)
> crashes inside `hsa_amd_memory_unlock → MemoryRegion::Unlock → KfdDriver::MakeMemoryUnresident →
> hsaKmtUnmapMemoryToGPU → hsakmt_fmm_unmap_from_gpu → vm_find_object` (NULL/garbage
> dereference). Copies ≤ 1 MiB from the *same* device address succeed.

⚠ **Important correction (added same day): this is NOT a general HIP/ROCm size limit.** A bare HIP
program on the same machine, same ROCm, does D2H copies of up to 16 MiB fine — including with 85 GiB
of GTT already committed. So the "1 MiB" boundary is a property of the **ds4 process state**, not of
`hipMemcpy` itself. See the "Update" section right below; read that before drawing conclusions from
the threshold table.

The copy is in-bounds (the source pointer is the base of a 128 MiB device allocation and only
~1.5 MiB are read). Within the ds4 process the trigger tracks the **copy size**, not the buffer: the
same 1,638,400-byte copy also crashes when taken from an unrelated, known-good workspace buffer.

I am reporting it here because it makes the PP coordinator unusable on this platform, and because
the ds4 side can work around it. I believe the defect itself is in ROCm; details for a robust
workaround and for a ROCm report are at the bottom. (I built from `kyuz0/ds4`, branch
`main-gfx1151`, which has issues disabled — hence this report.)

---

## Update — what the "1 MiB" threshold is *not*

Two controls added after the initial report:

**1) A bare HIP program does not reproduce it.** Same machine, same ROCm 10.0, same `gfx1151`:

```
hipGetDeviceCount -> hipSuccess, ndev=1
hipMalloc(268435456) -> hipSuccess
--- pageable destination ---
  D2H       4096 B ... hipSuccess (0)
  D2H      65536 B ... hipSuccess (0)
  D2H    1048576 B ... hipSuccess (0)
  D2H    1245184 B ... hipSuccess (0)
  D2H    1638400 B ... hipSuccess (0)
  D2H    4194304 B ... hipSuccess (0)
  D2H   16777216 B ... hipSuccess (0)
--- pinned (hipHostMalloc) destination ---
  ... all sizes up to 16 MiB: hipSuccess (0)
ALL OK
```

…and it still passes when the process first commits a large GTT allocation, i.e. GTT pressure alone
is not the trigger:

```
hipMalloc(32 GiB) -> hipSuccess ; hipMemset -> hipSuccess ; D2H up to 4 MiB -> all OK
hipMalloc(64 GiB) -> hipSuccess ; hipMemset -> hipSuccess ; D2H up to 4 MiB -> all OK
hipMalloc(85 GiB) -> hipSuccess ; hipMemset -> hipSuccess ; D2H up to 4 MiB -> all OK
```

**2) ds4's zero-copy host-registration path is not involved.** `ds4_rocm_runtime.cuh` has a
`cudaHostRegister(..., cudaHostRegisterMapped | cudaHostRegisterReadOnly)` fallback for
non-device-cached model ranges (`ds4_rocm_runtime.cuh:4651`), which would be a natural suspect for
`hsa_amd_memory_unlock`. Counting hits at that exact line while reproducing the crash:

```
readback hits        = 1
hostRegister attempts = 0
```

So the crash reproduces **without** any `cudaHostRegister` call. That hypothesis is out.

**Net effect on the diagnosis:** the reproducible facts are (a) the crash site/backtrace,
(b) the crash happens in the ds4 coordinator process and not in a bare HIP program, (c) inside that
process it is deterministic and size-tracking (≤1 MiB OK, >1 MiB crash, same address). What *ds4-side
process state* makes it fatal is **not yet identified** — treat the 1 MiB figure as an observed
boundary inside that process, not as a root cause. Any hint you have about ROCm-specific state that
ds4 sets up (streams, device flags, allocation flags, per-thread HIP contexts) would help narrow it.

---

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Hardware | 2× AMD Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S), `gfx1151`, 128 GB unified memory |
| OS | **Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (Noble Numbat)** on **both** ranks — kernel `6.17.0-23-generic`, `x86_64` |
| ROCm | **10.0.0** — 46 `amdrocm*` packages incl. `amdrocm-core-dev10.0-gfx1151 10.0.0-4`, installed at `/opt/rocm/core-10.0` |
| ROCm apt track | `deb [arch=amd64 trusted=yes] https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/core/packages/ubuntu2404 stable main` |
| Runtime libs in the crash | `libhsa-runtime64.so.1` → `libhsa-runtime64.so.1.21.0`; `libamdhip64.so.7` → `libamdhip64.so.7.15.26333-0000000` |
| Install layout | `/opt/rocm` is a symlink to `/opt/rocm-7.2.4`, so ROCm 10.0 physically lives at `/opt/rocm-7.2.4/core-10.0` (side-by-side with a pre-existing ROCm 7.2.4) |
| Interconnect | USB4 / Thunderbolt direct link, `10.10.11.1` ↔ `10.10.11.3` |
| Build | `make strix-halo -j4 ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151 HIPCC=/opt/rocm/core-10.0/bin/hipcc` |
| Source | `kyuz0/ds4`, branch `main-gfx1151` (tarball `codeload.github.com/kyuz0/ds4/tar.gz/refs/heads/main-gfx1151`) |
| Model | `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf`, `190,875,526,464` bytes, sha256 `c7a0d950363238dd7804782c88340d737775aba53a15f8d4fdcc34e984f25221` (identical on both ranks) |
| Ranks | coordinator = rank holding layers `0:22` (+ output head), worker = `23:output` |

Notes on the environment, in case they matter:

- Our hosts are **24.04.5 (noble)**, not the Ubuntu 26.04 setup mentioned in
  `docs/STRIX_HALO.md`; we consume the `ubuntu2404` ROCm 10 track. Flagging this because it is the
  one place where our environment differs from the documented gfx1151 reference.
- The model is the same artifact that `./download_model.sh glm53-q4` resolves to. We fetched it
  with `aria2c` from an HF mirror rather than through the script's `hf` CLI path (the mirror has no
  Xet endpoint, so the CLI path cannot handle a 178 GiB file); size and sha256 were verified on
  both ranks.
- `glm5-next.block_count` = 45 transformer blocks, so `--layers 0:22` is 23 blocks and
  `23:output` is 22 blocks plus the output head.

---

## Reproduction

Both ranks use the same binary and the same GGUF.

```sh
# ---- worker (station C, 10.10.11.3) ----
cd ~/ds4
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm/core-10.0/lib/rocm_sysdeps/lib:/opt/rocm/core-10.0/lib
./ds4 --rocm --role worker --layers 23:output --coordinator 10.10.11.1 9911 \
      -m gguf/GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf -c 4096

# ---- coordinator (station B, 10.10.11.1) ----
cd ~/ds4
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm/core-10.0/lib/rocm_sysdeps/lib:/opt/rocm/core-10.0/lib
./ds4 --rocm --role coordinator --layers 0:22 --listen 10.10.11.1 9911 \
      -m gguf/GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf -c 4096 -p "Hi"
```

The worker is started first (as documented) and retries while the coordinator loads.

Reproduced in **every** attempt — 6 runs total: launched through our orchestrator, a plain CLI
run, a `ds4-server --role coordinator` run, with `-c 4096` and `-c 8192`, and in the gdb sessions
below.

---

## Observed

The route forms normally, then the coordinator dies with `SIGSEGV` (exit status `139`, core dumped):

```
ds4: ROCm backend initialized on AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics (sm_115)
ds4: restricting rocm model map to layers 0:22+output (48 spans, 84.64 GiB tensor span)
ds4: startup model preparation covered 84.64 GiB of tensor spans in 0.000s
ds4: memory: KV 0.04 GiB (raw 0.00 + compressed 0.04) + buffers 2.86 GiB + resident model 84.64 GiB = 87.55 GiB planned
ds4: GLM graph using compact DSA KV only; expanded full-attention KV cache is skipped
ds4: GLM graph allocating compact DSA cache: rows=4096 logical_ctx=4096 kv_layers=23 indexer_layers=5 f16 0.02 GiB
ds4: distributed coordinator API: listening on 10.10.11.1:9911 model_id=3 layers=45 local=0:22 activation_bits=32
ds4: waiting for distributed route: distributed route incomplete: missing layer 23
ds4: distributed coordinator: registered worker 10.10.11.3:37436 data_port=35969 model_id=3 quant=Q4 layers=23:output hidden=1 ctx=8192
ds4: distributed coordinator: complete route ready: local 0:22 -> 10.10.11.3:35969 Q4 23:output
ds4: distributed route ready
--- SIGSEGV ---
timeout: the monitored command dumped core
```

(The excerpt is representative; the `ctx=8192` on the "registered worker" line is from the
`-c 8192` run — everything else is identical for `-c 4096`.)

The worker then logs `distributed worker: coordinator disconnected; reconnecting`.

---

## Backtrace (gdb, symbolized build)

```
Thread 1 "ds4" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x00007fffe5ddd66d in vm_find_object () from /opt/rocm/core-10.0/lib/libhsa-runtime64.so.1

#0  vm_find_object                                  libhsa-runtime64.so.1
#1  hsakmt_fmm_unmap_from_gpu                       libhsa-runtime64.so.1
#2  hsaKmtUnmapMemoryToGPU                          libhsa-runtime64.so.1
#3  rocr::AMD::KfdDriver::MakeMemoryUnresident(void const*) const
#4  rocr::AMD::MemoryRegion::Unlock(void*) const
#5  rocr::AMD::hsa_amd_memory_unlock(void*)
#6..#20  libamdhip64.so.7 (hipMemcpy internals)
#20 hipMemcpy                                        libamdhip64.so.7
#21 ds4_gpu_tensor_read        rocm/ds4_rocm_runtime.cuh:6048
#22 glm_graph_forward_indexed_tokens                   ds4.c:55032
#23 ds4_session_eval_layer_slice                       ds4.c:74518
#24 dist_coordinator_eval_span                         ds4_distributed.c:2733
#25 dist_coordinator_prefill_prompt                    ds4_distributed.c:3815
#26 ds4_dist_session_sync                              ds4_distributed.c:5620
#27 ds4_session_sync_internal                          ds4.c:75263
#28 ds4_session_sync                                   ds4.c:75108
#29 run_sampled_generation                             ds4_cli.c:575
```

The faulting instruction is a table walk with a corrupted base pointer:

```
vm_find_object+500: mov (%rax,%r10,1),%rax
rax = 0xbd08a4c4bb55ca79      <-- not a valid pointer
```

So `vm_find_object` is asked to look up an address that is not in the GPU VM map, and the lookup
path dereferences a bad pointer instead of returning "not found".

---

## Where the copy comes from, and that it is in-bounds

At `ds4.c:55032`:

```c
if (ok && output_hc) {
    ok = ds4_gpu_tensor_read(g->glm53 ? hc_cur : cur,
                             0,
                             output_hc,
                             (uint64_t)n_tokens * DS4_N_EMBD *
                                 (g->glm53 ? DS4_N_HC : 1u) *
                                 sizeof(float)) != 0;
}
```

`ds4_gpu_tensor_read` (DS4 ROCm runtime) is a plain D2H copy:

```c
extern "C" int ds4_gpu_tensor_read(const ds4_gpu_tensor *tensor, uint64_t offset, void *data, uint64_t bytes) {
    if (!tensor || !data || offset > tensor->bytes || bytes > tensor->bytes - offset) return 0;
    return cuda_ok(cudaMemcpy(data, (const char *)tensor->ptr + offset, (size_t)bytes,
                              cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost), "tensor read");
}
```

Values read at the breakpoint (`-c 4096 -p "Hi"`):

| Symbol | Value |
|---|---|
| `n_tokens` | 19 (the chat template makes even `"Hi"` 19 tokens) |
| `hc_cur->bytes` (requested bytes) | **1,245,184** = 19 × 4096 × 4 × 4 |
| `hc_cur->ptr` | `0x7fbc8d000000` |
| `g->batch_hc_next->ptr` | `0x7fbc8d000000` (**delta 0x0 — the view is not stale/dangling**) |
| `g->batch_hc_next->bytes` | `134,217,728` (128 MiB; the read uses < 1 % of it) |
| `output_hc` (host destination) | `0x55555809f660` (plain `malloc` in `dist_coordinator_eval_span`, `ds4_distributed.c:2708`) |

So: valid device source, in-bounds length, ordinary pageable host destination.

---

## Localization: manual `hipMemcpy` at the breakpoint

Rather than guess, I stopped at `ds4.c:55032` and called `hipMemcpy(dst, src, n, 2 /*D2H*/)`
directly from gdb.

| Copy size | Source | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 4,096 B | `batch_hc_cur->ptr` | OK (returned 0) |
| 4,096 B | `hc_cur->ptr` | OK (returned 0) |
| 65,536 B | `batch_hc_cur->ptr` | OK (returned 0) |
| 262,144 B | `batch_hc_cur->ptr` | OK (returned 0) |
| 524,288 B | `batch_hc_cur->ptr` | OK (returned 0) |
| **1,048,576 B** | `batch_hc_cur->ptr` | OK (returned 0) |
| **1,245,184 B** | `hc_cur->ptr` | **SIGSEGV** (19-token prompt readback) |
| **1,638,400 B** | `hc_cur->ptr` | **SIGSEGV** (25-token prompt readback) |
| **1,638,400 B** | `batch_hc_cur->ptr` (**a different, known-good buffer**) | **SIGSEGV** |

Conclusion: **within the ds4 process**, the fault is a function of the **single-copy size** (> 1 MiB),
not of the source buffer, not of the tensor bookkeeping, and not of alignment. 4 KiB from the exact
address that fails at 1.5 MiB succeeds. (Remember the Update section: a bare HIP program is fine at
16 MiB, so this table characterizes the ds4 process, not `hipMemcpy`.)

---

## Why single-rank GLM 5.3 Flash works and PP does not

The coordinator reads back **the entire prompt's** hidden state to ship it over TCP:

```
bytes = n_tokens * DS4_N_EMBD * DS4_N_HC * 4 = n_tokens * 65,536
```

so **any prompt longer than 16 tokens exceeds 1 MiB**. A chat-templated `"Hi"` is already 19
tokens → 1,245,184 B → crash. Longer prompts are proportionally worse.

Note this is about the *readback size*, and more fundamentally about the fact that **single-rank
inference never performs this readback at all**: `output_hc` is only passed on the layer-slice /
distributed path (`ds4_session_eval_layer_slice`). Single-rank generation calls
`glm_graph_forward_indexed_tokens` with `output_hc = NULL` and only reads back logits
(~593 KiB), which is why the same build/ROCm/machine is fine single-rank — independent of where the
size boundary happens to sit.

Single-rank GLM 5.3 Flash is fine on the very same build, same ROCm, same machine:

```
$ ./ds4 --rocm -m gguf/GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf --ssd-streaming --ctx 4096 -p "Say hello in one short sentence."
...
processing 25 input tokens: 25/25 (100.0%)
Hello there!
ds4: prefill: 0.41 t/s, generation: 0.44 t/s
```

---

## Ruled out

- **Context size** — crashes at `-c 4096` and `-c 8192`.
- **Server layer** — `ds4 --role coordinator` (CLI) crashes identically to `ds4-server`.
- **Race / concurrency** — `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0`
  changes nothing.
- **Pinned vs pageable host** — `ds4.c` contains no `cudaMallocHost` for this path; single-rank
  readbacks are pageable too and work.
- **Bad pointer / OOB in ds4** — source pointer equals the base of a live 128 MiB allocation
  (delta 0x0); requested bytes are 1.5 MiB.
- **Managed memory** — `batch_hc_*` workspace buffers come from `ds4_gpu_tensor_alloc`
  (`cudaMalloc`), not `..._alloc_managed`.

---

## Likely mechanism (hypothesis)

The crash is in the **unlock / make-unresident** path, i.e. HIP's `hipMemcpy` appears to switch to a
different implementation above ~1 MiB that locks/unlocks the host region (or reshapes residency),
and that path mismatches with the KFD/VM bookkeeping on `gfx1151` under ROCm 10.0. Two candidate
directions:

1. `hsa_amd_memory_unlock()` / `MakeMemoryUnresident()` should not fault when the region was never
   GPU-mapped — `vm_find_object()` should return NULL and the caller should handle it, rather than
   walking a corrupted table.
2. The >1 MiB `hipMemcpy` D2H path may be picking a copy engine / staging sequence that leaves the
   FMM map inconsistent on this APU.

I have not disassembled `libamdhip64.so.7` and, after the Update controls above, I can no longer
claim a specific HIP-side trigger — a bare HIP program does 16 MiB D2H without issue, so the fatal
part is some **ds4-process-specific state**. What is solid: the crash site (ROCr's host-unlock /
make-unresident path), and the fact that it is deterministic inside the ds4 process. Treat the
mechanism as open.

---

## Suggested fixes

**ds4 side (workaround, unblocks PP today):**

- Chunk the coordinator's hidden-state readback in
  `glm_graph_forward_indexed_tokens` / `ds4_gpu_tensor_read` call site into pieces of ≤ 1 MiB
  (e.g. per ≤16 tokens), or
- Stage the readback through a pinned host buffer (may also select a different HIP path), or
- Read back with several smaller `hipMemcpy` calls / a stream-ordered sequence.

Because the threshold is exactly at a power-of-two boundary (2^20), chunking at 1 MiB should be
sufficient, and it is a small, local change.

**ROCm side:** the unlock/unmap path should be robust to unmapped regions (see hypothesis above).

---

## Honest caveat about support status

I am aware that the docs describe GLM 5.3 Flash on ROCm via the **single-rank SSD-streaming** path
(`STRIX_HALO.md`: *"Flash's ROCm resident and pipeline paths should not be confused with the GLM
SSD-streaming path"*), that `glm53-q2` is the artifact marked *"ROCm also supported"*, and that
two-machine GLM is documented as **ownership-aware TP (Metal)** while ROCm TP is rejected by the
source gate. So `glm53-q4` + ROCm pipeline parallelism is very likely an untested combination — this
report is not a complaint about a promised feature being broken. I am filing it because:

- the **failure mode is silent-ish and drastic** (SIGSEGV with core, after a healthy-looking
  start-up and a complete route), which is expensive to diagnose, and
- the root cause is **not specific to GLM**: I was able to reproduce it as a pure
  `hipMemcpy` D2H > 1 MiB crash, independent of the model and of the source buffer, so it can bite
  any future ROCm PP path (or any readback of more than one token's hidden state).

---

## Artifacts available on request

- Full `gdb` transcripts (backtrace, registers, faulting instruction, the manual-copy matrix).
- Coordinator and worker logs for the run (`coordinator.log`, `worker.log`).
- Exact `--help distributed` output of the build.

Happy to run any additional experiment (e.g. a reduced repro, `--dist-activation-bits`, different
`--layers` split, or a two-rank test with a smaller model) — the cluster is idle and reproducible.

---

## Update 2 — the two failure modes are mutually exclusive, and the ROCm side is avoidable from ds4

Further experiments. I swept the **per-span readback size** on the coordinator with the existing
`--dist-prefill-chunk` knob (same two ranks, same model, `-c 4096`, everything else unchanged):

| `--dist-prefill-chunk` | per-span readback | result | failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (≥ prompt) | whole 19-token prompt = 1.22 MiB | exit **139** | ROCm HSA `vm_find_object` SIGSEGV (the original defect) |
| 16 | 1.00 MiB | exit **139** | same |
| 12 | 768 KiB | exit **139** | same |
| 10 | 640 KiB | exit **134** | **ds4 heap corruption**: `malloc(): unsorted double linked list corrupted` |
| 8 | 512 KiB | exit **134** | **ds4 heap corruption** — reproduced on *both* the pipelined path and the `DS4_DIST_DISABLE_PREFILL_PIPELINE=1` fallback loop |

Two conclusions:

1. **The HSA crash is avoidable from the ds4 side.** Below ~768 KiB per span the `hsa_amd_memory_unlock`
   SIGSEGV no longer occurs, which suggests it is the *large single D2H readback* in this process
   that trips the host-unlock/unmap path, not "ROCm cannot do this".
2. **A second, independent defect shows up instead: ds4 corrupts its own heap on the chunked-span
   path.** glibc aborts; the thread that actually trips is ROCr's `AsyncEventsLoop`, i.e. it is the
   victim of someone else's out-of-bounds write, not the culprit. Two different glibc messages seen
   (`unsorted double linked list corrupted`, `malloc_consolidate(): invalid chunk size`,
   `unaligned fastbin chunk detected`).

⇒ **There is no flag combination that makes PP run**: one failure mode brackets the other from
above and below. Getting PP working needs a source-level fix to the heap corruption (or to whatever
else in the distributed span machinery writes out of bounds), not a configuration change.

### Why the default always takes the single-span path

From `ds4_distributed.c`:

```c
static bool dist_coordinator_can_pipeline_prefill(..., uint32_t n_tokens, uint32_t chunk_cap) {
    if (getenv("DS4_DIST_DISABLE_PREFILL_PIPELINE")) return false;
    ...
    if (chunk_cap == 0 || n_tokens <= chunk_cap) return false;   /* <- chunk_cap defaults to the session prefill cap */
```

With the default, `chunk_cap` is the session prefill cap (thousands), so `n_tokens <= chunk_cap` is
always true for an ordinary prompt, the pipelined path is never taken, and
`dist_coordinator_prefill_prompt` falls through to the plain loop — which then evaluates the whole
prompt in **one** span, i.e. exactly one `n_tokens * 65536`-byte D2H readback. That is the copy
that dies.

### A note on localising the heap corruption

An ASan build would be the obvious next step, but it does not link with this toolchain:

```
ld.lld: error: ds4_cli.o: SHT_STRTAB string table section [index 37] is non-null terminated
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: __asan_report_store8        (and the other __asan_* symbols)
```

(i.e. `ld.lld` rejects clang's ASan-instrumented objects; the next attempt would be `-fuse-ld=bfd`
plus linking `libasan`). Minimal repro for whoever wants to chase it:
`./ds4 --rocm --role coordinator --layers 0:22 --listen <ip> 9911 -m <glm53 q4> -c 4096 --dist-prefill-chunk 10 -p "Hi"`.

title: speed-bench: M4 Max 64 GB — Qwen3.8 Flash Next Q2 (full 2K–64K sweep) and Flash Q2 with SSD streaming
body:
Adds two `ds4-bench` sweeps from a 64 GB Mac Studio M4 Max, both with the documented command and the full `--ctx-max 65536` range.

**Machine:** Mac Studio (Mac16,9), Apple M4 Max, 64 GB, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), internal 1 TB SSD. `iogpu.wired_limit_mb=57344` (raised; see notes). Metal, plain `make` at `0aaea5a`, clean worktree.
**Models:** `./download_model.sh qwen38-q2` and `./download_model.sh ds4f-q2`, sha256 checked against the HF LFS oids.

**Command:** `./ds4-bench -m MODEL --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt --ctx-start 2048 --ctx-max 65536 --step-incr 2048 --gen-tokens 128`, with no extra flags for Qwen and `--ssd-streaming` for Flash (automatic cache budget: 35.42 GiB effective dynamic cache + 3.38 GiB prefill headroom, 48.36 GiB planned).

Runs used alternating order, with other GPU workloads stopped. Each configuration has 3 valid runs. For Flash that took 4 attempts: one was excluded by a swap rule fixed before the runs (see notes). The committed CSV per configuration is one unmodified run: the valid run closest to the per-frontier medians. The table shows median (min–max) over the 3 valid runs:

| model | ctx | prefill t/s | gen t/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.8 Q2 | 2048 | 616.4 (595.6–617.0) | 41.24 (35.68–41.24) |
| Qwen3.8 Q2 | 16384 | 590.6 (590.2–591.1) | 40.98 (40.43–41.05) |
| Qwen3.8 Q2 | 32768 | 581.8 (580.2–582.3) | 40.81 (40.49–40.83) |
| Qwen3.8 Q2 | 65536 | 579.5 (578.7–580.4) | 40.34 (40.25–40.59) |
| Flash Q2, `--ssd-streaming` | 2048 | 156.0 (137.5–157.4) | 12.85 (12.34–13.66) |
| Flash Q2, `--ssd-streaming` | 16384 | 138.2 (93.1–141.1) | 15.59 (15.41–15.99) |
| Flash Q2, `--ssd-streaming` | 32768 | 138.0 (134.2–138.8) | 14.83 (14.60–15.36) |
| Flash Q2, `--ssd-streaming` | 65536 | 123.1 (86.2–132.5) | 14.39 (14.26–14.59) |

Notes:

- **Qwen needed no deviations here.** With the default chunk (the engine chose 8192; `--help` says 4096 for "others"), Qwen plans 52.05 GiB. The committed runs used a raised wired limit (56 GiB), with no swapping. At the macOS default limit (51.84 GiB measured on this Mac), `--prefill-chunk 2048` (46.11 GiB planned) ran at the same speed in 3 of 3 runs, and one run of the unmodified command also completed without swapping. See the follow-up comment for the numbers. For a stock 64 GB Mac, #1068's `--prefill-chunk 2048` is still the safer choice.
- **Qwen snapshots cross the 1 GiB limit at ~30K**, so later frontiers use prefix replay (`kvcache_bytes=0`). Replay sits outside the timed windows, so it only adds wall time (~25 min per sweep).
- **Flash streaming generation is steady at 13–16 t/s to 64K; prefill is not.** Each run has some frontiers that drop to 86–120 t/s, and one run dropped to ~48 t/s at 57K–63K. I haven't found the cause. The committed CSV shows a typical run; the medians and ranges above include the worst one.
- **Streaming on 64 GB pushes other processes into swap.** Runs with more than 100 MiB of system-wide swap-ins were excluded by a rule fixed beforehand, and replaced once. In the excluded Flash run, 403 MiB of swap-ins came from other processes; `ds4-bench` itself had 0 swaps.
- **Comparisons.** For the same Qwen model on a 64 GB M1 Max at `8db1d1d`, see #1068 (sweep to 16K). The earlier 64 GB streaming datapoint is #350 (M1 Ultra, June, 32 GB cache, ~5 t/s gen). These rows are not comparable with the resident 128 GB Flash rows in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`: they use a different residency mode and a different chip.

Per-run CSVs, the engine's startup report, `time -l` and 5 s memory/disk samples are available on request.

title: Clamp the Linux host memory probe to the cgroup limit
body:
`ds4_linux_nonmovable_memory()` reports MemAvailable minus CmaFree, which is
the host's number. Inside a container or a systemd scope with a memory limit
the kernel enforces the cgroup limit long before MemAvailable is reached, so
the guards that consume the probe (`ds4_rocm_memory.h` allocation checks and
`hipMemGetInfo` clamp, the CUDA integrated-GPU SSD-cache budget, the GLM
memory guard under ROCm) admit a model that cannot stay resident.
`docs/STRIX_HALO.md` sends users into a container, which is exactly where
this bites.

This reads the caller's own cgroup from `/proc/self/cgroup`: v2
`memory.max` minus `memory.current`, or the v1 memory controller's
`memory.limit_in_bytes` minus `memory.usage_in_bytes`, and returns the
smaller of that and the host number. `max`, the v1 LONG_MAX sentinel, and
unreadable or malformed files leave the host number unchanged, so the probe
never fails because of the cgroup. Only the process's own cgroup is read;
a limit set on an ancestor slice is not seen (deliberate, to keep this
small; Docker's private cgroup namespace and `systemd-run` scopes both put
the limit on the caller's own cgroup).

Test: `tests/test_linux_memory.c` gains a `cgroup_case` table (v2 pair,
usage above limit, `max`, v1 sentinel, `-1`, missing/empty/non-numeric
files) and, after the parse cases, prints the live probe and asserts it is
never above the live cgroup headroom. The existing `memory_case` table is
unchanged and `max` is byte-identical to today's behaviour.

## Evidence

Machine: Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, gcc 13.3),
16 cores, 125 GB RAM, no GPU. CPU build only; no model needed.

Before (main, a one-file probe calling the unchanged header):

```
$ ./probe                                                   # unscoped
main probe: 28049539072 bytes = 26.12 GiB
$ systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=12G -- ./probe
main probe: 28049080320 bytes = 26.12 GiB
```

After:

```
$ make test-linux-memory
live probe: 26.00 GiB usable
Linux nonmovable memory: PASS
$ systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=12G -- ./tests/test_linux_memory
live probe: 12.00 GiB usable, cgroup headroom 12.00 GiB
Linux nonmovable memory: PASS
$ systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=4G -- ./tests/test_linux_memory
live probe: 4.00 GiB usable, cgroup headroom 4.00 GiB
Linux nonmovable memory: PASS
```

(The scope's `memory.max` was 12884901888 and `memory.current` 1368064.)

Gates run:

- `make clean && make cpu`: rc 0, zero warnings with the default
  `-Wall -Wextra -std=c99` CFLAGS.
- `make test-linux-memory`: rc 0 (new test fails to link on main:
  `implicit declaration of function 'ds4_linux_cgroup_headroom_parse'`).
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Not run: `make test` (needs `ds4_test` linked against a GPU backend and
`ds4flash.gguf`; no GPU or model on this machine). No ROCm or CUDA host was
available to exercise the three consumers live; the header change is the
only one and all three call the same function.

title: Document the expert hotlist and locality profile formats
body:
`DS4_EXPERT_HOTLIST`, `--expert-profile` / `DS4_EXPERT_PROFILE` and
`DS4_METAL_STREAMING_EXPERT_HOTLIST` (`DS4_ROCM_...` on ROCm) are not
mentioned anywhere under `docs/`, and the hotlist's first line
`# ds4 expert hotlist v1` did not say what "v1" promises. The built-in
`ds4_streaming_hotlist*.inc` lists were generated from these files, and
anyone recording a hotlist for their own workload has to read
`ds4_expert_profile_write_hotlist_file()` and
`metal_graph_streaming_expert_hotlist_load_file()` to learn the format.

This adds `docs/EXPERT_HOTLIST.md` describing:

- how to produce both files and how to feed a hotlist back to SSD
  streaming;
- the hotlist v1 layout as written (header keys, the four columns, one
  line per (layer, expert) pair including zero-hit pairs, the sort order
  that doubles as preload priority) and the version rule (bump on a column
  changing meaning or on an ordering change; trailing columns and extra
  `#` header lines are additive);
- what the reader is more permissive about than the writer: comments and
  the fourth column are ignored, zero-hit lines and out-of-range or
  repeated pairs are skipped silently, the header is not checked against
  the running model, reading stops at the preload count, a non-numeric
  line rejects the file;
- the `--expert-profile` JSON object field by field, with `"source"` as
  the identifier readers should check.

One pointer line each in `docs/SSD_STREAMING.md` (next to the preload
flags) and in the README "Detailed Guides" list. No code change. The open
docs PRs #955 (Pi `thinkingLevelMap`) and #956 (stateless-client KV warm
recipe) touch different README sections.

Everything stated was read from the writer and reader in `ds4.c` on
current `main`; the numbers in the examples are illustrative shapes, not
a recorded run. `git diff --check` is clean. No build or model involved.

title: Refuse duplicate tensor names and name the file of a missing tensor
body:
Two small loader hardenings in `ds4.c`, both header-only testable.

**Duplicate tensor names.** `model_find_tensor()` is first-match. A GGUF
whose tensor directory lists a name twice (a broken merge or conversion
script; the Python side under `gguf-tools/` checks for it, the C loader
did not) loaded without complaint and bound the first copy to both roles.
`parse_tensors()` now sorts the names once (length, then bytes) after the
directory is read and refuses the file on the first adjacent equal pair:

```
ds4: duplicate tensor name in /path/to/model.gguf: test.weight
```

Cost is one `qsort` over the tensor directory at open, nothing per lookup.

**Missing required tensor.** `required_tensor()` printed
`required tensor is missing: X`. With a main model plus an MTP or DSpark
support GGUF loaded in the same process that does not say which file is
wrong. `ds4_model` keeps the path it was opened from (freed in
`model_close()`) and the message becomes
`required tensor is missing from /path/to/model.gguf: X`. Hand-built
models in tests have no path and print `model` there.

**Test.** `tests/test_deepseek41_gguf.c` gains `run_refusal()`: two
synthetic headers written with the file's existing `put32`/`putstr`/
`tensor` helpers, one with `test.weight` listed twice and one with a
required name absent. Each is opened in a forked child with stderr on a
pipe; the parent requires a non-zero exit, the expected phrase, the tensor
name, and the fixture path in the message. No model or GPU.

## Evidence

Machine: Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, gcc 13.3),
16 cores, no GPU. CPU build only.

Red on `main` (new test, unchanged loader): the duplicate fixture opens
successfully and the child exits 0:

```
test_deepseek41_gguf: tests/test_deepseek41_gguf.c:143: run_refusal:
Assertion `WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) != 0' failed.
```

Green with this change:

```
$ make test-deepseek41-gguf
V4.1 disk-only GGUF extent: PASS
GGUF tensor directory refusals: PASS
```

Gates run:

- `make clean && make cpu`: rc 0, zero warnings with the default
  `-Wall -Wextra -std=c99` CFLAGS.
- `make test-deepseek41-gguf`: rc 0, before and after a clean rebuild.
  The only compiler diagnostic in that target is the pre-existing
  `-Wpointer-sign` on `mincore()`'s `char resident` in `run_fixture()`,
  not touched here.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Not run: `make test` (needs `ds4_test` linked against a GPU backend and
`ds4flash.gguf`), and the `test_deepseek41_gguf <real.gguf>` layout mode
against the V4.1 GGUF. The duplicate check runs on every real open, so a
timing number on the 147 GB file's directory would be worth adding to this
PR from a machine that has it; it is a sort of a few thousand short
strings, so I expect it to be well under a millisecond.

title: Negative controls for the reference comparators: a rejected variant must fail
body:
## Summary

`ds4_test` has several comparators that judge a backend against a reference
(official continuation vectors, local golden vectors, cold-vs-resumed
prefill). Each one is only evidence when it is known to reject a wrong
backend, and today only one test in the tree demonstrates that. This issue
proposes adding a "rejected variant must fail" control to each comparator,
before any of the thresholds are touched or reused for new backends. It is
test infrastructure, so it is filed as an issue first rather than a PR.

## What exists

The one control is `tests/test_dspark_eos_contract.py`: line 6 says
"An optional source path admits a pre-fix negative control without editing
it", `--source` points the harness at a pre-fix `ds4.c`, and the report
line prints `observed_negative` so a run against the fixed tree and a run
against the old tree are distinguishable. That is the shape this issue asks
for elsewhere.

The comparators without one (line numbers on `main` at `0aaea5a`):

- `tests/ds4_test.c:5964` `test_local_golden_overlap` and `:5975`
  `test_local_golden_max_abs`, used by `--local-golden-vectors`
  (`:6036-6062`). Thresholds: top-1 equal, top-5 overlap >= 4, top-20
  overlap >= 15, top-64 overlap >= 40, top-20 max-abs logit delta <= 8.0.
  The comment says it is "intentionally tolerant" and meant to catch
  "wrong tiling, skipped work, bad dispatch". Nothing in the tree shows
  that a wrong-tiling or skipped-work backend actually lands outside those
  bounds; 8.0 logits and 40/64 could be wide enough to pass a mis-dispatched
  layer on a long prompt.
- `tests/ds4_test.c:5301` `test_glm53_continued_prefill` (`:5366-5384`):
  asserts resumed and cold top-1 agree and top-8 sets overlap, and only
  prints `max same-rank logit delta`. A resumed prefill that attends
  through a wrong schedule can keep the same argmax and still be a
  different model; the number that would show it is logged, not asserted.
- `--logprob-vectors` (CONTRIBUTING's "catches tokenizer, template,
  attention, and logits regressions"): same question, which class of fault
  has it been shown to catch, at what margin.

## Proposal

For each comparator, one control that runs the comparator against a
variant known to be wrong and asserts the comparator *fails* at the
calibrated floor. The control must be a real, shipped drift path, not a
synthetic perturbation of the reference, otherwise it only tests the
assertion, not the floor.

1. `--local-golden-vectors`: add `DS4_TEST_LOCAL_GOLDEN_EXPECT_FAIL=1`
   (or a `--local-golden-negative` selector) that runs the same cases with
   a known-bad backend knob and requires at least one of the five
   assertions to trip on every case. Candidate knobs that already exist and
   change numerics: `DS4_METAL_MATH_SAFE`, the pre-M5 router transform
   switch (`DS4_METAL_DISABLE_PRE_M5_ROUTER_TRANSFORM_FINALIZE_FUSION`),
   and the prefill chunk override. If none of those trips the floor, the
   floor is not calibrated and that is the finding: the control then
   documents the smallest margin (top-20 max-abs, overlap counts) each knob
   produces, so the thresholds can be tightened to sit between "sane kernel
   change" and "wrong dispatch".
2. `--glm53-continued-prefill`: promote `max same-rank logit delta` from a
   log line to an assertion with a floor chosen from a cold-vs-cold repeat
   (the noise floor), then add the negative: resume with the split placed
   one token too far (reuse one token too many) and require the assertion
   to trip. That fault is the first of the four colibri #1453 used to
   qualify its resumed-prefill test ("reuse one token too many, the old
   schedule condition, no rollback truncation, unguarded undo buffers, all
   four are caught"); it is the one that maps directly onto ds4's
   `ds4_session_sync` resume path without a new fixture.
3. `--logprob-vectors`: record, in `docs/TESTING.md`, one fault class the
   test was run against and the margin it failed by (for example the
   Q8 output-head tile vs the few-row matvec, both already in the tree
   under env switches). If the run does not exist, the control is that run.

Each control follows `test_dspark_eos_contract.py`'s convention: a flag or
env var selects the negative variant, the report line says
`observed_negative=true/false`, and the default `make test` path is
unchanged. No new model files; every control reuses the same GGUF the
positive test already needs, so the cost is one extra pass per comparator.

## Why now

The thresholds in `test_local_golden_case_run` are reused as the acceptance
gate for new Metal work (router softplus in 0719a0b, Q8 tiles, TP paths).
A comparator that has never been shown to fail on a wrong backend is not a
gate, it is a log. One negative control per comparator makes the tolerance
numbers falsifiable and gives contributors a way to state "my change is
inside the floor" with something behind it.

I can send the `--glm53-continued-prefill` piece as a PR first if the
approach is acceptable; it is the smallest (an assertion plus one
mis-split resume) and needs only the GLM 5.3 GGUF the test already loads.

title: Recover GLM Metal prefill speed with validated selection prefixes
body:
Closes #1029

Addresses the regression reported in #1029: `0e9cc2d4` reduced GLM Metal
prefill throughput by roughly **6-8%**. Patch-level isolation traced the loss
to the switch from the valid-row attention specialization to the fully
guarded kernel, not the added reduction barriers. The switch was necessary:
GLM's 2051-slot selection can contain `UINT32_MAX` padding.

This patch scans the selected IDs on the GPU before the attention loop. If
they form a valid prefix followed by padding, it runs the fast specialization
over that prefix. Interior invalid IDs retain the guarded fallback, and an
all-invalid selection produces zero output. Physical stride, valid-row order,
and attention arithmetic are preserved. The new dispatch is restricted to
full eight-head groups outside TP; no CUDA/ROCm or public API changes.

**Performance**
On an M5 Max with 128 GiB and resident `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`, the main-based
patch measured the following continued-prefill gains against diagnostic
rollback, using four same-engine passes with alternating 2048-token chunks
and reversed assignment on successive passes:

| Context interval | Before | Patched | Gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K-16K | 390.21 t/s | 418.27 t/s | **+7.2%** |
| 16K-24K | 384.10 t/s | 411.26 t/s | **+7.1%** |

All full-vocabulary logits were bit-exact. These are continued-prefill
measurements; cold-prefill timings were too variable for a precise claim.

**Validation**
- `tests/test_glm_attention` passes with Metal API and shader validation,
  including CPU-reference and bitwise rollback checks for tail padding,
  interior holes, empty selections, partial heads, RoPE and offset views.
- `./ds4_test --metal-kernels` passes.
- A 4K SSD-streaming check with a 16 GiB cache matches all logits.

`DS4_METAL_DISABLE_GLM_PREFILL_PREFIX=1` restores the guarded path for A/B
testing. Physical TP and other GPU backends were not tested; their dispatch
is unchanged.
