title: Metal: run Qwen3.8 QSA prefill attention on the tensor units
body:
## What

Ports oMLX's tensor-unit ("NAX") QSA main attention (jundot/omlx #4020, commit 2 - one query per threadgroup) to the ds4 Metal stack as `kernel_qwen4_attn_mm_nax`, dispatched in place of `kernel_qwen4_attn_mm` for Qwen3.8 prefill attention whenever the Metal 4 tensor API is live.

The restructure follows the merged oMLX design rather than op-swapping the classic kernel: one (kv head, token) per threadgroup of 2 simdgroups; the group's query heads fill ONE 16-row tensor tile (rows >= group idle) with the 256 head dims split 128/128 between the simdgroups, which exchange partial scores through threadgroup memory. The key loop walks the query's own selection list 32 keys per step (dense mode: every causal position), so every step is exactly the query's own keys - no per-row masks, only slots past the list and positions past the query are masked. Ops are 16x32x32 `matmul2d`: Q K^T over 32 head dims per run, and P@V with the step's two 16-key P fragments packed along K (ds4's softmax already rounds P to half, so oMLX's fp16 hi/lo pieces are not needed). O lives in persistent cooperative tensors across the whole key loop (no per-tile store/load), Q is re-read from device each step, and O is rescaled only when a row max changed. The scalar softmax (m/l per row, P rounded to half) and the normalize + sigmoid-gate epilogue match the classic kernel.

## Numerics

Only the accumulation order changes (tensor trees vs the classic sequential chains), so outputs drift by about an ulp on a fraction of elements:

- kernel tests: max |delta| <= 1.3e-4 vs the classic kernel (the suite allows 4e-3*scale against the decode path)
- e2e last-token logits on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4: max |dlogit| 1.14 / 0.91 / 1.68 at 8k / 32k / 64k prefill, mean <= 0.19, **top-1 identical in every run** - inside the model's own prefill-chunking spread (0.85-1.4)
- `tests/test_qwen4_kernels.c` now runs every mm case a third time with the kill switch and bounds NAX-vs-classic; T <= 8 tails and key-split runs are asserted bit-equal to the old path, which also proves the fallback routing

Context: #946 (closed Sep 2 pending a write-up, findings standing, planned to reopen) records whole-logit `matmul2d` accumulate drift vs the simdgroup reference kernels on M5 Max, verified on the GLM-5.3 path. This PR adds one more `matmul2d` consumer, so the numbers above are the attention-path datapoint: <= 1.14 logits max drift with identical top-1 across 8k-64k prefills, and `DS4_QWEN4_NO_ATTN_MM_NAX=1` reverts this path to the classic kernel.

## Performance (M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 27, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4)

| measurement | classic | NAX | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| QSA kernel, T=1024, 256k ctx, 512 random blocks | 8.94 ms | 6.83 ms | 1.31x |
| QSA kernel, same but blocks in the last 8k | 8.31 ms | 3.49 ms | 2.38x |
| e2e prefill 8k (4 runs/variant, ABBA/BAAB) | 1227 tok/s | 1311 tok/s | +6.9% |
| e2e prefill 32k | 1289 tok/s | 1325 tok/s | +2.8% |
| e2e prefill 64k | 1231 tok/s | 1322 tok/s | +7.4% |

Commands: `QWEN4_BENCH=1 ./tests/test_qwen4_kernels` A/B'd with `DS4_QWEN4_NO_ATTN_MM_NAX=1`; e2e via `speed-bench/metal_prefill_variant_bench --candidate-env DS4_QWEN4_ATTN_MM_NAX_AB --control-env DS4_QWEN4_NO_ATTN_MM_NAX=1 --tolerate-drift`. Decode kernels are untouched (A/B within noise).

## Validation

- `make clean && make`: warning-free
- `make test`: `metal-kernels`, `metal-tensor-equivalence`, `mtp-verify-depth`, `streaming-decode-prefill-correctness`, `server`, `tool-call-quality`, `qwen4-prefill-checkpoints`, `session-*`, `glm53-continued-prefill` pass. `long-context`, `logprob-vectors`, `local-golden-vectors`, `metal-short-prefill` fail on this host **identically with `DS4_QWEN4_NO_ATTN_MM_NAX=1 DS4_QWEN4_NO_HC_DEFER=1`** (both features disabled; e.g. golden `top20_max_abs=48.5702` bit-identical), so they pre-date this change - this host's `ds4flash.gguf` points at Qwen3.8-Flash-Next while several vector sets target DeepSeek V4 Flash. `metal-ssd-streaming-cache-pressure` fails at `ds4_engine_open` (16 GiB cache budget) and the TP loopback test hit a connection reset - both environmental.
- `make test-qwen4-kernels`: all pass, including the new NAX-vs-classic bounds

## Fallbacks

For `n_tokens > 8`, `head_dim == 256`, `n_splits == 1`: NAX when `ds4_gpu_mpp_available()` and `DS4_QWEN4_NO_ATTN_MM_NAX` is unset and the pipeline resolves; otherwise classic `kernel_qwen4_attn_mm`. Short tails (T <= 8), key splits, quality mode, pre-M5 devices and compiles without the tensor API keep today's kernels unchanged.

## Related open PRs

- #1056 touches the same files (SSD/MoE/MTP work) but not the attention kernels

title: Metal: defer hyper-connection residual writes into the next stream norm
body:
## What

Every prefill layer materialized the hyper-connection residual in its own pass - the branch's `R += 2*sigmoid(inj/hc) * blk` combine after attention (`kernel_qwen4_hc_combine`) and the same combine folded into `kernel_qwen4_moe_reduce` - and the next stream norm re-read R immediately afterwards. This carries the pending `(blk, inj)` write instead and lets a new `kernel_qwen4_hc_combine_norm_rows` apply it in place inside that norm pass (the design of jundot/omlx #3982 part A): one threadgroup per (stream, token) owns its R slice in the `hc_norm_reuse` layout, so the read-modify-write is race-free, and the inject partials ping-pong through `inj_alt` exactly as the single-token `hc_combine_norm` fusion already does.

## Bit-exact

Identical to the eager `kernel_qwen4_hc_combine` + `kernel_qwen4_hc_norm` pair: the combined stream is materialized with the same `qwen4_hc_inject_weight` reduction and the same expressions. `tests/test_qwen4_kernels.c` memcmps R/xn/inj byte for byte across f32/f16/q8 inject weights and T = 3..256 (15 new cases), and `metal_prefill_variant_bench` passes its logit exactness gate (run WITHOUT `--tolerate-drift`, `DS4_QWEN4_NO_HC_DEFER=1` as control).

Eager writes remain wherever a consumer reads R directly: T <= 3 verify/decode rows, layers feeding the PLE block, and the last trunk layer whose pre-mixer R the predictor captures. The debug ffn dump and an enabled FFN steering projection flush the pending write before they read R, and a failed layer drops its pending write at the end of the forward pass. `DS4_QWEN4_NO_HC_DEFER` keeps the eager writes everywhere.

## Performance (M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 27, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4, hc=4 streams x 2560)

| measurement | eager | deferred | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| write+norm pair at T=256 (kernel) | 122.2 us | 88.2 us | -28% |
| hc_ffn stage of a 4096-token chunk | 242.6 ms | 191.7 ms | -21% |
| e2e prefill 8k (12 runs/variant) | 1360 tok/s | 1392 tok/s | +2.4% |
| e2e prefill 32k (4 runs/variant) | 1440 tok/s | 1458 tok/s | +1.3% |

Commands: `QWEN4_BENCH=1 ./tests/test_qwen4_kernels` for the kernel pair; stage times via `DS4_QWEN4_TIMING=2`; e2e via `speed-bench/metal_prefill_variant_bench --candidate-env DS4_QWEN4_HC_DEFER_AB --control-env DS4_QWEN4_NO_HC_DEFER=1`. Decode is untouched (T <= 3 keeps eager writes).

## Validation

- `make clean && make`: warning-free
- `make test`: same pass set and the same failures as the base tree on this host - `long-context`, `logprob-vectors`, `local-golden-vectors`, `metal-short-prefill` fail **identically with `DS4_QWEN4_NO_ATTN_MM_NAX=1 DS4_QWEN4_NO_HC_DEFER=1`** (both features disabled; e.g. golden `top20_max_abs=48.5702` unchanged), so they pre-date this change and are host/model-mismatch artifacts. `metal-ssd-streaming-cache-pressure` fails at `ds4_engine_open` and the TP loopback test hit a connection reset - environmental.
- `make test-qwen4-kernels`: all pass, including the 15 new byte-exact `hc defer` cases

## Related open PRs

- #1042 fuses HC/MoE/attention glue for V4.1 decode - complementary (different model path)
- #1056 shares HC inputs/sigmoid values inside the kernels - complementary; same files, so worth rebasing one of the two
- #1127 overlaps prefill layers with two in flight - the pending write is plain host state consumed by an ordinary dispatch in the next layer's stream norm, but that PR's scheduling is worth a re-check when both land

title: V4.1 Flash Q4 SSD streaming on Metal: which of these bit-exact decode speedups would you take as PRs?
body:
We (Argonaut Labs) keep a fork of ds4 for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Q4 (518 GB GGUF) with Metal SSD streaming on an M5 Max with 128 GB: https://github.com/argonautlabsai/ds4-argodrive. It is pinned at bd66c40. Before we rebase onto main and open pull requests, we would like to know which of the changes below you would consider, if any, so we send only those, one per PR, following CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENT.md: default on, no permanent flags, tests under `tests/`, before/after `ds4-bench` sweeps with commands, machine, quant and failures recorded.

## Measurement

One interleaved session, 512-token prompt from `speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt`, greedy, 200 generated tokens. Output SHA-256 identical to upstream on every arm. Decode GPU clock held at 1,620 MHz, zero swap growth. "Steady" excludes the first decode step. Upstream is bd66c40 built with the same toolchain (Apple clang 14.0.3, macOS 26.4 SDK) with its automatic cache (3,688 experts); the fork locks 4,600 experts. This is against the pinned commit, not current main; we will re-measure against main next.

| Same machine, same model file | Decode tok/s | Prefill tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream bd66c40, internal SSD | 10.18 | 17.96 |
| fork, internal SSD only | 18.66 | 30.98 |
| fork, plus one NVMe replica over Thunderbolt 5 | 21.05 | 36.88 |
| fork, plus two NVMe replicas | 22.25 | 42.41 |

Upstream is the median of six arms, each fork rung the median of two; ranges stay within 0.2 tok/s. Arms, CSVs and the verification script are in the [ladder package](https://github.com/argonautlabsai/ds4-argodrive/blob/argonaut-v41-benchmark/argodrive/candidates/2026-09-27-ladder/README.md).

## Candidates, each bit-exact

1. **Router ids through a GPU-written mailbox, shared expert encoded before the commit.** A small kernel after the router writes the selected ids, a checksum and a sequence number into a shared buffer. The CPU commits without waiting, polls the mailbox, checks the expert cache and starts the miss reads while the GPU runs the shared expert. It falls back to the blocking readback after 50 ms; the qualification arms recorded 8,000 polls and no fallback. +6.6% steady decode, ABAB, two pairs.

2. **Missing-expert reads from byte-identical replica copies on additional drives, weighted per drive** (10:6:6 decode, 10:5:5 prefill here). 18.66 to 22.25 above. This would be a new option such as `--ssd-streaming-replica PATH`; without a replica nothing changes. On one SSD it is a no-op, so it is not itemized against upstream.

3. **Post-MoE flush and eviction pre-scan.** Commit a layer's routed MoE right after it is encoded when the layer waited for expert reads; rank eviction candidates while the CPU waits on the mailbox and re-validate each one at use. +1.5% at pp512/tg512, BAAB ([package](https://github.com/argonautlabsai/ds4-argodrive/blob/argonaut-v41-benchmark/argodrive/candidates/2026-09-28-flush/README.md)).

4. **Small fusions that keep the rounding boundaries.** A V4.1 single-token router fast path (same 512-wide bitonic selection network and tie rules; other shapes use the original path) plus four small fusions: +2.2 to +2.8% ([notes](https://github.com/argonautlabsai/ds4-argodrive/blob/argonaut-v41-benchmark/argodrive/reproduce/V41-ROUTER.md)). Three BF16 rounding passes folded into the kernels that produce their inputs, a pointer-keyed pipeline-state cache and a getenv cache: about +1.5% together ([notes](https://github.com/argonautlabsai/ds4-argodrive/blob/argonaut-v41-benchmark/argodrive/reproduce/V41-STACK.md)). Exact-output fixtures exist in the fork.

5. **Read path.** Nine persistent reader threads with split reads, the resident experts' down projection overlapped with missing-expert reads, asynchronous Engram row reads, a 32-token hotness decay. This is where most of the single-SSD gain comes from. It is measured against our earlier fork states, not itemized against upstream; we would measure it during the rebase.

Not proposed: the 4,600-expert locked cache (+3% here, machine-specific memory policy), keepalive settings and split ratios.

## Question

Which of these, in which order? "None" is a useful answer too; we keep them in the fork.

title: server: recover GLM argument types using existing property schemas
body:
## Summary

Fixes #569. GLM's `<arg_value>` carries no string/type flag, and the parser currently emits every argument as a string. Recover a non-string JSON value only when the request's property schema unambiguously permits its type.

- Reuse the existing `tool_schema_order.prop_schema` metadata and the response parser's existing `orders` argument; no new request-schema storage or public API changes.
- Support explicit integer, number, boolean, null, array, object, and non-string type-array declarations. Preserve JSON-looking strings, unknown tools/properties, missing schemas, string-capable unions, and schemas expressed only through `$ref`/combinators.
- Require a complete JSON literal, including strict lexical checks inside containers. Invalid literals and type mismatches remain strings rather than corrupting response JSON. Large integer text is never round-tripped through floating point.
- Preserve raw generated tool text for cache/replay. DeepSeek and Qwen behavior is unchanged.

This is conservative type recovery, not full JSON Schema validation. Integer recovery requires integer notation; decimal/exponent notation is supported for `number`. Nested values are preserved rather than recursively coerced.

## Relationship to existing proposals

Related: #571, #582, #729, #1016. In particular, #1016 already proposes the same conservative schema-aware approach. This is an alternative against current main (`0aaea5a238fb41a35106a551e73c8409dfb751ac`), taking advantage of the property schemas and response-parser schema plumbing that now exist for Qwen, instead of adding another schema store or changing all syntax-parser call sites. It also covers the three tool-definition formats, unknown tools/properties, and non-JSON control characters. It is not intended to claim a new discovery of the issue.

## Regression tests

All tests live alongside the existing server unit tests in `ds4_server.c`:

- 49 fixtures for typed values, nested containers, nullable/type-array declarations, string preservation, malformed JSON, and conservative fallback.
- OpenAI Chat, Responses, and Anthropic tool-schema inputs through `parse_tools_value`, with and without schema metadata, multiple calls, unknown tools, and unknown properties.
- OpenAI GLM SSE output asserts that a numeric argument is emitted as a number, not a quoted string.

Test-first development: the initial array regression failed on unchanged production code (1 assertion). Subsequent type, malformed-literal, and union extensions were each run red (7, 9, and 3 failures respectively) before implementation; the server suite is now green.

## Validation

Machine: Apple M3 Ultra, macOS 26.5.1. Default Metal build and CPU portability build. No model quant was loaded; these are model-free parser/frontend checks. Work was isolated in a separate worktree; the deployed server was not changed or restarted.

Passed:

- `make -j8 ds4_test && ./ds4_test --server`
- `make -j8` (default Metal build; no compiler warnings)
- `make -j8 test-frontends` (server, agent, Chrome recovery tests)
- `make -j8 cpu` (build only; no CPU model inference)
- Server suite with `tests/ds4_test.c` compiled and linked using `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer` (existing core objects linked unchanged); no sanitizer diagnostics.
- Remaining model-free executables: `test_layer_pack` (97/97), `test_engine_mgpu_placement` (114/114), `test_gpu_args`, `test_prompt_prefix`, `test_sampling`, `test_deepseek4_vision_image`, `test_image_decode`.
- `git diff --check`.

`make -j8 test` was attempted: its model-free prerequisites and evaluator/agent checks passed, then `./ds4_test` stopped at `qwen4-prefill-checkpoints` because another ds4 process holds the instance lock. The lock was respected; no running service was stopped or lock bypass attempted. Consequently, the full model/Metal runtime suite is **not** claimed to pass. No live model inference, CUDA, SSD-streaming, distributed inference, or throughput benchmark was run. The change is confined to server-side GLM argument parsing and tests, not an inference backend.

Developed and tested with AI assistance.

title: server: --image-prefix-snapshot reuses the text before a request's image (#1007)
body:
Addresses one case of #1007: **stateless image requests that share a long system prompt**. An example is a batch job that sends one photo per request behind the same ~1.7k-token instruction prompt. Today every such request re-prefills the whole prompt:

- the live-slot gate refuses a slot that holds a different image,
- Qwen's recurrent state cannot rewind to the text before the image, and
- disk KV load and cold saves are both off for multimodal requests.

## What it does

`--image-prefix-snapshot` (opt-in) keeps one in-memory `ds4_session_snapshot` per slot. The snapshot is the session state at the last message-start marker before the first image: the last `<|im_start|>` for ChatML, or the last user marker for role-token templates, with the scan stopping at the first assistant marker as `ds4_kvstore_chat_anchor_pos` does. On a multimodal request with no other cache hit:

- If the slot's snapshot tokens match the prompt up to that boundary, the server loads the snapshot and the multimodal sync resumes from there.
- Otherwise it prefills the text before the boundary on its own, snapshots it, then continues. Any stale vision state is dropped first.

The snapshot is taken from a text-only sync, so it never carries image state, and the restore checks `pos == anchor && !ds4_session_has_vision_state`. Everything is behind the flag. Without it, none of the new code runs. It makes no disk format or API change.

## Measurements

Apple M3 Max 128 GB, Metal, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2 (`--mtp --vision mmproj-…-Q8_0`, `--ctx 131072`). The workload is 50 photos from a captioning job, each with the same 1,734-token system prompt plus ~500 tokens of per-photo text and image, at temperature 0.2:

| Build | Mean s/photo | Median | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0aaea5a` | 9.21 | 8.80 | 10.00 |
| `0aaea5a` + this PR, `--image-prefix-snapshot` | **4.86** | **4.80** | **5.50** |

- Snapshot: 1,734 tokens, 166 MiB. Save ~19 ms, load 5–27 ms. Prefill per photo drops from ~4.1 s to ~1.25 s.
- One snapshot served all 57 image requests. Short image prompts in between, whose boundary falls below `min_tokens`, left it alone.
- It has been running in production on that job since 2026-09-29, restoring in 12–23 ms per photo.

## Correctness

- **The load is exact.** At temperature 0, a photo gives byte-identical output whether its prefix was loaded from the snapshot or freshly prefilled in the same two pieces.
- **Splitting the prefill at the boundary is not bit-identical to one prefill.** Flag on versus flag off matched on 3 of 8 photos at temperature 0. The differences were near-ties ("matte black helmet" versus "black helmet"). This is the mixed-prefill-schedule rounding that `docs/QWEN38_FLASH_NEXT.md` describes ("their full logits need not match"). Each mode is deterministic run to run (8/8), and at temperature 0.2 the field agreement over 50 photos was within run-to-run noise.

## Tests

```sh
make -j ds4-server ds4_test && ./ds4_test --server   # OK
make cpu                                             # builds
```

The boundary scan is split out as `image_prefix_anchor_pos()`, with three new `--server` unit tests: ChatML (last `<|im_start|>` before the image, none after it, `min_tokens`), role tokens (last user marker, stops at assistant, ignores `<|im_start|>`), and no marker.

## Notes

- #977 (with #961) persists image-conditioned checkpoints and would cover the disk side of this more generally. This PR is smaller and in-memory only. It targets the case where the image *differs* on every request but the text in front of it does not, and it does not depend on disk KV being enabled.
- While doing this we noticed that the cold-save anchor `ds4_kvstore_chat_anchor_pos` never fires for Qwen, because ChatML has no dedicated user or assistant token (`user_id == -1`). So text-only Qwen prompts get no cold boundary checkpoint either. This PR does not change that. Happy to open a separate issue or PR if useful.

title: Metal: overlap Qwen3.8 PLE reads with prefill
body:
## What

Qwen3.8 prefill currently waits for the next chunk's PLE n-gram rows to be read from the GGUF before it can run that chunk. This change stages the current chunk, then reads the following chunk's rows on one worker while Metal processes the current chunk. The worker has its own output buffer and a copy of the PLE history; the session thread retains graph state, GPU writes, callbacks, and cancellation.

The worker joins before the next progress callback or session frontier is exposed. If thread creation or a disk read fails, the next chunk uses the existing synchronous path. There is at most one extra host buffer, capped at 128 MiB (80 MiB with the measured 8,192-token chunks). Prefetch is skipped when the configured chunk capacity is below 256 tokens or the prompt fits in one chunk. `DS4_QWEN4_NO_PLE_PREFETCH=1` selects the original path for diagnosis. Ordinary decode still calls the original forward wrapper.

## Related work and review order

This PR is tracked in [prefill issue #1202](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1202), alongside [#1198](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1198). PLE prefetch hides host I/O latency; #1198 removes repeated packed Q4_K loads in the GPU loader. They have independent implementations and failure modes. #1198's speed measurements already include this prefetch as baseline, so its gain is incremental; merging this PR first aligns with that measurement sequence without creating a build dependency.

[Cache tracker #1201](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1201) separately groups history validation, replay identity and prompt checkpoints. Their replay-avoidance benefits are distinct from raw prefill throughput. This PR retains its own correctness, fallback and speed evidence below.

## Performance (Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, Metal, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4)

Prompt: `speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt`; 16K fresh prefill, 32K context, 8,192-token chunks, 16K warm-up per arm.

| Measurement | Synchronous | Prefetch | Change | Logits |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Controlled source-branch A/B, eight runs | 1,376.94 tok/s | 1,431.25 tok/s | +3.94% | exact, 8/8 |
| Post-transplant ABBA integration smoke, four runs | 1,366.63 tok/s | 1,452.29 tok/s | +6.27% | exact, 4/4 |
| 1K append after an 8K prefix, four runs | 1,179.24 tok/s | 1,182.89 tok/s | +0.31% | exact, 4/4 |

The eight-run result is the primary speed estimate; the later ABBA block checks this isolated transplant. A separate 768-token, three-chunk A/B exercised repeated buffer reuse and was +6.0%, with exact logits. The extra buffer is freed before prefill returns. Decode kernels and the one-token forward path are unchanged.

A separate 16K prefill + 64-token greedy decode guard used `ds4-bench` in control/prefetch/prefetch/control order. Mean generation throughput was **53.08 vs 53.49 tok/s** (steady tokens: **53.54 vs 54.08 tok/s**), so these four runs show no decode-throughput regression. Mean first-token latency was 26.63 vs 28.97 ms; this two-run-per-arm check is too small to attribute that difference to the change.

The post-transplant prefill command (the `candidate-env` value is a harness selector; the `control-env` sets the rollback variable):

```sh
./speed-bench/metal_prefill_variant_bench \
  --candidate-env DS4_QWEN4_PLE_PREFETCH_AB --candidate-value 1 \
  --control-env DS4_QWEN4_NO_PLE_PREFETCH=1 \
  --model gguf/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt \
  --prefill-chunk 8192 --prefix-tokens 16384 --warmup-tokens 16384 \
  --ctx 32768 --repeats 1

# Decode guard, repeated in control/prefetch/prefetch/control order:
DS4_QWEN4_NO_PLE_PREFETCH=1 ./ds4-bench --metal \
  -m gguf/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt \
  --ctx-start 16384 --ctx-max 16384 --step-incr 2048 \
  --prefill-chunk 8192 --gen-tokens 64 --csv /tmp/ple-control.csv
# Repeat with the rollback variable unset for the prefetch arm.
```

## Correctness and failure paths

- Full-vocabulary final logits were byte-equal in the prefill and append A/B runs above.
- A real session cancelled after the first 8,192-token chunk, joined the worker, then resumed to 16K with logits identical to the synchronous path.
- An injected `EBADF` in the worker's `pread` triggered a synchronous reread of the same rows; the recovered rows were byte-equal.
- The worker copies PLE history before launch, uses offset-based reads, and joins before a progress callback can expose the frontier.
- Checked-in `tests/test_qwen4_ple_prefetch.c` uses 256-token chunks and a 529-token prompt. It confirms two workers actually run, then compares full logits with rollback at all three chunk frontiers and after one decode. It also covers cancellation/resume, a worker-local `EBADF` with synchronous retry, and a failed thread start. The test adds no production hook.

## Validation

On this PR branch (`origin/main` plus the PLE implementation and test commits):

```sh
make clean && make -j8
make -j8 test-qwen4-ngrams
make -j8 cpu
make -j4 tests/test_qwen4_ple_prefetch
./tests/test_qwen4_ple_prefetch gguf/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

All passed on Metal. `test-qwen4-ngrams` covers native disk-reader success and error cases. The earlier integration build also passed `make`, `make metal-prefill-variant-bench`, and targeted cancellation/read-failure smokes. A full model-backed `make test` was not repeated for this host-only prefill change; the checked-in model-backed regression exercises the changed path directly. CUDA was not run. The source-branch A/B preceded the 128 MiB guard, but the measured 8,192-token chunks stay under that guard and the post-transplant A/B covers the guarded path.

The branch contains the PLE implementation and regression test on top of `origin/main`. It does not include the attention-kernel change from #1149.

title: Fix misleading prefill progress and false live cache hits after a backend state reset
body:
Closes #1114

After some turns, a Qwen3.8 server re-prefills the whole context while the log prints the same prefill chunk `0/16 (0.0%)` multiple times.

Root cause: the engine silently restarted the prefill at position 0 but the server had already counted `cached_tokens=132806`. `server_progress_cb` computed `display_current`, clamped to 0 for every chunk, and deduped on the raw advancing counter, so each chunk logged an identical-looking line with avg=0.00.

Changes:

- server: report rebuilt prefill progress against the full prompt
- server: treat detached backend state as a live cache miss

title: Fix the iq1_s and iq4_nl block sizes in the GGUF type table
body:
The GGUF type table had two wrong entries:

- `iq4_nl`: 256 values in 50 bytes, but ggml's `block_iq4_nl` is 32 values in 18 bytes (a half scale plus 16 bytes of nibbles).
- `iq1_s`: 110 bytes per block, but `block_iq1_s` is 50 bytes (a half scale, 32 bytes of qs, 16 bytes of qh).

With the old entries every iq4_nl tensor was sized at about a third of its real length. The official ds4 GGUFs use neither type, so this only shows up with third-party files. I hit it loading ISTA-DASLab's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO GGUF, which stores its n-gram table and some weights as iq4_nl.

The commit also adds `ds4_test --gguf-types`, which checks the block geometry of every quantized type against sizes spelled out from ggml's block structs (they match `GGML_QUANT_SIZES` in gguf-py). It needs no model.

Tested on an M1 Max (64 GB, macOS, Metal):

```
make && make cpu                  # both build cleanly
./ds4_test --gguf-types           # fails on main, passes with this commit
./ds4_test --server               # OK
```

This only changes table data, so there is no speed impact. With the corrected iq4_nl size, ISTA's iq4_nl n-gram rows decode to the original BF16 table at cosine 0.997.

title: Find the cold KV anchor in ChatML prompts
body:
The cold KV checkpoint is supposed to end right before the user message that asks the task, so a new agent session with the same system prompt and tools can load it from disk. `ds4_kvstore_chat_anchor_pos()` finds that point by scanning for the user and assistant marker tokens.

Qwen3.8 has no marker tokens. ChatML opens a turn with `<|im_start|>` followed by the role name, and the qwen4 vocab sets `user_id` and `assistant_id` to -1. So the anchor is never found and the server falls back to `kv_cache_store_len()`: the prompt length minus the trim, aligned down to 2048. With OpenCode (an ~11.3K token system prompt) and a short first message this gives `kv cache stored tokens=10240 trimmed=1151 reason=cold`, so every new session prefills the last ~1K tokens of the shared prefix again. When the first user message is long, the aligned point lands inside the task text and no other session can reuse the snapshot at all.

This change adds `ds4_chat_role_markers()`, which returns a prefix token plus the role tokens. For ChatML the prefix is `<|im_start|>` and the role ids come from tokenizing "user" and "assistant", the same way `qwen4_chat_open()` renders them. Both are single tokens in the Qwen3.8 vocab (846 and 74455). The anchor scan then matches the prefix followed by the role, so the words "user" or "assistant" inside message text do not count. DeepSeek and GLM pass -1 as the prefix and behave as before.

Tested on an M1 Max (64 GB, macOS, Metal), with the ISTA-DASLab Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO Q2_0 GGUF for the vocab check:

```
make && make cpu        # both build cleanly
./ds4_test --server     # OK, includes the new ChatML anchor test
```

The existing anchor tests pass -1 as the prefix. The new test covers role words inside text, a later user turn after the first assistant turn, and `min_tokens`.

title: Fix GLM imatrix collector reading stale MoE buffers
body:
The GLM routed imatrix collector writes the same statistics for every sparse layer.

`imatrix_collect_glm_one()` reads `ffn_norm`, `ffn_mid` and `router_selected` with `ds4_gpu_tensor_read()` right after the routed dispatch has been encoded. On Metal, `ds4_gpu_tensor_read()` is a plain memcpy of the shared buffer (`ds4_metal.m`). It does not wait for queued work. The graph reuses these scratch tensors in every layer and the batch is submitted later, so each layer reads the same stale contents.

Symptoms with a 1-prompt, 4096-token run on `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`:
- Every sparse layer reports exactly 265 used experts (`per sparse layer min=265 max=265`).
- Every layer misses the same 23 experts.
- `ffn_down_exps` vectors for the same expert are identical across layers.

The fix snapshots the three tensors per layer into a staging buffer with GPU copies in stream order. The host accumulates them after the token's command batch has completed. The collector also now receives the tensors the FFN actually used, and logs per-layer route counts and throughput. Only the imatrix collection path changes: the staging copies run only while `g->imatrix` is set.

## Validation

To check the numbers, I used a temporary, uncommitted CPU reference. With `DS4_GLM_MOE_REF_DUMP` set, the GPU is drained at each routed layer. The CPU then recomputes the FFN mHC pre-mix, `ffn_norm`, router top-k and weights, and the route-weighted SwiGLU rows from the GPU residual stream, using the existing CPU helpers. Those rows are turned into a `.dat` with the same layout.

On the same 32-token prompt (`GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`, `--imatrix-max-prompts 1 --imatrix-max-tokens 32`):

| build | max normalized error vs CPU reference | per-layer used experts | identical layer pairs |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | 1.4e-6 | 65..146, 42 layers | 0 of 861 |
| main | 7.3e3 | the same set in every layer | all |

Other checks:
- The fixed output is byte-identical with and without the reference dump enabled.
- In a full run (200k tokens, 396 prompts, 21.4 tokens/s), the route count per sparse layer is exactly tokens x 8, and every expert of every layer is covered.

I have not checked whether any published GGUF was quantized with an imatrix from this path.

## Testing

Machine: Apple M3 Max, 128 GB, macOS (Darwin 27), default Metal build.

- `make` (no warnings) and `make cpu` both build.
- `./ds4_test --server` passes.
- Speed, `ds4-bench` on `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`, main vs this PR: 

Runs in this order on the same machine and model; ctx 2048..16384 in steps of 4096, 64 generated tokens per frontier.

| ctx | main #1 prefill / gen t/s | PR #1 | main #2 | PR #2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 222.1 / 20.03 | 221.2 / 19.98 | 210.7 / 19.34 | 197.0 / 18.35 |
| 6144 | 192.6 / 19.86 | 194.3 / 19.88 | 178.9 / 18.85 | 171.2 / 18.30 |
| 10240 | 179.0 / 19.80 | 192.4 / 19.80 | 173.7 / 18.51 | 170.3 / 18.25 |
| 14336 | 183.5 / 19.71 | 188.7 / 19.50 | 170.1 / 18.18 | 169.4 / 18.20 |
| 16384 | 188.6 / 19.73 | 184.8 / 19.42 | 168.3 / 18.14 | 168.7 / 18.16 |

Differences are within run-to-run and thermal drift (later runs are slower for both builds). The changed code only runs while an imatrix is being collected.

Not run: the model-backed DeepSeek suites (`--logprob-vectors`, `--long-context`, `--tool-call-quality`), because there is no DeepSeek model on this machine. The change is limited to the GLM imatrix collector.

title: Keep chat marker strings in message content out of the special-token path
body:
The rendered-chat tokenizer turns every chat marker string into a special token, including ones that appear inside message content (`<｜User｜>`, `<|user|>`, `<think>`, `<tool_call>`, `｜DSML｜`, ...). This causes two problems:

1. **Turn-boundary injection.** Content that merely mentions a marker creates a fake turn boundary for the model. A coding agent that reads ds4's own sources runs into this constantly: `ds4_server.c` alone contains over a hundred `<｜` strings.
2. **Silent disk KV cache misses.** Cold snapshots are keyed by re-rendering their tokens to text (`ds4_kvstore_render_tokens_text`), but lookups compare against the raw prompt text. A marker that does not round-trip, such as `<｜User｜>` on GLM (re-rendered as `<|user|>`), breaks the byte-prefix match. The lookup then fails without any log line.

Reproduction on `GLM-5.3-Flash`: two chat requests with the same ~2.9k-token system prompt, differing only in the user message. The system prompt contains the literal text `<｜User｜>`.

| build | request B `cached_tokens` | request B time | server log |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0 | 15.8 s | no hit |
| this PR | 2868 | 0.33 s | `kv cache hit text tokens=2868 ... key=token-text` |

## Related

This addresses the injection reported in #95. #197 takes a different approach to the same report: it inserts a zero-width space into DeepSeek markers in user text. This PR instead:
- covers all four chat syntaxes and every kind of content, including tool results, tool-call arguments and schemas;
- leaves the bytes the model sees unchanged, because the markers are tokenized as their literal text rather than altered;
- also fixes the disk-cache key mismatch that the injection causes.

## Change

- **Escaping.** When the server renders a prompt, marker strings that come from message content (system, user, reasoning, tool results, tool names, arguments and schemas, assistant text) get a `0x01` byte in front; a literal `0x01` is doubled. The chat template's own markers are not escaped.
- **Tokenizer.** It drops the escapes and BPE-tokenizes the marker as ordinary text.
- **Cache keys.** `ds4_tokens_render_chat_text` produces the same escaped form from tokens, and `ds4_kvstore_render_tokens_text` now uses it. Token-derived keys therefore match the prompt byte for byte. A literal marker can no longer share a key with a real template marker.
- **Raw input.** Raw prompts without escapes (`-p`, `--prompt-file`, rendered-prompt input) are tokenized as before.
- **Assistant content** that starts with a think tag stays raw, as today (`text_starts_with_think_tag`).
- **GLM system role.** In `ds4_chat_append_message`, GLM system-role text is now plain text. The agent appends its trusted GLM tool prompt and reminder with the rendered tokenizer, so they keep their control tokens.
- **Debug log.** A disk-cache text lookup that finds nothing logs a debug line when `DS4_SERVER_KV_DEBUG` is set.

## Testing

Machine: Apple M3 Max, 128 GB, macOS (Darwin 27), default Metal build.

- `make` (no warnings) and `make cpu` both build.
- `./ds4_test --server`, `./ds4_agent_test` and `make test-chat-markers` pass. The CPU-only parts of `make test` also pass.
- `tests/test_chat_markers` builds synthetic tokenizer-only GGUFs for DeepSeek V4, V4.1, GLM and Qwen. It covers the marker table, escaping, tokenization, token-to-text rendering and the kvstore key path (store, lookup hit, and the miss log). Set `DS4_TEST_CHAT_MARKER_MODELS` to real GGUFs to also run it on real vocabularies; I ran it on two GLM 5.3 Flash GGUFs.
- The `--server` group renders every syntax with markers in each kind of content, tool call and schema. It also checks that each live tool tail and checkpoint suffix, appended to the prompt, equals the next request's full render.
- A tokenizer-only engine, `ds4_engine_open_vocab_only`, lets these tests use the real render, tokenize and key code without weights or a backend.
- Mutation check: I reverted each hunk of the change on its own and rebuilt from clean objects. Each of the 35 behavioural hunks, reverted alone, makes at least one test fail. The other 9 hunks only add helpers and cannot be reverted alone. I checked those with hand-written behaviour mutations instead, for example:
  - escaping as a no-op;
  - token-to-text rendering that does not escape;
  - assistant content always raw;
  - escape-parity checks ignored.

  All of them fail a test.
- **Old vs new on the GPU** (`GLM-5.3-Flash-IQ2-Down10Q2K-imatrix.gguf`, greedy, `ds4-server` from main vs from this PR): I sent 12 marker-free requests:
  - plain chat, a system prompt and Chinese text;
  - `reasoning_effort` high and max;
  - a 9 KB code system prompt and a cached second turn;
  - a tool call, a tool result follow-up with and without thinking;
  - a multi-turn chat;
  - Anthropic messages with and without `tool_use`/`tool_result`.

  All 12 have identical `prompt_tokens`, cached tokens, content, reasoning, tool calls and finish reason. Only the marker case differs, as shown above.

Not run: the model-backed DeepSeek and Qwen suites (`--logprob-vectors`, `--long-context`, `--tool-call-quality`). No DeepSeek or Qwen model is available here, so those families are covered only by the synthetic-vocabulary tests. No `ds4-bench` run: the change affects prompt rendering and tokenization, not the inference graph.

## Behaviour changes to be aware of

- Existing disk snapshots whose keys contain marker strings from content will miss once, then be rebuilt.
- Client content that only "worked" through injection (for example a raw `<think>` inside a user message) now reaches the model as text.
- `--trace` dumps of `prompt_text` show the `0x01` escape bytes.

title: Render GLM 5.3 low reasoning effort as Low
body:
GLM 5.3 (Flash and Full) chat templates accept `low` as a reasoning effort, but ds4 renders a requested `low` as `Reasoning Effort: High` for every GLM model.

The official templates:

- `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (rev 84c6a6a, also embedded in `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`) and `zai-org/GLM-5.3` (rev e0b07fd):
  `{%- set effective_reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort if reasoning_effort is defined and reasoning_effort in ['low', 'high'] else 'max' -%}`
- `zai-org/GLM-5.2` (main): `'high' if reasoning_effort == 'high' else 'max'`, so it has no low level.

This change renders an explicit `low` (and `minimal`, which ds4 already parses as low) as `Reasoning Effort: Low` when the loaded model's template supports it. The check runs once at model load, on the `effective_reasoning_effort` statement of the embedded `tokenizer.chat_template`. That covers GLM 5.3 Flash (`glm5-next`) and Full GLM 5.3, whose GGUFs use the `glm-dsa` architecture and load through the GLM 5.2 shape. A missing or unrecognised template keeps the old mapping, so GLM 5.2 is unchanged. `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, the unset default and disabled thinking are unchanged.

## Testing

Machine: Apple M3 Max, 128 GB, macOS (Darwin 27), default Metal build.

- `make` (no warnings) and `make cpu` both build.
- `./ds4_test --server` and `./ds4_agent_test` pass. The new `test_glm_template_low_effort_detection` and `test_glm_reasoning_effort_levels` pin:
  - template detection, using the opening lines of the official 5.3 and 5.2 templates;
  - the per-level mapping for both;
  - every request form that names an effort (OpenAI `reasoning_effort`, `chat_template_kwargs`, Anthropic `output_config` and `thinking`, Responses `reasoning`).
- The full official GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.2 templates give true and false through the detection function.
- End to end on `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`: `ds4-server --ctx 409600 --trace` with `reasoning_effort` set to low, medium, high and max rendered `Reasoning Effort: Low`, `High`, `High` and `Max`.

Not run: the model-backed suites (`--logprob-vectors`, `--long-context`, `--tool-call-quality`). There is no DeepSeek model on this machine, and only the rendered effort line changes. I had no Full GLM 5.3 or GLM 5.2 GGUF to load, so those two are covered through the detection function with the official template text. No speed test was run: the change only affects prompt text.

title: server: report Anthropic stop_sequence when a client stop matches
body:
## Summary

- `/v1/messages` now reports `stop_reason: "stop_sequence"` and the matched string in `stop_sequence` when a client `stop_sequences` entry ends the output, in both the full response and the streamed `message_delta`
- the matched sequence is recorded on the request when the decode loop finds it, next to the other per-request runtime fields, and cleared at the start of each decode
- other stop reasons are unchanged (`end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `tool_use`), and so is the OpenAI-style `finish_reason`
- add a no-model regression for the full and streamed responses, plus the plain `end_turn` case

## Why

The output is cut at the stop sequence correctly, but the response says the model ended its turn:

```
POST /v1/messages
{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","max_tokens":64,"temperature":0,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"},
 "stop_sequences":["5"],
 "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 10, separated by commas. Output only the numbers."}]}
```

Before:

```
"content":[{"type":"text","text":"1, 2, 3, 4, "}],"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null
```

After:

```
"content":[{"type":"text","text":"1, 2, 3, 4, "}],"stop_reason":"stop_sequence","stop_sequence":"5"
```

The streamed `message_delta` changes the same way. The Anthropic Messages API reports `stop_sequence` with the matched string in this case, and clients use it to tell a stop sequence from a natural end of turn.

## Testing

- Machine: Intel i5-13600KF, 128 GB RAM, Linux containers (Debian 12 with gcc 12.2 for `make cpu`, CUDA 12.9 devel for `ds4_test`).
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2.gguf` (the April Flash Q2, loaded from RAM).
- Live, `./ds4-server --cpu -c 8192 -t 12`: the request above before and after the change, non-streaming and streaming; a natural end still returns `end_turn` with `stop_sequence:null`, and `max_tokens:3` still returns `max_tokens`.
- `make ds4_test CUDA_ARCH=sm_86` (CUDA 12.9, RTX 3060), then `./ds4_test --server`: `server: OK`. Without the change the new test fails on its two `stop_sequence` assertions.

title: server: report max_output_tokens as the Responses incomplete reason
body:
## Summary

- `/v1/responses` now reports `incomplete_details.reason` as `"max_output_tokens"` when output is cut by the token budget, in both the full response and the streamed `response.incomplete` event
- add a no-model regression for both paths

## Why

The OpenAI Responses API defines `incomplete_details.reason` as `"max_output_tokens"` or `"content_filter"`. ds4 writes `"max_tokens"`, so a client that checks for `"max_output_tokens"` to detect a truncated answer does not see it:

```
POST /v1/responses
{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","input":"Count from 1 to 10.","max_output_tokens":3,"temperature":0,"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}
```

Before:

```
"status":"incomplete","incomplete_details":{"reason":"max_tokens"}
```

After:

```
"status":"incomplete","incomplete_details":{"reason":"max_output_tokens"}
```

## Testing

- Machine: Intel i5-13600KF, 128 GB RAM, Linux containers (Debian 12 with gcc 12.2 for `make cpu`, CUDA 12.9 devel for `ds4_test`).
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2.gguf` (the April Flash Q2).
- Live, `./ds4-server --cpu -c 4096 -t 12`: the request above before and after the change.
- `make ds4_test CUDA_ARCH=sm_86` (CUDA 12.9, RTX 3060), then `./ds4_test --server`: `server: OK`. With the old string in the two writers, the new test fails on both assertions.

title: Unterminated tool call: defer to the parse-failure recovery instead of erroring the turn
body:
## Summary

When the model opens a tool envelope in generated text and never closes it before the stop token, the generator sets `finish = "error"`. The response parser deliberately refuses to mark a result as recovered when `finish` is already `"error"` — correct for genuine faults — which makes the existing `recovered_tool_parse_failure` degrade path unreachable for exactly the case it was written for.

The two routes disagree today: an envelope the parser cannot execute degrades to assistant text with `finish_reason: "stop"`; an envelope that was never closed is reported as a server fault on every API surface:

- **OpenAI-compatible:** `finish_reason: "error"` on an HTTP 200 body — agent loops that branch on `finish_reason` treat the turn as failed and retry or abort.
- **Responses:** `status: "failed"` with `error.code = server_error` for something the server did not fail at.
- **Anthropic:** worse than visible-and-wrong — `anthropic_stop_reason` maps everything except `tool_calls`/`length` to `end_turn`, so the turn arrives as a normal completion with the raw truncated markup as the content and no indication anything happened.

An unclosed envelope is a model output shape (a truncated or rambling generation), not a server fault. This PR leaves `finish` alone on that branch so the existing recovery handles it the same way it handles an uncloseable-but-complete envelope: degrade to assistant text, `finish_reason: "stop"`, no `tool_calls`, and a WARNING log line plus a trace event so operators still see it.

Genuine faults keep their error: the enclosing guard still excludes `finish == "error"`, `finish == "length"`, and client stops, and the tool-error continuation route is tried first.

## Diff shape

```c
             } else {
-                finish = "error";
-                snprintf(err, sizeof(err), "unterminated tool call (%s; token=%d, generated=%d, limit=%d)",
-                         stop_detail, stop_token, completion, max_tokens);
+                /* model output shape, not a server fault: let the
+                 * parse-failure recovery below run ... */
+                server_log(DS4_LOG_WARNING, "... deferring to parse-failure recovery ...");
+                trace_event(s, trace_id, "unterminated tool call; deferring to parse-failure recovery");
             }
```

One behaviour change worth calling out: a turn whose entire output was an unclosed envelope now yields empty-ish content with `finish_reason: "stop"` instead of an error, which an agent loop may read as a successful no-op turn. The WARNING line is the operator's signal.

## Testing (per CONTRIBUTING.md)

Commands run, on an Apple M5 Max 128 GB, Metal backend, Qwen3.8 Flash Next Q4_K production model (test groups below are model-free):

```sh
make clean && make
./ds4_test --server          # server: OK   (parser/rendering/cache unit tests — the group that covers this path)
./ds4_test --metal-kernels   # metal-kernels: OK
```

Added a model-free unit case (`test_unterminated_envelope_recovers_when_finish_unset`) pinning both directions: a pre-set `"error"` finish blocks recovery (the shape this PR stops producing), an unset finish recovers to `"stop"` with zero executable calls and the raw text kept as fallback. The existing `test_incomplete_tool_call_keeps_stop_reason` continues to pass unchanged.

No inference backend is touched (server response path only), so no before/after `ds4-bench` CSV is attached; the change cannot affect prefill or decode throughput. `--logprob-vectors`, `--long-context` and `--tool-call-quality` were not re-run because the patch is in the response layer and does not alter rendered prompts, tokenization, or generation; happy to run them if you want belt-and-braces.

## Provenance

Found while investigating a transient `finish=error "unterminated tool call (stop token)"` at 239k context in production (1 of 149 tool turns). The mechanism that makes it reachable: message content is rendered verbatim and the tokenizer maps structural strings to real structural token ids anywhere in the rendered text, so content that quotes an envelope opener injects a real opener and the model continues inside a call it believes is open. That input-side behaviour is a separate question and this PR does not touch it.

Note: the recovery keeps the truncated envelope text in `content` (today it is included *and* reported as an error), so this PR does not make content worse; it only stops mislabelling the turn. A follow-up could strip the partial markup if you would rather it not reach clients.

title: Anthropic clients never see a failed turn: anthropic_stop_reason maps finish=="error" to end_turn
body:
## Summary

`anthropic_stop_reason` maps every finish state except `tool_calls` and `length` to `end_turn` — including `"error"`. A turn that failed server-side is therefore indistinguishable from a normal completion on the Anthropic API, and the error text is not surfaced anywhere in the response body or stream.

Current upstream code (`ds4_server.c` @ `0aaea5a`):

```c
static const char *anthropic_stop_reason(const char *finish) {   // :9038
    if (finish && !strcmp(finish, "tool_calls")) return "tool_use";
    if (finish && !strcmp(finish, "length")) return "max_tokens";
    return "end_turn";
}
```

Both Anthropic surfaces route through it: the non-streaming final message (`anthropic_final_response`, :9113, `stop_reason` at :9123) and the streaming terminator (`anthropic_sse_finish_live` → `message_delta`'s `stop_reason` at :9828).

The other two APIs are honest about the same event:

- **OpenAI-compatible**: `finish_reason: "error"` on the 200 body (the value is passed through verbatim).
- **Responses**: `finish == "error"` → `status: "failed"` with `error.code = "server_error"` (:8636, :8676).

And the SSE error event the server already has (`sse_error_event`, :7005, which emits a proper `type: "error"` / `api_error`) is called from exactly **one** place — `send_prefill_failure_response` (:12759). A failure raised *after* decoding (engine fault during generation, failed session append, unterminated tool call, stream-write failure) never reaches it on the Anthropic path.

## Observed in production

While investigating the case that became #1163: the model opened a tool envelope and never closed it, the generator set `finish = "error"`, and the Anthropic client received the raw truncated markup as ordinary assistant text with `stop_reason: "end_turn"`. Nothing in the response indicated anything had gone wrong; the only trace is in the server log. (#1163 removes that specific trigger by deferring to the parse-failure recovery, but the collapse itself stays for every other error class.)

## Why this is not a one-line mapping fix

Anthropic's `stop_reason` vocabulary (`end_turn | max_tokens | stop_sequence | tool_use | pause_turn`) has no error member, so the choices are shaped by what clients tolerate:

1. **Out-of-band surfacing (probably the smallest honest change):** keep `stop_reason: "end_turn"`, but deliver the failure alongside it — e.g. an `error` field on the message object, or a `message_delta`-adjacent `error` event reusing the existing `sse_error_event` machinery. Clients that ignore unknown fields keep working; clients that look can tell.
2. **HTTP-level errors for genuine server faults** (5xx, or a terminal error event mid-stream), while model-output shapes (unclosed envelope, parse failures) stay completions — which is the same distinction #1163 draws one layer down.
3. **Document the collapse** so an operator debugging a silent Anthropic failure knows to check the server log rather than the response.

Option 2 changes failure semantics clients can actually branch on, but risks breaking agent loops that today silently receive `end_turn` and treat the truncated markup as a real answer (a working failure mode, in a sense). I don't have a strong claim on which the project prefers — hence the issue rather than a PR; happy to implement whichever shape you pick, with the Anthropic unit cases pinned against the current `anthropic_final_response`/`anthropic_sse_finish_live` pair.

## Reproduction notes (per CONTRIBUTING.md)

Machine/backend/model: Apple M5 Max 128 GB, Metal, Qwen3.8 Flash Next Q4_K + vision, production server (`--thinking enabled`, Anthropic `/v1/messages` via `REQ_ANTHROPIC`). The error-finish trigger (unclosed envelope) is model-output-shaped and rare by construction (1 of 149 tool turns in a multi-day soak), so a deterministic local repro is easier through the parse layer than the model: generate/hold a result with `finish == "error"` and observe `anthropic_final_response` emits `stop_reason: "end_turn"` with the content verbatim.

`ds4_test --server` is green on current main at these line references; this issue reports behavior, it is not a crash.

title: Server: advertise loaded model modalities
body:
Adds `architecture.input_modalities` and `architecture.output_modalities` to `/v1/models` and `/v1/models/{id}`. Input includes `image` only when `ds4_engine_has_vision()` reports that the loaded engine is ready for vision; otherwise it contains only `text`. Output remains `text`, and compatibility aliases report the same loaded-engine capabilities. This lets discovery clients configure image support automatically.

title: Concurrent cold prefills of multiple sessions collapse throughput (1365 t/s solo -> 5-95 t/s each with 2 simultaneous prefills)
body:
## Environment

- Mac Studio M5 Ultra, 256 GB, Metal backend
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4 (`qwen38-q4k`, 69.7 GiB resident), BF16 n-grams on disk
- `ds4-server --ctx 2097152 --batched-session 4 --kv-disk-space-mb 153600 --prefill-chunk 8192` (+ `DS4_QWEN4_YARN_FACTOR=2`)
- Observed on two separate incidents on 2026-10-01, and reproducible on demand

## Solo cold prefill (reference, same machine/config)

| prompt | rate |
|---|---|
| 468,960 tok | 1365 t/s (343.7 s) |
| 188,960 tok | 1645 t/s |
| 33,960 tok | 1804 t/s |

## Two concurrent cold prefills

**Incident 1** — a 282k-token session and a 91k-token session started cold prefill at the same time. Both collapsed to ~5 t/s per chunk-progress entry (aggregate ~10 t/s vs 1365 solo):

```
chat ctx=0..282540:282540 prefill chunk 27136/282540 (9.6%) chunk=4.78 t/s avg=141.45 t/s 191.846s
chat ctx=0..91087:91087 prefill chunk 512/91087 (0.6%) chunk=4.75 t/s avg=5.40 t/s 94.810s
```

**Incident 2** — one ~70k session (turn 1) plus its next turns re-prefilling, two sessions prefilling concurrently. Both at 51-95 t/s:

```
chat ctx=20480..78997:58517 prefill chunk 36864/58517 (63.0%) chunk=83.92 t/s avg=79.88 t/s 461.510s
chat ctx=25728..70972:45244 prefill chunk 16384/45244 (36.2%) chunk=84.81 t/s avg=81.07 t/s 202.091s
```

Notes:
- The collapse is much worse than a fair time-share: two prefills should give ~600-700 t/s each; instead aggregate drops to 10-170 t/s (8-100x total loss).
- KV disk cache is not the cause: budget is 150 GiB, cache dir was purged between tests, no `disk-cache-full` evictions in the incident-2 window.
- Warm/decode behavior while another session prefills is fine (65 t/s decode alongside 500-800 t/s incremental prefill chunks in normal operation).

## What I tried

- `--mixed-prefill-quantum 4096` (default 128) — no improvement, concurrent prefills still ran at 83-95 t/s.

## Secondary observation (possibly related)

During/after concurrent prefill, the next turn of the same session only hit ~20-25k tokens of KV disk cache instead of the full 70k+ prefix — turn 2 re-prefilled from offset 20480/25728 (chunks are stored with `reason=continued`, `cold_max=30000`). Under solo operation, full-prefix hits work as expected (e.g. `kv cache hit text tokens=133120 ... load=295.9 ms`).

## Repro

```
# two parallel fresh (uncached) 70k+ prompts to /v1/chat/completions
# (stream=false, max_tokens small) -> both prefill at 50-95 t/s instead of ~1400
```

## Workaround

We now serialize big cold prefills at a proxy in front of ds4 (FIFO lock, released on first streamed token), which restores solo-speed prefills for queued requests. But it feels like the mixed-prefill scheduler could either serialize large prefills internally or interleave them without the collapse — is there a flag/approach I'm missing, or is this worth investigating in the scheduler?

Thank you for ds4 — it's genuinely impressive engineering; single-session performance is in a different league from anything else on this hardware.

title: Add n-gram prompt-lookup speculative drafting
body:
Opt-in draft source (--ngram-spec N) for greedy decoding: find the most recent earlier occurrence of the last few tokens (n=3) in the session context and propose the tokens that followed it, up to N per cycle. Drafts go through the existing DSpark batched verifier: a draft commits only if the target's recomputed argmax agrees, so greedy decoding is lossless with respect to the verifier's own logits.

Like the existing DSpark/MTP paths, accepted tokens keep the state produced by the batched verifier, whose floating-point reduction order can differ from one-token decode — so long greedy continuations need not be byte-identical to target-only decode (see docs/SPECULATIVE_DECODING.md, "Accepted tokens keep the state produced by the batched verifier"). This is pre-existing speculative-framework behavior, not specific to this drafter: on a 400-token greedy reasoning prompt, --dspark also diverges from target-only decode, earlier than --ngram-spec 5 does. The acceptance fixture's prompts (<=256 tokens) do produce byte-identical output on/off. For strict target-only comparison use --quality or --dspark-strict, which disable drafting.

Reuses the DSpark verifier, commit/rollback machinery and back-off scheduler; no draft weights. DeepSeek V4 Flash family, CPU and Metal backends only. Width 5 recommended: it matches the verifier prefix slots, wider widths pay rollback replays.

The flag is wired into ds4, ds4-agent, ds4-bench and (after the second commit) ds4-server; help text covers all four.

Measured on M5 Max (Flash Q2): +19% greedy decode on a code-shaped prompt (46.4 -> 54.8 tok/s); neutral to slightly negative on sparse prose/reasoning prompts (-0.7% to -2.4%), since gains scale with context repetition density. Recommended for repetitive/code/agent-replay workloads.

Adds tests/test_ngram_propose.py and tests/ngram_spec_acceptance_fixture.sh.

title: Back off speculative drafting on consecutive rejected proposals
body:
Stacked on top of #1167: only the last commit ("Back off speculative drafting on consecutive rejected proposals") is new here; the first two commits are #1167's n-gram drafter and its server flag fix. If #1167 merges first, this PR collapses to the single scheduler commit.

This one is independent of the n-gram drafter and governs DSpark as well: both draft sources share the speculative scheduler, and today rejection-heavy passages (prose, reasoning) are handled with flat windowed pauses — a ~50% probe duty cycle that pays a batched verify for every stale proposal.

Change:

- Consecutive rejected proposals now double the drafting pause (2, 4, 8 ... up to 64 cycles). The first miss is left unpunished: an echoed pattern usually re-locks on the very next proposal, and pausing there only shifts the drafting phase out of the repeating pattern.
- Accepted cycles accrue credit (one per accept, two for a full-width accept, capped at 16). A rejected proposal spends one credit instead of growing the miss streak, so a long high-acceptance stretch keeps drafting through its isolated misses, while a genuinely dead passage still reaches the exponential ladder once the saved credit runs out.
- Any accepted draft restores drafting immediately.

Knobs (all optional): DS4_DSPARK_SCHEDULER_EXP_BACKOFF_BASE (0 restores the old flat pauses only), _CAP, _MIN_STREAK and _CREDIT (0 disables credit and keeps the bare miss-streak ladder).

Measured on M5 Max (Flash Q2, draft width 5, interleaved A/B):
- Code-shaped echo: 44.1 -> 52.7 tok/s over drafting off (+19.5%); slightly above the old flat-pause scheduler (52.2).
- Reasoning prose (400 tokens): neutral (-0.1%).
- DSpark prose, two prompts: neutral.
- Greedy output stays byte-identical with drafting on/off; the acceptance fixtures pass unchanged.

Adds tests/test_dspark_exp_backoff.py (extracts the real scheduler helpers; covers the ladder and caps, reset-on-accept, no-draft neutrality, credit accrual/absorption/exhaustion, and the kill switches). docs/SPECULATIVE_DECODING.md documents the behavior and the knobs.

title: Preserve exact tool-call replay across KV checkpoint restores
body:
## Problem

Tool memory stores complete sampled spans, but checkpoint serialization derives delimiter fragments. These can differ for multi-call sequences, whitespace and literal tags, causing replay IDs to be lost. Canonical re-rendering then prevents reuse of the saved KV frontier.

There is also a turn-boundary mismatch: decode can stop before evaluating EOS, while replayed assistant messages include it. EOS commitment, live continuation tails and visible checkpoint keys must agree.

## Changes

- Persist complete remembered spans and their associated IDs, preserving exact whitespace and multi-call identity for Qwen, GLM and DSML.
- Match stored spans with a radix prefix walk. Normalize leading whitespace only in the index; retain the original bytes and identity.
- Keep EOS in live KV and Qwen tool-visible keys without duplicating it in continuation tails.
- Handle checkpoint keys that omit EOS when the loaded token payload already contains it. Payloads without EOS retain the incoming boundary.
- Publish closed-turn frontier mappings only after successful EOS commitment and valid session state.
- Add model-free and live regression tests. The live test owns its subprocesses and requires no external launcher scripts or vision artifact.
- Fix cache-trace parsing and check actual KV reuse rather than requiring retokenized BPE prefixes to match.

KTM v1, existing limits and checkpoint policy remain unchanged. Interrupted generation may still require replaying the gap after the last usable disk checkpoint.

## Related work and review order

This PR is tracked in [cache issue #1201](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1201), alongside [#1175](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1175) and [#1200](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1200). This repair preserves replay identity and the EOS boundary; #1175 separately validates whether the submitted parent history still matches the live context. #1200 adds bounded checkpoints at completed incoming prompts. Their responsibilities and merge decisions remain separate.

Review this PR and #1175 before #1200 so that additional reuse opportunities build on valid history and replay identity. This is a review recommendation, not a strict build dependency. EOS commitment, continuation tails, visible keys and legacy-key handling stay coordinated within this PR. Independent Metal throughput changes are grouped in [prefill issue #1202](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1202); implementation and validation for this repair remain below.

## Build and model-free verification

Base: `antirez/ds4` main at `0aaea5a`.

```sh
make cpu
make clean
make -j4 ds4_test ds4-server
./ds4_test --server
python3 -m py_compile tests/test_server_tool_replay.py tests/test_server_turn_boundary.py
```

CPU build, clean Metal builds, server tests, Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. No CPU inference was run.

Launcher checks covered startup, graceful shutdown, restart and failed-startup cleanup with a small HTTP fixture. Trace checks covered LF/CRLF input and full KV reuse despite a shorter retokenized BPE prefix.

ASan/UBSan checks covered the changed server, RAX and KV-store paths (`-fsanitize=address,undefined`, `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1`, `UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1`). Leak detection was unsupported on the tested macOS setup.

## Live cache-reuse verification

Machine/backend: Apple M5 Max, Metal, macOS 26.6.2.
Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf`, MTP exact sampling.

```sh
python3 tests/test_server_tool_replay.py \
  --model gguf/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf
```

The production repair was exercised with twelve sampled tool calls and a history exceeding 44k tokens. Nested argument key order was reversed in retained client history, preserving values while forcing canonical byte divergence. The self-contained launcher included here was checked separately; the full model run was not repeated after the launcher refactor.

| Case | Cached tokens | Prefill tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| Restart with replay map | 47,604 | 27 |
| Copied checkpoint key with EOS omitted | 47,604 | 27 |
| Copied cache with TOOL_MAP disabled | 392 | 46,336 |
| Subsequent live continuation | 47,681 | 22 |
| Recovery after stream cancellation | 47,604 | 158 |

Restart restored all twelve IDs without canonical fallback. The live continuation required no disk KV load. Cancellation retained the saved frontier and replayed the remaining checkpoint gap; this is not a zero-prefill guarantee.

GLM and DSML coverage is model-free; live validation used Qwen only.

## Serialization cost and remaining coverage

The model-free benchmark with 100k IDs and 500 parsed two-call spans measured 630,050 B text, a 1,270,788 B trailer, 0.79 ms selection and 2.09 ms writing. These are serialization measurements, not an inference-throughput comparison. Overlapping long body prefixes remain a documented matching-cost ceiling.

No inference kernels, quantization or distributed/CUDA implementations are changed. CUDA, distributed and SSD-streaming runtime validation was not performed.

title: Keep the disk KV checkpoint the next request loads when storing an evict snapshot
body:
When the server switches sessions, the disk KV snapshot it just stored for the outgoing session can be deleted moments before that same session comes back and needs it. The returning session then prefills its whole context again.

On a live KV miss, `generate_job_inner` does three things in order:

1. stores the outgoing session as an evict snapshot (`kv_cache_store_current(..., "evict", ...)`);
2. before that store, calls `ds4_kvstore_evict` to make room, deleting the lowest eviction score first;
3. calls `kv_cache_try_load` for the incoming prompt.

A fresh evict snapshot has zero hits, so its score is usually the lowest on disk. Any older checkpoint with a hit in roughly the last 40 hours outranks it. With two sessions taking turns (an agent and its subagent, for example), step 2 for one session can delete the snapshot that step 3 of the next switch back needs.

## Fix

- The evict store passes the incoming prompt text as `protect_text` in `ds4_kvstore_eviction_context`. Eviction never deletes the checkpoint a load of that prompt would pick. The pick uses `kv_cache_best_text_prefix`, which is now shared by eviction and lookup, so both apply the same longest-prefix and model/quant/ctx rules.
- If the budget cannot be met even after deleting every other entry, `ds4_kvstore_evict` returns false without deleting anything. The outgoing snapshot is then skipped with a log line, as before when a snapshot does not fit.
- Shutdown, cold and continued stores pass no protection.
- The eviction score formula is unchanged. The first commit added a grace period for young evict snapshots; the third commit removes it, because the protection alone fixes the switch.

## Reproduction (DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 Q2)

Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731.gguf`. Both binaries ran with `--ctx 32768 --kv-disk-space-mb 450` and a fresh `--kv-disk-dir`, and received identical HTTP requests (temperature 0, thinking off). The sequence:

1. Conversation X, then another conversation that pushes X out of the live session, then X's next turn, so X's snapshot gets one disk hit.
2. Session A (about 7.4k tokens), two turns.
3. Session B (about 11.9k tokens). A is stored as an evict snapshot.
4. A's next turn.

| | Deleted when storing B's evict snapshot | A's next turn | Prompt time | HTTP time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` 0aaea5a | A's evict snapshot (`tokens=7362 hits=0 size=119.50 MiB`) | `chat ctx=0..7376`, full prefill | 29.24 s | 29.37 s |
| this branch | B's cold snapshot (`tokens=11919 hits=0 size=179.34 MiB`) | `kv cache hit text tokens=7362 ... load=34.5 ms`, `chat ctx=7362..7376` | 0.36 s | 0.60 s |

The bug appears when the freshly stored evict snapshot is the lowest-scoring entry. If B is small, B's own cold snapshot scores lower and is deleted first, and the bug does not show. X, which has a hit, scores about twice as high and survives in both runs.

## Testing

Machine: Apple M3 Max, 128 GB, macOS (Darwin 27), default Metal build.

- `make` and `make cpu` build with no warnings.
- `./ds4_test --server` passes, with no model loaded. Three new tests use stub `.kv` files:
  - `test_kv_cache_eviction_protects_checkpoint_about_to_load`: the agent/subagent switch. The checkpoint survives with protection and is evicted without it.
  - `test_kv_cache_eviction_protects_after_earlier_victims`: the protected entry's index has to move when an entry before it is evicted.
  - `test_kv_cache_eviction_keeps_protected_checkpoint_when_full`: when the budget cannot be met, nothing is deleted.
  - The tests also stat the files left on disk and check that the remaining size plus the incoming bytes fits the budget after a successful evict.
- I tried seven mutations of the fix (for example, dropping the protection or the index adjustment). Each one makes a test fail.
- The same change has run on my local server with GLM 5.3 Flash since 2026-10-01. In an agent/subagent workflow, the main session's three returns all loaded from disk (11806, 12319 and 12490 tokens; 3.0, 0.4 and 1.5 s) instead of a 62–68 s prefill.

Not run: the model-backed suites (`--logprob-vectors`, `--long-context`, `--tool-call-quality`) and speed benchmarks. The change only touches KV disk-cache bookkeeping in the server and does not touch inference.

title: Metal: enable GLM expert cache for mixed Q2_K gate/up and Q4_K down
body:
## Summary

GLM SSD streaming bypasses its address-based expert cache when gate/up tensors are Q2_K and down tensors are Q4_K, although the existing Metal pair and down kernels handle their formats independently.

## Current Behavior

At 9139e2ae58a41503968a500f36f75895c1ba63fc, `glm_stream_expert_cache_addr_layout_supported` accepts only all-Q2 or all-Q4 for this path. The Metal decode and prefill wrappers repeat this restriction. A mixed GGUF passes layout validation but reports per-layer fallback.

On an M5 Max with 128 GiB, a local converted GLM artifact did not complete the first response after 13 minutes at a 16 GiB expert budget. A 32 GiB diagnostic was stopped after about ten minutes without first text. These are interrupted observations under background load, not controlled throughput results or proof that this predicate explains all latency.

## Expected Behavior

Permit Q2 gate/up with Q4 down through the existing Metal address kernels after verifying numerical agreement and cache lifetime behavior. Preserve all-Q2/all-Q4 and non-Metal behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Synthetic mapped/address comparisons cover mixed decode and prefill, including cold/hit cases.
- [x] Existing homogeneous paths remain correct.
- [x] A mixed GLM model uses the address-cache path and returns a response.

## Tasks

- [x] Add the narrowly scoped Metal capability predicates and regression coverage.
- [x] Align Q4 address-down fallback pipeline names with their SIMD dispatch.
- [x] Measure real-model behavior before selecting the local deployment.

## References

Local operational tracking: https://app.notion.com/p/3ed98b91d3ee812cb01ad87ce70d5eb6

## Implementation and local validation

Implemented in #1172 at commit `1a5d5966a6d7ddc8c5733d91b757712dc76048bc`; upstream merge remains pending.

- Mixed and homogeneous layouts passed 18 normal/statics-disabled decode and prefill cases, including mapped/cache numerical agreement, cache overflow, and verified cold/hit/changed-ID counters.
- Full build and CPU-only compilation passed; independent review found no remaining required changes. CUDA/ROCm hardware was not tested.
- A real mixed GLM completed the short-prefill smoke and all eight local evaluation requests. The same runtime also completed the DeepSeek comparison and a final normal-service generation after deployment. Shared background load prevents isolated throughput claims.

The completed checklist describes the implementation and local evidence, not an upstream release. This issue stays open while #1172 awaits maintainer review/merge.

title: fix(metal): cache GLM mixed Q2/Q4 routed experts
body:
## Problem and change

GLM routed layers with Q2_K gate/up and Q4_K down projections bypass Metal's file-backed expert cache. Allow this combination to use the existing independent pair/down address kernels, and share the layout predicate with the forward dispatch so mapping and `force_resident` agree. Correct the Q4 down fallback pipeline names to match their SIMD registrations.

CUDA/ROCm layout support is unchanged. Cache sizing, resident-layer policy and full-layer prefill behavior remain in place.

## Validation

- `make` and CPU-only object build pass.
- New `make test-glm-mixed-cache`: Q2/Q4, Q2/Q2 and Q4/Q4 at 1, 28 and 96 tokens, repeated with `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_HOT_PIPELINE_STATICS=1` (18 passing cases).
- Mapped references versus file-backed reads with the mapped weights zeroed; cold, repeated and half-changed selections. Decode counters verify 0/8, 8/8, 12/12 cumulative hits/misses.
- Real GLM SSD-streaming server: 28-token prompt followed by generation completes with the requested exact 1–20 list; no missing mapped-range errors. This exercises the C forward dispatch as well as Metal.
- Independent review and `git diff --check` clean. CUDA/ROCm hardware and distributed execution were not run.

Fixes #1171
