title: metal: stream GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 through the expert cache, for decode and prefill
body:
Currently GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 is unusable on RAM constrained Macs on main with decode collapsing to 0.03 tok/s on a 64GB Mac with the GPU starved and most of the time spent shuffling bytes. This branch fixes that and gets a usable 6.6 tok/s.

Also, I have a 128GB M3 Max and wanted to see if I can use GLM with SSD streaming to fit in a ~80GB budget with KV cache and all in (so I can keep working on full stack projects with several containers), but `-ssd-streaming-cache-experts` wasn't honoured and the whole model got wired anyway.

Claude's full write-up:

## Problem

GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 (`GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`: routed IQ2_XXS gate/up, Q2_K down, eight experts per token) has no bounded SSD-streaming mode on Metal.

`glm_stream_selected_expert_cache_supported` refuses IQ2/Q2_K on Apple unless `DS4_N_EXPERT_USED == 6`, because the IQ2/Q2 selected-slot down kernel (`kernel_mul_mv_slots6_q2_K_sum6_f32`) sums exactly six experts. No layer counts as streamed, so:

- **Default (static decode map):** the decode map covers every routed tensor, i.e. the whole 89.88 GiB file. It ignores `--ssd-streaming-cache-experts`: a 62 GB request becomes a 9 GiB cache inside a 106 GiB plan.
- **Where that map does not fit (Macs under 128 GB), or with `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_STREAMING_STATIC_DECODE_MAP=1`:** the per-layer fallback stays within budget, but it maps each layer's full expert span every token, and the cache is budgeted but never filled. Decode is **0.58 tok/s** on a 128 GB Mac, where spare RAM caches much of the file. With 64 GB locked away (a simulated 64 GB Mac), it is **0.03 tok/s**: 32 tokens took about 18 minutes.

Related: #1171 / #1172 fix the same kind of bypass for Q2_K gate/up with Q4_K down. That one only needs a predicate change; this one needs kernels.

## Who this helps

On a 128 GB Mac with default flags nothing changes: the whole-file map still fits and is still chosen. The cache route is taken on an explicit `--ssd-streaming-cache-experts`, or **automatically wherever the whole-file map does not fit**, which is the case for 64 and 96 GB Macs. There it replaces the per-layer fallback (0.03 tok/s decode on a simulated 64 GB Mac).

## Change (five commits)

1. **Decode through the cache.** `kernel_mul_mv_addr_q2_K_f32` (`metal/moe.metal`) is a per-expert Q2_K down projection through the streaming address table, the Q2_K twin of `kernel_mul_mv_addr_iq2_xxs_f32`. The IQ2 address-table route takes a Q2_K down whenever the six-slot path does not apply; with eight experts the existing `moe_sum_experts` reduces the rows. `ds4_engine_fit_glm_streaming_budget` picks the route once per engine. Metal TP refuses an engine on this route.
2. **Full-layer reads for continued chunks.** Continued prefill chunks of GLM 5.3 skipped the full-layer `pread` prepare so typed Flash layouts can reuse cached experts. This layout had no such route, so its layers were demand-faulted from the mmap at about 1.9 GB/s. They now use the prepare (about 5.3 GB/s, waits hidden).
3. **Seed the cache from the final full-layer chunk only.** The per-layer seed syncs and copies, and only warms the decode after the final chunk. Layouts whose continued chunks do not read full layers keep seeding from the first chunk.
4. **Short chunks through the cache.** Chunks under 256 tokens (chat appends, prompt tails) do not read full layers. IQ2/IQ2 already served them from the cache; with a Q2_K down they faulted whole layers in, since 128 tokens with eight experts touch nearly every expert of a layer. Adds Q2_K instantiations of the cached (`EXPERT_ADDRESSES`) `mul_mm_id` kernels and accepts a Q2_K down in the cached batch route and its decode-only map. The arithmetic is the resident kernels' with only the source pointer changed.
5. **Large chunks through the cache, misses read ahead.** A chunk of 128 or more tokens selects nearly all of a layer's 256 experts, so its misses are the uncached experts, known before routing. Such chunks take the cached batch route, and a page-in job reads each layer's uncached experts one layer ahead on the existing read threads (new `ds4_gpu_stream_expert_cache_layer_cached()` lists them without touching recency or hit counts). While the cache holds under a quarter of all routed experts, a chunk reads full layers and seeds instead, because copying almost every expert in costs more than it saves. `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_GLM_STREAMING_PREFILL_CACHE=1` restores full-layer reads.

DeepSeek V4 Flash (the same layout, six experts) is unchanged: `use_iq2_selected_slots` still wins at six, and the IQ2/IQ2 cached route keeps its 256-token limit.

## Validation

All on an M3 Max 128 GiB. Identical runs drift by up to 15% under sustained SSD reads, so the A/B pairs below were interleaved. "Simulated 64 GB Mac" means `--simulate-used-memory 64GB` (64 GB mlocked before load, so the page cache cannot hold the file) and a 28 GB cache, roughly what a 64 GB Mac auto-sizes.

**Decode and the 2K-step sweep** (`--ssd-streaming-cache-experts 62GB`, 2048-token steps, 128 generated tokens):

| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 | planned | prefill t/s 2K / 4K / 6K / 8K | decode t/s |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| before: static map, budget ignored | 106 GiB | 151 / 141–142 | 15.6–16.1 |
| before: static map disabled (per-layer, cache empty) | 73 GiB | 162 / — | **0.58** |
| commit 1 | 73 GiB | 118 / 43–45 | 11.0–13.1 |
| commits 1–2 | 73 GiB | 112 / 106 / 80 / — | 10.8–13.8 |
| **all five** | **73 GiB** | **124 / 132 / 138 / 122** | **11.2–13.8** |
| resident | — | 178 / 159–162 | 17.1–17.7 |

**Default flags on a 128 GB Mac** keep the whole-file map, and every prefill decision there reduces to upstream's: continued chunks don't re-read full layers, no seed is deferred, and the Q2_K batch is forced off the cache routes unless the engine chose the cache route (`glm_stream_selected_expert_cache_supported`). An interleaved A/B against `0aaea5a` stayed within run-to-run drift.

**Simulated 64 GB Mac, main against this PR** (28 GB cache, 2048-token steps, 32 generated tokens; main forced onto the per-layer fallback with `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_STREAMING_STATIC_DECODE_MAP=1`, since its budget sizing sees the physical 128 GB):

| | 2K prefill t/s | 2K decode t/s (steady) | 2K first token | 4K prefill t/s | 4K decode t/s (steady) |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| main, one run | 122.9 | **0.03** (0.03) | 32.7 s | not run (about 20 min per step) | — |
| this PR, two runs | 104.1, 110.0 | **5.9, 6.4** (7.3–7.4) | 0.82–1.25 s | 125.3, 128.2 | 8.7 (9.0) |

On the cold first chunk both read full layers, but this PR also seeds the cache from it so that decode starts warm, which costs 10–15% of that chunk's prefill.

**One 16K-token prompt, then 128 tokens** (interleaved, two runs each, commit 5 toggled with its env var):

| | prefill t/s | decode t/s | first token |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 62 GB cache, commits 1–4 | 114–124 | 9.5–9.6 | 0.84–0.89 s |
| 62 GB cache, all five | 111–112 | 12.1–12.4 | 0.16–0.17 s |
| simulated 64 GB Mac, commits 1–4 | 92–97 | 6.1–6.3 | 1.2–1.4 s |
| simulated 64 GB Mac, all five | 96–98 | 6.6 | 0.35–0.38 s |

Commit 5 leaves prefill level, because the cache inserts are still synchronous per layer. What it buys is the warm cache that decode starts from. Commit 3 alone took this prompt from 91 to 114 tok/s.

**128-token appends after a 2K prompt** (62 GB cache, 32 generated tokens each):

| | prefill t/s | time per append | decode t/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| commits 1–3 | 3.4–3.6 | ~36 s | 7.4–8.0 |
| all five | 36–51 | 2.5–3.6 s | 12.7–13.5 |

**Correctness**
- `make test-metal-iq2-q2k-stream-cache`: decode at six and eight experts; prefill batches of 4, 31, 64, 200 and 512 tokens at eight experts (tiny pair, `mul_mv_id` and `mul_mm_id` kernels). Each case takes a resident reference, then zeroes the mapped weights and streams with only the file holding real weights. It also checks that the cached-expert listing matches the batch's selection.
- Greedy parity, streamed vs resident, byte-identical (`cmp`) over 96 tokens, `--temp 0 --nothink`, `--ssd-streaming-cache-experts 62GB`. Prompts: 2183 tokens (a full chunk plus a 135-token tail), and 5477 tokens (cold, warm and short chunks).
- `make test` and `make test-metal-moe-prefill` pass, with `ds4flash.gguf` = DeepSeek V4 Flash IQ2XXS-w2Q2K.

Not run: a real 64 or 96 GB Mac (simulated only), CUDA/ROCm (untouched), and distributed/TP hardware (the TP guard is a refusal).

## Possible follow-up

Making the large-chunk cache inserts asynchronous should lift prefill toward compute-bound. That means staging misses into a transient buffer and building the address table without a per-layer readback, so no GPU drain per layer. It's a larger change (an estimated 700+ lines), best as a separate PR.

title: server: honor rewritten history in live tool continuations
body:
## Problem

The Responses and Anthropic live tool-output reuse tier can silently substitute cached history for the history supplied in a full replay request. It checks the pending tool-call IDs, then reuses the entire live KV frontier and appends only the new results, without checking the earlier input.

For example, a client compacts older history while retaining the latest assistant call and its matching result:

```text
Before: original history -> assistant call X -> result for X
After:  summary + retained history -> assistant call X -> result for X
```

The second request supplies the context the model should receive. Retaining the call/result pair preserves the exchange and its exact result; it does not ask the server to restore the discarded history. A call ID associates a result with its invocation, not with an immutable conversation prefix. Manual replay includes both items, as shown in the [Responses function-calling documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling).

ds4 nevertheless treats the unchanged IDs as proof that the whole live context still applies. The model receives the original history plus the result, and never sees the supplied summary. A fresh evaluation would render the compacted input, so cache reuse changes request semantics. This can defeat compaction, report inflated input-token usage, and trigger repeated compactions. Edited or branched replay histories can hit the same server error.

This full replay is distinct from a results-only request that depends on server-held continuation state. Deleting the call/result pair and folding its outcome into a summary can avoid the trigger, but a client should also be able to retain that pair while changing older history. The reuse optimization must validate the supplied parent before skipping it.

Related cache-reuse designs also bind reuse to preceding context. [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/edd6e2bbdad5930899a93db8fa73c3b61c7b9bcc/tools/server/server-context.cpp#L3087-L3287) compares the incoming token prefix before retaining KV. [oMLX](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/blob/68c8c09f6f6a54fe36181f9aabba9525797d1b58/omlx/cache/paged_cache.py#L75-L113) incorporates the parent prefix into each block's identity, following the principle documented by [vLLM](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/). These designs support validating parent context before reuse; this PR applies that principle to ds4's tool-ID continuation shortcut.

A tool result followed by ordinary user messages also disabled this tier: the old preparation scanned for results only at the absolute end of the request. When visible/token replay cannot match the sampled frontier, this unnecessarily discards usable KV even though the parent and call IDs are unchanged.

## Fix

Bind each live tool frontier to the canonical input that generated it. For a replay continuation, remove the latest declaring assistant turn, trailing results and following user messages from a shallow message view, then require that parent to match before taking the tool-ID tier.

Keep the results and following user messages together in the rendered continuation suffix, in their original order. The parent comparison still covers all earlier submitted history; edited parents, changed images and stale frontiers cannot gain reuse through this case.

Prepare keys before sampled tool-memory substitution. Normalize request-local image markers and compare their counts and positions as well as normalized text. Routing and execution share the guard; a mismatch falls through to the existing token/text/disk reuse paths.

Genuine results-only continuations retain their existing ID binding. They publish no full-history proof, so a later full replay cannot inherit their exemption. Anthropic input containing preceding history is not classified as results-only merely because its declaring assistant is absent.

The production change is confined to `ds4_server.c`, including model-free regression tests. The existing `tests/test_server_vision_live_state.py` gains a `responses-tool-users` section that requires the server log to verify the reuse tier. Backend computation and KV serialization are unchanged.

## Related work and review order

This PR is tracked in [cache issue #1201](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1201), alongside [#1169](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1169) and [#1200](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1200). This guard decides whether reuse is valid for the submitted parent; #1169 preserves exact tool replay/EOS identity across live and disk reuse; #1200 supplies additional completed-prompt checkpoints. Preserved tool IDs alone do not prove that earlier history is unchanged, so neither of those changes replaces this guard.

Prioritize this correctness fix and #1169 before #1200. That is a review recommendation, not a strict build dependency. Metal throughput changes are tracked independently in [prefill issue #1202](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1202). This PR remains server-only and retains its own regression and compaction evidence below.

## Validation

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB RAM, macOS 26.6.2, Metal; live model `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf`:

- `make -j4 cpu` passed (build only).
- `make clean`, `make -j4`, `make -j4 ds4_test`, `./ds4_test --server`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Model-free tests cover unchanged replay, summary replacement, middle-history edits/removal, changed system/tools/earlier-call arguments, results-only input, absent parent proof, anchorless Anthropic history, and image placement versus marker nonces.
- Live Qwen Responses A/B: unchanged replay reused 4,722 tokens with a 26-token suffix. Replacing history with a summary reduced the effective prompt from 4,748 to 401 tokens. The unpatched control retained the old frontier and grew to 4,852 tokens on the same compacted input.

The additional tool-result/user-message regression passes standalone `make -j4 all ds4_test`, `./ds4_test --server`, `make -j4 cpu` (build only), Python compilation and `git diff --check`. It covers one/nine following user messages, suffix order, edited parents, no-result/intervening-message cases, results-only binding, shifted retained-image offsets, changed image identity and stale frontiers.

A sequential live Qwen Responses control/candidate comparison retained one image and omitted emitted tool-turn reasoning to exercise the tool-ID tier. Both builds used the existing local integration of #1169 and #1206; only this preparation fix differed. Managed servers used isolated caches, medium reasoning, temperature 0 and opportunistic MTP. No actual tool or background task ran.

| Following user messages | Evaluated tokens, control → fix | Server prefill, control → fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 24 → 24 | 0.089 → 0.092 s |
| 1 | 1,151 → 37 | 0.932 → 0.132 s |
| 9 | 1,255 → 141 | 1.009 → 0.259 s |

The fix reused the full 1,130-token frontier in all three valid cases, with logged `match=tool-output-ids`. The one/nine-message responses included the newest notification marker. Edited earlier history and changed image pixels retained zero cached tokens in both builds. The unpatched control deliberately fails the new one/nine-message reuse assertions; the candidate passes the complete live section.

These are single small reproductions, not a matched total-response speed estimate: generated output lengths differ. They confirm the cache-tier defect, not the sole cause or the exact time saved in a historical long-context miss. The live comparisons cover Responses on Qwen; Anthropic remains model-free coverage. No CUDA, SSD-streaming, distributed runtime tests or broad throughput sweep were run for this server-only change.

title: Metal: split-K attention reduce and qwen4 indexer select dispatched at 1024 threads/threadgroup with no per-pipeline limit check
body:
### TL;DR

Two decode-hot dispatch families in `ds4_metal.m` request 1024 threads per threadgroup without ever consulting `pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`:

1. the dsv4 split-K flash-attention reduce (`kernel_flash_attn_ext_vec_reduce` / `..._rope`), dispatched at `32 * nwg` = 1024 with `nwg` baked into the pipeline as function constant 501, and
2. the qwen4 indexer top-k select kernels, dispatched at a literal `MTLSizeMake(1024, 1, 1)`.

`maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` is **per pipeline**, not per device — it shrinks with kernel register pressure. On a GPU where these pipelines' limit lands below 1024, the threadgroup is truncated to the allowed size. Neither kernel's work accounting adapts:

- **Reduce kernels:** the split-K reduction strides by the *baked* `NWG` constant (`for (short i = sgitg; i < DV4; i += NWG_)`, `metal/flash_attn.metal:1433`). simdgroups beyond the cap never run, so their `DV4/NWG` slices of every output row are never summed or written — the destination keeps stale data from the previous step. Wrong attention output on **every decode token**.
- **qwen4 IDX_SELECT kernels** are width-generic (`const uint nth = ntg.x`, `metal/qwen4.metal:1738`, strided histogram passes), so a smaller threadgroup leaves parts of the selection passes unscheduled — stale `sel` block indices → wrong sparse-KV blocks, again every decode token.

The host width and the kernel stride are two halves of one contract nothing checks. A dispatch over the pipeline's own limit surfaces either as a validation error or as a silent truncation depending on driver/GPU generation; where it is silent, the engine keeps serving confidently wrong tokens. This is the same bug class as oMLX #4063 (silently wrong decode attention on M1 Max).

Note this is **not** a "query the limit everywhere" gap: the older dsv4 dense paths do query the limit (~60 sites in `ds4_metal.m`, first at `:4964`, last at `:45586`). The hazard is that the two newest decode-hot families query nothing.

### Sites (line numbers at upstream main `0aaea5a`)

All pipelines below are created with plain `newComputePipelineStateWithFunction:` — no pipeline-descriptor limit declaration, and no runtime query at or near the dispatch:

| family | file:line | width | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| flash-attn reduce dispatch | `ds4_metal.m:27938`, `:28731`, `:29311`, `:29674` | `MTLSizeMake(32u * nwg, 1, 1)` | `nwg` defaults to 32 (`:29373`) → 1024; `DS4_METAL_FLASH_NWG` clamped to [1,32] at `:29364`–`:29383`; runs every decode step |
| reduce pipeline getters | `ds4_gpu_get_flash_attn_reduce_rope_pipeline` `ds4_metal.m:3783`, `ds4_gpu_get_flash_attn_reduce_pipeline` `:3831` | — | bake `nwg` as function constant 501 (`:3800`, `:3852`); neither checks the created pipeline's limit |
| qwen4 IDX_SELECT dispatches | `ds4_metal.m:49185`, `:49189`, `:49461` | `MTLSizeMake(1024, 1, 1)` | top-k select (`_pre`, plain, `_rows`) |
| qwen4 dispatch chokepoint | `qwen4_dispatch_resident` `ds4_metal.m:48352` | — | passes the caller's `tg` straight to `[enc dispatchThreadgroups:grid threadsPerThreadgroup:tg]` at `:48448`; the entire qwen4 path contains **zero** `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` queries |

Contrast: the single-pass packed reduce alternative already guards itself — `packed_pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup >= packed_threads` at `ds4_metal.m:29467`. The split-K path is the one left unchecked.

Clamping the dispatch width alone is *not* a valid fix for the reduce kernels: it would contradict the baked `NWG` stride and change the reduction, so the contract needs a guard (or an `nwg` re-creation at a width the pipeline can actually run).

### Minimal fix shape (fail-closed guard, ~15 lines)

1. In `ds4_gpu_get_flash_attn_reduce{,_rope}_pipeline`: after PSO creation, compare `pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` against `32 * nwg`; if below, print one stderr line naming the kernel/limit and return `nil` (callers already handle a nil reduce pipeline), or re-create with a smaller `nwg` / fall back to the guarded packed path (`:29467`).
2. In `qwen4_dispatch_resident`, before `dispatchThreadgroups:`: if `tg.width > pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`, one stderr line per kernel and `return 0` (callers propagate; loud beats silently truncated). Width-adaptive clamping can come later per kernel, with the width-invariance proofs each kernel needs.

```objc
/* ds4_gpu_get_flash_attn_reduce_pipeline(): after newComputePipelineStateWithFunction: */
if (pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup < (NSUInteger)(32u * nwg)) {
    fprintf(stderr, "ds4: kernel_flash_attn_ext_vec_reduce needs %u threads/threadgroup "
            "but pipeline limit is %lu — refusing (set DS4_METAL_FLASH_NWG<=N)\n",
            32u * (uint32_t)nwg, (unsigned long)pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup);
    return nil;   /* caller's existing nil-handling takes over */
}

/* qwen4_dispatch_resident(): before [enc dispatchThreadgroups:...] */
if (tg.width > pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup) {
    fprintf(stderr, "ds4: %s dispatch width %lu exceeds pipeline limit %lu\n",
            qwen4_kernel_names[kernel], (unsigned long)tg.width,
            (unsigned long)pipeline.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup);
    return 0;
}
```

Plus, to make device-generation questions answerable in one run: log `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` / `threadExecutionWidth` once per pipeline at creation behind `DS4_METAL_LOG_TG_LIMITS=1`.

### Repro sketch

Needs an M1/M2-class Apple GPU where these PSOs' per-pipeline limits land below 1024 (register-pressure dependent per pipeline; not guaranteed even there). One-shot diagnostic that settles it on any machine: add the `DS4_METAL_LOG_TG_LIMITS=1` dump, run a short decode, and inspect the limits reported for `kernel_flash_attn_ext_vec_reduce*` and `kernel_qwen4_idx_select*`. On machines where a limit < 1024 appears, the guards above should fire loudly; without them, greedy decode output diverges from the same model run with `DS4_METAL_FLASH_NWG=1` (single-warp reduce, which stays under any plausible limit) — a cheap bit-exactness A/B oracle.

### Scope / audience

Measured limits on M3/M4/M5-class GPUs sit at or above these widths, so this likely never fires on current hardware — it is an older-silicon correctness hazard. Upstream M1 Max field reports exist (e.g. #607), so the audience is real. The structural half — two decode-hot families with zero limit queries while the older paths query diligently — is what makes correctness device-generation roulette rather than an invariant.

(Reported from the nazerim/ds4 fork, where we shipped the guard shape above; happy to PR the reduce-getter + chokepoint checks if useful.)

title: metal: run the GLM-5.3-Flash prefill router on the tuned BF16 tensor-unit matmul
body:
GLM-5.3-Flash's batch router projection reads its F32 on-disk weights through
the generic fp32 matmul at ~0.76 TFLOP/s: 42 calls x 6.3 ms per 2048-token
chunk, 6.16 s = 7.2% of the 41k prefill GPU time on M5 Max.  Prepare()
converts each layer's router matrix once into a resident BF16 slab (slot =
layer index, idempotent, pages materialize on first write) so the prefill
router shares kernel_glm53_mul_mm_bf16_f32 with every other tuned GLM-5.3-Flash
projection; the generic F32 path stays as fallback.  Kill-switch:
DS4_METAL_DISABLE_GLM53_PREFILL_ROUTER_TENSOR.

Measured with this patch on top of current main, M5 Max, 41k prefill:
OFF 364.1 / ON 382.8 t/s (+5.2%); timeline anchor: the fp32 router matmul
disappears from the prefill window (42 cvt dispatches, mul_mv_f32_f32_4 ->
0 calls).

On a fork tree additionally carrying upstream PRs #1090 (exact GLM-5.3-Flash
kernels), #1120 (M5 resident MoE/KDA decode shape specializations) and #1147
(validated selection prefixes, restoring Metal GLM-5.3-Flash prefill speed)
plus fork-local M4/M5 (NAX) tensor-unit ports, the same patch measured
+7.3% (476.7-470.3 -> 500.3-512.0 t/s) with quality unchanged on the 100-case
GLM-5.3-Flash fixture: NLL 0.45841 vs reference 0.4580, first-match 90/100
vs 89, greedy prefix 7.40 vs 7.37; long 8-case rendered NLL 0.66857.
Kernel tests glm_attention / glm53_kda PASS.

title: v41: resolve the streaming MoE routing on a GPU-gated binding thread
body:
> **Update (2026-10-05):** the "bit-identical" claim below was wrong, and it is
> now fixed — see [#1178 (comment)](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1178#issuecomment-5982750031)
> for the root cause and the evidence.  Short version: the binding path declares
> the cache slabs to Metal instead of the six entries, and `use_slabs()` is a
> snapshot taken at *encode* time, while slabs are created by the service thread
> while the command buffer is *executing*.  Experts that land in a slab created
> after that snapshot were dispatched with no resource declaration at all, and
> the first token of every run was affected, which is why the divergence showed
> at step 0 and a warm run did not.  Fixed in `2c76fd3` + `4fce595` (grow the
> pool only at a token boundary, with a whole token's headroom reserved).
> OFF and ON are byte-identical again on every leg I have: cache sizes
> 60/800/3000/8793, the 12-token reproducer, a 128-step decode, `--ctx 32768`,
> a 6 KB prompt, and `ds4_test --logprob-vectors`.
>
> **The speed claim below is also retracted.** On M5 Max 128 GiB, Q2, default
> cache, 34-token prompt, 200 greedy steps, ABBA: OFF 13.67 / 12.38 t/s vs ON
> 9.16 / 10.70 t/s.  The gap narrows with a longer prompt (22.91 s vs 24.02 s
> wall for byte-identical output) but I cannot reproduce a win in either
> regime, and it is not the slab marking (a 32 GB slab target changes nothing).
> Treat this as a correctness fix with the speed question still open.

---

V4.1 Flash SSD-streaming decode ends the batch command buffer once per layer
before the routed MoE can be encoded: read the six router ids back, decide what
is resident, stage the missing preads, bind the six slots.  That is forty
readback boundaries per token on the thread that also has to encode the rest of
the layer, and on M5 Max it is this main-thread instruction count, not any GPU
wait, that sets decode wall clock.

The routed kernels already have an address-table entry point: they read the
router ids out of the router's own GPU buffer and dereference the per-layer
uint64 table of expert addresses.  That table is maintained by the streaming
cache itself (installing an expert sets its slot, evicting one zeroes it, an
in-flight slot is never evicted), so it is coherent on its own.  With
DS4_METAL_ENABLE_V41_MOE_GPU_BINDING (opt-in) the encode thread hands the layer
over instead of resolving it: the batch command buffer signals a shared event
after the router and waits on a second one before the routed dispatch, and a
service thread consumes the first edge, reads the ids, and runs the bookkeeping
the encode thread used to do -- route hotness, hotlist, peek, the pread of what
is missing, the in-flight mark, the six address slots, the two prunes -- before
releasing the second edge.  The table is complete by construction when the
dispatch runs, and the encode thread never learns the ids.  The addr-table and
the slots6 kernels call the same iq2/q2 matvec with the same nsg and the same
dispatch geometry, so a layer is bit-identical once all six experts are
resident, which the release gate guarantees.  Like the tensor-parallel gates, a
service-side failure releases the wait anyway (the GPU must not hang) and
latches; later layers then take the synchronous path and say so once on stderr.

Two properties the first version got wrong, both of them silent: the service
thread has to stamp the in-flight mark with the command-buffer sequence captured
at arm time, because by the time it serves, the encode thread has usually opened
a later buffer and just after a drain the ambient sequence names an
already-completed buffer or is zero, which leaves the six slots evictable under a
dispatch that is still reading them; and a dispatch that reaches its weights
through the address table binds no buffers, so the encode helper has to mark them
or Metal does not guarantee the kernel sees them -- the synchronous path marks
the six entries it hands over, the binding path does not know them at encode time
and marks the cache slabs instead (19 in this configuration, with every published
address inside one).

Measured with this patch on top of current main, M5 Max, V4.1 Flash Q2,
--ssd-streaming, ds4-bench --gen-tokens 512 --step-mul 1, ABBA (OFF ON ON OFF),
steady decode t/s: 2K 18.11 -> 18.48 (+2.0%), 32K 17.03 -> 17.54 (+3.0%), with
both ON legs above both OFF legs; time to first token unchanged within noise.
Output is bit-identical: CLI greedy A/B (--temp 0, 48 tokens, default env)
byte-identical; ds4_test --logprob-vectors under DS4_TEST_SSD_STREAMING=1 logs
byte-identical between ON and OFF (the same two pre-existing
short_code_completion asserts fail on both legs); tests/test_metal_ssd_experts
passes all four modes with the env on; and every 512-token ON leg reports no
binding decline and no binding failure, so the run really was served by the
binding thread.

On a fork tree additionally carrying upstream PRs #1041 (single-box decode
command queuing), #1042 (decode MoE / hyper-connection / router glue fusion),
#1043 (Q4_K group-6 expert table for the V4.1 routed shape), #1090 (V4.1
pipelined decode) and #1120 (M5 resident MoE / Q2 sum6 decode shapes) plus
fork-local streaming work, the same patch measured +3.2% (22.44 -> 23.17 t/s at
2K) and +2.7% (21.82 -> 22.40 at 32K), also bit-exact on the same gates plus
dspark --verify-parity-ssd and --short-prefill-ssd identical ON vs OFF.

No dependency beyond current main: the streaming expert cache with its slot,
in-flight and eviction rules (9ba160a "Implement SSD streaming", extended by
005afed), the address-table kernels, and the service-thread marker the second
commit uses (519c4d8) are all already upstream.  The first commit is +594/-67 in
ds4_metal.m alone -- no kernel and no arithmetic change.  The second commit adds
the missing on_service_thread() guard to the batch-reuse scan, the only one of
the four in-flight waits in the streaming cache without it: the new thread
reaches it through load_selected_missing, and the batch it would wait for may
itself be waiting for that thread.

title: Speed up Qwen3.8 Flash Next on Metal
body: WIP

title: CUDA: V4.1 expert hit profiler and resident fast path for SSD streaming
body:
## CUDA: V4.1 routed-expert hit profiler and a resident fast path for SSD streaming

Two additions to the single-GPU CUDA V4.1 path, both inert unless enabled or unless their precondition holds.

### 1. Routed-expert hit profiler for the `ds41_*` CUDA graph

`DS4_EXPERT_HITS_OUT=<csv>` (optional `DS4_EXPERT_HITS_EVERY=<rows>`, default 2048) records how often each `(layer, expert)` pair is selected, plus the summed router weight, for decode (`ds41_moe_partial`) and prefill/batched (`ds41_route_batch`). The CSV is rewritten atomically every N router rows and at exit, so a killed `ds4-server` still leaves a usable profile. The existing `--expert-profile` is Metal-only; this gives CUDA users the same data (it is what the SSD-streaming hotlists are built from).

Cost when disabled: one `getenv` at first use. When enabled it adds one device sync per layer per token, so it is a profiling tool, not a serving mode.

### 2. Resident fast path for the streaming expert cache

Today every layer of a streaming decode does a host round trip before the routed MoE: D2H copy of the selected ids, `cudaStreamSynchronize` on the decode stream, hash lookups, H2D copy of the slot remap. When the live expert set of a layer is entirely cached (which is the normal state for a model pruned through the router bias, i.e. experts whose `exp_probs_b.bias` is below -1000 can never be selected), this round trip resolves to the same slots every time and is pure overhead.

The patch keeps a per-layer `expert -> slot` table on the device, rebuilt lazily whenever slot ownership changes (`g_stream_slot_map_version` is bumped at every point that mutates `g_stream_expert_by_gate`), and resolves the selected ids with a tiny kernel on the decode stream. Nothing in the slot map changes, so no sync is needed. The slow path is untouched and remains the fallback: layers that are not fully resident, batched prefill (`n_tokens > 1`), multi-GPU, and any model whose live set is the full 384 experts and does not fit the cache never enter the fast path. `ds4.c` passes the layer's router-bias offset to the backend (`ds4_gpu_stream_expert_cache_set_layer_bias`) so the backend can compute the live set; the fast path also stages up to 64 never-yet-selected live experts so a layer can become resident (needs spare slots: size the cache above the live total).

`DS4_CUDA_DISABLE_RESIDENT_FAST_PATH=1` disables it. `DS4_CUDA_V41_QUEUE_LAYERS=1` is a separate opt-in that skips the per-layer `ds4_gpu_end_commands()` drain in the single-GPU V4.1 decode once no per-layer host dependency remains.

### Testing

Machine: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, 119 GiB), CUDA sm_121, Micron 2500 NVMe. Model: `antirez/deepseek-v4.1-flash-gguf` Q2 (340.6 GiB, sha256 `1ce6a8f8...`), `--ssd-streaming --ctx 4096`, 8546-8700 cache slots, router bias pruned to 8546 live experts with [router_bias_tool.py](https://github.com/cdome94/v41-expert-pruning).

| configuration | decode | prefill |
|---|---|---|
| streaming, unpruned model (55% of experts cached) | 7.3 t/s | 9.0 t/s |
| streaming, pruned, slow path (this PR disabled) | 10.3 t/s | 18.8 t/s |
| streaming, pruned, resident fast path | 10.0 t/s | 18.9 t/s |
| + `DS4_CUDA_V41_QUEUE_LAYERS=1` | 12.7 t/s | 19.2 t/s |

Correctness: 40 chat completions at temperature 0 (two passes of 20 prompts, 128 tokens each) are byte-identical between the slow path and the fast path. The profiler on the pruned runs recorded 0 selections of excluded experts over 2.54M expert calls, and `pruned_q2_hits` matched the expected live set exactly.

Unpruned models never enter the fast path (the live set is never fully cached), so the default streaming behaviour and the non-streaming paths are unchanged; `make test` / `./ds4_test --server` pass (see below).

```
make ds4_test CUDA_ARCH=sm_121 && ./ds4_test --server
server: OK
ds4 tests: ok
```
(run on both the development tree and this branch rebased on current `main`). The 40-prompt byte-identity check and the speed numbers above come from `ds4-server --cuda --ssd-streaming --ssd-streaming-cache-experts 8700 --ctx 4096`, 20 warm-up requests followed by 20 measured ones (128 generated tokens each, temperature 0), medians of the per-request `decoding ... avg=` log lines.

The fast path alone did not change the decode speed (10.3 -> 10.0 t/s, within noise): once the host round trip is gone, the per-layer `ds4_gpu_end_commands()` drain becomes the limiter, hence the second, opt-in switch. I kept it opt-in because I could only validate it on the single-GPU streaming configuration.

title: Native Agent: Qwen3.8 Flash Next image sessions cannot be saved
body:
On Qwen3.8 Flash Next with Metal, after a native Agent task calls `view_image`,
`/save` refuses the conversation:

```
sessions containing images cannot be saved yet
```

This prevents checkpointing a coding task after screenshot/image review. The
restriction is documented in the README; this is a request to support that
workflow, rather than a report that the current saver silently drops images.

Minimal reproduction with Qwen3.8 Flash Next on Metal:

1. Start `ds4-agent` with the matching `--vision` encoder.
2. Ask it to inspect a PNG using `view_image`.
3. Run `/save` after the task becomes idle.

I have a local implementation specifically for Qwen3.8 Flash Next on single-host
Metal that retains exact token IDs, image spans and the FP32 observations beside
the optional KV payload in the same `.kv` file. It can
restore with hot KV, or cold-prefill after `/strip`, without reopening or
re-encoding the original image. A 32K local test covers both paths, unseen image
details and subsequent native tool use.

The proposed compatibility boundary is deliberately narrow: image archives use
an Agent-only KVC v2 envelope, while text archives remain v1 and the graph
payload ABI remains unchanged. Ordinary server cache readers reject the new
archives. Initial support is single-host Metal, Qwen3.8 Flash Next, with the
same model and encoder files.

The implementation and live evidence are limited to this model/backend. The
tested weights are `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-Q8-UDQ4K.gguf` with
`mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0.gguf`. This does not claim image-session support
for Qwen Mini, GLM, DeepSeek or other backends, nor live validation of other
Qwen quantizations.

Would this Agent-only v2 format and initial scope fit the project's direction?
Implementation for review: [Draft PR #1182](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1182).
Existing text archives remain readable.

Storage is up to about 10 MiB of FP32 observations per image at the default
image-token cap (the existing environment override can increase this), plus
1 MiB of exact token IDs for a 262K conversation. The duplicate token IDs remain
authoritative when KV is stripped.

title: agent: persist Qwen3.8 Flash Next image sessions on Metal
body:
Refs #1181

Qwen3.8 Flash Next native Agent tasks on Metal cannot be checkpointed after
`view_image`: `/save` currently refuses image-bearing conversations. This adds
self-contained image-session
archives so a Qwen3.8 Flash Next conversation can resume from hot KV, or
cold-prefill after `/strip`, without the original PNG/JPEG.

**The new image-session capability is limited to Qwen3.8 Flash Next on
single-host Metal, with the same local model and vision encoder files.**
It is not a generic multi-model persistence implementation. Other model/backend
image sessions remain explicitly unsupported. Live validation used only the
specific GGUF and encoder listed below; other Qwen quantizations have not been
validated.

This PR is for review of that narrow persistence format and API boundary.
The shared validation/KV helpers and text-save durability also change common
code paths; their model-free regressions and CPU build do not establish
model-backed correctness for other models or backends.

### Implementation

Review order:

1. **KV store:** only the Agent reader accepts image KVC v2. Text archives stay
   v1, with graph payload ABI 2 unchanged. Generic server reads, scans,
   eviction, touch and trailer rewriting reject v2, including a forged v1 with
   the Agent input flag.
2. **Engine:** share the existing complete span validation and allocate-before-
   replace identity logic. Add `ds4_session_restore_vision_state()` to validate
   an idle checkpoint against exact tokens and attach copied span identities.
   It retains no embedding pointers.
3. **Agent:** append versioned `DS4V` input containing exact tokens, complete
   span metadata, original FP32 observations and CRC32. `/strip` streams this
   input unchanged while removing derived graph/KV state. Restore stages and
   validates input before replacing the live logical conversation.

FP32 observations are retained because they are the actual LM input; re-encoding
an image need not reproduce those exact floats. Token IDs are deliberately
duplicated outside KV so stripped archives do not need re-tokenization.

Explicit `/save` and `/strip`, including text sessions, share a durable commit:
`fflush`, file `F_FULLFSYNC` on macOS (`fsync` on other platforms), close,
same-directory rename, parent-directory `fsync`, and a final file barrier.
macOS failures do not downgrade to ordinary `fsync`. A failure before rename
preserves the old archive; a failure after publication retains the complete new
file and reports unconfirmed durability. Bootstrap caches keep their existing
disposable-cache policy. Tests use stage failure injection; no power-loss test
has been performed.

On macOS, new visual inputs use the persistent volume UUID plus local inode,
size and mtime, alongside existing model configuration checks. The mount's
`st_dev` number is not persisted as a stable volume identity. These are file
identities, not cryptographic hashes of weights; model replacements and future
payload ABIs do not gain unconditional portability.

Storage: 2,560 dimensions × 1,024 default image tokens × 4 bytes = 10 MiB/image,
adjustable by the existing image-token environment setting; 262,144 exact token
IDs use 1 MiB.
Span metadata is 68 bytes/image and checkpoint identity is 40 bytes/image.

`ds4_server.c` contains regression-test additions only. Local launchers, session
manager code, model files, download changes and the unrelated local TUI polling
patch are excluded.

### Validation

#### Upstream synchronization — 2026-10-20

Rebased both scoped commits onto upstream `5379c1c`, retaining image-session
persistence and the reboot-safe macOS volume identities as two focused commits.
The only textual conflict was at the end of `Makefile`; upstream verification
hooks/targets and the visual-session test target are both retained. The PR
still changes the same 13 files and excludes local TUI polling, launchers,
downloader edits, model files, session data and migration scripts.

The clean rebased PR tree passed a clean Metal Agent build, `test-frontends`,
`test-vision-state-restore` and `test-session-state`. `make cpu` also passed as
a build-only check, followed by relinking the Metal Agent. The production codec
and file-match predicate also accepted an existing 199,540-token, 11-image
DS4V v2 archive without modifying it: input CRC, span/FP32 validation and the
model/encoder file identities passed. This is an offline input check, not a
GPU restore or validation of the complete cached graph payload.

The isolated local combined tree (also containing the separate TUI polling
fix) passed the full Metal tool build, a separate CPU build, Engram regressions
and isolated Metal kernel numerical tests, including the new compressed-key
causality regression. Existing session files, Qwen model/encoder files and
launch parameters were preserved. Static comparison found the Qwen payload
save/load and vision-state helpers unchanged by this upstream update. The new
V4.1 drafter is model-gated, and the changed DeepSeek attention paths do not
enter Qwen's separate attention implementation.

No model weights were loaded for this update. The earlier live results below
remain tied to their original revisions; model-backed hot/cold restore,
continued inference with the large archive, sustained throughput, CUDA/ROCm
runtime and physical distributed inference were not rerun on this revision.

#### Reboot/remount identity fix — 2026-10-11

A real macOS reboot exposed a false rejection in this PR's original file
identity check. `/switch` rejected a previously saved 154,273-token, four-image
archive with `visual session belongs to different or replaced model/encoder
files`. Both model and encoder still had the recorded inode, byte size and
nanosecond mtime. Only `st_dev` changed, from `16777231` to `16777232`.
Treating that mount-local device number as persistent identity mistook the
reboot/remount for a replacement of the model files.

The follow-up commit stores the full volume UUID in DS4V input v2. File metadata
and the containing mount are obtained through the same read-only file descriptor
(`fstat`/`fstatfs`); UUID lookup uses that mount's root. Missing, truncated or
all-zero UUIDs fail explicitly, and v2 never falls back to comparing `st_dev`.
Inode, size, mtime and model-configuration checks remain in place.

The outer image archive remains KVC v2 with graph payload ABI 2. Only the inner
DS4V input version changes: its header grows from 96 to 112 bytes, because each
model/encoder identity grows from 32 to 40 bytes. Legacy DS4V v1 remains readable
with its original strict device check. A changed legacy mount number requires
explicit, verified migration; the loader does not invent a missing historical
UUID or silently ignore device mismatches. `/strip` preserves either input
version byte for byte.

The clean PR tree passed the Metal Agent build and model-free frontend,
vision-state, KV-trailer and session-state regressions. Added tests cover a
changed mount number with the same UUID, rejection of another volume or
changed inode/size/mtime, absent UUIDs, and legacy v1 decoding with strict device
matching, alongside the existing CRC/truncation and strip-preservation tests.

For the affected local archive, an explicit one-time migration retained a backup
and verified unchanged KV/text/title bytes, exact tokens, span metadata and FP32
observations. The updated clean-PR codec and production file-match predicate
accept the migrated archive. Local session-manager reader adaptations and the
one-time migration script are excluded from this PR.

No model was launched for this follow-up. The earlier live tests below predate
this identity fix; GPU restoration and continued inference with the large
archive, and a new model-backed run of the clean PR tree, remain untested.

#### Upstream synchronization — 2026-10-08

Rebased the single feature commit onto upstream `fc80bd6`. The only textual
conflict was in `Makefile`'s test-binary cleanup list; both sets of cleanup
entries are retained. The PR still contains only the same 13 scoped files and
excludes the local TUI polling change and all download/runtime artifacts.

The clean rebased PR tree passed the Metal Agent build and model-free frontend,
vision-identity, KV-trailer and session-state regressions. An identical isolated
combined tree also passed `make -j4 cpu` (build only).

The deployed local combination of `fc80bd6` plus this feature and the separate
local TUI polling fix passed the 32K native image-session test again: save,
exit, hide source PNGs, restart/hot restore, strip preserving complete input
bytes, restart/cold prefill, image/text switches and subsequent native tools.
The saved frontier was 3,233 tokens; hot continuation reused it and prefilled
only 117 new tokens, while cold recovery actually prefilled all 3,233 tokens
from zero. Existing user archives and editor history were restored unchanged.

A fresh local old-upstream/new-upstream comparison, both already containing
this feature, generated the same 691 numeric tokens byte for byte and measured
85.9/85.2 tokens/s in one short sample. This does not replace a full
context-frontier performance regression. Clean-PR model-backed rerun, full
262K and the other untested configurations listed below remain unqualified.

Machine: Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB unified memory, macOS, Metal.

Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-Q8-UDQ4K.gguf`, with mixed Q4_K and Q8_0
expert tensors and disk-backed BF16 n-grams.
Encoder: `mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0.gguf`.

On the clean upstream-based extraction:

```sh
make -j4 cpu
make -j4
make -j4 ds4-agent test-frontends test-vision-state-restore test-session-state
```

These cover CPU build only (no CPU inference), Agent codec/CRC/truncation/shape
checks, all six modeled commit failure stages, strip byte preservation, engine identity
replacement/clearing, actual server trailer rewriting, generic cache isolation
and model-free session-state regressions.

Earlier live validation on the local implementation:

- Qwen/Metal with `--ctx 32768 --prefill-chunk 1024 --mtp --mtp-draft 1
  --power 100 --temp 0 --nothink`.
- Save two image observations, exit, hide both source PNGs, restart and restore.
  Hot restore reuses the saved 3,245-token frontier; continuation prefills only
  the 117-token suffix and retrieves ticket details never transcribed into text.
- Strip, verify identical complete input bytes, exit and cold-restore. Actual
  cold prefill processes all 3,245 tokens from frontier zero. Spatial image
  details and subsequent `read`/`edit`/`bash` tasks succeed.
- Image → text → image session switching preserves observations and clears old
  image identities for text sessions.
- A two-image archive was 245,699,661 bytes; full-sync save took 132.7 ms. Strip
  reduced it to 15,912,813 bytes while retaining the same input CRC and bytes.

That live run included a separate two-line local TUI polling change, removed
from this upstream branch. A model-backed rerun of the clean extraction remains
pending; the serialization/restore implementation is otherwise the same.

Speed track: one previous/patched local comparison used the same 32K configured
capacity, `--temp 0 --nothink`, a 1,424-token prompt and 691 generated numeric
tokens, measuring 86.8/86.6 tokens/s.
This is a single sample, not a context-frontier benchmark or proof of no
performance regression.

A later real 154,273-token, four-image save with 262K configured capacity passed
offline CRC, FP32 finiteness, payload-size and exact KV/input-token checks. The
reboot-related identity rejection and verified migration are described above;
GPU restoration of this archive remains untested. It is not a full 262K test.

Not run: `make test` / `ds4_test --all`, a full speed-frontier CSV comparison,
full 262K use, actual SSD streaming, CUDA/ROCm, real distributed/TP inference,
or live recovery of the later large archive.

title: Add Kolibri-1 support
body:
## Summary

DwarfStar can now run Aleph Alpha's Kolibri-1 (78.10B parameters, 3.46B active, German/English mixture-of-experts) end to end: GGUF conversion, loader and tokenizer, a CPU reference forward, a Metal graph, the released chat template with think levels and sampling defaults, native tool calls in `ds4-agent` and `ds4-server`, and prebuilt Q8/Q4/Q2 downloads. The model was previously unsupported: the engine refused every backend, and these GGUFs could not be loaded at all.

Metal and the CPU reference backend run the model; CUDA, ROCm, tensor/pipeline parallelism, SSD streaming, speculation and vision stay refused for this family.

## Design notes

- **Windowed KV ring for the sliding layers.** 40 of the 50 attention layers are sliding-window; they keep `window + prefill chunk` K/V rows addressed by `pos % rows` instead of one row per absolute position. At the native 262,144-token context this cuts K/V from about 54 GiB to about 12 GiB with the default 8192-token chunk. Full layers keep absolute rows, a token never spans more than `window` rows, and each in-flight chunk stages its rows before attention, so positions inside one batch cannot collide modulo the ring.
- **Template-exact text path.** Chat rendering, think levels and tool calls are gated byte-for-byte against the released Jinja template rendered with jinja2 and encoded with the HF tokenizer: the system block keeps the effort sentence in one span so BPE merges match the reference encoder, tool schemas go through a jinja `tojson` reproduction, `--think-level 0` renders the disabled sentence, and grouped tool results share one user turn with a deferred close.
- **CPU reference as the correctness oracle.** An independent NumPy forward and a torch port gate the C path on a five-layer fixture, and the Metal graph matches the CPU reference to ~1e-7. Session continuation is checked against a fresh full prefill (max |d| <= 1e-5, same argmax) on CPU and Metal.
- **Server and agent integration.** `ds4-server` lists `kolibri-1`, parses and streams the released JSON tool-call stanzas (string-aware, calls inside reasoning suppressed), replays live tool tails so the KV frontier survives the next request byte-for-byte, shares one transient arena across sessions, and serializes Kolibri decode batches instead of failing them. `ds4-agent` uses the same template and think levels.
- **Quantization and distribution.** The converter pins the source revision and requires every released tensor to be claimed exactly once; `kolibri1_validate_gguf.py` audits finished artifacts. Prebuilt Q8/Q4/Q2 GGUFs with published SHA-256 sums ship at `aparusel/kolibri-1-gguf`, and `download_model.sh` gains `kolibri1-q8`, `kolibri1-q4` and `kolibri1-q2` with size and checksum verification.

## Verification

Per CONTRIBUTING, these ran during development on an Apple Silicon Mac (Metal) and the CPU reference path, with the mini fixture and the real Q8 artifact (77.42 GiB):

- `make test-kolibri1-gguf`: fixture build plus NumPy parity for 1/2/46-token prompts (max |d| ~3e-8) and session continuation versus a fresh prefill on CPU and Metal.
- `make test-kolibri1-torch`: torch reference parity, f64 anchor at ~6e-10, ds4 versus torch fp32 at ~1e-7 with identical argmax.
- `make test-kolibri1-chat`: server and agent renders byte-compared against the released template, including think-level gating and a tool transcript.
- `ds4_test` and the real-artifact smokes: Q8 pipeline, Responses/Anthropic surfaces, streamed tool calls, live continuations and a two-round agent loop.
- `make test` on the branch has the same 9 pre-existing failures as `main`; the Kolibri gates are green.
- On real weights, the quantized-activation arithmetic dominates the deltas between independent implementations; the Metal Q8 chain was gated on the published artifact.

title: Enable measured M4 Metal choices: Qwen decode +7% to +10%, prefill +9% to +11%, V4 Flash decode +2.7%
body: Most measured Metal choices are gated on M3 Ultra, M3 or M5, so M4 runs the generic paths for several of them. This PR adds M4 to the gates for choices that keep the same arithmetic. Each one was measured on an M4 Max, and every choice keeps its existing `DS4_*` override. Only M4 changes: each edit adds M4 to an existing device check in `ds4_metal.m`, so M4 now takes the paths M3 and M5 take, on one machine or two. Two-machine TP itself was not tested. Against main on an M4 Max, mean over the 2048–65536 context sweep: Qwen3.8 Q4 prefill +9.1% and decode +9.9%, Qwen3.8 Q2 prefill +10.8% and decode +7.3%, DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 decode +2.7%. With embedded MTP, Qwen3.8 Q4 gains +9.2% to +9.4% and Q2 +4.7% to +5.0%. ## Changes **Qwen, first commit** (`Enable the measured Qwen Metal kernel choices on M4`). M4 takes these M5 choices: - single-row plain matvec - single-row Q4_K gate/up schedule for decode and the MTP verifier - MXFP4 down specialization with sixteen groups and prefetch - MoE MM specialization - wider gate/up tile spread - 64-token tiles with their remainder tails - HC norm reuse It also takes M3 Ultra's blocked prefill convolution (`DS4_QWEN4_PREFILL_REUSE`). On the Q2 pack, the same switch also turns on 64-token Q2_K down-projection tiles at 8192 tokens and up. **DeepSeek** (`Enable the measured DeepSeek decode fusions on M4`). title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next exact MTP: draft from the sampled token, defer the residual, allow depth 3
body:
## Problem

With `--mtp --mtp-exact-sampling` at temperature > 0, the Qwen3.8 cycle (`ds4_session_qwen4_spec_cycle`) has three costs that the exact path does not need:

1. **The pending draft is conditioned on the argmax.** After each cycle the next draft is built for `parent = sample_argmax(logits)`, but the server then samples the real next token from those logits. Whenever the sample is not the argmax, the cycle start discards the draft (`first_token != glm_mtp_parent`) and the step runs without speculation. With `DS4_QWEN4_SPEC_TRACE=1` on the workload below, 663 of 2946 cycles (23%) ran plain at temperature 1.0.
2. **A rejected draft costs an extra forward.** The residual sample is replayed alone through `qwen4_graph_forward_tokens` before the next cycle.
3. **Exact sampling is pinned to depth 2.**

## Change

- The cycle draws the next token itself from the final logits, with the caller's sampler and RNG, and holds it in the session. `ds4_session_sample` returns the held token when it is asked at the same checkpoint position with the same sampler settings; otherwise it samples normally. The draft is therefore conditioned on the token that will actually be emitted.
- A rejected draft's residual sample is held the same way. It becomes the next cycle's `first_token` and is verified together with a fresh draft conditioned on it, instead of being replayed alone.
- Exact acceptance is applied position by position: accept draft *i* with p_i(draft_i), otherwise emit a residual sample of p_i with that draft removed, and stop. This is the standard sequential point-mass rule, and it lets exact sampling use the existing depth-2/3 policy (and `DS4_QWEN4_MTP_DEPTH`).

Every emitted token keeps exactly the target distribution: the held sample is the same draw the server would have made from the same logits, only one call earlier. Greedy and opportunistic decoding are unchanged. `qwen4_session_draft` lost its only caller and was removed. The hook in `ds4_session_sample` is compiled out with `DS4_NO_GPU`.

## Testing

Machine: MacBook Pro M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 26, Metal. Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF with every routed down projection in Q8_0, gate/up Q8_0 on layers 0-2 and 45, and Q4_K gate/up elsewhere; `--mtp --mtp-exact-sampling`, `-c 131072`, `--vision`, disk KV off. Base: `main` at 0aaea5a, compared against the same commit plus this PR, each binary running from its own tree.

Correctness:
- `make`, `make cpu` and `./ds4_test --server` all pass.
- Greedy (temperature 0) output is byte-identical to `main` on three prompts (prose, code, list), both with the default depth policy and with `DS4_QWEN4_MTP_DEPTH=3`.
- Distribution check at temperature 1.0 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20, thinking off. I collected 1500 samples of "Write one random 8-digit number" per binary, using the same 1500 prompts for each. Digits 2-8 are emitted inside MTP cycles (accept, residual and held-sample paths). I compared the per-position histograms with a paired permutation test, which swaps labels within each prompt and pools positions 2-8: p = 0.57 (pooled chi-square p = 0.67, no position below p = 0.18). A 300-sample run with `DS4_QWEN4_MTP_DEPTH=3` gave p = 0.32.
- A 20-question exact-answer quiz scored 19/20 on `main`, and 20/20 with this PR at both depth settings.

Cycle trace (`DS4_QWEN4_SPEC_TRACE=1`, same workload): plain cycles dropped from 663 to 329 of about 2950, i.e. one per request. The only remaining plain cycle is the first token, which the server samples from the prompt logits.

Speed: decode t/s at temperature 1.0 with card sampling, thinking off, measured client-side from the stream. The prompts were three short ones (prose, code, and a near-deterministic list: the first 40 Fibonacci numbers and the first 25 primes with their indices) plus a 25k-token code prompt for prefill. Arms ran in A B B A order, each starting after `com.apple.system.thermalpressurelevel` had read nominal for 3 minutes. Every arm's 25k prefill was within 0.6% of the others, so throttling didn't skew any run. Each prompt type has 4 samples per arm; the table shows medians.

| | prefill (25k) | prose | code | near-deterministic list |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 1168 | 59.6 | 68.8 | 70.3 |
| this PR, `DS4_QWEN4_MTP_DEPTH=3` | 1167 | 58.8 (-1.3%) | 76.6 (+11.3%) | 81.1 (+15.4%) |

With the default (adaptive) depth policy, this PR measured +1.3% to +3.4% on the same short prompts in a separate A/B, with prefill unchanged. Under exact sampling the adaptive policy rarely engages depth 3: it needs 8/8 accepted first drafts, and stochastic exact acceptance seldom produces that. Forcing depth 3 costs nothing measurable on prose here and gains 11-15% on code and the near-deterministic list. An independent M5 Max run (see comments) reproduced the code gain (+10.5%) but measured -2.3% on a free-text list, and with thinking on the gains shrank to about +6% code, +2% list, -1% prose. I left the policy unchanged; whether exact sampling should default to depth 3 is your call, and these numbers come from M5 only.

**Not tested:** CUDA and ROCm. The cycle is shared C code with no kernel changes, but I have no CUDA or ROCm machine. SSD streaming and distributed decode don't enter this cycle.

title: Disk KV: aligned-staircase churn + slot eviction evict the very checkpoint the next turn needs — long conversations collapse into cold prefill (repro + scripts inlined)
body:
## Summary

Under agent-style workloads (one long conversation + short auxiliary requests), the disk KV tier is self-defeating in two regimes, with one root cause: **when a deeper checkpoint is written, the supersede rule deliberately makes the predecessor the first eviction victim (`KV_CACHE_CONTINUED_PREFIX_MIN_FACTOR` = 0.05) — but prefix-preserving forks and slot-recovery reloads are exactly the case where the shallower predecessor is the correct restore point.**

- **Steady-state regime** (requests stay on their live slot): the disk tier is nearly write-only — 98% of 203 checkpoint files written in an 84.9 h production window were never read; 332 GiB written (~93 GiB/day SSD wear).
- **Slot-contention regime** (aux requests evict the long conversation's live slot): the disk tier *should* absorb the miss, but the successor-step eviction above has already removed the needed checkpoints — the conversation falls back to the shallowest survivor and re-prefills ~80–150K tokens **every turn** (107–195 s/turn in our repro, vs 12–22 s/turn at similar depth with an intact frontier).

The eviction side already has lineage awareness (`kv_cache_incoming_supersedes_continued()`) — but it draws the wrong conclusion from it ("deeper supersedes shallower" is only true for requests that *keep* the deeper prefix), and the score function receives the live frontier (`live_tokens` is passed at `ds4_kvstore.c:1058`) only to discard it on the second line (`(void)live;`). We suggest keeping the lineage concept but flipping which member of the lineage survives.

All numbers below are reproducible: one production log + one scripted minimal reproduction — scripts and the repro summary are inlined at the end of this issue; the repro log evidence is in the first comment.

## Environment

- ds4-server @ `0aaea5a` (upstream main), macOS, Apple M5 Max, 128 GB RAM
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4 (+ vision tower in production; text-only in repro)
- `--ctx 262144 --batched-session 4 --prefill-chunk 4096 --mtp`
- Disk KV defaults: `--kv-cache-continued-interval-tokens` 10000 (effective step 10240 after rounding to `boundary_align_tokens` 2048), `--kv-cache-min-tokens` 512, `--kv-cache-cold-max-tokens` 30000; budget 32 GiB (production) / 8 GiB (repro)
- Workload: personal agent harness — one long tool-loop conversation, short aux requests (title generation, translations, summaries) between turns, occasional prefix-preserving forks (undo/retry semantics)

## Minimal reproduction (newer, stronger evidence)

`repro_checkpoint_churn.py` (inlined below, stdlib Python): grows one conversation deterministically to ~158K tokens in ~10K-token turns with 2 unique 0.7–1K-token aux requests between turns, on a fresh server with an 8 GiB disk budget; then replays a truncated prefix + new tail (undo semantics).

Per-turn result (`prompt` / `cached` / wall seconds):

```
turn  7:  61338 / 51200 /  12.2s   <- healthy: aligned staircase reloads
turn  8:  70096 / 51200 /  22.9s   <- cached stalls: newer checkpoints already churned
turn  9:  78859 / 51200 /  36.1s
turn 10:  87622 /  8192 / 107.3s   <- collapse: only the 8192 cold checkpoint survives
turn 11:  96368 /  8192 / 118.0s
...
turn 18: 157692 /  8192 / 194.6s
fork (prefix of turn 11, 96388 tok):  cached=8192, 111.0s   <- ~88K tokens re-prefilled
```

`log_stats`: 174 evictions / 69 unique files / 64 zero-hit (93%) / 18 disk hits / staircase evicted at 40960, 51200, …, 153600 (all exactly `continued_interval_tokens`-aligned). Duration ≈ 28 min of serving.

**Write volume needs two measures**: the dedup-by-sha, evicted-only figure is 90.4 GiB, but summing the `kv cache stored` events gives **≈294 GiB written in 28 min** — the same aligned depth is re-written 11–12 times because after the live slot is displaced, the re-prefill crosses the same alignment boundary again. Three amplification factors stack up:

1. the step itself: KV footprint is 33.3 KiB/token (engine's own `memory: KV 8.33 GiB / ctx 262144` line), so each 10240 step ≈ 333 MiB;
2. same-depth rewrites: 10240×11, 20480×11 … 61440×12 store events — 35 GiB of distinct steps becomes 236 GiB of writes (`reason=continued` alone: 120 stores, 7,587,840 checkpoint tokens);
3. shallow anchors: 19 `reason=cold` aux checkpoints — 23,687 tokens of content, 2.8 GiB of writes (per-checkpoint payload floor ~134 MiB, measured on a 681-token checkpoint).

Relative to the final 157,692-token frontier: **48× checkpoint tokens written counting the continued stores alone (7.59M; 58× across all reasons) and 10.2× prefill compute (1.61M prefill tokens, 1598 s of pure prompt time)**.

### The three-step collapse chain, directly in the log

1. An aux request (681 tokens) is routed to the conversation's slot and evicts its live checkpoint — **even though it is marked protected**:

```
11:34:38 slot 3: request reuses nothing; evicting checkpoint (52588 tokens, idle 83 s, protected)
11:34:38 ds4-server: live kv cache miss live=52588 prompt=681 common=40 vision=match reason=token-mismatch
```

2. Persisting the evicted state to disk fills the budget, and the eviction scoring **deliberately** picks the predecessor staircase step first — the supersede penalty (`KV_CACHE_CONTINUED_PREFIX_MIN_FACTOR` 0.05 + 0.45×decayed-hits, applied by `kv_cache_incoming_supersedes_continued()`) marks it as "superseded" by the deeper write. That is the self-eviction cycle, and it is policy, not accident:

```
11:34:38 ds4-server: kv cache evicted reason=disk-cache-full tokens=71680 hits=0 size=2267.88 MiB
11:34:38 ds4-server: kv cache stored tokens=52588 trimmed=0 reason=evict size=1825.67 MiB
```

3. The next main-conversation request finds no live slot and no deep checkpoint; the deepest surviving prefix match is the 8192-token cold-start checkpoint (hit 11× in this run), so it re-prefills ~80–150K tokens every turn.

The same cycle is visible purely in the store path, no aux needed: `stored tokens=30720 reason=continued` at 11:35:12 is immediately preceded by `evicted tokens=20480 hits=0` at 11:35:11 — each staircase step evicts its predecessor within ~13 s of being written, i.e. within one turn.

Note the repro also shows the *read* side works well: 18 disk hits, ~50–260 ms loads, incl. the same 51200 checkpoint hit 3×. The problem is not lookup or load cost — it is retention.

## Production observation (84.9 h, same engine, 32 GiB budget)

The other regime — the harness mostly keeps conversations on their live slot, so disk is rarely read:

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| checkpoint files written & later evicted | 203 unique (264 eviction events) |
| evicted with `hits=0` | **199 / 203 (98.0%)** |
| GiB written — dedup lower bound (unique evicted) | 195.8 GiB |
| GiB written — by store events (true SSD wear) | **332.0 GiB ≈ 93 GiB/day** (continued 257.2, evict 64.7, cold 10.1) |
| disk hits logged in this window | **1** |

(The `hits` counter in the eviction header is a lifetime count — files in the disk dir persist across server restarts, so `hits=8` may include loads logged in earlier windows. The 98% zero-hit share is computed on that lifetime counter, so it is if anything an *underestimate* of waste.)

The single hit:

```
kv cache hit text tokens=92160 text=326157 quant=4 key=token-text load=498.9 ms
```

a 92,160-token checkpoint restored in 499 ms for a request carrying 326,157 bytes of visible text (at the measured 2.4–3.7 bytes/token, roughly the same depth — i.e. a slot-recovery reload, not a deep prefix match). The clean deep-prefix-match evidence is in the repro: turn 8 restored a 51200-token checkpoint into a 70,096-token prompt, 51200→3×, plus the 8192 fallback hit 11×. (Note `text=` is bytes, not tokens.)

The four files that ever got hits (`hits=8 @101307 tok`, `6 @190946`, `3 @49091`, `1 @92160`) were still all eventually evicted with `reason=disk-cache-full`.

### Staircase + frontier stores

Deep files (≥40K tokens) split into two kinds: **38 exact 10240-aligned `reason=continued` steps** — one long conversation's staircase — and **11 unaligned frontier stores** (`reason=evict` / `key=thinking-visible`, written at the exact frontier when a slot is displaced). Notably the three most-reused files (hits 8/6/3) are all *unaligned frontier stores*: the tier's actual value concentrates in frontier stores while its budget is consumed by the staircase. Same-depth rewrites happen in production too even without full collapse (40960 stored 9×, 51200 8×, …). One 190K conversation therefore wrote ~19 aligned steps + frontier dumps ≈ 60 GiB of distinct checkpoints; a budget that cannot hold two adjacent steps can never benefit from the tier.

### Shallow anchor noise

Short aux requests land in the **cold-anchor path** (`--kv-cache-cold-max-tokens`, default 30000 — prompts below this get a first-prompt checkpoint; `0` disables the path). Production: 70 `reason=cold` stores, 80,368 tokens of content → 10.1 GiB of files (payload floor ~129–147 MiB each, measured 134 MiB on a 681-token checkpoint), **146/146 files <20K tokens were zero-hit**. And anchors are *stickier* than continued steps in the scoring (`KV_CACHE_ANCHOR_REASON_SCORE_FACTOR` = 2.0, `ds4_kvstore.c:56`) — so single-shot aux checkpoints occupy budget longer than deep recovery checkpoints that actually get reused.

## Mechanism trace (function names, not line numbers)

- `kv_cache_store_current()` → aligned continued saves every `continued_interval_tokens` (effective step = interval rounded up to `boundary_align_tokens`) from `min_tokens` (512) upward; cold anchors for prompts ≤ `cold_max_tokens` (30000); `reason=evict` frontier stores when a slot's state is displaced — which aux requests trigger against the *main* conversation's slot despite `protected`.
- `ds4_kvstore_entry_eviction_score()` — receives `live` (the currently growing conversation's tokens, passed through from the store path at `ds4_kvstore.c:1058`) and discards it: the function body starts `(void)live;`. The supersede penalty applied by `kv_cache_incoming_supersedes_continued()` demotes the superseded continued step to ×0.05 score — i.e. the predecessor is intentionally the first victim whenever a deeper step is stored.
- `qwen4_session_save_payload()` — payloads include the recurrent-state snapshot, so a deep checkpoint restore is a complete, cheap reload (~0.5 s). All machinery for valuable deep restores exists; only the retention policy is missing.
- Lookup is prefix-match (repro turn 8: 51200→70096; 8192 fallback ×11), so a *sparse* set of deep checkpoints per lineage already serves prefix-preserving forks.

## What we are asking

Question first: **are the linear aligned interval and the supersede rule intended to stay as-is for 262K-context conversations?** As shipped, the disk tier is net-negative for our workload — we disabled it entirely in production.

Any of the following would flip the tradeoff positive, roughly in order of patch size:

1. **Use the `live` parameter that is already passed into `ds4_kvstore_entry_eviction_score()`** — the frontier of the conversation currently growing is right there in the call stack and discarded on the function's second line. A first use could be: never take a supersede penalty on the *deepest* checkpoint of a live lineage (the one the next turn's recovery would need).
2. **Lineage-deepest retention**: exempt the deepest N (1–2) continued checkpoints per lineage from budget eviction (anchors and other reasons unaffected). This directly breaks the self-eviction cycle: the newest step would demote its *predecessor's predecessor*, never the checkpoint the next turn might need.
3. **Geometric interval per lineage**: start at `continued_interval_tokens`, grow the step (e.g. ×1.5) per checkpoint of the same lineage, so a 200K conversation leaves ~8–10 steps instead of ~19 — cutting amplification factor 1 at the source — and fork recovery stays within ~1.5× of ideal depth. (This also reduces factor 2, since fewer boundaries get re-crossed after displacement.)
4. **Cold-anchor default review**: the path has a knob (`--kv-cache-cold-max-tokens 0` disables), so this is a defaults/docs question, not a feature: with a ~134 MiB payload floor, a default that checkpoints every prompt ≤30K tokens trades 10 GiB of near-zero-hit files per 3.5 days for what our data shows is single-shot-request reuse we never observed (146/146 zero-hit). Maybe the floor should scale the cutoff, or the docs should warn.
5. **One-line logging improvement**: the `evicted` line hard-codes `reason=disk-cache-full` and omits the *entry's* store reason (`cold`/`continued`/`evict`/`shutdown`), while the `stored` line omits `file=`. As-is, a log cannot attribute churn to shallow anchors vs deep steps without correlating sizes. Adding the entry reason to the evict line and `file=` to the store line would make future tuning discussions data-backed.

### Scope note

This targets **prefix-preserving forks** (undo / retry / resume / branch-again) and **slot-recovery reloads**: the new prompt keeps the old prefix and changes the tail — exactly what deep checkpoint prefix-match serves. It does not help history-rewriting compression (no shared prefix to match); we reduced those on the harness side separately.

## Related

#1170 (keep the checkpoint the next request loads when storing an evict snapshot — same cycle, store-side angle), #986 (age eviction value), #814 (cold checkpoints vs live dumps ordering), #711 (fixed payload cost bias — our ~130 MiB floor), #985 (preserve live KV across tool replay).

## Reproduction

`repro_checkpoint_churn.py` (inlined below): starts a dedicated server (`--kv-disk-space-mb 8192`, free port, refuses to run if the main port is busy), grows the conversation, interleaves aux requests, performs the fork, stops the server and prints JSON (turn table, `log_stats` incl. `staircase_tokens`, fork result). ≈30 min on M5 Max (our run: 28 min, 18 turns to 157,692 tokens).

Observed on `0aaea5a` (full `summary.json` inlined below): staircase 40960–153600 all evicted; 64/69 zero-hit; 90.4 GiB dedup lower bound (≈294 GiB by store events); turns 10–18 pinned to `cached=8192` at 107–195 s; fork `cached=8192` at 111 s. The server's own startup line confirms the effective parameters: `min=512, cold_max=30000, continued=10000, trim=32, align=2048`.

`analyze_checkpoint_log.py` (inlined below) regenerates every production number above from a raw `server.log`.

## Workaround status

We disabled disk KV in production (`--kv-disk-dir` off) pending a retention policy like the above; live in-memory slot reuse is unaffected. With depth-aware retention we would gladly re-enable it — the reused files (frontier stores hit 8×/6× in production; the 51200 step hit 3× and the 0.5 s restores in the repro) show exactly the value the current policy throws away.

```python
  - the fork likewise restores only the 8192 checkpoint (cached_tokens=8192)

  - the read side itself is fast (18 hits, ~50-260 ms loads) - the problem

import json
import os
import random
import re
import signal

import sys

    "tool result document segment anchor lineage budget reclaim aligned"

def continued_step(text):

        "--prefill-chunk", "4096", "--mtp",
```

```python
    for v in files.values():
        t = max(t for _, t, _, _ in v)
        depth[bucket(t)].append(max(h for _, _, h, _ in v))

    common_dist = [int(c) for _, _, c, _, _ in misses]

    ts = [TS_RE.match(l) for l in text.splitlines() if TS_RE.match(l)]
    span = ""
    if ts:
        a, b = ts[0], ts[-1]

        def secs(m):
            day = int(m.group(1)) % 100
            return (day * 86400 + int(m.group(2)) * 3600
                    + int(m.group(3)) * 60 + int(m.group(4)))
        delta = secs(b) - secs(a)
        if delta < 0:  # crossed a month boundary
            delta += 31 * 86400
        span = f"log span >= {delta / 3600:.1f} h"
        if delta >= 3600:  # a per-day rate from a minutes-long log is noise
            span += f", write rate ~{total_gib / (delta / 86400.0):.0f} GiB/day"

    print(f"== {path}")
    print(f"  eviction events: {len(evs)}  unique files: {len(files)}  "
          f"reasons: {dict(reasons)}")
    print(f"  zero-hit files: {len(zero)}/{len(files)} "
          f"({100.0 * len(zero) / max(len(files), 1):.1f}%)")
    print(f"  written (unique evicted): {total_gib:.1f} GiB, "
          f"of which zero-hit: {zero_gib:.1f} GiB")
    if span:
        print(f"  {span}")
    print(f"  disk hits: {len(hits)}")
    for t, txt, load in hits:
        # The log's text= field is the stored prefix in BYTES (ds4_kvstore
        # header text_bytes), not tokens.
        print(f"    hit: restored {t} checkpoint tokens, prompt prefix "
              f"{txt} text bytes, load={load} ms")
    nz = sorted({(h, t) for v in files.values()
                 for _, t, h, _ in v if h > 0}, reverse=True)
    if nz:
        print(f"  nonzero-hit survivors (hits, tokens): {nz[:8]}")
    if stair:
        print(f"  death staircase ({step}-aligned deep evictions, "
              f"tokens/hits/MiB):")
        print(f"    {[(t, h, f'{s:.0f}') for t, h, s in stair[:14]]}")
    for b in ("<20K", "20-80K", "80-150K", ">150K"):
        hs = depth.get(b)
        if hs:
            print(f"  depth {b}: n={len(hs)} "
                  f"zero-hit={sum(1 for h in hs if h == 0)}/{len(hs)}")
    if misses:
        med = int(statistics.median(common_dist)) if common_dist else 0
        one = sum(1 for c in common_dist if c <= 1)
        print(f"  live kv misses: {len(misses)} "
              f"(common<=1: {one}, median common: {med})")
    print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    for p in sys.argv[1:]:
        analyze(p)

```
