title: Add a Strix Halo (ROCm/gfx1151) benchmark harness and recorded baseline
body:
Adds the first recorded ROCm numbers for the Strix Halo reference platform, plus the
harness used to take them.

DwarfStar already has gfx1151-specific work (the tuned kernel path, and
`speed-bench/gfx1151-prefill-results.md`), but the recorded tables in
`docs/PERFORMANCE.md` cover Metal and CUDA only. These are the missing ROCm rows.

## What's here

- `speed-bench/bench-strix-halo.sh` — wraps the standard sweep with the environment
  capture and idle assertion this kind of measurement needs: ROCm version, gfx target,
  GTT totals, kernel/boot cmdline, commit and binary hash go into a `.meta.json` beside
  the CSV, and the script refuses to measure unless no other GPU tenant is running (a
  co-resident server changes exactly the load/memory numbers being recorded). The eval
  side defaults to the fast `hard-smoke` suite; `--eval-suite core` requests the full
  92-case run.
- `speed-bench/strix_halo.csv` + `strix_halo_ts.svg` — the sweep, in the same format and
  settings as `m5_max.csv` / `gb10.csv`.
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — the four frontier rows and an environment note.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, `gfx1151`) in a Framework Desktop
- 128 GB unified memory, Ubuntu 26.04.1, Linux `7.0.0-34`
- **ROCm 7.2.4**, `ttm.pages_limit=28835840`
- DeepSeek V4 Flash Q2 0731, **resident** (80.76 GiB), built with `make strix-halo`
- Single isolated run: no other GPU tenant (`rocm-smi --showpids` empty, GTT used ≈ 0)

## Commands run

```sh
make strix-halo
speed-bench/bench-strix-halo.sh --model <flash-q2-0731.gguf>   # the standard sweep
make test-mxfp4-rocm                                           # PASS: 0 failures
```

## Numbers

| Context | Prefill | Generation |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2048 | 197.11 t/s | 14.84 t/s |
| 16384 | 244.50 t/s | 13.74 t/s |
| 32768 | 226.52 t/s | 13.07 t/s |
| 65536 | 195.24 t/s | 12.09 t/s |

## Scope and honest notes

- Speed only. **This PR changes no inference code** — it is a harness plus a recorded
  baseline.
- Prefill is this platform's weak axis: it peaks around 265 t/s at 4k and falls to
  195 t/s at 64k. Generation sits in the DGX Spark band.
- Environment delta worth knowing when comparing against
  `speed-bench/gfx1151-prefill-results.md`: those numbers were recorded on **ROCm 7.14**
  with `ttm.pages_limit=32505856`, while this box runs **ROCm 7.2.4 / 28835840**. We
  measure 264.87 t/s at 4k against that doc's 292.86 (warm 4k). We have **not**
  attributed the difference — environment vs kernel is an open question on our side, and
  we are not claiming parity.
- `make test-mxfp4-rocm` passes on this box (0 failures at every token length,
  `RGROUP=4` bitwise OK), so the ROCm path is numerically sound here.

title: Fix RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell CUDA builds by gating native FP4 MMQfix(cuda): resolve R6K sm_120 MMQ compilation failures
body:
## Summary

Fix MMQ compilation failures on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell
Server Edition (R6K, compute capability 12.0).

## Root Cause

`cuda-generic` uses `-arch=native`, which can produce a plain
`sm_120` target. MMQ previously enabled native block-scaled FP4 MMA
based only on compute capability, causing ptxas to reject
`.kind::mxf4`, `.block_scale`, and `.scale_vec::2X`.

## Changes

- Gate device FP4 kernels and host dispatch on `DS4_CUDA_HAVE_MXF4`.
- Keep activation packing consistent with the compiled kernel path.
- Preserve MXFP4-weight/Q8-activation fallback for generic builds.
- Retain native FP4 for explicit `sm_120a`/`sm_121a` builds.
- Extend existing MXFP4 regression checks and document build options.

## Validation

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition.

- [x] Application build succeeded with `make cuda CUDA_ARCH=sm_120`,
      using the existing `compute_120a`/`sm_120a` mapping.
- [x] DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Q2 completed single-GPU SSD-streaming
      text generation at 4096-token allocated context.

Smoke-test command:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./ds4 --cuda -m "$MODEL" \
  --ssd-streaming --ctx 4096 --nothink --temp 0 \
  -n 64 -p "please explain redis usage"
```

Observed: 20 input tokens, 64-token output limit, 77.82 GiB planned
memory, 1.95 tokens/s prefill and 12.03 tokens/s generation.
These are single short-run observations, not comparative benchmarks.

## Remaining Validation

- Generic `CUDA_ARCH=native` rebuild and execution.
- MXFP4 parity tests for both generic and native FP4 paths.
- Long-context, continuation, and snapshot-restore checks on R6K.
- Cross-backend correctness and performance regression testing.

## Scope

This PR fixes CUDA build compatibility and feature dispatch.
It does not introduce CED/CSA2 or claim complete V4.1 validation.

title: metal: use shuffle network for non-causal top-k block sort
body:
The non-causal kernel_argsort_f32_i32_desc used the threadgroup-memory bitonic network; the simd_shuffle_xor variant added for DSv4.1 was only wired to the causal path. Instantiate it for the plain kernel too. Selected indices are bit-identical (154 shape/tie/-inf/odd-size cases).

The 1024-wide block sort is ~85% of top-k time, so whole ds4_gpu_indexer_topk_tensor calls (M5 Max, 256 rows, wall clock incl. ~250us fixed commit/wait), main vs this change:

  8192/512     973 -> 754 us  (-22%)
  16384/1024  2024 -> 1565 us (-23%)
  32768/2048  4275 -> 3424 us (-20%)
  32768/512   3646 -> 2793 us (-23%)

title: rocm: fix host-side rsqrtf() call that breaks the ROCm build
body:
`make strix-halo` currently fails on ROCm:

```
rocm/ds4_rocm_deepseek4_vision.cuh:239:25: error: no matching function for call to 'rsqrtf'
  239 |     const float alpha = rsqrtf((float)head_dim);
      |                         ^~~~~~
/opt/rocm-7.1.1/lib/llvm/lib/clang/20/include/__clang_hip_math.h:668:7: note: candidate
      function not viable: call to __device__ function from __host__ function
  668 | float rsqrtf(float __x) { return __ocml_rsqrt_f32(__x); }
1 error generated when compiling for gfx1151.
make[1]: *** [Makefile:793: ds4_rocm.o] Error 1
```

HIP declares `rsqrtf()` as `__device__` only. CUDA also provides a host overload, which is why this only surfaces on the ROCm path.

`alpha` is a host `float` passed by pointer to `cublasSgemmStridedBatched`, so it must be computed on the host. `1.0f / sqrtf(d)` is the same value and, being exact rather than a fast approximation, is never less precise.

The other 32 `rsqrtf()` uses under `rocm/` are inside `__device__` code and compile fine — this was the only host-side one.

### Tested on

| | |
|---|---|
| CPU / GPU | Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395 / Radeon 8060S, gfx1151 |
| Memory | 128 GB unified (96 GB BIOS carve-out) |
| ROCm | 7.1.1 (distro packages, no TheRock SDK) |
| OS / kernel | Ubuntu 24.04.4 / 6.17.0-35-generic, amdgpu 6.16.6 |

With the patch, `make strix-halo -j 8` completes with 0 errors and produces `ds4`, `ds4-server`, `ds4-bench`, `ds4-eval`, `ds4-agent`.

`ds4-server --rocm` then serves `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731.gguf` (81 GB): 80.76 GiB of tensor spans mapped in 17.7 s, `KV 0.78 GiB + buffers 0.25 GiB + resident model 80.76 GiB = 81.79 GiB planned` at ctx 32768.

`ds4-bench --rocm` across context frontiers:

| ctx | prefill tok/s | decode tok/s |
|----:|----:|----:|
| 2048 | 142.30 | 15.40 |
| 4096 | 166.64 | 14.44 |
| 16384 | 158.86 | 14.02 |
| 32768 | 150.11 | 13.52 |

Thanks for DwarfStar — it is the only engine we found that runs DeepSeek V4 Flash on this APU without a multi-machine setup.

title: responses: heal the forked live checkpoint on a token-mismatch miss
body:
A Responses request whose canonical re-render no longer matches the live checkpoint mid-history (compaction, abort, or a history edit rewrote the transcript) misses the live KV every turn instead of healing once. On a long agent session this shows up as a frozen `common` prefix for tens of minutes while `live` grows by ~50K tokens, with each turn re-prefilling from an old forked frontier.

**Root cause.** The miss path re-seeds the fork on every turn:
1. before a disk load it persists the forked live checkpoint (`kv_cache_store_current(..., "evict")`),
2. the next request loads that forked payload back (text-prefix key still matches),
3. the token compare keeps failing at the same frozen `common`, and the fallback re-prefills from the forked frontier every turn.

**Why not `ds4_session_rewrite_from_common`.** It reports `REBUILD_NEEDED` whenever `common < live` (it cannot mutate a mid-history fork), and the qwen4 GPU path resets its graph on any non-prefix prompt — a forked turn is a full prefill regardless. The cost is the re-seeding, so this patch stops the re-seeding.

**The change** (one guarded block in `generate_job_inner`, Responses protocol, text-only, `old_pos > 0`, `0 < common < old_pos`, `common < prompt`):
- skip the evict-store of the forked checkpoint,
- after a disk load, verify the loaded tokens are still a lockstep prefix of the client's canonical prompt; on a fork, discard the payload and invalidate,
- heal by full-syncing the client's canonical prompt so the checkpoint becomes the client's re-render; the next turn continues in lockstep.

Both the heal decision and a rejected forked disk load are logged at the KVCACHE level.

**Verification** — Apple M5 Max (128 GiB), Metal, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4 gguf, ctx 393216:
- fork repro (HTTP client re-rendering the history with a mid-history rewrite): the fork turn misses once and full-heals; every continuation after it continues from live with no frozen `common` and no forked evict-store. Same at ~5K-token prompts with thinking on, where the disk cache era engages.
- forked disk-load guard: a thinking era, a restart (shutdown store of the visible-keyed payload), then a mid-history rewrite on the next turn → the forked payload is loaded, rejected, discarded, and the turn heals; the follow-up turn continues in lockstep.
- clean in-lockstep runs are unaffected: tool turns take the call_id fast path and the first text turn continues from live with a small suffix.

Commands: `make clean && make && ./ds4_test --server` (passes) and `make cpu` (builds). No speed run needed: the change only alters the fallback path a forked session already took (it still prefills; it stops re-prefilling the fork every turn).

title: ds4-eval: strict grader marks correct answer INCOMPLETE when output ends with "</think>E" (no "Answer:" line)
body:
## Summary

`find_case_answer_strict()` requires the final line of the output to contain an
`Answer:` marker. When the model closes thinking and emits the bare answer glued
to the tag (e.g. `...</think>E`), the grader returns INCOMPLETE even though the
letter is correct.

## Repro (deterministic)

```
./ds4-eval --plain --case-id 4a1d1780a93f4093b6fb7d3c314cbea8
```

Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash Q2 (ds4flash.gguf), Metal, M5 Max 128GB, temp 0
(eval default). The model deterministically ends its output with:

```
...So answer E.</think>E
```

Result: `INCOMPLETE got ? expected E`. `--retry-incomplete` does not help — the
retry produces the same 183-token output.

## Root cause

`find_case_answer_strict()` (ds4_eval.c, ~line 3323):

1. trims trailing whitespace, takes the last line;
2. requires `answer_payload(line)` (an "Answer:" marker) — otherwise returns
   false → `EVAL_INCOMPLETE`.

The lenient extractor (`find_answer_letter()` reverse scan) would catch the
bare `E`, but it is only used by `--regrade-trace`, not live runs.

## Suggested fix

In the strict path, when the last line has no `Answer:` marker but contains
`</think>` followed by non-empty text, grade the text after the tag. A minimal
local patch of ~10 lines does this and flips the case to PASSED.

## Why it matters

INCOMPLETE is meant to separate "did not follow the format" from "answered
wrong". A correct bare answer glued to `</think>` is a common, benign deviation;
counting it as INCOMPLETE understates the model and wastes a retry budget.

title: greedy long-thinking runs can fall into verbatim repetition loops and burn the whole budget (7/92 core-suite INCOMPLETE)
body:
## Summary

During a full `core` suite run (92 cases, M5 Max 128GB, Metal, DeepSeek V4
Flash Q2, eval defaults: temp 0, 32000-token generation budget with
`--retry-incomplete`), 8 cases ended INCOMPLETE. 7 of them hit the budget cap.
At least one case shows a **verbatim repetition loop**: the same paragraph is
emitted over and over until the budget is gone.

Final tally: 77 passed / 7 failed / 8 incomplete, runtime 7h29m.

## Evidence

Case 28 (`GPQA Diamond/recb80OwMgNnceA9t`, chemistry): the trace shows the
paragraph beginning "Let's find numbering for cyclopenta[c]pyridine by analogy
with..." repeated character-for-character across thousands of tokens, right up
to `MODEL_OUTPUT_END` at the 32000-token cap.

Other budget-capped INCOMPLETE cases (same run):

- AIME2025/aime2025-05 (31491 tokens)
- GPQA recZWeueB7lSPR6wN, recVvpD8miVjmmyfe, recWxGU8Q4YReJ1tb (32000 each)
- AIME2025/aime2025-28, aime2025-15 (32000 each)

## Environment

- ds4 @ commit current as of 2026-10-07
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731.gguf
- Apple M5 Max, 128GB, macOS 27, Metal 4 tensor API enabled
- eval defaults: temp 0, soft-limit-reply-budget 1024, hard-limit 512

## Discussion

At temp 0 the soft/hard think-close logic apparently does not trigger because
the loop never puts `</think>` in the top ranks. Possible harness-level
mitigations:

1. Detect exact repetition of a trailing block (e.g. last N tokens identical to
   the previous N) and force the think-close sequence.
2. Offer a repetition penalty for eval runs.

Or is this considered pure model pathology at greedy decoding, out of scope for
the harness? A short statement either way would help downstream users interpret
INCOMPLETE counts in regression runs.

title: Accept WebP images on macOS via ImageIO
body:
Pasted screenshots and clipboard images often arrive as WebP, which the
server rejected with a generic `invalid JSON request` 400.

macOS already ships a WebP decoder in ImageIO, so `ds4_image_decode_memory`
now recognizes the `RIFF/WEBP` magic and draws the image into a premultiplied
RGBA8 context over white, reusing the shared `ds4_oriented_rgb` path. No new
dependency, no C++. Non-Apple builds keep JPEG/PNG and return an explicit
decoder error instead of a misleading one.

`image/webp` is also added to the server media-type whitelist and the
`data:image/webp;base64,` data-URI prefix, covering the OpenAI, Anthropic and
Responses input shapes.

Adds `test_openai_inline_webp_image_content` (inline 40-byte lossless WebP
fixture, parse + decode assertions) to the `--server` group.

## Regression notes

- Machine/backend: Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, macOS, Metal.
- Model: local Q4 MoE checkpoint + Q8_0 vision mmproj.
- Commands: `make ds4-server ds4_test` (no warnings); `./ds4_test --server` → `server: OK`.
- Live: `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` with `data:image/webp`
  (real 794x998 and 804x1010 screenshots) → HTTP 200, model described the
  images; JPEG and PNG paths unchanged.
- Notable failures: none.

title: Metal: reuse Q4_K raw loads in Qwen NAX prefill
body:
## What

Qwen NAX prefill currently reloads the same Q4_K header for each of eight
32-weight groups, and the same quant words for each low/high-nibble pair.
This change retains those registers in the gate/up and down lookahead loops:
the header reloads at a 256-weight superblock boundary and quant words reload
at each even group. Each new tile starts with the original complete load.

The dequantizer, arithmetic order, accumulators, barriers, expert ordering and
dispatch geometry are unchanged. Non-Q4 types call the original loader. There
is no additional buffer, production flag, model conversion or checkpoint
format change. The shared NAX templates cover half, float-activation and
compensated variants. Ordinary one-token GEMV kernels are unchanged.

Inspired by the Q4 register-reuse portion of StarForge commit
`08ea4d7eb2e780e2d31690766600880e8dea8718`; its other optimizations are excluded.

## Related work and review order

This PR is tracked in [prefill issue #1202](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1202), alongside [PLE prefetch #1154](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1154). The changes address separate costs: packed Q4_K reloads here, host PLE I/O latency there. This loader change is independently buildable; merging #1154 first simply matches the baseline used for the reported incremental gain. Keep each optimization with its own exactness and performance gates.

[Cache tracker #1201](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1201) separately covers history correctness and checkpoint reuse. Its workflow savings should not be added to this kernel-throughput percentage. This PR's implementation, per-run timing data and correctness tests remain self-contained below.

## Performance (Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, Metal, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4)

macOS 26.6.2, AC/high-power mode, resident Q4 GGUF with Q4_K routed gate/up and
MXFP4 routed down. Fresh 16384-token prefill, 8192-token chunks, context
allocation 262144, 64 ordinary greedy decode tokens, batching off. Text prompt:
`speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt`; second corpus: a frozen copy of `ds4.c`.

The measured patched-source host baseline was
`b51ae1ce23a59e5e5f7031c0144e76ac35f13e6c`. **#1154 was already applied in both
arms; these gains are incremental to PLE prefetch.** Only the shader selected
before GPU initialization differed between arms.

| Measurement | Sequential runs / balanced blocks | Prefill throughput change | Ordinary decode change | Full frontier logits |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Warmed text, fresh 16K | 16 / 4 | **+2.376%** | -0.061% | exact, 16/16 |
| Warmed C source, fresh 16K | 8 / 2 | **+2.274%** | -0.622% | exact, 8/8 |

Each process first warmed weights and a disposable complete prefill plus
64-token decode session, freed it, then measured fresh KV on the same engine.
There was only one live session/model process at a time. Weight warming alone
does not remove first-use specialized Metal pipeline compilation; the separate
session warmup does. Acceptance timing added no stage synchronization or state
dumps. Cold-process measurements are excluded from the estimates above.

ABBA/BAAB blocks compare mean B time / mean A time; the summary is the geometric
mean of block ratios, converted to throughput with `100 * (1 / ratio - 1)`.
Text block gains: +2.789%, +2.123%, +2.273%, +2.321%; code: +2.147%, +2.401%.
Conditional 95% block-bootstrap intervals: text **+2.172 to +2.660%**, code
**+2.147 to +2.401%**. These few-block intervals do not capture all host noise:
a warmed A/A block showed a false -1.83% difference, and text times drifted
approximately 6–7% first-to-last in each arm. No speedup at every context length
or MTP throughput improvement is claimed.

The executed per-arm benchmark command used a diagnostic copy of `ds4-bench`
that inserted the disposable session warmup described above. Paths normalized
below; `ds4-bench-warmed` and its generator are local experiment tooling, not
checked-in PR targets. `DS4_BENCH_DIAGNOSTIC_WARMUP` belongs to that tooling:

```sh
DS4_BENCH_DIAGNOSTIC_WARMUP=1 \
DS4_METAL_QWEN4_SOURCE=/tmp/qwen4-control.metal \
./ds4-bench-warmed --metal -m gguf/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt \
  --ctx-start 16384 --ctx-max 16384 --step-mul 1 --step-incr 8192 \
  --ctx-alloc 262144 --prefill-chunk 8192 --gen-tokens 64 \
  --warm-weights --show-output --csv /tmp/control.csv \
  --dump-frontier-logits-dir /tmp/control-logits
# Repeat with the candidate shader and distinct output paths in ABBA/BAAB order.
```

For a stock-checkout before/after CSV check, use `./ds4-bench` with the same
model, prompt, context/chunk/generation settings and `--warm-weights`. Its first
prefill includes lazy pipeline creation, so it does not reproduce the fully
warmed estimate without the disposable-session insertion.

## Correctness and failure paths

The PR includes the new fixture in **`tests/test_qwen4_kernels.c`**, selected by
`DS4_TEST_QWEN4_RAW16_ONLY=1`. It runs the actual baseline and candidate shaders
in separate processes at the same NAX level, rather than comparing different
reduction variants or reimplementing the new load rule as its oracle.

- Covers both changed gate/up and down lookahead sites, NAX levels 0–6,
  Q4/Q4 at K512/2560, Q4/MXFP4, all-MXFP4 and IQ2XXS/Q2_K fallback paths.
- Distinct finite signed/zero Q4 scale/min headers expose accidental reuse
  across superblocks; random packed fields exercise low/high nibble selection.
- Shuffled routes and expert counts 0,1,7,8,9,15,16,17,31,32,33,63,64,65.
  Every stage requires finite, written, nonzero live output and unchanged
  reserved output slots/trailing write sentinels.
- `DS4_TEST_QWEN4_RAW16_DUMP` writes metadata and all output bits. **87,492,020
  bytes matched directly**; a fixture pass or equal printed hashes alone is
  not the exactness gate. Both dumps have SHA256
  `6cd1882c9ede246f78cad98f0e6d13b63a045a5d0ba332e186e25e57e5dba554`.
- All 24 warmed model runs matched their corpus's full 248320-float frontier.
  Complete persisted payloads at 16384/16896, save/load/resave, 128 ordinary
  decode vocabulary rows, token IDs and positions matched exactly. This covers
  serialized KV/GDN/convolution/PLE state, not all ephemeral MTP scratch.
- Retained prefixes at 131072, 245760 and 246272 matched full frontier logits,
  including the final 512-token append. These are correctness guards, not
  repeated long-context speed estimates.
- Existing real-model PLE rollback/prefetch/cancel/resume/read-failure/thread-
  failure tests passed. Checkpoint/restore/snapshot/rewind passed with MTP on
  and exact sampling off; the snapshot test exercised 16 speculative cycles.
- Ordinary/MTP vision completion smokes and collateral synthetic Metal
  resident/SSD Q4 comparisons passed. A local sampled tool/history/restart
  fixture passed 11 requests at temperature 0.6, with 102 verifier cycles and
  94 drafts accepted. That additional API fixture is outside this PR and is
  not a multi-hour agent soak or image-quality assessment.

A pre-existing masked-row issue remains: the old 64/32 NAX templates can form
inactive weight-row addresses past a 65-row logical tensor. This happens in
both arms; register reuse preserves/subsets those addresses. Output sentinels
check writes, not logical weight-read bounds. Deployed row dimensions are
multiples of 64; a bounds repair needs separate validation. The finite fixture
is not exhaustive over all possible bit patterns.

## Validation

On the isolated PR branch (upstream `fc80bd695da76ee14bcb86820bf900a5cdfda806`
plus this commit):

```sh
make -j4 all tests/test_qwen4_kernels
make -j4 cpu
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

Builds passed; CPU inference was not run. The candidate shader/test are
byte-identical to the fully validated local integration, and the unmodified
upstream shader/test/Metal host match the campaign baseline. The complete
upstream host was not rerun through the model campaign. On that local
integration, the following checks passed:

```sh
make -j4
make test
./tests/test_qwen4_kernels
./tests/test_metal_ssd_experts --q4
./tests/test_qwen4_ple_prefetch gguf/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf
DS4_TEST_MODEL=gguf/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf \
DS4_TEST_GLM_MTP=1 DS4_TEST_MTP_EXACT=0 DS4_TEST_SNAPSHOT_CTX=8192 \
DS4_TEST_SNAPSHOT_PROMPT=/tmp/qwen-code-prompt.txt \
./ds4_test --qwen4-prefill-checkpoints --qwen4-restore-reuse \
  --session-snapshot --session-rewind
```

The snapshot prompt path above represents the saved 2444-token code fixture.
Run GPU/model checks sequentially with the managed server free. CUDA sources
are untouched; external CUDA/distributed execution was not performed.

To reproduce the checked-in focused exact test from the PR checkout on M5:

```sh
make tests/test_qwen4_kernels
git show fc80bd695da76ee14bcb86820bf900a5cdfda806:metal/qwen4.metal > /tmp/qwen4-control.metal
DS4_METAL_QWEN4_SOURCE=/tmp/qwen4-control.metal \
DS4_TEST_QWEN4_RAW16_ONLY=1 DS4_TEST_QWEN4_RAW16_DUMP=/tmp/qwen4-control.raw \
./tests/test_qwen4_kernels
DS4_METAL_QWEN4_SOURCE="$PWD/metal/qwen4.metal" \
DS4_TEST_QWEN4_RAW16_ONLY=1 DS4_TEST_QWEN4_RAW16_DUMP=/tmp/qwen4-candidate.raw \
./tests/test_qwen4_kernels
cmp /tmp/qwen4-control.raw /tmp/qwen4-candidate.raw
```

title: Feature/performance ds4.1 qwen3.8 halogen
Metal: retain bounded Qwen Responses prompt checkpoints
body:
## What and why

Save the complete incoming prompt before generation for eligible text-only Qwen Responses requests on Metal. This gives a long conversation a reusable checkpoint when the single server session switches to another task, so returning to that conversation can resume near the end of its history instead of evaluating tens of thousands of tokens again.

In the reproduced agent workflow, returning to a roughly 73K-token conversation restored only 16K tokens and replayed about 57K. With this change, the return restored roughly 73K tokens and evaluated only 48–51. Mean return time fell from **38.404 s to 0.976 s**, and the complete four-request workflow fell from **99.664 s to 62.872 s (−36.92%)** in one balanced measurement block. The improvement comes from avoiding repeated prefill work on affected returns. Eligible requests incur an additional full-state checkpoint write.

Two existing behaviors explain the missed reuse:

- Periodic continued checkpoints require an aligned token count. The long append started at 17,162 tokens (778 modulo 2,048), so 8,192-token prefill chunks never reached a multiple of the effective 10,240-token checkpoint interval. No continued checkpoint was saved.
- An outgoing checkpoint's Responses-visible key can cease to match the client-replayed history when sampled reasoning is represented differently. Saving the incoming prompt captures the history that the client already supplied, before new output is generated.

## Implementation and bounds

The save uses the existing exact-token payload and Responses-visible key/trailer mechanism at the already reached prompt frontier. A request is eligible only after at least one prefill chunk of new work beyond the greater of its incoming reusable frontier and any cold checkpoint successfully stored by that request. Prefill chunking, recurrent state, model arithmetic, MTP sampling/depth and the periodic checkpoint selector are unchanged.

Supplementary checkpoints are expendable:

- After successful publication, at most **two** supplementary files occupy at most **min(cache budget / 8, 16 GiB)**.
- Supplement admission never evicts ordinary checkpoints. Supplements are evicted first under ordinary cache pressure.
- Estimated-size and checked-inventory rejection happens before GPU readback/state staging. Actual-size and trailer checks still run after staging.
- Inventory failures skip saving; incompatible existing files are preserved. A supplementary attempt does not rewrite a compatible ordinary duplicate. An ordinary store can promote a compatible supplement by updating its reason byte.

Publication reuses the existing atomic per-file mechanism. Multi-file pruning is not transactional: an old supplement deleted before a later I/O failure cannot be restored. The bounds cover successfully published files; they do not repair externally modified caches at startup or include transient staging files.

The checkpoint file already contains a one-byte `reason` field recording why it was saved (for example, `cold` or `continued`). This change adds `near-tail` (`DS4_KVSTORE_REASON_NEAR_TAIL`, numeric value **7**) for the supplementary completed-prompt checkpoints. The cache uses this tag to identify them for the separate count/byte limits and to evict them before ordinary checkpoints. The file layout, key and state payload format are unchanged. Older readers can still load the state, but treat the new tag as unknown and do not apply its eviction priority.

## Related work and review order

This PR is tracked in [cache issue #1201](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1201), alongside [exact tool replay/EOS #1169](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1169) and [parent-history validation #1175](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1175). Those repairs preserve replay identity and reject stale parent reuse; this policy independently creates a useful completed-prompt checkpoint. Prioritize the two correctness repairs before this additional reuse policy. This is a review recommendation, not a strict build dependency: the standalone upstream pure-text checkpoint gates below passed without either PR, while the local tool-workflow gates use the existing history repairs.

The save policy, supplementary admission bounds and eviction priority remain together in this PR. [Prefill tracker #1202](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1202) covers #1154/#1198 separately; both are already baseline in the workflow timings below. Replay avoidance and additional write costs are assessed here, independently of their throughput gains.

## Performance

Hardware and configuration: Apple **M5 Max, 128 GiB**, Metal, resident Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4 (**Q4_K gate/up, MXFP4 down**), native context **262,144 tokens**, prefill chunk **8,192 tokens**, KV budget **256,000 MiB**, requested continued interval **10,000 tokens** (effective **10,240** after alignment), temperature **0.6**, and opportunistic/non-exact MTP. Existing PLE prefetch (#1154) and Q4 register reuse (#1198) are included in the baseline.

Four independently initialized workflows ran in original/release/release/original order (ABBA). Each workflow consisted of an initial A request, a long A append, a switch to B, and a return to A. Initial/user inputs were the same; each arm retained its own sampled output history. Client wall times include state staging, checkpoint save/load and generation, and exclude engine startup. No capacity eviction occurred.

| Measurement | Original mean | Release mean |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Complete four-request workflow | 99.664 s | 62.872 s (−36.92%) |
| A-return client wall | 38.404 s | 0.976 s |
| A-return cached / evaluated tokens | 16,384 / 57,120–57,124 | 73,454–73,456 / 48–51 |
| Long append client wall, including saving | 37.120 s | 37.719 s |
| Logical write estimate from rounded save logs | 5.579 GiB | 6.575 GiB |

Mean newly published file bytes increased by **1,068,813,966.5 bytes (+17.84%)** per workflow. These file-byte measurements and rounded logical write estimates do not measure physical SSD writes. The existing logged save clock excludes GPU state staging/readback; complete client wall time includes it.

Initial request means were **12.063 s → 12.198 s (+1.12%)**. Those requests did not meet the new-save threshold, so this small block does not establish a causal first-use regression. One balanced block provides descriptive evidence, with no confidence interval or claim of identical generated histories. This change does not increase raw prefill-kernel throughput.

## Correctness and recovery

- **Checked-in portable store fixture:** exercises the actual store with tiny mock payloads, including exact mock-state restore, ordinary checkpoint preservation/promotion, namespace/context/model compatibility, count/byte bounds, zero staging for known oversized saves, and injected staging/write/rename/inventory/prune failures. It adds no production test hooks.
- **Checked-in model regression:** compares complete serialized payloads and all finite vocabulary logits before/after saving, immediately after restore before any append, and after matched appends and the next ordinary decode against an uninterrupted reference with the same boundaries. It uses one active session, 32 speculative-API history tokens sampled at temperature 0.6, and a synthetic visible key/trailer. It makes no claim about a particular draft acceptance count. Real API renderer eligibility is covered separately by the managed API gates.
- **Local managed API recovery gates:** passed fresh-process restart, branches before/after the supplement, prefill cancellation, decode cancellation, and fallback with copied truncated/temporary files. Prefill cancellation intentionally invalidates the selected cache; retry recovers from an older intact anchor. Decode-cancellation retry discards partial output. All tool IDs were restored. These local gates depend on existing local Qwen tool-history, EOS and parent fixes, which this PR does not include; they do not establish equivalent coverage for upstream's existing Qwen tool-map scanner.
- **Notable fixture failure:** a completed-only assertion initially rejected a bounded 512-token retry that correctly ended as incomplete/max_tokens. Independent offline validation of the preserved request, events and trace confirmed recovery. The failed summary was retained, and missing retry timing was not reconstructed.

## Validation

All commands below passed on the isolated upstream checkout at `fc80bd695da76ee14bcb86820bf900a5cdfda806` plus this patch:

```sh
make -j8
make -j4 test-kvstore-near-tail ds4_test
./ds4_test --server
make -j4 tests/test_qwen4_prompt_checkpoint
./tests/test_qwen4_prompt_checkpoint \
  /path/to/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4.gguf \
  tests/long_context_story_prompt.txt \
  131072 8192 /tmp/qwen-checkpoint-128k-new
make -j8 cpu
git diff --check
```

The default Metal build, portable store fixture, frontend checks and strengthened model gate with a **131,072-token prefix / 8,192-token append** passed. CPU compilation passed; CPU model inference was not run. The same public model test linked against the frozen local engine/store passed with a **16,384-token prefix / 8-token append**. The saved frontier includes the additional 32 speculative-API history tokens in both public gates.

The earlier local prototype also passed the **16K/128K prefixes × 1/8/8,192-token appends** matrix for save neutrality, restored logits, and matched append/next-decode full-state checks. The public regression strengthens this coverage with immediate restored-payload comparison before append.

A standalone upstream managed text smoke test passed the **15K → 71K → B → A** workflow. Its first return selected an ordinary outgoing checkpoint, so a separate fresh process containing only the cloned new supplementary file verified that the supplement itself restored **71,340 tokens in 0.892 s**. Local long-tool workflow/recovery gates and balanced timings ran separately atop the existing local history fixes. All model/server runs were sequential, with isolated test caches and managed launch/stop scripts.

Inference kernels and engine arithmetic are unchanged. The new server hook is Metal-only; Qwen SSD/distributed/TP paths already reject this model configuration. Shared store behavior has portable regression coverage, but external CUDA/distributed hardware and a multi-hour agent soak were not tested. Promotion flush/close and rollback-unlink failure paths were source-reviewed, not directly fault-injected. The PR contains the checkpoint policy and focused regression tests.

title: Track Qwen3.8 agent-context correctness and checkpoint reuse
body:
## Goal

Track four focused PRs for long Qwen3.8 agent histories: ensure submitted history reaches the model, preserve replay identity across live/disk reuse, support final-answer replay with or without emitted reasoning, and retain a useful completed-prompt checkpoint. Each addresses a different failure mode and should retain its own review and merge decision.

## Changes to review

- [ ] #1175 — validate the parent history before taking the live tool-ID shortcut. Compaction or edits must reach the model even when the latest call/result IDs are unchanged. Also recognize matching tool results followed by user messages, keeping those messages in the new suffix and preserving all parent/image/frontier guards. Unchanged and genuine results-only continuations retain their applicable reuse paths.
- [ ] #1169 — preserve complete sampled tool-call spans and IDs across checkpoint restore, and make committed EOS, continuation tails and visible keys agree. This prevents canonical re-rendering and turn-boundary mismatches from discarding usable KV.
- [ ] #1206 — preserve the live Qwen Responses frontier when a client replays an emitted final-answer reasoning summary, while retaining compatibility with clients that omit it. Both visible keys bind the same frontier and keep image identity, image-offset and suffix-boundary checks. Includes model-free regressions and a portable streaming HTTP reproduction with six retained images. Merge after #1169's EOS commitment/publication guarantee.
- [ ] #1200 — save eligible completed text-only Qwen Responses prompts on Metal before generation. This supplies a reusable frontier when periodic alignment or a later sampled visible key would miss the returning conversation. Supplements are limited to two published files and min(cache budget / 8, 16 GiB), cannot evict ordinary checkpoints during admission, and are evicted first under ordinary cache pressure.

These responsibilities complement one another: #1175 checks whether reuse is valid; #1169 preserves replay identity and the closed-turn boundary; #1206 preserves final-answer reasoning replay compatibility at the live frontier; #1200 creates a useful checkpoint to reuse. #1169's EOS commitment/key/compatibility handling should remain coordinated. #1200's save policy should ship with its admission and eviction bounds.

## Evidence and tradeoffs

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, resident Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4 (Q4_K gate/up, MXFP4 down):

- #1175: the live Responses compaction comparison reduced the effective prompt from 4,748 to 401 tokens. The unpatched control retained the old frontier and grew to 4,852 tokens. Model-free regressions also cover edited parents, result-only/absent-proof cases and image placement. Follow-up commit `4e8706d` repairs the separate tool-output-plus-user-message eligibility case. With one retained image and omitted tool-turn reasoning, one/nine following user messages changed evaluated tokens from 1,151/1,255 to 37/141 and server prefill from 0.932/1.009 to 0.132/0.259 s. The fixed requests reused the 1,130-token frontier through the logged tool-ID tier and received the newest notification marker; edited parents and changed images still reused zero tokens. This generic Responses preparation change has standalone Metal/model-free/CPU-build checks; its live control/candidate comparison used the local #1169/#1206 integration with isolated caches and opportunistic MTP. These single small timings are not a matched total-response speed estimate or an exact replay of the historical long-context miss.
- #1169: a twelve-tool-call restart restored all IDs, reused 47,604 tokens and evaluated a 27-token suffix. A copied TOOL_MAP-off control reused only 392 tokens and evaluated 46,336. EOS/legacy-key and renderer/store regressions are included. The published live regression used exact MTP sampling; later local managed workflow gates also exercised non-exact MTP.
- #1206: in the six-image streaming reproduction, the upstream-plus-#1169 control reused no tokens and evaluated 5,159 after a final answer. The repair reused 5,107 and evaluated only 44; server prefill fell from 3.655 to 0.148 s, and the first streamed delta from 3.717 to 0.200 s. Preserved reasoning, omitted reasoning and summaries not requested all passed on the candidate with logged visible-prefix reuse. These are individual reproduction timings with opportunistic MTP, not a matched total-response speed estimate. The repair and live validation are Qwen-specific; no new checkpoint files or save policy are introduced.
- #1200: one balanced four-request task-switching workflow measured 99.664 → 62.872 s (36.92% less total wall time), including saves; return time was 38.404 → 0.976 s. This avoided roughly 57K tokens of replay and added about 1 GiB of logical checkpoint data (+17.84%) per workflow. The timing baseline already included #1154, #1198 and the existing history fixes.

These are distinct reproductions, not additive speed percentages or a measured complete-stack-versus-stock-upstream gain. #1200's result is workflow-specific and has no confidence interval from its single balanced block. Extra full-state writes are a material cost. Raw prefill kernels and production opportunistic/non-exact MTP policy are unchanged by the checkpoint policy.

## Review and integration

Prioritize #1175 and #1169 for history correctness, then #1206's final-answer compatibility repair, before #1200's additional checkpoint policy. #1206 must merge after #1169: it relies on EOS commitment and the guard that publishes only valid closed-turn frontiers. The broader review order is a recommendation, not a strict build dependency among the other PRs. #1200 also has standalone upstream pure-text save/restore coverage without the other PRs; its local tool-workflow evidence uses the existing history repairs.

Related [resident Metal prefill tracker #1202](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1202) covers #1154 and #1198. Those optimize throughput and can be reviewed independently. Their gains must remain separate from checkpoint replay avoidance.

At upstream `fc80bd695da76ee14bcb86820bf900a5cdfda806`, the earlier temporary integration of the original five PRs (#1154, #1169, #1175, #1198 and #1200) merged without text conflicts with #1169/#1175 in either order. The combined source passed:

```sh
make -j8 ds4_test test-kvstore-near-tail
./ds4_test --server
```

A separate integration on 2026-10-10 combined #1169, #1175 and #1206 on the same upstream base and passed `make -j8 ds4-server ds4_test` and `./ds4_test --server`. The #1175 overlap required retaining both cleanup additions and passing `NULL` for the new optional-key argument in its test helper. The live control/candidate comparison for #1206 used upstream plus #1169, sequential managed servers and isolated test caches. The new three-PR checks do not establish a six-PR integration result.

These are build and model-free server/store integration checks, not a new combined model-speed or multi-hour agent-soak campaign. Individual PR descriptions contain their complete implementation and validation evidence. Joint model/API runs must be sequential, use isolated test caches, and cover live continuation, restart, compaction/edits, branch fallback and cancellation under the chosen sampling policy.

Close this tracker when all four PRs are merged or explicitly resolved.

title: Track Qwen3.8 resident Metal prefill improvements
body:
## Goal

Track two independent resident Metal prefill optimizations for Qwen3.8 Flash Next. Keep their PRs separate: one hides PLE I/O latency; the other removes repeated packed Q4_K loads. Each has its own correctness, fallback and speed gates.

## Changes to review

- [ ] #1154 — read the next chunk's original BF16 PLE rows while Metal processes the current chunk. One extra host buffer is capped at 128 MiB (80 MiB at the measured 8,192-token chunk); thread/read failures fall back to synchronous reads. Worker completion is joined before exposing the next frontier.
- [ ] #1198 — reuse packed Q4_K header/quant words in the NAX prefill loader. Arithmetic order, dequantization, dispatch geometry and other quant loaders are unchanged.

## Evidence

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, resident Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4 (Q4_K gate/up, MXFP4 down):

| PR | Primary result | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #1154 | +3.94% fresh-16K prefill in an eight-run comparison | Full logits were exact. A separate four-run integration smoke measured +6.27%; it is not an additional gain. Worker cancellation/read/thread fallback tests are included. |
| #1198 | +2.376% warmed fresh-16K text; +2.274% code | Baseline already includes #1154. Exact kernel outputs, full frontier logits and serialized-state/ordinary-decode comparisons passed. |

The campaigns differ in baseline, warmup/context conditions and attention-path background. There is no direct final-combination-versus-stock-upstream measurement, so these results do not establish a universal combined percentage or a gain at every context length. No new decode throughput benefit is claimed; production opportunistic/non-exact MTP is unchanged.

## Review and integration

These are independent implementations, not a strict build dependency. #1154 before #1198 aligns with the latter's measured baseline. Keep each implementation with its focused tests and rollback/failure behavior.

Related [context correctness and checkpoint reuse tracker #1201](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1201) covers #1169, #1175, #1206 and #1200. Those change history/reuse behavior and have separate merge decisions. The checkpoint workflow timing includes these prefill changes as baseline and must not be counted as another kernel-throughput gain. #1206 measures avoided replay work against upstream plus #1169; its timings do not measure a kernel-throughput improvement.

The earlier temporary integration of the original five PRs (#1154, #1169, #1175, #1198 and #1200) at upstream `fc80bd695da76ee14bcb86820bf900a5cdfda806` merged without text conflicts and passed:

```sh
make -j8 ds4_test test-kvstore-near-tail
./ds4_test --server
```

These establish build and model-free server/store compatibility, not a combined model-speed campaign. Individual PRs contain their full model/kernel validation. Final performance qualification should use matching model, corpus, chunking, context, warmup and host-load conditions, with only one model process/session running at a time.

Close this tracker when both PRs are merged or explicitly resolved.

title: server: live prefill/decode status via GET /v1/status + macOS menu bar
body:
# server: live prefill/decode status via GET /v1/status + macOS menu bar

## What

Adds a read-only `GET /v1/status` endpoint and an opt-in `--menubar` flag
that surface live inference state, so you can watch prefill/decode progress
without tailing logs.

- `GET /v1/status` returns a JSON snapshot: per-slot prefill progress
  (`current/total/tps/elapsed`), decode speed (`tokens/tps/avg_tps/elapsed`),
  queue depth (`waiting`), a coarse `state` (`prefilling` > `generating` >
  `queued` > `idle`), and session `totals`.
- `--menubar` makes the server spawn `menubar/ds4_menubar.py`, a standalone
  PyObjC companion that polls `/v1/status` once a second and renders colored
  menu-bar text: `PP 45%` (blue) → `GEN 42.1 t/s` (green) → `WAIT n`
  (orange) → `idle`. The dropdown lists per-slot detail and session totals.

## Why a sidecar, and why the server spawns it

The menu bar lives in a separate process on purpose: it never imports ds4,
so engine upgrades cannot break it, and it keeps AppKit out of the inference
process. The server spawns it (rather than a shell alias) so `./ds4-server`
stays the single entry point and the icon's lifetime tracks the server's —
it appears on bind and is terminated on shutdown. If `python3` or PyObjC is
missing, the server prints a hint and runs unchanged. `--no-menubar` opts
out explicitly.

## Design notes

- **No lock-order inversion.** Stats live under a dedicated `stats_mu`.
  Update paths take only `stats_mu`. The snapshot builder copies the phases
  under `stats_mu`, releases it, then counts the job queue under `s->mu` in
  a *separate* critical section — the two locks are never nested.
- **Hot-path cost.** The prefill feed hooks the existing progress callback
  (already firing per chunk); the decode feed updates at the existing
  50-token log throttle plus request end — no per-token locking. Each update
  is a handful of stores under an uncontended mutex.
- **Purely additive.** New endpoint, new flag, new files. No existing API,
  response body, or backend kernel is touched.

## Machine / backend / quant

- Apple M5 Max (18 cores), 128 GB, macOS 26.5.1, arm64, Metal backend.
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-Layers37-42Q4KExperts-OtherExpertLayersIQ2XXSGateUp-Q2KDown-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8.gguf`
  (91 GB) — this machine's production quant. The stock `ds4flash.gguf`
  IQ2XXS weight was not present locally; one environmental fixture mismatch
  is called out below.

## Testing

- [x] `make` — `ds4-server` / `ds4_test` compile `-Wall -Wextra`, zero warnings.
- [x] CPU portability: server TU compiles clean with `-DDS4_NO_GPU` (POSIX-only:
      `fork`/`exec`/`waitpid`/`kill`/`access`).
- [x] `./ds4_test --server` — green, including new cases: JSON contract
      (full-string equality, idle + totals), state priority, `waiting` count,
      decode phase transitions, `--menubar/--no-menubar` flag parsing.
- [x] `./ds4_test --all` — green: session-snapshot, long-context (30 474-token
      story recall), tool-call-quality (fast + exact), think-tool-recovery,
      **logprob-vectors vs official 0731 vectors**, metal-short-prefill,
      metal-kernels, metal-tensor-equivalence, SSD cache-pressure, server.
      Model-family groups (qwen4-*, glm53-*, mtp-*) self-skipped as designed.
      Two environmental findings, both shown unrelated to this commit:
      - `local-golden-vectors` ERRs identically on the `origin/main` baseline
        at `fc80bd6` (same machine + weights): the local-golden fixture was
        recorded from a different quant than the Q4K-experts weight used
        here. Official-vectors `logprob-vectors` passes on the same weight.
      - `dspark-verify-depth` hits the pre-existing single-instance
        `/tmp/ds4.lock` when run after other model groups inside one `--all`
        process; it passes standalone (`worst_argmax_gap=0.000`).

## Speed

Engine files are untouched (`ds4.c`, `ds4_metal.m`, `metal/*.metal` — see
`git diff origin/main..HEAD`), and `ds4-bench` does not compile server code,
so a bench sweep would compare identical code paths. The actual hot-path
delta is the mutex-guarded stats store at existing throttle points, so it
was measured on the server itself: `./ds4-server -m <model> --metal -c 32768`
serving one fixed non-streaming completion (2.8k-char prompt → 256 tokens,
temp 0), one warmup + 3 timed runs per arm, arms interleaved baseline / PR /
baseline / PR so adjacent pairs cancel thermal drift:

| arm | decode avg over run (t/s) | mean wall (s) |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 45.2 | 7.30 |
| PR | 44.5 → 43.2 | 7.52 |
| baseline | 44.3 → 42.8 | 7.65 |
| PR | 40.8 → 39.6 | 8.56 |

Throughput declines monotonically across the whole window on **both**
binaries (Metal thermal drift under repeated loads); the PR arm sits within
its adjacent baseline in all three interleaved comparisons (≤ 1%), i.e. the
stats-hook cost is unmeasurable above noise.

## Out of scope

Auth/TLS, multi-server aggregation, historical curves, any change to the
inference engine or backends.

title: Metal: fuse the V4.1 shared expert's gate, up and SwiGLU
body:
962ac19 fused the V4.1 shared-expert activation stages on CUDA. This is the Metal counterpart.

## What changes

On Metal, V4.1 single-token decode runs the shared expert's first half as five dispatches per layer: a Q8_0 matvec for gate and one for up, each followed by a BF16 rounding pass, then SwiGLU and a third rounding pass. This PR does those in one dispatch.

`kernel_dsv41_shared_gate_up_swiglu_q8_0` is the existing V4 fused kernel (`kernel_dsv4_shared_gate_up_swiglu_q8_0_impl`) with a `BF16` template flag that rounds gate, up and mid at the points where the unfused V4.1 graph rounds them. The V4 instantiations pass `false` and are otherwise untouched. `ds41_moe` uses the fused call when both tensors are Q8_0; `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_SHARED_FUSION` restores the unfused sequence. The down projection and the batched prefill path are unchanged.

## Correctness

Machine: Apple M1 Ultra, 128 GiB, Metal backend. Base: fc80bd6.

- `./tests/test_deepseek41_metal --shared-fusion` compares fused against unfused bit for bit (gate, up and mid) at V4.1 shapes, 5120 to 2304, using Q8_0 scales that are not powers of two so the two paths only agree if they also reduce in the same order. It also checks that the comparison can fail: the unrounded V4 kernel must differ from the V4.1 result in more than half the rows, and the clamp must be reached. Passes.
- `./tests/test_deepseek41_metal` (the new check is part of the default run): passes.
- `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Q2.gguf`, `--ssd-streaming --ctx 4096 -n 48 --temp 0`: output is byte-identical with the fusion on and with `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_SHARED_FUSION=1`, across six runs.
- `make cpu` builds.
- `./ds4_test --metal-kernels` reports 29 failures on this machine, in the compressor-store and flash KV stage checks. Unmodified fc80bd6 reports the same 29, at the same nine assertions, so they are not from this change, but I have not looked into them.

Not run: `--logprob-vectors`, `--long-context`, `--tool-call-quality` and the V4 Flash model tests. I do not have a V4 Flash GGUF on this machine. The V4 kernels change only by the added template argument.

## Speed

`./tests/test_deepseek41_metal --shared-fusion-timing` runs one token's worth (40 layers) per arm in one command buffer, arms alternated, 15 rounds after two warm-up rounds:

| | ms per 40 layers |
|---|---|
| unfused | 2.68 to 4.19, typically about 3.2 |
| fused | 1.58 to 2.93, typically about 2.1 |

Fused was faster in 15 of 15 rounds, by a ratio of 0.58 to 0.71. The unfused arm always runs first within a round, and all 40 layers reuse one pair of weight matrices, so this measures dispatch and activation overhead, not weight traffic.

End to end I could not measure a difference. With the Q2 model streamed from a USB SSD, generation was 3.93 and 3.14 t/s fused against 4.01 and 2.98 t/s unfused (48 tokens, runs ordered fused, unfused, unfused, fused). That configuration is bound by expert streaming, and about 1 ms per token is below its run-to-run variation. I have no machine where V4.1 is fully resident, so I cannot say what it is worth there.

title: Rewind the live GLM-5.3 KV to a snapshot instead of rebuilding the prompt
body:
## Summary

- Snapshot the GLM-5.3 recurrent KDA state and pooled indexer tail on a token
  stride during prefill, into a small per-session ring, and restore from it.
- Rewind the live KV to the newest snapshot at or below the shared prefix when a
  prompt diverges below the frontier, instead of rebuilding the whole prompt.
- Ask the core which position is actually restorable before naming a rewind
  target, so the probe never promises a rewind the engine will refuse and then
  rebuild anyway.
- Document the two knobs (`DS4_GLM_REWIND_SLOTS`, `DS4_GLM_REWIND_STRIDE`) and
  their memory cost in `docs/SERVER.md`.

## Why

GLM-5.3 carries 34 layers of recurrent linear-attention state plus a pooled
indexer tail. None of it can be truncated: to put a session back at an earlier
position you have to have saved what was live there. So a request whose prompt
shares a long token prefix with the live session and then differs -- a client
that compacted its history, pruned tool results, or edited a message -- discards
the whole context and prefills from token zero.

The existing GLM rewind tier could not help. It accepted only a *strict
truncation* of the checkpoint, and for that it named `prompt_len - 1`, a
position GLM-5.3 cannot restore unless it happens to fall inside the two-token
speculative window. The probe claimed `memory-rewind`, the rewind refused, and
the request rebuilt from zero regardless -- and a prompt that *diverged* below
the frontier had no tier at all. In one recorded agent session a 149k-token
request spent 329 s of prefill to answer in two.

The gate was never the blocker: `ds4_engine_is_glm_dsa()` tests the shape
*family*, and GLM-5.3's shape is `{.family = GLM_DSA, .variant = GLM53}`, so the
tier was already reachable there -- which is why this branch *carves* GLM-5.3 out
of that tier (`&& !ds4_engine_is_glm53()`) instead of admitting it, and gives it a
tier that asks the core where it can actually land.

## Behavior

The new tier sits last in the probe ladder, after every tier that needs no
recompute, so a visible-transcript or rendered-text prefix still wins. It fires
only for GLM-5.3, only when the shared prefix is non-empty and strictly below
the frontier, and only when the core reports a restorable position. The target
is always strictly below `prompt_len`, so the final prompt token is re-read and
logits are fresh -- the same contract as the other tiers that recompute.

When the ring holds nothing for a strict truncation, the tier names
`prompt_len - 1` and the ordinary rewind path keeps the two-token rollback it
already supported: pre-existing behavior, unchanged. The older GLM frontier
rewind keeps the truncation tier untouched. A session whose checkpoint holds
images is never rewound -- replaying those positions would feed image rows to
the text path.

## Memory

| knob | default | effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DS4_GLM_REWIND_SLOTS` | 8 | snapshots kept; `0` turns the ring off |
| `DS4_GLM_REWIND_STRIDE` | 8192 | tokens between two snapshots |

One slot is 145.6 MiB at the GLM-5.3 shape, so the defaults cost about 1.1 GiB
per session and make the last ~65k positions rewritable: a divergence re-reads
at most one stride plus the new tail instead of the whole prompt. The ring is
allocated on the first snapshot and included in the session memory estimate, so
the existing host-memory guard accounts for it -- same box, same benchmark
session, the planned-memory line moves by exactly the ring:

```
before: buffers 3.04 GiB + ... = 93.64 GiB planned
after:  buffers 4.18 GiB + ... = 94.78 GiB planned     (+1.14 GiB = 8 x 145.6 MiB)
```

Swap stayed flat across a
210-step replay at 256k context.

## Correctness evidence

Machine: Apple M5 Max, 128 GB, Metal backend, `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2`,
`-c 256000`.

The invariant and the log line below are from **this branch's own build**
(`636bba7`). The replay-scale numbers come from the local tree this branch was
extracted from -- same ring, same floor, same two guards; the probe tier is the
only part rewritten to upstream's shape, and that part is covered by the unit
tests under Tests.

**The invariant: a rewound session must produce what a cold prefill would.**
A 30,586-token prompt at `temperature 0`, 48 tokens generated:

| path | prefill | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cold prefill from zero | 86.6 s | sha1 `217778c256573586` |
| snapshot rewind to 26,624 (ratio 0.87) | 14.4 s | sha1 `217778c256573586` |

Byte-identical continuation, 6.0x faster. The intervening probe request -- same
prefix, one token longer, different tail -- rewound from the same slot to the
same position and continued differently, as a different prompt must.

**Replay of one recorded 210-step agent session** (a real DSH session,
`tools/prefix_reuse_replay.py --replay --apply-prunes`, same file, same
harness; only the environment differs). Over the 49 replayed requests after the
first cold turn:

| | defaults (8 x 8192) | `DS4_GLM_REWIND_SLOTS=0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| requests rebuilt from zero | 0 | 13 |
| wall clock of those requests | 258 s | 2,054 s |
| prompt tokens re-prefilled | 105,686 | 935,092 |
| worst single request | 6.1 s | 91,617 tokens, 208.3 s |

That last row is one and the same request on both sides -- replayed request 49.
Without a snapshot it prefilled 91,617 tokens from zero in 208 s; with one it
reused 97.4% of its prefix and answered in 6.1 s.

Over the full 210 steps with defaults: 30,013,791 prompt tokens of which 625,684
were re-prefilled (aggregate reuse 0.9792), across 59 snapshot rewinds that
skipped 249,775 tokens -- about 454 s of cold prefill at the ~550 tok/s this box
sustains. Only two requests rebuilt from zero: the first turn, and the one deep
history edit outside the ring window (below).

What a rewind looks like -- the log line and the trace field, straight from this
branch's server:

```
ds4-server: rewound GLM live prefix from 30634 to 26624; final prompt token will be reevaluated

  cache_source: memory-rewind
```

## Speed

`ds4-bench`, same box, same model, same prompt file, before (`fc80bd6`) vs after.
The measurements are **paired**: short sweeps (`--ctx-start 8192 --ctx-max 24576
--step-incr 4096 --gen-tokens 64`) alternating the two builds in ABBA order, four
rounds, giving 20 matched (round, frontier) samples taken about two minutes
apart.

| metric | mean delta | 95% CI | median | per-pair scatter (90th pct) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefill_tps` | -0.08% | [-0.71%, +0.56%] | -0.04% | 2.5% |
| `gen_tps` | -0.19% | [-0.64%, +0.26%] | -0.29% | 2.0% |

No measurable regression: both intervals straddle zero and sit well inside the
scatter of individual pairs. That is the expected shape -- the only work added
inside prefill is one 145.6 MiB copy every `DS4_GLM_REWIND_STRIDE` (8192) tokens,
~18 KB/token amortized, and the decode path is untouched.

Why paired rather than one before/after CSV: two full 2048..65536 sweeps taken 40
minutes apart (baseline first) showed -15% prefill and -7% generation for this
build, with the loss concentrated in small clock-bound contexts and gone by 63k
where the work is bandwidth-bound. Minutes apart, the same comparison is -0.04%.
Run order dominates an effect of this size on a passively cooled box, so a
single before/after pair is not evidence in either direction.

## Known limits

- The ring covers the last `SLOTS x STRIDE` positions (~65k by default). One
  request in the recorded session -- a prune that dropped almost everything,
  leaving a common prefix of only ~20-35k of 149,173 tokens -- is beyond any
  ring setting, and rebuilt (328.9 s). Measured alternative: raising
  `DS4_GLM_REWIND_STRIDE` to 16384 (same memory) did reach it, landing on the
  oldest slot and re-reading 87% of the prompt for a 25 s win (303.4 s), while
  every ordinary rewind paid up to a 16k re-read -- over 126 requests, 17% more
  wall clock and 15% more re-prefilled tokens. So the defaults stay, and depth
  is worth buying with `DS4_GLM_REWIND_SLOTS` rather than stride.
- Snapshots are taken while reading prompts, not while generating, so a
  divergence inside freshly generated tokens is still served only by the
  speculative window.
- Tensor-parallel sessions take no snapshots. `ds4_session_rewind()` keeps ranks
  in step by sending the rewind to the workers; a snapshot restore has no such
  message, and restoring on the leader alone would leave them holding the
  positions above it. A TP session therefore reports no reachable position and
  keeps its current path.

## Tests

- `make -j8` -- clean, 0 warnings
- `make cpu` -- clean, 0 warnings (the CPU reference build has no graph state,
  so the two entry points answer "nothing reachable" and callers keep their
  ordinary rebuild)
- `./ds4_test --server` -- `server: OK`, including the new
  `test_slot_probe_glm_rewind_tiers`: divergence, divergence above the newest
  snapshot, strict truncation, ring empty, exact extension still wins, and an
  image-bearing checkpoint refused
- `./tests/test_session_state` and `./tests/test_session_state_gpu` -- the GPU
  one also proves that a restore from a non-zero ring slot reproduces the saved
  KDA conv and recurrent state exactly, and that an offset past the ring is
  refused instead of clamped
- `git diff --check`
- model-backed: the invariant run and the two replays above

## Related

- #1005 generalizes the probe's capability gate (`ds4_engine_can_rewind()`) and
  relaxes the fork target to `common`. That is the right shape for the probe,
  and this tier can call it directly if that lands. It does not by itself make
  GLM-5.3 rewindable mid-divergence: `ds4_session_rewind()` for GLM-5.3 succeeds
  only inside the two-token speculative window, so a `common` target below the
  frontier is refused and the request rebuilds anyway -- which is the failure
  `glm_live_rewind_target()` avoids by asking the core first. This PR supplies
  the restore mechanism the gate assumes.
- #1093 and #1089 attack the same rebuild from the checkpoint side; this one
  keeps the live KV usable.

title: server: preserve Qwen Responses final-answer cache reuse
body:
## Problem

**Merge dependency: #1169's EOS commitment and closed-turn publication fix must land first.** This branch contains only the final-answer replay repair and its tests; the live comparison below uses upstream plus #1169.

A streaming Qwen Responses conversation can lose its entire live cache after a completed final answer when the client replays the emitted reasoning summary. The server remembers only the final-answer surface without reasoning. Exact-token fallback sometimes masks that mismatch, but cannot recover when an earlier tool-output-ID continuation left canonical image/token offsets different from sampled KV.

The reproduction uses `stream=true`, `store=false`, medium reasoning and `summary=auto`: two user images → one tool call → a synthetic result with four more images → a final answer → a user continuation with no new images. All preceding input items remain unchanged. The control re-evaluates roughly 5.1K tokens on the last request.

## Change and scope

- Remember one optional final-answer key containing the emitted reasoning, alongside the existing key without it. Both bind the same live frontier.
- Match each key using its own suffix boundary, retaining the existing image identity, image-offset and live-frontier checks. Image offsets are shared because all input images precede the generated assistant suffix.
- Preserve trailing whitespace in plain Qwen answer suffixes, matching the existing replay renderer.
- Add a model-free parser/render/reuse regression and a portable streaming HTTP reproduction in `tests/test_server_vision_live_state.py`.

The replay choice and omitted-final-reasoning assumption occur in shared Responses logic. This repair is intentionally Qwen-only: that is the renderer and live failure tested here. Other model syntaxes and tool-call reasoning behavior keep their existing contracts. The added state is at most one extra normalized transcript string per live Qwen final-answer record that emits a summary. It is freed with the existing record; there are no new settings, cache files or format changes.

Related cache work is tracked in #1201. #1169 supplies the EOS guarantee required before enabling more closed-turn reuse; this PR does not duplicate that work. #1175 validates changed parent history on the tool-ID route, and #1200 supplies additional disk checkpoints. Those responsibilities remain separate.

## Reproduction and measured impact

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, macOS 26.6.2, Metal; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q4 (Q4_K gate/up, MXFP4 down), Q8_0 vision encoder, context 32,768, opportunistic MTP, temperature 0. Managed servers ran sequentially with isolated test caches and no private prompt trace.

Control: upstream `fc80bd695da76ee14bcb86820bf900a5cdfda806` plus #1169 at `995fba520d1242f8f1a254868dac5f90ca7d11ab`. Candidate: the same code plus this repair.

| Final continuation | Cached tokens | Evaluated tokens | Server prefill | First streamed delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Control, preserve final reasoning | 0 | 5,159 | 3.655 s | 3.717 s |
| Candidate, preserve final reasoning | 5,107 | 44 | 0.148 s | 0.200 s |
| Candidate, omit final reasoning | 5,106 | 44 | 0.148 s | 0.200 s |
| Candidate, summaries not requested | 5,106 | 44 | 0.152 s | 1.721 s |

The control's omit and summary-off cases also passed. All candidate final continuations logged `match=visible-prefix`; the tool result uses the tool-ID tier when its reasoning is replayed. Without summaries, the first visible delta follows hidden reasoning, so it is not a prefill latency measure.

These are individual reproduction timings, not a statistical speed estimate or a kernel-throughput improvement. Generated continuation lengths differ; total response wall time is not treated as a matched speed comparison. An observed 139.5-second long-session stall motivated the investigation, but its exact historical cause was not proven and no 139-second saving is claimed.

## Validation

On the standalone submission branch, based on upstream `fc80bd6`:

```sh
make clean
make -j8
make -j8 ds4_test cpu
./ds4_test --server
python3 -m py_compile tests/test_server_vision_live_state.py
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

All passed. CPU compilation only; no CPU model inference.

The model-free regression parses actual Responses reasoning/message items and forces the visible tier with divergent checkpoint tokens and image token offsets. It covers summary requested/not requested, reasoning preserved/omitted, trailing answer whitespace, request-local image marker nonces, changed image fingerprints, stale frontiers, suffix boundaries and cleanup.

For the live reproduction, run one idle Qwen server with its vision encoder, `--ctx 32768 --tokens 32768 --mtp --warm-weights`, an isolated KV directory and a server log, then:

```sh
python3 tests/test_server_vision_live_state.py \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8001 --model qwen3.8-flash-next \
  --section responses-final --reasoning-replay preserve \
  --log /tmp/ds4-server.log
# Repeat with --reasoning-replay omit and summary-off.
```

The checked-in HTTP probe needs only Python's standard library and repository image fixtures, launches no background task, checks unchanged preceding input, requires the previous generated frontier to remain cached, and verifies the actual visible tier when `--log` is supplied. The preserve case failed on the EOS-fixed control and all three cases passed on the candidate.

Build and full server fixtures also passed with #1169 and #1175 combined. Integrating #1175 required combining the two cleanup additions and adding the new optional-key argument (`NULL`) to its test helper. Those adaptations are confined to the temporary integration checkout.

No inference kernels or model arithmetic change. No DeepSeek/GLM live runs, CUDA/SSD/distributed runtime tests, broad throughput sweep or multi-hour agent soak were performed.

title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next: +40% decode on one DGX Spark (prose), +46% (code)
body:
This PR has two commits that speed up Qwen3.8 Flash Next decode on one DGX Spark.

**Top-5 checkpoints with a healed shared expert**
- `expert_used_count` and the shared-expert width are now read from the GGUF instead of being fixed at 10 and 640. A shared expert wider than the routed experts runs as dense projections.
- `gguf-tools/qwen4_graft_shared.py` grafts the healed 1280-wide shared experts of `azampatti/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-125B-A5B-INT4-AutoRound` (5 experts per token) into a stock Q4 GGUF.

**Decode kernels and dense retyping**
- The Q8_0 matvec reads 8 quants per lane and keeps two steps in flight.
- A split-K matvec handles short, wide F16 and Q8_0 matrices (the hyper-connection down projections).
- A dedicated Q4_0 matvec.
- `gguf-tools/qwen4_retype_dense.py` adds `--hc-q8` (hyper-connections from F16 to Q8_0) and `--head-gptq` (an exact conversion of a GPTQ int4 `lm_head` to Q4_0).

**Results** on one Spark: Q4, `--mtp`, `DS4_QWEN4_MTP_DEPTH=3`, `DS4_QWEN4_MTP_DRAFT_ROWS=65536`, greedy, 256 tokens.

| Model | Prose | Code |
|---|---:|---:|
| Upstream main, stock 10 experts | 35 t/s | 43 t/s |
| This PR, stock 10 experts | 37 t/s | 45 t/s |
| This PR, healed top-5 | 46 t/s | 57 t/s |
| This PR, healed top-5 + `--hc-q8 --head-gptq` | 49 t/s | 62 t/s |

Perplexity:

| Text | Stock | Healed top-5 | + retype | Unhealed top-5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| English | 6.72 | 6.83 | 6.92 | 7.89 |
| C | 1.65 | 1.64 | 1.65 | 1.74 |
| Italian | 3.56 | 4.45 | 4.60 | 6.19 |

**Checks**
- `make test-qwen4-cuda` passes.
- Greedy output with `--mtp` matches output without it on every prompt tried.
- The new kernels use the same per-row arithmetic for T = 1..8.
- Metal was neither built nor tested.

title: Add MiMo V2.6 Flash MOPD support on Metal
body:
## Scope

Add text-only Metal support for `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD`, pinned to `b12f5573350bb1704513fcf119fca48e498b0423`.

- Implement the MiMo backbone, mixed global/sliding-window attention, sigmoid/noaux routing, embedded MTP and the matching DFlash sidecar.
- Add MXFP4/Q8-attention conversion and validation, model-aware CLI/server/agent integration, and tool-call handling.
- Fix SSD residency pressure through MiMo-specific automatic cache sizing, cache short continued prefills, and reuse the existing parallel layer-preparation pipeline for bulk prefill.
- Extend the benchmark tools for streamed MiMo, DFlash token capture and concurrent sessions. Add audited expert-cache traces, frozen-policy replay tools and recorded experiments.

This contains all six commits on the MiMo branch. The diff includes numeric fixtures, benchmark reports and compressed cache traces. Model weights, large activation captures and full-vocabulary references are not included in Git.

## Supported scope and defaults

MiMo inference is Metal-only and text-only. This does not add MiMo CPU/CUDA/ROCm inference, vision, audio or tensor parallelism. MiMo chooses its own prefill chunk size.

Automatic MiMo cache sizing and layer preparation are enabled for their supported paths. Existing explicit cache overrides remain available. The following research controls remain disabled by default:

| Control | Scope and result |
| --- | --- |
| `DS4_MIMO2_CACHE_RANK_MODEL` | Learned eviction priority. Held-out logical misses fell 11.74%, but native throughput was mixed. |
| `DS4_MIMO2_EXPERT_ROWS` | Shared verifier scheduling. Output matched legacy DFlash; throughput gains were workload-dependent. |
| `DS4_MIMO2_DFLASH_ADAPTIVE` | Cost-aware draft depth. An output-matched speedup was not established. |
| `DS4_MIMO2_SESSION_BATCH` | Native streamed decode for 2-8 sessions. Full-logit/KV parity passed, but throughput and tail latency were mixed. |
| `DS4_MIMO2_VERIFY_EXPERT_BUDGET` | Quality-changing verifier experiment. Budgets 8/16/32 failed the numerical gates and were not promoted. |

Predictive staging increased total logical reads, so no prediction-driven expert prefetcher was added. The ANE study is an expert-weight feasibility pilot, not a serving integration or a new runtime dependency. The released Edge0 loader does not support this checkpoint.

## Measured performance

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB RAM, Metal, `MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD-MXFP4-Q8Attn.gguf`. Standalone comparisons used a 4096-token raw Promessi Sposi prefix, context 4353 and 128 greedy, non-EOS generation tokens. Rates below are pooled over measured time. Each comparison has its own control; absolute rates should not be compared across cohorts.

| Comparison and baseline | Metric | Before, t/s | After, t/s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| MiMo automatic residency budget, `5650358` | Decode | 0.235 | 9.972 |
| Parallel layer preparation, `fc36600` | Prefill | 32.89 | 51.79 |
| Final default-path guard, clean rebuilt `11001a3` | Prefill | 56.94 | 56.81 |
| Final default-path guard, clean rebuilt `11001a3` | Decode | 10.38 | 10.78 |

The residency result fixes a configuration-specific driver-stall cliff: the expert cache changed from 84.95 to 63.92 GiB. It is not a general model-speedup claim. The final guard used eight fresh processes in ABBA then BAAB order, identical 5134-slot caches and identical decoded output.

The experimental integration initially regressed ordinary decoding by doing floating-point cache-priority work even with learning disabled. The final implementation keeps stock comparisons integer-only, selects policy once per scan and encodes finite learned scores only when that policy is active. Signed-zero ties retain LRU behavior.

## Validation performed

Build and focused regression commands included:

```sh
make -j8 all ds4_test ds4_agent_test ds4_cpu.o ds4_bench_cpu.o
make test-session-state test-quality-api
make test-expert-cache-replay test-expert-cache-learned \
     test-expert-prefetch-replay test-expert-activation-prefetch
make test-cache-rank test-dflash-policy test-mimo-verify-quality
make test-mimo2-kernels test-dflash-kernels test-qwen4-kernels
./ds4_test --server
./ds4_agent_test
```

All 65 Python tests and the targeted C/Metal suites passed. Real-model checks covered MTP/DFlash verification, short appends including sliding-window wrap, and native batching at two and eight sessions with bitwise full-logit and saved-KV comparisons.

The final stock and learned cache captures each matched all 24,064 hit masks, logical byte counts and cache clocks against their CPU policies. Both matched the original 512 selected-token/top-20-logit steps. The final full-budget verifier check matched all 128 full-vocabulary rows.

Standalone performance command, repeated with the recorded frozen baseline/candidate binaries:

```sh
"$BENCH" -m "$MODEL" --ssd-streaming \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt \
  --ctx-start 4096 --ctx-max 4096 --ctx-alloc 4353 \
  --gen-tokens 128 --show-output --csv "$CSV"
```

## Limitations and failed gates

- An initial quality grid used rendered-chat tokenization instead of the reference captures' raw-text contract. Those results are explicitly invalidated. All 18 corrected runs checked prefix counts and teacher input/label pairs; all six unmasked/full-budget controls matched exactly. Reduced expert budgets failed the unchanged NLL/KL/argmax gates.
- Batched verification can differ from ordinary decoding near ties. The adaptive-versus-fixed-depth Rust comparison diverged after token index 219, so its rate difference is not presented as an output-matched speedup.
- Historical RL fixtures do not qualify MOPD quality. Checkpoint-matched hosted continuation scores, a fresh MOPD resident-Q2 quality gate and full release QA are not claimed.
- CPU-only core/benchmark objects build, but this does not imply CPU MiMo inference. No CUDA/ROCm or other-host performance claim is made.

## Evidence

- [Model setup and limitations](https://github.com/mvid/ds4/blob/c3844ee4f9bb562504bc96aa4bb5a64eb5e47448/docs/MODELS.md#mimo-v26-flash)
- [MiMo QA and before/after measurements](https://github.com/mvid/ds4/blob/c3844ee4f9bb562504bc96aa4bb5a64eb5e47448/QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md#20-mimo-v26-flash)
- [Machine-readable experiment summary](https://github.com/mvid/ds4/blob/c3844ee4f9bb562504bc96aa4bb5a64eb5e47448/speed-bench/mimo-cache/experiments-20261011/summary.json)
- [Final default-path receipts and policy audits](https://github.com/mvid/ds4/tree/c3844ee4f9bb562504bc96aa4bb5a64eb5e47448/speed-bench/mimo-cache/experiments-20261011/default-regression/final)

The optional-feature timing receipts predate the final cache-comparator correction and remain labeled with their frozen binaries; those historical rates are not assigned to the final build.
