title: CUDA: add resident V4.1 multi-GPU layer placement, validated on Turing
body:
## Value: another kind of local CUDA multi-GPU support

Enable **single-process, resident whole-layer placement for DeepSeek V4.1**, including Flash 1017 Q2 on four 48 GiB Quadro RTX 8000s (Turing, `sm_75`). Previously the V4.1 engine rejected local configurations with more than one GPU.

This is a **capacity-oriented alternative**, not another tensor-parallel implementation: complete layers' weights stay on their assigned GPUs, while one synchronized workspace carries activations and KV/index state between layer owners. It lets several older CUDA cards hold the model together without requiring Blackwell-native BF16/FP4 instructions for the tested quantization.

| Mode | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| **New V4.1 resident layer placement** | Multiple local CUDA GPUs; complete layers; serial scheduling |
| Existing `--cuda-tensor-parallel` | V4 Flash paired tensor/expert splitting; unchanged |
| Existing V4.1 network TP | Two single-GPU ranks; unchanged |

The implementation is not restricted to an RTX 8000 product ID, but **only the four-RTX-8000 configuration was hardware-validated**. This is not a claim of tested 3090, RTX Pro 6000, A100, Volta, Windows, or arbitrary-GGUF support.

## Implementation

- Allocate a shared serial graph, select each layer's owner, synchronize handoffs, and retag tensors so generic CUDA launches resolve the correct weights and device.
- Use managed state only when all selected peer probes pass. Otherwise use portable mapped pinned-host state: this machine's cross-NVLink-pair peer validation rejects links, and implicit managed migration could silently corrupt logits. Weights remain GPU-resident in either case.
- Keep Engram tables disk-only. Reserve the entire shared graph plus runtime scratch on every GPU, account for planned sessions, preserve original admission budgets, and refuse unsupported CPU-spill layouts.
- Preserve 256-byte alignment in selective weight caches, including tiny HC scale tensors. Misaligned following F16 projections caused numerical drift relative to the single-GPU SSD arena.
- Dispatch attention score tiles only when their dynamic shared-memory requirement fits the selected device; otherwise use the existing generic path on Turing.
- Make `--decode-consistency` reject constant or nonfinite logits instead of allowing identical all-zero vectors to count as success.

Rebased onto upstream `5379c1c`, preserving its DSpark and ROCm changes. DSpark/MTP remains available in its existing supported modes; it is explicitly excluded from the **new local placement mode**. ROCm multi-GPU is not enabled by this change.

## Validation

Linux, four Quadro RTX 8000s (48 GiB each), CUDA 13.4, explicit `44,44,44,44` GiB placement budgets. NVLink pairs are 0–1 and 2–3; the mapped-host fallback was exercised for rejected cross-pair peers.

**Exact model:** community DwarfStar-format `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Q2.gguf` from `nazeshinjite/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ds4-GGUF` at `796f58533a0e4b7a89cb006b22aeb44e783f0323`, sourced from `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` at `1bae0e1088993b9b82de08f59de5be5a34e42170`. File size: 365,713,686,528 bytes. Verified full SHA256: `f57e6c3e5e68c513249e1c472a2600bf59792ca78cacb7ac0531a6056376856e`. Model files and local logs are not included in the PR.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CUDA build, `CUDA_ARCH=sm_75` | CLI, server, and focused regression binaries built |
| CPU portability | `make cpu -j4` passed in an isolated source copy |
| V4.1 synthetic CUDA suite | Passed, including rounding, routing, projection, indexing, and attention checks |
| New four-GPU regression | Passed weight ownership, shared KV/index handoff, rejected-peer fallback, host restore, planner/admission checks |
| Cache alignment and diagnostic regressions | Passed odd-size packing/growth/payload checks and constant/NaN/Inf rejection |
| Existing prefill dispatch and placement tests | Passed; CPU placement 114/114 and layer packing 97/97 |
| Full next-token logits against same-weight single-GPU SSD reference | **All 129,280 logits exactly equal**, max absolute error 0, RMS 0, matching argmax |
| Incremental decode against fresh prefill | Four steps, max absolute error 0 and RMS 0 |
| 128-token generation, 8K allocated context | Coherent hash-table explanation; **5.60 generation tokens/s** after rebase |
| Two simultaneous HTTP requests, two slots, 4K allocated context | Independent correct `hello` and `goodbye` answers; server exited cleanly |

All rows above were checked again on the rebased code. An additional **857-token prompt plus four decode steps** passed with exact incremental/fresh equality on the original implementation before rebase. That longer case used 8K allocated context and took approximately 22 minutes including loading and both prefills; it was not repeated after rebase. The post-rebase consistency run used a short prompt and compared a final 24-token prefix.

The same 128-token generation command measured about 5.56 t/s before rebase and 5.60 t/s after rebase. These are bounded CLI measurements, **not a controlled `ds4-bench` before/after CSV sweep or proof of throughput scaling**.

Build and focused checks:

```sh
make ds4 ds4-server tests/test_deepseek41_cuda \
  tests/test_deepseek41_multigpu tests/test_gpu_model_cache \
  tests/test_decode_consistency tests/test_deepseek41_prefill \
  tests/test_engine_mgpu_placement tests/test_layer_pack CUDA_ARCH=sm_75 -j4
./tests/test_deepseek41_cuda
./tests/test_deepseek41_multigpu
./tests/test_gpu_model_cache
./tests/test_decode_consistency
./tests/test_deepseek41_prefill --dispatch
./tests/test_engine_mgpu_placement
./tests/test_layer_pack
```

Example invocation, with `MODEL` pointing to the exact artifact above:

```sh
./ds4 --cuda -m "$MODEL" \
  --gpu-devices 0,1,2,3 --gpu-vram 44,44,44,44 \
  --ctx 8192 --prefill-chunk 1 --nothink --temp 0 -n 128 \
  -p 'Explain how a hash table handles collisions and resizing. Give a detailed explanation with separate chaining, open addressing, load factors, and amortized complexity.'
```

For reference parity, run `--dump-logits` with the same prompt in each mode; the single-GPU reference used `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_LAYER_PREFILL=1`, `--ssd-streaming --ssd-streaming-cache-experts 256 --ssd-streaming-cold`. The resident and SSD comparison used `--ctx 1024 -p 'Reply with exactly: hello'`. The post-rebase consistency command used the resident placement above with `--ctx 8192 -p 'Count from one to ten, separated by commas.' --decode-consistency 4`.

## Limits

Token-major prefill and ordered session fallback prioritize correctness, not parallel compute or fused batching. Slow prefill is expected. **8K allocated context is not an 8K-token prefill test.** No production endurance, broad model-quality evaluation, full disk-checkpoint round trip, or Metal/ROCm/network-TP/vision validation is claimed.

The new local mode cannot be combined with SSD expert streaming, network TP, paired CUDA TP, DSpark/MTP, CUDA vision, or CPU spill. The existing single-GPU SSD reference path remains usable separately.

## Downloader correction

Closes #1235.

Correct the stale SHA256 for the stock downloader's `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf` to `5296e85ff64b42ecb62c8d0c0c54e1caa07e3df8e93112f2365ebbaed62ce93a`, independently verified against the Hugging Face tree API's LFS object ID and 365,713,686,528-byte size for `antirez/deepseek-v4.1-flash-gguf`. Keep both size and checksum verification enabled, and update the offline downloader fixtures to the current filename and identity.

This official downloader artifact is **different from the community artifact used for the GPU inference validation above**; their checksums are not interchangeable. No additional 341 GiB download or inference validation of the official artifact is claimed. `sh -n download_model.sh` and the existing offline downloader regression suite passed, including correct/existing-file acceptance, corruption rejection, and symlink preservation.

## Related issues

Related to #123, #538, and #1224:

- #123 asks for NVIDIA multi-GPU capacity on four 3090s plus RAM. This adds resident V4.1 layer placement, but does not validate 3090s or add CPU/RAM spill.
- #538 asks for one server process using multiple CUDA GPUs. This demonstrates that capability with V4.1 on four RTX 8000s, but does not reproduce or resolve every configuration in that report.
- #1224 requests the 10/17 Flash V4.1 update. This validates one exact DwarfStar-format 1017 Q2 artifact; it does not evaluate the checkpoint's reported model-quality concerns.

These are related/partial-scope links, **not automatic closure requests**. This does not fix the A100 paired-TP/DSpark issue #735 or the separate Turing prefill overflow #803.

title: metal: use exact divisions in the V4.1 FP4 activation quantizer
body:
`make test-deepseek41-metal` fails on an M5 Max (128 GB, macOS 26.4.1) at current main (5379c1c):

```
./tests/test_deepseek41_metal
quantization mode=3 index=5428: 11.25 != 7.5
make: *** [test-deepseek41-metal] Error 1
```

`kernel_dsv41_quantize` uses the default fast-math division for the E4M3 block scale (`amax / 6`) and the E2M1 value (`|x| / scale`). 11.25 and 7.5 are 3x and 2x the same block scale (3.75), so `|x| / scale` was exactly the 2.5 midpoint: round-to-nearest-even gives 2, but the reciprocal-based quotient lands just above 2.5 and rounds to 3. It fails the same way on every run.

This switches those two divisions to `precise::divide`. The `|x| / scale` line is shared with mode 2, whose scale is a power of two, so mode 2 results do not change. The FP8 path is untouched.

Testing (M5 Max 128 GB, macOS 26.4.1, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf`):

- `make test-deepseek41-metal`: fails as above on main. With this change the BF16/FP8/FP4 round trips are exact and the rest of the test passes.
- Speed, `ds4-server --ssd-streaming --ctx 262144`, a fresh server and an empty KV dir per run. Cold 16K-token prefill with `DS4_METAL_GPU_BUSY_PROFILE=1` (summed command-buffer GPU time over the first 384 command buffers), runs in the order main, this branch, this branch, main:

  | | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | GPU time, cold 16K prefill | 24.62 s, 24.14 s | 24.76 s, 24.53 s |
  | wall time, same request | 44.90 s, 44.51 s | 44.93 s, 44.54 s |

  Decode at ~17K context (17.0 and 16.9 t/s on main, 17.3 and 17.2 with this change) and a ~2K-word append to a cached ~14K prefix (73.0/72.4 vs 73.6/73.7 t/s) did not move either. Wall-clock cold prefill on this SSD-streamed path varies by about ±3% between identical runs, so GPU time is the better measure of the kernel change. The two main runs differ from each other by 0.48 s of GPU time, and the branch runs are 0.14 s and 0.39 s above the main run next to them, so any cost is within the run-to-run spread (about 2% of GPU time here).
- `score_official` against reference continuations I collected from the DeepSeek API for the repo's V4.1 core and general prompts (`deepseek-flash`, the 1017 checkpoint):

  | | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | core, 17 cases / 141 tokens: avg NLL, top-1 | 0.211, 131/141 | 0.233, 132/141 |
  | general, 100 cases / 3003 tokens: avg NLL, top-1 | 0.332, 2749/3003 | 0.327, 2749/3003 |

  Changing how ties round moves some expert routing, so per-case scores shift in both directions. The NLL deltas have opposite signs on the two sets and top-1 agreement holds, so I don't read a quality change into them.

title: download_model.sh: stale SHA-256 for the 1017 Q2 checkpoint rejects a correct 341 GiB download
body:
## What happens

After 5379c1c switched `DS41_Q2_FILE` to `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf`, `artifact_identity()` still expects the previous hash. `hf download` fetches the file correctly, then `verify_download()` aborts:

```
Downloading DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf
✓ Downloaded
Verifying SHA-256: .../DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf
Checksum mismatch: .../DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf. The file was not accepted.
```

## Why it is the script, not the download

| Source | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `lfs.oid` from the HF tree API for that file | `5296e85ff64b42ecb62c8d0c0c54e1caa07e3df8e93112f2365ebbaed62ce93a` |
| `shasum -a 256` of the local file, all 365713686528 bytes | `5296e85ff64b42ecb62c8d0c0c54e1caa07e3df8e93112f2365ebbaed62ce93a` |
| `download_model.sh`, line 462 at 5379c1c | `1ce6a8f8806205c13330d7ca287bd198331dc5ca35ccc5d8a9a92a188a6f6f42` |

The size check passes (365713686528 bytes); only the hash comparison fails. The vision encoder entry (line 478) is already correct, so this is specific to the Q2 entry.

## Impact

- 341 GiB are downloaded and then discarded.
- Re-running does not help: the file is present, so `verify_download()` hashes it again and fails the same way. `ds41f-q2` cannot be completed with this commit.
- The check also loses its diagnostic value here: "checksum mismatch" is indistinguishable from real corruption.

## Patch

```diff
--- a/download_model.sh
+++ b/download_model.sh
@@ -459,7 +459,7 @@
         "$DS41_Q2_FILE")
             expected_bytes=365713686528
-            expected_sha=1ce6a8f8806205c13330d7ca287bd198331dc5ca35ccc5d8a9a92a188a6f6f42
+            expected_sha=5296e85ff64b42ecb62c8d0c0c54e1caa07e3df8e93112f2365ebbaed62ce93a
             ;;
```

I have the same change on a fork branch (`cropduster/ds4`, branch `fix/ds41-1017-sha256`) and can open a PR if you prefer that over applying it here.

## Environment

macOS 27.2, arm64 (Metal), `hf` 1.27.0, checkout at 5379c1c, file fetched from `antirez/deepseek-v4.1-flash-gguf`.

Unrelated: #1189 reports `Model 'antirez/deepseek-v4.1-flash-gguf' not found` with the older `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Q2.gguf` name — different failure, not covered by this patch.

title: metal: process medium V4.1 SSD appends in one layer sweep
body:
e9e1baa made CUDA process a medium SSD append (2048 < N < 8192, final tile of at least 256 rows) in one layer sweep while keeping the 2048-row arithmetic partitions. The same rule is compiled out on Apple, so on Metal these appends still stream the experts twice: a 2048-row batch, then the remainder.

This enables the rule on Metal, with its own off switch `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_MEDIUM_SWEEP` next to the CUDA one. Below 8192 rows a Metal sweep already runs in 2048-row encoder chunks (`ds41_encoder_chunk_cap`) and does not take the decoder-suffix path, so the chunks are the same as with two sweeps.

Tests: the dispatch table expects the one-sweep count on Apple too, and the Metal model check runs its control session with the switch set, so `state_equal` compares the one-sweep and two-sweep paths (its 4095 and 8191 appends take it).

Testing (M5 Max 128 GB, macOS 26.4.1, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf`, `--ssd-streaming`):

- `tests/test_deepseek41_prefill --dispatch`: PASS.
- `tests/test_deepseek41_prefill MODEL speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt` (the bounded SSD variant): PASS ("V4.1 mixed small/large continued prefill, dispatch, progress and restore"). Its 4095- and 8191-token appends now run as one batch in the checked session (`batches=1`) and match the two-sweep control in full state, the following decode and the snapshot restore; the other appends (127 … 49153) pass too.
- `ds4-server --ssd-streaming --ctx 262144 --vision ... --kv-disk-dir ...`, with the same rule switched on by a measurement build that toggles it per run: a fresh server and KV dir per arm and the same requests on both: an 8,336-token base whose cold checkpoint lands at 8192, then ten appends on top of it, greedy, 160 tokens each. Prefill time from the server log:

  | prefilled tokens | main | one sweep |
  |---|---|---|
  | 2,662 | 32.9 s | 16.3 s |
  | 2,642 | 36.4 s | 18.0 s |
  | 3,549 | 34.8 s | 17.7 s |
  | 3,539 | 36.2 s | 20.0 s |
  | 4,673 | 37.8 s | 18.3 s |
  | 4,650 | 39.0 s | 20.0 s |
  | 5,674 | 38.1 s | 21.7 s |
  | 5,692 | 39.6 s | 24.0 s |
  | 7,073 | 44.0 s | 25.7 s |
  | 7,045 | 45.3 s | 27.2 s |

  384 s → 209 s in total (17.5 s saved per append on average), and all ten 160-token answers are identical.

One behavioural difference: the server writes a continued checkpoint when a prefill batch ends exactly on the continued step (10240 by default). A medium append that starts 2048-aligned and crosses such a multiple no longer stops there, the same as on CUDA since e9e1baa.

title: Run DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Q1 (Unsloth UD-IQ1_S) resident on a 128 GB Mac
body:
Six commits that let the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 checkpoint run fully resident on one 128 GiB Mac, using Unsloth's UD-IQ1_S routed experts:

- `73b6ae0` Cut the V4.1 mapping at the resident end, not the Engram start
- `4270726` Run IQ1_S routed experts and Q5_K/Q6_K dense weights on Metal
- `ca42ba9` Add a `ds41f-q1` target built from Unsloth UD-IQ1_S (`gguf-tools/mixed/deepseek41_q1_from_unsloth.py`)
- `8de6dc1` Fit the DeepSeek V4.1 resident context to the memory budget
- `dd328ad` Run single-token Q5_K/Q6_K matvecs on the GLM SIMD down kernels
- `a414653` Decode IQ1_S routed experts two rows per SIMD group

The resulting file keeps 106.27 GiB resident, under the existing 112 GiB V4.1 guard. ctx 8192 and 14335 open at full prefill width, and with `8de6dc1` ctx 262144 opens with a 2048-row prefill (109.79 GiB) instead of being refused.

## Please look at these first

- **Requantization.** `ds41f-q1` requantizes Unsloth's 32 IQ2_XXS expert tensors to IQ1_S (libggml plus Unsloth's imatrix). That is requantizing already-quantized data, against the gguf-tools guideline of quantizing from the original safetensors, and it costs quality on the layers Unsloth protected. It is what brings the resident weights under 112 GiB. I have **not** run `score_official` on the Q1 yet.
- **`dd328ad` changes every Metal model** whose dense weights are Q5_K/Q6_K, including GLM and Qwen K-quant GGUFs: single-token matvecs now use the GLM SIMD down kernels with one always-selected expert. Only the summation order changes. It is measured on V4.1 Q1 only. `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_QK_SIMD_MV=1` restores `mul_mv_ext`.
- **Metal and resident only.** IQ1_S, and Q5_K/Q6_K dense, are refused at open on CUDA, ROCm, SSD streaming, tensor parallelism and distributed inference (see `4270726`).

## Measurements

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, Metal, High Power. Decode is 128 greedy tokens at ctx 8192 with the `ds4` CLI, in alternating runs (not a `ds4-bench` sweep). The speed runs used a Q1 build whose 38 `attn_output_b` tensors came from an abliterated Q2; shapes and types are identical. Both arms also carried a local per-layer decode pipelining change that is not in this PR.

| change | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `dd328ad` Q5_K/Q6_K route | 22.70 t/s (`mul_mv_ext r1_1`) | 32.25 / 32.22 t/s |
| `a414653` IQ1_S rows per SIMD group 4 → 2 | 32.0 t/s | about +1.5%, token-identical (4/4 paired runs) |

- In the Metal encoder timeline, `dd328ad` brings Q6_K from 19.7 to 6.7 ms per token and Q5_K from 3.65 to 1.83 ms.
- Drift from `dd328ad`: prefill logits move by at most 3.9e-6 (top-5 identical). Decode vs a fresh prefill (`--decode-consistency 1`) is RMS 0.66, against 0.79 before.
- `8de6dc1`: a needle 46,804 tokens deep was recalled at ctx 262144. "Capital of France" answers Paris.
- I also tried rewriting the IQ1_S matvec (ggml's packed grid with the delta folded into `sumy`, and two float4 `dot` variants). None beat the existing kernel (-2.5% to +0%), so they are not here.

## Tests

On this branch, CPU only (I did not use the GPU for this branch):

```
make && make cpu                                      # clean, no warnings
make iq1s-dot-test                                    # PASS
./tests/test_deepseek41_graph --context-fit           # OK
python3 gguf-tools/tests/test_deepseek41_q1_convert.py  # OK
bash -n download_model.sh; ./download_model.sh --help   # lists ds41f-q1
```

On the same commits in my fork, on Metal (M5 Max):

- `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`. Its width-1 Q5_K/Q6_K check fails when either kernel's accumulation is scaled by 1.01.
- `./tests/test_deepseek41_graph --iq1s-routed`. This runs the Metal gate, up and down IQ1_S matvecs against ggml's scalar dequantization in double, and fails under two injected kernel mutations.
- `./ds4_test --server`, `ds4_agent_test`, `ds4-eval --validate-cases` and `--self-test-extractors`, `test_layer_pack`, `test_engine_mgpu_placement`, `test_gpu_args`, the q4k/mxfp4/iq1s dot tests, `test_deepseek41_graph --batch-admission`, and the individual `test_deepseek41_metal` flags all pass.
- Q2 `--inspect` passes, and Q2 `--ssd-streaming` output is unchanged.

Known failures:

- The default `test_deepseek41_metal` run stops in `check_quantization` (FP4 mode 3, index 5428: 11.25 != 7.5). It fails the same way without the later commits here, and the FP4 path is untouched. I have not checked it on `origin/main`.
- On the Q1, `ds4_test --tool-call-quality` asks for a 32768 context, which needed 116.16 GiB before `8de6dc1`. It has not been rerun since.

**Not run:** CUDA and ROCm builds and regressions, distributed/TP, a `ds4-bench` sweep, `score_official`, and `--logprob-vectors` (its fixtures are V4 Flash).


### Note added 2026-10-20: wired-memory limit on 128 GB Macs

The 112 GiB V4.1 budget is capped at Metal's recommended working set. On a 128 GB Mac at macOS defaults that is 107.52 GiB, and this Q1 is refused at open (`V4.1 needs 119.49 GiB before the expert cache; safe budget 107.52 GiB`, observed at ctx 256000 with the vision sidecar). With `sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=114688` Metal reports exactly 112.00 GiB, and the same launch opened with 1024-row prefill (108.98 GiB planned), answered text, read a strict OCR fixture back exactly, and decoded at about 37 t/s on a second 128 GB M5 Max. The earlier measurements in this PR were taken on a machine with the limit raised.

title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next: faster Metal decode (bit-exact)
body:
Qwen3.8 Flash Next decode on Metal (M5 Max) was latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound: a short-lived skip probe that bypassed one kernel at a time showed the time going to dependent load chains, register pressure and GPU idle gaps, not to reading weights. Each change below attacks one of those stalls. Every change was gated on bit-exact decode logits (teacher-forced, 112 rows across 2 fixtures), so model output is unchanged.

**Hide latency instead of moving fewer bytes**
- MoE mid spent about 7us of 35us waiting on IQ2_XXS grid/sign lookups from device memory. Staging those tables in threadgroup memory takes the lookup off the critical path.
- Several row dots (F32 for GDN alpha/beta, Q2_K, the hc norm squares) issued their loads one at a time behind the math. Unrolling, using aligned word loads and reordering the partial sums lets the loads go out early while keeping the in-order sum.
- The router read F32 rows that only ever hold BF16 values. Reading a BF16 copy halves that traffic and gives the same result.

**Fill idle gaps**
- The PLE n-gram read (~280us) ran serially before layer 0. It now overlaps the layer-0 GPU work, and layer 1 is flushed separately so the GPU starts sooner.
- hc norm uses spare threadgroups to prefetch its down-projection weights into the system cache before they are needed.
- Folding the weighted reduce into the MoE down kernel removes one dispatch and one round trip through memory per token.

**Fix occupancy**
- Attention decode cost about 0.55us per key per split. That was register pressure from three heads per simdgroup, not memory or exp. Two heads per simdgroup across six simdgroups was the best point in a sweep of NSG4/HPS3, NSG6/HPS2 and NSG12/HPS1.
- The attention merge loads the split maxima sixteen at a time instead of one by one.
- On M5, IQ2_XXS/Q2_K expert rows use function constants (nsg 8, nr 1) tuned to its simdgroup scheduling.

## Testing (M5 Max, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q2)
- `ds4_test`: same results as `main` (the same 23 pre-existing failures on both).
- `ds4-bench` 2k-32k context: generation 48 -> 54-56 t/s (+10-17%). Prefill is +4-23% up to 8k but -4-7% from 14k up. That is still under investigation.
- Not measured: M3 Ultra, CUDA/ROCm (no Qwen paths touched there), the Q4 model.

title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: a ~3-bit (or mixed Q2/Q4) build for 256 GB Macs
body:
## Request

A roughly 3-bit build of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (IQ3-class routed experts, or a mixed Q2/Q4 layout like the `ds4f-q2-q4` build that exists for V4 Flash 0731) that keeps the main weights resident on a 256 GB Mac.

## Why

The 256 GB tier currently has only two options for V4.1 Flash, and they sit on either side of it:

| Build | On disk | Main weights resident | 256 GB Mac |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ds41f-q2` (IQ2_XXS/Q2_K imatrix) | 341 GiB | 152 GiB | resident, ~100 GiB unused |
| `ds41f-q4` | 483 GiB | 294 GiB | SSD streaming only |
| MXFP4 experts (1017, 9 parts) | ~467 GiB | ~280 GiB | SSD streaming only |

A 3-bit expert quant would land around 225 GiB of main weights. With the server's own planning numbers for the Q2 at `--ctx 32768` (buffers 7.7 GiB, KV 0.2 GiB, 159.6 GiB planned), that is roughly 235 GiB planned, which fits with headroom for the OS. A mixed layout with Q4 experts on a subset of layers, as in the 0731 `ds4f-q2-q4` file, would be the other way to spend the ~100 GiB this tier leaves on the table.

The Q2 is the heaviest quant in the lineup, and there is no published number for how much of the model's quality it keeps. A 3-bit build would give 256 GB machines (M3 Ultra, M5 Ultra) the same "resident, best quant that fits" choice the 128 GB and 512 GB tiers have.

## Reference numbers from this machine

Mac Studio M5 Ultra, 256 GB, Metal, ds4 at 5379c1c, `ds4-server --ctx 32768`, resident `ds41f-q2`:

- model residency 16 s cold, server listening at 18 s
- prefill ~1380 t/s on a 16.5k-token chat prompt (~710 t/s on 4k)
- generation 28 to 30 t/s
- planned memory 159.6 GiB, so ~95 GiB of unified memory sits idle during inference

Happy to test a candidate build here (resident speed, `--logprob-vectors`, `--long-context`) if that helps.

title: engram speedup patch achieved 28 tok sec deepseek 4.1 flash on m3 ultra 512 gb
Batch the aligned head of ragged prefill tail chunks through the compressor replay
body:
For prompts crossing the 4096-token chunk cap, a ragged tail chunk (pos0 % ratio == 0 but n_tokens % ratio != 0) fell back from the batched compressor replay to the per-token state machine for the whole chunk.

Batch the aligned head (n_tokens / ratio * ratio tokens) through the existing ds4_gpu_compressor_prefill_ratio4_replay_tensor / ds4_gpu_compressor_prefill_tensor plus the state refresh, and run the per-token loop only for the ragged remainder. The remainder is smaller than one pooling window, so it can never emit: the loop degenerates to the state-row stores. Both the attention and the indexer compressor branches are patched.

Numerics: a ragged tail chunk now produces bit-identical compressed rows and end state to an aligned chunk of the same length. Previously it pooled each group with the decode-order kernel_dsv4_compressor_exact_pool and seeded its final state from the batch-projection rows, so a prompt's compressed KV depended on how its final chunk happened to align. The difference is rounding-level but observable: on near-tie top logits a greedy token can flip (seen on two of five multi-chunk test prompts, one of them natural text; the other three produced identical continuations).

On M5 Max this has 7-14% better prefill t/s.

title: CUDA GLM-5.3 --mtp: MTP step fails on every token once the MTP window exceeds ~12k positions (staged decode weights kernel exceeds 48 KiB dynamic shared memory)
body:
## Summary

With `--mtp` on CUDA, GLM-5.3-Flash's MTP draft step fails on **every** decode token once a session's MTP attention window grows past ~12,000 positions:

```
ds4: CUDA glm staged decode weights launch failed: invalid argument
ds4: glm mtp step failed at stage 'attention' (pos 27732)
```

The main decode keeps running correctly (the draft is simply dropped and the token is decoded normally), so output is fine, but MTP is silently dead for the rest of the session, each token still pays for the full MTP pre-attention work plus a `cudaDeviceSynchronize`, and the log gets two lines per token (779 pairs in ~30 minutes here).

Root cause: `glm_attention_decode_weights_staged_kernel` keeps all attention scores of the MTP window in dynamic shared memory, `(256 + n_selected) * 4` bytes, without `cudaFuncSetAttribute(cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize)`. The launch exceeds the 48 KiB default limit at `n_selected > 12032` and fails with `cudaErrorInvalidValue`.

## Setup

- `main` @ 5379c1c (`Download script now defaults to new DS4.1 Flash checkpoint.`)
- DGX Spark, NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121), driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0.2 (`nvidia/cuda:13.0.2-devel-ubuntu24.04` build image), Linux 6.17
- Model: `GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf`, resident
- `ds4-server --cuda --model /models/GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2.gguf --mtp --ctx 524288 --kv-disk-dir /data/kv --kv-disk-space-mb 16384`
- Client: an agent session (tool calls), greedy / default sampling

## Log

```
ds4: GLM session ctx=524288 (model max=1048576); prefill/work cap=4096; dense attention limit=2051
ds4: GLM graph allocating compact DSA cache: rows=524288 logical_ctx=524288 kv_layers=45 indexer_layers=11 f16 5.84 GiB
...
1021 08:41:41 ds4-server: chat ctx=9697..9729:32 gen=32 TOOLS DSML_START DSML_END decoding chunk=15.53 t/s avg=15.53 t/s 2.060s
1021 08:41:44 ds4-server: chat ctx=9729..27732:18003 TOOLS prompt start
...
1021 08:42:23 ds4-server: chat ctx=9729..27732:18003 TOOLS prompt done 38.646s
ds4: CUDA glm staged decode weights launch failed: invalid argument
ds4: glm mtp step failed at stage 'attention' (pos 27732)
ds4: CUDA glm staged decode weights launch failed: invalid argument
ds4: glm mtp step failed at stage 'attention' (pos 27733)
...   (two lines per generated token from here on, pos 27732 .. 29756 in this log)
1021 08:42:26 ds4-server: chat ctx=27732..27782:50 gen=50 TOOLS decoding chunk=14.51 t/s avg=14.51 t/s 3.446s
```

All decode positions before the 18,003-token tool-output prefill were below ~11,000 and produced no errors; the first decode after it (pos 27732) and every later token fail. Requests still complete normally.

## Analysis

1. `glm_graph_mtp_step()` (`ds4.c` ~L52257) attends over the whole MTP window with no indexer: `n_selected = pos - min_pos + 1`. The window start `s->glm_mtp_min_pos` is set once when MTP is first seeded in a session (`ds4.c` ~L75105) and never advances, so `n_selected` grows with the context.
2. `ds4_gpu_glm_attention_indexed_decode_typed_tensor()` (`ds4_cuda.cu` ~L31761) takes the "staged" path for `n_selected >= 512` and launches
   ```
   const uint32_t weight_shmem = (256u + score_stride) * (uint32_t)sizeof(float);
   glm_attention_decode_weights_staged_kernel<...><<<weight_grid, 256, weight_shmem>>>(...)
   ```
   The kernel stores one float per selected row in `extern __shared__ float glm_dec_stage_sh[]` for the max/exp/sum passes before writing the weights to global `scratch`.
3. No `cudaFuncSetAttribute(..., cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, ...)` exists for these kernels (other kernels in the file do opt in), so the default 48 KiB cap applies: `(256 + n) * 4 > 49152` ⇔ `n > 12032`. The launch returns `cudaErrorInvalidValue` → "invalid argument" → MTP step aborts at stage `attention`.
4. The non-staged fallback kernel (`DS4_GLM_ATTN_NO_STAGED_DECODE`) uses `(256 + n_selected + kv_lora_dim) * 4` bytes of shared memory, so it hits the same wall slightly earlier; the env var is not a workaround.
5. The main model's decode is unaffected because it goes through the DSA indexer with top-k ≤ 2048 selected rows.
6. There is no "give up" logic: after the first failure every subsequent token re-runs embed/eh_proj/q_a/q_b/kv_a/kv_store, fails the launch, and synchronizes.

## Expected

MTP keeps drafting for the whole configured context (`--ctx 524288`), or at least stops attempting after repeated failures instead of paying the cost and logging on every token.

## Possible fixes

- Minimal: opt the four `glm_attention_decode_weights_staged_kernel` instantiations in via `cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize)` up to `sharedMemPerBlockOptin` (~227 KiB on GB10 → ~57k rows). Helps, but still fails well before 512K.
- Proper: don't keep the scores in shared memory. The kernel already writes the weights to the global `scratch` buffer, so a two-pass (max, then exp/sum) or an online softmax over global memory removes the limit entirely. The same applies to the non-staged kernel.
- Additionally / alternatively: bound the MTP window by sliding `glm_mtp_min_pos`. The draft is verified by the target model anyway, so output stays exact; only acceptance rate may drop.
- Robustness: after N consecutive MTP step failures in a session, disable MTP for that session (one log line) instead of retrying every token.

Happy to test a patch on the Spark.

title: metal: fix session memory leak on /ctx
body:
Every `/ctx` in the CLI leaks the old session's Metal buffers. Alternate a
prompt with `/ctx 65536` and the process memory climbs each time.

Under ARC, `[buffer contents]` retains and autoreleases the buffer.
`ds4_gpu_tensor_contents/write/read` run on C threads with no autorelease
pool, so the reference is only dropped when the thread exits, and the REPL
thread never does. Freed sessions stay resident. The fix wraps the three
helpers in `@autoreleasepool`, like the other Metal entry points. +9/-3.

M3 Ultra, main 5379c1c9, memory after each free:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/ctx`, GLM 5.3 Flash, 64K ctx | +0.14 GiB each | flat |
| create + 2K prefill + free, V4.1 Flash | +1.02 GiB each | flat |

title: Allow up to 256 images per server request
body:
`ds4-server` rejected any request with more than 16 images:

```
400: {"message":"too many images; at most 16 are allowed","type":"invalid_request_error"}
```

Agent clients that keep screenshots in a conversation pass 16 images within a few turns.

**Why it's safe to raise.** The 16 was only the server's own check, plus the size of two stack arrays (`visible_image_key.offsets` and the `spans` copy in `build_live_prompt_suffix`). Everything downstream sizes image state dynamically: the engine's vision spans, session checkpoints (`checkpoint_images`), two-Mac TP mirroring (`ds4_tp` image payloads) and the KV disk cache.

**The change.** A `SERVER_MAX_IMAGES` constant (256) now sets the check, the error message and both arrays. That's at most about 22 KB of stack in request threads. Context remains the real limit, since each image costs its vision tokens.

## Testing

- `make` and `./ds4_test --server` pass on M3 Ultra.
- **Live test.** The same patch, on a branch build serving DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Q4 with `--vision` over two-Mac TP:
  - A 20-image chat request was accepted (3,723 prompt tokens) and answered.
  - A single-image request still works.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add experimental Muse Spark Open Metal support
body:
## Summary

- add experimental Metal inference for Meta Muse Spark Open (816B total / 42B active)
- support the six-shard UD-IQ2_XXS target and its Muse-specific graph and kernels
- add GPU routing, argmax, prompt lookup, and exact grouped IQ2 verification
- add an optional Muse DSpark checkpoint converter and proposal path
- document measured performance, unsuccessful experiments, and contribution targets

This is a draft so the Muse path and its remaining performance work can be reviewed and developed in public. Model weights are not included.

## Measured performance

Machine: Apple M3 Ultra, 256 GiB unified memory  
Model: Muse Spark Open UD-IQ2_XXS, six shards, about 210 GiB mapped

- plain decode: **18.30 tok/s steady** with a 128-token prompt and 24 generated tokens
- prompt prefill: about **47.9 tok/s**
- prompt lookup on repetitive code: **27.7-29.0 tok/s**, depending on the matched span

The higher prompt-lookup number applies when output repeats prompt tokens. Ordinary generation remains near 18 tok/s.

The parallel router reduced aggregate router time from about 11.0 ms to 1.4 ms per generated token. Exact-path kernel changes were checked against all 202,048 output logits.

## Verification performed

```sh
make -j8 ds4-bench

DS4_MUSE_NO_PROMPT_LOOKUP=1 ./ds4-bench --metal \
  -m /path/to/UD-IQ2_XXS/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-UD-IQ2_XXS-00001-of-00006.gguf \
  --chat-prompt-file /path/to/prompt.txt \
  --ctx-start 128 --ctx-max 128 --ctx-alloc 160 --gen-tokens 24
```

Current result: `gen_tps 18.27`, `gen_steady_tps 18.30`.

The full Muse benchmark and optimization record is in `docs/MUSE_SPARK.md`.

## Where contributions would help

1. A draft model distilled against this exact IQ2 target to improve speculative acceptance.
2. A Muse-specific IQ2 expert decode kernel that preserves values and left-to-right accumulation order.
3. Exact dense Q8/Q6 improvements that produce an end-to-end decode gain.
4. Reproduction on other Apple Silicon systems with at least 256 GiB unified memory.

title: Fix Engram unmapping on larger host pages
body:
Engram tables are read with `pread`, but the loader currently requires their file offsets to be aligned to the host page size. A GGUF with smaller alignment can therefore be rejected on a 64 KiB-page host.

Round the end of the resident tensors up to the host page size and unmap from that boundary. Require the disk-only tables to start after it. This preserves the resident mapping and still rejects tables overlapping resident data or its final mapped page.

The sparse fixture covers aligned and unaligned table offsets, both shared and private mappings, an unmapped disk region, a decoded `pread` row, and both invalid overlap cases.

Validation:

- macOS, Apple M5 Max, 16,384-byte pages: the new unaligned fixture fails against the old loader (exit 1). With the fix, `make clean && make -j6`, `make -j6 test-deepseek41-gguf`, and `make cpu` pass.
- Linux/DGX Spark, aarch64, 65,536-byte pages: `make -j6 test-deepseek41-gguf` and `make cpu` pass. The test prints `host page size: 65536` and `V4.1 disk-only GGUF extent: PASS`.
- `git diff --check` and engine LSP diagnostics are clean.

These are header-only sparse GGUF fixtures with a small F32 resident tensor and encoded disk-only Engram rows. No model inference or GPU allocation is performed. Full-model CUDA/Metal inference, distributed inference, and throughput were not tested for this loader-only change.

title: Handle quantized embeddings in non-Apple V4.1 prefill
body:
The non-Apple V4.1 layer-prefill path calls `ds4_gpu_embed_tokens_hc_tensor` unconditionally. That routine reads F16 weights, so a quantized `token_embd` is interpreted with the wrong layout even though scalar embedding already dispatches by tensor type.

Keep the fused gather/HC expansion for F16. For quantized embeddings, gather and dequantize the rows into the existing batch scratch tensor, then repeat those rows across the HC lanes. The normal Apple prefill path is unchanged.

The new `tests/test_deepseek41_prefill --embedding` check is a GPU unit test, not a model run. It uses a tiny synthetic model containing F16 and Q8_0 embedding tensors, nonconsecutive token IDs, row counts 1/3/5, all HC lanes, and a trailing canary. It calls the same helper used by non-Apple prefill. The F16-only dispatch passes the F16 cases but fails the Q8_0 case.

Validation:

- macOS / Apple M5 Max: default `make -j6`, `make -j6 tests/test_deepseek41_prefill`, `./tests/test_deepseek41_prefill --dispatch`, and `make cpu` pass without compiler warnings. The embedding helper and its new test entry are non-Apple only.
- DGX Spark / GB10 sm_121, CUDA 13.4.2: `make -j6 CUDA_ARCH=sm_121 all tests/test_deepseek41_prefill`, `./tests/test_deepseek41_prefill --dispatch`, and the embedding unit under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 99` pass. All F16/Q8_0 values are exact for row counts 1/3/5, the canaries are intact, and sanitizer reports zero errors.
- `git diff --check` and engine LSP diagnostics are clean.

The fixture uses the existing bounded device-copy mode for its small synthetic model. An initial mapping-based setup hit the GB10 driver's unsupported `cudaHostRegister` probe, which sanitizer reports as an API error even though the backend falls back and the numeric checks pass. Host registration/fallback behavior is not changed by this PR.

Untested: ROCm, tensor parallelism, distributed inference, a full GGUF with quantized token embeddings, model quality, and end-to-end throughput. No upstream-compatible quantized-embedding GGUF was loaded for this check. F16 still reaches the same fused backend call; its kernels and arithmetic are unchanged.

title: CUDA/Metal next-token distribution drift and MoE selection changes on V4.1
body:
I compared CUDA on a DGX Spark with Metal on an M5 Max using the same DeepSeek V4.1 Flash abliterated Q1 GGUF. Short-prefix top-1 tokens match, but full next-token distributions differ enough to change routed-expert selections.

This is a **fork-build report**, not a claim that upstream currently supports IQ1_S or that the same end-to-end result has been reproduced with an upstream-supported GGUF. Source and standalone quantization tests are on [audreyt/ds4, cuda-v41-q1-gb10](https://github.com/audreyt/ds4/tree/cuda-v41-q1-gb10), commit `d2f3696fb2e124d7a83f8c0c91684022d1f89d17`.

### Setup

- CUDA: NVIDIA GB10, sm_121, driver 615.78.08, CUDA 13.4.2, Linux aarch64 with 64 KiB pages, SSD-streamed experts.
- Metal: Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, resident weights with disk-only Engram.
- Model: `audreyt/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Abliterated-GGUF`, file `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Abliterated-Q1.gguf`, SHA-256 `d302c2caf7f12766eba2c431fc852261ddd0bf4d30b2760697d6036dac0f3cbd`. IQ1_S routed experts; Q5_K/Q6_K dense weights.
- Both backends used the same prompt, context allocation 512, no generated tokens, and full-vocabulary logits (129,280 entries) after 32/64/128 prompt tokens.

### Distribution comparison

KL is `KL(Metal || CUDA)` in nats. The acceptance threshold was fixed at 0.01 before inspecting the CUDA results.

| Prefix tokens | Metal/CUDA argmax | Top-10 overlap | Centered logit RMSE | KL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32 | 2395 / 2395 | 9/10 | 0.789642 | 0.246143 |
| 64 | 88773 / 88773 | 8/10 | 0.664158 | 0.006920 |
| 128 | 56518 / 56518 | 10/10 | 0.505251 | 0.072150 |

Forcing Metal through scalar layers with `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_LAYER_PREFILL=1` did not restore agreement: KL was 0.392525 / 0.100597 / 0.042087, with the same three argmax tokens. Different short-prefix prefill partitioning is therefore not a sufficient explanation.

### Layer 6: routing amplifies an existing difference

At token position 31, I dumped scalar-layer outputs on both backends. Layer 6 has the same tensor types and dimensions as layers 3–5. It is not the first MoE layer, has no Engram injection, and does not introduce a new compression or quantization type.

| Checkpoint | Relative RMS, `||CUDA-Metal|| / ||Metal||` |
| --- | --- |
| Layer input HC residual | 3.79% |
| Post-attention HC residual | 5.98% |
| FFN input | 6.71% |
| Shared expert output | 7.80% |
| Routed expert output | 40.21% |
| Final HC residual | 18.98% |

Two of six selected experts change:

```text
Metal: 44, 26, 122, 195, 138, 36
CUDA:  44, 26, 122, 368, 138, 315
```

The leading amplification is routed MoE selection. The router uses F32 weights, but its input already differs by 6.7%; changing the selected experts produces a much larger output difference.

CUDA MMVQ quantizes activations to Q8_1, whereas the Metal IQ1 vector kernel consumes float activations directly. Q8_1 also stores a half-precision block sum. A synthetic integer-activation fixture exposed rounding of sums above 2048; using balanced pairs (scale 1, sum 0) isolates packed-weight arithmetic and compaction, which then compare exactly against the scalar reference.

Activation rounding is a leading upstream candidate for the accumulated drift, not a proven exclusive cause. The measurements do not establish that all attention, accumulation-order, and backend rounding differences have been excluded. I have not treated matching top-1 tokens or exact packed-weight fixtures as a distribution-parity pass.

### Official continuation set

The tracked `deepseek-v4.1-flash-20260910/manifest.tsv` has 17 cases and 141 target tokens, including prompts through 16,385 tokens. Results use normal backend defaults.

| Build | Average NLL | Top-1 agreement with stored API reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 CUDA SSD, fork | 1.005161445 | 113/141 |
| Same Q1 Metal, fork | 0.979659680 | 113/141 |
| Supplied Q2 reference | 0.412 | 128/141 |

The Q2 result was supplied rather than rerun or hash-matched here. It does not isolate quantization from every other possible difference in those artifacts. Equal CUDA/Metal agreement counts also do not mean they agree at every target position.

### Suggested direction

A float-activation GEMV implementation for parity-sensitive quantized paths would provide a useful comparison against Q8_1 MMVQ. Comparing the same layer inputs before routing would help separate activation-rounding effects from later accumulation and selection effects. There is no existing IQ1/Q5/Q6 dequantize-then-GEMM switch in the fork that isolates this difference.

I have not forced identical expert IDs or relaxed the KL threshold. Either would hide the observed failure rather than explain it.

### Existing upstream SSD compaction and fork follow-up

Current upstream already has `cuda_stream_compact_prefill`, introduced in `a04f46f`, and invokes it for supported streamed IQ2/Q2 and MXFP4 batches. The fork's added Q1 dispatch bypassed that helper. This is a **fork-side follow-up for audreyt/ds4**: route Q1 through the existing compactor instead of maintaining a separate lower-level Q1 staging path. No upstream compaction change is proposed.

I validated the existing upstream helper on GB10 with a one-off white-box test: IQ2_XXS gate/up, Q2_K down, 13,159 cache slots, four active slots including 13,106/13,107 across the former chunk boundary, N=16,384, M=37, K=5120, and two selected slots. Packed weights, IDs and all output values match independent scalar references exactly. A dense four-ID run also matches exactly. `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 99` reports zero errors.

Single-run timings under sanitizer instrumentation, including host launch/synchronization and compact staging but excluding reference comparisons:

| ID space | Raw MMQ | Existing helper + compact MMQ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dense, four slots | 0.823199 s | 0.757797 s |
| Sparse, 13,159 slots | 5.193988 s | 0.755221 s |

These are instrumented fixture timings, not native inference benchmarks. Production upstream files were unchanged.

For context only, the **Q1 fork build** improved 4K prefill from 84.6 to 157.6 tok/s and the 8K-to-16K incremental segment from 121.9 to 329.2 tok/s after its compaction work. The 16,383-token case fell from 627.3 to 52.1 seconds with unchanged NLL (0.701125). Those numbers are not an upstream before/after result.

### Reproduction

On the fork branch, use the GGUF above and the same plain-text prompt on both hosts:

```sh
./ds4-bench --cuda --ssd-streaming --model "$MODEL" \
  --prompt-file prompt.txt --ctx-start 32 --ctx-max 128 --step-mul 2 \
  --ctx-alloc 512 --gen-tokens 0 --dump-frontier-logits-dir cuda-logits

./ds4-bench --metal --model "$MODEL" \
  --prompt-file prompt.txt --ctx-start 32 --ctx-max 128 --step-mul 2 \
  --ctx-alloc 512 --gen-tokens 0 --dump-frontier-logits-dir metal-logits

gguf-tools/quality-testing/score_official "$MODEL" \
  gguf-tools/quality-testing/deepseek-v4.1-flash-20260910/manifest.tsv \
  result.tsv 17408 --ssd-streaming
```

Omit `--ssd-streaming` for the Metal scorer. The prompt was:

```text
The observatory stood on a quiet hill above the town. Each evening, Mira opened the dome and checked the telescope before the first stars appeared. She kept a notebook beside the controls, recording the weather, the time, and anything unusual in the sky. One autumn night she noticed a faint light moving slowly between two familiar stars. Rather than announce a discovery, she checked the instrument, compared earlier images, and asked another observatory to look at the same patch of sky.

Careful measurement depends on comparison. A useful experiment changes one thing at a time, records its conditions, and keeps enough detail for someone else to repeat it. When two instruments disagree, the disagreement is evidence to investigate, not a reason to discard the less convenient reading. Precision describes how consistently measurements repeat; accuracy describes how close they are to the quantity being measured. Both matter, and neither can be established by confidence alone.

In a computer, memory and arithmetic work together. Moving data can cost more time than multiplying it. A small representation can reduce that movement, but its approximation must be checked against an independent calculation. The first successful answer proves less than a set of repeatable measurements across several inputs. Good engineering records both successes and limits so that the next person knows what has actually been demonstrated.
```

Not tested: same-GGUF end-to-end parity on unmodified upstream quantization paths, other GPUs, ROCm, tensor parallelism, or distributed inference.

The separate loader and batched-embedding correctness changes are in [#1247](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1247) and [#1248](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1248). Neither PR claims to resolve this distribution drift.

title: fix typo
server: stream Qwen tool-call arguments over OpenAI SSE
body:
Qwen tool calls were buffered until generation finished in OpenAI streaming responses: the live translator recognized DSML invoke tags but not Qwen's `<function=...>` / `<parameter=...>` syntax. Long tool arguments therefore arrived all at once instead of incrementally.

This change adds Qwen syntax to the live translator and streams schema-declared string arguments as they arrive. It strips Qwen's framing newlines and buffers other values until their closing tag so JSON values and inferred strings receive the appropriate representation. Tool markers and syntax descriptions are shared across the relevant parsing paths.

For responses containing repeated `<tool_call>` blocks, the first call streams incrementally and the remaining calls are emitted at completion, without replaying the first call or adding a leading comma to the remaining-call array.

Adds regression tests for partial tags and argument deltas, multiple calls, framing newlines, and enum-only string parameters.

Validation on Apple M5 Max (arm64), macOS 26.4, default Metal build, in a fresh worktree:
- `make -j4 ds4_test` — passed
- `./ds4_test --server` — passed
- `make -j4` — passed (all default binaries)
- `git diff --check` — passed before commit

The server unit suite is model-free and passed without test failures. The test build reported two unused-symbol warnings in unchanged `ds4_metal.m` code (`metal4_disabled` and `ds4_gpu_compile_tensor_probe`).

Live-model validation was also performed during development on this machine with `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q2.gguf`, Metal, and `--mtp --mtp-draft 5` (the Q8_0 vision projector was loaded, but these were text-only requests). A Node SSE client sent streaming chat-completion requests through the local proxy on port 8090 to ds4-server on port 8022, using a `write` tool with string `path` and `content` properties and `reasoning_effort=none`.

- A prompt requesting a 300-line Python file, including Chinese text, quotes, backslashes, entity-like text, and emoji: 37.6 s, 2,382 parsed delta events. Accumulated argument length grew from 3,444 to 7,217 to 8,737; final `JSON.parse` succeeded with `path` and `content` keys.
- After restarting the service, a prompt requesting a 120-line Python file: 25.0 s, 1,567 parsed delta events. Argument length grew from 3,354 to 5,133; final `JSON.parse` succeeded with the same keys.
- The recorded progress samples reported `idle=0.0s`. Lengths above are JavaScript string lengths, not UTF-8 byte counts.

The first live request was run with:
```sh
URL=http://127.0.0.1:8090/v1 TOOLS=1 MAX_TOKENS=6000 REASONING=none BEAT_MS=15000 \
  PROMPT='用 write 工具写一个 300 行的 Python 文件到 /tmp/pi-sse-repro/out/e2e.py：要包含中文注释、单双引号、反斜杠、& < > 实体、emoji 😀，不要省略。' \
  node /tmp/pi-sse-repro/client.mjs
```
The client was a local diagnostic script, not a committed test. These live runs validated incremental streaming after the syntax-table refactor, before the subsequent multiple-call and value-normalization fixes. Those later fixes are covered by the server regression tests run on the submitted version.

This change concerns server-side tool-call projection, not inference kernels. No before/after throughput benchmark, CPU build, or CUDA/SSD/distributed runtime validation is claimed. During earlier investigation, invoking `./ds4_test` without arguments twice caused OOM, as reported by the contributor; subsequent validation used `--server` to avoid loading an additional model. Those full-suite attempts did not complete. Three narrowly scoped server regression tests pass on the submitted version.

title: Makefile: link ds4_rocm_unavailable.o into test_mxfp4_rocm
body:
`make test-mxfp4-rocm`, the model-free routed-kernel check suggested in docs/STRIX_HALO.md, fails to link at 5379c1c:

```
ds4_rocm.o: in function `ds4_gpu_dsv41_attention_output_tp_batch':
ds4_deepseek41_cuda.cuh:791: undefined reference to `ds4_gpu_attention_output_low_q8_rows_exact_tensor'
ds4_deepseek41_cuda.cuh:796: undefined reference to `ds4_gpu_matmul_q8_0_kslice_rows_tensor'
```

`ds4_rocm.cu` includes `ds4_deepseek41_cuda.cuh` (since 4c64ae4, I think; I didn't bisect), and both symbols are defined only in `ds4_rocm_unavailable.o`. The ROCm binaries and `tests/test_deepseek41_rocm` link that object, but the `tests/test_mxfp4_rocm` rule does not. This adds it. Only the test link rule changes, so no inference binary is affected.

Tested on a Bosgame M5 (Strix Halo, Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 128 GB), ROCm 7.14.1 (`amdrocm-core-devel7.14-gfx1151`, Fedora 44 container) and ROCm 7.1 (Ubuntu 26.04 packages):

```
make strix-halo
make test-mxfp4-rocm
...
MXFP4 ROCm tokens=512 out max_abs=0.000112534 at=9542 max_tol_ratio=0.301675 at=15718 failures=0/2097152
MXFP4 ROCm variant DS4_ROCM_MXFP4_DOWN_RGROUP=4: bitwise OK
MXFP4 ROCm routed MoE: PASS
```

Before the change, the link fails as above on both ROCm versions. The test needs no model. The `test_deepseek41_rocm` rule also links `ds4_rocm_compat.o`. I kept this change minimal because the test passes without it, but I can add it for symmetry if you prefer.

title: Compile ds4_cuda.cu as C++17 like the other CUDA objects
body:
Ciao Salvatore,
ds4_cuda.o is the only nvcc rule in the Makefile without -std=c++17. Without -std, nvcc uses the host compiler's default C++ dialect. That default is older than C++17 before GCC 11 and Clang 16. CUDA 13 ships CCCL 3, which requires C++17, so with those host compilers the build stops at #include <cub/block/block_radix_sort.cuh>:

cccl/cub/util_cpp_dialect.cuh:65:8: error: #error CUB requires at least C++17. Define CCCL_IGNORE_DEPRECATED_CPP_DIALECT to suppress this message.

This happens, for example, with the system GCC on RHEL 8 (8.5) and Debian 11 (10.2). This PR adds the same -std=c++17 that the mmq and kernel objects already use.

Tested: make cuda CUDA_ARCH=sm_90 with CUDA 13.4.1 and GCC 8.5.0 fails before this change and builds after it. No runtime code changes.

title: Link the ROCm MXFP4 and GLM tests against ROCm compat and stub

title: Pre-tokenizer splits differ from the HF tokenizer for CJK punctuation + newline and for runs of spaces (DeepSeek V4 Flash)
body:
**Version:** `main` at 5379c1c, DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 MXFP4 GGUF, macOS (M5 Ultra).
**Reference:** the official HF `tokenizer.json` for the same model, via `tokenizers`.

ds4's tokenization matches HF exactly on English text we tried, but diverges on some Chinese / whitespace patterns. On our mixed zh/en long texts the token count differs by up to ~3%.

**1. Full-width colon followed by a newline**

Text excerpt around the first difference (from a longer document): `…以下內容：\n今天天氣晴朗，…`

- ds4: `['以下', '內容', '：', '\n', '今天', '天氣', '晴朗', '，']`
- HF:  `['以下', '內容', '：\n', '今天', '天氣', '晴朗', '，']`

HF's pre-tokenizer keeps `：\n` together and it maps to a single token; ds4 emits two.

**2. Runs of spaces before CJK**

Text excerpt around the first difference (three spaces): `…22。   多個空白   然後…`

- ds4: `['22', '。', '  ', ' ', '多', '個', '空白', '  ', ...]`
- HF:  `['22', '。', '   ', '多', '個', '空白', '   ', '然後']`

HF keeps the three-space run as one token; ds4 splits it into two-space + one-space.

Why it matters: prompts tokenized differently from training can shift model behavior slightly, and token counts (context budgeting, KV-cache prefix matching against prompts produced by other HF-based tools) won't line up.

Happy to share the comparison script and test texts if useful.

title: Add OdinLink (odl_tb5) TP transport: --transport odl
body:
> **Resubmission of #1018** — I accidentally deleted my fork, which closed that PR (its head repo is gone; it was **not** merged). This is the identical branch and head commit (`93a214c`); the review discussion on #1018 still applies.

Adds `--transport odl` to the two-node tensor-parallel data plane: the OdinLink (odl_tb5) Thunderbolt RDMA userspace library, loaded with `dlopen` at runtime exactly like the verbs stack — no link-time dependency, and builds without OdinLink installed fall back to TCP at zero cost. `auto` now prefers odl over verbs over tcp.

- Protocol v15 (over upstream's v14): the hello's pad word becomes `odl_ok`, negotiated like `rdma_ok`.
- Each rank receives on its own stream id; a zero-byte `ODL_READY` frame at slab attach is the rendezvous (a send to a stream the peer has not opened yet is dropped by its kernel demux).
- Gate exchanges: one `stream_send` per direction (the kernel fragments at 4024-byte frames internally); receive side runs `stream_recv` on an `O_NONBLOCK` fd with the same peer-death sampling and gate deadline as the verbs CQ poll loop.
- Batch/big gates ride a symmetric bulk swap with a 4 MiB send-ahead window (bounded by the kernel frame ring).
- Loss recovery (second commit, `51f2b49`): every stream message carries a 16-byte header and receivers request the chunks the driver dropped; details in the section below.
- Batch and big gates skip the TCP header rendezvous (third commit, `15b6d6b`): the reliable exchange numbers its rounds and validates chunk sizes, so the header round trip only added ~150 us per gate (harness batch gate 265 -> 104 us; about 6 ms of a GLM MTP verify cycle).
- No vendor header dependency: an 8-entry function table mirrors `odl_tb5.h` signatures through void pointers.
- `tp_odl_test.c` included: a model-free transport harness that drives the real `ds4_tp.o` on both ranks with a synthetic identity, verifies payload integrity, and prints latency stats.

## Test evidence (per CONTRIBUTING.md)

Machine: 2x AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 128 GB), Fedora 44, Thunderbolt 5 direct link, OdinLink-Five driver `odl_tb5`, ROCm build (`make strix-halo`).

Transport-level A/B on both ranks (24 KB gate vectors, payload integrity verified):

```
RESULT transport=odl vec=24576B iters=3000 min=6.4 p50=30.1 p90=41.9 p99=52.4 max=675.8 mean=33.1 us
RESULT transport=tcp vec=24576B iters=3000 min=17.2 p50=31.0 p90=38.2 p99=60.5 max=119.4 mean=32.3 us
BATCH transport=odl rows=8 bytes=196608 rtt=290.7 us
BIG   transport=odl bytes=2097152 rtt=1843.6 us   (~1.1 GB/s per direction)
```

A 50,000-gate soak is clean (no desync, no corruption). Notably, TCP over `thunderbolt_net` shows load-dependent variance (p50 between 31 and 262 us across runs taken while a large background download ran) while odl stays at ~30 us throughout — kernel bypass removes the tail under system load.

End-to-end (GLM 5.3 Flash Q4_K across the same two boxes, short-prompt exact prefill + decode, ctx 8192): prefill 25.8 t/s on odl vs 18.4 t/s on tcp; generation 8.7 t/s on both. (Decode turned out to be memory-bandwidth-bound on the replicated BF16 KDA attention weights rather than compute-bound; the kernel-level breakdown is in #1024.)

## Loss recovery (added after the initial submission, `51f2b49`)

In production the first version died twice in one afternoon: once in an MTP verify block, once 4096 tokens into an 11k-token ds4-server prefill. Both times dmesg on the receiving rank shows `odl_tb5: RX CRC error ... frame dropped` followed by `fragment gap ... dropping message`: when one Thunderbolt frame of a message fails CRC, the driver drops the *whole* message and the sender is never told. The gate then parks both ranks on their spin kernels (100% GPU) until the timeout and the TP session is dead for good. On this pair the link negotiates 10 Gb/s per lane (2 lanes) and drops a frame every few GB, so any long prefill was doomed.

The fix keeps the stream API and adds recovery on top:

- Every message carries a 16-byte header: magic, kind (`DATA`/`NACK`), chunk index, exchange sequence (both ranks number exchanges identically).
- A receiver asks for the first missing chunk as soon as a later index reveals the gap, or after a retry interval without progress: 2 ms for gate vectors, 50 ms for bulk (lockstep skew is far below both).
- A sender keeps the framed copies of its current and previous exchange. Lockstep bounds the peer's lag to one exchange (it cannot finish N+1 without our N+1 data, which we only send once we finished N), so those two buffers always cover a request. Chunks of the next exchange that arrive while the current one still misses data are parked and replayed.
- Requests are served from the exchange loop and, for a rank that is idle or waiting on the control channel (worker between commands, leader waiting for an ack, either side in the big-gate header handshake), from a polling wait that now fronts those reads. Without this an idle rank would leave a peer stuck one exchange behind until its deadline.
- No extra round trip on the fast path: a decode gate costs one 16 KB frame copy per side. `DS4_TP_ODL_DROP_TEST=N` drops every Nth data send as a diagnostic for this path; off unless set.

Harness over the real link (16 KB gate vectors, 3000 iterations, payload verified on every receive):

```
no drops:                 RESULT p50=29.0 p90=32.3 p99=52.7 us   BIG 2 MiB rtt=2196.7 us (1843.6 before: the header/frame copies)
DROP_TEST=5, both ranks:  RESULT p50=31.0 p90=2065.3 us, 751 drops -> 753 retransmissions, all payloads verified
DROP_TEST=3, leader only: RESULT p50=62.7 p90=2077.8 us, 1501 drops recovered, all payloads verified
no handshake (15b6d6b):    BATCH rows=8 rtt=104.3 us (264.6 before), gate p50 29.2 us unchanged
```

The p90 under injected loss is the 2 ms detection interval; the bulk case with the last chunk dropped waits the 50 ms interval.

End-to-end with the GLM-5.3-Flash TP setup of #1024 (2x gfx1151, odl, Q8-attention GGUF): decode 15.35 t/s without and 15.23 t/s with `DS4_TP_ODL_DROP_TEST=400` (12 dropped gate messages per rank recovered, greedy output byte-identical over 96 tokens); a 323-token prompt prefilled at 69.1 t/s without and 67.5 t/s with `DROP_TEST=50` (75 drops per rank recovered, output identical). Without injected drops the ranks still request a retransmission about once per second: a rank that reaches a gate more than the 2 ms interval late is asked as well, which costs a duplicate 16 KB send and nothing else, so the log prints only the first few and then every 100th request. With the batch/big-gate handshake removed the GLM MTP cycle went from 10.4 to 11.8 t/s and the 323-token prefill from 69 to 78 t/s (measurements in #1024).

Known limitation: bulk throughput is bounded by the odl stream API's per-fragment kernel path (~1.1 GB/s per direction, and the observed link speed above); the double-buffer DMA API should raise it and is left as future work. The full `make test` suite was not run for this change (needs the CPU test binary on hand); transport behavior was validated with the included harness on both ranks plus the end-to-end runs above.
