title: Enable GLM 5.3 tensor parallelism on the ROCm backend
body:
> **Resubmission of #1024** — I accidentally deleted my fork, which closed that PR (its head repo is gone; it was **not** merged). This is the identical branch and head commit (`5dc45b7`); the OdinLink transport it builds on is likewise resubmitted as #1256. The review discussion on #1024 still applies.

Enables GLM 5.3 (GLM_DSA family) on the two-node ROCm tensor-parallel backend from #813, then makes it fast enough to use. Before this, GLM TP never armed on ROCm: the GLM graph's TP initialization was guarded `#if defined(__APPLE__)`, so `tp_world` stayed 0 and every rank silently computed the full expert set against its half-resident weights (word salad, no error). With this PR, GLM-5.3-Flash Q4_K (177.76 GiB, unrunnable on one box) runs across two 128 GB Strix Halo boxes, including 47k-token contexts and ds4-server tool-call conversations.

Opt-in, like the backend itself: `DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1` on both ranks.

## Branch layout (stacked)

Integration lineage of `rocm-tensor-parallel` (#813) with upstream main merged in (`bd177c9`/`da15223`, `8025b22`, `0fff703`, `5dc45b7`). #813 stays at its original trunk point as the historical base (it shows conflicts with `main` and is not being rebased), so its ROCm TP transport is reviewable here; #835 and #1018 are kept mergeable on their own. Stack order: #813 → #835 → #1018 → this PR. Commits new here:

- Enablement: `ea7057d` merge fixups, `4dd3f4d` GLM TP on ROCm (the core change), `848fb67` lock static weight spans under streaming, `1a646f6` avoid the faulting Q4_K sorted down kernels, `682cdb4` restore the CPU build.
- Transport: `0e02528`, `4402b61`, `cb7cb70` verbs fixes (RDMA bulk-window reset, `DS4_TP_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS`, RC queue pairs, real `ibv_post_*` codes); `7598395` OdinLink loss recovery (same as #1018); `2a0977d` odl batch/big gates without the TCP header rendezvous (same as `15b6d6b` in #1018).
- Decode performance: `5272bda` pre-quantized k-slice Q8_0 matvec, `5b31f6d` gate arrive/wait split with the shared expert overlapping the FFN exchange, `b6f965b` vectorized small-output BF16 row matvec, `ebfe289` no periodic decode-stream flush on ROCm, `9b708e9` vocab-split output head, `50a3f9f` fewer and wider small launches, `5da2545` tiled long-context DSA kernels, `8f3505c` KDA attention split by heads, `4dac2b5` one-wave-per-row Q4_K expert gate/up kernel.
- Prefill performance: `10f5531` Q4_K routed experts through the vendored MMQ tensor-core GEMMs, `e9cfbde` indexer scores as batched f32 GEMMs, `e39e8dd` batch FFN big gate overlapped with the shared expert.
- Portability: `91ae988` guards the ROCm-only split gate wait (Metal and CUDA keep the single-call gate); the CPU build stub for the KDA state sync came in with `0fff703`.
- Disk KV cache under TP: `70b16d9` restores snapshots on both ranks (the leader restores, then streams the same payload to the worker over the control socket; before this a TP disk hit rebuilt both ranks with a full prefill, so a fresh 15k-token session took 123 s and now takes 4.3 s with a byte-identical answer); `5801a05` stages snapshots in the cache directory instead of /tmp (RAM-backed tmpfs, which OOM-killed the server once with a 6 GiB snapshot).

## Changes

- GLM graph TP init guard extended to `DS4_ROCM_BUILD`; the refusal gated behind `DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1`; GLM exempted from the Q8_0 output-head requirement (its head is replicated under TP).
- Streaming: operator-precedence fix in the ROCm GLM streaming gate; `mlock` of SSD static spans on ROCm and post-upload discards that skip locked spans (the GPU cannot fault file-backed pages back in).
- Q4_K sorted-pairs down GEMM routed through the proven per-pair kernel, `moe_sum` epilogue kept (see failures below).
- Decode path on ROCm TP: Q8 k-slice on prequantized activations; gate arrive/wait split; each rank projects half of the 154880-row head during single-token decode and the session merges the halves (off with `--mtp`); one launch for the KDA q/k/v projections and one for f_a/g_a/beta; 1024-lane float4 RMS norms; float4 router matvec.
- Long-context DSA layers: the indexed decode attention is now three kernels (a 16-key LDS tile scored against every head with RoPE applied once per key, a pv kernel handling all of the rank's heads per 128-key chunk, a chunk-order reduce), the indexer scorer runs one wave per key row. Old kernels stay as fallback (`DS4_ROCM_GLM_LEGACY_INDEXED_ATTN=1`). Kernel time per DSA layer 1000 + 776 us → 98 + 66 us.
- KDA head split (single-token decode only): each rank runs 32 of the 64 KDA heads (half-row projections, the conv + delta-rule recurrence on its half of the layer state, output projection K-sliced into the layer's ATTN gate, now in the gate schedule: 87 gates per token). Replicated KDA paths (prefill/verify rows, batched-session decode, session save via the new `DS4_TP_FRAME_GLM_KDA_SYNC` frame) re-gather the state halves first with one big-gate swap per layer. Off with `--mtp`, SSD streaming, an unsupported `kda_output` type, or `DS4_GLM_TP_KDA_HEAD_SPLIT_DISABLE=1` on both ranks. BF16 gets `ds4_gpu_glm53_matmul_bf16_kslice`.
- Prefill experts: Q4_K batches of 16+ tokens compact the rank's owned (token, slot) pairs and run gate/up and down as `ds4_mmq_q4_K_moe_pair` / `ds4_mmq_q4_K_moe` calls with one expert per row, then the existing scatter + `moe_sum` epilogue (gfx1151 default, `DS4_ROCM_MMQ_Q4K=0` keeps the tile kernels). The tile kernels ran at a few percent of both roofs.
- Prefill indexer: the GLM-5.3 indexer scores (every query against every pooled key, 34% of a 24.7k-token prefill in a one-block-per-pair kernel) run as strided-batched f32 hipBLAS GEMMs over the heads plus a reduce kernel for relu, per-head weights and the causal pooled mask; same f32 products, `DS4_ROCM_GLM_INDEXER_GEMM_CHECK=1` reports a relative deviation of ~3e-7 against the block kernel. `DS4_ROCM_GLM_INDEXER_GEMM=0` restores it.
- Batch FFN under TP: the routed-partial swap is kicked before the shared expert is encoded and waited on after it (`ds4_gpu_tp_big_gate_kick_nowait` / `ds4_gpu_tp_big_gate_wait_encode`); payload and add unchanged.

## Test evidence (per CONTRIBUTING.md)

Machine: 2x AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 128 GB unified), Fedora 44, ROCm, Thunderbolt 5 direct link (odl transport from #1018; rdma/tcp also work). Model: GLM-5.3-Flash Q4_K (`glm53-q4` GGUF, sha256 c7a0d950...). Build on both boxes:

```sh
make strix-halo -j32 CFLAGS="-O3 -ffast-math -g -march=native -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -fPIC -D_GNU_SOURCE -fno-finite-math-only" \
  ROCM_LDLIBS="-lm -pthread -lamdhip64 -lhipblas -lhipblaslt -lrocblas"
make cpu   # also verified clean
```

```sh
# box2                                                  # box1
env DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1 ~/ds4/ds4 -m GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf --tensor-parallel --role worker \
  --coordinator 10.0.2.1 7300 --transport odl --ctx 8192
env DS4_ROCM_GLM_TP=1 ~/ds4/ds4 -m GLM-5.3-Flash-Q4_K.gguf --tensor-parallel --role coordinator \
  --listen 10.0.2.1 7300 --transport odl --ctx 8192 -p "<prompt>"     # or --prompt-file
```

Correctness runs, all clean (no faults, desyncs or timeouts on either rank): short exact-prefill prompts ("two plus two" → "Four"); 227- and 323-token prompts with accurate summaries; a 47,288-token prompt at ctx 49152 with an accurate summary of the fed source file; ds4-server with `--batched-session 4` (two-turn weather-tool conversation with KV reuse, the same under a concurrent generation, a 6,181-token multi-chunk tool prompt reusing 6,192 cached tokens); after the head split, a server session with three turns, two concurrent requests, a follow-up, and an 810-token conversation saved to the KV disk cache.

Numerical checks: `DS4_ROCM_GLM_DSA_CHECK=1` and `DS4_GLM_TP_KDA_CHECK=1` run the previous or replicated kernels next to the new ones on the same inputs; over ~1000 (DSA) and 2800 (KDA) layer calls per rank the relative L2 deviations stay at 1e-7 to 1e-6, no non-finite values. Greedy texts flip at near-tie tokens against earlier builds (changed accumulation order; int8 activations in the k-slice path), with both continuations correct; the 45-token test prompt reproduces earlier outputs byte for byte across several builds. The MMQ prefill path was checked by running the same prompts with the path on and off.

## Performance

2x gfx1151 over odl, greedy. "Q8-attention GGUF" is a data-only requant of the official file (KDA projections + head to Q8_0) used to measure the code with the BF16 tensors out of the way; it is not part of the PR.

| Test | first submission | now |
|---|---|---|
| official Q4_K GGUF, 45-token prompt decode | 8.9 t/s | 13.1 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, 45-token prompt decode | 15.4 t/s | 19.4 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, decode after 24,764 tokens | 11.8 t/s | 19.0 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, decode after 44,267 tokens | 11.1 t/s | 15.4 t/s (at `5da2545`, not re-measured since) |
| Q8-attention GGUF, prefill 323 / 2,500 / 24,764 tokens | 69 / 72 / 52 t/s | 146 / 140 / 122 t/s |
| Q8-attention GGUF, MTP 1 draft | 10.4 t/s | 11.6 t/s (plain decode remains faster) |
| row-gate exchange (odl), average | 172 us | 86-106 us |

Where the time went, from roctracer timelines on both ranks: the first decode step (114 ms on the official GGUF) was 57 ms of BF16 KDA projections streamed at 160 GB/s, 13 ms of experts, 8.7 ms of gate spin, 5 ms of an 80 GB/s k-slice kernel, ~17 ms of ~1,500 small launches. After the rounds above a Q8-model step is ~52 ms: ~35 ms of memory-bound kernels near the 227 GB/s roof, ~6 ms of gates (84 exchanges of ~90 us, the odl round trip plus rank skew), ~4 ms of launch gaps, ~6 ms of small kernels. Prefill on a 2,500-token prompt spent 59% of its time in the Q4_K expert tile kernels before `10f5531`; at 24.7k the indexer scoring kernel was another 34% before `e9cfbde`. What remains of a 24.7k prefill (~200 s): MMQ expert GEMMs ~47 s, the exposed part of the big-gate exchanges ~20 s, the sequential KDA prefill recurrence 23 s, hipBLAS attention and dense GEMMs ~70 s.

Two intermediate pv-kernel designs for the long-context attention both sat at 200-240 us per layer: the scattered KV rows come from DRAM every token and both designs kept the same number of loads in flight per CU; reading each row once for all heads over 16 blocks brought it to 68 us.

## Transport reliability (`7598395`)

The OdinLink transport lost whole 1 MiB gate messages whenever a Thunderbolt frame failed CRC (`odl_tb5: RX CRC error ... dropping message`), which parked both ranks on their spin kernels until the 300 s bulk timeout and killed the session (seen 4096 tokens into an 11k-token ds4-server prefill). The loss-recovery commit reviewed in #1018 (per-message headers, receiver-driven retransmission from retained frames, idle ranks serving requests from their control-channel waits) is cherry-picked here. Validated with `DS4_TP_ODL_DROP_TEST`: 15.35 vs 15.23 t/s decode with every 400th gate message dropped (output byte-identical), 69.1 vs 67.5 t/s prefill with every 50th dropped (output identical).

## Speculative decoding (MTP)

Works with two-rank TP (CLI and ds4-server, 226 tokens to 47k, tool-call conversations) with no code beyond this PR; runtime settings: `--mtp` on both ranks, `DS4_GLM_MTP_DRAFTS=1`, `--batched-session 1` on ds4-server. It remains a net slowdown here: the 2-row verify span costs about twice a plain decode step and draft agreement stays below break-even. Default-off is right for this hardware. The KDA head split and the vocab-split head turn themselves off with `--mtp`.

## Notable failures root-caused on the way

1. **Q4_K sorted-pairs down-projection fault.** Batch prefills of 32+ tokens aborted both ranks with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION` (surfacing as "GLM TP batch gate failed" in ds4-server). Stage-skipping isolated it to the sorted/tile down kernels (`moe_down_q4K_expert_tile{4,8}_row32`, `moe_down_q4K_sorted_qwarp32`); every input validates clean and the per-pair kernel reads the same weights without faulting. `1a646f6` routes the sorted-path down GEMM through the per-pair kernel and keeps the `moe_sum` epilogue for q4k (without it, batches of 128+ tokens silently dropped the MoE output). Why the tile down kernels fault is still open (possibly related to #890 / #998 / #608 / #595); with `10f5531` the prefill down projection runs through MMQ anyway.
2. **Static-weight pageout under streaming**, fixed by the mlock extension and discard guards in `848fb67`.

## Not done / caveats

- Balancing the routed experts by splitting each expert's FFN dimension across ranks: the Q4_K `down` matrices' K-halves are strided per row, so it needs whole `down` matrices per rank or a ~27 GB repack at load.
- Prefill stays replicated for the KDA layers (a split would need a Q8 K-slice GEMM on ROCm and 34 more big gates per chunk).
- The KV disk-cache restore of a session under TP was not exercised after the KDA head split (saves were; the restore path clears the split flag).
- Not run: the full `make test` suite (needs the CPU test fixtures); everything above was validated end-to-end on real hardware on both ranks.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: kvstore: skip store attempts when the session has no checkpoint
body:
## Summary

`ds4_kvstore_store_live_prefix_text()` renders the prompt text for a store, hashes it, and only then asks the session to stage its KV payload. When the session has not captured a checkpoint yet, staging cannot succeed and the attempt is logged as a failure:

```
kv cache skipped tokens=147568 reason=continued because KV payload staging failed: session has no valid checkpoint to stage
```

That state is routine rather than an error: a continued-store frontier is crossed by an ordinary prefill or decode step, and the graph state only becomes checkpointable at the next drain. Each such attempt renders and SHA-1s the whole prompt (~486 KB here) for a store that cannot happen.

## Change

One early guard in `ds4_kvstore_store_live_prefix_text()`:

```c
if (!ds4_session_checkpoint_valid(session)) return false;
```

Sessions that do have a checkpoint take the unchanged path: same store, same eviction accounting, same successful store at the frontier. No retry and no on-demand checkpoint capture — taking one just to satisfy a store would change graph timing and belongs in its own change with its own measurement.

## Evidence

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (IQ2_XXS/Q2_K), Apple M4 Max, 128 GB, `--ctx 400000 --ssd-streaming --ssd-streaming-cache-experts 7336`, `temperature 0`, `seed 1234`, 512 generated tokens, prompt of 480.026 characters (~147.6k tokens).

Before (one cold+warm pair, 122 such lines):

```
kv cache skipped tokens=81920 reason=continued because KV payload staging failed: session has no valid checkpoint to stage
...
kv cache skipped tokens=147574 reason=continued because KV payload staging failed: session has no valid checkpoint to stage
kv cache stored tokens=147574 trimmed=0 reason=continued size=912.24 MiB save=232.4 ms
kv cache hit text tokens=147574 quant=2 load=182.9 ms
```

After (three requests: warm hit, cold with a fresh prompt identity, warm hit of that identity):

```
13:15:47 kv cache stored tokens=147575 trimmed=0 reason=continued size=912.25 MiB save=264.3 ms
13:16:27 kv cache stored tokens=148087 trimmed=0 reason=evict key=token-text size=915.38 MiB save=129.0 ms
13:16:27 kv cache hit text tokens=147575 text=486352 quant=2 load=185.2 ms
```

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `skipped … staging failed` lines | 122 | 0 |
| continued store at the frontier | 232.4 ms | 264.3 ms (still fires) |
| warm load | 182.9 ms | 185.2 ms |
| TTFT warm / cold / warm on the new identity | 0.97 s / 419.9 s / — | 0.26 s / 439.3 s / 0.65 s |

The cold run on a fresh prompt identity is the regression check: the store at 147.575 still happens and the next request loads it, so the guard removes only attempts that could never succeed.

The line is most frequent with PR #903 applied locally (it reaches the frontier per token instead of only on exact multiples); the guard is independent of that change and also silences the single attempt per frontier that the current `live_tokens % step == 0` schedule produces.

## Tests

- server unit tests (`-DDS4_SERVER_TEST`, built from this branch): `ds4-server tests: ok`
- `tests/test_deepseek41_metal` on this base: fails at `quantization mode=3 index=5428: 11.25 != 7.5`. That is unrelated to the change and is fixed by PR #1234 (`metal: use exact divisions in the V4.1 FP4 activation quantizer`), which is not in `main` yet; the failure is identical with the guard reverted, and the Metal path itself is untouched by this diff.

## Not changed

No retry when no checkpoint exists: if that is wanted, the store site should take a checkpoint deliberately and the effect on prefill/decode timing should be measured separately.

title: Pipeline V4.1 single-host decode command buffers
body:
## What

Single-host V4.1 decode waits for every layer's command buffer before encoding
the next one. On an M5 Ultra that is 40 waits per token; `DS4_METAL_CB_TIMES`
shows a 181 us p50 gap between GPU end and the next submit, a ~72% GPU duty
cycle, and 3968 command buffers for 96 tokens.

This commits each layer without waiting (`ds4_gpu_flush_commands`). The
final-layer drain remains. The third commit gives each Engram table its own
input buffer, which removes the layer-13 drain from the single-token decode
path. The fourth commit does the same for the single-host batched step with an
8-row second row buffer; TP keeps its layer-13 drain in both paths. Single-host
streaming already waits for its expert-cache reconfiguration, so it does not
need the layer-13 drain either. SSD streaming, imatrix and TP keep their
existing scheduling. The batched step gets the same treatment in the second
commit (single-host only, streaming and TP excluded).

`DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_DECODE_PIPELINE=1` restores per-layer waits for
single-token decode. `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_BATCH_DECODE_PIPELINE=1` restores
the batched single-command-buffer scheduling. The layer-13 drain is no longer
restored on single-host after the Engram row-buffer commits.

## Measurements

Machine: Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GiB. Model: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf`
(365,713,686,528 bytes, official antirez repo). Greedy decode, temperature 0.
Same binary, alternating runs:

| workload | old | pipeline |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| ctx 4096, 256 tokens (3 runs) | 27.4 | 38.0 |
| ctx 4096, 1024 tokens | 27.45 | 38.04 |
| 8K prompt, 512 tokens | 27.08 | 37.53 |
| ctx 16384, 64 tokens | 27.10 | 37.09 |
| ctx 32768, 64 tokens | 26.72 | 36.23 |
| ctx 65536, 64 tokens | 25.43 | 34.53 |

Batched step (second commit): session-batch oracle test 45.5 vs 43.5 rows/s
with identical max_abs; `ds4-server --batched-session 8`, 8 clients, ctx 8192:
43.5/43.7 vs 40.7/41.1 tok/s in repeated runs (+6.7% median).

Third commit (Engram input buffers), measured on this branch
(`57df7a5` + the commit), 64 teacher-forced tokens, alternating 3 runs:
ctx 4096 37.30 -> 37.96 t/s (+1.8%), ctx 32768 35.61 -> 36.16 t/s (+1.5%).
Prefill unchanged. The original commit message quotes integration-tree
numbers (4K +1.0% / 32K +2.0%), consistent within run and prompt variance.

Fourth commit (batched Engram row buffers), measured on `1be7b4d`, before this
commit, encoder timeline plus temporary phase markers (markers removed after
the run):

| path | batch step wall | layer-13 CPU wait | layer-13 GPU idle gap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| batched server, 4 sessions | 51.4 ms | 17.2 ms | 0.89 ms |
| batched server, 8 sessions | 85-91 ms | 31-32 ms | 1.2-1.4 ms |
| DSpark verify, rows 2-3 | 22-31 ms | 11-16 ms | 0.65-0.84 ms |

The CPU wait mostly overlaps GPU work; the GPU is actually idle for only
0.7-1.4 ms at layer 13, so the expected gain is 1-2%. Alternating before/after:
DSpark verify 4K prose, 512 tokens: 34.18 -> 34.66 t/s (+1.4%), verify
5949 -> 5850 ms (-1.7%); batched server 4 sessions: 22.34 -> 22.34 t/s
(neutral); batched server 8 sessions: 22.61 -> 23.19 t/s (+2.6%);
`test-metal-session-batch`: 42.19 -> 43.75 rows/s (+3.7%).

Provenance: the branch was rebuilt from `origin/main` alone and re-measured
at ctx 4096 / 256 tokens (37.89 vs 27.66 t/s), so the gain does not depend on
any other unmerged change. The 8K/16K/32K/64K rows above were taken on a tree
that also carries the 1017 vision pairing, which does not touch text decode.

Commands: `./ds4-bench -m ... --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt --ctx-start X --ctx-max X --gen-tokens 64`,
`DS4_TEST_MODEL=... DS4_TEST_LOGIT_TOLERANCE=1e-4 make test-metal-session-batch`,
and `python3` clients against `ds4-server --batched-session 8`. The third-commit
speed checks add `--teacher-forced-decode` to the same bench command. The
fourth-commit checks use the same client with 4/8 sessions and a temporary
phase marker around the layer-13 drain.

## Correctness

- `--dump-logits` byte-identical between the two paths.
- 256-token, 1024-token and 8K+512 greedy outputs byte-identical.
- `tests/test_deepseek41_graph --session-fixture` and `--prefill-parity` pass
  (prefill parity also with `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_BATCH_INDEX=1
  DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_BATCH_CORE=1`).
- `--decode-consistency 16` reports the same max_abs/rms with both paths.
- Engram input-buffer commit: `--dump-logits` and 64-token `--dump-logprobs`
  are byte-identical to `57df7a5`; `--decode-consistency 16` reports the same
  max_abs/rms (max_abs=1.28635859 at token 32793, rms=0.301163183).
- Batched Engram row-buffer commit: DSpark verify greedy text and
  `DS4_DSPARK_STATS` acceptance counts are byte-identical to `1be7b4d` in two
  runs; batched server 4/8-session responses are identical;
  `DS4_TEST_MODEL=... DS4_TEST_LOGIT_TOLERANCE=1e-4 make
  test-metal-session-batch` passes on both trees (default tolerance 0 fails
  identically on both, max_abs 3.8e-06); `--decode-consistency 16` and
  `--prefill-parity` are unchanged; `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1` short run has no
  validation errors.
- `make test-metal-command-memory test-engram` and `./ds4_test --server` pass.
- Two concurrent server sessions work; a 20-minute four-session load (872
  requests, 0 errors) shows steady throughput and no unbounded memory growth.

## Scope

Single-host resident Metal V4.1 decode. SSD streaming, TP and CUDA/ROCm are
unchanged. Verified on M5 Ultra only; pre-M5 Apple silicon was not tested.

Unrelated failure: `make test-deepseek41-metal` fails on this M5 Ultra at
`quantization mode=3 index=5428` (11.25 vs 7.5). The same failure reproduces on
a clean 5379c1c tree, so it is pre-existing and not caused by this change.

title: Optimize V4.1 long-context decode
body:
## What

Three independent changes for long-context V4.1 decode, all verified
byte-identical against the previous path:

1. **Prefix merge for the decode top-k.** The 512-row selection now uses a
   non-causal variant of `kernel_argsort_merge_f32_i32_desc_causal_prefix`, so
   each merge reads only a run's top 512 entries instead of the whole run.
2. **Score only the indexer candidate rows.** Layers after the block-selecting
   layer 20 score only the rows of the blocks layer 20 selected: the block ids
   are sorted, expanded into a ~16K-row list, scored by a row-indexed variant
   of the direct score kernel, reduced with top-k over the compact scores, and
   mapped back to original row ids. Layers 2/8/14/20 and short contexts keep
   the full-index path. Candidates are built only during single-token decode
   (`candidate_decode` + `candidate_pos`), never for copied-row paths or SSD
   streaming.
3. **One fewer barrier in the direct score kernel.** The two partial-sum
   buffers alternate so the next head group cannot overwrite the slots thread 0
   is reading; the accumulation order is unchanged.

`DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_TOPK_PREFIX=1` and
`DS4_V41_DISABLE_CANDIDATE_SCORING=1` restore the old paths.

## Measurements

Machine: Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GiB. Model: 1017 IQ2 GGUF (365,713,686,528 bytes).
`./ds4-bench -m ... --prompt-file <1M-token text> --ctx-start X --ctx-max X --gen-tokens 64`,
temperature 0:

| ctx | before | after | drop vs 4K |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | 37.90 | 37.90 | - |
| 65,536 | 35.25 | 35.95 | -5.1% |
| 262,144 | 29.97 | 33.06 | -12.8% |
| 524,288 | 24.90 | 30.73 | -18.9% |
| 1,000,000 | 19.09 | 27.14 | -28.4% |
| 1,048,500 (32 tokens) | - | 26.60 / 26.63 | -29.8% / -29.7% |

Prefill is not affected (1M prompt: ~1016 t/s before and after once the
candidate build is restricted to single-token decode).

These numbers were measured with #1261 (single-host decode pipelining) applied.
The two changes are independent and apply cleanly in either order (verified
with `git merge-tree`), but the absolute t/s above assume both.

At the absolute maximum context (1,048,500 tokens) the drop is 29.7-29.8% in
two runs: inside the 30% target, but with little margin. The headline result
is the 1M measurement (-28.4%).

This branch alone (without #1261), same model and bench settings: 4K 28.02,
1M 22.27 t/s, i.e. a -20.5% drop. The relative gain is larger without the
pipelining because the pipelined baseline is shorter.

## Correctness

- `--dump-logits` byte-identical with candidate scoring on/off at 32K, 64K and
  256K.
- `tests/test_deepseek41_graph --prefill-parity` passes on the default path and
  with `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_BATCH_INDEX=1 DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_BATCH_CORE=1`.
- `--session-fixture` passes; the session-batch oracle passes with the same
  max_abs (3.8147e-06).
- `--decode-consistency 16` reports the same max_abs/rms with both paths.
- SSD streaming smoke test still runs (the compact path is disabled there).

## Scope

Single-host resident Metal V4.1 decode. SSD streaming, TP and CUDA/ROCm keep
their existing scoring path. Verified on M5 Ultra only.

Unrelated failure: `make test-deepseek41-metal` fails on this M5 Ultra at
`quantization mode=3 index=5428`; it reproduces on a clean 5379c1c tree.

title: Pair V4.1 DSpark support files with the language checkpoint
body:
## What

V4.1 has several released checkpoints with the same DSpark support layout. The
runtime only compares family and architecture, so a drafter converted from a
different checkpoint loads without complaint and silently accepts fewer drafts.

Require `general.source.revision` to match the language GGUF for V4.1 DSpark,
the same way the vision sidecar is paired.

## Verification

With the 1017 language GGUF (official antirez Q2):

- a 1017 DSpark support file loads as before;
- a copy whose revision metadata is rewritten to `df42c109...` is refused with
  `DSpark support model does not match the language checkpoint revision`;
- `./ds4_test --server` passes.

The df42c109 language model is not on this machine, so that pair was not
re-run; it exercises the same code path. `--inspect` still does not compare
revisions (diagnostic only).

## Scope

Single-host Metal, runtime check only. No kernel or scheduling changes.

title: Nvidia discrete gpu fixes
body:
This is the first PR in a set which makes ds4 much faster on the nvidia rtx 6000 pro. These first fixes probably apply to other discrete nvidia gpus as well. 
 
My fork has a lot of performance improvements, new cuda kernels, batching support. The  It's pretty large so I want to see what smaller pieces would good to upstream. The kernel changes are mostly focused on sm120 but several improvements also carry over to the spark, especially around prefill. I put some informal performance numbers at the bottom.

 This first PR fixes some assumptions from the Spark code: the 6000 Pro needs to load the weights into vram since it doesn't have unified memory. It also has a couple of build fixes.

Let me know if this makes sense and if you're interested in upstreaming more - I'm happy to put in the work breaking it into reviewable pieces.

title: Disk KV: the pre-lookup "evict" save deletes the cold prefix the same request is about to load
Score four indexer rows per SIMD group
body:
## What

`kernel_glm_indexer_score_one_direct` gives each index row its own 128-thread
threadgroup: it stages the 512 B key row in threadgroup memory, then runs eight
head groups and closes each one with two `threadgroup_barrier`s. It also
re-reads the entire query vector (32 heads x 512 B = 16 KB) for every row, even
though that vector is identical for all rows of a token.

This gives one SIMD group four rows instead. Each lane keeps four float4 key
values in registers, and the head loop reads `q4[lane]` once and reuses it for
all four dots and all four `simd_sum` calls. No threadgroup memory, no
barriers, and a threadgroup covers 16 rows instead of 4.

## Measured

M5 Ultra (256 GiB). All numbers below come from this branch alone
(`origin/main` ee7e840 + this commit), which does **not** include #1261 or
#1262, so absolute throughput is lower than in those PRs' trees.

Kernel only, no model needed, printed by `make test-v41-indexer-score`
(per-call time including the command-buffer commit and wait):

| rows | scalar kernel | four rows per SIMD group | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,048,576 | 7.93 ms (68 GB/s) | 2.89 ms (186 GB/s) | **2.75x** |

End to end with `ds4-bench`, 64 forced tokens, 4K context, this branch alone
(no #1261), scalar vs row-grouped alternating three times (this is the "did 4K
regress" check):

| pair | scalar | row-grouped |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 27.18 | 27.46 |
| 2 | 27.29 | 27.30 |
| 3 | 27.28 | 27.32 |
| median | 27.28 | 27.32 (+0.15%) |

27.3 t/s is the expected 4K rate on `origin/main`; #1261 alone lifts it to
about 37.7 t/s (see that PR), so the absolute numbers in this table and in
#1261's are not comparable - only the scalar-vs-row-grouped columns are.

1M context, one back-to-back pair (scalar 12.54, row-grouped 13.38 t/s steady,
+6.7%). That gain is small because on this tree the 1M decode is dominated by
the full-index top-k over up to 1M rows in eight layers, which is exactly what
#1262 replaces; once #1261 and #1262 are applied the same kernel is worth
2.7 ms per token at 1M. Run-to-run drift on this machine is large when the page
cache is cold (one cold run measured 6.5 t/s), which is why the pair above was
measured back to back.

In a local tree that also carries #1261 and #1262 the same kernel runs the
indexer stream at 304 GB/s instead of 143 and the 130K-context score pass drops
from 1413 to 657 us per token. At 1M context, kept in one definition per
number:

| definition | 1M | 4K | drop |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `gen_tps`, before -> after | 27.14 -> 31.55 | 37.90 -> 37.40 | -28.4% -> -15.6% |
| `gen_steady_tps`, after | 32.14 | 37.69 | -14.7% |

That is a context tax of 4.58 ms per token on the steady medians (5.11 ms on
gen tps, 4.5-5.4 ms across the two rounds) against a 8.79 ms budget for -25%.
The pre-change tree has no steady reference, only `gen_tps`, which is why the
first row carries both contexts.

## Correctness

- `make test-v41-indexer-score`: memcmp of the two kernels over 1M random rows,
  fp4-representable keys (the live cache holds fp4-dequantized values) and a
  full-range f16 cache. Identical in every case.
- `--dump-logits`, and the generated text, byte-identical on and off at 32K
  (`DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_SCORE_ROWS4=1` selects the scalar kernel).
- `--prefill-parity` exact at every frontier; `--session-fixture` passes.

One thing worth knowing before merging: the `#pragma clang fp contract(off)`
around the accumulate is load-bearing. The library builds with fast math and
the scalar kernel rounds `max(s*scale,0)*w` through threadgroup memory, so
contracting the add into an fma drops a rounding. Removing the pragma moves
334,121 of 1M rows by one ulp (max_abs 8.9e-08) while `--dump-logits` still
passes, because these scores only feed a top-k and a one-ulp change is
invisible until it flips a selection at the boundary. That is why the PR adds a
kernel-level memcmp test instead of trusting the logits gate.

## Conflicts

Textually conflicts with #1262 in `ds4_metal.m` and `metal/dsv4_misc.metal`:
both touch `kernel_glm_indexer_score_one_direct` and the dispatch in
`ds4_gpu_glm_indexer_score_one_tensor` (`git merge-tree` reports CONFLICT in
both files). Whichever lands second needs a rebase. If #1262 lands first, the
compact-list variant (`kernel_glm_indexer_score_rows4`) follows in that rebase;
it is not part of this PR because #1262 is what introduces the compact entry
point.

## Scope

- Apple Metal only. The scalar kernel stays available behind
  `DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_SCORE_ROWS4=1`.
- The shared host entry point `ds4_gpu_glm_indexer_score_one_tensor` also serves
  GLM 5.2/5.3 indexer scoring (same 32 heads x 128 dim shape), so those paths
  take the new kernel too. Bit-identity is established at kernel level,
  including f16 caches, but no GLM model was available to run it end to end.
- Unrelated pre-existing failure on this machine: `make test-deepseek41-metal`
  fails at `quantization mode=3 index=5428` (11.25 vs 7.5) on a clean tree as
  well.

title: metal: preserve image embeddings during short streaming prefill
body:
Short SSD-streaming prefill can select the decode-style path for a range containing image tokens. That path reads ordinary token-table rows; image-conditioned rows need the batch path that substitutes vision embeddings. This becomes reachable when the short-prefill threshold is raised, including ranges that only partly intersect an image.

Exclude ranges overlapping a vision span from decode-style admission. Text-only ranges keep their existing thresholds and behavior. The overlap calculation uses 64-bit endpoints to avoid wrapping near `UINT32_MAX`.

Validation: `make test-streaming-vision-policy ds4-server` passes on Apple Silicon. The regression calls the production admission function without allocating a model or GPU, covering full/partial overlaps, adjacent text, multiple images, empty ranges, endpoint overflow, threshold limits and quality mode. This guard has also been used in a local vision deployment; this PR does not include its unrelated server or cache changes.

title: glm: bridge MTP verification across the indexed attention boundary
body:
Legacy GLM MTP verification can fail at the dense-to-indexed attention boundary: a pair beginning at `top_k - 1` needs two target rows, but the indexed-prefill chunk limiter admits only one. The session then reports `glm mtp: verify failed` and invalidates its checkpoint.

Use the existing ordinary target step at that boundary and seed the next draft from its resulting state. The decision uses the existing chunk limiter rather than a hard-coded context size. GLM 5.3's separate mixed-attention verifier, non-MTP decoding, and sampling are unchanged.

Validation:
- `make ds4-server tests/test_session_state_gpu` builds without warnings on Apple M4 Max.
- `tests/test_session_state_gpu` passes, including the new boundary/neighbor and GLM 5.3 exclusion checks.
- The equivalent guard was previously tested in an isolated Metal SSD-streaming GLM run starting at 2046 tokens: the unguarded run failed at 2047, and the guarded 32-token run matched the ordinary target output. That historical experiment used a locally maintained engine; it is supporting evidence, not a fresh full-model test of this exact upstream branch.
- Fresh integration check on M4 Max: Metal SSD-streaming GLM, 32K context and 64 GiB expert cache, started exactly at 2047 tokens. The guarded MTP path produced the same next 32 greedy target tokens as ordinary decoding. This used the maintained integration engine containing the same guard plus unrelated local patches; it is not a benchmark or a full-model test of pristine upstream.
- CUDA/ROCm and physical multi-GPU execution were not tested. No backend kernel or public API changes.

title: Metal GLM MTP batch verification updates hotness without advancing its decay clock
body:
In Metal SSD streaming, successful two-row GLM MTP verification updates expert route frequency without advancing `g_stream_expert_cache_decode_tokens` for those target rows. The route-hotness decay clock therefore can remain nearly stationary through a long MTP response.

I reproduced this in an isolated local engine derived from `5379c1c`; the relevant call structure is still present in current `main` (`ee7e840`). `ds4_gpu_stream_expert_cache_note_token()` is called from scalar expert paths, while `ds4_gpu_stream_expert_cache_prepare_selected_batch()` records the batched selections' hotness without a matching target-row tick. This report concerns the Metal GLM verifier, not every speculative backend.

Observed on M4 Max, 128 GiB, Metal SSD streaming, 32K context and a fixed 64 GiB expert cache:

| Two complete greedy responses | Unmodified accounting | Experimental accounting |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Output tokens | 352 | 352 |
| Target work clock after the responses | 3 | 377 |
| Additional target rows accounted | 0 | 374 |
| Last decay position | effectively stalled | 369 |

The experiment counted completed target-verifier rows, including rejected proposal positions; it subtracted scalar rows already counted inside the same verifier scope. It ended the scope before draft evaluation and rejection replay. Short-path accounting also matched the independently logged verification-row count. Corresponding greedy output, hidden-state and logits digests remained identical.

This is **not an established speedup**. Two-response generation time was 141.617 s for the original MTP and 145.263 s with accounting alone. Logical `pread` volume fell substantially, but most reads could be satisfied by the OS cache; logical bytes must not be presented as physical SSD traffic. Combining accounting with a separate slot-selection experiment only brought MTP approximately level with ordinary decoding. I have not enabled these experiments in the normal runtime.

A possible fix is a narrowly scoped target-work accounting API around successful batch verification, with protection against double counting and counter overflow. It needs a design decision about the clock's intended meaning and tests for scalar fallback, rejected proposals, prompt prefill and draft exclusion before becoming a default. I am reporting the reproducible accounting mismatch separately rather than proposing the experimental performance switches as a production patch.

These measurements are from the retained October 23 experiment, not a fresh full-model run on the current upstream tree. CUDA/ROCm and multi-GPU behavior were not tested.

title: Prefill: make the V4.1 decoder suffix bit-identical to full prefill
body:
## What

The V4.1 decoder dependency suffix (>=8192 tokens) started inside the full
prefill's 2048-row chunk grid. The batched attention core rounds
probabilities per key block and splits raw from compressed context by the
chunk start and count (`ds41_attention_batch`), so the same rows computed in
a chunk with a different start drifted in the low bits. Main has always
carried that drift: at 8406 tokens the suffix ON/OFF difference is max_abs
0.383 on an untouched `ee7e840` tree.

This starts the suffix at the full-prefill chunk boundary
(`first -= first % chunk`) and warms up 128 rows instead of 127, which also
leaves the raw ring exactly as the previous full chunk did.

One commit on `ee7e840`. No other local PR is included. This changes only
the existing >=8192 path; a follow-up extends the exact suffix below 8192.

## Exactness

`tests/test_deepseek41_graph --decoder-suffix-exact PROMPT [COUNT]` compares
a suffixed session against a full-prefill session with the **default batched
kernels** (the existing `--decoder-suffix` test disables batched MoE/attention
to isolate dependency pruning) and fails on any state or logit difference.

`--decoder-suffix-exact ... 8406` on this branch alone:
`state_spans=48 mismatched=0 logits_changed=0` (all 48 state tensors and all
129280 logits byte-identical). The same comparison on upstream `ee7e840`
differs by max_abs 0.383.

The test takes a count argument so the boundary cases can be exercised
separately; the >=8192 path shares this code for every count.

## Speed

M5 Ultra, 256 GiB, 1017 IQ2_XXS, resident (no `--ssd-streaming`), `ds4-bench`,
64 forced generated tokens, fresh prefill at each row.

| context | no suffix | this branch | delta | main's unaligned suffix |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8192 | 662.40 | 1015.70 | +53.3% | 1117.71 |
| 16384 | 668.25 | 1163.05 | +74.0% | 1228.29 |
| 32768 | 656.10 | 1249.98 | +90.5% | 1290.18 |

Compared with main's unaligned suffix, the exact version is slower by the
rows between the grid boundary and the old start (up to one 2048-row chunk
per decoder layer): 8192 -9.1%, 16384 -5.3%, 32768 -3.1%. That is the price
of exact output; the drift is gone.

Generation is unchanged (37.9-38.0 t/s at 8K, 36.8-37.0 at 16K-32K).

## Gates

- `--decoder-suffix-exact ... 8406`: PASS on this branch alone
- `--decoder-suffix` (existing, tiling fixed): PASS at both frontiers
- `--session-fixture`: PASS

## Reproduce

```sh
./tests/test_deepseek41_graph \
  gguf/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf \
  --decoder-suffix-exact misc/bench/p32k.txt 8406

./ds4-bench -m gguf/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt \
  --ctx-start 8192 --ctx-max 8192 --step-incr 8192 --gen-tokens 64
```

## Scope / not tested

- Single-host Metal, M5 Ultra, 1017 IQ2_XXS. TP and CUDA were not exercised;
  the change is chunk scheduling only and does not alter any kernel, but the
  chunk boundaries move on those paths too.
- SSD streaming was used only by the test harness; the speed table is
  resident full-prefill.
- Pre-existing unrelated failure on this machine: `make test-deepseek41-metal`
  fails at `quantization mode=3 index=5428` (11.25 vs 7.5) on a clean
  upstream tree as well.
- A follow-up will extend the exact suffix below 8192 after this lands; it is
  not part of this PR.

title: v4.1 vision: require the sidecar to match the language checkpoint's revision
body:
## What

The V4.1 vision loader accepts only a sidecar converted from the pinned
`df42c109` revision. `download_model.sh` now fetches the **1017** language GGUF
(`DS41_Q2_FILE=DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-...`) next to `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Vision.gguf`,
which is the `df42c109` sidecar. So the check accepts the old encoder and would
refuse one converted from 1017, which is backwards: 1017 changed every vision
tensor (the payload SHA-256 of all 266 BF16 tensors differs from `df42c109`), so
the pinned sidecar loads and encodes images for a different checkpoint without
any warning.

- The loader compares the sidecar's `general.source.revision` with the revision
  recorded by the loaded language GGUF and refuses a mismatch, printing both.
  When the language GGUF records no revision, it falls back to the pinned
  release exactly as before.
- `gguf-tools/deepseek41_vision.py` gains `--source-revision` / `--source-url`,
  so a sidecar can be converted from the same checkpoint as the language GGUF.
  Defaults are unchanged.

A 1017 sidecar would also need publishing next to the 1017 GGUF, with the
`ds41f-vision` download entry pointing at it. I left `download_model.sh` alone
because I can't publish to that repo.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal; language GGUF converted from the 1017
checkpoint with the ds4 Q2 recipe (IQ2_XXS/Q2_K routed experts); sidecar converted
from 1017 with `--source-revision`.

- 1017 sidecar + 1017 language GGUF: loads; images are read correctly. On a 24-image
  set of rendered codes and shapes: 24/24 codes, colours and shapes.
- `df42c109` sidecar + 1017 language GGUF: refused at load, both revisions printed.
- `deepseek41_vision.py --validate --verify-payload --source-revision ...`: 266/266
  payloads byte-identical to the source safetensors.
- `make && ./ds4_test --server && ./ds4_test --metal-kernels`: OK.

No inference path changes, so no speed run.

title: vision: tiled flash attention for the DeepSeek ViT encoder
body:
## What

The DeepSeek vision encoder runs attention through `kernel_glm53_vision_attention`,
which re-reads every key and value from device memory for each (row, head). For an
8.4k-patch image that is about 94% of encoder time (10.0 of 10.6 s on an M5 Max).

`kernel_deepseek4_vision_flash_attn` has the same contract (rows x 16 heads x 64, fp32
in and out, scale 1/8, full bidirectional attention over the image):

- one threadgroup per 128 query rows of one head (16 simdgroups, 512 threads);
- Q held in simdgroup registers;
- K/V streamed through threadgroup memory 32 rows at a time, stored as half;
- QK^T and PV on 8x8 simdgroup matrices with fp32 accumulation, online softmax.

The encoder's activations are bf16-rounded, so half holds K/V exactly in their range;
values above 65504 would overflow, and ViT activations stay far below that.
`DS4_VISION_SCALAR_ATTN=1` selects the old kernel. Only the DeepSeek encoder switches.
GLM-5.3's encoder uses the same layout and could take the same kernel, but I haven't
tested it there.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2 (IQ2_XXS/Q2_K experts) + 1017 vision
sidecar (with #1273 applied so it loads). A/B is the same binary with and without
`DS4_VISION_SCALAR_ATTN=1`.

- **Kernel**: new `ds4_test --metal-kernels` case against the scalar kernel at 1, 31,
  128, 129, 777 and 4100 rows (tile edges, plus a peaked-softmax case):
  relative RMS <= 1.4e-6, max |diff| 2.6e-4 at max |ref| 11.9.
- **Encoder alone** (standalone encoder bench driving this same kernel, 8.4k patches): 10.6 s -> 1.77 s. Native-resolution 4K screenshot
  (4,838 tokens, ~43k patches): > 240 s -> 33.9 s.
- **End to end, default 1024-token budget:**

  | | scalar | flash |
  |---|---|---|
  | request with a new 4K image (5 images) | 44.8-55.3 s | 36.9-39.5 s |
  | 24 images (~500 tokens each, 3 requests of 8) | 203.2 s | 155.7 s |
  | 24-image set: code / colour / shape | 24/24 | 24/24 |
  | 4K small-text grids, 5 seeds: exact codes | 192/440 | 218/440 |

  The small-text grids sit at the edge of legibility at 1024 tokens, and single
  glyph reads flip both ways between runs with any change to the embedding (per
  grid: 59/56, 44/26, 31/53, 21/31, 37/52). Taken together they show no
  degradation, but they aren't a tight equivalence test; the kernel test is.
- `./ds4_test --server` and `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`: OK. (`make test` runs `--logprob-vectors`, which needs the official V4 Flash GGUF; I only have the 1017 conversion.)

Text inference is unchanged, so no `ds4-bench` run.

title: server: advertise the image modality in /v1/models
body:
## What

`/v1/models` doesn't say whether the server accepts images. OpenAI-compatible clients
decide from that listing whether they may send `image_url` parts. Hermes Agent, for one,
probes it before taking its native image path. Finding no modality, it routes every image
through a "describe it elsewhere" side session, which on ds4-server took a resident slot,
evicted the live conversation, and forced a full rebuild of it: 624 s and 688 s in two
incidents on a long agent session.

With `--vision`, the model entry now carries
`"architecture":{"modality":"text+image->text","input_modalities":["text","image"],"output_modalities":["text"]}`;
without it, `text->text` / `["text"]`. These are the OpenRouter-style fields clients
already read.

## Tested

- `./ds4_test --server`: OK, including new assertions on both listings.

No inference changes.

title: vision: dynamic image token budgets for DeepSeek V4.1
body:
## What

DeepSeek V4.1 images are capped at 1024 LLM tokens. That number is the checkpoint's
preprocessing default (`config.json` `max_image_tokens`, `inference/model.py`
`vision_max_n_token`), not an architectural limit: the reference ViT
(`inference/vision.py`) builds its 2D RoPE per grid (`get_vision_cos_sin(n_h, n_w, ...)`)
and has no position table or size asserts. ds4 hardcoded 1024 in three places:
`safe_resize`, the V4.1 layout builder, and a load-time `config_expect` that rejected any
other value in the sidecar.

At 1024 tokens a 4K screenshot is downscaled about 4x per side, and small text becomes
unreadable.

- The budget comes from `deepseek4-vision.image.max_tokens`, so the default is unchanged.
- **Engine**: `ds4_engine_set_vision_max_tokens()` sets the default;
  `ds4_engine_vision_encode_{memory,file}_budget()` sets it per image.
  `DS4_VISION_BUDGET_NATIVE` keeps native resolution, clamped to the decoded-image
  limits (16384 px per side, 64 MP).
- **Reuse**: embeddings made at a non-default budget get a grid-qualified fingerprint,
  so KV/prefix reuse never mixes budgets. Default fingerprints are unchanged.
- **Planning**: `ds4_image_deepseek_token_cost()` / `ds4_engine_vision_token_cost()`
  return the cost before preprocessing.
- **Server**:
  - `--vision-max-tokens N|native` sets the default.
  - Per image: `image_url.max_tokens` (N or `"native"`), or `image_url.detail` of
    `"low"` (256) or `"native"`.
  - `"high"` and `"auto"` keep the server default, so clients that always send
    `"high"` don't change cost unless the operator opts in.
  - The embedding cache is keyed by budget.
  - `--max-images N` replaces the fixed limit of 16 per request (0 = unlimited).

## Measured

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2 (IQ2_XXS/Q2_K experts) + 1017 vision
sidecar; #1273 (so the sidecar loads) and #1274 (encoder speed) applied for the run.
The test image is a 3840x2160 grid of random 5-letter codes in 22 px Arial; the model
transcribes rows 1-4 (88 codes).

| budget | image tokens | exact codes | char similarity | first request | prefill |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 (default) | 1037 | 56/88 | 0.932 | 43.3 s | 17.2 s |
| 2048 | 2051 | 79/88 | 0.982 | 43.1 s | 18.7 s |
| native | 4907 | 87/88 | 0.998 | 95.0 s | 36.9 s |

Repeated runs at each budget gave identical results. A 1722x1008 screenshot costs 1010
tokens either way, since it fits under the default natively.

## Tests

- `tests/test_vision_budget.c` (now run by `make test`): token costs at default, 4096,
  and native for 1080p, 4K, and 16000x16000 (clamped); layouts far beyond 1024.
- `tests/test_deepseek41_vision_image.py --reference <official checkpoint>`: every resize
  plan still matches DeepSeek's `image_processor.py` exactly at the default budget. The
  test used to require a 32x32 grid (1058 tokens) to be refused; it now requires that grid
  to build, and still refuses degenerate and overflowing grids.
- `tests/test_deepseek4_vision_image`, `./ds4_test --server`, `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`: OK.

title: server: opt-in video input, file:// media, and WebP/GIF images via ffmpeg
body:
Builds on #1276 (dynamic image budgets): the first commit here is that PR. Review that one first.

## What

Opt-in media inputs for ds4-server. Nothing changes unless the operator passes the new flags.

- **Video** (`--video`): a `video_url` / `input_video` content part. ffmpeg (spawned with
  `posix_spawnp`, not linked) samples frames at `fps` (default 1) up to `max_frames`
  (default 256), scaled to fit `max_side`. Near-duplicate frames are dropped with a 32x18
  grayscale thumbnail diff. Each kept frame is spliced into the prompt as an ordinary image
  with a `[t=X.Xs]` line, so the model sees timestamps. The per-frame budget is
  `total_tokens / frames` (default `--video-tokens 32768`, clamped to 96..4096 per frame).
  When `duration * fps` would exceed `max_frames`, the duration is probed with the
  `ffprobe` next to ffmpeg and the rate lowered, so frames cover the whole clip instead
  of the first `max_frames / fps` seconds.
- **file:// images and videos** under `--media-root DIR` only (resolved with `realpath`,
  anything outside the root is refused), so a client on the same machine needn't
  base64 large files.
- **Other image formats**: the decoder reads PNG and JPEG. A WebP/GIF/BMP/HEIC image (data: or
  file://) is converted to PNG with ffmpeg (first frame of an animation) instead of
  failing the request. Clients do send these: Hermes Agent passes WebP and GIF through
  to OpenAI-compatible endpoints unchanged.
- **Request body cap** 64 MiB -> 2 GiB: a few native-resolution screenshots in base64,
  or one inline video, did not fit.
- New flags: `--video`, `--media-root DIR`, `--ffmpeg PATH`, `--video-tokens N`.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2 (IQ2_XXS/Q2_K experts) + 1017 vision sidecar.

title: server: persistent vision embedding cache; tools: batch vision client
body:
Builds on #1277 (which builds on #1276); only the last commit is new here.

## What

**Persistent vision embedding cache** (`--image-cache-dir DIR`, opt-in). Each encoded
image is written to one file named by sha256(format tag, model name, row width, token
budget, encoded bytes), so a repeated image skips the vision encoder across requests and
server restarts. Rows are stored as bf16 when that is lossless (every float's low 16
bits zero), else f32. Writes are atomic (temp file + rename), and the directory is
pruned oldest-first (mtime, touched on hit) past `--image-cache-disk-gb` (default 64).
`--image-cache-mb` sizes the existing in-memory tier: its 128 MiB default holds one
native-budget image (4096 floats x 4.9k tokens = 80 MiB). Its entry limit goes from
32 to 256.

**`tools/ds4-vision-batch.py`** (stdlib only): batch images and videos through the
OpenAI endpoint. It packs many images into one request and asks for a JSON object with
one answer per image, because ds4 prefill throughput grows with prompt length (streamed
experts are amortized over more rows). Images missing from a packed reply are retried
alone. Output is resumable JSONL.

## Measured

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2, SSD streaming with a 56 GB bank.
24 test images of about 500 tokens each, every one with a random 6-character code and
a coloured shape:

| images per request | time per image | correct (code, colour, shape) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~40 s (prefill ~12 tok/s) | — |
| 8 | 6.6 s | 24/24 |
| 24 | 2.7 s (prefill 252 tok/s) | 24/24 |

The single-image row comes from 5 images, stopped early. Two concurrent requests do
not help: prefill serializes.

After a restart, 18 of the 24 embeddings came from disk; the other 6 had only been
held in memory in an earlier run. `./ds4_test --server`, `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`: OK.

title: V4.1: store compressed KV rows as fp16 (bit-identical, half the memory)
body:
## What

V4.1 keeps its compressed KV rows as f32. The rows the compressor writes are FP4 (e2m1)
values times E4M3 block scales: at most five significant bits, magnitudes 2^-10..2688,
all exactly representable in fp16. The attention kernels already read fp16 compressed
rows (`comp_kv_f16`, used by V4). V4.1 now stores them that way:

- decode gathers rows with `kernel_get_rows_f16`;
- the fp16 flag goes to the mixed and indexed prefill/verify attention.

At 1M context that is 5.0 -> 2.5 GiB per session, and KV checkpoints shrink by the same
amount.

Checkpoints record the row format in the header marker (`A41` f32, `A42` fp16) and load
into either graph, converting rows on the way in, so existing KV-store entries keep
working (checked on my fork: an f32 checkpoint written by one server, loaded by an fp16
server, continues identically; not re-run on this base). `DS4_V41_COMP_F32=1` restores f32 rows.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2 (IQ2_XXS/Q2_K experts), SSD streaming,
56 GB expert bank.

- **Exactness**: 19,017-token prompt (`speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt`, first 60 kB),
  `ds4 --dump-logits`, `--temp 0 -n 48`. Next-token logits are **bit-identical** to
  current main (max |dlogit| 0.0 over 129,280 entries), and the 48 greedy tokens are
  identical.
- **Memory**: static context buffers at `-c 32768` go from 8073.5 to 7993.5 MiB
  (-80 MiB); the saving scales linearly with context (-2.5 GiB at 1M).
- **Speed** (`ds4-bench`, 2k-16k, step 4096, 64 generated tokens, two rounds each):
  mean of two rounds, t/s:

  | ctx | prefill main | prefill fp16 | gen main | gen fp16 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2048 | 120.5 | 121.2 | 13.19 | 11.76 |
  | 6144 | 204.5 | 193.6 | 13.74 | 13.54 |
  | 10240 | 199.2 | 206.0 | 13.22 | 14.61 |
  | 14336 | 206.6 | 210.5 | 16.21 | 15.39 |
  | 16384 | 113.5 | 115.3 | 13.95 | 13.78 |

  Mean prefill +0.3%, generation -1.8%. Individual rows swing about 10% either way
  between rounds under SSD streaming, so I read this as no measurable change.
- `./ds4_test --server`, `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`: OK.
- `make test-deepseek41-metal` stops at `quantization mode=3 index=5428: 11.25 != 7.5`
  on current main as well (ee7e840), before reaching anything this touches.

title: server: continued KV checkpoints that actually land during a long read
body:
## What

`--kv-cache-continued-interval-tokens N` is meant to write a KV checkpoint every N tokens,
so a long conversation survives a crash or restart part-way through a read. On V4.1 it
writes nothing during a single long prompt:

- The only attempt is in the prefill progress callback (`kv_cache_maybe_store_continued`).
  On V4.1's layer-major SSD-streamed prefill that callback fires only when a sync
  finishes, and with the cold anchor active the first sync runs straight to
  `cold_store_len`.
- The continued target must be an exact multiple of the (2048-aligned) step past the
  last store. Neither 18432 nor 19011 nor 40960 is one for a 4096/16384 step, so no
  store is even attempted.
- Even if a callback landed on a boundary, the session holds no valid checkpoint
  mid-sync, so there would be nothing to stage.

This change ends the read at each continued boundary and stores there:

- `kv_cache_segment_long_prefill(..., end)` syncs to each aligned boundary, stores a
  continued checkpoint, and continues.
- It runs **before** the cold-anchor sync, bounded by `cold_store_len`. Otherwise the
  cold sync covers almost the whole prompt in one call, leaving no boundary to stop at.
  It runs again up to the prompt end before the final sync.
- The prompt-end continued store is added; both stay inside upstream's
  `if (!multimodal)` guard.
- Segmenting needs a step of at least 16384 (`KV_CACHE_SEGMENT_MIN_STEP`). On the fork,
  back-to-back exactly-8192-row sweeps measured slower and hit a layer-39 failure; I
  have not re-measured smaller steps here. Below that, the server logs at startup that
  continued checkpoints only land between requests.
- Segment-sync failures go through the existing prompt-sync failure path.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2, SSD streaming. One slot, `-c 65536`,
`--kv-cache-cold-max-tokens 2000000 --kv-cache-continued-interval-tokens 16384`, fresh
`--kv-disk-dir` per run, one 42,981-token text request:

| | continued stores during the read | cold store | request |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (ee7e840) | none | 40960 | 85.2 s |
| this PR | 16384 (29.1 s in), 32768 (61.5 s in) | 40960 | 108.1 s |

**Crash test:** same PR build and prompt, `kill -9` of the server right after the
32768 store, then restart and resend. Result: `kv cache hit text tokens=32768 ...
load=30.3 ms`, only the remaining ~10k tokens prefilled, then a continued store at the
prompt end (42981).

**Cost:** splitting one sweep into three made this 43k read 23 s slower. It applies only
when an operator sets an interval >= 16384, which is a choice of crash safety over read
speed.

Also: `./ds4_test --server` and `./ds4_test --metal-kernels` pass.

title: server: a short live prefix no longer hides a longer disk-cache hit
body:
## What

When a slot's live session is a short token prefix of a new request, the
`memory-token` tier reuses it, `cached` becomes that length (often a few dozen
tokens), and the disk path, which only runs when `cached == 0`, never looks. A much
longer checkpoint for the same conversation can be sitting on disk while the server
re-prefills thousands of tokens.

It happens in normal use: a short side request ("Say hi.", a title or summary call
from an agent) leaves its live state in the slot, and the main conversation, which is
on disk, comes back as a continuation of that short prefix.

1. **`REUSE_MEMORY_TOKEN` asks the disk first.** New `kv_cache_disk_best_tokens()` makes
   the same lookup `kv_cache_try_load()` would (`ds4_kvstore_find_text_prefix` on the
   prompt text) without loading anything.
   - If the disk can restore more than the live match plus `min_tokens`, the live tier
     is dropped and the ordinary miss path runs (evict store, then disk load).
   - The lookup only runs when the prompt is longer than live + `min_tokens`, so
     ordinary continuations pay nothing.
   - Multimodal requests report 0 and keep the live tier, since upstream's disk path is
     text-only.
2. **A rewind that discards most of a session stores it first.** In upstream's
   `REUSE_MEMORY_REWIND` tier (GLM), a rewind that keeps less than half of a session of
   at least `min_tokens` is an eviction in all but name, and the eviction store runs only
   on a full miss. The session is now stored with reason `evict` before the rewind.

Model-free tests: `test_live_token_stub_yields_to_disk` (stub `.kv` files: hit, miss,
multimodal, unsupported quant, disabled store, thresholds); the rewind-threshold cases
are added to `test_live_prefix_rewind_target`.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2, one slot, fresh `--kv-disk-dir`,
temperature 0, thinking off. Sequence: A = "Say hi."; X = unrelated short chat; B = A +
reply + a 6.2k-token document; A again; B again.

| turn 4 (B again) | time | prefilled | log |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (ee7e840) | 32.6 s | 6250 tokens from position 26 | `memory-token` reuse of 26 tokens; no disk lookup |
| this PR | 11.7 s | 132 tokens | `live token prefix 26 skipped; disk cache offers 6144 tokens` -> `kv cache hit text tokens=6144` |

All other turns took the same time on both builds. Part 2 is GLM-only and covered by
the unit test; I have no GLM model here for a live run.

Also: `./ds4_test --server` and `./ds4_test --metal-kernels` pass.

title: V4.1: pack compressed KV rows to 4 bits (bit-exact, a quarter of fp16)
body:
Builds on #1279 (fp16 compressed KV rows); only the last commit is new here.

## What

V4.1 compressed KV rows are e2m1 values with an E4M3 scale per 16. #1279 stores them as
fp16 (2 B per value). This packs them as 4-bit codes plus an fp16 scale per block:
320 B per 512-dim row. At 1M context the compressed cache is 0.8 GiB per session,
against 2.5 GiB for fp16 and 5.0 GiB for the original f32.

- **Readers:** the attention kernels read the packed rows in place through their shared
  row loader. Gathering into a staging buffer with renumbered indices would break the
  masks, which compare the selected index value. New kernels: a pack, a run unpack, and
  an unpack-gather for one-token decode. The small-context path, which stages through
  flash attention, unpacks into the existing `selected_kv` scratch.
- **Checkpoints** record the format (`A41` f32, `A42` fp16, `A43` packed) and convert on
  load in either direction.
- **Format choice:** `DS4_V41_COMP=packed|f16|f32`; packed is the default.

**Exactness.** Both writers run the e2m1/E4M3 quantizer first, so the pack must
*recover* each block's scale, not re-derive it. Re-deriving it as
`e4m3(max(amax)/6)` is only safe while the scale is a normal E4M3 value. With a
subnormal scale (block peak below ~0.094) the top code can be 4 or 3, and peak/6 then
lands on a different scale: values moved by up to 2^-8. The pack kernel now tries
peak/{6,4,3,2,1.5,1,0.5}, rounds each to half, and keeps the first that reproduces all
16 values bit for bit. The original scale always qualifies, and a fallback quantizes
input that isn't quantizer output. Signs come from `signbit`, so -0 survives. The CPU
checkpoint converter already recovered scales this way.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2, SSD streaming.

- **Logits**: 19,017-token prompt, `ds4 --dump-logits --temp 0 -n 48`. Packed matches
  current main bit for bit (max |dlogit| 0.0 over 129,280 entries), and the 48 greedy
  tokens are identical. Before the scale-recovery fix the same test gave max |dlogit|
  1.43.
- **New `--metal-kernels` test `test_metal_v41_packed_comp_exact`**: 640 rows from the
  production quantizer, including 7,411 subnormal-scale blocks and -0. Each packed reader
  is compared bitwise with its f32 twin: run unpack, decode gather with -1 slots, and
  `indexed_mixed_batch` attention (split, rb16, heads8, heads16-dual; quality on and off).
  Before the fix: 56,773 unpack / 2,512 gather / 7,061 attention mismatches. After: 0.
- **Memory**: static context buffers at `-c 32768`: f32 8073.5 MiB, fp16 7993.5, packed
  7938.5 MiB. That scales to -4.2 GiB per session at 1M against f32.
- `./ds4_test --server`, `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`: OK.
- **Speed**: the fork measured prefill 355/319 t/s against f32's 370/303, and decode
  5.63/5.67 against 5.56/5.81, over two runs each: no difference. Not re-run on this base.

title: v4.1: rewind sessions with images in the kept prefix
body:
Builds on #1089 (V4.1 live rewind, text-only). The first commit here is that PR; the
image commit and the test commit are new.

## What

#1089 refuses to rewind a session whose kept prefix holds an image, so every
multimodal agent turn still re-reads the whole context. This lifts that limit:

- **Engram history**: `ds41_graph_rewind(g, tokens, pos, image_tail)` takes a bitmask
  of image rows from the session's retained image identities and writes them into the
  rebuilt Engram history as `DS4_ENGRAM_DEAD`, exactly as the original prefill's text
  mask did.
- **Odd targets**: the replay of `pos-1` only runs when that row is text; otherwise the
  rewind invalidates as before.
- **Image identities**: after a successful rewind, identities at or after the target
  are dropped. A span straddling the target is kept, and `ds4_session_sync` rebuilds if
  the request changes it.
- **No retained projection.** The graph's `images` pointer stays NULL outside a
  multimodal sync, so batching, TP decode islands and the text prefill variants (all
  gated on `image_count`) stay available for sessions that once saw an image.
- **Server**: the V4.1 rewind tiers require `token_image_prefix` instead of a text-only
  checkpoint. Execution re-validates V4.1 multimodal rewinds with
  `ds4_session_vision_prefix_matches`, because a request may add images after the
  target. GLM keeps the exact `vision_state_matches`. New `ds4_test --server` probe
  cases cover checkpoints with an image.

**Tests.** `tests/test_metal_rewind_vision` (new; `make test-metal-rewind-vision`) checks
even rewinds against a staged reference. Odd rewinds replay one row through the
decode kernels, so a single-sweep reference can't be bit-identical: that difference is
1.31 in logits with no rewind at all, which is batch shape, not rewind. Both rewind
tests therefore now compare odd rewinds against a reference that computes that row
the same way: `sync(prefix)`, `eval(row)`, `sync(full)`. That check must be exact.

## Tested

M5 Max 128 GiB, macOS 26.5, Metal, V4.1 1017 Q2 + 1017 vision sidecar (with #1273 so it
loads), SSD streaming. A 423-row image sits at rows 6..428 of a 1500-token prompt.

| rewind | target | delta vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| even, deep | 1200 | 0 |
| even, right after the image | 428 | 0 |
| odd, deep (row 1200 replayed as decode) | 1201 | 0 |
| odd, right after the image (row 428 replayed) | 429 | 0 |

In the right-after-the-image cases the Engram history tail consists of image rows.
For information: against the single-sweep reference the odd delta is 1.39 with the
image and 0.96 for the text-only control, and in this run one greedy token flipped at a
near-tie. `ds4_test --server` and `--metal-kernels`: OK. `test_metal_rewind` (text,
including the new exact odd check): PASS: even rewind (n=1800, deep=1500) exact; odd rewind to 1501 rewound-vs-staged-decode 0; long-sweep rewind PASS.
