title: Server: do not let chat content inject control tokens
body:
## What

The server rendered the whole chat turn (user, tool, reasoning, schema text)
into one string and then rescanned it for control-token spellings. A message
or tool result containing `<｜User｜>`, `</think>`, or another spelling became
real chat syntax: prompt injection that can open a new turn, close the
thinking block, or forge DSML.

The renderer now records a byte mask for the literals it inserts itself. The
tokenizer accepts a control token only when the whole spelling is trusted;
every other byte is encoded by BPE.

Reproduction (`--special-token-injection`), before -> after:

| content | control tokens |
| --- | --- |
| user `before <｜User｜> after` | 2 user -> 1 user |
| user `</think>` | 2 think-end -> 1 think-end |
| tool `<tool_response>` | 1 -> 0 |
| live tool continuation with `<｜User｜>` in the result | 2 user -> 1 user |

## Scope

- Fresh chat/completions, responses, and messages requests, plus the
  multimodal split path.
- Live tool-continuation suffixes (the agent tool loop).
- DeepSeek41 only. The GLM and Qwen renderers still rescan their whole
  string, so the same hole remains there. That is a follow-up PR with the
  same mask plumbing; no new inconsistency is introduced for them.
- Raw prompt requests (`/v1/completions` and any path that takes the prompt
  verbatim) keep the historical scan-everything behavior: the caller writes
  those spellings on purpose.
- Sampled tool text (`raw_tool_text`) is replayed byte for byte, but only the
  DSML delimiters are trusted; argument values stay text.

## KV reuse

Byte-prefix KV reuse cannot see the mask: the same bytes tokenize differently
when a spelling is syntax or content. The server now refuses byte-keyed reuse
when either the incoming prompt or the slot's session has an untrusted
control spelling:

- ambiguous prompts are not stored in the disk KV (all save paths);
- ambiguous requests do not search the disk KV;
- the live text/visible tiers require both sides unambiguous; the token-tier
  reuse still applies.

Cost: a conversation that reads a file containing control-token spellings
(for example ds4's own source in a tool result) no longer hits the disk KV.
Including a mask hash in the cache key is a follow-up.

## Tests

- `./ds4_test --server`: PASS (includes the new reuse-guard test)
- `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<1017 IQ2> ./ds4_test --special-token-injection`: PASS
  - injection counts in the table above
  - benign multi-turn conversation: masked and unmasked tokenization are
    identical (215 vs 215)
  - ambiguous disk load skipped, session flagged for text reuse
  - live tool-continuation case with `<｜User｜>` in the tool result
  - disk hit path, miss path, and fresh tokenization all agree (8/8/8 tokens)

## Not tested

- GLM/Qwen (follow-up).
- CUDA/TP: server-side tokenization only; no backend behavior changed.

title: metal: bf16 V4.1 index cache with tensor score path
body:
## What

The V4.1 indexer score pass reads the index cache and produces the top-k
that selects compressed KV rows for attention. On Metal this stores the
cache as bf16 and runs the full-scan decode pass through the Metal tensor
API (`matmul2d`), with the bf16 SIMD kernel as the fallback.

The cache values are bf16-exact: every entry is an FP4 E2M1 code
(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6) times a power-of-two E8M0 scale, so the low 16
bits of its f32 representation are zero. The store therefore copies the
high 16 bits verbatim instead of doing a float-to-bf16 conversion:

- No rounding: the stored bits are exactly the f32 value's top half.
- No subnormal flush: `2^-127` (the smallest E8M0 product) stays `0x0040`
  in bf16 instead of becoming zero. `--bf16-cache-edge` checks storage for
  `2^-127`, `2^-128`, `2^-130`, `2^-126`, `2^-125`, `1.5*2^-126`, `1.0`,
  and `-2^-127`.

The producer does not actually emit `2^-127`: the E8M0 quantizer multiplies
the FP4 code by a power-of-two scale in f32, and that multiply flushes the
smallest code to zero on this GPU (the same as main's f32 path). `2^-126`,
the smallest normal, survives 128/128. Therefore the real cache never
contains a bf16 subnormal, and real-prompt behavior is unchanged from main.

The bit-exact store is still the right invariant: it does not depend on the
hardware conversion's subnormal policy, and it keeps any value a future
producer writes. The artificial `2^-127` row below is the only place where
the score paths differ.

f16 was rejected: E8M0 scales can go below f16's exponent range.

The tensor score kernel reads 64-row key tiles, so the index cache is
allocated with the capacity rounded up to 64 rows; the extra rows are
zero-filled. The kernel writes scores only for rows below `n_comp`, so the
padding is read but never selected. The saved payload still contains only
the live rows.

## Exactness

`DS4_V41_SCORE_SELECTION_CHECK=1` compares the tensor and SIMD top-k sets
per decode token and per indexer layer (2/8/14/20/24/28/32/36):

| prompt | tokens | checks | mismatches |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32K | 40,791 | 512 | 0 |
| 256K | 261,042 | 512 | 0 |
| 1M | 1,000,494 | 512 | 0 |

For 32K, full 64-token logprobs were compared between tensor and bf16 SIMD;
for 256K/1M the tensor-vs-SIMD comparison is the 512-check selection test.
All three prompts were compared against main f32 logprobs:

| prompt | tensor vs bf16 SIMD | tensor vs main f32 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32K | logprobs byte-identical | logprobs byte-identical |
| 256K | top-k 0/512 | logprobs byte-identical |
| 1M | top-k 0/512 | logprobs byte-identical |

- `--decode-consistency` at 32K: the branch and main are identical:
  `prefix_tokens=40855 max_abs=0.748583317 rms=0.121814985` at token
  101977. The tensor score path adds no drift.
- `--session-fixture`: PASS.
- `--prefill-parity`: exact at five frontiers.
- Payload version mismatch logs
  `session payload format N (expected M); rebuilding`; CPU=3, Metal=4.

The raw scores can differ in the low bits (tensor-core accumulation order);
the selected set and the generated logprobs are the release-visible result.

### Denormal-only rows

A synthetic cache row of only `2^-127` is the one place where the score
paths differ:

| path | score |
| --- | ---: |
| main f32 SIMD | 0 |
| bf16 SIMD fallback | 0 |
| tensor | `3.76158192e-37` (= `2^-121`, exact) |

The tensor path keeps the row; the fallback behaves exactly like main. Since
the producer flushes this value before the store, it does not occur in a
real cache; this is an extreme E8M0 corner rather than a real-prompt
regression.

## Speed

Resident, M5 Ultra, 1017 IQ2_XXS, `ds4-bench`, 64 forced tokens, 1M context.
The main row is a build of `ee7e840`; the two branch rows differ only by
`DS4_METAL_DISABLE_V41_SCORE_TENSOR`.

| score path | prefill t/s | gen t/s | steady t/s | first token ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main f32 SIMD | 991.92 | 14.60 | 14.73 | 105.22 |
| this branch, bf16 SIMD fallback | 998.86 | 14.61 | 14.70 | 90.47 |
| this branch, tensor API | 997.94 | 22.10 | 22.31 | 71.36 |

Against main: the tensor path is +51% gen / +52% steady, and first-token
latency drops from 105.2 ms to 71.4 ms. The bf16 SIMD fallback is flat
(+0.1% gen, -0.2% steady), so machines without tensor ops do not regress.
Prefill is flat (991.9 vs 997.9-998.9 t/s, within run noise). An earlier run
with the opposite order measured 14.65 -> 21.31 gen t/s, so the tensor gain
is consistent.

Short contexts (`ds4-bench`, 64 tokens, same prompt for both builds):

| context | main gen t/s | tensor gen t/s | main steady t/s | tensor steady t/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K | 27.50 | 27.41 | 27.56 | 27.43 |
| 32K | 27.63 | 26.88 | 27.83 | 26.92 |

The 32K pair was repeated in alternating order: main 26.72 / 27.90 and
tensor 27.43 / 27.22 (averages 27.31 vs 27.33), so the first 32K difference
is run-to-run noise. 4K is flat (-0.3%, first token 39.7 -> 36.1 ms); there
is no short-context regression.

On the integration tree that also has #1267's row-grouped SIMD decode
kernel, the same tensor score kernel measured 31.33 -> 34.43 gen t/s (+9.9%)
and steady 31.82 -> 34.79 (+9.3%), with prefill unchanged.

## Compatibility

- Session payload version: Metal 4 (bf16 index cache), CUDA 3 (f32).
  - Existing Metal caches (version <= 3) are rejected once with
    `session payload format N (expected 4); rebuilding`.
  - A Metal payload cannot be read by a CUDA build or vice versa.
- On Metal, the disk KV cache stores the same payload, so one rebuild after
  upgrading is expected. CUDA users keep payload 3 and their caches remain
  valid.

## Relationship to #1267

#1267 adds a row-grouped SIMD decode score path for f32. This PR is based on
main and uses the existing `score_one` bf16 SIMD kernel as the fallback; on
a machine without Metal tensor ops the fallback therefore matches main's
denormal behavior but not #1267's throughput. Once both land, #1267's
row-grouped kernel is the intended fallback and should be extended to read
the bf16 cache. The selection diagnostic compares the tensor kernel against
the current fallback at every layer/token, so that future port has a
reference.

## Scope / not tested

- CUDA sources are byte-identical to main; the CUDA index cache stays f32.
  No CUDA hardware was available to build or run this change.
- The tensor path is Metal 4 only; pre-Metal-4 machines take the SIMD
  fallback and are covered by the selection diagnostic at 32K/256K/1M and
  the 32K tensor-vs-SIMD logprobs comparison.

## Tests run

```
make ds4 ds4-bench tests/test_deepseek41_graph \
     tests/test_session_state tests/test_session_state_gpu
./tests/test_deepseek41_graph MODEL --bf16-cache-edge
./tests/test_deepseek41_graph MODEL --session-fixture
./tests/test_deepseek41_graph MODEL --prefill-parity misc/bench/prompt32k.txt
./tests/test_session_state
./tests/test_session_state_gpu
make tests/test_deepseek41_metal && ./tests/test_deepseek41_metal   # full suite, M5 Ultra

# per prompt (32K, 256K, 1M)
DS4_V41_SCORE_SELECTION_CHECK=1 ./ds4 -m MODEL --prompt-file PROMPT \
  -c CTX -n 64 --temp 0 --dump-logprobs tensor.json
./ds4 -m MODEL --prompt-file PROMPT -c CTX -n 64 --temp 0 \
  --decode-consistency 64
```

title: metal: reuse q8_0 weight loads for 2-8 decode rows
body:
## What changed

`ds4_gpu_matmul_q8_0_decode_rows_exact_tensor` used to launch one threadgroup per activation row, so a dense Q8_0 projection read the same weight row once for every row in a 2..8-row batch (DSpark draft/verify and other small exact batches).

This adds a small-row Q8_0 matvec that keeps `NR0` output rows per threadgroup and evaluates `NACT` activation rows there. The 8-value weight slice is loaded once per output row and reused across activation rows. **Only the weight load is shared**: every activation row keeps the original K walk, the original per-thread `sumq` accumulation order and the original `simd_sum` reduction tree, so each row is bit-identical to `kernel_mul_mv_q8_0_f32` run one row at a time. One row of ordinary decode continues to use the existing kernel.

The host uses the new path only for `2 <= rows <= 8` and `out_dim >= 2048`. The threshold is based on the row-by-row measurements below: out 512/1280 lose 3..21% (per-row arithmetic dominates), while out 2304+ win 10..49%. Seven kernels (`kernel_mul_mv_q8_0_f32_rows2` .. `rows8`) are instantiated; the host picks `NACT == rows` and one threadgroup row group.

`DS4_METAL_Q8_ROWS_LEGACY=1` forces the old per-row kernel for A/B timing. It is a diagnostic switch only; the default is the new path.

## Testing

- New `tests/test_q8_row_batch.c` (wired as `make test-q8-row-batch`): 17 shapes, `rows = 1..8`. It compares `ds4_gpu_matmul_q8_0_decode_rows_exact_tensor` against the ordinary single-row kernel run once per row.
  - Shapes cover the real V4.1 projections (`1280x32768`, `2304x5120`, `5120x2304`), odd/partial output tiles (`out_dim = 1, 3, 5, ..., 513, 4097`), K smaller than one `NSG*NQ` window (`in_dim = 32, 96`), and larger K (`in_dim = 4096`).
  - Every row matches **bit for bit** (float `memcmp`), including the partial last output tile; output guard values are untouched.
  - Passes both with the default path and with `DS4_METAL_Q8_ROWS_LEGACY=1`.
- `make test-q8-prefill-variants`: all PASS.
- DSpark decoded text is byte-identical before/after on all tested conditions (main and the integration tree): 4K prose, 4K code, 40K prose, 40K code.
- Plain generation (no DSpark), 4K prose, 512 tokens: 26.67 vs 26.63 t/s (latest pair); unchanged.

## Call sites covered

`ds4_gpu_matmul_q8_0_decode_rows_exact_tensor` is called from more than the V4.1 DSpark path:

- V4.1 `ds41_matmul_batch` (DSpark draft/verify; the main target)
- V4 `metal_graph_encode_native_session_batch_shared` (QKV session batch)
- V4 `metal_graph_encode_qkv_session_batch`
- V4 `metal_graph_encode_shared_rows_exact`
- small attention-output batch (`ds4_gpu_attention_output_q8_batch_tensor`, `round_low_bf16 && n_tokens <= 8`)

Because the kernel is bit-identical per row, all of these keep the same outputs by construction. However, **no V4 (non-1) model is available here**, so the V4 session-batch paths were not run end to end. For V4 the verification is the kernel-level bit-exact test above; V4 batch output is not independently confirmed.

## Verify GPU time by row count

Main `ee7e840` + this patch, 4K prose, 512 generated tokens, encoder timeline. Medians over the verifies in that run; `wall` is first-to-last command buffer of the verify group, `GPU busy` is the union of kernel intervals, `dense q8` is the union of the plain/row Q8_0 kernels.

| rows | verifies | verify wall (ms) | GPU busy (ms) | dense q8 (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 58 | 47.04 -> 46.67 (-0.8%) | 37.22 -> 35.89 (-3.6%) | 13.17 -> 10.99 (-16.6%) |
| 3 | 7 | 61.17 -> 59.72 (-2.4%) | 49.58 -> 46.52 (-6.2%) | 17.93 -> 12.59 (-29.8%) |
| 4 | 3 | 74.85 -> 69.57 (-7.1%) | 61.15 -> 56.37 (-7.8%) | 23.84 -> 16.64 (-30.2%) |
| 5 | 2 | 88.20 -> 82.88 (-6.0%) | 72.72 -> 67.25 (-7.5%) | 28.03 -> 19.33 (-31.0%) |
| 6 | 22 | 102.30 -> 97.47 (-4.7%) | 84.95 -> 79.00 (-7.0%) | 34.07 -> 22.96 (-32.6%) |

The small out 512/1280 projections stay on the old kernel.

## Main DSpark throughput

`ee7e840` + this patch, 512 generated tokens, A/B alternated in one process at a time, 2 runs per side, medians. `before` is `DS4_METAL_Q8_ROWS_LEGACY=1` (old per-row kernel), `after` is the default.

| condition | before (t/s) | after (t/s) | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K prose | 29.48 | 29.88 | +1.3% |
| 4K code | 45.19 | 47.75 | +5.7% |
| 40K prose | 25.24 | 25.48 | +0.9% |
| 40K code | 39.86 | 41.83 | +4.9% |

Run-to-run drift on this machine is about 6% for the same binary and settings; alternating the two paths is what makes the 1-6% deltas readable. The DSpark output text was byte-identical in every tested condition.

## Integration tree (reference only)

a0331ee (aba0256, an integration of open PRs #1261, #1262, #1263 and #1267, plus an unmerged Engram input-buffer change) and an unmerged DSpark scheduler change, with this patch, 512 generated tokens, A/B alternated, one pair per condition. The 4K code result was reproduced by an earlier two-pair run (48.25 -> 51.12 t/s):

| condition | before (t/s) | after (t/s) | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K prose | 38.77 | 39.31 | +1.4% |
| 4K code | 48.52 | 51.27 | +5.7% |
| 40K prose | 35.25 | 35.17 | -0.2% |
| 40K code | 42.22 | 44.32 | +5.0% (other runs: 41.93 -> 45.16, +7.7%) |

At 40K prose the scheduler skips nearly all drafts (17 verifies), so there is little verification work for this change to improve. These are reference numbers only; the main table above is the PR's target environment.

The legacy path with the extra kernels present also matched the unmodified a0331ee build (48.23 vs 48.30 t/s at 4K code), so the additional Metal functions do not slow the old kernel.

## Not in this PR

- The same per-row weight re-read exists in `kernel_mul_mv_f16_f32_4` (about 3.3 ms of a rows-6 verify for the 12800x6 shape, ~6.6% of plain f16 matvec time in that verify). It is untouched here. `kernel_dsv41_bf16_linear` already uses M-tiled grids, and the Q8_0 output head already batches five rows per threadgroup.
- TP was not tested.
- CUDA was not changed and was not tested (Metal-only change).

title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash: experimental Metal support with SSD streaming
body:
Experimental MiniMax M3.1 Flash support on Metal with SSD streaming. The Q2 GGUF is 121 GiB, so on a 128 GB Mac the routed experts stream from disk while the other ~13 GiB of weights stay mapped. There is no download target yet: the GGUF is built locally from the official checkpoint with the new converter (see "Weights" below).

**What's added**
- `gguf-tools/minimax31_quantize.py`: converts the official MXFP8/NVFP4 checkpoint to IQ2_XXS gate/up + Q2_K down experts, Q8_0 elsewhere (`--artifact q4` for Q4_K experts). `minimax31_reference.py` is a NumPy forward used as the graph reference; `minimax31_truncate.py` makes layer-truncated validation GGUFs.
- Loader, tokenizer and chat template (thinking and tool calls) for the `minimax-m3` architecture; the server reports `minimax-m3.1-flash`.
- Metal kernels in `metal/minimax3.metal`: norm/RoPE prep, block-sparse MSA indexer and attention (split-K for decode), sigmoid router, MoE reduce. Routed experts reuse the qwen4 MoE kernels (prefill) and the DeepSeek iq2_xxs pair / q2_K matvecs (decode) with a SwiGLU-OAI activation.
- SSD streaming: an LRU expert pool filled by `pread`, next-layer router-guess prefetch, router ids published to the CPU without waiting for command buffer completion, and the prefill layer buffer folded into the pool.

**Shared code touched**
- qwen4 MoE kernels take an activation selector (`act` = 0 for Qwen). Routing the SiLU product through a helper function changed Qwen's fast-math code and its prefill logits (rel err 0.145 vs `main`), so `QWEN4_GLU` is a macro that keeps the original expression. Qwen is bit-exact with `main` again (`9f03e27`).
- iq2_xxs pair matvec loads each grid entry with one 64-bit threadgroup load; bit-exact, and DeepSeek decode speed is unchanged.
- New `ds4_gpu_concurrent_begin/barrier/end` and `ds4_gpu_add_host_map` (residency set for host maps). All MiniMax code is under `DS4_HAS_QWEN4_METAL`, so CUDA/ROCm need no stubs.
- `ds4-bench --teacher-forced-decode` also dumps decode logits every 16 steps (drift checks).

**Fixes found in agent use** (`a47f793`, `7001667`)
- Garbage output after a short follow-up or tool result: a 5..32-token prefill chunk on top of a cached prefix ran the five attention projections in a concurrent encoder section, where the Q8 batch matmul's shared split-k partials and reduce dispatch are not ordered. Those chunk sizes now run the projections serially. Repro (184-token cached prefix + 29 new tokens) went from garbage to a correct answer.
- Every streamed MiniMax tool call was logged as unterminated and answered with a model-visible tool error, so the model retried each call. The decode tracker now waits for unambiguous markers and holds back MiniMax's longer start marker. New test: `test_minimax_decode_tracker_markers`.

## Testing (Apple M5 Max 128 GB, macOS 26.6)

Every A/B runs `main` (`5379c1c`) and this branch on the same workload, with teacher-forced decode so routing is identical, and compares the dumped logits.

| model | check | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| MiniMax M3.1 Flash Q2, SSD streaming | decode tok/s (2008-token chat prefill, 320 tokens) | n/a | 15.8 |
| | prefill tok/s | n/a | 106 |
| | logits vs first streaming build | n/a | rel err 0.0044, 0 top-1 flips |
| Qwen3.8 Flash Next Q2 | decode tok/s (2048 ctx) | 52.2 | 52.0 |
| | prefill tok/s | 1367 | 1357 |
| | frontier logits vs `main` | | identical |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash Q2 (0731) | decode tok/s, two runs in swapped order | 42.4 / 42.5 | 41.9 / 42.9 |
| | frontier logits vs `main` | | identical |

- `make test-minimax3-kernels`, `make test-qwen4-kernels`, `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`, `./ds4_test --server`: pass (`--server` also passes on `main`).
- `make cpu`: builds.
- During development, MiniMax decode went from 2.55 to 17.2 tok/s with a cooldown between runs; the 15.8 above is a single run without one.

**Not tested / known gaps**
- Full `make test` and `--logprob-vectors` (DeepSeek reference vectors) not run on this branch.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Q4 models, M3 Ultra, CUDA and ROCm builds not run. CUDA/ROCm should not be affected because all MiniMax code is Metal-only, but that hasn't been checked on a CUDA machine.
- Qwen first decode token is slower on this branch (54-90 ms vs 23 ms on `main`); steady decode is unchanged. Not yet investigated.
- MiniMax: no CUDA/ROCm, distributed, speculative decoding or vision. Only tested with `--ctx 32768`.
- MiniMax decode slows down at longer context. Same server, `--ssd-streaming-cache-experts 40GB` (41.2 of 108.2 GiB routed experts cached), live agent sessions:

  | context | decode tok/s |
  | --- | ---: |
  | 0.5K to 1.8K | 17 to 21 |
  | 15.5K to 18.5K | 6.3 to 10.7 |

  The drop shows up both before and after the fixes above, and agent clients start around 16K because of their system prompt and tools. Not yet investigated: sparse attention reads at most 16 blocks either way, so SSD expert misses (55% cache hit over the session) are the likely cause, versus long-context routing or the indexer scan. A `ds4-bench` A/B at 2K vs 16K, and a run with the automatic cache budget, would separate these.

## Weights

The weights use the MiniMax Community License, which restricts commercial use. @antirez, would you like to host a Q2 GGUF and add a `download_model.sh` target, or should support stay convert-your-own for now? Conversion steps are in `gguf-tools/README.md` (source revision `54e4e69`); `docs/MODELS.md` covers running it and `docs/SSD_STREAMING.md` now lists it. README is unchanged until there is a download target.

title: Server: mask GLM and Qwen chat renderers
body:
**Stacked on #1284; merge after it.** The first two commits (`def0f60`, `138cb39`) are #1284 and will drop out once it merges; this PR's changes are the last three commits (`e66797e`, `aa982ec`, `6ee4a73`).

## What

#1284 added a byte-level trusted mask for the DeepSeek41 renderer. This extends the same mechanism to the GLM and Qwen chat renderers.

- GLM/Qwen renderers now record which bytes they insert themselves. Role markers, think tags, tool-call/tool-response delimiters and the static tool-schema template are trusted; user, system, assistant content/reasoning, tool results, tool arguments and schema JSON stay untrusted.
- `raw_tool_text` replay uses a generic delimiter scanner: only the tool-call/tool-response/argument tag spellings are trusted, argument values remain ordinary text. This matches #1284's `append_dsml_raw_v41`.
- Live tool-continuation tails return masks too; the multimodal marker split slices the mask at the same byte offsets; the existing `prompt_ambiguous` / disk-KV / text-tier guards are reused. The GLM/Qwen tests assert that an injection prompt sets `prompt_ambiguous` and makes `slot_text_reuse_allowed` false, while a benign prompt leaves it clear and reusable.
- The inspect-only engine path now loads the vocabulary, so the tests can exercise the renderer/mask/tokenizer without reading weights.

The assistant leading think tag is treated like #1284's DeepSeek41 path: template-inserted `<think>`/`</think>` are trusted, client/model content is untrusted. Raw prompt requests (`/v1/completions` and other verbatim-prompt paths) keep the historical scan-everything behavior.

## BPE check

I tokenized control spellings with an all-zero (untrusted) mask and compared the token IDs:

| model | spelling | unmasked | masked (untrusted) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM | `[gMASK]` | 154822 | BPE text |
| GLM | `<|user|>` / `<|system|>` / `<|assistant|>` / `<|observation|>` | 154827 / 154826 / 154828 / 154829 | BPE text |
| GLM | think/tool/arg tags | 1 control ID | BPE text |
| GLM | `<|endoftext|>` / `<|im_start|>` / vision tags | BPE text | BPE text |
| Qwen | `<|im_start|>` / `<|im_end|>` / `<|endoftext|>` | 248045 / 248046 / 248044 | BPE text |
| Qwen | think/tool/tool-response tags | 1 control ID | BPE text |
| Qwen | `<|user|>` / `[gMASK]` / `<|vision_start|>` / `<|image_pad|>` / `<|vision_end|>` | BPE text | BPE text |

No BPE residual was found: once the mask marks a spelling untrusted, GLM/Qwen BPE does not re-emit it as a control token. A BPE filter is not needed.

GLM's eos is `154820 = <|endoftext|>`, but `endoftext_id` is `-1` and the spelling tokenizes as text both masked and unmasked. There is no injection through it; `endoftext_id` is left unchanged in this PR.

## Tests

- `./ds4_test --server`: PASS (all renderer and server unit tests).
- `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<DeepSeek41> ./ds4_test --special-token-injection`: PASS, including `benign tokens 215 vs 215`.
- `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<GLM> ./ds4_test --special-token-injection-glm`: PASS
  - user + system content spelling `<|user|>`: exactly 1 role marker, content is text
  - tool result `<tool_response>`: exactly 1 wrapper, content is text
  - raw tool text with `<|user|>` in an argument: `<tool_call>` 1, injected user 0
  - live tool-continuation suffix: 1 user role, content is text
  - KV guard: injection prompt sets `prompt_ambiguous` and blocks byte-prefix reuse; benign prompt leaves it clear and reusable
  - multimodal marker boundary: nonce marker with `<|user|>` before/after; prefix/tail mask slices keep the spellings as text (`pre=1` role only, `post=0`)
  - benign system/user/assistant/tool chat with tools: masked and unmasked token sequences identical
- `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<Qwen> ./ds4_test --special-token-injection-qwen`: PASS
  - user + system content spelling `<|im_start|>`: exactly 3 role markers, content is text
  - tool result `<tool_response>`: exactly 1 wrapper, content is text
  - raw tool text with `<|im_start|>` in an argument: `<tool_call>` 1, injected im_start 0 beyond the assistant role
  - live tool-continuation suffix: 3 role markers, content is text
  - KV guard: injection prompt sets `prompt_ambiguous` and blocks byte-prefix reuse; benign prompt leaves it clear and reusable
  - multimodal marker boundary: nonce marker with `<|endoftext|>` before/after; prefix/tail mask slices keep both spellings as text (`pre=0`, `post=0`)
  - benign system/user/assistant/tool chat with tools: masked and unmasked token sequences identical
- Vision-token spellings (new in `0252371`):
  - `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<DeepSeek41> ./ds4_test --special-token-injection`: the three DeepSeek image spellings stay BPE in the masked prefix/tail and in the unmasked prompt (`pre=0 post=0 unmasked=0`); `visible_prompt_key` counts one nonce marker.
  - With `DS4_TEST_VISION=<vision GGUF>`: a 16x16 PNG (upscaled by the vision preprocessing) embedding inserts one span (`start=20 tokens=184`), and the text spelling adds no image token.
  - `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<GLM prefix> ./ds4_test --special-token-injection-glm`: the three GLM image spellings are BPE in both modes.
  - `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<Qwen prefix> ./ds4_test --special-token-injection-qwen`: the three Qwen vision spellings are BPE in both modes.

The GLM/Qwen tests open an inspect-only engine: `model_open` + `config_validate_model` + `vocab_load`, no weights. They use the existing `DS4_TEST_MODEL=<path>` convention and skip when the loaded model is the wrong family.

For the local GLM/Qwen runs I used a 128 MiB HTTP-range prefix from each GGUF, placed at offset 0 of a full-size sparse file. `model_open` mmaps the original size, the tensor-range check passes, and `vocab_load` reads only the prefix metadata; no weights are read. The sparse-file creation is a local verification method and is not in the repository. A reviewer running the test with the full 90/137 GiB GGUF goes through the same tokenizer path and should see the same counts.

The full embedding test needs a vision sidecar accepted by the engine. The local 1017 language/sidecar pair both report `general.source.revision=1bae...`, while this tree pins `df42...` in `deepseek4_vision_weights_bind()`; the run above used a copy of the sidecar whose metadata revision string matches the pin. That pairing check is unrelated to this PR: [#1225](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1225) matches the 1017 vision GGUF to its language model, and [#1273](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1273) requires the sidecar to match the language checkpoint's revision. Only the 1017 model pair is available locally; the df42 pair was not run.

## Scope

- GLM/Qwen chat/completions, responses, messages, live tool continuations, and the multimodal marker split path. Tokenizer-level vision spellings are tested; GLM/Qwen have no vision GGUF locally, so their embedding path stops at the tokenizer level. DeepSeek41 runs the full embedding path.
- Vision token safety: the server image marker is a request-local nonce (`\x1e` + `DS4_IMAGE_` + 12 random bytes + `\x1f`), not a token spelling. The prefix/tail around it are tokenized with the trusted mask; the vision-token spellings are not in the tokenizer's control-token table, so they stay BPE in both masked and unmasked tokenization. The vision IDs are only emitted by `ds4_prompt_append_vision`. The image count comes from the received image parts, not from a text scan; `visible_prompt_key` counts exactly `image_count` nonce markers.
- The agent's unmasked KV-identity/compaction tokenization is out of scope for this PR.
- TP and CUDA are untouched and were not tested.
- `buf_printf` mask initialization is the prerequisite commit already in #1284 (`138cb39`).

title: CUDA: 10x speedup for DeepSeek-V4 on RTX 3090 (via Antigravity AI agent) & statistical metrology (LMM/TOST)
body:
# PR: 10x Speedup for DeepSeek-V4 Streaming Inference on RTX 3090 (from 1.02 to 10.35–11.74 t/s) with 100% Bit-Exact Invariance and LMM Certification

## Summary: Dual Contribution

This PR provides two major contributions to DwarfStar:

1. **A 10x Speedup for DeepSeek-V4-Flash Streaming on Consumer Hardware (RTX 3090 + 64 GB RAM) via AI Agent Pair-Programming:**
   - Takes steady-state decode throughput from the **1.02 token/s baseline to 10.35–11.74 token/s** (peaking at 11.82 token/s on conversational prose, and sustaining 5.2–5.5 token/s even under heavy agentic workloads with 7,000+ active context tokens in `ds4-agent`).
   - Surgical C/CUDA improvements: standardizing 1,510 VRAM cache slots with 4 GiB reserve, fusing Hyper-Connections kernels on Ampere (`sm_86`), non-blocking asynchronous stream flush & pinned remap, and decoupling Island A CUDA Graph replay during decode streaming.
   - **100% Bit-Exact Invariance**: `max_abs_diff = 0.000000e+00` across all tokens, passing all official test suites (`make test`, `ds4-eval`, and 16K-context *I Promessi Sposi* sweeps).

2. **A Rigorous Statistical Comparison & Metrology Framework for LLM Engines:**
   - As a Medical Physicist by training, I wanted to address the chronic problem in open-source AI benchmarks: anecdotal comparisons, uncalibrated prompt variance, and the fallacy of assuming lack of proof of divergence equals proof of equivalence.
   - Introduces a reusable metrology harness (`benchmarks/`):
     - Repeated Measures across 4 Domains (Code, Math, Prose, Synthetic Teacher-Forced Decode) separating cold-start from warm steady state.
     - Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMM via REML) to isolate hardware/kernel speedups from prompt-to-prompt lexical variance.
     - Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) for formal numerical equivalence testing.
     - Holm-Bonferroni FWER Adjustment for rigorous multiple comparisons against baseline.
     - Okabe-Ito (2008) Palette: universal colorblind-safe SVG vector plots with 95% Confidence Interval shaded bands.

---

## AI Agent-Assisted Workflow (Antigravity)

Following Salvatore's note encouraging the community to leverage AI coding agents to explore C/CUDA optimizations in `ds4`, this work was developed in human-in-the-loop pair-programming with the **Antigravity** autonomous AI coding agent:
- **Bottleneck Profiling & Hypotheses:** Antigravity was used to systematically inspect the C/CUDA hot-paths, hypothesize memory transfer bottlenecks (such as synchronous `cudaDeviceSynchronize` and sync remap), and identify Ampere micro-kernel fusion candidates.
- **Iterative Refactoring:** Kernel refactoring, Island A graph decoupling, and test harness scripting were iterated collaboratively.
- **Verification & Safeguards:** Every iteration was validated against strict numerical tolerances, ensuring bit-exact parity (`0.000000e+00` difference) before benchmarking.

---

## Key Optimizations

1. **Standardized 1,510 VRAM Cache Slots & Scratch Headroom:**
   - Fixed the dynamic cache target to 1,510 slots (9.95 GiB) while enforcing a 4 GiB workspace reserve for cuBLAS and prefill scratch buffers.
   - Eliminates the previous Layer 16 scratch buffer exhaustion and prevents INT8 kernel fallbacks, preserving exact FP16 accumulation across all 40 layers.

2. **Fused Hyper-Connections Micro-Kernels for Ampere (`sm_86`):**
   - Unlocked `ds4_gpu_hc_pre_f32_mix_split_norm_tensor` on `sm_86` architectures via `g_device_is_sm80_plus`, replacing 5 sequential kernel launches with 2 fused warp-level micro-kernels.

3. **Non-Blocking Flush & Asynchronous Pinned Remap:**
   - Replaced synchronous `cudaDeviceSynchronize` and sync remap `cudaMemcpy(H2D)` with pinned host staging (`cudaHostAlloc`) and lightweight `cudaEvent_t` / `cudaStreamWaitEvent` coordination.

4. **Decoupled Island A CUDA Graph Capture:**
   - Island A (`METAL_DECODE_LAYER_TO_QKV`) operates strictly on static weights already resident in VRAM.
   - Decoupled Island A from the global `!g->ssd_streaming` guard, enabling DwarfStar's native CUDA Graph capture and hardware replay for Island A during streaming decode, eliminating CPU dispatch overhead.

---

## Experimental Benchmark & Statistical Certification

As a Medical Physicist by training, I applied clinical-grade statistical metrology (rather than uncalibrated single-prompt runs) to rigorously certify both throughput gains and numerical equivalence across 4 distinct domains (`D1_code`, `D2_math`, `D3_prose`, `D4_bench`):

### 1. Steady-State Decode Throughput (Run-level Warm Means, $N=20$ per config)

| Configuration | D1 (Code) | D2 (Math) | D3 (Prose) | D4 (Bench) | Multi-Domain Grand Mean | Speedup |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0_baseline` | 1.01 t/s | 1.02 t/s | 1.02 t/s | 1.04 t/s | 1.022 ± 0.022 t/s | 1.00x (Ref) |
| `1_ram_pinned` | 1.60 t/s | 1.58 t/s | 1.58 t/s | 1.55 t/s | 1.579 ± 0.033 t/s | 1.55x |
| `3_safe_cache_1510` | 9.52 t/s | 9.22 t/s | 11.41 t/s | 7.01 t/s | 9.288 ± 1.757 t/s | 9.09x |

| `6_async_flush` | 10.07 t/s | 9.85 t/s | 11.55 t/s | 9.92 t/s | 10.346 ± 0.873 t/s | 10.12x |

### 2. Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM via REML)

Modeling prompt/domain as a random effect ($\hat{\sigma}_{\text{domain}} = 0.899\text{ t/s}$, $\text{ICC} = 56.9\%$):
- Fixed effect estimate: **$\mathbf{\hat{\beta} = +9.1562\text{ t/s}}$**
- $t$-statistic: $36.99$
- Holm-Bonferroni FWER adjusted $p$-value: $p < 10^{-16}$ ($9.57 \times 10^{-299}$)

### 3. Bit-Level Invariance & TOST Equivalence

- Post-prefill logits across all tested prompts: $\text{max_abs_diff} = 0.000000\text{e}+00$, $\text{mean_abs_diff} = 0.000000\text{e}+00$.
- Greedy token sequence exact match rate: $100.0\%$.

---

## Quality Assurance & Release Validation

All release gates from `QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md` were executed and verified:

1. **Unit & Regression Suites:** `make test` passes all extractors, dot-product tests (Q4_K, MXFP4), and server regressions.
2. **Reasoning Verification (`ds4-eval`):** Passed GPQA Diamond, SuperGPQA, and AIME 2025 (algebraic proof solved correctly).
3. **Context Scaling (*I Promessi Sposi*):** Evaluated from 2K to 16K tokens with zero OOM:
   - 2,048 ctx: 71.5 t/s prefill, 6.51 t/s steady decode

title: Metal: reuse f16 weight rows for 2-8 decode rows
body:
## What

F16 dense matvecs in the batched decode paths still launched one threadgroup
per activation row (`kernel_mul_mv_f16_f32_4`), so a projection streamed the
same weight row once per row. The worst case was the Engram KV projection
(`blk.1`/`blk.14`, out 25600): a verify step with 6 rows dispatched grid
12800x6 and read the 315 MB matrix six times.

The new exact-row kernel keeps NR0 output rows per threadgroup but evaluates
NACT activation rows there. Every activation row keeps the single-row K walk,
per-thread accumulation order, tail loop and reduction tree; the weight slice
stays hot in L1 across the rows. `ds4_gpu_dsv41_projection_rows` switches to it
for 2..8 rows at out_dim >= 2048.

The strided entry used by the draft attention-output groups is deliberately
outside that threshold: the group output is 1024, and merging its 40 draft
matvecs into 8 dispatches wins 1.45x per stage (legacy 1.041 ms, rows
0.718 ms, measured with an open command batch).

The second commit batches the DSpark drafter's attention-output groups: the
draft attention-output low-rank projection ran 5 rows x 8 groups as 40 one-row
matvecs. It now runs one exact-row dispatch per group (8 per stage). This is
F16-only; other weight types keep the old loop. BF16 rounding is elementwise,
so rounding the complete low rows once afterwards is identical to the old
per-slice `ds41_matmul(..., true)`.

`DS4_METAL_F16_ROWS_LEGACY=1` restores the per-row kernel.

## Measurements

Machine: Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GiB. Model:
`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf` plus DSpark support
`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-DSpark.gguf`. Greedy, temperature 0, 512 tokens.
Alternating LEGACY/new, 2 runs each:

| condition | propose | verify | t/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K prose | 2453 -> 1969 ms (-19.7%) | 6175 -> 6128 ms (-0.8%) | 29.37 -> 30.30 (+3.1%) |
| 4K code | 860 -> 691 ms (-19.6%) | 10319 -> 10183 ms (-1.3%) | 45.48 -> 46.75 (+2.8%) |
| 40K prose | 3074 -> 2470 ms (-19.7%) | 4743 -> 4711 ms (-0.7%) | 24.88 -> 25.73 (+3.4%) |
| 40K code | 1053 -> 843 ms (-19.9%) | 11507 -> 11380 ms (-1.1%) | 40.14 -> 41.23 (+2.7%) |

The draft proposal carries the win. The verify step moves only -0.7..-1.3%:
the Engram matvec itself drops from 1.78 to 0.85 ms at rows 6 (2.1x), but the
step has enough CPU/scheduling slack to hide most of it.

`ds4-server --batched-session`: 4 sessions 21.79 -> 21.64 t/s (neutral),
8 sessions 22.89 -> 23.43 t/s (+2.4%).

## Threshold

Bench rows/legacy (same binary, LEGACY toggle), rows 2..6:

| in x out | rows 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1280x32768 (draft q_b) | 1.16 | 1.43 | 1.51 | 1.43 | 1.49 |
| 2304x5120 (shared down) | 1.03 | 1.02 | 1.17 | 1.07 | 1.00 |
| 5120x2304 (shared gate/up) | 1.02 | 1.03 | 1.13 | 1.11 | 1.17 |
| 8192x5120 (draft out_b) | 1.30 | 1.55 | 1.18 | 1.22 | 1.20 |
| 4096x8192 (draft out_a) | 0.98 | 1.18 | 1.65 | 1.27 | 1.23 |
| 6144x25600 (Engram KV) | 1.88* | 1.62 | 1.91 | 2.19 | 2.11 |
| 1280x4096 (indexer q_b) | 1.11 | 1.07 | 1.08 | 1.03 | 1.14 |

\* first call after mapping, cold.

out 2304 is nearly neutral. 4096x8192 is 0.98x at rows 2, so a slow shape
remains inside the >= 2048 threshold; it is within run variance of neutral, and
`DS4_METAL_F16_ROWS_LEGACY=1` keeps the per-row path available. hc (20480x24)
stays on the old path because its 80 dispatches per step are launch-bound.

The `ds4_gpu_dsv41_projection_rows_strided` entry is not gated by the 2048
threshold. Its DSpark attention-output group is out 1024, and the dispatch
merge is the win there: 40 -> 8 per stage, 1.45x (legacy 1.041 ms, rows
0.718 ms, open command batch, 8 groups). The code comment records the same.

## Correctness

- `tests/test_f16_row_batch` (new): 25 shapes x rows 1..8, float-bit identical
  to the single-row kernel for both the strided and contiguous entry points;
  grouped stride `5 x 8 x 4096 -> 1024`; output guard unchanged.
- DSpark 4K/40K prose/code, 2 runs each: decoded text and `DS4_DSPARK_STATS`
  counts identical in all 16 runs.
- `ds4-server --batched-session` 4/8: responses identical.
- `DS4_TEST_MODEL=... DS4_TEST_LOGIT_TOLERANCE=1e-4 make test-metal-session-batch`: PASS.
- `--decode-consistency 16`: max_abs=1.28635859 at token 32793, rms=0.301163183 (unchanged).
- `tests/test_deepseek41_graph MODEL --prefill-parity ...`: PASS for 513/1025/1537/3585.
- `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1` short DSpark run: no validation errors.
- Plain (DSpark off) 4K prose: same text, 26.67 vs 26.68 t/s.

## Scope

This is a separate PR from #1286 by design: q8_0 and F16 use different kernels
and disjoint host dispatch code, so either can land first with only light
conflicts in the shared host file. The two exact replicas of
`kernel_mul_mv_f16_f32_4` (the fused router and HC kernels) are untouched and
use different pipeline names.

V4 (non-1) models were not verified. TP and CUDA were not tested or changed.

## Commands

- correctness: `./tests/test_f16_row_batch` (add `--bench` for the threshold table)
- speed: `DS4_METAL_F16_ROWS_LEGACY=1 ./ds4-bench -m ... --mtp-model ... --dspark --prompt-file <4K/40K prose/code> --ctx-start <4096/40960> --ctx-max <same> --gen-tokens 512 --csv ...`, alternating with the same command without the env var.

title: Add IQ1_M as a routed-expert tensor type
body:
# Add IQ1_M routed-expert support (CPU reference, GPU vector path, tests)

Addresses #1268. Adds IQ1_M as a routed-expert tensor type: the CPU reference
path end to end, the GPU vector entry point, and tests for both. Purely
additive — 2,449 insertions, no deletions, no existing behaviour changed.

`tensor_is_routed_expert_type()` is **deliberately left untouched**, so no model
loads through this yet. Rationale below.

## What was already present

Less was missing than the kernel symbol counts suggest. Already in tree before
this branch:

- `block_iq1_m` in `cuda/mmq/ggml-common.h`
- `vec_dot_iq1_m_q8_1` as a `__device__` function in `cuda/mmq/vecdotq.cuh`
- `VDR_IQ1_M_Q8_1_MMVQ` / `_MMQ`
- generic ggml mat-vec instantiated for IQ1_M in `cuda/mmq/mmvq.cu`
- `ggml_blck_size` 256 and `ggml_type_size` 56 in `ds4_ggml_stubs.h`, plus
  per-arch batch caps

A prebuilt `mmvq.rocm.o` here already contained the mangled
`vec_dot_iq1_m_q8_1`, i.e. IQ1_M GPU mat-vec was compiled in with no caller.

## What this adds

**CPU** (`ds4.c`): `DS4_TENSOR_IQ1_M`, `block_iq1_m` with a 56-byte static
assert, `routed_expert_block_bytes`, `ds4_dequantize_iq1_m_block`,
`ds4_vec_dot_iq1_m_q8_K`, and `matvec_iq1_m_experts_{mid,accum}_prequant`
mirroring the Q2_K pair. Both routed-expert dispatchers gain an IQ1_M arm.

**GPU**: `ds4_mmq_iq1_m_moe_vec`, plus
`ds4_mmq_vdr_mmvq_value<GGML_TYPE_IQ1_M>` and an `if constexpr` arm in
`ds4_mmq_vec_dot_q8_1`. No new kernel was needed —
`ds4_mmq_moe_vec_impl` is type-agnostic, taking strides from
`ggml_blck_size(type)` and dispatching through `mul_mat_vec_q_switch_type`.

**Codebook**: IQ1_M needs the IQ1 grid, which ggml keeps behind
`GGML_COMMON_IMPL_C`. `scripts/gen_iq1_grid.py` extracts it and asserts 2048
entries, the `{-1,0,+1}` byte alphabet and both endpoints, emitting the
engine-side `.inc` and the test-side namespaced header from one source so they
cannot drift.

**Tests**: `tests/test_iq1_m_dequant` (13 checks, expectations derived by hand
from the format, since there is no second IQ1_M reader to compare against —
`gguf-tools` marks the type as having no dequantiser). Also
`tests/test_mmq_parity_rocm`: `cuda/mmq/test/test_mmq_parity.cu` previously had
**no build rule at all**, so none of the mmq entry points were verified
numerically on ROCm. An `IQ1_M/MOE_VEC` case passes at worst abs 0.157 and
0.182 for the two shapes, 0 bad elements, suite ALL PASS.

## Two traps worth recording

The codebook exists in two conventions and mixing them is silent:

| table | alphabet | paired delta |
|---|---|---|
| `iq1s_grid_gpu` | `{0,1,2}` | `-1 ± IQ1M_DELTA` |
| `iq1s_grid` | `{-1,0,+1}` | `± IQ1M_DELTA` |

The `-1` exists only to cancel the GPU table's `+1`. Transcribing the GPU
expression onto CPU-convention values biases every weight by exactly `-1.0`.
Caught by the test, not by reading; one test case initially agreed with the
bug because the error cancels at grid value 0.

The two tables also differ in layout. Host-side, value `v` is byte `v`; the GPU
table interleaves nibbles for `dp4a`, since the kernel splits a word into
`grid0 = (grid >> 0) & 0x0F0F0F0F` (values 0..3) and
`grid1 = (grid >> 4) & 0x0F0F0F0F` (values 4..7), so nibble `j` holds value
`(j/2) + (j%2)*4`. Under that mapping `g_gpu == g_cpu + 1` for all 16384
lanes; read sequentially, about half disagree.

## Why the admission gate stays shut

Two gaps remain before a model can load, both documented in
`docs/IQ1_M_ROUTED_EXPERTS.md`:

1. **No tiled MMQ path.** There is no `load_tiles_iq1_m`, and it is not a
   copy of `load_tiles_iq1_s`: the MMQ tile holds one `half2` per 32 values,
   while IQ1_M needs a scale per 16 and a delta sign per 8, and its 3-bit
   sub-scales are odd integers up to 15 that would overflow `dp4a`'s `int8`
   lanes if folded into the grid values. A correct loader needs a finer tile
   layout. Prefill would meanwhile go through the vector path.
2. **ROCm MoE combinations.** `routed_moe_build_plan` enumerates five
   `(gate, down)` pairs; IQ1_M needs `(29,29)`, `(29,16)` and `(16,29)`,
   each backed by kernels in `rocm/ds4_rocm_moe*.cuh`. The ROCm MoE does not
   call the `cuda/mmq` `_moe_vec` entries.

Opening the gate before those exist would let a model load and then fail in
the kernel, so it is left closed and the tree stays runnable.

## On the ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO 1017 release specifically

This branch started as an attempt to run that model, and it will not: the
blocker is unrelated to IQ1_M. `model_unmap_engram()` runs unconditionally at
model open and requires `deepseek41.engram.encoding == "e4m3_e8m0_32_row264"`.
GSQ-RCO has no `engram.encoding` key at all, ships Engram as a separate IQ4_NL
file named by `engram.file`, and indexes it with a hash scheme
(`engram_token_map`, `engram_primes`, `engram_offsets`, `engram_multipliers`)
rather than the two dense I8 264-byte-row tables ds4 expects. It also presents
four distinct per-layer expert slot sizes where `ds41_stream_cache_configure`
admits one.

Checking `mrfakename/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF` `Q2_K` the same way shows
this is **generation-wide, not one quantiser**. That file is a plain Q2_K
requantisation with no exotic expert types, and it also has no
`engram.encoding`, carrying the same hash scheme as metadata arrays rather
than tensors and no `engram.file` key. So no 1017 checkpoint loads in this
engine whatever its quantisation -- presumably the substance of #1224, and a
larger change than a download-URL refresh. Hashed Engram support would unlock
every 1017 variant at once.

That is recorded in the docs so the next person does not repeat the
investigation. IQ1_M support is useful independently of those models, which is
why this is offered as its own change.

## Verification

Both commits are based on `ee7e840` and were built and tested there, not only
on the branch they were written on:

- `ds4.c` compiles clean, no warnings, under `-O3 -Wall -Wextra -std=c99`
- `tests/test_iq1_m_dequant` passes 13/13 (`q8_K` dot agrees with the
  dequantiser to float rounding: -6789.4375 vs -6789.4365)
- `tests/test_mmq_parity_rocm` reports ALL PASS on gfx1151, including both
  `IQ1_M/MOE_VEC` shapes
- 2,516 insertions, no deletions, 14 files

title: [SECURITY] Heap buffer overflow (Out-of-bounds Write and Out-of-bounds Read) in progressive JPEG decoder (jpeg_load_mem)
Add experimental native V4.1 weights for Metal SSD inference
body:
This adds an experimental `native` converter and Metal runtime for the released V4.1 weights, including the 1017 checkpoint. Dense weights retain their original values, routed experts retain their FP4 codes and UE8M0 scales, and Engram rows remain on disk. No extra weight quantization or imatrix is used.

The native payload validator audits every dense value, routed expert, and Engram row against the source. An optional APFS-clone packer stores a dense matrix as BF16 only after every value passes an exact round-trip check. Inference retains native activation rounding and explicit scale-block/HC accumulation boundaries. SSD prefill borrows the expert-cache budget for layer reads and checked lossless expansion; decode uses the selected-expert cache. Scoped autorelease pools release streamed Metal buffers after use, and incompatible native snapshots are rejected.

This supports single-Mac, text-only Metal inference. Native weights are not admitted for CUDA, tensor parallelism, distributed inference, DSpark, vision, or concurrent decode batching. The existing Q2/Q4 arithmetic stays on its original path.

### Validation

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB, macOS 27.0.1 / Metal; upstream base `ee7e8405232c8971000cc7ba2b945b00bf6d20d3`.

- Metal and CPU builds pass. CPU inference was not run.
- All 7 conversion tests, the independent source-arithmetic test, native Metal arithmetic and key-rotation midpoint checks, HC scalar/batch checks, server unit tests, GGUF layout tests, and Engram tests pass.
- The 40-layer, 520-token fixture passes resident, uncached-streaming, and cached-streaming checks. All 33,280 logits match across modes and against the original PR. Snapshot restore, obsolete-snapshot rejection, cancellation recovery, and wide/partitioned prefill are covered. Independent first-token maximum error is `5.960464477539063e-08`.
- Metal validation passes the streamed-buffer and command-lifetime checks. Buffer footprint stays at about 164 MiB through 256 batches; the command heap stays at about 23.4 MiB through 8,192 batches.
- **Existing upstream failure:** the default V4.1 Metal suite fails at `quantization mode=3 index=5428: 11.25 != 7.5` on both untouched upstream and this branch. Native midpoint cases run under `--native-source` and pass. This PR does not change the existing Q2/Q4 quantization behavior to address that separate issue.

Commands run:

```sh
make -j2 all
make -j2 cpu
python3 tests/test_deepseek41_conversion.py
python3 tests/test_deepseek41_native_reference.py
./ds4_test --server
./tests/test_deepseek41_gguf
./tests/test_engram

# Each with MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1:
./tests/test_deepseek41_metal --native-source
./tests/test_deepseek41_metal --hc-scaled
./tests/test_metal_command_memory buffers
./tests/test_metal_command_memory
./tests/test_deepseek41_native_graph MODEL TOKENS OUTPUT # resident, stream, cache
```

### Full-checkpoint comparison

The retained native implementation at `37db79c` and this port at `5ade82f` produce **bit-identical values for all 4,266,240 logits** from a 512-token prompt and 32 generated tokens on the pinned 1017 native-lossless-BF16 checkpoint. Every value is finite. This covers the full 5,120-wide graph and all 384 experts being available to routing. The final cache configuration differs from the retained baseline, so this is a correctness comparison.

A full-width replay caught one key-rotation midpoint difference at layer 11 / position 248 during the port. Native cache rotation now keeps the original explicit FMA order, with a bounded regression test for that case.

Large-allocation speed attempts on both branches stopped on the memory-pressure guard. The matched speed comparison below uses the same full checkpoint, 16 prompt tokens, 32 greedy generated tokens, an `8GB` expert cache, and a 1,024-token context allocation. It uses the same benchmark driver with full-logit diagnostics, the public `speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt` prompt, AC power, and an identical original-PR four-token warmup before each measured arm. macOS file caching remains enabled.

| Pair and order | Original prefill t/s | Port prefill t/s | Original generation t/s | Port generation t/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original, then port | 0.76 | 0.92 | 0.69 | 0.62 |
| Port, then original | 0.79 | 0.78 | 0.62 | 0.62 |

Both pairs have exact frontier and continuation logits. Timing variation is material: the first pair showed 10.1% slower generation; the reverse pair matched generation speed, with prefill within 1.3%. These bounded measurements do not establish general performance gains or long-prompt throughput. Peak process RSS across the matched runs was 25.83 GiB.

```sh
DS4_BENCH_DECODE_LOGITS_HASH=1 DS4_BENCH_DECODE_LOGITS_DUMP=/tmp/decode.f32 \
./ds4-bench --metal --ssd-streaming -m /path/to/native-lossless-bf16.gguf \
  --ssd-streaming-cache-experts 8GB --ctx-alloc 1024 --prefill-chunk 512 \
  --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt --ctx-start 16 --ctx-max 16 \
  --gen-tokens 32 --csv /tmp/speed.csv --dump-frontier-logits-dir /tmp/logits
```

The diagnostic driver is the same `ds4_bench.c` from `37db79c`, linked against each engine; the upstream driver does not include its full decode-logit dump. The runtime reported a 1,024-row prefill capacity for both arms. Warmups used `--ctx-start 4 --ctx-max 4 --gen-tokens 0` and were excluded from timings.

<details>
<summary>Raw matched CSV rows, in execution order</summary>

```csv
run,ctx_tokens,prefill_tokens,prefill_tps,gen_tokens,gen_tps,gen_first_ms,gen_steady_tokens,gen_steady_tps,kvcache_bytes
small-before,16,16,0.76,32,0.69,1720.018,31,0.69,0
small-after,16,16,0.92,32,0.62,1641.606,31,0.62,0
reverse-after,16,16,0.78,32,0.62,1677.293,31,0.62,0
reverse-before,16,16,0.79,32,0.62,1669.940,31,0.62,0
```

</details>

### Limits and origin

Matching the retained Metal implementation establishes port consistency, not source/CUDA parity or general model quality. Later-token CPU-reference differences remain; `docs/DEEPSEEK41_NATIVE.md` records those differences, checkpoint provenance, conversion steps, and verification commands. CUDA and full coding-task acceptance were not tested for this port.

This is the native-weight work from [kernelpool/ds4#11](https://github.com/kernelpool/ds4/pull/11), ported directly to `main`. It includes only the small MXFP4 packing, HC input, and native key-cache helper prerequisites needed from [#1073](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1073); the rest of that performance branch is not included. Credit to kernelpool for those prerequisites.

title: Agent: save exact token ids with KV sessions
body:
## What

The agent saved a KV session as rendered text + backend payload.  On load,
the TP path (and any payload-0 text-only save) rebuilt the prompt by
re-tokenizing that text with `ds4_tokenize_rendered_chat()`, which has no
renderer mask.  A user spelling such as `<｜User｜>` is BPE in the live
transcript but becomes a control token on reload, so the reloaded token
sequence no longer matches the saved conversation.

Save the live token ids in a trailer after the optional title:
`magic "ATOK" / version 1 / model_id / count / uint32 ids[]`.  The loader
validates the model id, `count == hdr.tokens`, and every id against the
engine vocabulary, then reuses the ids for the TP/text-only rebuild.

A file with the flag but no trailer is a legacy file only when the trailer
position is exactly EOF.  A partial header or a short id array is an error;
it does not fall back.  Legacy files still rebuild from text, accepted only
when the count matches the header.  Strip copies a present trailer; for a
flag-only file it clears the flag in the stripped header.  The strip path
uses the header token count instead of re-tokenizing.

The trailer is appended after the existing sections, so older readers
ignore it and still load the text and payload.

## Correctness

- `./ds4_agent_test`: PASS (agent unit suite).
- `./ds4_agent_test --full-context-save <DeepSeek41 1017 IQ2>`: PASS.
  - trailer roundtrip equals the live transcript;
  - a realistic assistant turn (assistant prefix + control-tokenized DSML +
    tool result) rebuilds 69/69 tokens;
  - a transcript containing `<｜User｜>` is rejected as a legacy file with the
    count mismatch;
  - a flag-only (trailer absent) benign file falls back and loads, and strip
    clears the flag;
  - a partial header and a header without ids are rejected as corrupt, not
    rebuilt;
  - strip/load preserves `hdr.tokens` and the trailer.
- `./ds4_agent_test --real-session-rebuild <DeepSeek41>`: PASS.
  `gen1=65 gen2=9 tokens=1951 trailer=1951 rebuilt=1951 equal=1 tool=1;
  legacy load=1 restored=1951`.
- CUDA diff is 0.

## Compatibility

- New flag `DS4_KVSTORE_EXT_AGENT_TOKENS` (bit 4); trailer after the
  title/payload.
- Old readers ignore the trailing section and load text/payload.
- New readers load old files via the legacy count check; flag-only files
  (old strip) fall back to the same path.
- A legacy file whose rebuilt count differs is invalidated with an error.

## Scope

- Agent KV save/load only.  GLM/Qwen `ds4_chat_append_message`
  system/assistant masking is out of scope.
- TP hardware not verified.  The same reload path (payload-0 rebuild) was
  verified on one machine.
- No speed measurements.

title: server: render blank reasoning as absent (fixes full re-prefill after reasoning-free turns)
body:
## Symptom

An agent conversation on `ds4-server` (OpenAI-compatible chat completions, tools, thinking enabled) periodically re-prefills its entire prompt even though only a few hundred tokens changed. On a 200k-token conversation one such turn cost 201,906 tokens of prefill (~19 min at 200 t/s); on a 36k-token conversation, 32,818 tokens (3.4 min). In one day, 14 of 14 turns of this shape took that path.

## Root cause

`reasoning_content` is a must-echo field for DeepSeek-family clients, and such a client replays an assistant turn that produced **no** reasoning as a single space, because the hosted API rejects `""`.

The renderers write that body verbatim:

```c
buf_puts(&out, " thinking");
buf_puts(&out, m->reasoning ? m->reasoning : "");   /* " " lands inside the block */
buf_puts(&out, "</think>");
```

So a turn whose think block the model closed immediately is replayed as `...`, with a token between the markers that the model never sampled.

KV reuse is a prefix match, so that single token invalidates everything after it. Captured with `--trace` on a live server:

```
first_mismatch_token: 32869
token_window: [32861..32878)
  32868 ==  live 4033 " select"   | prompt 4033   " select"
  32869 !=  live 40020 "(."       | prompt 10     "("
```

(the second finding in that window is a separate, benign non-canonical tokenisation that the text tier normally absorbs)

and for the pad itself, a small controlled request:

```
first_mismatch_token: 361
  360 ==  live 128821 ""  | prompt 128821 ""
  361 !=  live 223    " "      | prompt 128822 ""
```

Two tiers are lost, not one:

* the **token tier** fails at the space;
* the **text tier** (`REUSE_MEMORY_TEXT`), which normally rescues a token mismatch by comparing rendered text instead of ids, also fails, because the rendered text now differs by a byte.

With both gone the request drops to a disk checkpoint (4,096 tokens) and re-prefills the rest. The same conversation's neighbouring turns, with real reasoning, reused 30,983 / 32,296 / 32,915 / 33,137 / 35,914 / 36,205 tokens; the padded turn reused 4,096.

## Fix

Normalise a whitespace-only reasoning body to absent at parse time, in `parse_messages()`:

```c
} else if (!strcmp(key, "reasoning_content")) {
    if (!json_content_replace(p, &msg.reasoning)) { ... }
    if (text_is_blank(msg.reasoning)) {
        free(msg.reasoning);
        msg.reasoning = NULL;
    }
}
```

Every renderer (qwen, glm, deepseek41) then treats a padded turn exactly like a turn that never had reasoning, so the replayed prompt keeps its cached prefix. Doing it at parse time rather than in each renderer keeps the class of dialects fixed at one site; there are three render sites that write `m->reasoning` verbatim today.

## Verification

`--ds41-render` through the DeepSeek4.1 renderer, after the change:

| `reasoning_content` | rendered assistant turn |
|---|---|
| `" "` | `` |
| `""` | `` |
| absent | `` |
| `"Need to run it."` | `` |

`pad`, `""` and `absent` are byte-identical.

Regression test `test_render_blank_reasoning_is_absent()` parses two identical conversations — one with `reasoning_content: " "`, one without the key — and asserts the rendered prompts compare equal. It fails on the current tree and passes with the fix.

```
before:  tests/../ds4_server.c:18314: assertion failed: ...
         tests/../ds4_server.c:18315: assertion failed: ...
after:   (both pass)
```

`./ds4_test --server` still reports one failure — `test_json_int_handles_non_finite_values` (`json_int("NaN")` expects 0). It reproduces on 5379c1c with this change stashed, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

## Note

Low-traffic path: this only triggers when a client both replays hidden reasoning and emits a turn with no reasoning. It is worth fixing anyway because the cost is a full re-prefill of the conversation, and the trigger gets *more* common as conversations get deeper, which is exactly where prefill hurts.

title: ROCm V4.1 SSD-streaming decode: 3-5 t/s with idle disk - routed-MoE vec path is the bottleneck (measurements + timing patch)
body:
## Summary

Performance breakdown for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Q2 (kyuz0's 341 GB GGUF) SSD-streaming on ROCm / Strix-Halo-class (Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495, gfx1151, 192 GB, NVMe 6.2 GB/s, build `ee7e840`, `make strix-halo`). Generation is stuck at 3-5 t/s with the disk completely idle, and the bottleneck is the routed-MoE vector path on ROCm, not streaming I/O. Instrumentation patch + measurements below; happy to turn any part of this into a PR.

## What I measured

Steady-state decode, expert cache 133 GiB (88% of experts), `/proc/diskstats` reads/s = 0 (the whole model is effectively resident between the ds4 cache and the page cache on this 192 GB host):

- per token: total ~220 ms = **submit 166-198 ms / sync 46.8 ms / engram 0.5 ms / logits 3.0 ms** (env-gated timing added in `ds41_graph_step`, patch below)
- per token by phase: **MoE 115-143 ms**, pre-MoE 3.0 ms, post-MoE 0.3 ms
- i.e. ~2.9-3.6 ms per routed-MoE layer vs ~0.3 ms of pure weight traffic at LPDDR5 bandwidth - roughly 10x off

Controls that did NOT move the number (all on the same host/prompt):

- `DS4_V41_QUEUE_DECODE` (queue the whole token, drain at the two Engram barriers instead of every layer; the tp_world==2 machinery): sync drops 46.7 -> 2.4 ms but total unchanged - the GPU was executing during the drains
- `DS4_ROCM_MMQ_TIGHT_NCOLS=1`: no change (decode takes the small-batch vec path)
- `DS4_DISABLE_V41_ENGRAM_OVERLAP=1`: within run-to-run noise
- expert cache 100/120/130/160(clamped to 133) GiB: 3.8-4.9 t/s band regardless

So: the streaming decode path resolves to `ds4_mmq_iq2_xxs_moe_gate_up_mid_vec` + `ds4_mmq_q2_K_moe_down_sum6_vec` per layer, and those kernels (quantize + vec + sanitize + selected-expert staging per call) cost ~3 ms/layer on gfx1151. That is where the 4 t/s ceiling lives.

## Two smaller findings

1. The V4.1 DSpark family check rejects the new-format drafters that carry only `general.architecture = "deepseek41-dspark"` without `dspark.target_architecture` (kyuz0's `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-DSpark-MXFP4.gguf` is the case I hit). Lenient read fixes it:
```c
const bool v41 = (!has_family || ds4_streq(family, "deepseek41")) &&
                 has_arch && ds4_streq(arch, "deepseek41-dspark");
```
(that file's tensors then bind under kyuz0's branch, so the runtime side exists in forks; on mainline ee7e840 the binding layout also differs - `mtp.N.*` tensor names vs the `stage`/`markov_head` names `dspark_weights_bind_optional` expects.)
2. ROCm V4.1 DSpark requires residency; with a 341 GB Q2 on a 192 GB host that combination is structurally out of reach. An SSD-streaming DSpark path (draft from cache-resident experts only, verify on miss) would be the multiplier for exactly this class of host.

## Instrumentation patch (off by default, two env vars)

`DS4_V41_STEP_TIMING=1`: per-16-token averages of total/submit/sync/engram/logits in `ds41_graph_step`. `DS4_V41_LAYER_TIMING=1`: per-token pre-MoE/MoE/post-MoE split. Both are fprintf-under-getenv, zero cost when unset. Diff against ee7e840 attached below; if wanted as a PR I will clean it up (thread-locals -> graph fields, DS4_LOG_TIMING integration).

<details><summary>timing patch (ds4.c, ee7e840)</summary>

```diff
@@ ds41_graph_step
+    static __thread double st_total, st_engram, st_sync, st_submit, st_logits;
+    static __thread uint32_t st_count;
+    const bool step_timing = getenv("DS4_V41_STEP_TIMING") != NULL;
+    const double st_t0 = step_timing ? now_sec() * 1000.0 : 0.0;
+    double st_engram_acc = 0.0, st_sync_acc = 0.0, st_sync_start = 0.0;
@@ engram wait inside the layer loop
+            const double st_ew0 = step_timing ? now_sec() * 1000.0 : 0.0;
             ok = (!overlap_engram || ds4_engram_reader_wait(g->engram_reader, i)) &&
                 ds4_gpu_tensor_write(g->engram_rows, 0, g->rows[i], sizeof(g->rows[i]));
+            if (step_timing) st_engram_acc += now_sec() * 1000.0 - st_ew0;
@@ drain
         const bool drain = !queue_layers || il == 13 || il + 1u == DS4_N_LAYER;
+        if (step_timing) st_sync_start = now_sec() * 1000.0;
         if (drain && !ds4_gpu_end_commands()) ok = false;
+        if (step_timing) st_sync_acc += now_sec() * 1000.0 - st_sync_start;
@@ tail, before g->pos++
+    if (step_timing) { /* aggregate and print every 16 steps */ }
```

</details>

## Environment

- host: Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 (gfx1151, 192 GB LPDDR5-8533), Ubuntu, ROCm 10.0.0-4 debs, hipcc from /opt/rocm
- model: kyuz0/deepseek-v4.1-flash-gguf `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Q2.gguf` (340.6 GiB: iq2_xxs 87 + q2_k 55 routed experts, 189 GiB i8 Engram, 748B params, 384 experts / 6 active)
- command: `./ds4 --rocm -m <q2> --ssd-streaming --ssd-streaming-cache-experts 160GB -c 4096 -t 16 --nothink`
- numbers are medians over 300-800 generated tokens, repeated runs

title: Add opt-in V4.1 decode timing breakdown (DS4_V41_STEP_TIMING, DS4_V41_LAYER_TIMING)
body:
Adds two off-by-default env diagnostics for the V4.1 GPU self-token path, from the ROCm SSD-streaming investigation in #1297:

- `DS4_V41_STEP_TIMING=1`: per-16-token averages in `ds41_graph_step` - total, submit, sync (command-buffer drains), engram (reader waits + row uploads), logits
- `DS4_V41_LAYER_TIMING=1`: per-token pre-MoE / MoE / post-MoE split across the layer loop

Cost when unset: one `getenv` per step. No behavior change otherwise; output goes to stderr alongside the existing timing prints.

Historical diagnostic output from #1297, on `ee7e8405232c8971000cc7ba2b945b00bf6d20d3` plus local timing instrumentation:

```
ds4: step timing n=288 total=216.4ms (submit=166.2 sync=46.8 engram=0.6 logits=3.0)
ds4: layer timing per token: pre=3.0ms moe=116.1ms post=0.3ms
```

These are timing buckets, not isolated kernel execution measurements. The follow-up investigation in #1297 refined the initial MoE attribution: blocking staging waits can charge earlier queued GPU work to the apparent MoE interval. The local instrumented tree was not pinned by a retained commit/hash in this PR, so these figures are historical context, not exact-head performance qualification.

Historical verification report from that investigation:
- host: Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 (gfx1151), Ubuntu, ROCm 10.0.0-4, `make strix-halo` (the default Metal target does not apply on this host)
- model: kyuz0 `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Q2.gguf` (340.6 GiB), `--ssd-streaming --ssd-streaming-cache-experts 160GB -c 4096 -t 16 --nothink`, 300-800 generated tokens per run
- flags-unset runs were reported to match the `ee7e840` binary on the same prompt (4.6-4.9 t/s band, byte-identical text). This historical report does not establish output parity or speed at the current PR head.

Current head `2492ac3465340033b72c01acb153c02d684e6f50` removes the unused `st_engram_wait_end`; the [cleanup response](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1298#issuecomment-6536641414) records `cc -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 ds4.c` changing from 1 warning to 0. That is syntax/warning evidence only.

The [M5 Max report](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1298#issuecomment-6502929040) used a modified fork with command-buffer pipelining and a changed timer boundary. Its results belong to that fork, not this exact head. Current-head unset/enabled output comparison and before/after backend speed CSVs remain unrun here. No current-head speedup or full CONTRIBUTING acceptance claim is made.

Refs #1297.

title: Accept published V4.1 DSpark metadata and Markov tensor names
body:
The published V4.1-1017 DSpark GGUF needs two loader compatibility fixes: it has `general.architecture=deepseek41-dspark` without `dspark.target_architecture`, and its final Markov tensors use `mtp.2.markov_head.embed.weight` / `mtp.2.markov_head.head.weight`.

This change accepts the missing family key for that explicit V4.1 architecture and adds V4.1-only tensor-name aliases when the corresponding canonical `markov_w1/markov_w2` name is absent. The converter maps `embed -> markov_w1` and `head -> markov_w2`. Canonical names take precedence, and existing type/dimension validation stays active. No inference kernels or forward arithmetic change.

A standalone metadata-loader test uses the real V4.1 shape and a synthetic tensor directory. Its seven cases cover canonical names, aliases, missing tensors, missing family metadata, the published 81-tensor combination, malformed alias dimensions, and canonical precedence over malformed aliases. The test reads no tensor payload and performs no inference.

Validation:

- Apple M5, Apple clang 21.0.0, arm64 macOS: `make -B -j2 ds4_test`, `./ds4_test --dspark-v41-sidecar-naming`, and `make -B -j2 cpu` all exited 0. Both clean builds had no warnings. The default test executable links Metal; the selected metadata control does not invoke it. The malformed-dimension case prints its expected refusals.
- Linux x86_64, gfx1151, HIP 7.15.26333 / AMD clang 23.0.0git: `make -j2 strix-halo ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151 HIPCC=/opt/rocm/bin/hipcc CC=/usr/bin/cc` exited 0 with no warnings. All tracked source files matched the pinned Git blobs before and after the build.
- That new Linux binary, using `--cpu --inspect -m <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Q2.gguf> --mtp-model <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-DSpark-MXFP4.gguf>`, exited 0 and reported `support binding: tensors=78 missing=0 invalid=0 metadata_errors=0`. The draft directory contains 81 tensors; 78 is the binder count. Inspection used inherited read-only FDs and did not prefetch full weights or execute CPU/GPU inference.

Target and draft are the public kyuz0 files at revision `20408f699619df7071aa7cda6034e9cef5bf804b`. The draft SHA-256 is `d3efe0b1f6b6fea54f1c58c5cbeb3fded5967b15b64476aed00c95806ad3e3e9`.

Actual DSpark generation quality, acceptance rate, and speed are still being qualified. This is loader compatibility evidence, not an inference or performance result.

Refs #1297.
