title: Metal ssd-streaming: one hung pread() wedged the whole server forever — the pread task pool waits on the done condvar with no timeout
body:
## Symptom

`ds4-server` on macOS (M5 Max 128 GB, Metal, `--ssd-streaming`, main V4.1 Flash GGUF on the internal SSD) froze completely at 2026-11-09 05:40:10, after ~7 h of continuous agentic traffic on one boot: the log froze mid-request (ctx 37.9k, `gen=200`) and the process sat at CPU 0.0%; the request thread's sample stack runs through speculative verification (`ds41_session_verify` → `ds41_moe_batch` → `ds4_gpu_stream_expert_pread_tasks`), the in-flight request never returned and later requests just queued. Not an error — silence.

## Diagnosis

Thread sample: one streaming-pool worker blocked inside `pread()` on `g_model_fd` (`ds4_gpu_stream_expert_pread_into`, ds4_metal.m:13805 at `b3f5018`), coordinator waiting for task completion with no timeout (`pthread_cond_wait` on `g_stream_expert_pread_pool_done_cond`, ds4_metal.m:14005). The server serves one request at a time: one hung read = total service loss.

Exonerated: system sleep / thermal / jetsam (no events; kernel log clean); the disk itself as a failing device in general (a `ls` of the volume was instant and a different GGUF on the same volume read fine — the hung read was the main GGUF specifically); the read loop logic (this is a plain `pread()` that simply never returns).

The escalation is the worst part: `SIGKILL` did not reap it: the process sat forever in `?Es` ("trying to exit", thread stuck in kernel) and never died, and a `dd` of the same file from a fresh process on a fresh fd hung too. That is consistent with a vnode- or driver-level wedge — unrecoverable from userspace; recovery required a system reboot.

## Why this is worth hardening even without a deterministic repro

First occurrence of this signature in ~2 weeks of near-daily 10 h sessions (to 320k context) on this box. But the pool has zero tolerance for this failure class: `ds4_gpu_stream_expert_pread_tasks` waits for all workers indefinitely and the kernel I/O path offers no cancellation point — so a single hung read converts into a forever-silent stall: the operator sees a frozen engine with no signal anywhere.

Related prior work (both PRs):
- #238 (May, PR closed unmerged as "fixed more organically") reported a worker stall in a GPU/Metal kernel call — same "stuck worker stops the server" shape, but that process was SIGKILL-able and the layer was GPU, not file I/O.
- #1125 (open PR) hardens the paths where `pread()` *returns* an error (slot return, etc) — a pread that never returns can never take an error path.

## Proposal

A bounded completion wait: the coordinator waits the done condvar with a deadline (say 30–60 s, env-tunable). On expiry, mark outstanding tasks failed (the slot-return machinery from #1125 covers these error paths once landed), treat the wedged task's destination buffer as leaked (a late-returning `pread()` would still write into it), return an error to the in-flight request, and print one line naming the wedged `(offset, len)`. Deliberately not a watchdog thread (cf. #238): no new thread, no process restart — just a deadline on the existing pool wait (the pooled path; the single-task inline path has no wait to bound). It cannot resurrect a driver-level-stuck thread (our instance showed even SIGKILL failing there) — but it turns a silent unbounded hang into a visible bounded failure, and in the milder case (device hiccup that recovers) the server survives.

Happy to send a small PR (deadline + error path + one log line) if wanted.

Environment: macOS 26.7.2 (Darwin 25) arm64, M5 Max, Metal backend, `--ssd-streaming`. Our build is a fork — but `ds4_gpu_stream_expert_pread_tasks`, `ds4_gpu_stream_expert_pread_into` and the pool-wait function holding the 14005 condvar are all byte-identical to upstream `b3f5018` (verified by diff), so the seam is upstream code as-is. The `spindump` capture was lost in the reboot's tmp cleanup; the description above is everything we recorded at the time.

title: Metal GLM indexed decode attention returns wrong values for large windows (threadgroup memory not checked; hits the MTP draft)
body:
**What happens**

`kernel_glm_attention_indexed_decode` (`metal/dsv4_misc.metal`) computes the attention scores of one GLM decode step over the selected positions and stores all of them in threadgroup memory: `red[256]`, then `scores[n_selected]`, then `lora_sum[kv_lora_dim]`. `ds4_gpu_glm_attention_indexed_decode_typed_tensor` in `ds4_metal.m` requests `(256 + n_selected + kv_lora_dim) * 4` bytes of threadgroup memory for it, without comparing that to `maxThreadgroupMemoryLength`, which is 32 KiB on Apple GPUs. With `kv_lora_dim = 512` the request exceeds 32 KiB from 7,425 positions on.

The GLM 5.3 MTP draft step attends to every position since drafting started in the session (`glm_mtp_min_pos .. pos`), so in a long `--mtp` session the window passes that size. On CUDA the equivalent kernel fails loudly (#1243). On Metal nothing is reported: the dispatch goes through and, past a hardware-dependent size, the kernel reads outside its allocation and returns wrong attention outputs. The verifier then rejects the drafts, so the visible symptom is MTP acceptance falling to nothing while every token still pays for the draft.

**Reproduction, no model needed**

M1, 16 GB, macOS 15.7.4, Xcode Command Line Tools 16.4. The test case `large_decode_window_cases()` added to `tests/test_glm_attention.c` in the PR for #1243 (branch https://github.com/n7olkachev/ds4/tree/glm-staged-decode-smem) calls `ds4_gpu_glm_attention_indexed_decode_typed_tensor` on synthetic inputs and compares the result with a double-precision softmax on the CPU. On Metal that test skips sizes above the limit so the suite passes; to see the failure, delete the `#ifdef __APPLE__` block in that function (or change the list of sizes) and run `make test-glm-attention`. Output on `main` @ b3f5018 with sizes added between 7,424 and 32,768:

```
large decode window count=7424 f16=0: PASS
large decode window count=7425 f16=0: PASS
large decode window count=12033 f16=0: PASS
large decode window count=16000 f16=0: PASS
large decode window count=16384 f16=0: FAIL head=0 0.26433906 != -9.0279781e-05
large decode window count=20000 f16=0: FAIL head=0 0.264205039 != -9.96857057e-05
large decode window count=32768 f16=0: FAIL head=0 0.221164003 != -6.48633294e-05
```

The f16 cache format gives the same values. With Metal API validation on (`METAL_DEVICE_WRAPPER_TYPE=1`) the first size above the limit is rejected before any result:

```
-[MTLDebugComputeCommandEncoder setThreadgroupMemoryLength:atIndex:]:816: failed assertion `length(51200) must be <= 32768.'
```

(51,200 bytes is the request for 12,032 positions.) So the API contract is violated from 7,425 positions on; that the results stay correct until about 16k on this M1 is luck of the hardware, and other chips may differ.

**Possible fixes**

Same shape as the CUDA fix in the #1243 PR: keep the threadgroup row for windows that fit (the DSA window of 2,051 positions always does) and write the scores of larger windows to a device buffer that the same thread reads back in the same order, so the softmax and the reductions do not change. Until then, refusing the dispatch when the request exceeds `maxThreadgroupMemoryLength` would at least turn the silent wrong output into the visible `glm mtp step failed` that CUDA users see.

I can send the Metal change if you want it from me. I can verify correctness on an M1 but not performance on M3 Ultra or M5.

Logs of these runs: https://github.com/n7olkachev/ds4-qa-logs/tree/main/1243-glm-staged-decode-smem/mac-metal

title: Stage GLM decode attention scores in global memory past 12,032 rows
body:
Fixes #1243.

**The bug**

The CUDA kernel `glm_attention_decode_weights_staged_kernel` (`ds4_cuda.cu`) computes the attention scores of one GLM decode step over the selected positions and keeps all of them in dynamic shared memory, `(256 + n_selected) * 4` bytes. It never raises the 48 KiB launch limit, so at 12,033 positions the launch fails with `invalid argument`. The GLM 5.3 MTP draft attends to every position since drafting started in the session, so long sessions reach that size, and from then on every token logs

```
ds4: CUDA glm staged decode weights launch failed: invalid argument
ds4: glm mtp step failed at stage 'attention' (pos N)
```

while decoding continues without MTP. Raising the limit with `cudaFuncSetAttribute` would only move the failure to the device maximum (99 KB on Ada and consumer Blackwell, 227 KB on Hopper), that is about 24k or 56k positions.

**The change**

The kernel gets a compile-time template parameter `SHARED_SCORES`. For windows that fit in the 48 KiB every CUDA device allows without an opt-in (up to 12,032 positions) the kernel keeps the shared-memory score row exactly as before; that instantiation is the existing code. For larger windows the scores go to the global `weights` scratch buffer that the lora stage reads next, and shared memory holds only the 256 reduction slots. Each thread reads back only the scores it wrote itself, in the same order, so the softmax passes and the two block reductions perform the same operations in the same order in both layouts. The launch site picks the instantiation from the window size. No new flags, no device queries. ROCm is not affected, its GLM decode kernels are separate.

**Test**

`tests/test_glm_attention.c` gets `large_decode_window_cases()`: it calls `ds4_gpu_glm_attention_indexed_decode_typed_tensor` (the entry the MTP step uses) with windows of 511, 512, 2051, 12032, 12033, 16384 and 65536 positions, f16 and f32 cache formats, and compares the result with a double-precision softmax computed on the CPU (tolerance 0.005), plus a repeat run for determinism. On `main` the 12,033 case fails with the error above. The CUDA build had no test of this kernel before: the existing indexed decode check in that file is compiled for Metal and ROCm only, because the non-typed entry it uses does not exist on CUDA. On Metal the kernel has its own, larger problem with these window sizes (see below), so the test skips sizes above the Metal threadgroup limit there and prints a SKIP line with the reason.

**Checks, before (main @ b3f5018) and after (this branch), same machine for every pair**

Kernel level:

- `make cuda-generic && make CUDA_ARCH=native test-glm-attention` and `make tests/test_glm53_kda && ./tests/test_glm53_kda`: pass on an A40 (sm_86), an H200 (sm_90) and an H100 (sm_90).
- Output unchanged where the old kernel worked: a small program calls the same function on both builds with identical inputs and hashes the heads output (FNV-1a) for 511, 512, 600, 2048, 2051, 4096, 8192, 12000 and 12032 positions, f16 and f32, 8 and 64 heads. All hashes equal on the A40 and the H200.

With GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2 (96,505,816,384 bytes, sha256 e81fd624…5b32, which is also the Hugging Face ETag), single-tier CUDA on one GPU:

- `gguf-tools/quality-testing/score_official` on the 100-case GLM 5.3 Flash Z.AI fixture at ctx 4096 and on the eight long cases with rendered prompts at ctx 8192 (the two checks QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md lists for a GLM 5.3 attention change): result files byte-identical before and after. H100 values: avg NLL 0.460780550, first-token match 88/100, greedy prefix 7.000; long cases 0.677514420, 6/8, 2.500.
- The scenario from the issue: `ds4-server --cuda --mtp --mtp-timing --ctx 32768`, three greedy turns, the second user message about 17,000 tokens. Before: 96 `launch failed` plus 96 `mtp step failed` lines, one pair per generated token from the second turn on, drafts accepted only in the first turn. After: no failures, 36 drafts accepted on the H200 and 38 on the H100 across the whole window, and the generated text (from `--trace`, thinking included) is byte for byte the text of the same chat run without `--mtp`.

Speed: the hashing program also times each call of `ds4_gpu_glm_attention_indexed_decode_typed_tensor` from launch to synchronize, 64 heads (as in GLM 5.3 Flash), f16 cache (the format the model path uses), median of 101 calls per size, old and new build alternated three times, H200:

| positions in the window | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 2,051 | 506-509 µs | 507-508 µs |
| 4,096 | 961-974 µs | 962-978 µs |
| 12,032 | 2,794-2,813 µs | 2,796-2,814 µs |
| 12,033 | launch fails | 2,933-2,956 µs |
| 16,384 | launch fails | 3,970-4,001 µs |

Up to 12,032 positions it is the same code, so the same numbers. Two other variants were measured and dropped: a kernel that always uses global memory (on an A40 30% faster for 4k-12k positions, on the H200 4.5% slower at every size) and a runtime choice between shared and global through one pointer (the compiler then uses generic addressing and the shared path gets 47-51% slower).

Not run: the Q4_K fixture (178 GiB file) and Metal with the model.

**Metal**

`kernel_glm_attention_indexed_decode` (`metal/dsv4_misc.metal`) stores its scores in threadgroup memory the same way, `(256 + n_selected + kv_lora_dim) * 4` bytes, and `ds4_metal.m` requests that size without checking `maxThreadgroupMemoryLength` (32 KiB on Apple GPUs). On an M1, Metal API validation rejects the dispatch above 7,424 positions; without validation the output is correct up to 16,000 positions and wrong from 16,384 on, with no error. Reported separately with the same test case: #1336. This PR only skips those sizes in the test on Apple.

**Logs**

Every log has a header with date, host, GPU, driver, nvcc version, commit and the command that produced it: https://github.com/n7olkachev/ds4-qa-logs (the H100 and H200 runs with `00-COMPARISON.txt` and `MANIFEST.sha256`, the A40 kernel logs, the hashing program, the two rejected variants as patches).

I have no GB10; a run on a Spark would be welcome.

title: Copy model tensors into device memory on a discrete CUDA GPU when they fit
body:
On a single discrete NVIDIA GPU, ds4 can leave the whole model in host RAM and read it over PCIe on every token, even when the card has plenty of free memory. On an H200 with 139 GiB free, GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 generates at 3.2 t/s.

This PR copies the weights into GPU memory at startup when they fit. Same machine, same model file: 36 t/s, and the output is byte-identical to main. DGX Spark and other integrated GPUs keep the current behavior.

## Why it happens

On the default single-GPU path (single-tier, no SSD streaming), the engine registers the whole GGUF mmap with `cudaHostRegister` (`cudaHostRegisterMapped`), which pins it and lets the GPU read it in place. After that, `cuda_model_range_ptr` returns a pointer into that mapping for every tensor, and the `cudaMalloc` + `cudaMemcpy` code further down is never reached.

On a Spark this is right, because host memory and GPU memory are the same memory. On a discrete card every weight read goes over PCIe.

It's easy to miss:

- The startup log looks normal. It prints `startup model preparation covered 89.87 GiB of tensor spans in 0.059s` and `resident model 89.87 GiB`, but nothing was copied.
- The env vars that should force a copy do nothing here. `DS4_CUDA_COPY_MODEL` only triggers a copy in `ds4_gpu_set_model_map`, which this path doesn't call. `DS4_CUDA_COPY_MODEL_CHUNKED` calls `cuda_model_copy_chunked`, which returns right away when the mapping is registered.
- Some setups are fast by accident. If the driver refuses the registration, ds4 falls through to the copy path. That's the RTX PRO 6000 in #431 (`host registration skipped: operation not supported`). The H200 accepts the registration and gets the slow path.

## What this PR changes

At startup the engine already loops over all the tensor spans of the model. Before that loop it now asks the CUDA backend (`ds4_gpu_plan_model_cache`) whether to copy the spans into device memory or leave them mapped like today.

It copies only when all of these are true:

- the GPU is discrete (`cudaDevAttrIntegrated` is 0)
- this model's mapping is the registered one (see the DSpark note below)
- SSD streaming is off and `DS4_CUDA_NO_MODEL_COPY` is not set
- tensors + context + reserve fit in free device memory

Context is the estimate the startup memory line already prints, times the planned sessions. Reserve is max(1 GiB, 2% of the card). It covers what is allocated after the model and is not in that estimate: CUDA graphs, cuBLAS workspaces, transient buffers.

In every other case the loop does exactly what it does on main.

Startup prints one line when it copies, and one when the model doesn't fit:

```text
ds4: CUDA copying 89.87 GiB of model tensors into device memory (2.97 GiB context planned, 139.05 GiB free)
ds4: CUDA model stays host-mapped: 89.87 GiB tensors + 2.97 GiB context + 2.80 GiB reserve exceed 28.53 GiB free device memory
```

A few details:

- The copy reads from the mapping that is already pinned, so it is fast: 89.87 GiB in 1.8 s on the H200 (132 allocations of 0.5 to 1 GiB).
- `cuda_model_range_ptr` already looks for a device copy before the mapping, so anything the loop didn't copy works as it does now.
- If an allocation fails anyway, the remaining spans stay mapped and startup continues.
- No new flags. The existing `DS4_CUDA_NO_MODEL_COPY=1` turns the copy off, to compare the two on the same machine.

## What doesn't change

- DGX Spark and other integrated GPUs: the check returns before anything is copied.
- SSD streaming.
- Multi-GPU placement: it has its own per-device caches and doesn't go through this code.
- TP shards: `ds4_gpu_set_model_map_spans` doesn't register the mapping, so nothing is copied.
- ROCm and Metal: the new call is only compiled for CUDA.

DSpark needs a note. Loading a support model (`--dspark --mtp-model`) replaces the main model's registration, because there is only one slot. So today the main model already goes through the fd cache and ends up on the card, and the support model is the one read over PCIe. This PR leaves the main model alone there and copies the support model.

## Tests

Everything ran on one machine: H200 (141 GB), driver 595.91.07, nvcc 12.8, Ubuntu 24.04. main is b3f5018. The branch was tested at 136e766, which is the commit the logs name. Its head is now 31c44dc: same tree, only the commit message was reworded. The models are GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 and DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 Q2.

Logs and the scripts that produced them are in https://github.com/n7olkachev/ds4-qa-logs/tree/main/cuda-resident-model. `00-COMPARISON.txt` has main and the branch side by side, and every log starts with the commit and the command that was run.

### Correctness

main and the branch give the same result in every test. Where a test writes a file (scorer TSVs, CLI stdout), the files are byte-identical.

| Test | Result on both |
|---|---|
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2, 100-case fixture, ctx 4096 | avg_nll 0.459560487, first_match 89, avg_lcp 7.390 |
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2, eight long cases, ctx 8192 | avg_nll 0.669916439, first_match 6, avg_lcp 2.500 |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2, 100-case `data/flash` scorer, ctx 4096 | avg_nll 0.412182337, first_match 53, avg_lcp 4.670 |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2, `ds4_test --logprob-vectors` | OK |
| Greedy 64-token CLI answer (GLM, V4 Flash, V4 Flash + DSpark) | same stdout |

The first four are the section 3 gates from `QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md`.

The GLM CLI answer is also the same in the two cases where the branch doesn't copy: with `DS4_CUDA_NO_MODEL_COPY=1`, and with another process holding 110 GiB of the card so the model doesn't fit. Speed in both is main's (3.39 and 3.38 t/s, main is 3.38).

Also:

- `make test-cuda-model-copy` is new and needs no model file. It uses a 64 MiB fake mapping with three spans and a gap. It checks the copy / don't copy decision, the opt-out, and that free device memory drops by the size of the spans. It also checks that reads return the same values before and after the copy: at a span start, inside a span, and in the gap that is never copied. It passes under Compute Sanitizer (memcheck, initcheck, racecheck, synccheck).
- `make cuda-regression` passes.
- `make cuda-generic` and `make ds4_test` on the H200, and `make` on an M1, build with no new warnings.

Ignore the wall times in the logs: some of main's runs shared the GPU with other jobs. The benchmark below ran on an idle GPU.

### Speed

`ds4-bench --cuda --prompt-file speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt --ctx-start 2048 --ctx-max 8192 --step-incr 2048 --gen-tokens 64`

Each cell is main → this PR.

| Model | Context | Prefill (t/s) | Generation (t/s) | First token (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 | 2048 | 117.6 → 962.7 | 3.23 → 36.17 | 305 → 26 |
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 | 4096 | 114.8 → 824.0 | 3.22 → 35.85 | 313 → 28 |
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 | 6144 | 112.9 → 824.4 | 3.22 → 35.76 | 310 → 28 |
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 | 8192 | 115.0 → 818.6 | 3.22 → 35.40 | 310 → 28 |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2 | 2048 | 394.5 → 1347.5 | 3.90 → 47.42 | 245 → 18 |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2 | 4096 | 406.7 → 1452.0 | 3.88 → 46.34 | 257 → 21 |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2 | 6144 | 404.3 → 1435.2 | 3.88 → 46.21 | 257 → 21 |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2 | 8192 | 403.4 → 1425.0 | 3.88 → 45.10 | 257 → 21 |

Generation speed in the CLI, short prompt, 64 tokens:

| Model | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 | 3.38 t/s | 47.38 t/s |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2 | 4.20 t/s | 71.26 t/s |
| V4 Flash 0731 Q2 + DSpark | 47.05 t/s | 61.27 t/s |

The DSpark row moves less because the main model was already on the card there (see the DSpark note above).

For reference, the repo's docs list a DGX Spark at 531 / 14.35 t/s (prefill / decode) for GLM 5.3 Flash Q2 and 826 / 18 t/s for Flash Q2.

## What I haven't tested

**DGX Spark.** I don't have one. So "nothing changes on a Spark" comes from reading the code, and the integrated-GPU part of the new test has never run. On a Spark, `make test-cuda-model-copy` should print `integrated GPU keeps the mapping: PASS`, and a Flash or GLM startup log should contain neither `CUDA copying` nor `stays host-mapped`.

**A tight fit.** The H200 had a lot of room: 139 GiB free for 90 GiB of tensors and 3 GiB of context. I haven't tried a card where the model only just fits. Take a 96 GB card with the 81 GiB Flash Q2 file: 81 GiB of tensors + 0.4 GiB of context (ctx 4096) + 1.9 GiB of reserve leaves about 11 GiB for everything else, including the q8 fp16 cache. That cache has its own budget check, so I expect it to just cache less, but I haven't seen it. `DS4_CUDA_NO_MODEL_COPY=1` gives the old behavior to compare against. (The RTX PRO 6000 in #431 refused the registration. If it still does, this PR changes nothing for it.)

## Seen on main, not part of this PR

- GLM 5.3 on this H200 logs `CUDA glm shared swiglu one failed: operation would make the legacy stream depend on a capturing blocking stream` and `matmul_q8_0 quantize launch failed` on every run, on main and on the branch. The results are still correct.
- With a support model loaded, the main model's mapping is no longer registered (the DSpark note above). If the fd cache runs out of room on a small card, its fallback is a pointer into a mapping that is not pinned anymore. I haven't reproduced this, it comes from reading the code.

title: Speed up DeepSeek V4 Flash prefill on ROCm gfx1151 (Strix Halo)
body:
Prefill on Strix Halo is 58-73% faster from 2K to 16K context. Decode speed is unchanged, and official-continuation quality on the 0731 release GGUF is as good as `main` or slightly better.

The first five commits are standalone fixes found along the way, and each builds on its own:

1. **Compute the ROCm visual attention scale with host math.** `main` does not build with ROCm 7.14, because HIP's `rsqrtf` is device-only.
2. **Make the paired ROCm Q8_0 matmul match the single kernel.** An explicit FMA pins the `-ffast-math` reassociation. Without it, `main` fails the paired Q8_0 exactness check in `./ds4_test` on ROCm.
3. **Split ROCm model weight copies at pinned registration edges.** HIP rejects a host-to-device copy that crosses two pinned registrations.
4. **Link the ROCm kernel tests against the compat object.** Before this, `test-mxfp4-rocm`, `test-glm53-kda-rocm` and `test-glm-attention-rocm` failed to link.
5. **Add an IQ2_XXS MMQ pair entry without the output sanitize pass.** The ROCm SwiGLU consumer already drops non-finite values.

The sixth commit, **Speed up DeepSeek V4 Flash prefill on ROCm gfx1151**, is the speedup itself:

- Projections on batches of 32 or more tokens run as hipBLASLt F16 GEMMs, with each class of shapes autotuned once.
- One 32-head WMMA attention kernel handles every prefill chunk.
- The Q2_K routed-down projection is a tiled F16 WMMA kernel. It runs only when the MMQ gate/up pair has written every routed mid row in F16. Every other gate/up route keeps the existing hot/cold split.
- The indexer's weighted head sum stays in WMMA registers.
- The rocBLAS F32 path, the custom WMMA row-tile kernels and the transposed F16 weight cache are removed.

The only change outside ROCm is in `ds4.c`, where ROCm now gets two things Metal already had:
- the F16 staging buffer;
- the F16 RMS-fold HC projection.

Metal and CUDA behavior is unchanged. `cuda/mmq` gains one entry point, `ds4_mmq_iq2_xxs_moe_pair_unsanitized`, which the CUDA paths do not call.

## Test setup

- Framework-class Strix Halo: Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 128 GB.
- ROCm 7.14, using the `rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.14.0-full` container.
- Main model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731.gguf`, with `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-support-0731.gguf`. Both are checked against their SHA-256 sums.
- Second model: the Vision-Exp Q2 GGUF (text only), scored against its own matched fixtures.
- Baseline: `main` (b3f5018) plus commit 1, because `main` alone does not build on ROCm.
- Only one model process ran at a time, on an idle machine, with a `MemAvailable - CmaFree` watchdog that stops the run below 3 GiB.
  - The lowest usable memory during model runs was 7.9 GiB.
  - There was no OOM, GPU reset or watchdog stop.

## Build gates

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `make clean && make strix-halo` | builds, 0 warnings |
| ROCm test binaries and `score_official` | build, 0 warnings |
| `make cpu` | builds, 0 warnings |
| Each intermediate commit | builds |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

## Tests that need no model

All of these pass:

- `./ds4_test --server`, `./ds4-eval --self-test-extractors` and `./ds4_agent_test`
- `tests/test_layer_pack` (97/97), `tests/test_engine_mgpu_placement` (114/114) and `tests/test_gpu_args`
- `tests/test_gpu_args_cli.sh` (86 pass, 0 fail) and `tests/test_prompt_prefix`
- `q4k-dot-test` (4/4), `mxfp4-dot-test` (4/4) and `test-session-state`
- `make test-linux-memory test-rocm-memory`
- `make test-mxfp4-rocm`: zero failures for `mid` and `out` at 1, 3, 32, 128 and 512 tokens
- `make test-glm53-kda-rocm test-glm-attention-rocm`, also with `DS4_ROCM_GLM_SELECTED_ATTN_HEAD_TILE=1`
- `tests/test_deepseek41_rocm` and `tests/test_mmvq_rocm`
- `./ds4_test --metal-kernels`, which runs the isolated GPU kernel checks on ROCm

## Full `./ds4_test` with the 0731 model

Command:

```
DS4_TEST_MODEL=<0731 q2> DS4_TEST_DSPARK=<0731 DSpark support> ./ds4_test
```

- **Branch: `ds4 tests: ok`.** Every check passes.
  - Highlights: `logprob-vectors`, `local-golden-vectors` (top5 5/5, top20 20/20), `metal-tensor-equivalence`, `dspark-verify-depth`, the session tests, `long-context` and `server`.
  - Tests that need Metal, Qwen, GLM, MTP or SSD streaming are skipped.
- **Baseline: fails.** The failure is the paired Q8_0 exactness check (`mismatches=57/77`), which commit 2 fixes.

## Speed

On the 0731 model:


| 8192 | 258.38 | 414.12 | 14.01 | 14.00 |
| 12288 | 252.16 | 411.24 | 13.87 | 13.86 |
| 16384 | 247.58 | 404.62 | 13.76 | 13.75 |

All numbers are tok/s. The Vision-Exp model gives the same numbers within 1%.

## Quality

`score_official` on each GGUF, before and after the change:

| Model / fixture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 0731: `data/flash` (100 cases, API logprobs) @4096 | NLL 0.402278, first-token 55/100, API top-1 86.04% | NLL 0.399036, first-token 54/100, API top-1 86.17% |
| Vision-Exp: `flash-vision-exp-openrouter-novita-100` @4096 | NLL 0.393933, first-token 60/100 | NLL 0.394799, first-token 61/100 |
| Vision-Exp: `tests/test-vectors/flash-vision-exp`, 5 cases (two are about 5K tokens) @8192 | NLL 0.380246, 4/5 | NLL 0.345902, 4/5 |

- On 0731, `compare_scores.py` gives an NLL change of -0.81%, and the branch wins 52 of the 100 cases.
- With `--quality`, the logits are bit-identical to `main` (max-abs 0), so the full-FP32 reference path is untouched.

## DSpark

On the 0731 model:

- **hipBLASLt timing varies between processes and engines.** Algorithm autotune is timed per engine, so two runs can pick different algorithms for the same shape. That moves the full logits by about max-abs 1.

  - With the Vision-Exp model (not 0731), `logprob-vectors` and `local-golden-vectors` sit at their thresholds and flip between runs, and they flip on `main` too. Vision-Exp's own FP32 `--quality` reference agrees with this branch on the case that flips.

title: server: align the continued KV checkpoint step with the prefill chunk schedule
body:
Continued checkpoints are written from the prefill_chunk listener, so the only positions the cache can store are the backend's chunk boundaries.  The default interval (10000, rounded to 10240 by the 2048 alignment) is not a multiple of the default graph prefill chunk (4096, or 8192 for PRO; CUDA tensor parallelism uses 2048), so frontiers landed only at lcm(10240, chunk): every second intended rung at 4096, every fourth at 8192.  Measured on V4 Flash with a 25.8k-token prompt resent by a stateless client: one rung at 20480 and 5,307 tokens re-prefilled per request; with a chunk-aligned step, rungs at 12288 and 24576 and 1,211 tokens per request.

Default the interval to 8192, the smallest value every current chunk size divides, name the chunk defaults, and expose them through the test helper ds4_test_default_prefill_caps() so a unit test can replay each chunk schedule and require a frontier at every multiple of the step.  The test fails on the old default.

This fix was inspired by the investigation into #1323 root cause.

title: ds4-server rejects WebP images with a misleading "invalid JSON request" error
body:
## Environment

- ds4 commit: b3f5018 (2026-11-03)
- Mac Studio M3 Ultra, 256 GB, macOS 26.4
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-Q2.gguf, with --vision DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Vision.gguf
- Flags: --ctx 262144 --kv-disk-dir ... --kv-disk-space-mb 65536

## What happens

A chat completion request whose image_url is a WebP data URL is refused before any processing:

```
HTTP 400
{"error":{"message":"invalid JSON request","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

The JSON is valid. The same request with the same picture as JPEG or PNG works.

Results on /v1/chat/completions, one user message with one text part and one image part:

| Image | Result |
|---|---|
| JPEG, 2 KB to 37 KB | 200 |
| PNG, 51 KB, 2.2 MB and 8.9 MB | 200 |
| WebP lossy (VP8), 372 and 500 bytes | 400 |
| WebP lossy (VP8), 81 KB photo | 400 |
| WebP lossless (VP8L), 23 KB | 400 |

## Why it matters

Agent harnesses that transcode images to WebP fail on the first such image. DeepSeek Harness does this for PNG files read by its read_image tool. Because the image stays in the conversation history, every later request fails as well and the session cannot recover. The error text points at JSON, which makes the cause hard to find.

## Request

1. Accept WebP input, or
2. return a specific error such as "unsupported image format: image/webp", and list the supported formats in the README.

title: server: write a continued KV checkpoint at the first chunk past each step
body:
The continued-checkpoint listener runs only on `prefill_chunk` events and stored a frontier only when the live length was an exact multiple of the step.  The positions it is offered are the backend's chunk boundaries, which need not include those multiples: the default graph prefill chunk is 4096 (8192 for PRO), so the 10240 step landed on every second or fourth rung, and DeepSeek V4.1 SSD streaming sweeps most of a prompt in one chunk followed by a token-major tail, so no rung was ever reachable.

Store at the first chunk that enters a step bucket past the last frontier instead.  This stores everywhere the exact-multiple rule did (a multiple of the step above the last frontier is always in a later bucket) and additionally at the first chunk past each boundary.  Every bucket gets one frontier whatever the chunk schedule, a token-major tail does not add a frontier per token, and a cold cut inside a bucket claims it through the existing continued suppression, so no near-duplicate rung follows it.  A disk hit seeds the slot's frontier, as the kvstore already does for its own counter, so resuming inside the loaded bucket does not immediately re-store it.

Measured on V4 Flash with the default interval and a 32.9k-token history resent by a stateless client: frontiers at 12288, 20480 and 32768 instead of 20480 alone, and later requests prefill 135 tokens in 0.6 s instead of 12.4k.

This fix was inspired by the investigation into https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1323 root cause.

title: Save image conversations in the disk KV cache
body:
A session that holds an image is never written to the disk KV cache, and a request with an image never reads from it. The cache key is rendered text, and in rendered text every image is the same run of placeholder tokens. After a restart or a slot switch an image conversation prefills from zero, its text included (#908, #1007).

**The change**, in two commits:

1. *Keep the live text tier when the checkpoint holds an image.* An image stands in rendered prompt text as a marker with a per-request nonce. The marker now has room for the image identity instead: the fingerprint and the row count, which is what a live session already checks before it reuses image rows. The request text and the text rendered from the live tokens are both written with it, and the memory-text tier compares those. Before, that tier could not match once an image was in the session (#1214).
2. *Save image conversations in the disk KV cache.* Checkpoints are keyed by that same text, and the image identities are stored with the payload. Lookup is unchanged: the longest stored text that is a byte prefix of the request's. A request therefore reaches a checkpoint only with the same images at the same places, and a request with a different image still reuses the text before it.

**Why it is safe.** Text cannot impersonate an image. A transcript that spells a marker outside its images gets no key, and after a load `build_live_prompt_suffix()` checks the restored identities against the images of the request, as it does for live reuse. A checkpoint that fails that check is not used. Text-only cache files keep their format: the identities are a new section under a new header flag. Tensor-parallel and distributed sessions do not save image checkpoints, because their payload load cannot restore image rows.

**One fix on the way.** `build_live_prompt_suffix()` assumed wrapper tokens around the image rows only for GLM. Qwen wraps its rows the same way, so an image appended to a live Qwen text checkpoint lost both tokens. I could not run Qwen vision, so this part is by inspection. #1221 measured the same wrapper token on a real Qwen model.

**Overlap with open PRs.** #1221 fixes the live text tier alone, with a smaller patch. The first commit here does it differently because the disk key needs the same text. #1322 covers two cases of the second commit: the text conversation that an image request evicts, and the text before the first image. #961 also persists image KV and has conflicted with main since September. I will rebase on whichever of these you take.

About half of the added lines are tests.

## Testing

- `make`, `./ds4_test --server` and `make test-session-state` pass on an M5 Max, and the CPU objects compile. New unit cases cover the payload and store round trips, the refusals, the key naming, and the #1214 probe, which fails when the probe compares the raw prompt text.
- **Live test.** M5 Max 128 GiB, Metal, GLM 5.3 Flash IQ2 (an uncensored variant of the GGUF) with the GLM 5.3 vision encoder. The new `tests/test_server_vision_disk.py` starts its own server and restarts it between steps. On main the first restart reuses 0 of 3605 prompt tokens and the test stops there. With this PR:

  | after a restart | prompt tokens reused |
  | --- | --- |
  | one-image conversation, continued with a second image | 2540 of 3605 |
  | two-image conversation, next turn | 3625 of 3639 |
  | the same when the client omits hidden reasoning | 3632 of 3645 |
  | checkpoint written during a long prefill | 10240 of 12049 |
  | first image changed | 1448 of 2520, the text before it |

  The answers read the right image each time. `tests/test_server_vision_cache.py` passes with and without `--kv-disk-dir`. Its changed-image probes now accept a hit on the text prefix.
- Not run: CUDA, ROCm, Qwen and DeepSeek vision models, tensor-parallel and distributed setups. For those two setups only the refusal is unit-tested.

AI disclosure: this pull request was prepared with AI assistance. The tests and measurements above were run on my machine.

title: Keep the images of a conversation in the embedding cache
body:
Fixes #1317.

A client that resends the conversation sends every image again with each request. `ds4-server` runs the vision encoder for each image that is not in its RAM cache, even when the session already holds the rows of that image. The cache keeps 32 images within 128 MiB. Since #1245 a request can carry 256 images, and 128 MiB is 12 Qwen3.8 images of 1024 tokens, or a single 5346-token GLM 5.3 screenshot (84 MiB). Every request names its images in the same order, so the entry that the cache drops is the one the request needs next: past either limit, each request encodes every image again.

**The change.** The cache is sized for what the resident sessions can name. It has 256 entries for each session. Its budget is, for each session, the image rows that fit the context plus one request body of image files: 576 MiB at the default `--ctx 32768` with a 4096-wide model, 1626.5 MiB at `--ctx 100000`. A conversation that fits its context no longer encodes an image twice while the server runs. The cache allocates only for the images it has received, and the server logs the budget when it starts with `--vision`.

**No new option.** #1317 suggests configurable limits. The limits now follow `--ctx`, and I did not see a second value that is worth an option.

**Not changed.** Every request still looks up every image. Skipping the images that the live KV already holds, which #1317 also suggests, is an engine change, because `ds4_session_sync_multimodal()` takes the rows of every image. This patch only sizes the cache.

`docs/SERVER.md` gave 16 images as the request limit. It now says 256.

## Testing

- `make ds4-server ds4_test` and `./ds4_test --server` pass on an M5 Max, and the CPU server object compiles. The cache test now fills the entries of two sessions. It fails when the table is held at 32 entries.
- **Live test.** M5 Max 128 GiB, Metal, GLM 5.3 Flash IQ2 (an uncensored variant of the GGUF) with the GLM 5.3 vision encoder. A conversation got two screenshots of 5346 and 5700 tokens, then a text-only turn:

  | | text-only turn |
  | --- | --- |
  | old limits, `--ctx 32768` | 123.3 s, the encoder ran twice |
  | this change, `--ctx 393216`, budget 6208 MiB | 0.4 s, the encoder did not run |

  With this change, a follow-up to a 40-image request took 0.2 s and did not run the encoder.

  These runs used my fork build, which has this cache code together with #1343. I did not repeat them on this exact commit.
- Not run: CUDA, ROCm, Qwen and DeepSeek vision models. The change is in `ds4_server.c` and touches no backend.

title: DeepSeek V4.1: make layer-major prefill chunk boundaries saveable
body:
The V4.1 session sync cleared `checkpoint_valid` before every mid-prefill prefill_chunk event and ran the output head once after the whole prompt, because a saved frontier carries the logits of its last token.  ds4-server's continued KV checkpoints are written from exactly those events, so on V4.1 every mid-prefill store was refused with "session has no valid checkpoint to stage" and a stateless client resending a long fixed history re-prefilled all of it on every request.

Run the output head for one row after each layer-major chunk when a progress listener is installed and the decoder is not deferred, and leave the checkpoint valid.

This fix was inspired by the investigation into https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1323 root cause.

title: fix(tokenizer): match the HF DeepSeek V4 pre-tokenizer splits
body:
Fixes #1255

## Problem

The DeepSeek V4 Flash pre-tokenizer (`tokenizer.ggml.pre = "joyai-llm"`) approximated the official one in a single pass and treated every non-ASCII character as a letter. Two splits then differed from the HF tokenizer:

- Non-ASCII punctuation never kept its trailing newline: `：\n` became two tokens instead of one.
- The whitespace lookahead ran past number and CJK runs: `。   多` split the three spaces into `"  "` + `" "`.

On mixed Chinese/English text the token count came out several percent higher than with the HF tokenizer, as the issue reports. The same happens with English text such as `—\n` or `(“`.

## Fix

The HF pre-tokenizer is a sequence of three `Split` stages, each applied to every piece the previous one left: `\p{N}{1,3}`, then the CJK/kana ranges, then the main regex. `ds4.c` now follows the same structure:

- `joyai_pretokenize` isolates number and CJK runs and runs the last regex on each piece, so its lookahead stops at the piece boundary. The last stage also runs inside CJK runs: the kana ranges hold punctuation such as `・` and `゛`, so `ア゛ア` is three pieces.
- `joyai_match_at` tries the alternatives of the last regex in order. It uses Unicode letter, mark, number and whitespace classes, plus a new punctuation/symbol class.
- Characters that no alternative matches stay together, as the `Isolated` split behavior keeps the text between matches.
- The pieces go out through a callback (`joyai_emit_bpe` calls `bpe_emit_piece`, as before), so a test can check them without a model.

The new `punct_symbol` table comes from `gguf-tools/gen_qwen4_unicode.py`, regenerated with the same `regex` 2026.9.3 release; the Qwen tables are byte-identical. The GLM and Qwen branches are unchanged.

## Tests

Apple M3, macOS 26.6.2, Apple clang 21.0.0, default Metal build.

```sh
make                          # no warnings
make test-joyai-pretokenizer  # 241/241 vectors match
make test-session-state       # ok
```

`make test-joyai-pretokenizer` is new and needs no model: it compares the pieces of 241 inputs against the ones the official `tokenizer.json` produces. The vectors are committed; only regenerating them with `tests/gen_joyai_pretokenizer_vectors.py` needs Python and the `tokenizers` package. The commit before this fix fails 4 of them.

Outside the repo I also compared the pieces with HF `pre_tokenize_str` (`tokenizers` 0.23.3):

| Input | Inputs that differ from HF |
|---|---|
| 1,018 repo texts (test prompts, docs, `ds4.c`) | 0 |
| 100,000 random Unicode strings | 201 |
| every codepoint, in several contexts | 4,803 of 1,112,063 |

All the remaining differences involve codepoints that are unassigned in Unicode 15. The tables come from a current `regex` release, while the Oniguruma engine inside `tokenizers` uses an older Unicode version.

Speed, with a BPE vocabulary rebuilt from `tokenizer.json`, per MB: English 0.096 s → 0.103 s, Chinese 0.687 s → 0.207 s, Japanese 1.007 s → 0.264 s. The splitter alone is about 2x slower on ASCII, but it is a small share of the total, and CJK gets faster because pieces are much shorter.

**Not tested:** I could not run a model here, so `./ds4_test --logprob-vectors` and `local-golden.vec` are not checked against this change.

## Notes

- **Disk KV checkpoints:** checkpoints saved by earlier builds are still found by their text prefix, and keep the old token split of that prefix until they are replaced. Nothing gets corrupted. I did not bump `KV_CACHE_PAYLOAD_ABI`, because that would also drop the GLM and Qwen checkpoints, which are unaffected; #1020 adds a tokenizer fingerprint for this case.
- **BPE merge loop (#853):** correct splits keep some mixed punctuation runs together, such as `!！!！…`, that used to be one-character pieces, so more input shapes reach the quadratic merge loop. The worst case does not change: `a`×N was already quadratic at the same cost. #1219, #1027 and #873 address the loop itself.
- **Overlap with #1219:** it changes the signature of the same `bpe_tokenize_text` function, so the two PRs will conflict; I am happy to rebase on whichever lands first.

title: Run the Metal queue keepalive every 250 ms
body:
The main-queue keepalive runs once a second. On an M5 Ultra (256 GB, macOS 27.0) that is not quite often enough: the driver drops the idle process's GPU mappings after about 1 s, so the keepalive loses the race roughly every 6 s and the mappings are rebuilt.

With 205 GB of model views (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, mixed Q4_K / IQ2_XXS / Q2_K quant, ctx 196608) a request that arrives during the rebuild is slow. Measured with a 1-token chat request repeated every 1.4 s, plus 60 s idle sampling "In use system memory" from `ioreg`:

| `DS4_METAL_QUEUE_KEEPALIVE_MS` | drops while idle | request latency |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 (current default) | one every ~6 s | 0.41 s, or 3–11 s during a drop (6 of 24) |
| 500 | none in 60 s | 0.37 s (15 of 15) |
| 250 | none in 60 s | 0.37 s (15 of 15) |

This PR changes the default to 250 ms and updates the comment. Nothing else changes; the environment variable still overrides it.

Decode speed is unchanged: 56.8 t/s at 1000 ms vs 56.6 t/s at 250 ms (300-token generation, three runs each). I did not measure idle power.

Tests: `make test` builds and passes up to `./ds4_test`. `./ds4_test` with `DS4_TEST_MODEL` set to the mixed quant above reports 9 failures (the logprob-vector and SSD-streaming checks, which expect the standard quant, and the `ds4_think_mode_for_context` assertion at `ds4_server.c:18238`). The same 9 fail with `DS4_METAL_QUEUE_KEEPALIVE_MS=1000`, so they are not from this change; I don't have `ds4flash.gguf` on this machine to run the vectors against.

title: feat(image): decode WebP images
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1341. Image input only accepted PNG and JPEG, so a request with an
`image/webp` data URI failed with a misleading `invalid JSON request`. Agent
harnesses that transcode images to WebP then broke on the first image, and
every later request in the session failed too.

This PR adds WebP decoding:

- **`ds4_webp.h`**: a new dependency-free single-header decoder, written in
  the style of the Iris `png.h`/`jpeg.h` (`webp_image`, `webp_load_mem()`,
  `webp_load()`, `webp_free()`, `NULL` on error, `WEBP_MAX_*` limits).
  - Lossy `VP8 ` key frames (RFC 6386).
  - Lossless `VP8L` with all four transforms (RFC 9649).
  - Extended `VP8X` container with an `ALPH` chunk, raw or lossless, with
    any of the four alpha filters.
  - Metadata chunks are skipped. Animated files are rejected with
    `animated WebP images are not supported`.
- **`ds4_image.c`**: WebP is decoded like PNG and JPEG. Alpha is dropped by
  `ds4_oriented_rgb`, exactly as for RGBA PNGs.
- **Server**: `image/webp` is accepted as an OpenAI data URI and as an
  Anthropic `media_type`.
- **CLI and agent**: `/read` recognises WebP files, and the `view_image`
  description mentions WebP.
- **Docs**: `docs/SERVER.md` and `docs/MODELS.md` list WebP. The server doc
  now states the real limit of 256 images per request (it said 16).

## Correctness

The output matches libwebp's default decoding (`dwebp`) bit for bit,
including alpha. VP8 reconstruction is normative, and the YUV to RGB step
reproduces libwebp's fancy chroma upsampler and fixed-point BT.601
conversion. Checked with libwebp 1.6.0:

- **667 files decode to RGBA identical to libwebp** (`channels` equal to
  libwebp's `has_alpha`). They cover:
  - lossy q0 to q100 with every method;
  - normal and simple loop filter, sharpness and segments;
  - 1 to 4 token partitions;
  - odd sizes and 1x1;
  - alpha with every method and filter;
  - lossless z0 to z9, near-lossless, palettes and `-exact`;
  - 12 MP images.
- **Differential fuzzing against a C-only libwebp build** (more than 24M
  mutated inputs across runs, under ASan and UBSan):
  - no crashes or sanitizer reports;
  - the same files are accepted and rejected;
  - pixels differ only on corrupt streams whose coefficients overflow
    libwebp's 32-bit IDCT. That is undefined behavior in libwebp, and its
    C and NEON builds disagree there too; this decoder uses 64-bit
    products.
- **Reviewed** independently for C correctness, security and performance,
  with a second pass that re-checked each finding.

## Tests

- `tests/vision-fixtures/webp/` has 10 small fixtures (about 30 KB in
  total) with the PNG that `dwebp` produces for each. `generate.sh`
  regenerates them.
- `tests/test_image_decode` compares each fixture with its reference,
  through `webp_load()` (RGBA) and through `ds4_image_decode_file()` (RGB).
  It also:
  - cuts each bitstream at every length;
  - corrupts the container (animation flag, canvas size, `ALPH` header,
    RIFF size);
  - checks that a still image carrying an `ANIM` chunk still decodes, as
    RFC 9649 requires.
- `ds4_test --server` checks WebP data URIs for the OpenAI and Anthropic
  APIs.

Not tested: an end-to-end request with a vision model. My machine (M3,
16 GB) cannot load one. Once decoded, the model receives the same RGB
buffer a PNG would produce.

## Performance

On an M3, a 1 MP lossy image decodes in about 20 ms. A 12 MP one takes
about 150 ms, against 127 ms for libwebp built as plain C and 76 ms with
NEON. This is faster than the existing PNG path for images of the same
size.

## License

Parts of the decoder are derived from libwebp (BSD-3-Clause, © Google):
- the VP8 boolean decoder and coefficient parsing;
- the filter strength setup;
- the upsampler and the YUV to RGB conversion.

The header says so, and the license text is in
`licenses/BSD-3-Clause-libwebp.txt`. The VP8 tables come from RFC 6386.

## Open points for the maintainer

- **Patents:** libwebp ships a `PATENTS` file for VP8. Please judge whether
  that matters for an independent implementation.
- **Smaller alternative:** if you prefer not to carry a decoder (about
  1,900 lines plus about 500 lines of tables), the minimal fix for #1341 is a clear
  error such as `unsupported image format: image/webp`. That still leaves
  WebP clients broken, since both upstream APIs accept WebP.
- **Possible follow-ups, not in this PR:**
  - GIF input, which both APIs also accept.
  - A per-request budget of decoded pixels, or decoding outside the
    inference lock. A tiny file can expand to 64 MP. That was already
    possible with PNG and JPEG, but WebP makes it cheaper in bytes.

title: Recursive Flint on Metal with SSD streaming of the experts (looking for measurements on 16 to 32 GB Macs)
body:
Refs #1260.

Flint is 40B total, 2.5B active, 49 layers with 256 experts and 6 routed per token, 4-bit checkpoint of 22.6 GB. Recursive's own engine, `rec`, runs it at 125 tok/s or more on an M4 Pro but requires 48 GB and keeps the whole checkpoint resident. The point of putting it in ds4 is the Macs rec refuses: ds4 already streams routed experts from SSD through a bounded cache, and gets sessions, disk KV checkpoints, the agent and the server with it. This branch does that for Flint, with rec as the reference for tokens, logits and speed. It is a new family in fork-owned files (`ds4_flint_*`, `metal/flint*.metal`, `tests/flint/`, about 8K lines) with some 200 lines of hooks in `ds4.c`, `ds4_metal.m`, `ds4_server.c`, `ds4_cli.c` and the Makefile, following the same rules as the Bonsai 2 branch (`docs/FORK_MAINTAINING.md`). The plan with every measurement is `docs/RECURSIVE_FLINT.md`.

**Why I am opening it now:** everything below was measured on one M4 Pro 48 GB, where streaming can only be simulated with a capped cache. The branch needs numbers from real 16, 24 and 32 GB Macs, and I would rather collect those before deciding what shape an upstream version should take. If you have one of those machines, the section "Field measurements (how to help)" in `docs/RECURSIVE_FLINT.md` has the exact commands; a comment here with the row and the log lines is all it takes. The PR can sit open for that.

## What is done (M4 Pro 48 GB, mains, High Power Mode)

- **Weights.** `gguf-tools/flint_int4_to_gguf.py` writes rec's INT4 checkpoint (the file `rec pull` downloads) into a GGUF bit for bit, one contiguous pack per expert so a miss is one 1.7 MB read. Checked against `mx.dequantize` on all 1375 tensors.
- **Decode.** rec's megakernel ported to Metal (`metal/flint.metal`, Apache 2.0, `licenses/rec-NOTICE.txt`). The per-layer residual trace and all 150144 logits are bit-identical to rec on identical KV, over 56 decode steps at prompts from 5 to 8445 tokens. Speed equals rec: 7.6 vs 7.7 ms/token at 256 tokens, 8.6 vs 9.0 at 4K, 13.2 vs 14.0 at 28K, 21.4 vs 23.7 at 64K, 34.2 vs 39.4 at 128K.
- **Prefill.** Own kernels (chunked, 513-token sliding window, sorted-expert GEMMs). Logits agree with rec to KL 1e-8 on the last row; teacher-forced golden cases match rec's argmax 94.5 to 100%, within rec's own spread across chunk sizes. Faster than rec at every length: 852 vs 684 tok/s at 1K, 708 vs 573 at 16K, 400 vs 349 at 64K, 239 vs 220 at 128K.
- **Server and agent.** Flint's chat template rendered byte-identical to rec's jinja on nine message sets, `<tool_call>NAME<arg_key>...` parsed, reasoning split out, thinking on and off, `ds4-agent` works. Sessions, snapshots and the long-context test pass.
- **SSD streaming of the experts.** Resident weights (1.19 GiB) in an owned bank, experts in an LRU cache of GPU-addressed slots. Apple GPUs do not make a CPU store visible to a running kernel for seconds, so a miss is handled by abort and resume: the megakernel stops at the first layer with an uncached expert, publishes the ids, the host reads the packs and relaunches from that layer. Streamed output is bit-identical to resident output on all eight golden cases, including a 20K-token one, with a 1 GB cache where every layer misses.
- **Streaming speed.** Prefetch and cache-policy ideas were studied on routing traces first and none pays (consecutive tokens share 16% of a layer's experts; LRU variants save at most 4% of misses). The real cost was the GPU power manager dropping the clocks during the 0.3 to 1 ms read gaps, which made every relaunch run 1.7x slower; a 30 µs keep-alive kernel on a side queue (like the TP one) fixes it. With caches capped to what smaller Macs hold, a 300-token agent-style greedy generation runs at 36 tok/s with an 8 GB cache (16 GB class), 41 at 14 GB (24 GB class), 38 at 22 GB, against 22 to 27 without the keep-alive and 85 to 90 resident. Random 1.7 MB reads from this SSD plateau at about 6.5 GB/s over 6 threads.

## What is missing

- Any run on a real 16, 24 or 32 GB Mac: decode speed against cache size, whether the keep-alive behaves the same on M1 to M3 chips and what it costs there, a long-context sweep to 128K with `ds4-bench`, the exactness check. Those are the four measurements in the doc section.
- Lookahead prefetch for caches of 14 GB and up (about 10% in simulation), CUDA (the megakernel is Metal), quants other than Recursive's INT4.

Tests: `make test-flint-kernels`, `make test-flint-stream` (model-free), `tests/flint/stream_check.py`, `ds4_test --server` with the Flint renderer test.

title: Agent: Option/Alt/Ctrl + arrows/backspace
body:
## What

Word-wise cursor motion in the linenoise editor used by `ds4-agent` and the CLI:

- **Option+Left / Option+Right on macOS** (`ESC b` / `ESC f`, also `ESC B` / `ESC F`): previous / next word.
- **Modified arrows on other terminals**: `ESC [ 1;3 D/C` (Alt), `1;4` (Alt+Shift), `1;5` (Ctrl, the word-jump key on most Linux terminals and tmux) and `1;9` (iTerm Meta), in both CSI and SS3 (`ESC O 1;3 D`) form.
- **Option+Backspace** (`ESC DEL`): delete the previous word.

Words are whitespace-delimited (`isspace`). Motion goes through the existing `linenoiseEditPrevLen` / `NextLen` helpers, so multibyte UTF-8 characters are never split and a folded multiline paste is stepped over as one unit. Ctrl+W now shares the same word-boundary helper instead of duplicating the loop.

Behaviour change worth knowing about: a lone ESC followed by `b`, `f`, `B`, `F` or DEL is now a command, as in readline, rather than ESC being dropped and the character inserted.

## Who did what

Most of this was written by DS4 itself (the agent in this repo), working on the original request: the word-motion functions, the CSI/SS3 modifier parsing, the `ESC b/f` handling, and the first version of `tests/test_linenoise_wordnav.c`.

I then had it reviewed, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 made these adjustments on top:

- Switched word delimiters from `' '` to `isspace`, and pulled the boundary scan into two shared helpers (`linenoiseWordStartBefore` / `linenoiseWordStartAfter`), also used by `linenoiseEditDeletePrevWord`.
- Added Ctrl (5) and iTerm Meta (9) modifiers to the accepted arrow modifiers.
- Added Option+Backspace (`ESC DEL`) word deletion.
- Made `linenoiseEditMovePrevWord` / `MoveNextWord` `static`.
- Removed a redundant condition in the `ESC` handling.
- Extended the test: Ctrl/Meta arrows, uppercase `ESC B/F`, `ESC DEL`, UTF-8 words, and word motion across a folded multiline paste.
- Added the test binary to `.gitignore` and `make clean`.

## Testing

- macOS, default (Metal) build: `make tests/test_linenoise_wordnav && ./tests/test_linenoise_wordnav` passes (drives `linenoiseEditFeed` through pipes using `LINENOISE_ASSUME_TTY`, no terminal needed), and `make ds4-agent` builds without warnings. The test is also wired into `make test`.
- Tried by hand in `ds4-agent` on macOS: Option+Left/Right jump words.
- Not run: the full `make test` (needs a model), `make cpu`, CUDA. No inference code is touched, so there is no speed or correctness impact on the backends.

This touches `linenoise.c`, as do #426 and #699, so I'd expect small rebases against those if they land first. I didn't find an existing PR or issue for word navigation.

title: K3: bound SSD streaming memory and accelerate Metal prefill/decode
body:
## Summary

Improve Kimi K3 GGUF SSD streaming on memory-constrained Apple Silicon, validated on an M1 Max with 32 GiB of unified memory.

This PR combines memory accounting fixes, Metal kernel optimizations and lossless static-weight streaming. With `--ssd-streaming`, the engine now selects the optimized configuration automatically while preserving explicit overrides.

## Changes

- Share a bounded memory budget across runtime tensors, expert caching, static buffers and transient mappings. Retire temporary mappings and stop with diagnostics when memory headroom is insufficient.
- Optimize M1 BF16 projections and fused QKVG, and reuse streamed weights across prefill chunks of up to 64 tokens while retaining the existing FP32 arithmetic.
- Overlap aligned static reads with computation and stream the output head through bounded buffers.
- Add an optional lossless static cache with source-identity and CRC checks, used by both prefill and decode. The original GGUF remains unchanged.
- Make `--ssd-streaming` default to a 10 GiB expert-cache target, chunk64 and automatic discovery of the adjacent static cache. Preserve explicit settings and existing API context defaults.

The sidecar requires approximately 59 GiB for the tested model. Without a sidecar or libzstd support, ordinary GGUF streaming remains available.

## Performance

Machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GiB RAM, Metal.
Model: `Kimi-K3-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K.gguf`.
Configuration: 10 GiB expert cache, chunk64, ctx1024, greedy decoding.
Prompt: `Ciao, come stai?` — 44 formatted tokens.

| Incremental comparison | Reference | Optimized | Time reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill, median of two runs per version | 180.819 s | 102.796 s | 43.15% |
| Decode, eight steps, average per step | 41.488 s | 28.379 s | 31.60% |

Prefill compares against `bb4ae3e9`, using alternating reference/optimized runs. Decode compares against `8ba3fac3` in one measured pair.

These are separate incremental comparisons with different baselines. They do not measure the total branch speedup against upstream.

The final automatic-configuration check completed prefill in 102.14 s, with normal memory pressure and no new swap.

## Validation

Commands run on the final implementation:

```sh
make -j2 all
make test-k3-streaming
make -j2 test-k3-static-staging test-k3-static-cache
```

Additional validation during development covered memory planning, mapping lifetime, BF16/fused QKVG, and MLA/KDA prefill.

- All 163,840 final FP32 logits matched bitwise across the four prefill benchmark runs.
- All 931,840 boundary values matched in the multi-chunk KDA/MLA check.
- All 5,309 blocks of the real-model static cache passed byte-for-byte roundtrip verification.
- CPU fixtures covered override precedence, discovery, invalid files and the no-zstd fallback.
- The automatic configuration reproduced the full logits of the explicit optimized configuration.

## Limitations and outstanding checks

The measurements cover a short prompt. Longer contexts and sustained sessions were not benchmarked; filesystem cache, temperature and external load were not controlled.

An earlier test run hit the K3.1 FP8 keys/power-of-two scale assertion in `tests/test_k3_metal`. It was observed before the BF16 optimization and remains unresolved; the entire test suite is not claimed to pass.

The CPU portability build and a full-branch before/after `ds4-bench` CSV comparison requested by CONTRIBUTING.md remain to be completed.

title: Looking for volunteer testers: Kimi K3 SSD streaming on Apple Silicon
body:
I’m looking for volunteers to test the Kimi K3 inference optimizations proposed in [PR #1353 — K3: bound SSD streaming memory and accelerate Metal prefill/decode](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/pull/1353).

Testing has so far been done on an M1 Max with 32 GB. Results from other Apple Silicon machines would be very helpful, especially Macs with 64, 96, 128 GB or more unified memory. Additional 32 GB testers are also welcome.

We need help checking:
- Prefill and generation performance.
- Automatic expert-cache sizing with --ssd-streaming.
- Memory pressure, swap usage and stability.
- Output correctness and possible regressions.
The PR includes Metal kernel optimizations, improved SSD reads, an optional lossless cache for static weights, and automatic memory-aware configuration.

You don’t need to contribute code. We’re looking for people willing to build the PR, run reproducible tests and share logs. Ideally, you already have the original Kimi K3 mixed-Q2 GGUF, which requires approximately 800 GiB of SSD storage.

Interested in helping? Please comment with:
- Mac model and chip.
- Unified memory capacity.
- macOS version.
- SSD model and connection type.
We can then coordinate suitable test commands and comparisons for your machine. Reports of failures and regressions are just as valuable as performance improvements.

title: server: stream the text held at a tool-call marker when the final parse finds no call
body:
## Problem

With tools in the request, a streamed reply that mentions a tool-call marker in plain text is cut off at the marker, while the same request with `"stream": false` returns it whole.

The live streams stop projecting text at the first thing that looks like the start of a tool-call block (`find_any_tool_start()`, which also matches the GLM/Qwen `<tool_call>` wrapper) and leave the decision to the final parser. When the final parser then finds no tool call, the held bytes are ordinary text, but:

- the OpenAI chat stream and the Anthropic stream never send them;
- the Responses stream sends them only after a DSML parse failure (the existing recovery path), not when the parse succeeds with no call.

The turn ends with `finish_reason: "stop"` and no tool call, so the client has no way to tell the reply was truncated.

The case that hit me: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017, `IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix`), an agent reply that explained another model's tool-call output quoted `<tool_call>` in backticks, and the client received it only up to the backtick, three turns in a row. Because the client replays the text it received, the next request no longer matched the live KV state either, so each following turn reloaded from disk and re-prefilled ~22K tokens.

A marker mentioned inside reasoning is worse: the thinking projection holds everything after it, so the rest of the reasoning and the whole answer are never sent.

Repro (any of the three streaming APIs, thinking on or off):

```sh
curl -sN localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"deepseek-v4-flash","stream":true,"temperature":0,"max_tokens":300,
  "thinking":{"type":"disabled"},
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"bash","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"command":{"type":"string"}}}}}],
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Do not call any tool. Write exactly two short sentences. The first must contain the literal text `<tool_call>` in backticks. The second must start with the word Afterwards."}]}'
```

On b3f5018 the streamed content is ``Some models wrap tool calls in ` `` on OpenAI, Anthropic and Responses alike; non-streaming returns both sentences.

## Fix

At finish, when the response has no tool calls and is not an error, send the unsent tail, split at `</think>` exactly like `split_reasoning_content()` (reasoning before it, content after it). Each stream now tracks `sent_end`, the cursor up to which bytes were sent or consumed as syntax (`<think>`, `</think>`), so whitespace held before the marker is not lost either. One shared helper (`stream_unsent_tail_split()`) is used by the OpenAI, Anthropic and Responses streams; the Responses recovery path now goes through it too, so a reply that stopped inside reasoning is no longer dumped into `output_text`.

Unchanged: real tool calls (DSML and the live `tool_calls` / `tool_use` projection), error turns, and every stream that never hit a marker (its tail is already empty at finish). The final parser stays authoritative, as the existing comment on the stream state structs says.

## Tests

New unit tests in `ds4_server.c`:

- `test_stream_quoted_tool_markers_match_final_parse`: ten cases (marker quoted in content, at the very start, after `\n\n`, plain-XML `<tool_calls>`/`</tool_calls>` pair, complete and incomplete `<tool_call>` wrapper inside reasoning, a V4.1 DSML name inside reasoning, requests without tools, a non-ASCII tail). Each one is streamed through all three protocols in 1, 3, 7 and 4096 byte steps and must end with the same content and reasoning as the non-streaming result, including the worker's recovery when a quoted marker does not parse as DSML.
- `test_stream_real_tool_calls_unchanged_by_tail_catch_up`: DS4 and V4.1 DSML calls, all three protocols: content is `Before.`, the call arrives structured, no DSML text leaks.
- `test_stream_error_finish_does_not_flush_held_text`.

Without the fix the new tests fail 81 assertions; with it `./ds4_test --server` passes, no new warnings (`-Wall -Wextra`).

Live, M5 Ultra 256 GB, V4.1 Flash 1017 resident, DSpark, same requests before/after:

| Check | b3f5018 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| quoted `<tool_call>`: OpenAI stream, thinking off / on | cut at the backtick | full, equal to non-stream |
| quoted `<tool_call>`: Anthropic stream | cut | full |
| quoted `<tool_call>`: Responses stream | cut | full |
| real `bash` tool call: OpenAI (thinking off / on), non-stream, Anthropic, Responses | structured call | identical |
| plain `PONG`, greedy prime list (text hash) | — | identical |

Request timings and generated token counts were the same on both builds; the change only touches the wire projection.

title: Sanitizer and fuzzing findings: JPEG decoder undefined behavior and two data races
body:
I ran the model-free tests on current `main` (b3f5018) under ASan, UBSan,
LeakSanitizer and ThreadSanitizer, and fuzzed `ds4_image_decode_memory` with
libFuzzer. The test suite itself is clean under ASan, UBSan and LSan on macOS
arm64, Linux arm64 and Linux x86-64. The findings below are in the JPEG decoder
and in two places where threads share state.

## JPEG decoder (`third_party/iris/jpeg.h`), found by fuzzing

1. **Out-of-bounds read of a subsampled luma plane** (`jpeg_load_mem`, the
   YCbCr to RGB loops), when luma has a smaller sampling factor than chroma.
   This is the bug #1112 fixes: its `jpeg.h` change resolves every crashing
   input the fuzzer found, though the PR no longer applies cleanly to `main`.
2. **Negative index into the Huffman symbol table** (`jpeg_decode_huffman`,
   slow path). Two causes: a scan that names a Huffman table the file never
   defines, which the decoder then uses with zeroed `maxcode` entries, and an
   oversubscribed table whose codes do not fit their lengths. The read stays
   inside the table struct, so ASan does not see it; UBSan does.
3. **Shift past the width of an int in `jpeg_get_bits`**, when a malformed
   table asks for more than 16 extra bits (up to 255). #981 noted this and
   left it for a separate PR.
4. **Signed integer overflow** in the IDCT and in the DC predictor, from
   coefficients that corrupt data can make arbitrarily large.

Items 2-4 are undefined behavior on corrupt input; I saw no memory corruption
from them, but they are reachable from any image a client sends.

## Data races, found by ThreadSanitizer

5. `ds4_tp_big_gate_exchange` (`ds4_tp.c`) initializes two function statics on
   first use without synchronization. ThreadSanitizer reports it in
   `test_tp_commands` and `test_tp_tcp`, where two ranks share a process. The
   arrival grace also takes its floor from whichever `tp` calls first.
6. The Metal queue keepalive stop flag (`ds4_metal.m`) is a `volatile int`
   written by the main thread while the keepalive thread polls it.

Both are low impact in production, where each rank runs in its own process and
`volatile` keeps the loop from spinning forever, but they are real races.

## Fixes

I have fixes for items 2-6 on a branch, with regression tests in
`tests/test_image_decode.c`, and will open a PR referencing this issue:

- Huffman tables start with no codes, and oversubscribed tables are rejected.
- Bit reads longer than 16 bits are rejected.
- Coefficients and the DC predictor are kept 16-bit, as libjpeg and the
  progressive path already do, and the IDCT uses 64-bit intermediates.
- The big-gate settings are read per call; the keepalive flag uses the
  `__atomic` builtins `ds4_metal.m` already uses elsewhere.

Decoded pixels are identical to `main` on 309 valid JPEG and PNG files.
With these fixes plus the `jpeg.h` change from #1112, another eight minutes
of fuzzing under ASan and UBSan found nothing.

title: fix: reject corrupt JPEG Huffman data, bound coefficient math and fix two data races
body:
Closes #1356

Fixes items 2-6 of #1356: undefined behavior in the JPEG decoder on corrupt
input, and two data races. Item 1, the out-of-bounds luma read, is left to
#1112.

## Changes

`third_party/iris/jpeg.h`:

- Every Huffman table starts with no codes, so a scan that names a table the
  file never defines fails to decode instead of indexing `values[-1]`.
- Oversubscribed Huffman tables are rejected when they are built, the same
  check libjpeg makes.
- `jpeg_get_bits` rejects reads longer than 16 bits, the most JPEG ever codes.
- Coefficients and the DC predictor are kept 16-bit, as libjpeg's `JCOEF` and
  this decoder's progressive path already do, and the IDCT uses 64-bit
  intermediates, like libjpeg's `JLONG`.

`ds4_tp.c`: `ds4_tp_big_gate_exchange` reads `DS4_TP_BIG_GATE_DEBUG` and
`DS4_TP_BIG_GATE_ARRIVAL_MS` on each call instead of caching them in function
statics. The arrival floor now comes from the calling `tp`'s own gate timeout.

`ds4_metal.m`: the queue keepalive stop flag uses `__atomic` loads and stores
instead of `volatile`.

`tests/test_image_decode.c`: four JPEGs built in memory cover an oversubscribed
table, an undefined table, a DC category of 17 and extreme coefficients with
16-bit quantizers.

## Testing

On an M3 Max (macOS, Metal) and in Ubuntu 26.04 containers (arm64, and x86-64
under Rosetta):

- `tests/test_image_decode`: passes. On `main`, three of the new checks fail;
  the extreme-coefficient check fails only under UBSan.
- Decoded pixel fingerprints are identical to `main` on 309 valid JPEG and PNG
  files: Pillow-generated baseline and progressive images at several
  qualities and subsamplings, plus the repository fixtures.
- Release builds have no warnings: `make` on macOS, `make cpu` on Linux.
- ThreadSanitizer: no reports in `test_tp_commands` and `test_tp_tcp` (macOS
  and Linux), or in `test-qwen4-ssd-experts` and
  `test-qwen4-resident-arithmetic` (macOS).
- libFuzzer on `ds4_image_decode_memory` with these fixes and the `jpeg.h`
  change from #1112: eight minutes under ASan and under UBSan found nothing.

No model was used. Distributed inference over a real network, CUDA and ROCm
were not run; the `ds4_tp.c` change only affects how the arrival timeout is
computed.

## Conflicts

`tests/test_image_decode.c` conflicts with #1348, #1112, #1113 and #1110, which
also add checks to that file. The conflict is only where the new functions and
the `main()` calls go. `jpeg.h` merges cleanly with #1112, #1113 and #1110.
